body.text: abhidharmadīpaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s> (The Lamp of <s>Abhidharma</s>)

body.text: vibhāṣāprabhāvṛttisahitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Together with the <s>Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s> (Commentary [Illuminating] the <s>Vibhāṣā</s>).

body.text: prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: First chapter.

body.text: prathamaḥ pādaḥ |
body.translated_text: First quarter (<s>pāda</s>).

body.text: om svasti | namaḥ sarvajñāya |
body.translated_text: Oṃ. May there be well-being! Homage to the Omniscient One!

body.text: yo duḥkhahetuvyupaśāntimārgaṃ pradarśayāmāsa narāmarebhyaḥ /
body.translated_text: He who showed to humans and gods the path of the cessation of the cause of suffering —

body.text: atra ṣaṣṭhīsamāsaparigrahe sati mārgasatyaṃ pradhānam | tathā coktam- "mārgavidahaṃ mārgasya ..........." iti vistaraḥ | taduktaṃ bhavati- yo devamanuṣyebhyo mārgaṃ pradarśitavāniti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] When a genitive compound (<s>ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa</s>) is accepted, the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>) is primary. And thus it is said: 'I am the knower of the path, of the path...' and so on in detail. What is stated is: He who showed the path to gods and humans.

body.text: samāhāralakṣaṇadvandvaparikalpe tu caturṇāmapyāryasatyānāṃ prādhānyam | tathā coktam- "idaṃ duḥkhasatyamiti bhikṣavaḥ pūrvamananuśruteṣu dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurudapādi" iti vistaraḥ | taduktaṃ bhavati- yo devamanuṣyebhyaścatvāryāryasatyāni pradarśitavāniti |
body.translated_text: But when a collective-type compound (<s>samāhāralakṣaṇadvandva</s>) is construed, all four Noble Truths (<s>āryasatya</s>) are primary. And thus it is said: 'This, O monks, is the truth of suffering — regarding <s>dharmas</s> not previously heard, the <s>dharma</s>-eye arose,' and so on in detail. What is stated is: He who showed the four Noble Truths to gods and humans.

body.text: tatra duḥkhasatyamekavidhamabhinirvṛttisvābhāvyāt | tathā coktam- "duḥkhā hi bhikṣavo bhavābhinirvṛttiḥ" iti | jātyādyaṣṭaprakāraṃ vā phalabhūtā (

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 2)

children.text: ) vā pañcopādānaskandhāḥ | athavā paurvāntikaṃ pañcāṅgamaparāntikaṃ dvyaṅgaṃ tadubhayamabhisamasya saptāṅgam |
children.translated_text: ) it is the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>). Or alternatively, the prior-end [component] has five limbs; the posterior-end, two limbs; combining both, it has seven limbs.

body.translated_text: There, the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>) is of one kind, due to its nature as coming-into-being (<s>abhinirvṛtti</s>). And thus it is said: 'For, O monks, coming-into-being in [the cycle of] existence is suffering.' Or it is of eight kinds, beginning with birth (<s>jāti</s>) and the rest; or as the result-aspect (

body.text: samudayasatyamekavidhaṃ tṛṣṇānirdeśāt | dvividhaṃ karmakleśātmakatvāt | pañcāṅgāni vā paurvāntikāparāntikāṅgasaṃgrahāt, hetubhūtā vā pañcopādānaskandhāḥ |
body.translated_text: The truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>) is of one kind, from the teaching of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). It is twofold, being constituted by <s>karma</s> (action) and <s>kleśa</s> (affliction). Or it has five limbs, from the inclusion of prior-end and posterior-end limbs; or, as the cause-aspect, it is the five aggregates of clinging.

body.text: nirodhasatyamekaprakāramapratisandhijanmanirodhāt | satyadvayaprahānṇabhedād dvividham, sopadhinirupadhiśeṣadhātubhedādvā | triprakāraṃ vā prahāṇavirāganirodhadhātubhedāt | catuṣprakāraṃ vā catuṣphalabhedāt |
body.translated_text: The truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) is of one kind, being the cessation of rebirth-linking birth. It is twofold, from the distinction of abandoning the two [preceding] truths, or from the distinction of the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element with remainder (<s>sopadhiśeṣa</s>) and without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>). Or it is threefold, from the distinction of the elements of abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>), dispassion (<s>virāga</s>), and cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). Or it is fourfold, from the distinction of the four fruits [of the path].

body.text: mārgasatyamekaprakāraṃ samyagdṛṣṭinirdeśāt | dviprakāraṃ vā sāsravānāsrabhedāt, darśanabhāvanābhedādvā | triprakāraṃ śīlasamādhiprajñāskandhabhedāt catuṣprakāraṃ vā prayogāmārgādibhedāt | pratipadbhedādvā | aṣṭaprakāraṃ samyagdṛṣṭyādyaṅgabhāvāt |
body.translated_text: The truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>) is of one kind, from the teaching of right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>). Or it is twofold, from the distinction of with-outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) and without-outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>), or from the distinction of the path of seeing (<s>darśana</s>) and the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). It is threefold, from the distinction of the aggregate of morality (<s>śīla</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). Or fourfold, from the distinction of the preparatory path (<s>prayogamārga</s>) and so forth. Or from the distinction of practices (<s>pratipad</s>). It is eightfold, due to the limb-nature of right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest.

body.text: ityetāni catvāryāryasatyāni parijñeyaprahātavyasākṣātkartavyabhāvayitavyānīti bhagavān pradarśayāmāsa narāmarebhyasteṣāṃ satyadarśanabhavyatvāttadarthamudbhūtatvāt | atastāneva mārgapradarśanakarmaṇābhipretān | atasteṣu saṃpradānābhidhāyinī caturthī |
body.translated_text: Thus these four Noble Truths are to be fully known (<s>parijñeya</s>), to be abandoned (<s>prahātavya</s>), to be directly realized (<s>sākṣātkartavya</s>), and to be cultivated (<s>bhāvayitavya</s>) — this the <s>Bhagavān</s> showed to humans and gods, because they are capable of seeing the truths, and because [the <s>Bhagavān</s>] arose for their sake. Therefore, those very [beings] are intended by the act of showing the path. Hence, the dative case denoting the recipient (<s>saṃpradāna</s>) is used for them.

body.text: taṃ satpathajñaṃ praṇipatya buddhaṃ śāstraṃ kariṣyāmyabhidharmadīpam // Abhidh-d_1 //
body.translated_text: Having bowed to that <s>Buddha</s>, the knower of the true path (<s>satpatha</s>), I shall compose the treatise [called] <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s> (Lamp of <s>Abhidharma</s>). (Abhidh-d 1)

body.text: 'tam'; iti yaḥ prativiśiṣṭaviśeṣaṇaparichinnayacchabdacodanayā parigṛhītaḥ sa tacchabdena pūrvaprakṛtāpekṣopajanitayacchabdasaṃbandhena saṃspṛśyate | saṃścāsau panthāśca satpathaḥ | athavā satāṃ panthāḥ satpathaḥ | taṃ satpathaṃ jānīta iti satpathajñaḥ | 'taṃ satpathajñaṃ praṇipatya'; iti kāyavāṅmanaskarmabhirabhyarthyetyarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'That' (<s>tam</s>) — he who is delimited by the distinguished qualifier through the relative-pronoun construction is here referred to by the demonstrative pronoun, through the connection with the relative pronoun generated by reference to the previously stated [subject]. 'True path' (<s>satpatha</s>): It is both 'true' (<s>sat</s>) and a 'path' (<s>pantha</s>); or, the path of the good (<s>satām panthāḥ</s>). 'Knower of the true path' (<s>satpathajña</s>): he who knows that true path. 'Having bowed to that knower of the true path' — meaning: having entreated through the actions of body, speech, and mind.

body.text: 'buddham'; iti viśiṣṭaviśeṣaṇaparicchinno 'pi buddhānusāripudgalapratipattyarthaṃ sākṣātpratītapadārthakena nāmnāpadiśyate buddha iti | atra buddhaśabdasya prasiddhiḥ budherakarmakatvavivakṣāyāṃ kartari kto bhavati | sarve vā jñānārthā gatyarthā iti karmakartari ktavidhānam | abhidhānalakṣaṇatvācca kṛttaddhitasamāsānāmacodyam | dṛṣṭaṃ cedaṃ buddha ityabhidhānaṃ kartari loke prayujyamānam | tadyathā nidrāvigame padārthānubodhe 'vidyānirāse ca vibuddhaḥ prabuddho devadatta iti | evaṃ bhagavānapyavidyānidrāvigamāt, sarvārthāvabodhācca buddho vibuddhaḥ prabuddha ityucyate | yathā vā paripākaviśeṣāt svayameva buddhaṃ padmamevaṃ bhagavānapi prajñādiguṇaprakarṣaparipākād buddho vibuddhaḥ prabuddha iti | sarvaśiṣṭaprayogācca | dṛṣṭo hyatra śiṣṭaprayogaḥ | yathoktaṃ vyāsena |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Buddha</s>' — although delimited by the distinguished qualifier, he is designated by a name whose meaning is directly understood, for the purpose of [guiding] the practice of persons who follow the <s>Buddha</s>. Here, the etymology of the word <s>buddha</s>: from the root <s>budh</s>, when intransitivity is intended, the past participle (<s>kta</s>) is formed in the agent sense. Or, since all roots meaning 'to know' also mean 'to go,' the <s>kta</s> suffix is prescribed in the agent-patient sense (<s>karmakartari</s>). And since <s>kṛt</s>, <s>taddhita</s>, and compound [formations] are of the nature of designation, there is no objection. And this designation '<s>buddha</s>' is seen being used in the world in the agent sense. For example: at the removal of sleep, at the comprehension of an object, and at the destruction of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), [one says] '<s>Devadatta</s> is awakened (<s>vibuddha</s>), enlightened (<s>prabuddha</s>).' Thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> too, due to the removal of the sleep of ignorance and the comprehension of all objects, is called '<s>Buddha</s>,' 'awakened,' 'enlightened.' Or, just as a lotus (<s>padma</s>) blooms (<s>buddha</s>) by itself through the excellence of ripening, so the <s>Bhagavān</s> too, through the ripening of the excellence of qualities such as wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), is '<s>Buddha</s>,' 'awakened,' 'enlightened.' And [this is confirmed] by the usage of all learned authorities. For learned usage is observed here. As stated by <s>Vyāsa</s>:

body.text: "etadbuddhvā bhaved buddhaḥ kimanyad buddhalakṣaṇam" iti |
body.translated_text: 'Having known this, one becomes a <s>Buddha</s> — what other characteristic of a <s>Buddha</s> is there?'

body.text: tasmādaśiṣṭacodyeṣvanādaraḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, no attention is paid to objections by the unlearned.

body.text: atra punaḥ ślokasya pūrvārdhe parārthasaṃpādakaṃ vaiśāradyadvayaṃ pradarśitam | tṛtīye pāde svārthasampaddyotakaṃ vaiśāradyadvayamāviṣkṛtam | na hyakṣīṇāsravaḥ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 4)

children.text: ) śakto mārgamākhyātumiti | na cāsamyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sarvadharmānabhisaṃboddhumalamiti | kathaṃ punareta
children.translated_text: ) is not capable of proclaiming the path. Nor is one who is not a perfectly and fully awakened one (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>) capable of comprehending all <s>dharmas</s>. But how then these

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here again, in the first half of the verse, the two kinds of confidence (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) that accomplish the welfare of others are shown. In the third quarter, the two kinds of confidence illuminating one's own attainment are revealed. For one whose outflows (<s>āsrava</s>) are not destroyed (

body.text: digātmāno vaiśeṣikaparikalpitā asattvādeva naiva nityāḥ nānityāḥ | asattvaṃ pūrvamāviṣkṛtam |
body.translated_text: [refutation of <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>:] The selves (<s>ātman</s>) imagined by the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, being without real existence, are neither permanent nor impermanent. Their non-existence has already been revealed.

body.text: sāṃkhyīyamapi pradhānaṃ na nityam | kutaḥ ? traiguṇyasya
body.translated_text: The <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> school too is not permanent. Why?

children.translated_text: If the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the rest — do not undergo change, the non-appearance of the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) would follow;
and since the <s>Prakṛti</s> (primal nature) is non-different from its modifications (<s>vikāra</s>), [it would follow that Prakṛti too is] subject to modification. (Abhidh-d 2)

body.text: yadi sattvādayo guṇāḥ nānyathā bhavanti hrāsavṛddhibhāvena, na tarhi kiñcittebhyo vyaktamutpadyate | athānyathā bhavanti, anityāstarhi prāpnuvanti | karmavaśādadoṣa iti cet, atra brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] If the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the rest — do not undergo change through increase and decrease, then nothing manifest arises from them. But if they do undergo change, then they are proved to be impermanent. If [one objects:] 'there is no fault, due to the power of <s>karma</s>' — to this we reply:

children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> (action) is not [applicable here], because of its own [nature as] abandonment;

body.text: yadi pratipuruṣaṃ karmāṇi buddhipūrvāṇyabuddhikṛtāni vā pradhāne vidyante sādhāraṇapradhānakalpanāvaiyarthyaṃ tarhi prāptamiti | kiñca,
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] If <s>karmas</s> — whether intentional or unintentional — exist in the <s>Pradhāna</s> individually for each <s>puruṣa</s> (person), then the postulation of a universal <s>Pradhāna</s> becomes purposeless. Furthermore,

children.translated_text: the state of being constituted by the knower (<s>jña</s>), the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>), and the self; impurities (<s>mala</s>);
and in the first position [where karma belongs to puruṣa], the absence of liberation (<s>mukti</s>); and in the second [where karma belongs to pradhāna], other calamities too [follow]. (Abhidh-d 3)

body.text: yadi tāni karmāṇi puruṣātmakāni nanvevaṃ sati mokṣābhāvaḥ prāpnoti | puruṣanityatve karmanityatvaprasaṅgāt | caśabdāt puruṣakartṛtvādidoṣāśca | 'dvitīye 'nye 'pyupaplavāḥ |'; prādhānātmakapakṣa ete ca doṣāḥ prasajantyanye 'pi copaplavāḥ sādhāraṇatvādakṛtābhyāgamānirmokṣaprasaṅgāt | tasmāt trīṇyeva ca sarvajñābhihitānyasaṃskṛtāni nityānīti siddham |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] If those <s>karmas</s> belong to the <s>puruṣa</s>, then indeed the absence of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) would follow, since if <s>puruṣa</s> is permanent, <s>karma</s> would also be permanent. By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), [there follow] the faults of <s>puruṣa</s> being an agent and so forth. 'In the second [position], other calamities too' — in the position [where karma belongs to] <s>Pradhāna</s>, these faults and still other calamities follow, because of [<s>Pradhāna</s>'s] universality — the consequences of actions not done accruing [to one] and of non-liberation [follow]. Therefore, it is established that there are only three unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) [dharmas] proclaimed by the Omniscient One that are permanent.

body.text: vyākhyātāḥ aṣṭau padārthāḥ- saṃskṛtāḥ pañca, trayaścāsaṃskṛtāḥ | etāvaccaitatsarvaṃ yaduta saṃskṛtaṃ cāsaṃskṛtaṃ ceti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus eight categories of existents (<s>padārtha</s>) have been explained — five conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and three unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). This much is all that exists, namely the conditioned and the unconditioned.

body.text: taccaitadāyatanadhātuvyavasthānena vyavasthāpyate |
body.translated_text: And this is systematized through the arrangement of sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) and elements (<s>dhātu</s>).

body.text: dvādaśa khalvāyatanāni | cakṣurādīni dharmāyatanāntāni |
body.translated_text: There are indeed twelve sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) — beginning with the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) and ending with the <s>dharma</s>-base (<s>dharmāyatana</s>).

body.text: aṣṭādaśa dhātavaḥ | cakṣurdhātū rūpadhātuścakṣurvijñānadhāturyāvanmanodhāturdharmadhāturmanovijñānadhāturiti |
body.translated_text: There are eighteen elements (<s>dhātu</s>) — the eye-element, form-element, and eye-consciousness-element, up to the mind-element, <s>dharma</s>-element, and mind-consciousness-element.

body.text: tatra tāvat
body.translated_text: Therein, now:

children.translated_text: The form-aggregate (<s>rūpaskandha</s>) indeed [comprises] the ten sense-bases and elements beginning with the eye;

The three aggregates designated as '<s>dharma</s>' [comprise] the perception, etc., together with <s>avijñapti</s> (non-informative matter), and the three permanent [unconditioned dharmas]. (Abhidh-d 4)

body.text: manaḥsaṃjñakamanyo 'pi saptavijñānadhātavaḥ /
body.translated_text: The one designated as 'mind' (<s>manas</s>) is also the seven consciousness-elements.

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: kaḥ punarāyatanadhātvarthaḥ ? taducyate |
body.translated_text: What then is the meaning of 'sense-base' (<s>āyatana</s>) and 'element' (<s>dhātu</s>)? To that it is said:

body.text: āyadvāraṃ hyāyatanaṃ dhāturgotraṃ nirucyate // Abhidh-d_5 //
body.translated_text: A sense-base (<s>āyatana</s>) is a door of arising (<s>āyadvāra</s>); an element (<s>dhātu</s>) is explained as 'lineage' (<s>gotra</s>). (Abhidh-d 5)

body.text: taduktaṃ bhavati- cittacaitasikākhyamāyametāni tanvantītyāyatanāni | yasmātsapta cittadhātavaścatvāraścārūpiṇaḥ skandhā ebhyaścatuṣpratyayātmakebhyaḥ pratāyante tadutpattiṃ vā pratyāyante tasmādāyatanāni |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] What is stated is: These [sense-bases] extend (<s>tanvanti</s>) the arising (<s>āya</s>) designated as mind and mental factors (<s>cittacaitasika</s>) — hence they are 'sense-bases' (<s>āyatana</s>). Since the seven consciousness-elements and the four formless aggregates arise from these, which are constituted by the four conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>), or since [these bases] serve as conditions for the arising of those — therefore [they are called] 'sense-bases.'

body.text: dhātvarthastu gotrārthaḥ | taduktaṃ bhavati- ekasmiṃñccharīraparvate 'ṣṭādaśa (

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 6)

children.text: ) dharmagotrāṇi- iti | dhruvadvayasyāpyatra pratinidhisthānīyāḥ prāptayo gotrabhūtā vidyante | ākāśaṃ ca sarvabhūtabhaumikarūpādhāramiti tadapyatrāstīti | svalakṣaṇadhāraṇādvā taddhātutvam |
children.translated_text: ) <s>dharma</s>-lineages. For the two permanent [unconditioned dharmas, i.e., analytical and non-analytical cessation] too, their representative acquisitions (<s>prāpti</s>), which are of the nature of lineage, exist here [in the body]. And space (<s>ākāśa</s>), being the support of all elemental and derivative forms, also exists here. Or, [they are called] 'elements' because they bear their own characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>).

body.translated_text: The meaning of 'element' (<s>dhātu</s>) is 'lineage' (<s>gotra</s>). What is stated is: In the single mountain of the body, there are eighteen (

body.text: atha kasmāddvādaśāyatanānyaṣṭādaśa ca dhātavaḥ pṛthaṅnirucyante ? nanvanyataranirdeśādgatārthametaditi | atrocyate |
body.translated_text: Now, why are the twelve sense-bases and eighteen elements taught separately? Is not the teaching of one [system] sufficient to convey the meaning of the other? To this it is said:

children.translated_text: The Sage (<s>Muni</s>) taught the twelve sense-bases due to suitability for meditation (<s>yoga</s>) and the like,
and the eighteen elements for those [who hold] the notion of unity of cognition and so forth. (Abhidh-d 6)

body.text: skandheṣu hi dṛśyamāneṣu yoginorasarvajñeyapratibimbakānyupatiṣṭhanti | dhātuṣvapi saptacittadhātupratibimbakāni sādṛśyād duravadhārāṇi bhavanti | dhātuskandhavyavasthā cāyataneṣūkteṣvabhihitakāraṇā bhavanti sulakṣā ceti dhātudeśanā | tadūrdhvaṃ skandhaprajñaptiḥ | yathoktam- "cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpaṃ cotpadyate cakṣurvijñānam | trayāṇāṃ sannipātāt sparśaḥ | sahajā vedanā cetanā" iti | tasmādāyatanāni dhātūnāṃ yoniḥ, dhātavaḥ skandhānāmiti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For when the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) are observed, not all [objects] serve as reflections for the yogin's [contemplation of] the knowable. But in the case of the elements too, the reflections of the seven consciousness-elements are difficult to distinguish due to their similarity. The arrangement of elements and aggregates, when the sense-bases are taught, becomes well-established with [clear] causes. And [the classification by] sense-bases is also easy to discern — hence the teaching of elements. After that comes the designation of aggregates. As stated: 'Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises; from the meeting of the three, there is contact; co-arising are feeling, volition.' Therefore, the sense-bases are the source (<s>yoni</s>) of the elements; the elements are the source of the aggregates.

body.text: 'buddhyādyekatvadhīhānyai dhātūṃścāṣṭādaśoktavān |'; sapta vijñānadhātavo hi deśyamānā buddhyaikatvagrāhaṃ nivartayanti | piṇḍaikātmagrāhaṃ ca nivartayanti |
body.translated_text: 'And the eighteen elements for those [who hold] the notion of unity of cognition and so forth' — For the seven consciousness-elements, when taught, remove the grasping of unity regarding cognition (<s>buddhi</s>). They also remove the grasping of a unitary self in the [body-mind] aggregate.

body.text: vaibhāṣāḥ punarāhuḥ- "rūpasaṃmūḍhānāmāyatanadeśanā | cittacaittasaṃmūḍhānāṃ skandhadeśanā | rūpacittasaṃmūḍhānāṃ dhātudeśanā | tīkṣṇendriyāṇāṃ vā skandhadeśanā | madhyendriyāṇāmāyatanadeśanā | mṛdvindriyāṇāṃ dhātudeśanā | evaṃ saṃkṣiṃptamapyavistararucīnām |"
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> say: 'The teaching of sense-bases is for those confused about form. The teaching of aggregates is for those confused about mind and mental factors. The teaching of elements is for those confused about both form and mind. Or, the teaching of aggregates is for those of sharp faculties; the teaching of sense-bases for those of medium faculties; the teaching of elements for those of dull faculties. Likewise [these are] also for those who prefer the concise, the moderate, and the detailed [expositions].'

body.text: athavā 'buddhyaikatvādidhīhānyai dhātūṃścāṣṭādaśoktavān |'; ye khalu buddhyaikatvamadhyavasitā (

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 7)

children.text: ) manasaścetanāyāṃ vā rūpacittaikatvaṃ vā teṣāṃ mamatva buddhinirāsārthamaṣṭādaśadhātūnuktavāniti |
children.translated_text: ) or the unity of mind and consciousness, or the unity of form and mind — for the removal of their sense of 'mine' (<s>mamatva</s>), [the Sage] taught the eighteen elements.

body.translated_text: Or: 'And the eighteen elements for those [who hold] the notion of unity of cognition and so forth' — those who have determined the unity of cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) (

body.text: kaḥ punarayaṃ ṣaḍbhyo vijñānakāyebhyo 'nyo manodhātuḥ ? na khalu kaścidanyaḥ | kiṃ tarhi ?
body.translated_text: What then is this mind-element (<s>manodhātu</s>), different from the six consciousness-bodies (<s>vijñānakāya</s>)? There is certainly nothing different. What then?

body.text: ṣaṇṇāmanyo nyatantratvātkāraṇaṃ yaddhi tanmanaḥ /
body.translated_text: Because one [consciousness] functions as the cause of the other six, that is [called] 'mind' (<s>manas</s>).

body.text: svaviṣayālambanakriyāpekṣayā vijñānāntarotpādanādiśaktyapekṣayā caikasya vijñānasya tridhā nirdeśaḥ kriyate- 'manaścittaṃ vijñānaṃ ca'; ityanāgatasyātītasyāpi bhūtabhāvinyā saṃjñayā vyapadeśaḥ | evaṃ sati "aṣṭādaśadhātavastraiyadhvikāḥ" ityabhidharmagrantho 'pyanulomito bhavati | sūtre 'pi coktam- "yatpunastadbhavati cittamiti vā mana iti vā" iti vistaraḥ | tadevaṃ vyācakṣāṇena bhavatā nityaṃ karaṇaṃ mano 'nityaścātmā kartā'; iti pratiṣiddhaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] With respect to the function of apprehending its own object, and with respect to the capacity of producing another consciousness and so forth, a single consciousness is taught in three ways: 'mind (<s>manas</s>), thought (<s>citta</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>).' Even the future [mind] and the past [mind] are designated by the name applicable to the present. Thus, the <s>Abhidharma</s> text [stating] 'the eighteen elements belong to all three times' is also upheld. And in the <s>sūtra</s> too it is said: 'That which is called thought (<s>citta</s>), or mind (<s>manas</s>),' and so on in detail. By explaining it thus, [the view that] 'mind is a permanent instrument and the self (<s>ātman</s>) is an impermanent agent' is refuted.

body.text: atha kasmāttadeva cakṣurvijñānādīnāṃ pañcānāmapyāśrayatvena noktamiti ?
body.translated_text: Now why is that very [mind-element] not stated as the support (<s>āśraya</s>) of all five [sense-]consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness?

body.text: atra brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: To this we say:

body.text: rūpyarūpāśrayāstitvātpañcānāṃ rūpyudāhṛtaḥ // Abhidh-d_7 //
body.translated_text: Because there exist both material and immaterial supports for the five [sense-consciousnesses], the material [support] is stated [for them]. (Abhidh-d 7)

body.text: cakṣurādīnāmasādhāraṇatvāditi |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because [the five sense organs] beginning with the eye are non-shared (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) [supports of their respective consciousnesses].

body.text: atha yaduktam- 'sasaṃprayogā sahasaṃgraheṇa iti | kau punarimau saṃgrahasaṃprayogāvityetadapadiśyate |
body.translated_text: Now, as stated: 'together with association and inclusion' — what then are these 'inclusion' (<s>saṃgraha</s>) and 'association' (<s>saṃprayoga</s>)? This is indicated [as follows]:

body.text: skandhāyatanadhātūnāṃ svātmanā saṃgrahaḥ smṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text: The inclusion of aggregates, sense-bases, and elements is remembered as [being] by their own nature (<s>svātman</s>).

body.text: kṣaṇaparamāṇujātisaṃkhyānāṃ pratyekaṃ yathāyogaṃ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ | kasmāt ?
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The inclusion of moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>), atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>), genus (<s>jāti</s>), and number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>) should be understood individually as appropriate. Why?

children.translated_text: Because of permanent non-separation from one's own nature.

body.text: tasmād dravyātmasaṃgrahaḥ | sacchabdanimittaṃ hi sato bhāvaḥ sattā dravyaṃ prakṛtyarthaḥ | dravyātmasaṃgrahaḥ pratyayārthaḥ, satkriyā vopacārasattārūpā | vaiśeṣikasattā tu nobhayamarthāntaratvāt | na hyarthāntaraṃ svātmopapadyate | kiñca, svātantryāt | niruktyapabhraṃśācca | nahi ghaṭena sattotpādyate | āvaraṇābhāvāttannityatvābhyu pagamācca | niruktyapi bhraśyate- sattāyogātsantī ti | syānmālyādivatsattāvānvā kriyāvaditi | yastvayaṃ saṃgravastvādiṣu saṃgrahaḥ proktaḥ sa kādācitkatvād gauṇo mantavyo na mukhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, [it is] a collection of substantial entities (<s>dravyātmasaṃgraha</s>). For the cause of the word 'sat' (existent) is: the existence (<s>sattā</s>) of what is real (<s>sat</s>) is substance (<s>dravya</s>), which is the primary meaning; the collection of substantial entities is the secondary meaning, or the conventional existence in the form of efficacious action (<s>satkriyā</s>). But the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> [concept of] existence (<s>sattā</s>) is neither [of these], because it is a different entity. For a different entity does not establish its own self. Moreover, because of [its] independence. And because of the corruption of etymology — for existence is not produced by a pot. Because of the absence of obstruction, and because of the acceptance of its permanence. Etymology also fails — 'they are existent (<s>santī</s>) because of connection with existence (<s>sattā</s>).' It could be [said that they are existent] like possessing a garland and the like, or possessing existence like possessing action. But the collection [of dharmas] that you have stated in relation to aggregates and the like — that, because of being occasional, should be considered secondary, not primary.

body.text: saṃprayogastu
body.translated_text: Association (<s>saṃprayoga</s>), however, [means]

body.text: samatvaṃ cittacaitasām // Abhidh-d_8 //
body.translated_text: the equality of mind and mental factors. (Abhidh-d 8)

body.text: pañcabhiḥ samālambane prayujyanta iti | samprayuktāścittacaitasā eva dharmā nānya iti ||
body.translated_text: They are associated with the five [qualities], being directed toward the same object (<s>samālambana</s>). Only mental (<s>citta</s>) and mental-factor (<s>caitasa</s>) dharmas are associated — not others.

body.text: atha ya ete sūtrāntareṣu skandhāyatanadhātusaṃśabditā dharmāḥ śrūyante te kimeṣveva saṃgrahaṃ gacchanti, āhosvinneti ? atrocyate |
body.translated_text: Now, those dharmas that are heard in other sūtras designated by the terms <s>skandha</s> (aggregate), <s>āyatana</s> (sense-base), and <s>dhātu</s> (element) — are they included in these very [categories], or not? To this it is said:

children.translated_text: Those bearing those names that are stated in other sūtras — their inclusion in these very [categories]
should be stated by one who knows the system of the treatise, having considered their own characteristics with the intellect. (Abhidh-d 9)

body.text: tatra tāvacchīlaskandhādīnāṃ pañcānāṃ skandhānāṃ śīlaskandho rūpaskandhena saṃgṛhītaḥ | śeṣāḥ saṃskāraskandhena | daśa kṛtsnāyatanānyapyalobhasvābhāvyādaṣṭānāṃ dharmāyatanena | saparivāṇāṇi tu manodharmāyatanābhyāṃ pañcaskandhasvabhāvatvāt | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 10)
The last two totality-bases, because of having the nature of four aggregates, [are included] in the mind-base and dharma-base.

body.translated_text: There, to begin with, of the five aggregates such as the morality-aggregate (<s>śīlaskandha</s>) and the rest: the morality-aggregate is included in the form-aggregate (<s>rūpaskandha</s>); the rest in the formations-aggregate (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>). The ten totality-bases (<s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>) also, due to their nature of non-greed and the like, are [included] in the eight dharma-bases (<s>dharmāyatana</s>). But with their retinues, [they are included] in the mind-base and dharma-base, because of having the nature of the five aggregates.

body.text: dhātūnāmapi ṣaḍ dhātavaḥ | tebhyaścatvāraḥ spraṣṭavyadhātūnām, pañcamo rūpadhātūnāṃ, ṣaṣṭhaḥ saptabhiścittadhātubhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Also among the elements, [there are] six elements. Of those, four are [included] among the tangible elements (<s>spraṣṭavyadhātu</s>); the fifth among the form-elements (<s>rūpadhātu</s>); the sixth with the seven consciousness-elements (<s>cittadhātu</s>).

body.text: anyonyasaṃgraho jñeyaḥ skandhādīnāṃ yathāyatham /
body.translated_text: The mutual inclusion of aggregates and the like should be known accordingly.

body.text: rūpaskandhasya daśasvāyatanadhātuṣu rūpiṣu saṃgraho veditavyaḥ | dharmāyatanadhātupradeśena trayāṇāmapi skandhānāṃ yathāyogadharmāyatanadhātubhyām | antyasya tu manaāyatanasya saptabhiścittadhātubhiriti ||
body.translated_text: The inclusion of the form-aggregate should be understood in the ten form-possessing sense-bases and elements. By a portion of the dharma-base and dharma-element, three aggregates [are included] appropriately in the dharma-base and dharma-element. But the last, the mind-base, [is included] with the seven consciousness-elements.

body.text: atha kasmādasaṃskṛtaṃ skandhairasaṃgṛhītam ? brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, why is the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) not included in the aggregates? We say:

body.text: nādhvasvapatanādibhyo nityānāṃ skandhasaṃgrahaḥ // Abhidh-d_10 //
body.translated_text: There is no inclusion of permanent [dharmas] in the aggregates, because of non-falling into the three times, and the like. (Abhidh-d 10)

body.text: ādiśabdānniṣkriyatvaskandhalakṣaṇaviyuktatvācceti ||
body.translated_text: By the word 'and the like' — because of being without activity and being separated from the characteristics of the aggregates.

children.translated_text: The inclusion of the eighty thousand dharma-aggregates (<s>dharmaskandha</s>)
should be known in the entries (<s>avataraṇa</s>) alone, since through them there is entry into the noble path. (Abhidh-d 11)

body.text: aśītiḥ khalvavataraṇasahasrāṇi yairvineyāḥ sanmārgamavatāryante ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, eighty thousand entries are those by which beings to be trained are led to enter the noble path.

body.text: kiṃ punasteṣāmekaikasya pramāṇam ? brūmaḥ | atrācāryāṇāṃ bhedaṃgatā buddhayaḥ | kecidāhuḥ
body.translated_text: What then is the measure of each one of those? We say: Here the understandings of the teachers have gone in different directions. Some say:

body.text: dharmaskandhapramāṇaṃ tu satyāderekaśaḥ kathā /
body.translated_text: The measure of a dharma-aggregate is: a single discourse on the truths and the rest,

body.text: satyadhyānasamādhisamāpattivimokṣapratītyasamutpādaskandhādīnāmekaśaḥ kathā dharmaskandhaḥ | rāgādicaritapratipakṣo dharmaskandha ityācāryakam |
body.translated_text: a single discourse on the truths, meditations (<s>dhyāna</s>), concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>), liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), aggregates, and the like, is a dharma-aggregate. The antidote to conduct [dominated by] passion and the like is a dharma-aggregate — this is the teachers' [view].

body.text: tatsatattvaṃ tu keṣāñcidvāṅnāmāpīṣyate paraiḥ // Abhidh-d_12 //
body.translated_text: The true nature of that, however — for some, even speech and name are accepted by others. (Abhidh-d 12)

body.text: yeṣāṃ tāvadvāksvabhāvaṃ buddhavacanaṃ teṣāmaśītidharmaskandhasahastrāṇi rūpaskandhaikadeśena saṃgṛhītāni | yeṣāṃ punarnāmasvabhāvaṃ teṣāṃ saṃskāraskandhasaṃgṛhītāni | ayaṃ tvāgamaḥ- "jīvato bhagavato vāṅnāma svabhāvaṃ buddhavacanaṃ gauṇamukhyanyāyena | parinirvṛtasya tu nāmasvabhāvameva, na vāksvabhāvam, brahmasvaratvānmunīndrasya, lokavācāṃ tatsādṛśyānupapatteḥ ||"
body.translated_text: For those for whom the Buddha's word has the nature of speech — for them, the eighty thousand dharma-aggregate-thousands are included by a portion of the form-aggregate. But for those for whom [it has] the nature of name — for them, [they are] included in the formations-aggregate. But the tradition [states]: 'While the Blessed One was alive, the Buddha's word had the nature of both speech and name, by the principle of secondary and primary [meanings]. But after [his] final nirvāṇa, it has the nature of name alone, not of speech, because the Lord of Sages had a divine voice (<s>brahmasvara</s>), since the similarity of worldly speech to that is impossible.'

body.text: kasmātpunarete ṣaḍ dhātavaḥ pṛthagucyante ? yasmādete
body.translated_text: Why then are these six elements stated separately? Because these

children.translated_text: are considered the fundamental basis for the designation of beings — the six elements,
stated because, through their differentiation, the conceit 'I am' ceases. (Abhidh-d 13)

body.text: ete hi ṣaḍdhātavo garbhāvakrāntikāle maulaṃ sattvadravyaprajñaptyupādānam | katham ? yasmādayaṃ kāyākhyaḥ samucchrāyaḥ pṛthivīdhātunā khakkhaṭalakṣaṇena sandhārito bhūtāntaravṛttyudreko 'sthisnāyunakhadantaromādisaṃcayaḥ | abdhātunā dravasnehalakṣaṇena śleṣmarudhirādimayenābhiṣyanditasaṃśleṣitabhūtāntaraḥ | tejodhātunoṣṇasvabhāvena paripācitakledadaurgandhaḥ | vāyunā ca preraṇātmakena saṃcāritabhojanarasadhātuviṇmūtraśleṣmapittasaṃcayaḥ | nabhodhātunā ca mukhanāsikākarṇādicchidrajanitabhojanapānādipraveśaniṣkramaṇakriyaḥ | vijñānadhātunā vastūpalabdhilakṣaṇena vāyudhātukriyādhyāsinotpāditasaṃjanitāṅgapratyaṅgaceṣṭo maulaṃ sattvadravyamityupacaryate | indriyāṇi cakṣurādīni khalvatra bhūtagrahaṇena gṛhyante, caitasikā vijñānagrahaṇeneti prādhānyād bhūtacittagrahaṇam |
body.translated_text: For these six elements, at the time of descent into the womb, are the fundamental material basis for the designation of a being-substance. How? Because this bodily mass called 'body' is sustained by the earth-element characterized by solidity — an excess of activity of the other great elements — the accumulation of bones, sinews, nails, teeth, hair, and the like. By the water-element, characterized by fluidity and cohesion, consisting of phlegm, blood, and the like, [the body is] moistened and held together with the other great elements. By the fire-element, of hot nature, the moisture and bad odor are cooked away. By wind, whose nature is propulsion, the accumulation of food-essence, bodily constituents, feces, urine, phlegm, and bile is circulated. By the space-element, through the apertures of mouth, nostrils, ears, and the like, the activities of entering and exiting food, drink, and the like [are possible]. By the consciousness-element, characterized by apprehension of objects, [the being] — whose limbs and minor limbs are set in motion by relying upon the activity of the wind-element — is conventionally designated as a fundamental being-substance. The sense-faculties such as the eye are here grasped by the term 'great elements,' and the mental factors by the term 'consciousness' — thus the terms 'great elements' and 'mind' are [used] by predominance.

body.text: kimarthaṃ punareta eva dhātuṣaṭkamupadiṣṭam ? yasmādasya bhedāt 'asmimāno nivartate'; | katham ? ṣaḍdhātuprabhedādātmadṛṣṭinirāsaḥ | tannirāsādasmimānasamuddhātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: For what purpose then is this sixfold element taught? Because through its differentiation, 'the conceit "I am" ceases.' How? Through the analysis into six elements, the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) is removed. Through its removal, the conceit 'I am' is uprooted.

body.text: 'satkāyadṛṣṭipuṣṭatvāt'
body.translated_text: 'Because of being nourished by the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>)' —

body.text: ityatra punaḥ
body.translated_text: in this regard, moreover,

children.translated_text: afflicted consciousness alone

body.text: vijñānadhāturabhipretam | kasmāt ?
body.translated_text: is what is intended by the consciousness-element. Why?

body.text: draṣṭavyaṃ janmani śrayāt /
body.translated_text: It should be seen [thus], because in birth [it is] the support.

body.text: yasmādete ṣaḍdhātavo janmano niśrayabhūtāstasmāt | 'kliṣṭameva vijñānaṃ'; atra draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: Because these six elements are the basis of birth, therefore 'afflicted consciousness alone' should be understood here.

body.text: kaḥ punarayamākāśadhāturanyaḥ punaḥ pṛthagākāśāt ? taducyate |
body.translated_text: What then is this space-element, which is other than and separate from space itself? To that it is said:

body.text: khadhātuḥ pṛthagākāśādrūpāyatanasaṃgrahāt // Abhidh-d_14 //
body.translated_text: The space-element [is different] from space, because of being included in the form-base. (Abhidh-d 14)

body.text: ākāśaṃ hi dharmāyatanasaṃgṛhītaṃ nityaṃ ca | ākāśadhātustu cākṣuṣo rūpāyatanasaṃgṛhītaḥ, ālokatamaḥsvabhāvo varṇaviśeṣo vātāyanacchidrādyabhivyaktarūpaḥ | tatpunaḥ
body.translated_text: For space is included in the dharma-base and is permanent. But the space-element is visible, included in the form-base — it is a color-variety of the nature of light and darkness, manifested as the form of window-apertures and the like. That, moreover:

children.text: nabhaḥ khalu nabho dhātorāsanno hetureṣa tu /
children.translated_text: Space indeed — the space-element is a proximate support; this [is the support]

children.text: bhūtānāṃ tāni tajjasya rūpasyaitattu cetasaḥ // Abhidh-d_15 //
children.translated_text: of the great elements; those [are the support] of derivative form born from them; and that [is the support] of consciousness. (Abhidh-d 15)

body.text: uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "pṛthivyapsu niśritā | āpo vāyau | vāyurākāśe | ākāśaṃ tu nityatvātsvapratiṣṭhitam" iti |
body.translated_text: For the Blessed One said: 'Earth rests on water; water on wind; wind on space; but space, being permanent, is self-supported.'

body.text: yadi khalu svapratiṣṭhamākāśaṃ kasmāttarhyuṃktam- ākāśamāloke sati prajñāyate |" brūmaḥ | naiṣa doṣaḥ | ādheyenādhāraprajñāpanāt | sarvasya khalu saṃskṛtasya mūrtikriyāpratilambhe gaganamādhāraḥ | athavākāśadhāturatrākāśaśabdenoktaḥ | sa hi brāhmaṇaḥ praṣṭā tasminnākāśadhātāvākāśasaṃjñītyata evoktamāloke sati prajñāyate | na cākāśamāloke sati prajñāyate, (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 14)

children.text: ) anidarśanatvāt | eṣa akāśadhāturbhūtānāmāsanno niśrayaḥ | tāni tu tajjasyopādāyarūpasya | tadapi vijñānasya | vijñānamadhicaitasikānāṃ viprayuktānāṃ ca dharmāṇām | ata ākāśaṃ trailokyapratiṣṭhā | tadabhāve trailokyamapratiṣṭhitamanādhāraṃ, na prajñāyeta | tasmādākāśaṃ jagadutpattipralayanimittaṃ na nārāyaṇa iti siddham | gatametat ||
children.translated_text: because it is non-demonstrable. This space-element is the proximate support of the great elements. Those [great elements] are [the support] of derivative form born from them. That [derivative form is the support] of consciousness. Consciousness [is the support] of the mental factors and the disjoined formations (<s>viprayukta</s>). Therefore, space is the foundation of the triple world. In its absence, the triple world would be without foundation, without support — it would not be cognized. Therefore, it is established that space is the cause of the world's arising and dissolution, not <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. This point has been covered.

body.translated_text: If indeed space is self-supported, why then was it said: 'Space is cognized when there is light'? We say: There is no fault here — because the container is designated through the contained. For all conditioned [things], space is the container for the attainment of material form and activity. Alternatively, the space-element is here referred to by the word 'space.' For that brahmin questioner had the notion of 'space' regarding the space-element — therefore it was said 'it is cognized when there is light.' But space [itself] is not cognized when there is light,

body.text: idānīṃ vaktavyam | ṣaṇṇāmadhyātmikānāṃ dhātūnāṃ ko 'nukramaḥ ? brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now it should be stated: What is the order of the six internal elements? We say:

children.translated_text: That which functions through direct perception is [stated] first; that which grasps without contact, even —
beyond that, what is more distant in object; and what is sharper than the other. (Abhidh-d 16)

body.text: pratyakṣavṛttīni khalu cakṣurādīni pañca prāguktāni | tebhyo 'pyaprāptagrāhiṇī dve prāgukte | tayorapi yadya(dda)vīyo 'rthaṃ tatprāguktam | prāptagrāhiṇāṃ tu 'paṭiṣṭhamitarādapi'; yatpaṭutaraṃ tatprāguktamiti ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, the five [faculties] beginning with the eye, stated earlier, function through direct perception. Beyond even those, two grasping without contact were stated earlier. Of those two, whichever is more distant in object — that was stated first. But of those grasping with contact — 'what is sharper than the other': whichever is sharper — that was stated first.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vimāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau prathamādhyāsya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the commentary called <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>, [this is] the second quarter of the first chapter.

body.text: prathamādhyāye
body.translated_text: In the first chapter,

body.text: tṛtīyapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: the third quarter.

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | ya ete 'ṣṭādaśadhātavaḥ, eṣāṃ kati sanidarśanāḥ katyanidarśanāḥ ? kati sapratighāḥ katya pratidhāḥ ? kati vyākṛtāḥ katyavyākṛtā iti ? ata idaṃ pratāyate ||
body.translated_text: Now this should be stated: Of these eighteen elements, how many are demonstrable (<s>sanidarśana</s>) and how many non-demonstrable? How many are resistant (<s>sapratigha</s>) and how many non-resistant? How many are determined (<s>vyākṛta</s>) and how many undetermined? Therefore this is expounded:

children.translated_text: Demonstrable is the object of the first [i.e., the eye-element] —

body.text: ādyasya cakṣurdhātoryortho rūpadhātvākhyaḥ sa sanidarśanaḥ | saha nidarśanena nirdiṣṭa iti kṛtvā | nidarśanaṃ vāsya saṃbandhi vidyata iti sanidarśanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: the object of the first, the eye-element — that which is called the form-element — is demonstrable; because it is pointed out together with demonstration (<s>nidarśana</s>). Or, demonstration is related to it, therefore [it is] 'with demonstration' (<s>sanidarśana</s>).

body.text: mūrtāḥ sapratighā daśa /
body.translated_text: The ten material [elements] are resistant (<s>sapratigha</s>).

body.text: saptacittadhātūndharmadhātuṃ ca hitvā daśānye mūrtā dhātavaḥ 'sapratighā daśa'; |
body.translated_text: Excluding the seven consciousness-elements and the dharma-element, the other ten material elements are 'resistant — ten.'

body.text: pratigho nāma pratighātaḥ | sa ca trividhaḥ | āvaraṇaviṣayālambanapratighātaḥ | tatrāvaraṇapratighātaḥ svedeśe parasyotpattipratibandhaḥ | sa tu mūrtānāmeva saṃsthānavatāṃ paramāṇūnāṃ digdeśanirdeśyānāṃ dharmāṇām | yathā hastohastena pratihanyate upalo vopalena | viṣayapratighātaścakṣurādīnāṃ viṣayiṇāṃ rūpādiṣu sveṣu viṣayeṣu pratighātaḥ | yasya yasmin vṛttiḥ sannipātalakṣaṇā kāritrākhyā ca sa tasmin pratihanyate tato 'nyatrāvṛtteḥ | ālambanapratighātaścittacaittānāṃ sveṣvālambaneṣu pratighātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Resistance means counter-impact (<s>pratighāta</s>). And it is threefold: obstruction-resistance (<s>āvaraṇapratighāta</s>), object-resistance (<s>viṣayapratighāta</s>), and object-of-cognition-resistance (<s>ālambanapratighāta</s>). There, obstruction-resistance is the prevention of another's arising in one's own place. That belongs only to material [dharmas] having spatial configuration — atoms that can be indicated by direction and place. Just as a hand is resisted by a hand, or a stone by a stone. Object-resistance is the resistance of possessors of objects such as the eye and the like, in their respective objects such as form and the like. That in which there is functioning characterized by contact and called efficacy — that is resisted in that [object], because it does not function elsewhere. And object-of-cognition-resistance is the resistance of mind and mental factors in their respective objects of cognition.

body.text: kaḥ punarviṣayālambanayorviśeṣaḥ ? yasminyasya kāritraṃ sa tasya viṣayaḥ | yaccittacaittairgṛhyate tadālambanam | tadihāvaraṇapratighātena daśānāṃ sapratighatvamanyonyāvaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: What then is the difference between object and object-of-cognition? That in which something has efficacy is its object (<s>viṣaya</s>). That which is grasped by mind and mental factors is the object-of-cognition (<s>ālambana</s>). Here, by obstruction-resistance, the ten [material elements] are resistant, because of mutual obstruction.

body.text: 'ye dharmā viṣayapratighātena sapratighā āvaraṇapratighātenāpi te'; iti ? catuṣkoṭikaḥ | prathamā koṭiḥ- saptacittadhātavodharmadhātupradeśaśca yaḥ saṃprayuktaḥ | dvitīyā- pañca viṣayāḥ | tṛtīyā- pañcendriyāṇi | caturthī- dharmadhātupradeśaḥ saṃprayuktakavarjaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Are those dharmas that are resistant by object-resistance also [resistant] by obstruction-resistance?' — [This forms] a four-cornered [inquiry]. First corner: the seven consciousness-elements and the portion of the dharma-element that is associated [with consciousness]. Second: the five objects. Third: the five sense-faculties. Fourth: the portion of the dharma-element excluding the associated [dharmas].

body.text: 'ye viṣayapratighātena sapratighā ālambanapratighātenāpi te'; iti paścātpādakaḥ- ye tāvadālambanapratighātena viṣayapratighātenāpi te syuḥ | viṣayapratighātena, nālambanapratighātena pañcendriyāṇi |
body.translated_text: 'Are those resistant by object-resistance also [resistant] by object-of-cognition-resistance?' — [The answer is given] by the last quarter: those that are [resistant] by object-of-cognition-resistance would also be [resistant] by object-resistance. But [resistant] by object-resistance, not by object-of-cognition-resistance — the five sense-faculties.

children.translated_text: 'Where resistance can be made by others to mind that is about to arise —
that should be known as resistant; from the opposite, non-resistant is accepted.'

body.text: iti bhadantakumāralātaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus [says] the venerable <s>Kumāralāta</s>.

body.text: uktāḥ sapratighāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The resistant [elements] have been stated.

body.text: kuśalādayo 'bhidhīyante |
body.translated_text: The wholesome and the rest are declared:

body.text: anyatra rūpaśabdābhyāṃ ta evāvyākṛtā matāḥ // Abhidh-d_17 //
body.translated_text: Except for form and sound, those same [ten] are considered undetermined (<s>avyākṛta</s>). (Abhidh-d 17)

body.text: ta eva daśāvyākṛtā rūpaśabdadhātuvarjāḥ | tau hi triprakārau kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtau ||
body.translated_text: Those same ten are undetermined, excluding the form-element and sound-element. For those two are of three kinds: wholesome, unwholesome, and undetermined.

children.translated_text: The rest are threefold —

body.text: saptacittadhātavo hi triprakārāḥ | dharmadhātuśca | saṃprayuktastriprakāraḥ, viprayukto 'saṃskṛtaśca | yathāśāstraṃ kaścit triprakāraḥ kaścidekaprakāraḥ saṃbhavato draṣṭavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: for the seven consciousness-elements are of three kinds. And the dharma-element [is also threefold]: the associated [portion] is of three kinds; the disjoined and unconditioned [portions are also counted]. According to the treatise, some are of three kinds, some of one kind — [this] should be seen based on possibility.

body.text: kaḥ punaḥ kuśalārthaḥ ? śikṣitārthaḥ kuśalārthaḥ pravīṇavat | vipākahetāvaupamiko draṣṭavyaḥ | evamakuśalo 'pi avyākṛtastūbhayapakṣāvyākaraṇādavyākṛta ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What then is the meaning of 'wholesome' (<s>kuśala</s>)? The meaning of 'wholesome' is 'trained' — like 'skilled.' It should be seen analogically in the sense of the cause of [pleasant] fruition. Similarly 'unwholesome' also. 'Undetermined' (<s>avyākṛta</s>) — the intent is that [it is] undetermined because of non-declaration regarding either side.

body.text: kati kāmadhātupratisaṃyuktāḥ kati yāvadapratisaṃyuktā iti | tadidamārabhyate |
body.translated_text: How many are associated with the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>)? How many, up to how many, are unassociated? This [topic] is now commenced.

children.translated_text: Here, all

body.text: kāmadhātau sarve 'pyaṣṭādaśa vidyante |
body.translated_text: in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), all eighteen exist.

children.text:
rūpadhātau caturdaśa /
rasagandhau savijñānau dhātū hitvā
children.translated_text: In the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), fourteen, excluding the <s>dhātus</s> of taste (<s>rasa</s>) and smell (<s>gandha</s>) along with their cognitions —

body.text: gandharasadhātū tadvijñānadhātū ca hitvā | ārūpye
body.translated_text: excluding the <s>dhātu</s> of smell (<s>gandha</s>) and taste (<s>rasa</s>), and the <s>dhātus</s> of their cognitions. In the formless realm (<s>ārūpya</s>) —

body.text: trayontimāḥ // Abhidh-d_18 //
body.translated_text: the last three. (Abhidh-d 18)

body.text: agrapaścāntimaḥ smṛtaḥ | antāścetyupasaṃkhyānam | paścimā manodhātumanovijñānadhātudharmadhātava evamārūpyadhātau santi ||
body.translated_text: The last of a sequence is remembered as 'final' (<s>antima</s>). 'The final ones' — this is an enumeration. The last [three] are: <s>manodhātu</s> (mind-element), <s>manovijñānadhātu</s> (mental-consciousness-element), and <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of phenomena) — thus these exist in the formless realm.

body.text: kati sāsravāḥ katyanāsravāḥ
body.translated_text: How many are with influxes (<s>sāsrava</s>)? How many are without influxes (<s>anāsrava</s>)?

children.translated_text: The last three are [both] with and without influxes (<s>sāsrava</s> and <s>anāsrava</s>).

body.text: anantaroktāstatra sāsravāḥ duḥkhasamudayasatyasaṃgṛhītāḥ | anāsravāstu mārgasatyāsaṃskṛtasaṃgṛhītāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those just mentioned — when with influxes, they are included in the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>) and the truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>). But when without influxes, they are included in the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>) and the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>).

body.text: śeṣāstu sāsravāḥ /
body.translated_text: The rest, however, are with influxes (<s>sāsrava</s>).

body.text: pañcadaśadhātavaḥ sāsravāḥ, āsravasaṃyogitvavyavakīrṇatvāṅgabhāvebhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Fifteen <s>dhātus</s> are with influxes, because of their conjunction with influxes, their being intermixed, and their being constituents [thereof].

body.text: kośakārastvāha- "anuśayānuśayanātsāsravāḥ |" tadetadabrahma | na | niruktānuśayārthāparijñānāt | niruktāparijñānaṃ tāvat | anuśayānuśayanāt sānuśayāḥ |
body.translated_text: But the author of the <s>Kośa</s> (<s>kośakāra</s>) says: 'They are with influxes because of the clinging (<s>anuśayana</s>) of the latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>).' This is improper. No — because the etymological meaning of <s>anuśaya</s> is not understood. First, the failure to understand the etymology: 'they have latent dispositions because of the clinging of latent dispositions' —

body.text: na sāsravā na yāvadoghāḥ | āsravā hi ābhavāgrādyāvadavīcimupādāya cittasantatiṃ strāvayanti svayaṃ ca sravantītyāsravāḥ | anuśayāstvanuśerate | kleśāḥ kliśnanti | granthā grathnanti | saṃyojanāni saṃyojayanti | oghāḥ apaharanti | iti svakriyādvāreṇaiteṣu vargeṣvetā nairuktyasaṃjñā niviśanta ityeṣā vyākhyānītirjyāyasī |
body.translated_text: [this makes them] 'with latent dispositions,' not 'with influxes,' not even 'with floods' (<s>ogha</s>). For influxes (<s>āsrava</s>) flow (<s>srāvayanti</s>) through the continuum of consciousness from the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) down to <s>Avīci</s>, and they themselves flow — hence 'influxes.' But latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>) lie latent (<s>anuśerate</s>). Afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) afflict (<s>kliśnanti</s>). Bonds (<s>grantha</s>) bind (<s>grathnanti</s>). Fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) fetter (<s>saṃyojayanti</s>). Floods (<s>ogha</s>) carry away (<s>apaharanti</s>). Thus, through their respective activities, these etymological designations are applied to these [respective] groups — this interpretation is superior.

body.text: anuśayārtho 'pi yadi puṣṭyarthastena mārganirvāṇālambaneṣu mithyādṛṣṭyādiṣu poṣotkarṣadarśanāt, nirvāṇamārgayorapi rūpādivat sāsravatvaprasaṅga iti | gatametat ||
body.translated_text: If the meaning of <s>anuśaya</s> is taken as 'nourishment' (<s>puṣṭi</s>), then since the enhancement of nourishment is seen even in wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) and the like that take the path and <s>nirvāṇa</s> as their objects, there would be the absurd consequence that <s>nirvāṇa</s> and the path too would be with influxes, just like form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like. This [objection] has been answered.

body.text: kati savitarkāḥ kati savicārā iti vistaraḥ |
body.translated_text: How many are with <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought)? How many are with <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought)? — and so forth in detail.

body.text: sālambaprathamāḥ pañca sopacārāstrayastridhā // Abhidh-d_19 //
body.translated_text: The first five among those that have objects, together with three that have [both <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>], are threefold. (Abhidh-d 19)

body.text: sālambanānāṃ dhātūnāṃ ye prathamāḥ pañca te savitarkāḥ savicārāḥ | 'trayastridhā'; | ye tvantyāstrayaste tredhā | savitarkāḥ savicārāḥ | vicāramātrāścāvitarkāḥ | avicārāśca | kāmadhātau prathame ca dhyāne vitarko naiṣu triṣu prakāreṣu praviśati | sa khalvavitarko vicāramātraśca ||
body.translated_text: Of the <s>dhātus</s> that have objects (<s>sālambana</s>), the first five are with <s>vitarka</s> and with <s>vicāra</s>. 'Three are threefold' — the last three are of three kinds: with <s>vitarka</s> and with <s>vicāra</s>; with <s>vicāra</s> only and without <s>vitarka</s>; and without <s>vicāra</s>. In the desire realm and in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>vitarka</s> enters into [all] three of these modes. But that [which is] in the intermediary [dhyāna] is without <s>vitarka</s> and with <s>vicāra</s> only.

body.text: atrāha- yadi pañcavijñānakāyāḥ savitarkāḥ savicārāḥ kathaṃ tarhi avikalpā ityucyante ? brūmaḥ
body.translated_text: Here one objects: if the five groups of consciousness (<s>pañcavijñānakāya</s>) are with <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, then how are they said to be non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>)? We reply:

children.translated_text: Non-conceptual [means] their quality is their own object —

body.text: guṇaḥ svārtho yeṣāṃ te bhavanti 'guṇasvārthāḥ'; | ete hi
body.translated_text: those whose quality (<s>guṇa</s>) is their own object (<s>svārtha</s>) — they are 'having their own object as quality.' For these —

body.text: asmārādanirūpaṇāt /
body.translated_text: because of non-determination from recollection and the like —

body.text: avikalpā ityucyante | etau hi pradhānau vikalpau traiyadhvikadharmaviṣayau | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 20)

children.text: ) yogināṃ kṛtākṛtakarmāntapratyavekṣaṇā cittarakṣaṇe smṛtiḥ pradhānī bhavati | dharmasvasāmānyalakṣaṇahetuphalasaṃbandhādiṣu pravicayākhyaḥ prajñāsvabhāvaḥ prādhānyamanubhavati | atra tu
children.translated_text: For <s>yogins</s>, mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) becomes primary in guarding the mind through the review of completed and uncompleted actions. The discriminating [faculty], which is of the nature of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), attains primacy regarding the investigation of phenomena, their universal and specific characteristics, cause-and-effect relations, and the like. But here —

body.translated_text: they are said to be non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>). For these two [types of conceptualization] are primary, having phenomena of the three times as their objects.

body.text: manobhaumī smṛtiḥ pūrvo dvitīyo dhīrnirūpikā // Abhidh-d_20 //
body.translated_text: mindfulness, belonging to the mental plane (<s>manobhaumī</s>), is the first [type of conceptualization]; the second is discernment (<s>dhī</s>), which determines. (Abhidh-d 20)

body.text: 'manobhaumī'ti vartate | pañcānāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ jātibadhirapuruṣarūpadarśanavadvṛttiḥ | tatrāpi ca smṛtiḥ samāhitā cāsamāhitā ca anusmṛtivikalpaḥ, ālambanābhilapanatulyatvāt | prajñā tvasamāhitaivābhinirūpaṇā vikalpaḥ, samāhitāyāḥ prakāraviśeṣanirūpaṇābhāvāt, pūrvanirūpitopalakṣaṇamātravṛttitvācca ||
body.translated_text: 'Belonging to the mental plane' continues [from the previous verse]. The functioning of the five groups of consciousness is like a deaf person seeing forms. And therein, mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), both concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>) and unconcentrated (<s>asamāhita</s>), constitutes the conceptualization of recollection (<s>anusmṛtivikalpa</s>), because it is equivalent to the verbal designation of the object. But wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), only when unconcentrated, constitutes the conceptualization of determination (<s>abhinirūpaṇāvikalpa</s>), because when concentrated, there is no determination of specific modes, and because its functioning is merely that of observing what was previously determined.

body.text: athaiṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ kataradvijñānaṃ kiyadbhiḥ savikalpakam ? tadidamāviṣkriyate |
body.translated_text: Now, of these six groups of consciousness, which consciousness is conceptual (<s>savikalpaka</s>) with how many [types of conceptualization]? This is now revealed:

body.text: vijñānapañcakaṃ kāmeṣvekena savikalpakam /
body.translated_text: The five [types of sense-]consciousness, in the desire realm, are conceptual with one [type] —

body.text: svabhāvavikalpena |
body.translated_text: with the inherent conceptualization (<s>svabhāvavikalpa</s>).

children.translated_text: The other [consciousness], with three [types] —

body.text: manovijñānaṃ kāmeṣu tribhiḥ savikalpakam |
body.translated_text: mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>), in the desire realm, is conceptual with three [types].

body.text: dhyāne prathame cāsamāhitam // Abhidh-d_21 //
body.translated_text: And in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, [mental consciousness] when unconcentrated — (Abhidh-d 21)

body.text: prathame hi dhyāne yadasamāhitaṃ manovijñānaṃ tat tribhireva |
body.translated_text: for in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, that mental consciousness which is unconcentrated is [conceptual] with three [types] indeed.

children.translated_text: When undistracted (<s>avyagra</s>), with two —

body.text: yatpunaḥ samāhitaṃtaddvābhyāmevābhinirūpaṇavikalpamapāsya |
body.translated_text: but that which is concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>) is with two only, having excluded the conceptualization of determination (<s>abhinirūpaṇāvikalpa</s>).

body.text: ekena cakṣuḥśrotratvagāśrayam /
body.translated_text: That based on eye, ear, and touch — with one. (Abhidh-d 22 beginning)

body.text: yatpunaścakṣuḥśrotratvagāśrayaṃ vijñānaṃ prathame dhyāne tadekenaiva |
body.translated_text: But that consciousness based on eye, ear, and touch in the first <s>dhyāna</s> is with one only.

children.translated_text: In the [stages] above that, [when] distracted (<s>vyagra</s>), with two —

body.text: dvitīyādiṣu dhyāneṣu dvābhyāṃ vyagramiti vartate |
body.translated_text: in the second and subsequent <s>dhyānas</s>, 'with two when distracted' — this continues.

body.text: ekenaiva samāhitam // Abhidh-d_22 //
body.translated_text: When concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>), with one only. (Abhidh-d 22)

body.text: anusmṛtivikalpenaiva | evaṃ yāvadbhavāgram ||
body.translated_text: With the conceptualization of recollection (<s>anusmṛtivikalpa</s>) only. Thus up to the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>).

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | kutra kasya ṣaṭprakāraṃ vijñānaṃ kuśalādivikalpakaṃ bhavati ? tadidamabhidharmagahvaraṃ prastūyate |
body.translated_text: Now this should be stated: in which [realm], for which [being], does the six-fold consciousness become conceptual as wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>) and the like? This profound matter of <s>Abhidharma</s> is now set forth:

children.translated_text: For one whose wholesome seeds (<s>śubhabīja</s>) are cut off, the seeing [consciousness] is conceptual,
but there is no wholesome consciousness, except at the time of reconnection (<s>pratisandhi</s>). (Abhidh-d 23)

body.text: iha tāvaducchinnakuśalamūlasya pañca rūpondriyāśrayabalotpannaṃ darśakaṃ vijñānaṃ kuśalaṃ na vidyate, anyatra kuśalamūlapratisandhānāt |
body.translated_text: Here, first, for one whose wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) have been cut off, the five seeing consciousnesses arisen by the power of the sense-faculties based on form (<s>rūpa</s>) are not wholesome, except from the reconnection of wholesome roots.

children.translated_text: For an ordinary person (<s>bāla</s>) who is free from desire for the desire realm (<s>kāma</s>), who has the nature of non-decline (<s>ahāni</s>), there is no unwholesome [consciousness] of either kind —

body.text: darśakaṃ ca manovijñānaṃ ca yadyaparihāṇadharmā bhavati |
body.translated_text: neither seeing [consciousness] nor mental consciousness — if one has the nature of non-decline.

body.text: kliṣṭaṃ cāryasya nottamam // Abhidh-d_24 //
body.translated_text: And for a noble one (<s>ārya</s>), there is no defiled (<s>kliṣṭa</s>) [consciousness] of the highest [type]. (Abhidh-d 24)

body.text: na cāryasyordhvabhūmyālambanaṃ kliṣṭaṃ vijñānaṃ vikalpakamasti ||
body.translated_text: And for a noble one (<s>ārya</s>), there is no defiled consciousness that is conceptual and takes an upper-realm object.

body.text: kiñca,
body.translated_text: Moreover,

body.text: nākliṣṭāvyākṛtaṃ kiñcidūrdhvabhūmivikalpakam /
body.translated_text: there is no undefiled-indeterminate (<s>akliṣṭāvyākṛta</s>) [consciousness] that is conceptual of an upper realm,

body.text: na cānivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ kiñcidūrdhvabhūmivikalpakamasti |
body.translated_text: and there is no unobstructed-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>) [consciousness] that is conceptual of an upper realm.

body.text: kliṣṭaṃ vikalpakaṃ cāpi nāstyadhobhūmigocaram // Abhidh-d_25 //
body.translated_text: And no defiled [consciousness] that is conceptual has a lower realm as its domain. (Abhidh-d 25)

body.text: na ca kliṣṭaṃ vijñānamadharabhūmyālambanaṃ vikalpakamasti |
body.translated_text: And there is no defiled consciousness that is conceptual and takes a lower realm as its object.

children.translated_text: Here, both [types are] threefold for a noble one (<s>ārya</s>) —

body.text: iha kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtaṃ darśakaṃ ca manovijñānaṃ ca vikalpakamasti |
body.translated_text: here, both seeing [consciousness] and mental consciousness are conceptual as wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>).

body.text: rāgiṇaḥ saśubhasya ca /
body.translated_text: and for one who has desire (<s>rāgin</s>) and possesses wholesome [roots] —

body.text: avītarāgasyāpyanucchinnakuśalamūlasya pṛthagjanasya trividhaṃ dvayamasti |
body.translated_text: for an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) who has not become free from desire and whose wholesome roots have not been cut off, both [types of consciousness exist] in threefold [manner].

body.text: na śubhaṃ nāpi ca kliṣṭaṃ dvitīyādiṣu darśakam // Abhidh-d_26 //
body.translated_text: In the second and subsequent [<s>dhyānas</s>], there is no seeing consciousness that is wholesome, nor one that is defiled. (Abhidh-d 26)

body.text: vijñānamastīti ||
body.translated_text: — [no such] consciousness exists.

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | kathamasatyātmani śāśvate tadguṇe ca saṃskāre smṛtihetāvasati pratikṣaṇavinaśvareṣu ca vijñāneṣu ca parasparākṛtasaṃketeṣu pūrvānubhūto 'rthaḥ smaryate ? tadapadiśyate | yadyapi dattottara eṣa vādaḥ, tathāpīdaṃ śāstrānugatamārabhyate |
body.translated_text: Now this should be stated: when there is no eternal self (<s>ātman</s>) that is permanent, nor any permanent quality (<s>guṇa</s>) thereof, when the conditioned factors (<s>saṃskāra</s>) that are causes of memory do not exist [permanently], and when consciousnesses perish every moment and have no mutually established conventions — how is a previously experienced object remembered? This is explained. Although this argument has been answered [before], nevertheless this exposition following the <s>śāstra</s> is undertaken.

children.translated_text: Through effort (<s>prayoga</s>), through proximity of factors (<s>aṅgasānnidhya</s>), and through similarity (<s>sabhāgatva</s>) of the continuum (<s>santati</s>),
regarding an object experienced by a prior consciousness, memory (<s>smṛti</s>) arises in the mind. (Abhidh-d 27)

body.text: praṇidhānānubhavajñānapāṭavasātatyakāritvābhyāmasahakāritvābhyāmasahakārikāraṇasānnidhye santatyānukūlebhyaḥ pūrvavijñānānubhūte rūpādau vastuni smṛtirutpadyate |
body.translated_text: Through [the forces of] resolve (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), experience (<s>anubhava</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), skill (<s>pāṭava</s>), continuity (<s>sātatya</s>), habitual action (<s>kāritva</s>), and non-conjunction [with obstructors]; in the proximity of non-associated causes; from [conditions] favorable in the continuum — regarding objects such as form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like, previously experienced by an earlier consciousness, memory (<s>smṛti</s>) arises.

body.text: ātmamanaḥsaṃyogātsaṃskārāpekṣā tadutpattiriti cet | na | ātmamanaḥ- saṃyogaḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ śaśaviṣāṇavadasiddhatvānnityasyāsyātmanaḥ saṃskārāṇāmanupapatteḥ | saṃskārasaṃyogaśca sakalātmavyāpitve pradeśavṛttyabhyupagamadoṣācca | tasmāt suṣṭhūktaṃ prayogādaṅgasānnidhyādibhyaḥ smṛtirutpadyate paramārthasaṃvṛttiviṣayā ||
body.translated_text: If [one objects that memory arises] from the conjunction of the self (<s>ātman</s>) and mind (<s>manas</s>), dependent on impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — no, because the conjunction of self and mind, and impressions, are unestablished like a hare's horn, since for this permanent self, impressions are impossible. And the conjunction with impressions [would involve] the fault of having to accept a partial occurrence when the self pervades everything. Therefore, it is well said: memory arises from effort, proximity of factors, and the like — [memory] that has both ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) and conventional (<s>saṃvṛtti</s>) objects.

children.translated_text: From the opposite of this, from dullness (<s>māndya</s>), and from being overwhelmed by afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and disease (<s>roga</s>),
forgetfulness (<s>vismṛti</s>) arises regarding things previously known. (Abhidh-d 28)

body.text: idamidānīṃ vicāryate | duḥkhadarśanaheyādinā pañca prakāreṇa vijñānena yadanubhūtaṃ tatkatamena smaryate ? tadidaṃ prastūyate |
body.translated_text: Now this is examined: when something is experienced by consciousness in five modes — [that] to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) and so forth — by which [mode of consciousness] is it remembered? This is now set forth:

children.translated_text: What is seen is remembered by consciousness of two, three, four, or five modes,
and by that [mode] itself and by others — but not one by another in the case of the destruction of the seeing of floods (<s>vyoghadṛk</s>). (Abhidh-d 29)

body.text: sarvāṇi khalu duḥkhadarśanādiheyāni pañcaprakārāṇi paramparānubhūtaṃ smaranti | ayaṃ tvatra niyamaḥ- 'nānyo 'nyaṃ vyoghadṛkkṣaye |'; nirodhamārgadarśanaprahātavyānubhūtaṃ tu nānyo 'nyaṃ smṛtipratiniyatālambanatvāt | śeṣāstu trayaḥ prakārāḥ sambhinnālambanatvānna pratiṣidhyante ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, all five modes — those to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and so forth — remember what was experienced sequentially. But this is the restriction here: 'not one by another in the case of the destruction of the seeing of floods' — what was experienced by [factors] to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) and path (<s>mārga</s>) is not [remembered] one by another, because memory has a fixed object for each. But the remaining three modes are not excluded, because their objects are mixed.

children.text:
vijñānānāṃ tu pañcānāṃ yadekenānubhūyate /
tatsmaryate 'pi cānyena
children.translated_text: But of the five consciousnesses, what is experienced by one is also remembered by another —

body.text: manovijñānenetyarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: by mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>), is the meaning.

body.text: tena khalvitarairapi // Abhidh-d_30 //
body.translated_text: And what is [experienced] by that [mental consciousness] is [remembered] by the others too. (Abhidh-d 30)

body.text: manovijñānenāpi yadanubhūtaṃ tat ṣaḍbhirapi smaryate ||
body.translated_text: What was experienced by mental consciousness too is remembered by all six [types of consciousness].

body.text: atha dvādaśānāṃ cittānāṃ ko 'rthaḥ kenānubhūtaḥ katibhiḥ smaryate ? dvādaśacittāni | kāmāvacarāṇi kuśalādīni catvāri | rūpāvacarāṇi trīṇyanyatrākuśalāt | evamārūpyāvacarāṇyetānyeva trīṇi | śaikṣamaśaikṣaṃ ca | smṛtirapi tatsaṃprayuktā dvādaśavidhaiva |
body.translated_text: Now, of the twelve [types of] consciousness, what object experienced by which [consciousness] is remembered by how many? The twelve consciousnesses are: four belonging to the desire realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) — wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>) and the like; three belonging to the form realm (<s>rūpāvacara</s>) — excluding the unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>); likewise three belonging to the formless realm (<s>ārūpyāvacara</s>) — these same three; and the trainee's (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and the adept's (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). Memory (<s>smṛti</s>) associated with these is also twelve-fold.

body.text: tatra kiṃ kenānubhūtaṃ tad dvādaśabhirapi smaryate ? kāmāvacarakuśalānubhūtaṃ tad dvādaśavidhayā smarati | evamakuśalena | tannivṛtāvyākṛtānubhūtamaṣṭavidhayā smarati | kāmāvacaryā sarvayā | rūpārūpyāvacaryayānyatra nivṛtāvyākṛtānivṛtāvyākṛtāyāḥ śaikṣāśaikṣābhyāṃ ca | evamanivṛtāvyākṛtena | rūpāvacarakuśalānubhūtaṃ sarvābhiḥ smarati | tannivṛtāvyākṛtānubhūtaṃ daśabhiranyatra kāmāvacaranivṛtāvyākṛtānivṛtāvyākṛtābhyām | tadanivṛtāvyākṛtānubhūtaṃ daśabhiranyatrārūpyāvacaranivṛtāvyākṛtānivṛtāvyākṛtābhyām | ārūpyāvacaraḥ kuśalānubhūtaṃ daśabhiranyatra kāmāvacaranivṛtāvyākṛtānivṛtāvyākṛtābhyām | tannivṛtāvyākṛtānubhūtaṃ navabhiranyatra kāmāvacaraṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtānivṛtāvyākṛtābhyām | rūpāvacarāccānivṛtāvyākṛtāt | evamanivṛtāvyākṛtena | śaikṣānubhūtamekādaśabhiranyatrakāmāvacaranivṛtāvyākṛtādevamaśaikṣeṇeti | saṃkṣepārthastvayaṃ ślokaiḥ pradarśyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, is what is experienced by one [type] remembered by all twelve? What is experienced by desire-realm wholesome [consciousness] is remembered by twelve-fold [memory]. Likewise with the unwholesome. What is experienced by its obstructed-indeterminate [consciousness] is remembered by eight-fold [memory]: by all of the desire-realm [types]; by those of the form and formless realms excluding the obstructed-indeterminate and unobstructed-indeterminate; and by the trainee's and adept's. Likewise with the unobstructed-indeterminate. What is experienced by form-realm wholesome [consciousness] is remembered by all. What is experienced by its obstructed-indeterminate is by ten, excluding the desire-realm obstructed-indeterminate and unobstructed-indeterminate. What is experienced by its unobstructed-indeterminate is by ten, excluding the formless-realm obstructed-indeterminate and unobstructed-indeterminate. What is experienced by formless-realm wholesome is by ten, excluding the desire-realm obstructed-indeterminate and unobstructed-indeterminate. What is experienced by its obstructed-indeterminate is by nine, excluding the desire-realm obstructed-indeterminate and unobstructed-indeterminate, and the form-realm unobstructed-indeterminate. Likewise with the unobstructed-indeterminate. What is experienced by the trainee's [consciousness] is by eleven, excluding the desire-realm obstructed-indeterminate. Likewise with the adept's. This summary meaning is shown by [the following] verses:

children.translated_text: What is experienced by the two indeterminate [types of] consciousness — the twelve and so forth here —
excluding the formless and form obstructed [types], is remembered by eight only. (Abhidh-d 31)

body.text: kāmadhātau nivṛtāvyākṛtānivṛtāvyākṛtābhyāṃ yadanubhūtaṃ tadaṣṭābhiḥ smaryate | rūpārūpyāvacare dve nivate hitvā | śekṣamaśaikṣaṃ caivamanivṛtāvyākṛtena |
body.translated_text: What is experienced by the desire-realm obstructed-indeterminate and unobstructed-indeterminate is remembered by eight [types]. Excluding the two obstructed [types] of the form and formless realms, and the trainee's and adept's — likewise with the unobstructed-indeterminate.

children.translated_text: But what [is experienced] by the form and formless [realm] obstructed and wholesome, respectively —

children.text: kāmāptāvyākṛte hitvā smaryate daśakena tat // Abhidh-d_32 //
children.translated_text: excluding the desire-realm [two] indeterminate [types], is remembered by ten. (Abhidh-d 32)

body.text: kāmāvacaranivṛtāvyākṛte hitvā |
body.translated_text: Excluding the desire-realm obstructed-indeterminate.

children.translated_text: But what is seen by the unobstructed-named [consciousness] of the form [realm] —

children.text: ārūpyāvyākṛte hitvā tadanyaiḥ smaryate punaḥ // Abhidh-d_33 //
children.translated_text: excluding the formless-realm [two] indeterminate, is remembered by the others again. (Abhidh-d 33)

body.text: yatkhalu rūpadhātau anivṛtāvyākṛtenānubhūtaṃ tadārūpyāvyākṛte hitvā tadanyairdaśabhiḥ smaryate ||
body.translated_text: What is indeed experienced by the unobstructed-indeterminate of the form realm is remembered by ten others, excluding the formless-realm [two] indeterminate [types].

children.translated_text: And what is known by the formless-realm indeterminate [consciousness] — that, by nine —
excluding the desire-realm [two] indeterminate and the form-realm unobstructed. (Abhidh-d 34)

body.text: gatametadaupodghātikaṃ prakaraṇam | prakṛtamevābhidhīyatām ||
body.translated_text: This introductory (<s>aupodghātika</s>) section is concluded. Let the main subject now be stated.

body.text: ya ete 'ṣṭādaśadhātava eṣāṃ kati sālambanāḥ katyanālambanāḥ katyupāttāḥ katyanupāttāḥ kati saṃcitāḥ katyasaṃcitāḥ ? tadidamārabhyate |
body.translated_text: Of these eighteen <s>dhātus</s>, how many have objects (<s>sālambana</s>)? How many are without objects (<s>anālambana</s>)? How many are appropriated (<s>upātta</s>)? How many are unappropriated (<s>anupātta</s>)? How many are accumulated (<s>saṃcita</s>)? How many are not accumulated (<s>asaṃcita</s>)? This [topic] is now commenced:

body.text: cittākhyāḥ sapta sālambā dharmākhyaḥ saṃprayuktakaḥ /
body.translated_text: The seven called consciousness (<s>citta</s>) have objects (<s>sālamba</s>); [also] the one called <s>dharma</s>, [when] associated (<s>saṃprayuktaka</s>) —

body.text: sālambanā iti vartate | śeṣāstvanālambanā viṣayāgrahaṇāt ||
body.translated_text: 'Have objects' continues [from the verse]. The rest, however, are without objects, because they do not apprehend a domain (<s>viṣaya</s>).

children.translated_text: The immaterial [dharmas] are unappropriated (<s>anupātta</s>) along with sound.

body.text: ya ete saptacittadhātavo dharmadhātvardhena sahoktāste śabdena sahānupāttāḥ | ato 'nye
body.translated_text: These seven consciousness-elements (<s>cittadhātus</s>), together with a portion of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, are stated as unappropriated (<s>anupātta</s>) together with sound. The remaining

body.text: nava dvidhā // Abhidh-d_35 //
body.translated_text: nine [are] twofold. (Abhidh-d 35)

body.text: ye santānādhirohiṇaḥ pratyutpannāścakṣurādayastadavinirbhāgiṇaśca rūpādayaḥ | śeṣāstvanupāttāḥ | niścetanatvādanātmabhāvaparyāpannatvācca | śeṣā ye bāhyāḥ kāyendriyasaṃtānavyatirekavartinaste 'nupāttā iti siddham ||
body.translated_text: Those that ascend to the [bodily] continuum (<s>santāna</s>) — the present eye and other [sense-faculties] — and the forms and other [objects] inseparable from them [are appropriated]. The rest, however, are unappropriated — because of being non-sentient, and because of being included in the category of non-self. The rest — those that are external, existing apart from the continuum of the body-faculty — they are unappropriated; this is established.

body.text: kati bhūtāni kati bhautikāḥ ? tatrāpyucyate |
body.translated_text: How many are primary elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) and how many are derivative (<s>bhautika</s>)? On this too it is said:

children.translated_text: The tangible (<s>spṛśya</s>) is twofold.

body.text: atra bhūtāni catvāri bhautikaṃ ca gurutvādisaptaprakāram |
body.translated_text: Here, the primary elements are four; and the derivative is of seven kinds — heaviness and so forth.

body.text: sadharmāṃśāḥ saha tā nava bhautikāḥ /
body.translated_text: Together with the <s>dharma</s>-portion, those nine are derivative (<s>bhautika</s>).

body.text: saha dharmadhātvaṃśenāvijñaptyākhyena 'saha tā nava bhautikāḥ'; ||
body.translated_text: Together with the portion of <s>dharmadhātu</s> called <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifestation), 'those nine are derivative.'

body.text: evaṃ kati mūrtāḥ ?
body.translated_text: Thus, how many are material (<s>mūrta</s>)?

children.translated_text: Ten, possessing parts, are material (<s>mūrta</s>).

body.text: śeṣāstvamūrtāścakṣurvijñānadhātvādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: The rest, however — the eye-consciousness element and so forth — are immaterial.

body.text: ta eva daśa saṃcitāḥ // Abhidh-d_36 //
body.translated_text: Those very ten are composite (<s>saṃcita</s>). (Abhidh-d 36)

body.text: paramāṇusaṃghātā ityarthaḥ | ta evāṣṭau cakṣurvijñānadhātvādayo hitvā śeṣā daśa saṃcitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Meaning: aggregates of atoms (<s>paramāṇusaṃghāta</s>). Those very [ten] — excepting the eight [viz.] the eye-consciousness element and so forth — the remaining ten are composite.

body.text: kati cchettāraḥ kati cchedyāḥ, kati dagdhāraḥ kati dāhyāḥ, kati tolayitāraḥ kati tolyāḥ ? tadidamatrocyate |
body.translated_text: How many are cutters, how many are to-be-cut? How many are burners, how many are to-be-burnt? How many are weighers, how many are to-be-weighed? This is stated here:

children.translated_text: Form, smell, taste, and touch are regarded as having the nature of cutter and to-be-cut,
burner, and weigher — and these [same ones] are the to-be-burnt and to-be-weighed, or [alternatively]: (Abhidh-d 37)

body.text: 'vā'; śabdo matavikalpārthaḥ | keṣāñcittejodhātureva dagdhā gurutvameva tolyam ||
