body.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) is for expressing a doctrinal alternative. According to some, only the fire-element is the burner; only heaviness is the to-be-weighed.

body.text: kati vipākajāḥ katyaupacayikāḥ ?
body.translated_text: How many are resultant of maturation (<s>vipākaja</s>) and how many are of the nature of growth (<s>aupacayika</s>)?

body.text: pañca rūpīndriyātmāno vipākopacayātmakāḥ /
body.translated_text: The five, having the nature of material faculties (<s>rūpīndriya</s>), have the nature of maturation and growth.

body.text: vipākakāraṇahetvadhīnajanmatvāt naiṣyandikāni cakṣurādīni pañca na vidyante | mṛtasya vipākajavyatiriktatanniṣyandābhāvāt | tatra vipākahetorjātā vipākajāḥ, madhyapadalopaṃ kṛtvā gorathavat |
body.translated_text: Because their birth depends on the maturation-cause (<s>vipākakāraṇahetu</s>), the eye and other five [faculties] that are outflow-resultants (<s>naiṣyandika</s>) do not exist [independently]; because for a dead person, apart from the maturation-born, there is no outflow of those [faculties]. Therein, those born from the maturation-cause are maturation-born (<s>vipākaja</s>) — by elision of the middle word, like 'cow-cart' (<s>goratha</s>).

children.translated_text: The immaterial are not of growth (<s>naupacayika</s>).

body.text: saptacittadhātavo dharmadhātuścāmūrtā naiṣyandikavipākajāstu vidyante sabhāgavipākahetubalotpatteḥ |
body.translated_text: The seven consciousness-elements and the <s>dharmadhātu</s> are immaterial; outflow-resultants and maturation-born, however, do exist [among them], because they arise through the force of the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāga</s>) and maturation-cause.

children.translated_text: The rest are threefold.

body.text: rūpadhātvādyāścatvārastriprakārā ye kāyendriyasahavartinaste tridhā | bāhyāḥ te dvidhā |
body.translated_text: The form-element and the [other] four — [being] of three kinds — those that co-exist with the body-faculty are threefold. The external ones are twofold.

body.text: dhvanirdvidhā // Abhidh-d_38 //
body.translated_text: Sound is twofold. (Abhidh-d 38)

body.text: śabdastu vipākajo nāstītyāgamaḥ | yuktirapīcchātastatpravṛtteḥ ||
body.translated_text: However, sound that is maturation-born does not exist — this is the scriptural tradition (<s>āgama</s>). Reasoning too [supports this]: because its production depends on volition (<s>icchā</s>).

body.text: idānīmidamucyate | yaścakṣurdhātunā samanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate cakṣurvijñānadhātunāpi saḥ ? yo vā cakṣurvijñānardhātunā cakṣudhātunāpi saḥ ? āha | nātraikāṃśaḥ | yasmāt
body.translated_text: Now this is stated: Is one who possesses (<s>samanvāgata</s>) the eye-element necessarily also possessed of the eye-consciousness element? Or one who possesses the eye-consciousness element — is he necessarily also [possessed] of the eye-element? He says: There is no single alternative here. Because:

body.text: cakṣustadupalabdhiśca pṛthagvā saha vāpnuyāt /
body.translated_text: The eye and its apprehension may be obtained separately or together.

body.text: cakṣurdhātuṃ tāvallabhate na cakṣurvijñānadhātum | kāmadhātau krameṇa cakṣurindriyaṃ pratilabhamānaḥ, ārūpyadhātucyutaśca dvitīyādiṣu dhyāneṣūpapadyamānaḥ | syāccakṣurvijñānadhātunā na cakṣurdhātunā | dvitīyādiṣu dhyāneṣūpapannaścakṣurvijñānamasaṃmukhīkurvāṇaḥ | tataścyutaścādhastādupapadyamānaḥ | ubhābhyāmapi- ārūpyadhātucyutaḥ kāmadhātau brahmaloke copapadyamānaḥ | nobhābhyām- etānākārān sthāpayitvā |
body.translated_text: [Case 1:] One obtains the eye-element but not the eye-consciousness element — one who in the desire-realm is gradually acquiring the eye-faculty, or one who, having died in the formless realm, is being reborn in the second <s>dhyāna</s> and above. [Case 2:] One may [possess] the eye-consciousness element but not the eye-element — one born in the second <s>dhyāna</s> and above who is not activating the eye-consciousness; or one who, having died from there, is being reborn below. [Case 3:] Both — one who, having died in the formless realm, is being reborn in the desire-realm or in the Brahmā-world. [Case 4:] Neither — excluding these cases.

body.text: yaścakṣurdhātunā samanvāgataḥ cakṣurvijñānadhātunāpi saḥ ? catuṣkoṭikāḥ | prathamā- dvitīyādiṣu dhyāneṣūpapannaścakṣurvijñānamasaṃmukhīkurvāṇaḥ | dvitīyā- kāmadhātāvalabdhavihīnacakṣuḥ | tṛtīyā- kāmadhātau labdhāvihīnacakṣuḥ prathamadhyānopapanno dvitīyādidhyānopapannaśca paśyan | caturthī- etānākārān sthāpayitvā ||
body.translated_text: Is one who possesses the eye-element necessarily also possessed of the eye-consciousness element? [This yields] four alternatives (<s>catuṣkoṭikā</s>). First — one born in the second <s>dhyāna</s> and above who is not activating the eye-consciousness. Second — one in the desire-realm who has lost or lacks the eye. Third — one in the desire-realm who has acquired and retains the eye, or one born in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, or one born in the second <s>dhyāna</s> and above who is seeing. Fourth — excluding these cases.

body.text: gatametat | prakṛtamidānīmanuvartyatām | katyādhyātmikāḥ kati bāhyāḥ ?
body.translated_text: This topic is concluded. Now let us return to the main subject. How many are internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) and how many external (<s>bāhya</s>)?

children.translated_text: Twelve are to be known as internal.

body.text: pañcendriyātmikaḥ saptacittadhātavaśca, ahaṃkārasanniśrayatvāt | "ātmanā hi sudāntena svargaṃ prāpnoti paṇḍitaḥ |" iti |
body.translated_text: The five having the nature of sense-faculties and the seven consciousness-elements — because of being the support for the notion of 'I' (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>). 'For by the well-tamed self, the wise person attains heaven.'

body.text: bāhyāṣṣaḍviṣayātmakāḥ // Abhidh-d_39 //
body.translated_text: The external are six, having the nature of objects (<s>viṣaya</s>). (Abhidh-d 39)

body.text: kati darśanaheyāḥ kati bhāvanāheyāḥ katyaheyāḥ ? tadārabhyate |
body.translated_text: How many are to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaheyāḥ</s>)? How many to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāheyāḥ</s>)? How many are not to be abandoned (<s>aheyāḥ</s>)? This is now undertaken:

children.translated_text: The last three are threefold.

body.text: manodhāturmanovijñānadhāturdharmadhātavastriprakārāḥ | aṣṭāśītyanuśayasahacariṣṇavastatprāptayaśca darśanaheyāḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>manodhātu</s> (mind-element), <s>manovijñānadhātu</s> (mental-consciousness element), and <s>dharmadhātu</s> are of three kinds. Those accompanied by the eighty-eight <s>anuśayas</s> (latent afflictions), and those that are acquisitions thereof, are to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaheya</s>).

body.text: śeṣā bhāvanāpathasaṃkṣayāḥ /
body.translated_text: The rest are destroyed on the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>).

body.text: ye sāsravāḥ | ye tvanāsravāste 'praheyā nirdoṣatvāt ||
body.translated_text: Those that are with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>). But those that are without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>) are not to be abandoned, because of being faultless.

body.text: na rūpamasti dṛggheyaṃ nākliṣṭaṃ nāvikalpakam // Abhidh-d_40 //
body.translated_text: No form (<s>rūpa</s>) exists that is to be abandoned by seeing, nor that is unafflicted (<s>akliṣṭa</s>), nor non-conceptual (<s>avikalpaka</s>). (Abhidh-d 40)

body.text: pṛthagjanatvamiti cet | na | tasyānivṛtāvyākṛtatvāta, samucchinnakuśalamūlavītarāgāṇāmapi tatsamanvāgamāt | āpāyikaṃ ca kāyavākkarmarūpasvabhāvaṃ tadapyāryamārgavirodhitvādvihīnaṃ na tu prahīṇaṃ tasmādubhayaṃ na darśanaheyaṃ satyeṣvavipratipatteḥ | duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāntau pṛthagjanatvaprasaṃgācca |
body.translated_text: Objection: What about 'the state of being an ordinary person' (<s>pṛthagjanatvam</s>)? No — because it is of the unobstructed indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>) [category]; and because those who have destroyed all wholesome roots and those freed from passion also possess it. And the bodily and vocal action that is of the nature of form belonging to the lower realms — that too, being contrary to the noble path, is [merely] absent, not abandoned. Therefore both are not to be abandoned by seeing, because there is no error regarding the truths. And because [otherwise] the state of being an ordinary person would be entailed at the [moment of] the patience of knowledge of suffering in the truth of suffering.

body.text: pañcavijñānakāyā avikalpakāste 'pi na darśanaheyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The five consciousness-groups are non-conceptual (<s>avikalpaka</s>) — yet they too are not to be abandoned by seeing.

body.text: kati sabhāgāḥ kati tatsabhāgāḥ ?
body.translated_text: How many are <s>sabhāga</s> (homogeneous) and how many are <s>tatsabhāga</s> (similar thereto)?

body.text: sabhāga eva dharmākhyaḥ śeṣāstūbhayathā smṛtāḥ /
body.translated_text: That called <s>dharma</s> [i.e., the <s>dharmadhātu</s>] is <s>sabhāga</s> only; the rest, however, are remembered as being of both kinds.

body.text: dharmadhātuvarjyā anye dhātavo dvidhā | sabhāgāstatsabhāgāśca ||
body.translated_text: The elements other than the <s>dharmadhātu</s> are twofold: <s>sabhāga</s> (homogeneous) and <s>tatsabhāga</s> (similar thereto).

body.text: kaḥ punaḥ sabhāgārthaḥ ko vā tatsabhāgārthaḥ ?
body.translated_text: What then is the meaning of <s>sabhāga</s>? And what is the meaning of <s>tatsabhāga</s>?

body.text: sabhāgastatsabhāgatve svakriyābhāktu tulyate // Abhidh-d_41 //
body.translated_text: The <s>sabhāga</s> is distinguished by engaging in its own activity with respect to its <s>tatsabhāga</s> counterpart. (Abhidh-d 41)

body.text: yaḥ svakriyāṃ bhajate sa sabhāga ityucyate | yaḥ svakriyāvirahitaḥ sa tatsādṛśyamātrabhajamānatvāt tatsabhāga ityākhyāyate |
body.translated_text: That which engages in its own activity is called <s>sabhāga</s>. That which is devoid of its own activity — since it partakes only of similarity to that — is designated <s>tatsabhāga</s>.

body.text: atra sabhāgastrividhaḥ | adhvasu svakriyābhedena vācyaḥ | evaṃ tatsabhāgaḥ kriyāvirahito vācyaḥ | anutpattidharmakaṃ caturthamiti kāśmīrāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, <s>sabhāga</s> is threefold — to be stated according to the distinction of its own activity in the three times. Likewise, <s>tatsabhāga</s> is to be stated as devoid of activity. The fourth, having the nature of 'that which will never arise' — [this is the view of] the <s>Kāśmīras</s>.

body.text: kati dṛṣṭiḥ kati na dṛṣṭiḥ ?
body.translated_text: How many are 'view' (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) and how many are not 'view'?

body.text: cakṣuḥ sadharmadhātvaṃśaṃ navadhā dṛṣṭirūcyate /
body.translated_text: The eye, together with a portion of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, is called 'view' in nine ways.

body.text: cakṣustāvalloke 'pi dṛṣṭiriti pratītam | dharmadhātorapi pradeśo dṛṣṭisvabhāvo 'ṣṭavidhaḥ kliṣṭākliṭaprajñātmakaḥ | śeṣastu na dṛṣṭiḥ |
body.translated_text: The eye is first [called] a 'view' — as is well-known even in the world. A portion of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> too has the nature of view — eightfold, having the nature of afflicted and unafflicted <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). The rest, however, are not views.

body.text: pāñcavijñānakī prajñā na dṛṣṭiranitīraṇāt // Abhidh-d_42 //
body.translated_text: The wisdom associated with the five sense-consciousnesses is not a 'view,' because of not ascertaining decisively. (Abhidh-d 42)

body.text: nitīrikā hi dṛṣṭayo vicāraṇāśrayāt | sā tvavikalpikā jaḍasvabhāvā | atyalpamidamucyate | manovijñānabhaumyanirāsādisaṃprayuktā na dṛṣṭirityupasaṃkhyātavyam ||
body.translated_text: For views are decisive [in character], since they serve as a basis for deliberation (<s>vicāraṇā</s>). But that [five-sense wisdom] is non-conceptual and inert in nature. Only this little is stated [here]; it should be added that [wisdom] associated with disassociation from the mental-consciousness sphere and so forth is also not a view.

body.text: kathaṃ punaretāḥ prajñāḥ paśyanti ? tadidamāviṣkriyate |
body.translated_text: But how do these wisdoms see? This is made clear:

children.translated_text: Just as the eye sees what is visible on cloudy and cloudless nights and days —
so do the afflicted and unafflicted views, and those of the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), see. (Abhidh-d 43)

body.text: yathā sameghāyāṃ timirapaṭalāvaguṇṭhitacandranakṣatracakraprāyāṃ rajanyāṃ rūpāṇi dṛśyante tathā kliṣṭāḥ pañcadṛṣṭayo jñeyaṃ paśyanti | yathā tu vigatarajāṃsi niśākarakiraṇāṃśukāvaguṇṭhitāyāṃ triyāmāyāṃ rūpāṇi dṛśyante, tathā laukikī samyagdṛṣṭiḥ paśyati | yathā tu meghapaṭalāvaguṇṭhite divākarakiraṇānudbhāsite divase rūpāṇi dṛśyante tadvacchaikṣī dṛṣṭiḥ paśyati | yathā tu dravyakanakarasāvasekapiñjaradinakarakiraṇaprotsāritatimirasaṃcaye divase cakṣuṣmato devadattasya rūpaṃ cakṣurīkṣate, tathā buddhānāmarhatāṃ prajñācakṣuravidyākleśopakleśamaladūṣikātimirapaṭalavarjitaṃ jñeyaṃ paśyatīti |
body.translated_text: Just as on a night with clouds — shrouded by a veil of mist, the sky resembling [one whose] moon and star-wheel are concealed — forms are seen, so the five afflicted views see the knowable. But just as on a night free of dust, wrapped in moonbeams, forms are seen during the three watches, so does worldly right view see. And just as on a day when the disk of the sun is shrouded by a veil of clouds and its rays are not radiant, forms are seen — so does the view of the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) see. But just as the eye of <s>Devadatta</s> who possesses sight sees form on a day when the accumulated darkness has been driven away by sun-rays tinged golden like a wash of liquid gold — so does the wisdom-eye of Buddhas and <s>Arhats</s>, free from the cataract-veil of ignorance, afflictions, secondary afflictions, and impurities, see the knowable.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau prathamasyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the third section (<s>pāda</s>) of the first chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: prathamādhyāye
body.translated_text: First chapter,

body.text: caturthapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: fourth section.

body.text: āha | yaduktam- cakṣurdarśanamaṣṭaprakārā ca prajñā dṛṣṭiriti | atha vijñānaṃ paśyatyatha na paśyati ? yadi paśyati daśadharmā dṛṣṭisvabhāvā bhavanti | atha na paśyati dārṣṭāntikapakṣastarhyujjhito bhavati | devā enaṃ grahīṣyanti grahītavyaṃ cenmaṃsyante |
body.translated_text: Question: It was stated that the eye is a view and that <s>prajñā</s> of eight kinds is a view. Now, does consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) see or does it not see? If it sees, then ten dharmas would have the nature of view. If it does not see, then the illustrative thesis is abandoned. 'The gods will seize him — if they think he should be seized.'

body.text: yattūktaṃ daśadharmā dṛṣṭisvabhāvāḥ prāpnuvantītyatra vijñānasya mukhyadarśanakalpanāpratiṣedhamupariṣṭāt kariṣyāmaḥ | idaṃ tu vaktavyam | cakṣuścakṣurvijñānaprajñāsāmagrīṇāṃ kaḥ paśyati ? kutaḥ saṃśaya iti cet | sarvatra doṣadarśanāt | yadi tāvaccakṣuḥ paśyati yāvatkāyaḥ spṛśati tato yugapat sarvaviṣayopabhogaprasaṃgaḥ | atha cakṣurvijñānaṃ paśyati kastarhi vijānāti ? vyavahitamapi kiṃ na paśyati, apratighatvāt ? atha prajñā paśyati śrotravijñānādiṣvapi prajñā vidyata iti tatrāpi darśanaprasaṃgaḥ | atha cakṣurādisāmagrī paśyati sāpi khalu cakṣurādisāmagryaṅgavyatiriktā svabhāvakriyābhāvānna vidyate |
body.translated_text: As to the statement that ten dharmas would have the nature of view — we shall later make the refutation of the attribution of primary seeing to consciousness. But this must be said: Among the eye, eye-consciousness, and the assemblage of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) — who sees? Why the doubt? Because faults are seen in every [option]. If the eye sees — just as the body touches — then there would be the consequence of simultaneous enjoyment of all objects. If the eye-consciousness sees, then who cognizes? Why would it not see even what is obstructed, since [consciousness] is non-resistant (<s>apratigha</s>)? If wisdom sees — since wisdom exists in the ear-consciousness and others too — there would be the consequence of seeing there as well. If the assemblage of eye and so forth sees — that assemblage too, being devoid of an inherent nature and activity apart from its constituent members of eye and so forth, does not exist [as a separate entity].

body.text: cakṣurādisāmagryaṅgānāmapi pratyekaṃ darśanaśaktikriyābhāvo 'ndhaśatavadityasattvam | sarvasāmagrīṇāṃ sarvakāryakaraṇāpattitvāt, viśeṣābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: The members of the assemblage of eye and so forth also individually lack the power of the activity of seeing — like a hundred blind men — hence [the assemblage] is non-existent. Because all assemblages would produce all effects, there being no distinction.

body.text: hetupratyayasāmagrīṃ pratītya kriyāmātraṃ vijñānamutpadyata iti cet | na | janikartṛbhāve janmakriyāsvātantryānupapatteḥ, naśyādivat | hetupratyayānāṃ paratantrāṇāṃ svātmanyavasthitānāṃ nirātmakānāṃ nirātmakakaraṇaśaktyayogāt |
body.translated_text: Objection: Dependent on the assemblage of causes and conditions, mere activity — consciousness — arises. Reply: No — because in the case of the producer-agent being [also] the production, the independence of the activity of birth would be untenable, like destruction and so forth. Because of the impossibility for causes and conditions — which are dependent on others, established in their own nature, and devoid of self — of possessing the power to produce something devoid of self.

body.text: kiñca, vijñeyābhāve vijñānānupapatteḥ, dāhyadahanavat |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, because in the absence of the knowable (<s>vijñeya</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is untenable — like fuel and fire.

body.text: kiñca, vijñānakriyāśritābhāve tadabhāvāccitrakuḍyavat | janmanāśayorddharmidharmatve viruddhānāmanyataropapattirvināśasya vā sajātihetutvaprasaṃgaḥ | yajjātyanuvṛttistadbījamiti cet | na | kuśalākuśalādicittanirodhe bījatvānupapatteḥ, sāmagrīpakṣotsargātsāṃkhyamatābhyupagamadoṣācca | teṣāmapi pradhānākhyādbījādekasmānnirapekṣātsarvaṃ saṃbhavati | nimittāntarāpekṣā śaktaśakteriti cet | na | akṣaṇikatvadoṣāt | sarvasāmagryaṅgabījābhyupagame kāryasvabhāvādivaicitryaprasaṃgaḥ | tasmānnirdoṣaḥ pakṣo vaktavyaḥ | so 'yaṃ prakramyate |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, because in the absence of a substratum for the activity of consciousness, [consciousness] would be absent — like a painted wall. If birth and destruction are property and property-holder, there would be the consequence of one of two contradictories arising; or of destruction being a homogeneous cause (<s>sajātihetu</s>). Objection: That which [accounts for] the continuation of the type is the seed. Reply: No — because when wholesome, unwholesome, and other minds cease, seed-nature is untenable; because of abandoning the assemblage-thesis; and because of the fault of accepting the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view. For them too, from a single [entity] called <s>Pradhāna</s> — from one seed, independent [of conditions] — everything arises. Objection: The dependence on other conditions [distinguishes our view:] 'The capable from the capable.' Reply: No — because of the fault of non-momentariness. If one accepts seeds as members of every assemblage, there would be the consequence of variety in the nature of effects and so forth. Therefore, a faultless thesis must be stated. This [thesis] is now set forth:

children.translated_text: The eye sees; consciousness cognizes its own domain.
Because [the eye has] the nature of viewing (<s>ālocana</s>) and [consciousness has] the nature of apprehending (<s>upalabdhi</s>), the distinction between the two is very great. (Abhidh-d 44)

body.text: cakṣurdravyaṃ hi draṣṭṛsvabhāvam | tasya hetupratyayasāmagrīparigrahaprabodhitaśakteḥ rūpadarśanakriyāmātramutpadyate | dravyakriyayoścānyatvaṃ siddhasādhyamānarūpatvānnirapekṣasāpekṣavyapadeśitvācca draṣṭavyam | tatra cakṣurmūrtikriyāvadvijñānādhiṣṭhitaṃ darśanakriyāmārabhate | na vijñānaśūnyam | yathaiva cakṣurvijñānamālocanādhiṣṭhitakriyaṃ vijānāti, na kevalam, paramparānugrahabalāddhyanayoḥ pradīpādipratyayāntaraparigṛhītayoryugapadekasmin viṣaye vṛttilābho bhavati |
body.translated_text: For the eye is a substance (<s>dravya</s>) whose nature is that of a seer. When its power has been awakened through the assemblage of causes and conditions, the mere activity of seeing form arises from it. And that substance and activity are different — this is to be understood from their being of proven and to-be-proven nature respectively, and from their being designated as independent and dependent respectively. Therein, the eye, like physical activity, being superintended by consciousness, commences the activity of seeing — not [when] devoid of consciousness. Just as eye-consciousness, [whose] activity is superintended by viewing (<s>ālocana</s>), cognizes — not merely [by itself]; through the force of mutual successive assistance, these two, grasped by other conditions such as light and so forth, simultaneously obtain operation with respect to a single object.

body.text: yastvetadatipatyaivaṃ kalpayati- 'kāraṇabhūtābhyāṃ prāgutpannābhyāṃ cakṣūrūpābhyāṃ kāryabhūtaṃ vijñānaṃ sahaikasmin kāle nāvatiṣṭhate'; iti tasya sakṣādviṣayānubhavanābhāvādanumānāgamābhāvaprasaṃgaḥ | anubhavajñāne cāsati manovijñānasmṛtigocarābhāvādanutpattiprasaṃgaḥ | niyataviṣayasmaraṇābhāvācca | tasmādvijñānaṃ niyatāśrayālambanalabdhapratiṣṭhaṃ sahakārikāraṇasāmagrīsannipātopajanitakriyaṃ sākṣādviṣayamupalabhate | cakṣurapyālocayati pradīpastatkālamevāvabhāsayati | ya ete vijñānacakṣūrūpādayaḥ svahetusāmagrīprabodhitaśaktayaḥ te viṣayaprativijñaptyālocanāvabhāsanākhyāṃ yugapat saudhīṃ saudhīṃ vṛttiṃ pratipadyanta iti yuktimatī nītiḥ |
body.translated_text: But one who, bypassing this, constructs [the argument] thus — 'the consciousness, which is an effect, does not coexist at one and the same time with the eye and form, which are the pre-arisen causes' — for such a person, since there is no direct experience of the object, the consequence is that inference and scriptural testimony (<s>āgama</s>) would also be absent. And in the absence of experiential knowledge, since there would be no object for the recollection by mind-consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>), the consequence is non-arising [of recollection]. And because there would be no recollection of a determinate object. Therefore, consciousness, having obtained its basis in a determinate support (<s>āśraya</s>) and object (<s>ālambana</s>), and having its activity produced by the concurrence of cooperative causal conditions (<s>sahakāri-kāraṇa-sāmagrī</s>), directly apprehends the object. The eye also illuminates; a lamp illuminates at that very time. These — consciousness, eye, form, and the like — whose powers have been awakened by the concurrence of their own causes, simultaneously assume their respective functions called object-discernment (<s>prativijñapti</s>), illumination (<s>ālocana</s>), and manifestation (<s>avabhāsana</s>) — this is the reasoned principle.

body.text: tasmātsatsvapyanyeṣu pratyayeṣu darśanakriyāyāścakṣuṣaḥ prādhānyāt, tadevāñjasā paśyatītyucyate | yathā vā devadattaḥ sthālījalajvalanataṇḍulādiṣu satsvapi pāke pravartamāne svasyāmadhiśrayaṇodakāsecanataṇḍalāvapanadarvīparighaṭṭanācāmanisrāvaṇakriyāyāṃ labdhasāmarthyaḥ sādhanasanniyoge ca paraprāptaiśvaryo devadattaḥ prādhānyātpacatātyucyate | yadā punastaṇḍulānāṃ (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 33]

children.text: ) vikledo vivakṣitaḥ pāko vā tadā jalānalayoḥ prādhānyādvyapadeśo bhavatyambu kledayatyagniḥ pacatīti | tasmātsāmagryāṃ satyāṃ darśane pravartamāne prādhānyāccakṣuḥ paśyatītyucyate | kathaṃ prādhānyamiti cet ? tatprakarṣe darśanaprakarṣāt | tulye hi prathamadhyānacakṣurvijñāne dvitīyādiṣu cakṣuṣprakarṣāddarśanaprakarṣo dṛśyata iti | tasmādyuktam- "cakṣuḥ paśyati nayanaṃ paśyati manasi tu bhaktyā prajñāvṛttirupacaryate manasā paśyati" iti |
children.translated_text: ) is intended, or the cooking [itself], then the designation is made according to the predominance of water and fire [respectively] — 'water softens,' 'fire cooks.' Therefore, when the complete aggregate [of conditions] exists and seeing is taking place, it is the eye that is said to 'see' because of predominance. How is there predominance? Because when that [the eye] excels, seeing excels. For, given equal first-<s>dhyāna</s> eye-consciousness, in the second and higher [<s>dhyānas</s>], because of the excellence of the eye, excellence of seeing is observed. Therefore it is proper [to say]: 'the eye sees, the organ sees; but with reference to the mind, the expression 'the mind sees' is used figuratively, [meaning] the operation of insight (<s>prajñā</s>) in devotion to the mind.'

body.translated_text: Therefore, even though other conditions exist, because of the predominance (<s>prādhānya</s>) of the eye in the activity of seeing, it alone is directly said to 'see.' Just as, when <s>Devadatta</s> — though the pot, water, fire, rice, and other [ingredients] exist — is engaged in cooking, having obtained his capacity through the activities of placing on the stove, pouring water, adding rice, stirring with the ladle, and skimming, and having authority over others in the employment of the instruments, <s>Devadatta</s> is said to 'cook' because of [his] predominance. But when the softening of the rice grains (

body.text: tatrayaduktaṃ kośakāreṇa- "kimidamākāśaṃ khādyate | sāmagrayāṃ hi satyāṃ dṛṣṭamityupacāraḥ pravartate | tatra kaḥ paśyati ?" iti | tadatra teta bhadantena sāmagryaṅgakriyāpaharaṇaṃ ? kriyate | abhidharmasaṃmohāṅkasthānenātmāpyaṅkito bhavatyayogaśūnyatāprapātābhimukhyatvaṃ pradarśitamiti ||
body.translated_text: Regarding what the <s>Kośakāra</s> (author of the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>) has said — 'What is this empty space being consumed? For when the aggregate [of conditions] exists, it is seen — this is merely a figurative usage. Who then sees?' — to this [we reply]: is it not the case that the <s>Bhadanta</s> (i.e., <s>Vasubandhu</s>) is here stealing the functional role of the members of the aggregate? By standing in the position of one confused about <s>Abhidharma</s>, he himself is also marked [with that confusion], and has shown [himself to be] facing the precipice of the emptiness of [logical] disconnection.

body.text: kiṃ punarekenāpi cakṣaṣā paśyati, āhosvid dvābhyāmeveti ? nātra niyamaḥ | yasmāt
body.translated_text: Does one see with even a single eye, or necessarily with both? There is no fixed rule here. Because:

body.text: ekasya cakṣuṣaḥ kāryaṃ vijñānamathavā dvayoḥ /
body.translated_text: The effect of one eye is consciousness, or [the effect] of both;

body.text: iti dvicandradarśanādervijñānasya .......... ||
body.translated_text: from the seeing of a double moon and the like, the consciousness [arises]...

body.text: prāptagrāhīṇi āhosvidaprāptagrāhīṇīti ? taducyate |
body.translated_text: Do [the sense-faculties] grasp by reaching [the object], or do they grasp without reaching [it]? To that it is said:

body.text: aprāpyārthaṃ manaścakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ca trīṇyato 'nyathā // Abhidh-d_45 //
body.translated_text: The mind, eye, and ear — these three [grasp] without reaching the object; the others are otherwise. (Abhidh-d 45)

body.text: ghrāṇarasanakāyendriyāṇi prāptagrāhīṇītyarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The meaning is that the nose, tongue, and body sense-faculties grasp by reaching [the object].

body.text: atra kāṇādaḥ paśyati | nāprāptagrāhīṇīndriyāṇi | cakṣuṣo hi raśmirgatvā paśyati | śrotraṃ tra sarvagataṃ prāpyaiva sarvaṃ śrṛṇoti | taṃ pratīdamucyate |
body.translated_text: Here the <s>Kāṇāda</s> [i.e., <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>] objects: the sense-faculties do not grasp without reaching. For the eye's ray, having gone forth, sees. And the ear, being all-pervading, hears everything only by reaching [it]. Against him, this is said:

body.text: aprāptagrāhiṇaḥ siddhā dūrāsannasamagrahāt /
body.translated_text: The non-reaching graspers are established, because they grasp [objects] far, near, and equidistant alike;

body.text: yāvatā hi kālena devadattaḥ svapāṇitalalekhāṃ paśyati tāvataiva candralekhām | na cāyaṃ gatimatāṃ dharmaḥ | gatimanto hi devadattādayo dūraṃ cirādgacchantyāsannaṃ kṣipramiti | na | pradīpavat tatsiddheḥ |
body.translated_text: for in the same amount of time that <s>Devadatta</s> sees the lines on his own palm, he also sees the crescent moon. And this is not the nature of things that travel. For things that travel — <s>Devadatta</s> and others — go far slowly and go near quickly. [The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> says:] No; because it is established like a lamp.

children.translated_text: If [you say it is like] the power of a lamp and the like —

body.text: yathā khalu yāvatā kālena pradīpo nediṣṭhaṃ rūpamabhivyanakti tāvatā daviṣṭhaṃ tadvaditi | tatra pratyavasthānam-
body.translated_text: just as a lamp manifests a near form in the same amount of time as a far form, so too [with the eye] — to this, the response:

body.text: na samaṃ tatsamudbhavāt // Abhidh-d_46 //
body.translated_text: No, because of its being equally arisen [from a cause]; (Abhidh-d 46)

body.text: yadi pradīpo gacchet, tatrāpyeṣa doṣaḥ prasajyeta | prabhādimadhyānteṣu ca tāpaviśeṣadarśanāt tadekatvāsiddhiḥ | tasya punaḥ pratītya yugapat sarvapradīpaprabhāmupādāya rūpaparamāṇūnāmutpattistasyaiṣa doṣo nāsti ||
body.translated_text: if the lamp [itself] traveled, this fault would apply to it too. And because differences in heat are observed at the beginning, middle, and end of the light, the unity [of the traveling ray] is not established. Rather, because all the light-atoms arise simultaneously, dependent [on the lamp], taking up all the lamp's luminosity, this fault does not apply to it.

body.text: sarvagrahaprasaṃgaścennāyaskāntādidarśanāt /
body.translated_text: If [you object that there would be] the consequence of grasping everything — [we respond:] no, because of the observation of a magnet and the like;

body.text: yadyaprāptagrāhi cakṣuḥ brahmaloke brahmāṇaṃ kasmānna paśyati ? tatredamucyate | nāyaskāntavattatsiddheḥ | yathā tulye 'pyaprāptākarṣaṇe na prācīno 'yaskānto maṇirudīcīnamayaḥ samākarṣati tadvaditi ||
body.translated_text: if the eye grasps without reaching, why does it not see <s>Brahmā</s> in the <s>Brahmaloka</s>? To this it is said: because it is established like a magnet. Just as, even though there is equally non-contact attraction, an ancient magnet does not attract a piece of iron in the north from [its position in the south], so too [with the eye].

body.text: atra punarvindhyavāsī paśyati sarvagatatvamindriyāṇām | taṃ pratīdamucyate |
body.translated_text: Here, however, the <s>Vindhyavāsin</s> (a <s>Sāṃkhya</s> thinker) holds that the sense-faculties are all-pervading. Against him, this is said:

body.text: sarvagatvādadoṣaścennāyogāttilatailavat // Abhidh-d_47 //
body.translated_text: If [you say there is] no fault because of all-pervasiveness — [we respond:] no, because of [the consequence of] disconnection, like oil in sesame; (Abhidh-d 47)

body.text: ko hyanunmatto brūyāttileṣu tailaṃ sarvagatamastīti ? tadvakcakṣuḥśrotrādyadhiṣṭhānebhyo bahirindriyāṇi kaḥ kalpayedamūḍhacetāḥ ?
body.translated_text: for who, not being mad, would say 'oil pervades sesame in all [its parts]'? Similarly, who of unconfused mind would posit sense-faculties outside the bases of the mouth, eyes, ears, and the like?

body.text: idaṃ vaktavyam | yatra kāye sthitaścakṣuṣā rūpāṇi paśyati kiṃ tāni kāyacakṣūrūpavijñānāni ekabhaumāni, āhostidanyabhaumikānyapi ? sarveṣāmaniyamaḥ | tatra kāmadhātūpapannasya tāvat svena cakṣuṣā svāni rūpāṇi paśyataḥ sarvaṃ svabhaumam | tasyaivāsya dhyānacakṣuṣā svarūpāṇi paśyataḥ kāyarūpe svabhūmike dvayaṃ prathamāddhyānāt | prathamadhyānabhūmīni paśyato rūpāṇyapi tatratyāni | dvitīyadhyānacakṣuṣā samīkṣamāṇasya kāyarūpe svabhūmike, cakṣurdvitīyād dhyānāt, vijñānaṃ prathamāt | prathamadhyānabhūmīni paśyato vijñānarūpe prathamāddhyānāt, kāyaḥ kāmāvacaraḥ, cakṣurdvitīyāddhyānāt | dvitīyadhyānabhūmīni paśyataścakṣūrūpe dvitīyadhyānabhūmike kāyaḥ kāmāvacāro vijñānaṃ prathamadhyānāt | evaṃ tṛtīyacaturthadhyānabhūmikena cakṣuṣā tadbhūmikādharabhūmikāni rūpāṇi paśyato vijñātavyam | prathamadhyānopapannasya svena cakṣuṣā svānarūpāṇi paśyataḥ sarvaṃ svabhūmikam | adharāṇi rūpāṇi paśyatastrayaṃ svabhūmikaṃ rūpāṇi kāmāvacarāṇi | dvitīyadhyānacakṣuṣā svāni rūpāṇi paśyatastrayaṃ svabhūmikaṃ cakṣurdvitīyāt | kāmāvacarāṇi paśyataḥ kāyavijñāne svabhūmike, kāmāvacarāṇi rūpāṇi, cakṣurdvitīyāt | dvitīyadhyānabhūmīni paśyataścakṣūrūpe tadbhūmike śeṣaṃ svabhūmikam evaṃ tṛtīyādidhyānacakṣuṣā yojyam | dvitīyādidhyānopapannasya svaparacakṣurbhyāṃ svaparabhūmikāni rūpāṇi paśyato yathāsaṃbhavaṃ draṣṭavyam ||
body.translated_text: This must be stated: when one situated in a particular body sees forms with the eye, are those body, eye, form, and consciousness of a single plane (<s>bhauma</s>), or can they also be of different planes? There is no fixed rule for all [cases]. In that regard, for one born in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), seeing one's own forms with one's own eye, everything is of one's own plane. For that same person seeing one's own forms with the <s>dhyāna</s>-eye, body and form are of one's own plane, and the pair [eye and consciousness] are from the first <s>dhyāna</s>. When seeing forms of the first-<s>dhyāna</s> plane, the forms too are of that [plane]. When looking with the second-<s>dhyāna</s> eye, body and form are of one's own plane, the eye is from the second <s>dhyāna</s>, and the consciousness is from the first. When seeing first-<s>dhyāna</s> plane [forms], consciousness and form are from the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the body is of the desire realm, and the eye is from the second <s>dhyāna</s>. When seeing second-<s>dhyāna</s> plane [forms], eye and form are of the second-<s>dhyāna</s> plane, the body is of the desire realm, and the consciousness is from the first <s>dhyāna</s>. In the same way, one should understand [the arrangement] when seeing forms of one's own and lower planes with the eye of the third and fourth <s>dhyāna</s> planes. For one born in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, seeing one's own forms with one's own eye, everything is of one's own plane. When seeing lower forms, the triad is of one's own plane, and the forms are of the desire realm. When seeing one's own forms with the second-<s>dhyāna</s> eye, the triad is of one's own plane, and the eye is from the second. When seeing desire-realm [forms], body and consciousness are of one's own plane, the forms are of the desire realm, and the eye is from the second. When seeing second-<s>dhyāna</s> plane [forms], eye and form are of that plane, and the rest is of one's own plane. In the same way, one should apply [this analysis] with the eye of the third and subsequent <s>dhyānas</s>. For one born in the second and subsequent <s>dhyānas</s>, seeing forms of one's own and other planes with one's own and other eyes, one should examine according to possibility.

body.text: niyatastvayam-
body.translated_text: But this is fixed:

children.text: na hyūrdhvaṃ cakṣuṣaḥ kāyo na rūpaṃ nākṣijaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: The body is never above the eye; form [is never above the eye]; and the mind born from the eye [is never above the eye];

children.text: vijñānasya tu netrārthastau ca kāyasya savaṃtaḥ // Abhidh-d_48 //
children.translated_text: but for consciousness, the eye and object [can be from anywhere]; and both [eye and form] can be from anywhere relative to the body. (Abhidh-d 48)

body.text: pañcabhaumāni kāyacakṣūrūpāṇi dvayoḥ savitarkasavicārayorbhūmyoścakṣurvijñānam | tatra yadmūmikaḥ kāyastadbhūmikamūrdhvabhūmikaṃ vā cakṣurbhavati na tvadhobhaumikam | yadbhūmikaṃ cakṣustadbhūmikamadharabhūmikaṃ vāsya rūpaṃ gocarī bhavati nordhvabhūmikam | evaṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ nādharime cakṣuṣi saṃmukhībhavati | asya tu cakṣurvijñānasya rūpaṃ sarvato viṣayībhavati | kāyasyāpyubhe rūpavijñāne sarvato bhavata iti ||
body.translated_text: Body, eye, and form are [each possible across] five planes; eye-consciousness [occurs] on the two planes that possess <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application). The body is of its own plane or a higher plane relative to the eye, but never of a lower plane. The form that serves as the eye's object is of the eye's own plane or a lower plane, but never of a higher plane. Likewise, eye-consciousness does not arise in a lower eye. But for this eye-consciousness, form becomes its object from all [planes]. And for the body too, both form and consciousness can be from all [planes].

body.text: evaṃ
body.translated_text: Similarly,

children.text: nopariṣṭācchru teḥ kāyo na śabdo na svakaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: the body is never above the ear; neither is sound, nor is the mind its own [i.e., of the ear];

children.text: vijñānasya tu nihrādastau ca kāyasya sarvataḥ // Abhidh-d_49 //
children.translated_text: but for consciousness, sound [can be from anywhere]; and both [ear and sound] can be from anywhere relative to the body. (Abhidh-d 49)

body.text: ghrāṇādīnāṃ punaḥ
body.translated_text: As for the nose and the rest,

children.translated_text: for the [remaining] three, all three are their own [plane];

body.text: kāyagandhādiviṣayavijñānāni svabhūmikānyeva | utsargasyāyamapavādaḥ kriyate |
body.translated_text: body, smell/taste/touch, and consciousness [of smell, taste, touch] are of their own plane only. This exception to the general rule is made:

body.text: tanorvijñānamapyadhaḥ /
body.translated_text: but body-consciousness can also be lower;

body.text: kāyaspṛṣṭavye svabhūmike eva | kāyavijñānaṃ tu keṣāñcidadharabhūmikam | yathā dvitīyādidhyānopapannānāmiti |
body.translated_text: the body and tangible object are of one's own plane only. But body-consciousness can, in some cases, be of a lower plane — as in the case of those born in the second and higher <s>dhyānas</s>.

children.translated_text: The mind, however, is unrestricted,

body.text: samāpattyupapattikāleṣu kāyasya sarvato bhāvāt | traikālikādhvanirmuktasarvadharmaviṣayitvāt ||
body.translated_text: because the body can exist in all [planes] during the times of attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>) and rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>); and because [the mind] has as its object all <s>dharmas</s> freed from the three time-periods.

body.text: kimarthaṃ punarayamalpārthaḥ sumahāgranthasandarbhavidhirārabhyata iti ? (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 37]

children.text: ) kośakṛdācaṣṭe- nahyatra kiñcitphalamutprekṣyata iti | taṃ pratīdaṃ phalamādarśyate | tatra khalu
children.translated_text: ) The <s>Kośakāra</s> states: 'no fruit whatsoever is discerned herein.' Against him, this fruit is shown. For indeed,

body.translated_text: For what purpose, then, is this extensive textual composition of minor import undertaken? (

body.text: yogivaiśvarūpyaṃ pradarśitam // Abhidh-d_50 //
body.translated_text: the manifold powers of the <s>yogin</s> are demonstrated. (Abhidh-d 50)

body.text: etadvaiśvarūpyaṃ yogināṃ yadanyataḥ kāyo 'nyataścakṣuranyataḥ rūpamanyato vijñānaṃ gṛhītvā paśyanti | vibhūni ca śarīrāṇi nirmāya manojavayā ṛddhyā gatvā buddhā bhagavanto yathecchaṃ lokadhātvantareṣu vineyānāṃ buddhakāryaṃ kurvaṃti | divyābhyāṃ cakṣuḥśrotrābhyāṃ rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā śabdāṃśca śrutvā yathecchaṃ yugapadanekāni pāñcagatikāni śarīrāṇi nirmāyānekagatidhātvantareṣu vineyakāryaṃ kurvantīti |
body.translated_text: This manifold power of the <s>yogins</s> is that they see by taking the body from one [plane], the eye from another, form from another, and consciousness from another. And the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavats</s>, having created numerous bodies, going by the mind-swift <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power), perform the Buddha's work for those to be trained in world-realms at will. And having seen forms with the divine eye and heard sounds with the divine ear, they at will simultaneously create numerous bodies of the five destinies and perform the work of training [beings] in world-realms of multiple destinies.

body.text: gatametat prāsaṅgikaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: This concludes the incidental topic.

body.text: idamadhunā vācyam | skandhopādānaskandhayoḥ kaḥ prativiśeṣaḥ ? taducyate | skandhāstribhiḥ satyaiḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ | yasmāt
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: what is the distinction between <s>skandha</s> (aggregate) and <s>upādāna-skandha</s> (aggregate of clinging)? To that it is said: the <s>skandhas</s> are comprised under three truths. Because:

children.translated_text: The <s>skandhas</s> can be with or without <s>āsrava</s> (influx/defilement); but those designated as <s>upādāna</s> (clinging)
should be known as exclusively with <s>āsrava</s>, by reason of their association, activity, and the like. (Abhidh-d 51)

body.text: kāraṇairiti vākyādhyāhāraḥ | tasmādupādānaskandhāḥ satyadvayasaṃgṛhītāḥ | nirodhasatyaṃ tu skandhalakṣaṇānupapatteḥ skandhalakṣaṇavyatiriktamiti draṣṭavyam ||
body.translated_text: 'By causes' — this is the completion of the sentence. Therefore, the <s>upādāna-skandhas</s> are comprised under two truths. But the truth of cessation (<s>nirodha-satya</s>), since it does not conform to the characteristic of a <s>skandha</s>, should be regarded as distinct from the <s>skandha</s>-characteristic.

children.translated_text: The synonyms of <s>skandha</s>, beginning with 'time-period' (<s>adhvan</s>):

body.text: adhvānaskandhāḥ saṃskṛtāḥ kathāvastvityevamādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: The time-periods, the <s>skandhas</s>, the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), the subject of discourse (<s>kathāvastu</s>), and so forth;

body.text: dharmādyā vastunaḥ sataḥ /
body.translated_text: [those] beginning with '<s>dharma</s>' [are synonyms] of existing reality (<s>vastu</s>):

body.text: sat vastu dharmo dravyamāyatanaṃ dhāturityevamādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: reality (<s>sat</s>), entity (<s>vastu</s>), <s>dharma</s>, substance (<s>dravya</s>), sense-sphere (<s>āyatana</s>), element (<s>dhātu</s>), and so forth;

body.text: ye tu sāsravasaṃjñāste proktā duḥkhādināmabhiḥ // Abhidh-d_52 //
body.translated_text: but those designated as 'with <s>āsrava</s>' are expressed by names beginning with '<s>duḥkha</s>' (suffering) and the like. (Abhidh-d 52)

body.text: duḥkhaṃ loko bhavaḥ samudaya ityevamādibhirnāmabhiḥ śabdayante ||
body.translated_text: They are designated by names such as suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), world (<s>loka</s>), existence (<s>bhava</s>), origination (<s>samudaya</s>), and so forth.

body.text: atha kasmāccakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇānāṃ dvitve satyekadhātutā ? tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: Now, why is there a single <s>dhātu</s> (element) when the eye, ear, and nose are [each] two [in number]? This is now undertaken:

children.translated_text: Because of the unity of intrinsic nature, object-domain, and function, there is a single element-hood, even though the eye and the rest are two [in number];

body.text: trayāṇāmapi khalveteṣāmekasvabhāvatvādekagocaratvādekakāryatvācca dvitve 'pi satyekādhipatyaṃ caikadhātutā ca nirvartete |
body.translated_text: for each of these three [sense-faculties], because of having a single intrinsic nature, a single object-domain, and a single function, even though there are two [organs], there is a single sovereignty and hence a single element-hood.

body.text: dvyutpattiḥ karmatritvaśāt // Abhidh-d_53 //
body.translated_text: The duality of arising is because of the triplicity of action. (Abhidh-d 53)

body.text: ye tu kathayanti "śobhārthaṃ tu dvayodbhavaḥ" iti teṣāṃ ślīpadagaṇḍaprabhṛtīnām atiśobhārthamutpattirityāpannam ||
body.translated_text: But those who say 'the duality arises for the sake of beauty' — for them, the consequence is that tumors, goiters, and the like arise for the sake of supreme beauty.

body.text: idamidānīṃ vācyam | cakṣurādikāraṇasāmagrīsannidhāne sati cakṣurvijñānotpattau kasmāccakṣuḥśrotrādivijñānamityucyate ? tatra visarjanaṃ kriyate-
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: when the complete aggregate of causal conditions, beginning with the eye, is present and eye-consciousness arises, why is it called 'eye-consciousness,' 'ear-consciousness,' and so forth? The answer is given:

children.translated_text: Because of the distinctive [role of] the uncommon [cause], because of sovereignty, because of being the inner [factor],
even though there are multiple causes, consciousness is specified by those [sense-faculties]. (Abhidh-d 54)

body.text: cakṣurādīndriyaviśeṣādvijñānaviśeṣo dṛṣṭaḥ | cakṣurādīnāṃ ca caturbhiḥ kāraṇairīśitvaṃ dṛṣṭam | asādhāraṇakāraṇatvena cāntaraṅgya iti ||
body.translated_text: The specification of consciousness is observed due to the specification of the sense-faculties, eye and the rest. And the sovereignty of the eye and the rest is observed for four reasons: because of being the uncommon cause and because of being the inner [factor].

body.text: atrāha | atha kasmāt sarvapadārthānāṃ dravyasvabhāvatve nirvāṇameva paramārthato dravyamityucyate yato dharmadhātureva tadyogāddravyavānityākhyāyate | kasmācca sarvasaṃskṛtānāṃ kṣaṇikatve sati traya evāntyā dhātavaḥ kṣaṇikā ityucyante ? tadubhayaṃ pradarśyate |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here one asks: If all categories of existents have substance-nature (<s>dravyasvabhāva</s>), then why is <s>nirvāṇa</s> alone said to be ultimately a substance (<s>dravya</s>), such that only the <s>dharma</s>-element is declared 'possessing substance' by virtue of its connection [with nirvāṇa]? And why, when all conditioned [dharmas] are momentary, are only the last three elements said to be momentary? Both [points] are now demonstrated:

children.translated_text: Because of its permanence and its being wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), <s>nirvāṇa</s> is truly a substance (<s>dravya</s>);
by virtue of that essential substance, the one [element] called '<s>dharma</s>' is considered 'possessing substance.' (Abhidh-d 55)
The first pure mind (<s>nirmala citta</s>) is recalled as a 'moment' (<s>kṣaṇa</s>) due to its incomparability (<s>asābhāgya</s>);
by virtue of that extraordinary moment, these last three [elements] are [called] 'momentary.' (Abhidh-d 56)

body.text: kiṃ punarete cakṣurādayastulyaṃ viṣayaṃ gṛhṇanti, āhosvinnyūnamavikaṃ vā ? tadāviṣkriyate-
body.translated_text: Do these [faculties] beginning with the eye apprehend their objects equally, or more, or less? This is revealed:

body.text: ghrāṇaṃ jihvā ca kāyaśca tulyārthagrāhyadastrayam /
body.translated_text: The nose, tongue, and body — these three apprehend objects equally.

body.text: dvayoścakṣuḥśrotrayoraniyama ityākhyātaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: For the two — eye and ear — there is no fixed rule. This is what is stated.

body.text: kiṃpunareṣāṃ cakṣurvijñānādīnāṃ sahaja evāśrayaḥ, āhosvidatīto 'pi ? taducyate |
body.translated_text: Is the support (<s>āśraya</s>) of these consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness simultaneous [with them], or also past? To that it is said:

children.translated_text: The support of the last [i.e., mind-consciousness] is past.

body.text: manovijñānasya kriyāvato nityamāśrayo 'tītaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the active mind-consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>), the support is always past.

body.text: pañcānāṃ taiḥ sahāpi ca // Abhidh-d_57 //
body.translated_text: And for the five [sense-consciousnesses], [the support is] also simultaneous with them. (Abhidh-d 57)

body.text: pañcānāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ taiḥ sahāpi cātītaśceti 'ca'śabdāt |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the five consciousness-bodies (<s>vijñānakāya</s>), [the support is] 'also simultaneous with them and past' — by the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>).

body.text: evaṃ catuṣkoṭika ārabhyate | ye dharmā vijñānaniśrayāḥ samanantarā api te ? praśnaścatuṣkoṭikaḥ | niśraya eva cakṣurādayaḥ | samanantarā eva vedanādayaḥ | ubhayaṃ samanantaraniruddhaṃ vijñānam | nobhayametānākārān sthāpayitvā ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus a fourfold classification (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>) is commenced: 'Which <s>dharmas</s> that are supports (<s>niśraya</s>) of consciousness are also immediately-preceding (<s>samanantara</s>)?' The question is fourfold. Support only: the eye and others. Immediately-preceding only: feeling and others. Both: the consciousness that has just ceased. Neither: setting aside these categories.

body.text: idamidānīmabhidharmasarvasvaṃ kośakārakasmṛtigocarātītaṃ vaktavyam | athaiṣāmaṣṭādaśānāṃ dhātūnāṃ katamaṃ niśrayaṃ niśrityānāsraveṇa mārgeṇa katamo dhāturnirudhyate !
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now this, the very essence of <s>Abhidharma</s>, which lies beyond the range of the <s>Kośa</s>-author's memory, must be stated. When these eighteen elements are considered — relying on which support is which element ceased by the outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) path?

children.translated_text: Relying indeed on the <s>anāgamya</s> (access [concentration]), or on the four supports,
the eye-element is ceased by the outflow-free path. (Abhidh-d 58)

body.text: navasu bhūmiṣu khalvanāsravo mārgaḥ | cakṣurdhātustu pañcabhūmikaḥ | tatra prajñāvimuktasyālabdhadhyānasyāryasyānāgamyaṃ niśritya cakṣurdhāturnirudhyate | nirodhamārgajñānātmakasya tridhātupratipakṣatvāddhyānalābhinaḥ punaścaturo niśrayānniśritya dhyānāntarikāyāḥ prathamena grahaṇāt ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The outflow-free path exists in nine grounds (<s>bhūmi</s>). The eye-element belongs to five grounds. For the noble one (<s>ārya</s>) who is liberated by wisdom (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>) and has not attained <s>dhyāna</s>, the eye-element is ceased relying on <s>anāgamya</s>. For one who is of the nature of cessation-and-path-knowledge (<s>nirodhamārgajñānātmaka</s>), being the antidote to all three realms, and who has attained <s>dhyāna</s>, [it is ceased] relying on the four supports — because the <s>dhyānāntarikā</s> (intermediate [absorption]) is included in the first [dhyāna].

body.text: anāgamyaṃ tu niśritya gandhadhāturnirudhyate /
body.translated_text: The odor-element (<s>gandhadhātu</s>) is ceased relying on <s>anāgamya</s> [alone],

body.text: dhyānālābhinastannirodhāt |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] because its cessation [occurs only through] one who has not attained <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: manodhāturanāgamyaṃ yadi vā saptaniśrayāt // Abhidh-d_59 //
body.translated_text: The mind-element (<s>manodhātu</s>) [is ceased] relying on <s>anāgamya</s>, or on seven supports. (Abhidh-d 59)

body.text: catvāri dhyānāni trīṃścārūpyān, tasya traidhātukatvāt ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The four <s>dhyānas</s> and the three formless [attainments] — because [mind-element] belongs to all three realms.

body.text: anāgamyaṃ tathaivādyaṃ cakṣurvijñānasaṃjñakaḥ /
body.translated_text: Relying on <s>anāgamya</s> and likewise the first [<s>dhyāna</s>], the one designated as eye-consciousness

body.text: nirudhyata iti vartate | tasya kāmaprathamadhyānasamāpannatvāt |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] is ceased — this is the continuation. Because [eye-consciousness] belongs to the desire-realm and the first-<s>dhyāna</s> attainment.

body.text: dharmadhātorvicitratvādyathāyogaṃ vinirdiśet // Abhidh-d_60 //
body.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s>-element, due to its variety, one should specify according to applicability. (Abhidh-d 60)

body.text: dharmadhātuḥ khalu kaścitkāmāvacara eva yathā pratighādayaḥ | kaścitkāme prathamadhyānayoryathā vitarkavicārādayaḥ | kaścitkāme prathamadvitīyadhyānayoryathā prītiḥ | kaścitkāme tṛtīyadhyānayoryathā sukhendriyam | kaścittraidhātuko yathā jīvitendriyādayaḥ | ata ucyate 'yathāyogaṃ vinirdi śet | evamanyānapi dhātūnanenaiva yathoktena nyāyena 'yathāyogaṃ vinirdiśet'; iti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The <s>dharma</s>-element is indeed various: some belong only to the desire-realm, such as hostility (<s>pratigha</s>) and others; some belong to the desire-realm and the first <s>dhyāna</s>, such as applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>) and others; some belong to the desire-realm and the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>, such as joy (<s>prīti</s>); some belong to the desire-realm and the third <s>dhyāna</s>, such as the pleasure-faculty (<s>sukhendriya</s>); some belong to all three realms, such as the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>) and others. Therefore it is said 'one should specify according to applicability.' Thus for the other elements too, by this very stated method, 'one should specify according to applicability.'

body.text: idamidānīmanyadvaktavyam | yadā pṛthagjanaścakṣurdhātuṃ rūpāptaṃ parijānāti tadā katamāddhātorvairāgyamāpnoti ? kati ca kutratyānanuśayān jahāti ? kāni ca saṃyojanāni paryādāya jahāti ? tadāviṣkriyate-
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now another matter must be stated. When an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) fully comprehends (<s>parijānāti</s>) the eye-element as belonging to the form[-realm], from which element does he attain dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>)? How many latent afflictions (<s>anuśaya</s>) belonging to which [realm] does he abandon? And which fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) does he fully abandon? This is revealed:

children.translated_text: When an ordinary person fully comprehends the eye-element as belonging to the form[-realm],
he attains dispassion from the entire form-constituted element. (Abhidh-d 61)
From that element, he abandons thirty-one latent afflictions,

children.text: paryādatte na kiñcittu saṃyojanamasau tadā // Abhidh-d_62 //
children.translated_text: but he does not fully exhaust any fetter at that time. (Abhidh-d 62)

body.text: anuśayānāṃ hi dhātuparicchedo na saṃyojanānām |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For latent afflictions (<s>anuśaya</s>) are delimited by realm (<s>dhātu</s>), but not fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>).

body.text: rūpavairāgyamāpnoti jahātyanuśayatrayam /
body.translated_text: He attains dispassion from form[-realm] and abandons three latent afflictions —

body.text: satkāyadṛṣṭiśīlavrataparāmarśavicikitsākhyaṃ rūpadhātuparyāpannam |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] namely those called view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), clinging to rules and vows (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), belonging to the form-realm.

body.text: tadā saṃyojanaṃ tvāryaḥ paryādatte na kiñcana // Abhidh-d_63 //
body.translated_text: But at that time, the noble one (<s>ārya</s>) does not fully exhaust any fetter. (Abhidh-d 63)

body.text: anuśayatrayaṃ kataradāryo jahāti bhavarāgamānāvidyākhyam ? bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ tu na dhātuparicchinnamiti na kiñcittadā jahāti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Which three latent afflictions does the noble one abandon? Those called craving for existence (<s>bhavarāga</s>), conceit (<s>māna</s>), and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). [These are] to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>). But fetters are not delimited by realm, therefore he does not abandon any at that time.

children.translated_text: When fully comprehending the eye-consciousness-element, one also [comprehends] that very [eye-element],
and one necessarily attains dispassion from the <s>Brahma</s>-world. (Abhidh-d 64)

children.text: na tu saṃyojanaṃ kiñcitparyādatte tadā hyasau /
children.translated_text: But one does not fully exhaust any fetter at that time;

children.text: gandhadhātuṃ rasākhyaṃ ca parijānan pṛthagjanaḥ // Abhidh-d_65 //
children.translated_text: when an ordinary person fully comprehends the odor-element and the one called taste[-element], (Abhidh-d 65)
he attains dispassion from the desire[-realm]; and the latent afflictions too,
at that time he abandons thirty-six, and three fetters. (Abhidh-d 66)

body.text: kāmāvacarācchaṭtriṃśadanuśayāñjahāti | trīṇi ca saṃyojanāni pratighasaṃyojanamīrṣyāmātsaryasaṃyojane ca | gandharasadhātūparijānan pṛthagjanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] He abandons thirty-six latent afflictions belonging to the desire-realm. And three fetters: the fetter of hostility (<s>pratigha</s>), the fetter of envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), and the fetter of avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>). [This applies to] the ordinary person fully comprehending the odor and taste elements.

children.translated_text: But the noble one (<s>ārya</s>) attains dispassion from the desire[-realm] and [abandons] four latent afflictions too —

body.text: pratighakāmarāgamānāvidyākhyān bhāvanāheyān ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] namely those called hostility (<s>pratigha</s>), desire-realm craving (<s>kāmarāga</s>), conceit (<s>māna</s>), and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) — to be abandoned by cultivation.

body.text: paryādatte 'pi ca trayam // Abhidh-d_67 //
body.translated_text: and fully exhausts three [fetters] too. (Abhidh-d 67)

body.text: pratigherṣyāmātsaryasaṃyojanākhyam ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Called the fetters of hostility, envy, and avarice.

body.text: parijānanmanodhātumārūpyebhyo virajyate /
body.translated_text: When fully comprehending the mind-element, [the noble one] attains dispassion from the formless [realms];

body.text: ārya iti vartate |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'noble one' (<s>ārya</s>) is the continuation.

children.translated_text: and abandons three latent afflictions,

body.text: rāgamānāvidyākhyān |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] namely those called craving (<s>rāga</s>), conceit (<s>māna</s>), and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>).

body.text: paryādatte trayaṃ tathā // Abhidh-d_68 //
body.translated_text: and likewise fully exhausts three [fetters]. (Abhidh-d 68)

body.text: etadeva ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The same [as above].

children.translated_text: When fully comprehending joy (<s>prīti</s>), one abandons that very [joy] itself,

children.text: ābhāsvarācca vairāgyaṃ yāti hanti tu nāsravān // Abhidh-d_69 //
children.translated_text: and attains dispassion from the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Radiant) [heaven], but does not destroy outflows (<s>āsrava</s>). (Abhidh-d 69)

body.text: tasyāstaduparyabhāvāt |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because [joy] does not exist above that [level].

children.translated_text: When the yogin fully comprehends pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), he abandons that here,

children.text: śubhakṛtsnācca vairāgyaṃ yāti kleśānna hanti tu // Abhidh-d_70 //
children.translated_text: and attains dispassion from <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (All-Beautiful [heaven]), but does not destroy the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). (Abhidh-d 70)

body.text: sukhendriyasya tatīyādhyānāduparyabhāvādakṛtsnadhātūnna kleśāñjahāti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because the pleasure-faculty does not exist above the third <s>dhyāna</s>, [and because] the elements are not complete [above it], he does not abandon the afflictions.

body.text: gamatetatprayojanāgataṃ prakaraṇam | prakṛtamevocyatām | athaiṣāṃ dhātūnāṃ ke kati vijñānavijñeyāḥ ? tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This topic has arrived at its purpose. Let the original subject be resumed. Now, of these elements, which are cognizable by how many consciousnesses? This is commenced:

children.translated_text: The five qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) are cognizable by two [consciousnesses];

body.text: pañcarūpādiguṇākhyā dhātavaścakṣurādivijñānamanovijñānavijñeyāḥ | śeṣā manovijñānavijñeyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The five elements called qualities, beginning with form (<s>rūpa</s>), are cognizable by eye-consciousness and the like [respectively] and by mind-consciousness. The rest are cognizable by mind-consciousness alone.

body.text: kati hetuḥ kati na hetuḥ ? tadākhyāyate-
body.translated_text: How many are causes (<s>hetu</s>)? How many are not causes? This is stated:

body.text: hetuḥ sarve kṣarākṣarāḥ /
body.translated_text: All are causes, both with-outflows (<s>kṣara</s>) and without-outflows (<s>akṣara</s>).

body.text: sarvadharmā hi kāraṇahetusvabhāvāḥ | kṣarāstu yathāyogaṃ cintyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For all <s>dharmas</s> are of the nature of the causal condition (<s>kāraṇahetu</s>). Those with outflows should be considered according to applicability.

body.text: katīndriyātmakāḥ ? kati nendriyasvabhāvāḥ ? tadāviṣkriyate-
body.translated_text: How many are of faculty-nature (<s>indriyātmaka</s>)? How many are not of faculty-nature? This is revealed:

body.text: anyatra dharmadhātvardhācchaḍbāhyā nendriyātmakāḥ // Abhidh-d_71 //
body.translated_text: Except for half of the <s>dharma</s>-element, the six external [elements] are not of faculty-nature. (Abhidh-d 71)

body.text: arthādāyātamādhyātmikāḥ sarve dhātavaḥ | bāhyāḥ pañcarūpaśabdagandharasasparśadharmadhātoścārdhaṃ nendriyasvabhāvaṃ jīvitendriyaśraddhādisukhādipañcakavarjamiti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] By implication, all internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) elements are [of faculty-nature]. The six external — the five form, sound, odor, taste, and touch [elements] — and half of the <s>dharma</s>-element are not of faculty-nature, excepting the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>), the faith-faculty (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the rest, and the fivefold [set] of pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and the rest.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: [End of] the first chapter in the <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s> commentary on the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>.

body.text: dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Second chapter.

body.text: prathamaḥ pādaḥ |
body.translated_text: First quarter (<s>pāda</s>).

children.translated_text: Of the entire section on the twenty-two types of faculties (<s>indriya</s>),
the <s>dharmas</s> [such as] etymology and the rest will be stated in brief. (Abhidh-d 72)

body.text: cakṣurādīnyājñātāvīndriyaparyantāni khalvindriyāṇi etāvānindriyagrāmo na bhūyānnālpīyān |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The faculties are indeed [those] beginning with the eye and ending with the faculty of final knowledge (<s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>) — this is the totality of faculties, neither more nor less.

body.text: uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "dvāviṃśatirindriyāṇi katamāni dvāviṃśatiḥ ? cakṣurindriyaṃ śrotrendriyaṃ yāvadājñātāvīndriyam" iti |
body.translated_text: For it is said by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'The faculties are twenty-two. What are the twenty-two? The eye-faculty, the ear-faculty, up to the faculty of final knowledge.'

body.text: tasyendriyarāśernirvacanānukramadhātubhūmyādiprakārabhedāḥ saṃkṣepeṇābhidhāyiṣyanta iti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The distinctions of etymology, sequence, realm (<s>dhātu</s>), ground (<s>bhūmi</s>), and other categories of this collection of faculties will be stated in brief.

body.text: kiṃ punardravyato dvāviṃśatirindriyāṇyatha nāmataḥ ? tadidamākhyāyate-
body.translated_text: Are the faculties twenty-two in substance (<s>dravya</s>) or in name (<s>nāman</s>)? This is stated:

children.text: nāmnā dvāviṃśatistāni dravyato daśa sapta ca /
children.translated_text: In name they are twenty-two; in substance, seventeen.
Because the [first] pair [male/female] is not different from the body [faculty], and [each of] the three triads of pleasure and the rest [comprises only nine substances]. (Abhidh-d 73)

body.text: kāyendriyapradeśa eva hi kaścitstrīpuruṣendriyākhyaṃ labhate, viśiṣṭakliṣṭavijñānasaṃnniśrayabhūtatvāt | śraddhādīnāṃ ca navānāṃ samudāyeṣu triṣvanājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyāditrayākhyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For a certain portion of the body-faculty itself acquires the designation of male or female faculty, because it constitutes the actual support of a distinguished afflicted consciousness. And of the nine [faculties] beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), in [each of] the three groups, the triad of designations — the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown' (<s>anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriya</s>) and the other two — [are different only in name].

body.text: anye punaḥ paśyanti-
body.translated_text: Others, however, hold:

children.translated_text: Because the defining characteristic of a [merely] nominal [entity] does not apply, and because the name is meaningful,
even though the three [faculties] function within [the same] groups, their [distinct] purpose is accepted by others. (Abhidh-d 74)

body.text: yatkhalu saṃvṛtisatyasya lakṣaṇaṃ tatteṣāṃ nāsti kriyāpauruṣyadvāreṇa tacchabdapravṛtteḥ, laukikāgradharmavat | sārthakatvāttannāmno 'rthavattatkhalvetannāmneti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The characteristic that belongs to conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>) does not apply to them, because those terms function through the door of functional potency (<s>kriyāpauruṣya</s>), like the supreme mundane <s>dharma</s> (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>). Because the name is meaningful — that is indeed meaningful which bears that name.

body.text: strīpuruṣendriyasyāpi-
body.translated_text: Regarding the male and female faculties too —

children.translated_text: because of being the cause of a distinguished cognition, and due to a special mastery (<s>ādhipatya</s>),
the two are distinct from the body-faculty, like the eye-faculty and the rest. (Abhidh-d 75)

body.text: yathaiva hi cakṣurādīni kāyendriyaviśiṣṭāni viśiṣṭabuddhijanakatvādādhipatyaviśeṣācca, tadvadanayorapīti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Just as the eye and other [faculties] are distinct from the body-faculty because of generating a distinguished cognition and due to a special mastery, so too are these two [male and female faculties].

body.text: kaḥ punarindriyārthastadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: What then is the meaning of 'faculty' (<s>indriya</s>)? This is commenced:

body.text: aiśvaryārtho vipaścidbhirindriyārtho 'bhidhīyate /
body.translated_text: The meaning of 'faculty' is declared by the wise to be 'sovereignty' (<s>aiśvarya</s>).

body.text: keṣu punarartheṣu keṣāmīśitvam ? vayaṃ tāvatpaśyāmaḥ-
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] In which domains does each have sovereignty? We observe the following:

children.translated_text: For the five [sense-faculties], in the manifestation of their own objects;

body.text: cakṣurādīnāṃ pañcānāṃ svārthaprakāśanakriyāyāmādhipatyaṃ samaviṣamamārgālocanādityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the five beginning with the eye, sovereignty lies in the activity of illuminating their own objects — the viewing of even and uneven paths, and so forth — this is the meaning.

body.text: caturṇāṃ tvarthayordvayoḥ // Abhidh-d_76 //
body.translated_text: But for the four [remaining faculties], in two domains [each]. (Abhidh-d 76)

body.text: jīvitamanastrīpuruṣendriyāṇāṃ pratyekamarthadvaye | tatra tāvajjīvitendriyasya nikāyasabhāgasaṃbandhasandhāraṇayoḥ | manaindriyasyāpi saṃkleśavyavadānayoḥ | yathoktam- "cittasaṃkleśāt sattvāḥ saṃkliśyante cittavyavadānahetorviśuddhyante" (

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 46)

children.text: ) iti | punarbhavasaṃbandhavaśibhāvānuvartanayorvā | punarbhavasaṃbandhe tāvadyathoktam- "gandharvasya tasmin samaye dvayościttayoranyataratsaṃmukhībhūtaṃ bhavatyanunayasahagataṃ vā pratighasahagataṃ vā |" tathā "vijñānaṃ cedānanda mātuḥ kukṣiṃ nāvakrāmet" iti | vaśibhāvānuvartane yathoktam- "cittenāyaṃ loko nīyate" iti vistaraḥ |
children.translated_text: ) Or, in the linking to renewed existence (<s>punarbhava</s>) and in mastery over continuity. Regarding linking to renewed existence, as stated: 'At that time, for the <s>gandharva</s> (intermediate being), one of two minds arises — accompanied by attachment or accompanied by aversion.' And: 'If consciousness, <s>Ānanda</s>, were not to descend into the mother's womb...' As for mastery over continuity, as stated: 'This world is led by mind,' and so on in detail.

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The life-faculty, mind-faculty, and male and female faculties each [have sovereignty] in two domains. The life-faculty: in the connection with the class-homogeneity (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>) and in sustaining [it]. The mind-faculty too: in defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>). As stated: 'Through the defilement of mind, beings are defiled; through the purification of mind, they are purified.' (

body.text: strīpurūṣendriyayorapi sattvotpattivikalpanayorādhipatyam | sattvotpattau tāvat, prāyastadadhīnatvāttadutpatteḥ | sattvavikalpe 'pi tadvaśāt | prāthamakalpikānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ ceṣṭā strīpuruṣasvarācārādivikalpabhedāt |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The male and female faculties have sovereignty in two domains: in the production of beings and in their differentiation. In production, because [birth] is mostly dependent on them. In differentiation of beings too, because of [gender's] power. And the activities of beings in the first cosmic age (<s>prāthamakalpika</s>) [differ] due to the differentiation of female-male behaviors, appearances, and the like.

body.text: svagocaropalabdhyādāvīśitvamapare viduḥ /
body.translated_text: Others know [the faculties to have] sovereignty in the apprehension of their own objects, and so forth.

body.text: paurāṇāḥ punarācāryāḥ kathayanti- "cakṣurādīnāṃ pañcānāṃ pratyekaṃ caturṣvartheṣvādhipatyam | cakṣuḥśrotrayostāvadātmabhāvaśobhāyāmandhabadhirayorakāntarūpatvāt | ātmabhāvaparikarṣaṇe, dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca viṣayavivarjanāt | cakṣuḥśrotravijñānayoḥ sasaṃprayogayorūtpattau | rūpadarśanaśabdaśravaṇayoścāsādhāraṇakāraṇatve | ghrāṇajihvākāyānāṃ tvātmabhāvaśobhāyāṃ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 47)

children.text: ) pūrvavat | ātmabhāvaparikarṣaṇe, taiḥ kabaḍīkārāhāraparibhogāt | anyat prāgvat |
children.translated_text: ) as before. In the discipline of the personal existence, because through them, morseled food (<s>kabaḍīkārāhāra</s>) is enjoyed. The rest is as stated before.

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The ancient teachers, however, state: 'For each of the five beginning with the eye, sovereignty lies in four domains. For the eye and ear: first, in the beauty of the personal existence (<s>ātmabhāva</s>), because the blind and deaf have an unattractive form. In the discipline of the personal existence, because having seen and heard, one avoids [harmful] objects. In the production of their respective consciousnesses together with their associates. And in being the non-shared cause of form-seeing and sound-hearing. For the nose, tongue, and body, however: in the beauty of the personal existence (

body.text: caturṇāṃ punaḥ strīpuruṣajīvitamanaindriyāṇāṃ dvayorarthayoḥ | strīpuruṣendriyayostāvat- sattvabhedasattvavikalpayoḥ | sattvabhedaḥ strīpuruṣa iti | vikalpabhedo 'pi saṃsthānavacanagamanādi prāgvat | saṃkleśavyavadānayorvā | tadviyutavikalpānāṃ saṃvarāsaṃvarādīni na bhavanti | tadvatāṃ tu saṃvaraphalaprāptiḥ |
body.translated_text: Of the four faculties — female, male, life, and mind — [each has] two purposes. First, the female and male faculties: in the differentiation and distinction of beings. Differentiation of beings is [the distinction of] female and male. The distinction of characteristics also [includes] bodily configuration, speech, gait, and the like, as before. Or, in affliction and purification — those separated from them [i.e., lacking sex-faculties] do not possess the restraints and non-restraints and the like. But those possessing them attain the fruit of restraint.

body.text: jīvitendriyamanaindriyayorapyarthadvaye pūrvavat ||
body.translated_text: The life-faculty and mind-faculty also [have] two purposes, as before.

body.text: svārthavijñāna evānya āhuḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ // Abhidh-d_77 //
body.translated_text: Those who fancy themselves learned say [the sovereignty is] only in the cognition of one's own object. (Abhidh-d 77)

body.text: kośakārādayaḥ punarāhuḥ- "svārthopalabdhāveva cakṣurādīnāṃ pañcānāmādhipatyam |" tadetadvaibhāṣikīyameva kiñcidgṛhītam | nātra kiñcit kośakārakasya svakarṣasvakaṃ darśanam | vaibhāṣaireva svārthopalabdhirukteti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Kośakāra</s> (<s>Vasubandhu</s>) and others, however, say: 'The sovereignty of the five [faculties] beginning with the eye is only in the apprehension of their own objects.' This is merely something partially taken from the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> [position]. There is no original insight of the <s>Kośakāra</s>'s own here. For the apprehension of one's own object was stated by the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> themselves.

body.text: dārṣṭāntikasya hi sarvamapratyakṣam | pañcānāṃ vijñānakāyānāmatītaviṣayatvādyadā (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 48)

children.text: ) khalu cakṣūrūpe vidyete tadā vijñānamasat | yadā vijñānaṃ sat, cakṣūrūpe tadāsatī, vijñānakṣaṇasthityabhāve svārthopalabdhyanupapatteśca ||
children.translated_text: the eye and form exist, then consciousness is non-existent. When consciousness exists, then the eye and form are non-existent — because of the absence of duration at the moment of consciousness, and because the apprehension of one's own object is untenable.

body.translated_text: For the <s>Dārṣṭāntika</s>, indeed, everything is non-perceptual — because the five consciousness-groups have past objects as their domain. When

body.text: kleśotpattau sukhādīnāṃ śraddhādīnāṃ guṇāptiṣu /
body.translated_text: In the arising of afflictions [there is sovereignty] of pleasure and the like; in the attainment of qualities, of faith and the like.

body.text: sukhādīnāmapi pañcānāmindriyāṇāṃ rāgādikleśotpattāvādhipatyam | yathoktam- "vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā" iti | "sukhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ rāgo 'nuśete" iti vistaraḥ | śraddhādīnāṃ punaraṣṭānāṃ sarvaguṇotpattau prabhutvamiti |
body.translated_text: The five faculties of pleasure and the like also have sovereignty in the arising of afflictions such as passion. As it is said: 'Craving is conditioned by feeling.' 'In pleasant feeling, passion lies latent' — and so on in detail. But the eight [faculties] of faith and the like have mastery in the arising of all qualities.

body.text: vaibhāṣāḥ punarāhuḥ "saṃkleśavedanābhiḥ" | tathā hyuktam- "sukhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ rāgo 'nuśete" iti vistaraḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>, however, say: 'In affliction, [the sovereignty is of] the feelings.' For thus it is said: 'In pleasant feeling, passion lies latent' — and so on in detail.

body.text: vyavadāne śraddhādīnāṃ pañcānāṃ taiḥ kleśān viṣkambhya mārgotpādanāt | yathoktam- "śraddheṣīkāsaṃpanno baladhairyasmṛtidauvārikasaṃpannaḥ samāhitacitto vimucyate prajñāśastreṇāryaśrāvakaḥ sarvāṇi saṃyojanāni saṃchinatti" ityādi |
body.translated_text: In purification, [the sovereignty is] of the five [faculties] of faith and the like — because through them, having suppressed the afflictions, the path is produced. As it is said: 'The noble disciple, endowed with faith like a water-strainer, endowed with the strength of firmness, mindfulness, and the gatekeeper, with concentrated mind, is liberated; with the weapon of wisdom, he cuts through all fetters' — and so forth.

body.text: anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyādīnāṃ tu trayāṇāmuttarottarāṅgabhāve nirvāṇe cādhipatyamiti ||
body.translated_text: But the three [faculties] of the 'I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown' faculty and the like have sovereignty in the progressive stages and in <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: kaḥ punareṣāmindriyāṇāmanukramaḥ ? brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: What then is the order of these faculties? We say:

body.text: phalasaṃkleśasaṃbhāraviśuddhitvādanukramaḥ // Abhidh-d_78 //
body.translated_text: The order is by fruition, affliction, accumulation [of the path], and purification. (Abhidh-d 78)

body.text: prākkarma phalaṃ tāvadaṣṭau vipākajatvāttasmāttāni pūrvamuktāni | tasmin vipāke sati saṃkleśasukhādibhiḥ | pañcabhirmārgasaṃbhāraśraddhādibhiḥ | viśuddhiranāsravaistribhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: First, fruition — the eight [faculties: eye etc.], because of being maturation-born; therefore they are stated first. When that maturation exists, affliction [arises] through the five [faculties] of pleasure and the like. The five [faculties] of faith and the like are for the accumulation of the path. Purification [is accomplished] by the three outflow-free [faculties].

body.text: kasmāt punardvāviṃśatireva yathā parikīrtitānyuktāni na bhūyāṃsi nālpīyāṃsīti ? tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: Why then are exactly twenty-two proclaimed and stated — not more and not fewer? That is indicated:

children.translated_text: That by which there is the designation of beings, the variety of beings, sustenance, the arising of afflictions,
the means for the path, and the attainment of the fruit — the faculty-nature of those is accepted. (Abhidh-d 79)

body.text: sattvākhyā khalu pravartate cakṣurādiṣu manaḥparyanteṣu ṣaṭsu | etaddhi maulasattvadravyam | sattvavaicitryaṃ dvābhyāṃ strīpuruṣendriyābhyām | dhṛtirjīvitendriyeṇa | kleśodbhavaḥ pañcabhirvedanābhiḥ | mārgopāyaḥ śraddhādibhiḥ | phalaprāptistribhirantyaiḥ | ityetasmādeṣāmindriyatā matā ||
body.translated_text: The designation of beings indeed operates through the six [faculties] from the eye to the mind. For this is the fundamental being-substance. The variety of beings [is established] by the two — the female and male faculties. Sustenance by the life-faculty. The arising of afflictions by the five feelings. The means for the path by the [faculties] of faith and the like. The attainment of the fruit by the last three. Therefore, the faculty-nature of these is accepted.

children.translated_text: Because of being the support for contact, arising, foundation, and enjoyment — fourteen [faculties];
because of being the cause of heaven and liberation — the other group of eight faculties. (Abhidh-d 80)

body.text: tatra sparśāśrayaścakṣurādīni ṣaḍindriyāṇi | prādurbhāvaḥ strīpuruṣendriyāmyām | ādhāro jīvitendriyeṇa | saṃbhogo vedanābhiḥ pañcabhiḥ | atastāvaccaturdaśoktāni | svargopapattinimittāni śraddhādīni pañca | apavargakāraṇāni trīṇyanājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyādīni ata etāvantyeva ||
body.translated_text: There, the support for contact is the six faculties of the eye and the like. Manifestation [is established] by the female and male faculties. The foundation by the life-faculty. Enjoyment by the five feelings. Thus, fourteen have been stated. The five [faculties] of faith and the like are the causes for attaining heaven. The three — the 'I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown' faculty and the like — are the causes of liberation. Therefore, just this many [exist].

body.text: yadyādhipatyārtha indriyārthaḥ kasmācchandasparśamanaskārasaṃjñācetanāmahābhaumānāṃ satyādhipatye nendriyatvam ? uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "chandamūlakāḥ sarvadharmāḥ sparśajātīyāḥ manaskāraprabhāvāḥ |" saṃjñācetanayośca saṃkleśavyavadānayorādhipatyamuktameva kuśalacetanāyāśca | evaṃ kleśānāmapi saṃsārahetupravartane ādhipatyam | nirvāṇasya ca dharmāgryatve kasmānnendriyatvam ? tadidamucyate-
body.translated_text: If the meaning of 'faculty' is the meaning of 'sovereignty,' why is there no faculty-nature for desire (<s>chanda</s>), contact (<s>sparśa</s>), attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), volition (<s>cetanā</s>), and the great-ground [mental factors], even though they have sovereignty? For the Blessed One said: 'All dharmas have desire as their root, are of the class of contact, are empowered by attention.' And the sovereignty of perception and volition in affliction and purification has been stated — and also of wholesome volition. Likewise, afflictions too have sovereignty in propelling the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>. And <s>nirvāṇa</s>, being supreme among dharmas — why does it not have faculty-nature? To this it is said:

children.translated_text: Desire, because of being a component of vigor; contact, because of nourishing feelings;
perception, because of being overcome by wisdom — the Sage did not declare [these] as faculties. (Abhidh-d 81)

body.text: chando hi kartukāmatā sā ca vīryāṅgabhūtā | vīryaṃ tu sākṣāt kriyayābhisaṃbadhyate | tadevendriyamuktam | sparśo 'pi "sparśapratyayā vedanā" iti tadutpattau parikṣīṇaśaktiḥ | saṃjñāpi prāyo 'pi (prāyo) lokavyavahārapatitā | sā prajñayā paramārthaikarasayābhibhūteti nendriyamuktā ||
