body.translated_text: For desire is the wish to act, and that is a component of vigor. But vigor is directly connected with action — that alone has been declared a faculty. Contact too — 'feeling is conditioned by contact' — its power is exhausted in producing that [feeling]. Perception too is mostly fallen into worldly conventional usage. It is overcome by wisdom, which has the single flavor of ultimate [truth] — therefore it is not declared a faculty.

children.text: śraddhādīnāṃ vidāṃ caiva doṣaḥ śuddhau malodaye /
children.translated_text: Of faith and the like, and of the knowers too, in purification and in the arising of defilements — the fault [would apply to attention];
because of predominance, attention is not declared a faculty. (Abhidh-d 82)

body.text: yoniśo manasikāraḥ khalu śraddhādīnāṃ saṅgībhavati | ayoniśo manasikāro 'pi vedanādīnāṃ rāgādisaṃprayuktānāmiti so 'pi nendriyam ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, proper attention (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>) is a companion of faith and the like. Improper attention too [is a companion] of feelings and the like that are associated with passion and so forth — therefore it too is not a faculty.

body.text: saṃbhāvanānukūlatvādadhimokṣo 'pi nendriyam /
body.translated_text: Because of being favorable to belief (<s>saṃbhāvanā</s>), determination (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) too is not a faculty.

body.text: adhimokṣo 'pi śraddhopakārīti nendriyam ||
body.translated_text: Determination too is a helper of faith — therefore it is not a faculty.

body.text: kālāntaraphalotpādasaṃdehābhyāṃ na cetanā // Abhidh-d_83 //
body.translated_text: Volition (<s>cetanā</s>) is not [a faculty] because of [its fruit arising at] a different time and because of doubt. (Abhidh-d 83)

body.text: cetanāyāḥ khalvapi kālāntareṇa phalamiti tasya nāsati phale śaktirāvirbhavati | lokopi tasyāḥ phalasattvāvināśaṃ dṛṣṭvā vipratipannaḥ | kaścid brūte nirhetukaṃ phalamiti kaścidīśvarakṛtaṃ kaścidadṛṣṭādihetukamiti | cetanāyāḥ phalamanabhivyaktamiti | īśitvaṃ bhagavatā jānānenāpyatastasyāstrailokyakāraṇatve 'pi sati cetanā nendriyeṣu vyavasthāpitā ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, the fruit of volition arises at a different time — therefore its power does not become manifest when the fruit is absent. The world too, seeing the non-destruction of beings [despite their] possessing the fruit [of volition], is confused. Some say the fruit is without cause; some say it is made by God; some say it is caused by unseen [forces] and the like — because the fruit of volition is not manifest. The Blessed One, knowing this [and] even [possessing] sovereignty — nevertheless, even though [volition] is the cause of the triple world, volition was not established among the faculties.

body.text: kuśalamahābhaumebhyo 'pi
body.translated_text: Among the wholesome great-ground [mental factors] too:

children.translated_text: Diligence (<s>apramāda</s>) is not [a faculty] either, because of vigor; nor is modesty (<s>hrī</s>), because of [its] restraint of boldness;
nor equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), nor non-attachment (<s>alobha</s>), because of being overcome by vigor and faith. (Abhidh-d 84)

body.text: apramādastāvadvīryasya bhāṇḍāgārikasthānīyaḥ | vīryaṃ kuśalān dharmānupājeyati satān rakṣati | hrīrapi vaiśāradyasapatnabhūtā navavadhūrivāpragalbhā | tasyāḥ kuta ādhipatyam ? upekṣāpi śraddhābhibhūtā | alobhaśva vīryavirodhīti nendriyam ||
body.translated_text: Diligence is like the treasurer of vigor — vigor guards wholesome dharmas and protects those that exist. Modesty too is like an enemy of boldness, like a shy new bride — how could it have sovereignty? Equanimity too is overcome by faith. And non-attachment is opposed to vigor — therefore it is not a faculty.

body.text: na prasrabdhirvidautkaṭyādvinindyatvācca nāsravāḥ /
body.translated_text: Tranquility (<s>prasrabdhi</s>) is not [a faculty] because of being surpassed by feeling in [mental] excitement; and the outflows are not, because of being blameworthy.

body.text: prasrabdhiḥ khalu vedanāyāḥ vṛttiprādhānyenābhibhūtā | sāpi nendriyam | akuśalānāmapi dharmāṇāṃ vinindyatvāttu nāsravāścaṇḍālarājavat ||
body.translated_text: Tranquility indeed is overcome by feeling in the predominance of [its] functioning. It too is not a faculty. The unwholesome dharmas too are not [faculties], because of being blameworthy — like a <s>caṇḍāla</s>-king.

body.text: viprayuktānāmapi
body.translated_text: Among the disjoined [formations] too:

children.translated_text: Birth and the like are not [faculties], because of serving others —

body.text: paratantrā hi jātyādayo dharmāḥ paricārakavat teṣāṃ kutaḥ prabhutvam ?
body.translated_text: for birth and the like are dharmas dependent on others, like servants — how could they have mastery?

body.text: niṣkriyatvānna nirvṛtiḥ // Abhidh-d_85 //
body.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not [a faculty] because of being without activity. (Abhidh-d 85)

body.text: nirvāṇamapi niṣkriyamasatphalaṃ satkriyāśca dharmāḥ phalavanta ādhipatyayuktā iti bhagavatā nirvāṇaṃ nendriyaṃ vyavasthāpitamiti | nātra kiñcidupasaṃkhyeyaṃ nāpyapaneyamiti ||
body.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> too is without activity; [it is] a non-existent fruit. But dharmas that possess real activity possess fruit and are endowed with sovereignty — therefore <s>nirvāṇa</s> was not established as a faculty by the Blessed One. Nothing here is to be added, nor is anything to be removed.

body.text: lakṣaṇamidānīmindriyāṇāṃ vaktavyam | tatra cakṣurādīnāmuktam | jīvitaśraddhādīnāṃ saṃprayuktaviprayukteṣūcyamāneṣu vakṣyate | duḥkhādīnāṃ tvadhunocyate |
body.translated_text: Now the characteristics of the faculties are to be stated. Those of the eye and the like have been stated. Those of life, faith, and the like will be stated when the associated and disjoined [dharmas] are being discussed. But those of suffering and the like are stated now:

body.text: kāyasya bādhanaṃ duḥkhaṃ daurmanasyaṃ tu cetasaḥ /
body.translated_text: Suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) is affliction of the body; displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) is [affliction] of the mind.

body.text: bādhanamiti vartate ||
body.translated_text: 'Affliction' is to be supplied [in both cases].

body.text: sukhaṃ ca sumanastā ca sātaṃ śārīramānasam // Abhidh-d_86 //
body.translated_text: Pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and mental satisfaction (<s>sumanastā</s>) are agreeableness — bodily and mental respectively. (Abhidh-d 86)

body.text: sātamiti prahlādanāparyāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Agreeableness' (<s>sāta</s>) is a synonym for 'refreshing.'

body.text: vaiśiṣṭyānmānasaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ kvacidudāhṛtam // Abhidh-d_87 //
body.translated_text: Due to its excellence, mental agreeableness is sometimes called 'pleasure.' (Abhidh-d 87)

body.text: tṛtīye dhyāne mānasaṃ sātaṃ sukhamityudāhṛtaṃ bhagavatā pañcendriyasukhātiśayatvāt | saumanasyaṃ tu prītisvabhāvaṃ sā ca tṛtīyadhyāne nāstīti sukhaṃ ca tatroktamiti |..........
body.translated_text: In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, mental agreeableness was called 'pleasure' by the Blessed One, because of surpassing the pleasure of the five [sense-]faculties. But <s>saumanasya</s> (mental satisfaction) has the nature of joy (<s>prīti</s>), and that does not exist in the third <s>dhyāna</s> — therefore 'pleasure' is said there.

body.text: ......... bhaumam tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: ......... of the ground — that is indicated:

body.text: ṣaṭsu bhūmiṣu vijñeyaṃ nīrajaskādyamindriyam /
body.translated_text: The faculty beginning with the 'immaculate' should be known in six grounds. (Abhidh-d [partial])

body.text: anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyaṃ ṣaṭṣu bhūmiṣu, caturṣu dhyāneṣvanāgamye dhyānāntarikāyāṃ ca |
body.translated_text: The 'I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown' faculty is in six grounds — in the four <s>dhyānas</s>, in <s>anāgamya</s> (the access concentration), and in <s>dhyānāntarikā</s> (the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> [ground]).

body.text: tadanye nirmale tvakṣe draṣṭavye navabhūmike // Abhidh-d_88 //
body.translated_text: The other two, being immaculate, should be seen in nine grounds. (Abhidh-d 88)

body.text: ājñendriyamājñātāvīndriyaṃ ca navasu bhamiṣu- āsveva ṣaṭṣu triṣu cādyāsvārūpyabhūmiṣu ||
body.translated_text: The <s>ājñā</s> (knowledge) faculty and the <s>ājñātāvin</s> (one-who-has-known) faculty are in nine grounds — in those same six and in the first three formless-realm grounds.

body.text: atha kāni dvāviṃśatirindriyāṇi kāni rki prahātavyāni ? dudāhriyate-
body.translated_text: Now, which of the twenty-two faculties are to be abandoned by what? It is stated:

children.translated_text: Displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) is to be abandoned in two ways —

body.text: darśanabhāvanāprahātavyam |
body.translated_text: to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśana</s>) and by cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>).

body.text: manovittitrayaṃ tridhā /
body.translated_text: The mental faculty and the three feelings are [to be abandoned] in three ways.

body.text: manaindriyaṃ sukhasaumanasyopekṣāśca darśanabhāvanāheyāścāheyāśca |
body.translated_text: The mind-faculty, pleasure, mental satisfaction, and equanimity are to be abandoned by seeing, by cultivation, and are also not to be abandoned.

children.translated_text: Nine are to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>abhyāsa</s>) —

body.text: cakṣurādīni jīvitāvasānānyaṣṭau duḥkhendriyaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: the eight [faculties] from the eye and the rest up to the life-faculty, and the suffering-faculty.

children.translated_text: Five are twofold —

body.text: śraddhādīni bhāvanāheyānyaheyāni ca | sāsravānāsravāt |
body.translated_text: the [faculties of] faith and the like are to be abandoned by cultivation and are also not to be abandoned — because of being with-outflows and without-outflows [respectively].

body.text: na tu trayam // Abhidh-d_89 //
body.translated_text: But the three are not [to be abandoned]. (Abhidh-d 89)

body.text: trīṇyanāsravāṇyapraheyānyeva nirdoṃṣatvāt ||
body.translated_text: The three outflow-free [faculties] are never to be abandoned — because of being faultless.

body.text: yadi tarhi śraddhādīni sāsravānāsravatvātpraheyāni cāpraheyāni ca dvidhā bhavanti, trayamevānāsravam | idaṃ tarhi sūtraṃ kathaṃ nīyate ? yaduktaṃ bhagavatā- (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 54)

children.text: ) "yasyemāni pañcendriyāṇi sarveṇa sarvaṃ na santi tamahaṃ bāhyaṃ pṛthagjanapakṣāvasthitaṃ vadāmi" iti ?
children.translated_text: 'One who completely lacks these five faculties — him I call an outsider, one standing in the camp of ordinary persons.'

body.translated_text: If then the [faculties of] faith and the like, being both with-outflows and without-outflows, are twofold — to be abandoned and not to be abandoned — and only the three are outflow-free, then how is this sūtra to be interpreted? As the Blessed One said:

body.text: anāsravādhikārādajñāpakametat | anāsravāṇi khalvadhikṛtyaitaduktam | yasmādāryapudgalavyavasthānaṃ kṛtvā "yasyemāni" iti bhagavānavocat | pṛthagjano vā dvividhaḥ | ābhyantaraścāsamucchinnakuśalamūlaḥ, bāhyaśca samucchinnakuśalamūlaḥ | tamadhikṛtyoktam- "bāhyaṃ pṛthagjanapakṣāvasthitaṃ vadāmi" iti | "sarveṇa sarvāṇi" iti vacanādvā 'yasya laukikānyapi na santi'; ityākūtam | bāhyamityaśākyaputrīyaṃ pṛthagjanapakṣāvasthitamityāryadharmavipakṣāvasthitam | anyathā hyevamavakṣyat- 'yasyemāni pañcendriyāṇi na santi tamahaṃ pṛthagjanapakṣāvasthitaṃ vadāmi'; iti | uktaṃ hi- "santrasanti sattvā loke jātā loke vṛddhāstīkṣṇendriyā api madhyendriyā api mṛdvindriyā api" ityapravartita eva dharmacakre | punaścoktam- "yāvaccāhameṣāṃ pañcānāmindriyāṇāṃ samudayaṃ cāstaṅgamaṃ cāsvādaṃ cādīnavaṃ ca niḥsaraṇaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 55)

children.text: ) nāpyajñāsiṣaṃ na tāvadahamasmātsadevakāllokāt" iti vistaraḥ | na cāyamanāsravāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ parīkṣāprakāraḥ |
children.translated_text: I did not [claim] from this world with its gods...' — and so on in detail. And this is not the mode of examining outflow-free dharmas.

body.translated_text: This is indicative, having the outflow-free [faculties] as its subject. Indeed, this was said with reference to the outflow-free [faculties]. Because the Blessed One spoke 'one who has these,' having established [the context of] noble persons. Or, an ordinary person is of two kinds: internal — one whose wholesome roots are not cut off, and external — one whose wholesome roots are cut off. With reference to the latter it was said: 'I call him an outsider, standing in the camp of ordinary persons.' Or, from the expression 'completely all,' the intent is 'one who lacks even the worldly [faculties of faith etc.].' 'Outsider' means not a follower of the <s>Śākya</s>'s son; 'standing in the camp of ordinary persons' means standing in the camp opposed to noble dharmas. Otherwise [the Blessed One] would have said: 'One who lacks these five faculties — him I call one standing in the camp of ordinary persons.' For it was said: 'Beings in the world tremble — those born in the world, those matured [in it] — even those of sharp faculties, even those of middling faculties, even those of soft faculties' — even before the Dharma-wheel was turned. And again it was said: 'As long as I did not know as it truly is the arising, ceasing, gratification, danger, and escape of these five faculties —

body.text: vayaṃ tvatremamāgamaṃ brūmaḥ- "trīṇīmāni śrāddhasya śraddhāliṅgāni" iti vistaraḥ | kathaṃ kṛtvā jñāpakam ? śraddhāyāṃ hyasatyāmāryāṇāṃ darśanakāmatā na bhavet | saddharmaśrotukāmatā ca, vigatamātsaryeṇa cetasā agāramadhyavastukāmatā ca | yasya ca pṛthagjanasyaitānīndriyāṇi na santi sa sarvathā bāhyapṛthagjano bhavati kuśaladharmopaniṣaddhetuvaikalyāt | tasmātsāstravāṇīti siddham ||
body.translated_text: We, however, cite this tradition here: 'These three are the marks of faith of one who has faith' — and so on in detail. How is [this] indicative? Because in the absence of faith, noble ones would not have the desire to see [the truth], the desire to hear the good Dharma, and the desire — with a mind free from selfishness — to renounce household possessions. And the ordinary person who lacks these faculties is entirely an outsider-ordinary-person, because of the deficiency of the causes that support wholesome dharmas. Therefore, [it is] established that they are with-outflows [as well].

body.text: uktaḥ prakārabhedaḥ | lābha idānīṃ vaktavyaḥ | katīndriyāṇi kasmin dhātau vipākaḥ prathamato labhyate ? tadidamārabhyate |
body.translated_text: The distinction of types has been stated. Now the acquisition (<s>lābha</s>) must be stated. How many faculties (<s>indriyas</s>) are obtained as maturation (<s>vipāka</s>) first in which realm? This is now undertaken:

body.text: pūrvaṃ kramodbhavaiḥ kāme vipāko labhyate dvayam /
body.translated_text: In the desire-realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), for those born gradually, maturation is obtained — two [faculties] first.

body.text: kāmadhātau kramodbhavaiḥ - aṇḍajajarāyujasaṃsvedajaiḥ pūrvaṃ indriyadvayaṃ labhyate | kāyendriyaṃ jīvitendriyaṃ ca | etaddhi dvayaṃ tasmin śukraśoṇitabindau prathamaṃ vipākajaṃ bhavati | kliṣṭatvāttu na manaupekṣendriye vipākaḥ |
body.translated_text: In the desire-realm, for those born gradually — egg-born, womb-born, and moisture-born — two faculties are first obtained: the body-faculty (<s>kāyendriya</s>) and the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>). For these two arise first as maturation-born in that drop of semen and blood. But the mind-faculty and equanimity-faculty are not maturation[-born at that point], because of being afflicted.

children.translated_text: For others, six, seven, or eight.

body.text: aupapādukaiḥ punaḥ ṣaṭ | cakṣurādīni pañca jīvitendriyaṃ ca | yadyavyañjanā bhavanti yathā prāthamakalpikaḥ | sapta punaryadyekavyañjanā yathā devādiṣu | aṣṭau vā yadyubhayavyañjanā bhavanti yathāpāyeṣu | evaṃ tāvat kāmadhātau |
body.translated_text: For the spontaneously-born (<s>aupapāduka</s>), however, six: the five [beginning with] the eye and the life-faculty. If they are sexless, like the first-eon beings. Seven, if they are of one sex, as in the case of gods and others. Or eight, if they are of both sexes, as in the lower realms. Thus [it is] in the desire-realm.

children.translated_text: Six in the form-realm.

body.text: rūpadhātau punaḥ ṣaḍindriyāṇi vipākaḥ prathamato labhyante | cakṣurādīni pañca jīvitendriyaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: In the form-realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), six faculties are obtained as maturation first: the five [beginning with] the eye and the life-faculty.

body.text: antye tu jīvitam // Abhidh-d_90 //
body.translated_text: But in the last [realm], only the life-faculty. (Abhidh-d 90)

body.text: ārūpye jīvitendriyaṃ vipāko labhyate | ukto lābhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the formless realm (<s>ārūpya</s>), the life-faculty is obtained as maturation. The acquisition has been stated.

body.text: tyāgo vaktavyaḥ | so 'yamāviṣkriyate-
body.translated_text: The abandonment (<s>tyāga</s>) must be stated. This is made clear:

children.translated_text: For those dying, three cease at the end:

body.text: jīvitam, manaḥ, upekṣā ceti |
body.translated_text: the life-faculty, mind, and equanimity.

body.text: aṣṭau tu madhyame /
body.translated_text: But eight in the middle [realm].

body.text: rūpadhātau mriyamāṇairaṣṭau nirudhyante | tāni ca trīṇi, cakṣurādīni ca pañca |
body.translated_text: In the form-realm, eight cease for those dying: those three, plus the five [beginning with] the eye.

body.text: daśāṣṭau nava catvāri kāme pañca śubhāni vā // Abhidh-d_91 //
body.translated_text: Ten, eight, nine, four in the desire-realm; or five wholesome [faculties]. (Abhidh-d 91)

body.text: ubhayavyañjanairdaśa nirodhyante | tāni cāṣṭau strīpuruṣendriye ca | ekavyañjanairnava | avyañjanairaṣṭau | sakṛnmaraṇe khalveṣa nyāyaḥ | krameṇa tu mriyamāṇaiścatvāri nirodhyante kāyajīvitamanaupekṣendriyāṇi | na hyeṣāṃ pṛthaṅnirodhaḥ | epa ca vidhiḥ kliṣṭāvyākṛtacittasya maraṇe draṣṭavyaḥ | kuśale tu citte sarvatra śraddhādīni pañcādhikāni | evamārūpyeṣvaṣṭau, rūpeṣu trayodaśa | ityevaṃ vistareṇa gaṇayitavyāni ||
body.translated_text: For those of both sexes, ten cease: those eight plus the female and male faculties. For those of one sex, nine. For the sexless, eight. This rule applies in the case of single-moment death. But for those dying gradually, four cease: body, life, mind, and equanimity faculties — for there is no separate cessation of these. And this rule is to be seen in the case of death with afflicted or indeterminate consciousness. But with wholesome consciousness, everywhere five additional [faculties cease] — faith and the others. Thus in the formless realm, eight; in the form-realm, thirteen. In this way the count should be elaborated.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau dvitīyasyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the first section of the second chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: dvitīyādhyāye
body.translated_text: Second chapter,

body.text: dvitīyapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: second section.

body.text: indriyaprastāve sarva indriyadharmā vicāryanta ityataḥ pṛcchati | athaiṣāṃ kuśalānāmindriyāṇāṃ katareṇendriyeṇa kataracchrāmaṇyaphalaṃ prāpyata iti ? tadidaṃ prastūyate-
body.translated_text: In the context of the faculties, all dharmas related to the faculties are examined; therefore the question is asked: By which faculty is which fruit of the ascetic life (<s>śrāmaṇyaphala</s>) attained? This is now discussed:

body.text: ādyantalābho navabhiḥ saptāṣṭābhiśca madhyayoḥ /
body.translated_text: The first and last [fruits] are attained by nine [faculties]; the middle two by seven, eight [or nine].

body.text: yā khalveṣā catuṣphalamayī mālā tasyāḥ prathamaṃ strotaāpattiphalamantyamarhattvaṃ madhye sakṛdāgāmyanāgāmiphale | tatrādyāntayoḥ phalayornavabhirindriyairlābhaḥ | strotaāpattiphalasya tāvat- śraddhādibhiḥ pañcabhirājñāsyāmīndriyājñendriyābhyāmekamanayorānantaryamārgād, dvitīyaṃ vimuktimārgādveditavyam | prathamena kleśaprāpticchedo dvitīyena visaṃyogaprāptyākarṣaṇam | manaupekṣendriyābhyāṃ ceti | arhattvasya punaḥ śraddhādibhirājñāsyāmīndriyavarjjaiḥ, manaindriyeṇa sukhasaumanasyopekṣendriyāṇāṃ cānyatamena |
body.translated_text: This garland consisting of four fruits — its first is the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpatti</s>), its last is <s>Arhatship</s> (<s>arhattva</s>), and the middle are the fruits of once-return (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>) and non-return (<s>anāgāmin</s>). Of these, the first and last fruits are attained by nine faculties. For the fruit of stream-entry: by the five [beginning with] faith, by the 'I-shall-come-to-know' faculty (<s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s>), and by the 'one-who-knows' faculty (<s>ājñendriya</s>) — one of these [last two] from the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), the second from the liberation path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>); by the first, the severance of the acquisition of afflictions; by the second, the attraction of the acquisition of disjoining (<s>visaṃyogaprāpti</s>); and by the mind and equanimity faculties. For <s>Arhatship</s>, however: by the [five] faith and others, excluding the 'I-shall-come-to-know' faculty; by the mind-faculty; and by one among the pleasure, joy, or equanimity faculties.

body.text: 'saptāṣṭābhiśca madhyayoḥ |'; sakṛdāgāmyanāgāmiphalayoḥ punaḥ saptabhiraṣṭābhirnavabhiśceti 'ca'śabdāt | tatra sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ tāvadyadyānupūrviko labhate, sa ca laukikena mārgeṇa tasya saptabhirlābhaḥ | pañcabhiḥ (

children.translated_text: [Reference:] Jaini p. 58.

children.text: ) śraddhādibhiḥ, manaupekṣendribhyāṃ ca | atha lokottareṇa mārgeṇa tasyāṣṭābhiḥ, ājñendriyamaṣṭamaṃ bhavati | atha bhūyovītarāgaḥ prāpnoti, tasya navabhiryaireva strotaāpattiphalasya | anāgāmiphalaṃ yadyānupūrvīkaḥ prāpnoti, sa ca laukikena mārgeṇa, tasya saptabhiryathā sakṛdāgāmiphalasya |
children.translated_text: The fruit of non-return: if one attains it sequentially, and by the mundane path, for that one by seven — as for the fruit of once-return.

body.translated_text: 'The middle two by seven, eight, [or nine]' — for the fruits of once-return and non-return, by seven, eight, or nine — the word 'ca' [implies the additional option]. The fruit of once-return: if one attains it sequentially, and by the mundane path — for that one, attainment is by seven: by the five [beginning with] faith, and by mind and equanimity faculties. But if by the supramundane path, for that one by eight — the 'one-who-knows' faculty becomes the eighth. But if one who has already become dispassionate attains it, for that one by nine — by those very [faculties] as for stream-entry.

body.text: atha lokottareṇa, tasyāṣṭābhistathaiva | atha vītarāgaḥ prāpnoti, tasya navabhiryathā strotaāpattiphalasya | tasya tu niśrayaviśeṣāt sukhasaumanasyopekṣendriyāṇāmanyatamadbhavati | yadāpyayamānupūrviko navame vimuktimārge dhyānaṃ praviśati laukikena mārgeṇa, tadāpyaṣṭābhirindriyairanāgāmiphalaṃ labhate | tasya navame vimuktimārge saumanasyamaṣṭamaṃ bhavati, ānantaryamārge tūpekṣendriyameva | nityamubhābhyāṃ hi tasya prāptiḥ | atha lokottareṇa praviśati, tasya navabhirājñendriyaṃ navamaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: But if by the supramundane [path], for that one by eight, likewise. But if one already dispassionate attains it, for that one by nine — as for stream-entry. But due to the distinction of support, one among the pleasure, joy, or equanimity faculties [is involved]. And when this sequential practitioner enters <s>dhyāna</s> on the ninth liberation path by the mundane path, then too the fruit of non-return is attained by eight faculties; for him on the ninth liberation path, joy becomes the eighth, but on the uninterrupted path only the equanimity faculty [is present]; for always by both [paths] is his attainment. But if he enters by the supramundane [path], for him by nine — the 'one-who-knows' faculty becomes the ninth.

body.text: yattarhyabhidharme paṭhyate- "arhatphalasyaikādaśabhiḥ" iti | tatkathamucyate 'navabhistasya prāptiḥ'; iti ? naiva doṣaḥ | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: As to what is recited in the <s>Abhidharma</s>: 'The fruit of Arhatship by eleven' — how then is it said 'its attainment is by nine'? There is no fault at all. Because:

body.text: ekādaśabhirāptistu phalasyāntyasya hānitaḥ // Abhidh-d_92 //
body.translated_text: The attainment of the last fruit is by eleven due to falling away. (Abhidh-d 92)

body.text: parihāya parihāyāyaṃ samayavimukto 'rhanniśrayaviśeṣātpunarlabhate | kadācit tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ niśritya | kadācid dvitīyaṃ prathamaṃ vā | kadāciccaturthamanāgamyaṃ vā | ityatastisṛṇāṃ vedanānāṃ saṃbhavādekādaśabhiruktam ||
body.translated_text: This time-liberated (<s>samayavimukta</s>) <s>Arhat</s>, having fallen away and fallen away, attains again due to the distinction of support. Sometimes relying on the third <s>dhyāna</s>, sometimes the second or first, sometimes the fourth or the 'access' (<s>anāgamya</s>). Therefore, because of the possibility of three feelings, it is stated as 'by eleven.'

body.text: athaiṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ kāmarūpārūpyadhātūnāṃ kataradhātubhūmyālambanena mārgeṇa katarasya dhātoḥ parijñānaṃ bhavatīti ? tadāvirbhāvyate |
body.translated_text: Now, by a path directed at which realm and level, does the full knowledge (<s>parijñāna</s>) of which realm occur among these three — desire-realm, form-realm, and formless realm? This is made clear:

body.text: svasya dhātoḥ parijñānaṃ svavipakṣadṛśā pathā // Abhidh-d_93 //
body.translated_text: Full knowledge of one's own realm [occurs] by the path that sees one's own [realm] and its opposite. (Abhidh-d 93)

body.text: svavipakṣadṛśā ca mārgeṇānāsraveṇa parijñānaṃ bhavati | tatra svadhātudṛśā tāvad duḥkhasamudayālambanena, svavipakṣadṛśā nirodhamārgālambanena traidhātukaparijñānaṃ bhavati | sāsraveṇa tvānantaryamārgeṇa saṃgṛhītena sannikṛṣṭādhobhūmiviṣayeṇordhvasannikṛṣṭabhūmyālambanena ca vimuktimārgasaṃgṛhītenādhobhūmiparijñānaṃ bhavati | ānantaryamārgāṇāmadhobhūmiviṣayatvādvimuktyākhyānāmūrdhvabhūmyālambanatvācca | anāsravāṇāṃ tūbhayeṣāmekabhūmigocaratvāditi |
body.translated_text: Full knowledge occurs by the path that is uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>) and that sees one's own [realm] and its opposite. Therein, by the [path] seeing one's own realm — that which has the truths of suffering and origination as its object; by the [path] seeing its opposite — that which has cessation and the path as its object — full knowledge of all three realms occurs. But by the contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>) uninterrupted path, [which has] the immediately lower level as its object, and by the liberation path [which has] the immediately higher level as its object — full knowledge of the lower level occurs. Because uninterrupted paths have the lower level as their object, while liberation paths have the higher level as their object. But for the uncontaminated [paths], both types have a single level as their range.

body.text: atha katibhīrindriyaiḥ kāmadhātuparijñānaṃ katibhī rūpārūpyadhātuparijñānamiti ? tadidaṃ pratāyate-
body.translated_text: Now, by how many faculties does full knowledge of the desire-realm occur? By how many, full knowledge of the form and formless realms? This is made clear:

children.translated_text: Full knowledge of the desire-realm is generally held [to be] by seven.
But it is stated as by eight with the uncontaminated [faculties]. (Abhidh-d 94)

body.text: kāmadhātostāvat- sāsravaiḥ saptabhiḥ parijñānaṃ bhavati prahāṇamityarthaḥ | pañcabhiḥ śraddhādibhiḥ manaupekṣendriyābhyāṃ ca | prāyo grahaṇātsaumanasyendriyeṇāpi kasyacitsamāpattyabhiprāyasya yogino maulabhūmipraveśāt | anāsravaistvindriyairaṣṭābhiḥ | ebhireva saptabhirājñedriyeṇa ca | prāyo vacanātsaumanasyendriyeṇa ca navamena ||
body.translated_text: For the desire-realm: full knowledge, meaning abandonment, occurs by seven contaminated [faculties] — by the five [beginning with] faith, and by the mind and equanimity faculties. The word 'generally' [implies:] also by the joy faculty, for a certain <s>yogin</s> intent on attainment, due to entering the basic level. By uncontaminated faculties, however, by eight — by those very seven plus the 'one-who-knows' faculty. [And because of the word] 'generally,' also by the joy faculty as the ninth.

body.text: rūpadhātuparijñānamiṣṭaṃ daśabhirindriyaiḥ /
body.translated_text: Full knowledge of the form-realm is held [to be] by ten faculties.

body.text: pañcabhiḥ śraddhādibhiḥ, mana indriyeṇa, tisṛbhirvedanābhiḥ, niśrayaviśeṣādājñendriyeṇa ca ||
body.translated_text: By the five [beginning with] faith, the mind-faculty, the three feelings, and the 'one-who-knows' faculty due to distinction of support.

body.text: antyadhātuparijñānamekādaśabhirucyate // Abhidh-d_95 //
body.translated_text: Full knowledge of the last realm is stated as by eleven. (Abhidh-d 95)

body.text: yathoktairdaśabhirājñātavadindriyeṇa ca | ubhābhyāṃ tasya parijñānamekaṃ vajropamasamādhisahacaram, dvitīyaṃ kṣayajñānasahagatamiti ||
body.translated_text: By the ten as stated, plus the 'one-who-has-fully-known' faculty (<s>ājñātāvadīndriya</s>). Its full knowledge is twofold: one is accompanied by the diamond-like concentration (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>), the second is accompanied by the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>).

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam- kaḥ katibhirindriyaiḥ samanvāgata iti ? tatra tāvadayaṃ niyamaḥ-
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: Who is possessed of how many faculties? First, there is this rule:

body.text: sarvasattvāstridhātusthā upekṣāyurmano 'nvitāḥ /
body.translated_text: All beings in the three realms are endowed with equanimity, life, and mind.

body.text: ebhistribhiḥ sarvasattvāḥ samanvāgatāḥ |
body.translated_text: All beings are possessed of these three. For there is no possession of any without the others. The rest are not fixed.

children.translated_text: In the desire-realm, [also] with skin, femininity, and [male] characteristics.

body.text: kāmāvacarāḥ sattvāḥ kāyapuruṣastrīndriyairebhiḥ pūrvāktaśca |
body.translated_text: Beings in the desire-realm [are possessed] of body, male, and female faculties — these and also those previously stated.

body.text: rūpiṇaścakṣurādibhiḥ // Abhidh-d_96 //
body.translated_text: Those with form [are possessed] of the eye and so forth. (Abhidh-d 96)

body.text: rūpiṇaḥ khalu sattvāścakṣurādibhistribhiścopekṣāyurmanobhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Beings with form are [possessed] of the three — eye and so forth — plus equanimity, life, and mind.

body.text: kāminaḥ khalu duḥkhena tadrāgī durmanastayā /
body.translated_text: One in the desire-realm [is possessed] of suffering; one with desire [of that realm], of displeasure.

body.text: avītarāgaḥ kāmadhātau duḥkhadaurmanasyābhyāṃ samanvāgataḥ |
body.translated_text: One not yet freed from passion in the desire-realm is possessed of suffering and displeasure.

body.text: ūrdhvajastu sukhenāryaḥ śubhāhvādharajau tathā // Abhidh-d_97 //
body.translated_text: But one born above, [if] noble, [is possessed] of pleasure; those born below the 'Good' [realms are possessed] likewise. (Abhidh-d 97)

body.text: ūrdhvajo rūpārūpyadhātuja āryaḥ sukhena samanvāgataḥ | anāsraveṇa śubhakṛtsnaparīttaśubhāpramāṇaśubhāḥ kliṣṭākliṣṭena ||
body.translated_text: One born above — born in the form or formless realm — [if] a noble being (<s>ārya</s>) — is possessed of pleasure, by the uncontaminated [path]. Those [born in the levels] below the 'Pure Abodes' (<s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>) — the 'Limited Good' and 'Immeasurable Good' [levels] — [are possessed of pleasure] by the afflicted and unafflicted [types].

children.translated_text: By joy, one born in or below the 'Radiant' [realms].

body.text: ābhāsvareṣūpapannastadadharajaśca prītyā samanvāgataḥ |
body.translated_text: One born in the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> [heavens], or born below them, is possessed of joy.

body.text: śubhaiḥ sa śubhamūlakaḥ /
body.translated_text: By the wholesome [faculties], one who has wholesome roots.

body.text: śraddhādibhiḥ pañcabhiḥ kuśalairanucchinnakuśalamūlaḥ sarvatra samanvāgataḥ |
body.translated_text: By the five wholesome [faculties beginning with] faith — one whose wholesome roots are not destroyed is possessed [of them] everywhere.

children.translated_text: By the two learner's [faculties], one on the path of liberation.

body.text: dvābhyāṃ śaikṣābhyāṃ indriyābhyāṃ darśanabhāvanāmārgasthau ||
body.translated_text: By the two learner's (<s>śaikṣa</s>) faculties — one stationed on the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) or the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>).

body.text: aśaikṣo 'rhan svamārgagaḥ // Abhidh-d_98 //
body.translated_text: The non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) — an <s>Arhat</s> — on his own path. (Abhidh-d 98)

body.text: atha niyamena kaḥ katibhirindriyaiḥ samanvāgata iti ? tadidamupadarśyate-
body.translated_text: Now, necessarily, who is possessed of how many faculties? This is shown:

body.text: upekṣāyurmanoyukto 'vaśyaṃ trayasamanvitaḥ /
body.translated_text: One endowed with equanimity, life, and mind is necessarily possessed of [at least] three.

body.text: ebhireva tribhiḥ | na hyeṣāmanyonyena vinā samanvāgataḥ | śeṣairaniyamaḥ |
body.translated_text: By these very three. For one is not possessed of any of these without the others. The rest are not fixed.

body.text: tatra tāvaccakṣurādibhiḥ saptabhirārūpyopapanno na samanvāgataḥ | kāmadhātau ca yenāpratilabdhavihīnāni | sukhendriyeṇa caturthadhyānādyupapannāḥ pṛthagjanāḥ, saumanasyena tṛtīyādyupapannāḥ pṛthagjanāḥ, sukhendriyeṇa rūpārūpyopapannāḥ, daurmanasyena kāmavītarāgaḥ, śraddhādibhirniḥśubhaḥ, anāsravaestribhiḥ pṛthagjanā na samanvāgatāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein: one born in the formless realm is not possessed of the seven [beginning with] the eye. In the desire-realm also, [those faculties] that are unacquired or lost. Ordinary persons born in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and above [are not possessed] of the pleasure-faculty; ordinary persons born in the third [<s>dhyāna</s>] and above, of the joy-faculty; those born in the form and formless [realms], of the pleasure-faculty; one freed from desire-realm [passion], of displeasure; one whose wholesome roots are destroyed, of the five [beginning with] faith; ordinary persons, of the three uncontaminated [faculties] — [they] are not possessed [of these].

children.translated_text: One possessing the body [faculty is possessed] of four.

body.text: yaḥ kāyendriyeṇa so 'vaśyaṃ caturbhistaiśca tribhiḥ kāyendriyeṇa ca | yo 'pi sukhandriyeṇa sa caturbhiḥ- taiśca tribhirupekṣādibhiḥ sukhendriyeṇa ca |
body.translated_text: One who possesses the body-faculty is necessarily [possessed] of four — those three plus the body-faculty. One who possesses the pleasure-faculty is also [possessed] of four — those three (equanimity and the rest) plus the pleasure-faculty.

body.text: cakṣuṣmānapi pañcabhiḥ // Abhidh-d_99 //
body.translated_text: One possessing sight is [possessed] of five. (Abhidh-d 99)

body.text: 'api'śabdācchotraghrāṇajihvendriyairveditavyam | yaścakṣurindriyeṇa so 'vaśyaṃ pañcabhiḥ- upekṣājīvitamanorūpendriyaiścakṣuṣā ca ||
body.translated_text: From the word 'also' (<s>api</s>), [this applies] to the ear, nose, and tongue faculties as well. One who possesses the eye-faculty is necessarily [possessed] of five: equanimity, life, mind, form-faculty, and the eye.

children.translated_text: One possessed of the female faculty and so forth — of eight.

body.text: taiśca saptabhiḥ strīṃndriyeṇa ca | ādigrahaṇāt puruṣendriyadaurmanasyaśraddhādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ veditavyam | tadvānapi pratyekamaṣṭābhiḥ- taiśca saptabhiḥ puruṣendriyeṇa cāṣṭamena | ebhiśca kāyajīvitamanobhiścatasṛbhirvedanābhiḥ, daurmanasyendriyeṇa ca | śraddhā dibhistaiśca pañcabhirupekṣājīvitamanobhiśca |
body.translated_text: [Possessed] of those seven plus the female faculty. From the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), the inclusion of the male faculty, displeasure, and the five [beginning with] faith should be understood. One possessing any of these is also [possessed] of eight individually — those seven plus the male faculty as the eighth; or those [including] body, life, mind, and the four feelings, plus the displeasure faculty; or the five faith and so forth plus equanimity, life, and mind.

body.text: duḥkhī yuktastu saptabhiḥ /
body.translated_text: But one in pain is possessed of seven.

body.text: yo duḥkhena sa saptabhiḥ- kāyajītimanobhiścatasṛbhirvedanendriyairdaurmanasyaṃ hitvā, tadvītarāgasya nāstīti |
body.translated_text: One with suffering [is possessed] of seven: body, life, mind, and the four feeling-faculties excluding displeasure — because that does not exist for one freed from passion [of the desire-realm].

children.translated_text: By the last two [faculties] — of eleven.

body.text: dvābhyāmantyābhyāṃ yukto 'vaśyamekādaśabhiḥ, pratyekaṃ sukhasaumanasyopekṣājīvitamanaḥśraddhādibhirājñendriyeṇa ca | evamājñātavadindriyeṇa tena taiśceti |
body.translated_text: One endowed with the last two [faculties] is necessarily [possessed] of eleven: individually, [including] pleasure, joy, equanimity, life, mind, the five [beginning with] faith, and the 'one-who-knows' faculty. Likewise with the 'one-who-has-fully-known' faculty — with that and those [eleven].

body.text: sapta ṣaḍbhistadādyavān // Abhidh-d_100 //
body.translated_text: One possessing the first [uncontaminated faculty is possessed] of seven or six. (Abhidh-d 100)

body.text: prathamena tvanāsraveṇa yaḥ samanvāgataḥ so 'vaśyaṃ trayodaśabhirmanojīvitakāyendriyaiścatasṛbhirvedanābhiḥ śraddhādibhistena ceti ||
body.translated_text: But one who is possessed of the first uncontaminated [faculty] is necessarily [possessed] of thirteen: mind, life, body faculties, the four feelings, the five [beginning with] faith, and that [first uncontaminated faculty].

body.text: atha sarvabahubhiḥ kiyadbhiḥ samanvāgatāḥ ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now, with all [faculties] or with many — with how many are [beings] endowed? This is stated:

children.translated_text: Those born in the three continents and in the hells, and those fixed in wrong [view] (<s>mithyātvaniyata</s>) —
at most are endowed with nineteen, and at fewest with eight. (Abhidh-d 101)
Intermediate-existence beings (<s>antarābhavika</s>), hungry ghosts (<s>preta</s>), animals (<s>tiryak</s>), and those following faith (<s>śraddhānusārin</s>) —
are endowed with ten plus three more, or with ten plus nine more. (Abhidh-d 102)

body.text: svalpaistrayodaśabhī rūpabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ śraddhādibhiśca jīvitamanaupekṣābhiśca | nārakasya tūcchinnaśubhabījasya cakṣurādīni pañcaikaṃ vyañjanaṃ vedanāśca pañca jīvitaṃ manaśca | tiraścāṃ nāstyucchedaḥ | ya ihocchinatti so 'vaśyamavīciṃ gacchati | tena natra narake śraddhādyā na santi | pañca cakṣurādīni pañca ca vedā, ekaṃ vyañjanaṃ jīvitaṃ manaśceti trayodaśa bhavanti | syurbahubhiścāntarābhavikādyāḥ pṛthagjanāstrīṇyamalāni hitvaikānnaviṃśatibhiḥ, āryāstu śraddhānusāriṇo dve amale hitvaikaṃ ca vyañjanamityekānnaviṃśatibhireva samanvāgatāḥ ||
body.translated_text: At fewest, with thirteen: five form [faculties], five beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), and life (<s>jīvita</s>), mind (<s>manas</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). But for a hell-being whose wholesome seeds have been cut off: the five [faculties] of eye and so forth, one sex-characteristic (<s>vyañjana</s>), five feelings (<s>vedanā</s>), life, and mind. Among animals there is no cutting off [of wholesome roots]; one who cuts off here necessarily goes to <s>Avīci</s>. Therefore, in that [animal realm], there are no [faculties] beginning with faith and the like. Five [faculties] of eye and so forth, five feelings, one sex-characteristic, life, and mind — these are thirteen. At most, the intermediate-existence beings and so forth, being ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), excluding the three impurities (<s>amala</s>), are endowed with nineteen. But noble ones (<s>ārya</s>), being followers of faith (<s>śraddhānusārin</s>), excluding the two impurities and one sex-characteristic, are endowed with exactly nineteen.

children.text: samyaktvaniyatā ye tu ye ca śraddhādhimuktikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are fixed in rightness (<s>samyaktvaniyata</s>), and those who are faith-liberated (<s>śraddhādhimukti</s>) —
they are endowed with eleven, or with ten plus nine more. (Abhidh-d 103)

body.text: tatra samyaktvaniyatā āryā ityarthaḥ | te pañcabhiḥ śraddhādibhirmanojīvitābhyāṃ ca tisṛbhirvedanābhirekena cānāsraveṇa | sarvaprabhūtaiḥ punarekānnaviṃśatibhirekaliṅgadvyamalavarjitaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, 'those fixed in rightness' means noble ones (<s>ārya</s>). They [are endowed] with five beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), mind (<s>manas</s>) and life (<s>jīvita</s>), three feelings (<s>vedanā</s>), and one undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) [faculty]. With all faculties at maximum, [they are endowed] with nineteen, excluding one sex-characteristic and two impurities.

children.translated_text: Those called the wisdom-liberated (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>) <s>arhat</s>, the body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣin</s>), and the one named 'both' (<s>ubhaya</s>) —
are endowed with eleven faculties, or else with eighteen. (Abhidh-d 104)

body.text: sarvālpairekādaśabhiḥ śraddhādibhiḥ sukhasaumanasyopekṣājīvitamanobhirekena cānāsraveṇa | bahubhistvaṣṭādaśabhiḥ, dve anāsrave daurmanasyamekaṃ ca vyañjanaṃ hitvā ||
body.translated_text: At fewest with eleven: five beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), joy (<s>saumanasya</s>), equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), life (<s>jīvita</s>), mind (<s>manas</s>), and one undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) [faculty]. At most with eighteen: excluding the two undefiled [faculties], displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>), and one sex-characteristic.

body.text: kāmadevā mṛtāḥ svalpairdaśabhiḥ saptakādhikaiḥ /
body.translated_text: Beings in the desire-realm heavens who have died — at fewest with ten plus seven more —

body.text: anāsravatrayaṃ hitvā daurmanasyaṃ ca | tatratyaḥ pṛthagjano yadi vairāgyaṃ gacchati sa devarṣirbhavati | ekaṃ ca vyañjanaṃ hitvā pariśiṣṭaiḥ saptadaśabhiḥ samanvāgataḥ |
body.translated_text: excluding the three undefiled [faculties] and displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>). If an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) there attains dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), he becomes a divine sage (<s>devarṣi</s>). Excluding one sex-characteristic, he is endowed with the remaining seventeen.

body.text: ta evaikonaviṃśatyā yuktā bahubhirindriyaiḥ // Abhidh-d_105 //
body.translated_text: Those same [beings] are endowed at most with nineteen faculties. (Abhidh-d 105)

body.text: dve anāsrave hitvaikaṃ ca vyañjanam | atrāpi hi satyāni dṛśyante ||
body.translated_text: Excluding the two undefiled [faculties] and one sex-characteristic. Here too, truths are indeed seen.

body.text: dvirdhyāna jāstu sarvālpairdaśabhiḥ pañcakādhikaiḥ /
body.translated_text: Those born in the two [lower] <s>dhyānas</s> — at fewest with ten plus five more —

body.text: prathamadvitīyadhyānopapannānāṃ pṛthagjanānāṃ duḥkhadaurmanasye hitvā dve ca vyañjane trīṇi cāmalāni, pañcadaśabhiḥ samanvāgamaḥ |
body.translated_text: for ordinary persons born in the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>, excluding pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>), the two sex-characteristics, and the three impurities — they are endowed with fifteen.

body.text: daśabhiḥ sacatuṣkaistu śubhakṛtsnāḥ samanvitāḥ // Abhidh-d_106 //
body.translated_text: Those in the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> [heaven] are endowed with ten plus four. (Abhidh-d 106)

body.text: śubhakṛtsneṣu pṛthagjanasya saumanasyaṃ ca hitvā caturdaśabhiḥ samanvāgamaḥ |
body.translated_text: For an ordinary person in the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> [heavens], excluding joy (<s>saumanasya</s>) as well, he is endowed with fourteen.

body.text: bṛhatphalā hi atyalpaistrayodaśabhiranvitāḥ /
body.translated_text: Those in <s>Bṛhatphala</s> [heaven] indeed — at very fewest with thirteen —

body.text: bṛhatphaleṣu pṛthagjanasya sukhaṃ ca hitvā duḥkhādīni pūrvoktāni trayodaśa bhavanti |
body.translated_text: for an ordinary person in <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, excluding pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) as well, and the previously mentioned [exclusions beginning with] pain — there are thirteen.

body.text: yuktāḥ ṣoḍaśabhistvete sarvabhūribhindriyaiḥ // Abhidh-d_107 //
body.translated_text: But these [beings] are endowed with sixteen when possessing all abundant faculties. (Abhidh-d 107)

body.text: yadyāryā bhavanti teṣāṃ sukhasaumanasyābhyāmanāsravābhyāṃ samanvāgama iti ṣoḍaśa bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: If they are noble ones (<s>ārya</s>), then with pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), joy (<s>saumanasya</s>), and the undefiled [faculties], they are endowed — thus there are sixteen.

body.text: aṣṭābhirdaśabhiḥ saikairārūpyāḥ svalpabhūribhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Those in the formless realm (<s>ārūpya</s>) — at fewest with eight, at most with ten plus one —

body.text: svalpairaṣṭābhiḥ | pṛthagjanasyāṣṭāḥ svalpāni bhavanti | pañca śraddhādīni, jīvitaṃ manaupekṣā ca | bahubhirekādaśabhirāryasya samanvāgamaḥ | pañcabhiḥ śraddhādibhiḥ, dvābhyāṃ sukhasaumanasyābhyāmanāsravābhyām, jīvitamanaupekṣendriyaiścaturbhiranāsraveṇa caikena |
body.translated_text: at fewest with eight: for an ordinary person there are eight minimal [faculties] — five beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), life (<s>jīvita</s>), mind (<s>manas</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). At most, a noble one (<s>ārya</s>) is endowed with eleven: five beginning with faith, two — pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and joy (<s>saumanasya</s>) — that are undefiled, and four — life, mind, equanimity — and one undefiled [faculty].

body.text: sadevakauravāḥ sattvāstrayodaśabhiranvitāḥ // Abhidh-d_108 //
body.translated_text: All beings, including gods and those of <s>Kuru</s>, are endowed with thirteen. (Abhidh-d 108)

body.text: pañcabhiḥ śraddhādibhiḥ pañcabhiḥ sukhādibhiḥ, kāyamanojīvitaiśca tribhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: With five beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), five beginning with pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), and three — body (<s>kāya</s>), mind (<s>manas</s>), and life (<s>jīvita</s>).

body.text: aṣṭābhirniḥśubho yukto daśabhirvā trayādhikaiḥ /
body.translated_text: One devoid of wholesome [roots] is endowed with eight, or with ten plus three more —

body.text: ucchinnaśubhamūlo niḥśubhaḥ sarvālpairaṣṭābhiḥ samanvāgataḥ | sukhādibhiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāyajīvitamanobhiśca | sarvaprabhūtaistu trayodaśabhiryathoktairaṣṭābhiścakṣurādibhiścaturbhirekena ca vyañjanena |
body.translated_text: one whose wholesome roots are cut off — 'devoid of wholesome' — is endowed at fewest with eight: five beginning with pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), and body (<s>kāya</s>), life (<s>jīvita</s>), and mind (<s>manas</s>). At maximum with thirteen — the stated eight, plus four [faculties] of eye and so forth, and one sex-characteristic.

body.text: dviliṅgāḥ paścimaiḥ svalpairviśatyāpyekayā param // Abhidh-d_109 //
body.translated_text: Those with both sex-characteristics — at fewest with the last-stated [number], with twenty at most. (Abhidh-d 109)

body.text: ubhayavyañjanastrayodaśabhiḥ svalpaiḥ sukhādibhiḥ kāyajīvitamanobhiḥ śraddhādibhiśca pañcabhiḥ | cakṣurādīnāmalabdhavihīnatvādaniyamaḥ | sarvabahubhistvekonaviṃśatibhistrīṇyamalānyapāsya | samāpto 'yaṃ matsyakagranthasamudraḥ |
body.translated_text: One possessing both sex-characteristics (<s>ubhayavyañjana</s>), at fewest with thirteen: pleasure and the other [feelings], body, life, mind, and five beginning with faith. Regarding [the faculties of] eye and so forth, there is no fixed rule since one may lack them or not have obtained them. At most with nineteen, excluding the three impurities. This ocean of the fish-like treatise is completed.

body.text: vyākhyāta indriyāṇāṃ dhātugatiprabhedapradarśanāgatānāṃ vistareṇa prabhedaḥ | adhunā tu momāṃsyate | kimete saṃskṛtā dharmā yathā bhinnasvabhāvāḥ, evaṃ bhinnotpādā atha niyatasahotpādā api kecidvidyanta iti ? vidyanta ityāha |
body.translated_text: The detailed classification of faculties — arriving at through the exposition of their <s>dhātu</s>, <s>gati</s> (destiny), and division — has been explained. Now, however, this is investigated: Are these conditioned <s>dharmas</s>, just as they are of different intrinsic natures, also of different arising, or are there some that are necessarily of co-arising? There are, he says.

body.text: tatra saṃkṣepeṇa pañcemā dharmajātayaḥ- rūpaṃ cittaṃ caitasikāścittaviprayuktā asaṃskṛtaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: Therein, in brief, there are five classes of <s>dharmas</s>: form (<s>rūpa</s>), consciousness (<s>citta</s>), mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>), factors dissociated from consciousness (<s>cittaviprayukta</s>), and the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>).

body.text: tatrāsaṃskṛtaṃ nodeti na ca vyeti |
body.translated_text: Therein, the unconditioned does not arise and does not perish.

body.text: rūpiṇāṃ tu dharmāṇāmayaṃ niyamaḥ-
body.translated_text: But for material (<s>rūpin</s>) <s>dharmas</s>, this is the rule:

children.translated_text: An atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>), when external, is inseparable from seven substances;
in the desire realm, one additional [substance accompanies it] in the body, and two additional in [the domains of] the eye and so forth. (Abhidh-d 110)

body.text: sarvasūkṣmaḥ khalu rūpasaṃskāropādānasaṃcayabhedaparyantaḥ paramāṇuriti prajñāpyate | sa tu saptadravyāvinirbhāgī caturbhirbhūtaistribhiścopādāyarūpaistribhistribhirvā bhūtaiścaturbhiścopādāyarūpairavinirbhāgavartyasāvaṣṭama iti |
body.translated_text: The most subtle [unit] of form (<s>rūpa</s>) — the ultimate limit of the division of the composite of conditioned formations — is designated as an atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>). It is inseparable from seven substances: the four great elements (<s>bhūta</s>) and three derivative forms (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>) — or three great elements and four derivative forms — being inseparable [in combination], it constitutes the eighth [substance].

body.text: kośakārastvāha- "sarvasūkṣmo rūpasaṃghātaḥ paramāṇuḥ" iti | tena saṃghātavyatiriktaṃ rūpamanyadvaktavyam | yadi nāsti saṃghāto 'pi nāsti | ataḥ siddhaṃ 'sarvasūkṣmaṃ rūpaparamāṇuḥ'; iti ||
body.translated_text: But the author of the <s>Kośa</s> says: 'The most subtle aggregate of form is the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>).' Accordingly, form other than the aggregate must be stated. If none exists, then the aggregate too does not exist. Therefore it is established: 'the most subtle form is the atom.'

body.text: kāyedriyasahagastvaṣṭābhiścakṣurādisahito navabhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: But [an atom] accompanied by the body-faculty is [inseparable from] eight [substances]; and accompanied by [a faculty of] eye and so forth, [inseparable from] nine.

body.text: evaṃ rūpe 'pi vijñeyo hitvā gandharasadvayam /
body.translated_text: In the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) too, it should be understood similarly, excluding the pair of smell (<s>gandha</s>) and taste (<s>rasa</s>) —

body.text: rūpadhātau bahirgataḥ pañcadravyāvinirbhāgī gandharasau hitvā | kāyasahagatastu ṣaḍbhiścakṣurādiṣu saptabhiravinirbhāgibhiḥ | yadā punassaśabdakaḥ sa saṃdhāto jāyate, tadā sarvatra yathokteṣu śabdo 'dhiko gaṇayitavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: in the form realm, an external [atom] is inseparable from five substances, excluding smell and taste. [An atom] accompanied by body [faculty] is [inseparable from] six, and in [the domains of] eye and so forth, [from] seven inseparable [substances]. But when that aggregate arises together with sound (<s>śabda</s>), then everywhere, in the cases stated, sound should be counted as additional.

body.text: atra punarmahābhūtāni sarvopādāyarūpāśrayabhāvaprādhānyāccatasro dravyajātayo vivakṣyante | upādāyarūpadhātucatuṣṭayaṃ tu ghaṭādidravyaprajñaptinimittatvādāyatanagaṇanayā gaṇyata iti vivakṣitāparijñānānnāsti codyāvakāśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, furthermore, the great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>) are designated as four substance-classes by virtue of their predominance in being the substratum of all derivative forms (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>). But the fourfold group of derivative-form <s>dhātus</s>, since it serves as the basis for the designation of substances like pots and so forth, is counted by the enumeration of <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) — thus there is no room for objection from a failure to understand the intended [meaning].

body.text: arūpiṇāṃ punaḥ
body.translated_text: But for the immaterial [<s>dharmas</s>] —

children.translated_text: consciousness (<s>citta</s>), together with mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>) —

body.text: avinirbhāgeṇa jāyata iti vartate |
body.translated_text: arises inseparably — this continues [from the verse].

body.text: saṃskṛtaṃ tu svalakṣaṇaiḥ // Abhidh-d_111 //
body.translated_text: And the conditioned, with [its] own characteristics. (Abhidh-d 111)

body.text: sarva hi saṃskṛtaṃ svalakṣaṇaiḥ saha jātyādibhirutpadyata iti veditavyam ||
body.translated_text: For all that is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) arises together with its own characteristics such as birth (<s>jāti</s>) and the like — this should be understood.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau dvitīyasyaadhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the second section (<s>pāda</s>) of the second chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text:
dvitīyādhyāye
tṛtīyapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: Second chapter, third section.

body.text: yaduktaṃ caitasikāstu sahotpadyanta iti tadabhidhīyatām | ke punaste caitasikā dharmāḥ ?
body.translated_text: It was stated that mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>) arise together [with consciousness]. Let that be explained. What then are those mental (<s>caitasika</s>) <s>dharmas</s>?

body.text: te pañcaprabhedāḥ- mahābhaumāḥ, kuśalamahābhaumāḥ, kleśamahābhaumāḥ, akuśalamahābhaumāḥ, parīttakleśamahābhaumikāśca | mahatī cittabhūmireṣāmiti ta ime mahābhaumāḥ | bhūmirgatirityarthaḥ | eva sarvatra vigrahaḥ kāryaḥ |
body.translated_text: They are of five classes: <s>mahābhaumāḥ</s> (universal mental factors), <s>kuśala-mahābhaumāḥ</s> (universal wholesome factors), <s>kleśa-mahābhaumāḥ</s> (universal afflictive factors), <s>akuśala-mahābhaumāḥ</s> (universal unwholesome factors), and <s>parīttakleśa-mahābhaumikāḥ</s> (limited afflictive factors). 'The great ground (<s>bhūmi</s>) of consciousness is theirs' — hence they are '<s>mahābhauma</s>' (belonging to the great ground). '<s>Bhūmi</s>' means 'course' (<s>gati</s>). The same analysis should be applied everywhere.

body.text: tatra tāvanmahābhaumā nirdiśyante |
body.translated_text: Therein, first, the universal mental factors (<s>mahābhauma</s>) are enumerated:

children.translated_text: The ten <s>dharmas</s> that are universal: feeling (<s>vid</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), volition (<s>cetanā</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>),
desire (<s>chanda</s>), contact (<s>sparśa</s>), conviction (<s>adhimokṣa</s>), wisdom (<s>dhī</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and attention (<s>manaskṛti</s>). (Abhidh-d 112)

body.text: ete daśadharmāḥ sarvasyāṃ cittabhūmau traidhātukyāmanāsravāyāṃ ca samagrā bhavanti |
body.translated_text: These ten <s>dharmas</s> are present in their entirety on every ground of consciousness — in all three realms (<s>traidhātukya</s>) and on the undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) [ground] as well.

body.text: tatra vedanā sukhādistrividho 'nubhavaḥ | trividhaṃ saṃveditamiti paryāyaḥ | iṣṭāniṣṭobhayaviparītaviṣayendriyavijñānasannipātajā dharmayoniḥ kāyacittāvasthā viśeṣaḥ prahlādyupatāpī tadubhayaviparītaśca tṛṣṇāheturvedanetyucyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) is threefold experience (<s>anubhava</s>) — of pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and so forth. 'Threefold felt experience' is a synonym. Born from the conjunction of object, sense-faculty, and consciousness, it is a <s>dharma</s>-source — a particular state of body and mind — delighting, tormenting, or the opposite of both — being a cause of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), it is called feeling (<s>vedanā</s>).

body.text: nimittanāmārthaikyajñā saṃjñā vitarkayoniḥ |
body.translated_text: Perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) is the cognition of the unity of sign (<s>nimitta</s>), name (<s>nāma</s>), and referent (<s>artha</s>); it is the source of applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>).

body.text: cittābhisaṃskāraścetanā |
body.translated_text: Volition (<s>cetanā</s>) is the mental construction (<s>abhisaṃskāra</s>) of consciousness.

body.text: cittavyāpārarūpā smṛtiḥ | cittasyārthābhilapanā kṛtakartavyakriyamāṇakarmāntāvipramoṣalakṣaṇā |
body.translated_text: Mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) is of the nature of the operation of consciousness — the verbal designation (<s>abhilapana</s>) of objects by consciousness — characterized by non-loss (<s>avipramoṣa</s>) of actions done, to be done, and being done.

body.text: chandaḥ kartukāmatā vīryāṅgabhūtaḥ |
body.translated_text: Desire (<s>chanda</s>) is the wish to act (<s>kartukāmatā</s>); it is a constituent of effort (<s>vīrya</s>).

body.text: viṣayendriyavijñānasannipātajā cittasya viṣayaspṛṣṭiḥ, caitasikadharmo jīvanalakṣaṇaḥ sparśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Contact (<s>sparśa</s>) is the touching of consciousness to the object, born from the conjunction of object, sense-faculty, and consciousness — a mental factor (<s>caitasika dharma</s>) characterized by vivification (<s>jīvana</s>).

body.text: cittasya viṣaye 'dhimuktiradhimokṣo rucidvitīyanāmā cittasya viṣayāpratisaṃkocalakṣaṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: Conviction (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) is the determination (<s>adhimukti</s>) of consciousness regarding an object — its second name is 'inclination' (<s>ruci</s>) — characterized by the non-retraction (<s>apratisaṃkoca</s>) of consciousness from the object.

body.text: dhīḥ prajñā dharmasaṃgrahādyupalakṣaṇasvabhāvā |
body.translated_text: Wisdom (<s>dhī</s>) is <s>prajñā</s> — of the nature of the discernment marked by [the ability to] compile <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasaṃgraha</s>) and so forth.

body.text: cittasyaikāgratā samādhiścittasthitilakṣaṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: Concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) is one-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā</s>) of consciousness, characterized by the steadiness (<s>sthiti</s>) of consciousness.

body.text: cittasyābhogo manaskāraḥ pūrvānubhūtādisamanvāhārasvarūpaḥ |
body.translated_text: Attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) is the bending (<s>abhoga</s>) of consciousness — of the nature of recalling (<s>samanvāhāra</s>) what was previously experienced and the like.

body.text: sūkṣmaḥ khalu cittacaittānāṃ viśeṣo duravadhāro rūpiṇīnāmeva tāvadoṣadhīnāṃ bahurasānāmindriyagrāhyo 'pi rasaviśeṣo duravadhāraḥ, kimaṅga punaramūrtānāṃ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 71)

children.text: ) cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāmekakalāpavartināṃ buddhigamyaḥ ? sa tu hetuphalasvabhāvairmatimadbhirabhyūhya iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s> of consciousness and mental factors that operate in a single group (<s>ekakalāpa</s>) — which are cognizable only by the intellect? But that [distinction] is inferred (<s>abhyūhya</s>) by the wise through [consideration of] the nature of cause and effect.

body.translated_text: The distinction among consciousness and mental factors is indeed subtle and difficult to ascertain. Even among material things (<s>rūpin</s>), such as medicinal herbs having many constituents (<s>rasa</s>), a distinction of constituents that is even graspable by the sense-faculties is difficult to ascertain — how much more so, then, the immaterial

body.text: kuśalamahābhaume bhavāḥ kuśalamahābhaumāḥ | te punaḥ
body.translated_text: Those that exist on the wholesome great ground (<s>kuśala-mahābhauma</s>) are the universal wholesome factors. They are:

children.translated_text: Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), heedfulness (<s>apekṣā</s>), non-negligence (<s>apramāda</s>), pliancy (<s>prasrabdhi</s>), moral shame (<s>hrī</s>), moral dread (<s>apatrapā</s>),
the [two] roots (<s>mūla</s>), effort (<s>vīrya</s>), non-harming (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) — these ten belonging to the wholesome ground are remembered. (Abhidh-d 113)

body.text: tatra śraddhā cetasaḥ prasādo guṇiguṇārthitvābhisaṃpratyayākāraḥ, cittakāluṣyāpanāyī | tadyathodakaprasādako maṇiḥ sarasi prakṣiptaḥ sarvaṃ kāluṣyamapanīyācchatāmutpādayati tadvaccittasarasi jātaḥ śraddhāmaṇiriti |
body.translated_text: Therein, faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) is the clarity (<s>prasāda</s>) of the mind — an attitude of trust in the virtuous and their virtues, and in the [four] truths — removing the turbidity of consciousness. Just as a water-clarifying gem, when cast into a lake, removes all turbidity and produces clarity — so the gem of faith, born in the lake of consciousness.

body.text: apramādaḥ kuśaladharmabhāvanā tadavahitatetyarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Non-negligence (<s>apramāda</s>) is the cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — meaning attentiveness thereto.

body.text: prasrabdhiścittakarmaṇyatā | kāyaprasrabdhirapyasti | sā tu tadānukūlyādbodhyaṅgaśabdaṃ labhate | tadyathā prītiḥ | prītisthānīyāśca dharmāḥ prītibodhyaṅgamuktaṃ bhagavatā | samyagdṛṣṭisaṃkalpavyāyāmāśca prajñānukūlyāt prajñāskandha ityuktāḥ | tadvatkāyakarmaṇyatā cittakarmaṇyatā bodhyaṅgāvāhakatvāttacchabdenoktā |
body.translated_text: Pliancy (<s>prasrabdhi</s>) is workableness (<s>karmaṇyatā</s>) of consciousness. Bodily pliancy (<s>kāyaprasrabdhi</s>) also exists; but because of its conformity with [mental pliancy], it receives the designation of a factor of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>). Just as joy (<s>prīti</s>): <s>dharmas</s> that are on the level of joy — the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke of [them as] the joy factor of awakening. And right view, right intention, and right effort — because of their conformity with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) — are called the aggregate of wisdom. Similarly, bodily workableness (<s>kāyakarmaṇyatā</s>) is called by the term 'factor of awakening' for the same reason — because it is a vehicle for [awakening].

body.text: upekṣā cittasamatā cittānābhogaḥ saṃskārānimittābhogamadhyupekṣānimittapravaṇatā |
body.translated_text: Equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) is evenness (<s>samatā</s>) of consciousness — the non-application (<s>anābhoga</s>) of consciousness — an inclination toward the signless (<s>animitta</s>) of conditioned factors, the non-engaged, and the equanimous.

body.text: hrīḥ svātmāpekṣā | akāryakaraṇe lajjā |
body.translated_text: Moral shame (<s>hrī</s>) is regard for oneself (<s>svātmāpekṣā</s>) — shame in performing what should not be done.

body.text: apatrāpyantu parāpekṣā |
body.translated_text: Moral dread (<s>apatrapā</s>), however, is regard for others (<s>parāpekṣā</s>).

body.text: dve tu kuśalamūle alobhādveṣau | amohastu prajñāsvabhāvatvānmahābhaumeṣūkta iti na gaṇyate |
body.translated_text: The two wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) are non-greed (<s>alobha</s>) and non-hatred (<s>adveṣa</s>). But non-delusion (<s>amoha</s>), being of the nature of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), has been stated among the universal [factors] and is therefore not counted [separately].

body.text: vīrvaṃ kuśalākuśaladharmotpādanirodhābhyutsāhaḥ, saṃsāranimagnasya cetaso 'bhyunnatirityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Effort (<s>vīrya</s>) is the enthusiastic exertion toward the arising and cessation of wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> — meaning the uplifting of the mind that is sunk in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: avihiṃsā sattvāviheṭhanā |
body.translated_text: Non-harming (<s>avihiṃsā</s>) is non-affliction of sentient beings.

body.text: uktāḥ kuśalamahābhaumāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The universal wholesome factors have been stated.

children.translated_text: Torpor (<s>styāna</s>), negligence (<s>pramatti</s>), faithlessness (<s>āśraddhi</s>), laziness (<s>ālasya</s>), delusion (<s>mūḍhi</s>), and restlessness (<s>uddhati</s>) — six in the afflictive [ground] —

body.text: tatra
body.translated_text: therein,

body.text: styānaṃ kāyacittākarmaṇyatā |
body.translated_text: torpor (<s>styāna</s>) is the un-workableness (<s>akarmaṇyatā</s>) of body and mind.

body.text: pramādaḥ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmabhāvanā | bhāvanāvipakṣabhūto dharmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Negligence (<s>pramāda</s>) is the non-cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — a <s>dharma</s> that is the counterpart (<s>vipakṣa</s>) of cultivation.

body.text: āśraddhyaṃ cittāprasādaḥ, cittakāluṣyamityarthaḥ | guṇeṣu guṇavatsu cāsaṃpratyayo 'narthitvaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: <s>Āśraddhya</s> (lack of faith) is the non-clarity of mind — meaning the turbidity of mind. It is disbelief in good qualities and in those who possess them, and indifference [to them].

body.text: kausīdyaṃ cittasyānabhyutsāhaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Kausīdya</s> (laziness) is the lack of enthusiasm of the mind.

body.text: mūḍhiravidyānukārāsaṃprakhyānarūpā |
body.translated_text: <s>Mūḍhi</s> (delusion) is that which imitates <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), having the nature of non-discernment.

body.text: auddhatyaṃ cittasyāvyupaśamaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Auddhatya</s> (restlessness) is the non-tranquility of the mind.

body.text: uktāḥ ṣaṭ kleśamahābhaumāḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus the six <s>kleśa-mahābhūmikas</s> (defilement-universals) have been stated.

body.text: abhidharme tu daśa paṭhyante- "āśraddhaym, kausīdyam, muṣitasmṛtitā, cetaso vikṣepaḥ, avidyā, asaṃprajanyam, ayoniśo manasikāraḥ, mithyādhimokṣaḥ, auddhatyam, pramādaśca" iti |
body.translated_text: But in the <s>Abhidharma</s> [tradition], ten are enumerated: lack of faith (<s>āśraddhya</s>), laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), lost mindfulness (<s>muṣitasmṛtitā</s>), mental distraction (<s>cetaso vikṣepa</s>), ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), non-clear-comprehension (<s>asaṃprajanya</s>), improper mental engagement (<s>ayoniśo manasikāra</s>), wrong resolve (<s>mithyādhimokṣa</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), and heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>).

body.text: tatra muṣitasmṛtivikṣepāsaṃprajanyāyoniśomanasikāramithyādhimokṣāḥ pañcamahābhaumeṣu paṭhitāḥ | kliṣṭākliṣṭānāmubhayeṣāṃ smṛtyādisvābhāvyāditīha na pṛthaggaṇyante | tasmāt ṣaḍeva kleśamahābhaumāḥ |
body.translated_text: Among those, lost mindfulness, distraction, non-clear-comprehension, improper mental engagement, and wrong resolve — these five are enumerated among the [general] universals (<s>mahābhauma</s>). Since both defiled and non-defiled [varieties] of mindfulness and the like have [these as] their intrinsic nature, they are not counted separately here. Therefore, the defilement-universals are exactly six.

body.text: aśubhe tu dve āhrīkyamanapatrapā // Abhidh-d_114 //
body.translated_text: But in the unwholesome [mind], two [are added]: shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrapā</s>). (Abhidh-d 114)

body.text: akuśale tu cetasi āhrīkyamanapatrāpyaṃ ca dvau dharmāvakuśalamahābhaumikau bhavataḥ | tatrāhrīkyaṃ hrīvipakṣabhūto dharmaḥ | anapatrāpyamapatrāpyasyeti | akāryaṃ kurvāṇasyālajjā svātmano 'hrīḥ | parebhyo 'lajjā anapatrāpyamityapare |
body.translated_text: In the unwholesome mind, shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>) — these two <s>dharmas</s> are unwholesome-universals (<s>akuśala-mahābhaumika</s>). Among these, <s>āhrīkya</s> is the <s>dharma</s> that is the opposite of shame (<s>hrī</s>). <s>Anapatrāpya</s> is [the opposite] of moral dread (<s>apatrāpya</s>). Shamelessness before one's own self when doing what ought not be done — that is <s>ahrī</s>. Shamelessness before others — that is <s>anapatrāpya</s>, according to some.

body.text: parīttakleśamahābhaumā nirdiśyante |
body.translated_text: The minor defilement-universals (<s>parīttakleśa-mahābhauma</s>) are taught:

body.text: māyāśāṭhyamadakrodhavihiṃserṣyāpradaṣṭayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Deceit (<s>māyā</s>), dissimulation (<s>śāṭhya</s>), pride (<s>mada</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), malice (<s>vihiṃsā</s>), envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), miserliness (<s>pradaṣṭa</s>),

body.text: sūkṣmopanāhamātsaryāṇyalpakleśabhuvo daśa // Abhidh-d_115 //
body.translated_text: subtle resentment (<s>sūkṣmopanāha</s>), and avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>) — [these are] the ten minor defilement-grounds. (Abhidh-d 115)

children.text: ete hi kleśā bhāvanāheyenāvidyāmātreṇa manobhūmikenaiva saṃprayujyante |
children.translated_text: For these defilements are associated only with ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) alone, which is to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāheya</s>) and belongs only to the mental plane (<s>manobhūmika</s>).
But their definitions will be stated in the fifth chapter, in the discussion of secondary defilements (<s>upakleśa</s>).

body.text: kathaṃ punaridaṃ vijñāyate cittādarthāntarabhūtāścaitasikāḥ ? cittameva hi tadvedanādināmabhirvyapadiśyata ityevaṃ ceṣyamāne buddhasūtramanulomitaṃ bhavati | yaduktaṃ bhagavatā- "ṣaḍdhāturayaṃ bhikṣavaḥ puruṣapudgalaḥ" ityatra vijñānadhāturevoktaḥ | tasmānnārthāntarabhūtāścaitasikā iti bhadantabuddhadevaḥ | taṃ pratīdamabhidhīyate-
body.translated_text: But how is it known that the mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>) are entities distinct from mind (<s>citta</s>)? For it may be maintained that it is mind itself that is designated by [the terms] feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) and the like — and if this is accepted, it would be in conformity with the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>sūtra</s>, where the <s>Bhagavat</s> said: 'This person-<s>pudgala</s>, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, consists of six elements' — here only the consciousness-element (<s>vijñānadhātu</s>) is mentioned. Therefore, mental factors are not entities distinct [from mind] — so says the <s>Bhadanta</s> <s>Buddhadeva</s>. Against him, this is stated:

children.translated_text: Just as a substance like earth and the like, through conjunction with qualities such as blue and the like,
is specified by various words — so too the mind, through conjunction with mental factors. (Abhidh-d 116)

body.text: yathā hi pṛthivīdhāturabdhāturvā rūparasagandhādyupādāyarūpairviśeṣyate | nīlā grāvāṇaḥ, nīlamudakaṃ madhurā drākṣā madhurāḥ kharjūrā madhurataro guḍa ityevaṃ sukhitaṃ cittaṃ duḥkhitaṃ cittaṃ samāhitaṃ cittaṃ sotsāhaṃ kusīdaṃ mūḍhaṃ raktaṃ dviṣṭamityevamādibhiḥ śabdaiścaitasikairdharmairyogādviśeṣyate | sādhyasamatvādayuktamiti cet | na | uktottaratvāt | vihitamatra- bhūtabhautikānyatvacintāyāmuttaramiti | tasmādviśeṣapratyayānāmanākasmikatvātsiddhamanyatvaṃ caitāsikānāmiti |
body.translated_text: For just as the earth-element or water-element is specified by derivative forms (<s>upādāya-rūpa</s>) such as form, taste, smell, and the like — 'blue stones,' 'blue water,' 'sweet grapes,' 'sweet dates,' 'sweeter jaggery' — in the same way, 'a happy mind,' 'a suffering mind,' 'a concentrated mind,' 'an enthusiastic [mind],' 'a lazy [mind],' 'a confused [mind],' 'an attached [mind],' 'a hostile [mind]' — by such words it is specified through conjunction with mental factors (<s>caitasika dharmas</s>). If [one objects:] this is improper because the thing to be proved is equal [to the example] — no, because the answer has been given. It has been stated: 'the answer is provided in the discussion of the distinction between elements and derivative forms.' Therefore, since the conditions for specification are not arbitrary, the distinctness of the mental factors is established.

body.text: itaśca cittacaitasikānyatvam-
body.translated_text: And further, [proving] the distinctness of mind and mental factors:

children.translated_text: Just as the multiplicity of elements and derivative forms is not produced by intrinsic nature alone in this [system],
so too should the separateness of mind and mental factors be understood. (Abhidh-d 117)

body.text: yathā khalu bhūtānāṃ bhautikasya ca rūpasya svabhāvabhedāt, kriyābhedāccānyatvam; tathā cittasya caittānāṃ ca svabhāvakriyābhedādanyatvaṃ draṣṭavyam ||
body.translated_text: Just as the distinctness of elements and derivative forms is [established] because of the difference in intrinsic nature and the difference in function — so too, the distinctness of mind and mental factors should be seen as due to the difference in intrinsic nature and function.

children.translated_text: Just as a transformation in water is observed through contact with a related substance,
so too should the transformation of mind be seen through association with associated [factors]. (Abhidh-d 118)

body.text: yathā khalu vahniharītakīguḍalavaṇādidravyasaṃbandhādvikāro 'mbuni dṛśyate, uṣṇamamblaṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ lavaṇamiti | tadvaccaitasikasaṃbandhāccittamapi sukhitaṃ duḥkhitaṃ prasannamabhyunnataṃ sālokaṃ sāndhakāramiti |
body.translated_text: Just as a transformation in water is seen through contact with substances such as fire, <s>harītakī</s> (Terminalia chebula), jaggery, salt, and the like — 'hot water,' 'sour water,' 'astringent water,' 'sweet water,' 'salty water' — so too, through the association of mental factors, the mind also [becomes] 'happy,' 'suffering,' 'clear,' 'elevated,' 'illuminated,' 'darkened,' and so forth.

body.text: sūtre 'pi cānyatvamuktam- "saṃjñā ca vedanā ca caitasika eṣa dharmaḥ" iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s> also, distinctness is stated: '<s>Saṃjñā</s> (perception) and <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) — these are mental (<s>caitasika</s>) <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | yugapadutpannānāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kathaṃ caitasikā dharmā ityucyante ? ko vā dharmārthaḥ? tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: of the mind and mental factors (<s>caitta</s>) that arise simultaneously, how are [some] called 'mental factors'? And what is the meaning of '<s>dharma</s>' [in this context]? This is explained:

children.translated_text: Quality (<s>guṇa</s>), qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>), <s>dharma</s>, dependent-measure (<s>mātrāvṛtti</s>), and dependent-on-support (<s>āśrayī</s>) —
these and similar words function with reference to the principal. (Abhidh-d 119)

body.text: pradhānaṃ hi dravyaṃ viśeṣyabhūtamapekṣya guṇadharmaviśeṣeṇa mātrāvṛttayaḥ śabdāḥ pravartante | ki punaratra pradhānam ?
body.translated_text: For with reference to the principal — the substance (<s>dravya</s>) that is the qualificand — words like 'quality,' '<s>dharma</s>,' and 'qualifier' function as measures [of specification]. What then is the principal here?

children.translated_text: Mind is the principal among these —

body.text: kuta iti cet |
body.translated_text: if asked why,

body.text: vastumātragrahādibhiḥ /
body.translated_text: [it is] because of mere apprehension of the object and the like;

body.text: vastūpalabdhimātraṃ hi cittaṃ tenopalabdhe vastuni saṃjñāsmaraṇe lakṣaṇānusmaraṇābhinirūpaṇādayo viśeṣāḥ saṃjñāprajñāsmṛtyādibhirgṛhyante | 'ādi'grahaṇādatrātmābhiniveśādrājasthānīyatvācca | kiñca,
body.translated_text: for mind is merely the apprehension of an object (<s>vastupalabdhimātra</s>); having apprehended the object, the specific functions such as recollection of characteristics by perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), detailed examination, and the like are grasped by perception, insight (<s>prajñā</s>), memory (<s>smṛti</s>), and the like. From the word 'and the like,' [mind is principal] also because of self-grasping (<s>ātmābhiniveśa</s>) and because of being in the position of a king. Moreover,

body.text: bījaṃ caitatpravṛttīnāṃ śuddhisaṃkarayorapi // Abhidh-d_120 //
body.translated_text: this is the seed of [all] activities — of both purification and defilement. (Abhidh-d 120)

body.text: uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "cittasaṃkleśātsattvāḥ saṃkliśyante | cittavyavadānahetorviśudhyante" iti | tasmātpradhānaṃ cittam | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bhagavat</s> has said: 'Through the defilement of mind, beings are defiled; through the purification of mind, they are purified.' Therefore, mind is the principal. As stated:

children.translated_text: 'Far-wandering, solitary, bodiless, cave-dwelling —

children.text: ye cittaṃ damayiṣyanti te mokṣyante mārabandhanāt ||"
children.translated_text: those who will tame the mind will be freed from the bonds of <s>Māra</s>.'

body.text: tatra dūraṅgamaṃ śāstuḥ sarvalokadhātusthavineyakāryakaraṇāt | ekacaraṃ yugapad dvitīyacittābhāvāt | aśarīraṃ mūrtyabhāvāt, kriyāmātrānumeyasvabhāvatvācca | guhāśayaṃ śarīrabalena | tadvṛttivyakteriti | tasya dharmāḥ saṃprayogiṇaścaitasikā iti |
body.translated_text: There, 'far-wandering' — because the Teacher performs the work of training beings situated in all world-realms. 'Solitary' — because a second mind does not arise simultaneously. 'Bodiless' — because it has no physical form, and because its intrinsic nature is inferable only from activity. 'Cave-dwelling' — by the power of the body; because its activity is manifested [through the body]. Its <s>dharmas</s> — the associated [factors] — are the mental factors.

body.text: vyākhyātāḥ pañcaprakārāścaittāḥ | anye 'pi cāniyatāḥ paṭhyante- vitarkavicārakaukṛtyamiddhādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: The five categories of mental factors have been explained. Others too are enumerated as indeterminate — <s>vitarka</s> (initial application), <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application), <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret), <s>middha</s> (torpor), and the like.

body.text: tatredaṃ vaktavyam | kasmiṃścitte kati caittā bhavanti ?
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: in which mind do how many mental factors arise?

body.text: kāmāvacaraṃ tāvat pañcaprakāraṃ cittam | kuśalam, akuśalaṃ dvividhamāveṇikamanyatkleśasaṃprayuktaṃ ca | avyākṛtaṃ dvividhaṃ nivṛtānivṛtāvyākṛtākhyam ||
body.translated_text: The desire-realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) mind is of five types: wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>); unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>), which is twofold — distinctive (<s>āveṇika</s>) and other, associated with defilements (<s>kleśa-saṃprayukta</s>); and indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>), which is twofold — called obstructed-indeterminate (<s>nivṛtāvyākṛta</s>) and unobstructed-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>).

body.text: tatra tāvatkāmāvacaraṃ cittamavaśyaṃ savitarkasavicāram | atastat
body.translated_text: The desire-realm mind necessarily possesses <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application). Therefore:

children.translated_text: The desire-realm unobstructed-indeterminate mind arises together with twelve <s>dharmas</s>,
like a radiant one with its rays. (Abhidh-d 121)

body.text: kāmāvacaramanivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ cittaṃ daśabhirmahāmaumairvitarkavicārābhyāṃ ca sahāvaśyamudeti ||
body.translated_text: The desire-realm unobstructed-indeterminate mind necessarily arises together with the ten universals (<s>mahābhauma</s>), plus <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>.

body.text: tathāṣṭādaśabhiścittairnivṛtaṃ jāyate manaḥ /
body.translated_text: And the obstructed [indeterminate] mind arises with eighteen mental factors;

body.text: satkāyāntagrāhadṛṣṭisamprayuktaṃ cittaṃ kāmadhātau nivṛtāvyākṛtam | tatrāṣṭādaśa caitasikā bhavanti | daśamahābhaumāḥṣaṭ kleśamahābhaumāḥ vitarkavicārau ca | dṛṣṭirnādhikā pūrvavat |
body.translated_text: the mind associated with the [false] view of the self-existent body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) or the extreme view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>) is obstructed-indeterminate in the desire realm. Therein, eighteen mental factors arise: ten universals, six defilement-universals, and <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>. The [false] view is not additional, as before.

body.text: dvāviṃśatyā sahāvaśyaṃ śubhaṃ bhavati mānasam // Abhidh-d_122 //
body.translated_text: The wholesome mind necessarily arises together with twenty-two. (Abhidh-d 122)

body.text: daśamahābhaumāḥ daśakuśalamahābhaumāḥ vitarkavicārau ca ||
body.translated_text: Ten universals, ten wholesome-universals (<s>kuśala-mahābhauma</s>), and <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>.

body.text: cetasossaha viṃśatyā cittamutpadyate 'śubham /
body.translated_text: The unwholesome mind arises with twenty mental factors;

body.text: yadakuśalaṃ cittamāveṇikaṃ tatra viṃśatiścaittāḥ- daśamahābhaumāḥ ṣakleśamahābhaumā dvāvakuśalamahābhaumau vitarko vicāraśca | āveṇikaṃ nāma cittaṃ yatrāvidyaiva kevalā nānyaḥ kleśo 'sti rāgādiḥ |
