body.translated_text: the unwholesome mind that is distinctive (<s>āveṇika</s>) — therein twenty mental factors [arise]: ten universals, six defilement-universals, two unwholesome-universals, and <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>. A distinctive (<s>āveṇika</s>) mind is one in which ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) alone exists, without any other defilement such as attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the like.

children.translated_text: That which is associated with [false] view and delusion alone —

body.text: dṛṣṭiyukte 'pyakuśale viṃśatirya evāveṇake | nanu ca dṛṣṭiradhikā ? nādhikā, prajñāviśeṣa eva hi kaścid dṛṣṭirityucyate | sa ca mahābhaumeṣu paṭhitaḥ |
body.translated_text: in the unwholesome mind associated with [false] view too, [there are] the same twenty as in the distinctive [type]. But is not [false] view additional? No, it is not additional, for a certain specification of insight (<s>prajñā</s>) itself is called [false] view. And that [prajñā] is already enumerated among the universals.

body.text: kaḥ punarayaṃ vitarkaḥ ko vā vicāraḥ ? vitarko nāma cittaudāryalakṣaṇaḥ saṃkalpadvitīyanāmā viṣayanimittaprakāravikalpī saṃjñāpavanoddhatavṛttiḥ, audārikapañcavijñānakāyapravṛttihetuḥ | vicārastu cittasaukṣmyalakṣaṇo manovijñānapravṛttyanukūlaḥ | ityetau dvau dharmau kāmāvacare cetasi sarvasminniyamenotpadyete |
body.translated_text: What then is <s>vitarka</s> (initial application)? And what is <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application)? <s>Vitarka</s> is characterized by the coarseness of mind, having 'intention' (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) as its second name, discriminating the modes and aspects of the object, its activity uplifted like wind by perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), and it is the cause of the activity of the coarse five sense-consciousnesses (<s>pañcavijñānakāya</s>). <s>Vicāra</s> is characterized by the subtlety of mind and is conducive to the activity of mind-consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>). These two <s>dharmas</s> necessarily arise in every mind in the desire realm.

body.text: tadidamatisāhasaṃ vartate yadviruddhayorapi dvayordharmayorekatra citte samavadhānaṃ pratijñāyate | na hyetalloke dṛṣṭaṃ yadviruddhayorekatra sahāvasthānamiti kośakāraḥ |
body.translated_text: This indeed is a great rashness — that the co-existence of two mutually opposed <s>dharmas</s> in a single mind is being asserted. For it is not observed in the world that two opposed [things] co-exist in one [place] — so says the <s>Kośakāra</s> (<s>Vasubandhu</s>).

body.text: tatra kecidāhuḥ- sarpiryathāpsu niṣṭhyūtaṃ nātiśyāyate nātivilīyate, evaṃ vitarkavicārayogāccittaṃ nātisūkṣmaṃ bhavati nātyudāramityubhayorapi tatra vyāpāraḥ | evaṃ tarhi nimittabhūtau vitarkavicārāvaudāryasūkṣmatayoḥ prāpnuto yathāpaścātaśca sarpiṣaḥśyānatvavilīnatvayorna punastatsvabhāvau |
body.translated_text: To this, some say: just as ghee [mixed] in water, when expelled, neither freezes excessively nor melts excessively — so too, through the conjunction of <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, the mind becomes neither excessively subtle nor excessively coarse, and thus both have their function therein. If so, then <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> would be [merely] the causes of coarseness and subtlety — just as ghee afterward [exhibits] congealing and melting — but would not be of that intrinsic nature themselves.

body.text: anye punarāhuḥ- vāksaṃskārā vitarkavicārāḥ sūtre 'bhihitāḥ |
body.translated_text: Others say: <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> are declared in the <s>sūtra</s> as the formative forces of speech (<s>vāk-saṃskāra</s>) —

body.text: "vitarkya vicārya vācaṃ bhāṣate nāvitarkyāvicārya" iti | tatra ya audāryāste vitarkāḥ | ye sūkṣmāste vicārāḥ | yadi caikatra citte 'nyo dharma audāriko 'nyaḥ sūkṣmaḥ ko 'tra virodha iti ? na virodho yadi jātibhedaḥ syāt | ekasyāntu jātau mṛdvadhimātratā yugapanna saṃbhavati | jātibhedo 'pyasti sa tarhi vaktavyaḥ | durvaco hyasau | ato mṛdvadhimātratayā vyajyate | naivaṃ vyakto bhavati | pratyekaṃ jātīnāṃ mṛdvadhimātratvāt |
body.translated_text: 'Having applied initial and sustained thought, one speaks; one does not speak without initial and sustained thought.' Among these, those that are coarse are <s>vitarkas</s>; those that are subtle are <s>vicāras</s>. If, in a single mind, one <s>dharma</s> is coarse and another is subtle, what contradiction is there? [Reply:] There is no contradiction if there is a difference of class (<s>jāti</s>). But within a single class, mild and intense [degrees] do not occur simultaneously. [Objection:] And if there is indeed a difference of class, it should be stated. [Reply:] But it is difficult to articulate. Therefore, it is indicated by [the distinction of] mild and intense. [Counter:] It is not made evident in this way, because each class individually [can be] mild, moderate, or intense.

body.text: tadidamandhavilāsinīkaṭākṣaguṇotkīrtanakalpaṃ codyamārabhyate | yadanavabudhya tallakṣaṇaṃ codyavidhiḥ mithyā pratāyate | tayorhi yathoktalakṣaṇayorekasmiṃścetasi sadbhāvamātraṃ pratijñāyate na yugapad vṛttyudrekatālābhaḥ | yathā vidyavidyayoḥ saṃśayanirṇayayośceti tūṣṇīmāsva | mā vidvadbhiravajīhasaḥ svamātmānam |
body.translated_text: This objection begins like the praise of the glancing virtues of a blind woman's sidelong glance [i.e., is pointless]. For without understanding their [true] definition, the objection-method is falsely extended. For of those two, having the definitions as stated, only their mere existence in a single mind is asserted — not the attainment of excess of simultaneous function. Just as with knowledge and ignorance, doubt and certainty — be silent! Do not demean yourself before the learned.

body.text: sā punardṛṣṭistriprakārā mithyādṛṣṭyādyā veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: That [false] view, moreover, is to be understood as of three types, beginning with wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) and the like.

body.text: krodhādyaistvadhikaṃ vadet // Abhidh-d_123 //
body.translated_text: But with anger and the like, [the count] should be stated as higher. (Abhidh-d 123)

body.text: krodhādyaistūpakleśairadhikaṃ bhavati | sa ca krodhādirupakleśo 'dhikaḥ | kleśaiśca saṃprayuktaṃ rāgapratighamānavicikitsābhiśca yuktaṃ cittaṃ tena ca kleśādhikaṃ bhavatītyekaviṃśatirbhavanti ||
body.translated_text: With anger and the other secondary defilements (<s>upakleśa</s>), [the count] becomes higher. And that secondary defilement of anger and the like is additional. And the mind associated with defilements — conjoined with attachment (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>) — becomes higher by that defilement as well, thus making twenty-one.

children.translated_text: Since torpor (<s>middha</s>) can occur everywhere, wherever it is [present], it should be indicated there;
and likewise regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) — one should count it as additional in some cases. (Abhidh-d 124)

body.text: yatra middhaṃ tatra tadevādhikaṃ gaṇayet | yatrāpi tadevādhikamiti ya eṣa kāmadhātau caittānāṃ niyama uktastataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Wherever torpor is [present], there one should count that very [factor] as additional. Wherever that [regret] too is additional, [it should be counted]. This rule regarding mental factors in the desire realm has been stated. From that:

children.translated_text: Unwholesome [mind], torpor, and regret are not found in the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>);
in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>vitarka</s> [is absent]; and <s>vicāra</s> also is not [present] above. (Abhidh-d 125)

body.text: na kiñcidakuśalaṃ middhaṃ kaukṛtyaṃ ca prathamadhyānādau vidyate | tena tatra pratighaśāṭhyamadamāyāvarjyāśca krodhādayaḥ, āhrīkyānapatrāpye ca na santi | ya eva prathame dhyāne santi ta eva 'dhyānāntare', 'vitarkaśca na vidyate | pūrvoktāśca na santīti 'ca'śabdāt | vicāraścāpi nopari |'; dhyānāntarāttūparivicāraścāpi nāsti pūrvoktāśca | 'ca'śabdāt māyā śāṭhyaṃ ca nāstīti gamyate |
body.translated_text: No unwholesome [mind], torpor, or regret exists from the first <s>dhyāna</s> onward. Therefore, there [in the form realm], aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), dissimulation (<s>śāṭhya</s>), pride (<s>mada</s>), and deceit (<s>māyā</s>) are excluded, as are anger (<s>krodha</s>) and the other [secondary defilements]; and shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>) do not exist. Those that exist in the first <s>dhyāna</s> are the same in the 'intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>' [between first and second], except '<s>vitarka</s> is not found.' And the previously mentioned [factors] also do not exist — from the word 'and.' '<s>Vicāra</s> also is not [present] above' — from the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> upward, <s>vicāra</s> also does not exist, nor do the previously mentioned [factors]. From the word 'and,' it is understood that deceit (<s>māyā</s>) and dissimulation (<s>śāṭhya</s>) also do not exist.

body.text: brahmaṇo hi yāvacchāṭhyaṃ paṭhyate, parṣatsaṃbandhāt | sa hi svasyāṃ parṣadi aśvajitā bhikṣuṇā praśnaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ "kutra tāni catvāri mahābhūtānyapariśeṣaṃ nirudhyante" ityaprajānan kṣepamakārṣīt- "ahamasmi brahmā mahābrahmā īśvaraḥ kartā nirmātā sraṣṭā sṛjaḥ pitṛbhūto bhāvānām" iti | gatamidam ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For <s>Brahmā</s>'s deceptiveness is recited, due to [his] connection with his assembly. For he, when questioned in his own assembly by the monk <s>Aśvajit</s>: 'Where do these four great elements cease without remainder?' — not knowing [the answer], made a boast: 'I am <s>Brahmā</s>, the Great <s>Brahmā</s>, the Lord, the Creator, the Fashioner, the Maker, the Generator, the Father-being of all things.' This point has been covered.

body.text: idaṃ vaktavyam | saṃprayuktāḥ saṃskārāḥ kasmāducyante ? tadārabhyate |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This must now be stated. Why are formations said to be 'associated' (<s>saṃprayukta</s>)? This is commenced:

children.translated_text: An associated formation (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is one that has equality in five respects;

children.text: viprayuktaśca boddhavyaḥ samatā yasya nāstyasau // Abhidh-d_126 //
children.translated_text: and a disjoined [formation] (<s>viprayukta</s>) should be understood as one that does not have [such] equality. (Abhidh-d 126)

body.text: pañcabhiḥ samatābhiḥ saṃprayuktāḥ saṃprayuktāḥ | tāḥ punarāśrayālambanākārakāladravyasamatākhyāḥ | "yathaiva hyekaṃ cittamevaṃ caittā apyekaikāḥ" iti vistaraḥ | yasya punaretāḥ samatā na vidyante sa viprayukta iti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Those associated by means of five equalities are 'associated.' These are called: equality of support (<s>āśraya</s>), of object (<s>ālambana</s>), of aspect (<s>ākāra</s>), of time (<s>kāla</s>), and of substance (<s>dravya</s>). 'Just as there is one mind, so too the mental factors are [each] one individually' — and so on in detail. But one that does not possess these equalities is 'disjoined.'

body.text: codakaḥ- kaścidrūpaṃ tarhi viprayuktaṃ prāpnoti, asaṃskṛtaṃ ceti ? saṃpratyucyate |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The objector [asks]: 'Would not form then be disjoined, and the unconditioned too?' To this it is now replied:

children.translated_text: Due to the non-existence of the specified [features in form], there is no unwarranted consequence for material [dharmas];
and due to the qualification 'formation' (<s>saṃskāra</s>), [the objection] does not apply to space and the rest. (Abhidh-d 127)

body.text: viśiṣṭena khalu niyogena rūpiṣu saṃjñā sanniviśanta iti teṣvaprasaṃgaḥ | saṃskāragrahaṇācca khādiṣu viprayuktasaṃjñā na pravartata iti siddham ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Since designations are applied to material [dharmas] by a specific conventional assignment, there is no unwarranted consequence for them. And since the designation 'disjoined' does not apply to space and the rest due to the qualification '<s>saṃskāra</s>' — this is established.

body.text: ke punaste viprayuktāḥ saṃskārāḥ ? kiyanto veti ? nahi vayameteṣāṃ svabhāvamupalabhāmahe | nāpi kṛtyam | nacaite dharmā loke prasiddhā nāpi buddhavacane | na vedādiṣu śāstreṣviti | tadatropavyāhrīyate-
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] What then are these disjoined formations? And how many are there? For we do not apprehend their intrinsic nature, nor their function. Nor are these <s>dharmas</s> well-known in the world, nor in the <s>Buddha</s>'s word, nor in treatises such as the Vedas. To this it is replied:

children.translated_text: The disjoined formations, beginning with acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>), are thirteen.
The marks of authoritative testimony and intrinsic function [serve as evidence] — their marks will be stated. (Abhidh-d 128)

body.text: yattāvat svabhāvakriyābhāvāditi | tadatrobhayamabhidhāyiṣyate | yadapi buddhavacane na paṭhyanta iti | tatrāpyāptavacanaṃ sārvajñaṃ vyāhariṣyate | yatta loke na vedādiṣu paṭhyanta iti taccodyam | ye khalu sarvajñaviṣayā dharmāḥ pratisaṃvillābhināṃ buddhivṛttiviṣayamāyāntyāryamaitreyasthaviravasumitrācāryāśvaghoṣapramukhānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ buddhiprasādavidhāyinastejolpānāṃ stanandhayabudvīnāmabhidharmaparīkṣamativṛttīnāṃ ca kathaṃ sāndhakāreṣu manassu gocaratāmāyāntīti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] As for [the objection] that they lack intrinsic nature and function — both will be stated here. As for [the objection] that they are not recited in the <s>Buddha</s>'s word — for that too, the authoritative statement of the Omniscient One will be cited. As for the objection that they are not [found] in the world or in [treatises like] the Vedas — that objection [is misguided]. For those <s>dharmas</s> that are the domain of the Omniscient One come within the range of the intellect of those who have attained discrimination (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> foremost among whom are the noble <s>Maitreya</s>, the Elder <s>Vasumitra</s>, and the teacher <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s>, and of those whose brilliance purifies cognition — how could they come within the range of [minds] as dark as those of infants, of those whose intellects have gone beyond the examination of <s>Abhidharma</s>?

body.text: tatra tāvat
body.translated_text: Therein, now:

body.text: rāptiḥ samanvitirlabdhirdharmavattā vyavasthitiḥ // Abhidh-d_129 //
body.translated_text: Acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>) is the same as possession (<s>samanviti</s>), obtainment (<s>labdhi</s>), <s>dharma</s>-possession (<s>dharmavattā</s>), and establishment (<s>vyavasthiti</s>). (Abhidh-d 129)

body.text: prāptarnāma samanvāgamo lābha iti paryāyaḥ | sarvathā bhāvāñchabdaireva śabdānācaṣṭe | yathaiṃva khalu prāptirityetacchabdagaḍumātraṃ śrūyate tathaiva samanvāgamo lābha ityetadapi padadvayaṃ vāgvastumātramiti na paryāyanāmnā lakṣaṇamudyotitaṃ bhavati | tasmādavyabhicāri tatprasādhakaṃ liṅgamucyatām | ime brū maḥ | śrotramavadhatsva manaścaikāgratāyāṃ sanniyuktvā | 'dharmavattā vyavasthitiḥ |'; dharmāḥ khalu tridhā kuśalāḥ.........
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Prāpti</s> — possession (<s>samanvāgama</s>) and obtainment (<s>lābha</s>) are synonyms. In every case, [the author] describes entities merely by means of words. Just as the term '<s>prāpti</s>' is heard as a mere sound-mass, so too the pair of words '<s>samanvāgama</s>' and '<s>lābha</s>' are mere verbal matter — the definition is not illuminated by synonymous names. Therefore, let the non-deviating logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that establishes it be stated. We say [this]: Lend your ear and fix your mind in one-pointed concentration. '<s>Dharma</s>-possession and establishment' — <s>dharmas</s> are indeed threefold: wholesome.........

body.text: ............rūpe 'pi kuśalayā vijñaptyā vartamānayā yāvadvijñāpayati, atītayā ca samanvāgataḥ |
body.translated_text: ..........even in the case of form, while the wholesome informative action (<s>vijñapti</s>) is present — as long as one informs [others through it]; and one is possessed of the past [vijñapti] too.

body.text: śrutacintāmayānāṃ ca samāpattidvayasya ca // Abhidh-d_130 //
body.translated_text: [Acquisitions] of those born of hearing and reflection, and of the two [formless] attainments. (Abhidh-d 130)

body.text: śrutacintāmayānāmapi | sahajā paścād bhavati dvayoścācitta samāpattyossaha paścād bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Of those born of hearing and reflection too. [Acquisition] is simultaneous and later. And of the two mindless attainments — [acquisition] is simultaneous and later.

children.translated_text: For the outflow-free, conditioned, and unprecedented [dharmas], and for the wholesome [dharmas] of one who has outflows,

children.text: ādilābhe saha prākca tadūrdhvaṃ vā tridheṣyate // Abhidh-d_131 //
children.translated_text: at the initial obtainment, [acquisition is] simultaneous, before, or — above that, it is taught as threefold. (Abhidh-d 131)

body.text: anāsravāṇāṃ ca skandhānāṃ, anucitānāṃ ca kuśalasāsravāṇāṃ na pūrvajā | eṣāmeva yattoktānāṃ 'tadūrdhvaṃ tu tridheṣyate |'; yadā tena saṃmukhībhūtā tadā dvidhaiveti vartate ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] And for the outflow-free aggregates, and for the wholesome with-outflow [dharmas] that are unprecedented — [acquisition] is not prior to them. For these very ones that have been stated, 'above that, it is taught as threefold' — when one has come face-to-face with them, then [acquisition is] just twofold; this is the continuation.

body.text: kliṣṭāṇāṃ kuśalānāṃ ca tadanyeṣāṃ tridhā matā /
body.translated_text: For the afflicted and the wholesome, and for others [distinct from these] — [acquisition is] considered threefold.

body.text: kliṣṭāṇāṃ ca skandhānāṃ traiyadhvikī prāptiḥ | 'kuśalānāṃ ca tadanyeṣāṃ'; tebhyo 'nāsravebhyastebhyaścānucittebhyaḥ kuśalasāsravebhyo 'nyeṣāṃ kuśalasāsravāṇāṃ traiyadhvikyeva |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] And the acquisition of afflicted aggregates is of all three times. 'And for the wholesome that are other than those' — for the wholesome with-outflows other than those outflow-free ones and those unprecedented wholesome with-outflows — [acquisition] is of all three times indeed.

body.text: nivṛtāvyākṛtā jñānanirmāṇamanasāṃ tathā // Abhidh-d_132 //
body.translated_text: For the obscured-indeterminate, and for the [<s>dharmas</s> of] knowledge-consciousness and transformation-consciousness, likewise — (Abhidh-d 132)

body.text: traiyadhvikīti vartate ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] of all three times — this is the continuation.

body.text: nirvāṇasyādito lābhe nityasyānyasya sarvadā /
body.translated_text: For <s>nirvāṇa</s>, at the initial obtainment — for the permanent, and for another, always.

body.text: nirvāṇasya tatprathamato lābhe dvaiyadhvikyeva | anāgatavartamānālabdhasyātītāpi | 'nityasyānyasya sarvadā |'
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For <s>nirvāṇa</s>, at the initial obtainment, [acquisition is] of just two times — of the future and present for [<s>nirvāṇa</s> that is] unobtained-yet-past too. 'For the permanent other [than nirvāṇa], always' —

children.translated_text: [acquisition is] of the future and present only,

body.text: apratisaṃkhyānirodhasyānāgatavartamānaiva nityam |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] for non-analytical cessation (<s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>), [acquisition is] always of the future and present only.

body.text: kadācittu tridheṣyate // Abhidh-d_133 //
body.translated_text: but sometimes it is taught as threefold. (Abhidh-d 133)

body.text: yena labdhastasya traiyadhvikītyuktametat |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For one who has obtained it, [acquisition is] of all three times — this is what is stated.

body.text: vyākhyāte prāptyaprāptī ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>) and non-acquisition (<s>aprāpti</s>) have been explained.

body.text: sabhāgatā vaktavyā | keyaṃ sabhāgatā nāma ? nahīha pravacane tīrthyaparikalpitasāmānyaviśeṣapadārthagandho 'pyasti | tatkeyaṃ tadabhyāsagateti ? tadidaṃ pratāyate |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Class-homogeneity (<s>sabhāgatā</s>) must now be stated. What is this thing called 'class-homogeneity'? For in this Teaching, there is not even a whiff of the categories of 'universal' (<s>sāmānya</s>) and 'particular' (<s>viśeṣa</s>) as imagined by the <s>Tīrthyas</s> (non-Buddhists). So what is this [thing] that resembles [those concepts]? This is explained:

body.text: ekārtharuciheturyaḥ sattvānāṃ sa sabhāgatā /
body.translated_text: That which is the cause of beings having a single purpose and inclination — that is class-homogeneity (<s>sabhāgatā</s>).

body.text: sabhāgatā nāma dravyam | sattvānāmekārtharuciḥ sādṛśyahetubhūtam | nikāyasabhāga ityasya śāstrasaṃjñā | sā punarabhinnā bhinnā ca | abhinnā sarvasatvānāṃ sattvasabhāgatā | sā pratisattvaṃ sarveṣvātmasnehāhāraratisāmyāt | bhinnā punasteṣāmeva sattvānāṃ dhātubhūmigatiyonijātistrīpuruṣopāsakabhikṣuśaikṣāśaikṣādīnāmekārtharucitvabhedapratiniyamahetuḥ | tasyāṃ khalvasatyāṃ sarvāryānāryalokavyavahārasaṃkaradoṣaḥ prasajyeta | tasyāṃ tu satyāmeṣa doṣo na bhavatītyasti sabhāgatā nāma dharmaḥ, 'ekārtharucihetuḥ'; iti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Class-homogeneity is a [real] substance (<s>dravya</s>). It is the cause of beings having a single purpose and inclination — the cause of similarity. Its technical term in the treatise is <s>nikāyasabhāga</s>. It is further undifferentiated and differentiated. The undifferentiated is the being-homogeneity (<s>sattvasabhāgatā</s>) of all beings — for each being, [it arises] from the equality of self-love, food, and delight in all [beings]. The differentiated, however, is the cause that determines the specific distinction of single-purpose-inclination among those very beings according to realm (<s>dhātu</s>), ground (<s>bhūmi</s>), destiny (<s>gati</s>), mode of birth (<s>yoni</s>), class (<s>jāti</s>), female, male, lay follower, monk, learner, adept, and so forth. In its absence, the fault of confusion among all worldly transactions of noble and non-noble beings would follow. But in its presence, this fault does not arise — therefore there exists a <s>dharma</s> called 'class-homogeneity,' the 'cause of single purpose and inclination.'

body.text: syāccyavetopapadyeta na ca svasabhāgatāṃ vijahyāt, na ca pratilabheteti ? catuṣkoṭikaḥ | prathamā kauṭiḥ- yataścyavate tatravopapadyamānaḥ | dvitīyā- niyāmamavakrāman, sa hi pṛthagjanasabhāgatāṃ vijahātyāryasabhāgatāṃ pratilabhate | tṛtīyā- gatisaṃcārāt | caturthī- etānākārān sthāpayitvā |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Could one die and be reborn without losing one's own class-homogeneity and without acquiring [a new one]? [This is] a fourfold classification. The first case: one who is reborn in the very [realm] from which one died. The second: one who enters the certain path (<s>niyāma</s>), for such a one loses ordinary-person-homogeneity and acquires noble-person-homogeneity. The third: due to migration between destinies. The fourth: setting aside these categories.

body.text: atha pṛthagjanatvasyāsyāśca kaḥ prativiśeṣaḥ ? pṛthagjanasabhāgatā khalūktarūpā | pṛthagjanatvaṃ tu sarvānarthakarabhūtamiti sumahāṃstadviśeṣaḥ | āptavacanenāpi tadanyatvasiddhiḥ | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "sa ceditthatvamāgacchati manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāṃ pratilabhate" iti | na caivaṃ pṛthagjanatvaṃ pratilabhyate vā tyajyate vā |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, what is the distinction between ordinary-person-nature (<s>pṛthagjanatva</s>) and this [class-homogeneity]? Ordinary-person class-homogeneity is as described. But ordinary-person-nature is the cause of all misfortune — so the distinction between them is very great. Its otherness is also established by authoritative testimony. For the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'When one comes to such a state, one acquires the class-homogeneity of humans.' But ordinary-person-nature is not acquired or relinquished in this way.

body.text: siddhā sabhāgatā | kośakāraḥ punastāṃ vaiśeṣikaparikalpitajātipadārthena samīkurvan vyaktaṃ pāyasavāyasayorvarṇasādharmyaṃ paśyatīti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Class-homogeneity is established. The <s>Kośa</s>-author, however, equating it with the category of 'universal' (<s>jātipadārtha</s>) as imagined by the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, evidently sees a color-similarity between milk-pudding and a crow!

body.text: atha kimidamāsaṃjñikaṃ nāma ? tadapadiśyate |
body.translated_text: Now, what is this thing called '<s>āsaṃjñika</s>' (pertaining to non-perception)? This is indicated:

body.text: āsaṃjñikaṃ vipāko yaccittopacchedyasaṃjñiṣu // Abhidh-d_134 //
body.translated_text: That which is the resultant [<s>dharma</s>] effecting the cessation of mind among beings without perception — that is the <s>āsaṃjñika</s>. (Abhidh-d 134)

body.text: asaṃjñisattveṣu deveṣūpapannānāṃ yaccittopacche didharmāntaraṃ viprayuktaṃ vipākajamutpadyate tadāsaṃjñikaṃ nāma | yena tatropapannānāṃ cittamanāgate 'dhvani kālāntaraṃ sannirudhyate, notpattuṃ labhate | tatpunarekāntena vipākajasvabhāvam | kasya vipākaḥ ? asaṃjñisamāpatteḥ pūrakasya karmaṇaḥ | keṣu punastat ? devanikāyeṣu bhavati | tadāha- "asaṃjñiṣu | asaṃjñisattvā nāma devā bṛhatphaladevanikāyasaṃgṛhītā dhyānāntarikāvat |" kiṃ punaste naiva kadācit saṃjñino bhavanti ? bhavantyutpattikāle cyutikāle ca | "prakṛṣṭamapi kālaṃ sthitvā sahasaṃjñotpādātteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasmāt sthānāccyutirbhavati" iti sūtrapāṭhaḥ | te ca tato dīrghasvapnavyutthitā iva cyutvā kāmadhātāvupapadyante, nānyatra | tadupapannānāmavaśyaṃ kāmāvacarāparaparyāyavedanīyakarmasadbhāvāt | yathottarakauravāṇāṃ devopapattivedanīyaṃ karmeti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For those reborn among the gods called beings-without-perception (<s>asaṃjñisattva</s>), the disjoined, resultant (<s>vipākaja</s>) <s>dharma</s> that arises and effects the cessation of mind — that is called '<s>āsaṃjñika</s>.' By which [force], for those reborn there, mind ceases for a period of time in the future and is not able to arise. That is exclusively of resultant nature. Whose result? Of the <s>karma</s> that fulfills the attainment of non-perception (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>). In what [beings] does it exist? It exists in a class of gods. Hence it says: 'Among beings without perception. The beings without perception are gods included in the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> (Great Fruit) class of gods, like the <s>dhyānāntarikā</s> [intermediate absorption].' Do they then never have perception? They do — at the time of rebirth and at the time of death. 'Even after abiding for a long time, with the arising of perception, those beings pass away from that state' — this is the <s>sūtra</s> reading. And they, having passed away from there like [beings] waking from a long sleep, are reborn in the desire-realm — not elsewhere. Because for those reborn there, there necessarily exist desire-realm <s>karmas</s> to be experienced in the next [life]. Just as for the <s>Uttarakurus</s>, there is <s>karma</s> to be experienced at rebirth among the gods.

body.text: kā punarasāvasaṃjñisamāpattiriti ? tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: What then is the attainment of non-perception (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>)? This is indicated:

body.text: śubhāsaṃjñisamāpattirdhyāne 'ntye cittarodhinī /
body.translated_text: The wholesome attainment of non-perception, belonging to the last <s>dhyāna</s> (the fourth), inhibits mind.

body.text: āsaṃjñikamavyākṛtam | vipākaphalatvāt | iyaṃ tu śubhā | sā punariyaṃ 'dhyāne 'ntye'; caturthadhyānasaṃgṛhītetyarthaḥ | 'cittarodhinī', yathaiva tatphalaṃ cittasannirodhi tathaiveyamapi cittasaṃrodhinī | cittagrahaṇācca caittānāmanuktasiddhirādityāstagamane kiraṇāstagamanavat |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The <s>āsaṃjñika</s> is indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) — because of being a resultant fruit. But this [attainment] is wholesome. It belongs 'to the last <s>dhyāna</s>' — meaning included in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. It 'inhibits mind' — just as its fruit [i.e., the āsaṃjñika] causes the cessation of mind, so too this [attainment] restrains mind. And by the word 'mind' (<s>citta</s>), the mental factors (<s>caitta</s>) too are implicitly included — like the setting of rays when the sun sets.

body.text: kimarthaṃ punaretāṃ yoginaḥ samāpadyante ?
body.translated_text: For what purpose then do yogins enter into this [attainment]?

children.translated_text: Because of the activity of the desire for escape (<s>niḥsṛtīcchā</s>).

body.text: te hi nissaraṇasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇa manaskāreṇa tāṃ samāpadyante mokṣakāṅkṣayā | sā punariyam-
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For they enter into it through a mental attitude preceded by the perception of escape (<s>nissaraṇasaṃjñā</s>), with the aspiration for liberation. This [attainment], however —

children.translated_text: is not [for] the noble one (<s>ārya</s>).

body.text: āryā hi tāmapāyasthānamiva manyante | pṛthagjanāstu kecinmokṣasthānamiti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For noble ones regard it as a place of misfortune (<s>apāya</s>). But certain ordinary persons [regard it] as a place of liberation.

body.text: kiṃ punariyamupapattyā vā vairāgyeṇa vā labhyate ? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi ?
body.translated_text: Is this obtained by rebirth or by dispassion? No, he says. By what then?

body.text: āpyā prayogataḥ // Abhidh-d_135 //
body.translated_text: It is obtainable through deliberate effort (<s>prayoga</s>). (Abhidh-d 135)

body.text: yatnena tāmutpādayatīti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] One generates it through effort.

body.text: nirodhākhyā tu vijñeyā vijihīrṣorbhavāgrajā /
body.translated_text: But the one called 'cessation' [attainment] should be known as belonging to the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>), of one who wishes to withdraw [from mental activity].

body.text: nirodhasamāpattirapi cittacaittānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kañcitkālamutpattisannirodhinī | sā punariyaṃ vihārasaṃjñāpūvakeṇa manasikāreṇa nirvāṇasadṛśaṃ sukhamanubhavitukāmairyogibhiḥ saṃmukhīkriyate | 'bhavāgrajā'; ceyaṃ samāpattiḥ |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) too inhibits the arising of mental <s>dharmas</s> — mind and mental factors — for some time. This [attainment] is entered into by yogins who wish to experience a happiness resembling <s>nirvāṇa</s>, through a mental attitude preceded by the perception of dwelling [in peace] (<s>vihārasaṃjñā</s>). And this attainment belongs 'to the summit of existence' (<s>bhavāgra</s>).

body.text: śubhāryasya prayogāpyā dvivedyāniyatā matā // Abhidh-d_136 //
body.translated_text: It is wholesome, belongs to the noble one, is obtainable through effort, is to-be-experienced in two [lifetimes], and is considered indeterminate [as to its result]. (Abhidh-d 136)

body.text: dvayoḥ kālayorvedyā 'dvivedyā'; | upapadyavedanīyā cāparaparyāyavedanīyā ca | aniyatavedanīyā ceyam | yo hyetāmutpādya parinirvāti sa nāsyā vipākaṃ pratisaṃvedayate | tasyā hi bhavāgre catuskandhako vipāko vipacyate | āryaścaitāmutpādayituṃ śaknoti nānāryaḥ | ucchedabhīrutvācchāśvatadṛṣṭiprahāṇādāryamārgavalotpādanācca | āryasyāpi ceyaṃ prayogalabhyā na vairāgyalabhyeti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'To be experienced in two [lifetimes]' (<s>dvivedyā</s>) — to be experienced at two times: to be experienced in the present life and in the life immediately following. And this has indeterminate experiential result. For one who, having produced this [attainment], passes into final <s>nirvāṇa</s>, does not experience its result. For its result — a four-aggregate [existence] — ripens at the summit of existence. And only the noble one is capable of producing this, not the non-noble — because of fear of annihilation, because of having abandoned the eternalist view, and because of the power to produce the noble path. And this is obtainable by the noble one only through deliberate effort, not through dispassion.

body.text: atra punaḥ kośakāraḥ pratijānīte- "sacittikeyaṃ samāpattiḥ" iti |

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 94)

children.text: ) "samāpatticittameva hi taccittāntaraviruddhamutpadyate | yena kālāntaramanyasya cittasyāpravṛttimātraṃ bhavati | tadviruddhāśrayāpādanāt sāsau samāpattiriti prajñāpyate |"
children.translated_text: 'For it is the attainment-mind itself that arises in opposition to another mind. By which, for a period of time, there is merely the non-functioning of another mind. Because it brings about a support incompatible [with other minds], it is designated as that attainment.'

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here, however, the <s>Kośa</s>-author claims: 'This attainment possesses mind.'

body.text: tadetadabauddhīyam | kutaḥ ?
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This is un-Buddhist. Why?

children.translated_text: Because of the impossibility of a fourfold mind [at the summit of existence], from scripture, and from reasoning,
this [attainment] is established as mindless, because of the state of mind being renounced. (Abhidh-d 137)

body.text: bhavāgre khalu catvāri cittāni vidyante | vipākajaṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ kuśalamupapattilābhikaṃ prāyogikaṃ ca | tebhyaścaturbhyaḥ kataraccittaṃ yannirodhasamāpannasyānyacittanirodhītyucyate ?
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] At the summit of existence, there exist four kinds of mind: resultant (<s>vipākaja</s>), obscured-indeterminate (<s>nivṛtāvyākṛta</s>), wholesome, and that obtained through rebirth and through effort (<s>prāyogika</s>). Of these four, which mind is it that is said to inhibit other minds for one in the cessation-attainment?

body.text: tatra tāvadvipākajaṃ tatratyāṃ .............................
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] First, the resultant — there.............................

body.text: ".............dharme pratipattyevājñāmārādhayati | nāpi maraṇakālasamaye | bhedācca kāyasyātikramya devān kabaḍīkārabhakṣānanyatamasmin divye manomaye kāya upapadyate | sa tatropapannaḥ abhokṣṇaṃ saṃjñāveditanirodhaṃ samāpadyate ca vyuttiṣṭhate ca | asti caitatsthānamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti" iti |
body.translated_text: '...through practice in this very dharma, he fulfills knowledge. Not at the time of death either. After the breaking up of the body, having transcended the gods who consume material food, he is reborn in a certain divine mind-made body. Having been reborn there, he attains and emerges from the cessation of perception and feeling repeatedly. And he knows as it truly is: "This state exists."'

body.text: atra sthavira udāyī sthaviraśāriputramidamavocat- "mā tvamāyuṣmannevaṃ vocaḥ |" sa hi manyate sma bhāvāgrīkīyaṃ samāpattirdivyaśca manomayaḥ kāyaścaturthadhyānabhūmika ukto bhagavatā tatkathametadupapatsyate | tadetad bhadantodāyinā parihāṇimajānānenābhidharmasaṃmūḍhena pratyuktaḥ sa bhagavatā paramābhidhā makeṇāvasādanārthamabhihitaḥ- "tvamapi mohapuruṣa śāriputreṇa bhikṣuṇā sārdhaṃ gabhbhīre 'bhidharme saṃlapituṃ manyase ?" iti
body.translated_text: Thereupon the elder <s>Udāyin</s> said this to the elder <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Do not, venerable one, speak thus.' For he thought: 'The attainment belonging to the Summit of Existence and the divine mind-made body have been declared by the Blessed One as belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> level — how then would this be possible?' This [objection] was replied to by the venerable <s>Udāyin</s>, who was ignorant of falling away and confused about the <s>Abhidharma</s>. He was addressed by the Blessed One with the supreme <s>Abhidharma</s> [authority], for the purpose of humiliation: 'Do you too, foolish man, think yourself fit to converse with the monk <s>Śāriputra</s> about the profound <s>Abhidharma</s>?'

body.text: nikāyāntarīyāścaturthadhyānabhūmikāmapi nirodhasamāpattimicchanti | teṣāṃ vinā parihāṇyā siddhatyetatsūtram | etadeva tu na siddhyati- caturthadhyānabhūmikāpyasāvastīti | katham ? "navānupūrvasamāpattayaḥ" (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 97)

children.text: ) iti sūtre vacanāt | prāptakāmavaśitvāttu santaḥ paścādvilaṃdhyāpi vyutkrāntasamāpattiṃ samāpadyanta iti ||
children.translated_text: But those who have attained mastery over the desire[-realm], being noble ones, subsequently — even after delay — enter the transcendent attainment (<s>vyutkrāntasamāpatti</s>).

body.translated_text: Those of other schools, however, accept the cessation-attainment as belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> level also. For them, this sūtra is established without [recourse to the concept of] falling away. But this very [claim] is not established — that [the cessation-attainment] belongs to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> level. How? Because of the statement in the sūtra: 'There are nine successive attainments.'

body.text: vyākhyāte samāpattī |
body.translated_text: The [two] attainments have been explained.

children.translated_text: The life-span is the basis for the designation of the [five] destinies, and it is the duration of warmth and consciousness.
From scripture, reasoning, and as a substance — that is so accepted. (Abhidh-d 138)

body.text: āyurjīvitamityanarthāntaram | uktaṃ hyabhidharme- "jīvitendriyaṃ katarat ? traidhātukamāyuḥ" iti | tatpunaḥ 'gatiprajñaptyupādānaṃ'; vipākajasvabhāvatvāt | uktaṃ hi sūtre- "nirvṛtte vipāke nāraka iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati | evaṃ yāvannavasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanopagasaṃkhyāṃ gacchati" iti | na cānyadindriyaṃ vipākajaṃ traidhātuka vyāpyasti yajjanmaprabandhāvicchedena vartamānaṃ gatiprajñaptyupādānaṃ syāt, anyatra jīvitendriyāt |
body.translated_text: 'Life-span' (<s>āyus</s>) and 'life' (<s>jīvita</s>) are synonymous. For it is said in the <s>Abhidharma</s>: 'What is the life-faculty? The three-realm life-span.' That, moreover, is 'the basis for the designation of the [five] destinies,' because of having the nature of a maturation-result. For it is said in the sūtra: 'When maturation is complete, one comes to be designated as a hell-being. Likewise, up to one who comes to be designated as one born in the Realm of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception.' And no other faculty exists that is maturation-born, pervading the three realms, and — continuing in an unbroken stream of births — would serve as the basis for the designation of the destinies, other than the life-faculty.

body.text: tatpunarastīti kathaṃ gamyate ? āgamādyuktitaśca | āgamastāvadayam-
body.translated_text: How then is it known that it exists? From scripture and reasoning. The scripture is this:

children.translated_text: 'When life-span, warmth, and consciousness — these three abandon the body,
then it lies cast aside, like an unconscious piece of wood.'

body.text: sarvaṃ hi jīvitendriyaṃ kāmadhātāvavaśyaṃ kāyendriyoṣmasahacariṣṇu | tattvavaśyaṃ vijñānasahavarti nāpi cakṣurādīndriyasahavarti | rūpadhātau tu sarvaṃ kāyādipañcendriyasahavarti | na tvavaśyaṃ cittasahacariṣṇa | ārūpyadhātau tu sarvaṃ vijñānasahavarti, anyatra nirodhasamāpatteḥ |
body.translated_text: For all life-faculty in the desire-realm necessarily accompanies the body-faculty and warmth. That [life-faculty] necessarily coexists with consciousness, but not necessarily with the eye and other faculties. In the form-realm, however, all [life-faculty] coexists with the five faculties beginning with the body. But it does not necessarily accompany consciousness. In the formless realm, however, all [life-faculty] coexists with consciousness, except during the cessation-attainment.

body.text: jīvitendriyaṃ gatiprajñaptyupādānamastīti dravyam | anyathā hi kuśalanivṛtte cetasi nirmale vādhobhaume tadgatiprajñaptyupādānavipākajaṃ kiṃ kalpyeta yatsadbhāvādasau tato na pracyutaḥ syāt ? na ca śakyaṃ pratijñātumanāsravāṇāmadhobhūmivijñānabījaṃ tadgatisaṃjñaptyupādānaṃ kalpayitum, anāsravasya cittasya samucchedāya pravṛttatvāt | na cānyadvijñānaṃ tadbhaumaṃ śakyaṃ kalpayituṃ manovijñānadhātuvyatiriktasyānākāramālambanasya vijñānasyāprasiddhatvāt | manodhāturiti cet | na | manovijñānadhātorevāvasthāntare tannāmaprajñapteḥ | yuktirapi- cakṣurādivattadādhipatyaviśeṣāt |
body.translated_text: The life-faculty, being the basis for the designation of the destinies, exists as a substance (<s>dravya</s>). For otherwise, when the wholesome or immaculate mind ceases [and there is] a lower-realm [mind], what maturation-born [entity] belonging to that destiny's designation-basis would be posited, by whose existence one would not have fallen from that [destiny]? Nor can one posit that the outflow-free consciousness has seeds of a lower-level consciousness as the basis for that destiny-designation, because outflow-free mind proceeds toward the cessation [of afflictions]. Nor can one posit another consciousness belonging to that level, because a consciousness without aspect and object that is distinct from the mental-consciousness element is not established. If [one says] the mind-element (<s>manodhātu</s>) — no, because it is merely a designation for another state of the mental-consciousness element itself. Reasoning also [supports this] — because of the distinctive sovereignty, like the eye and the other [faculties].

body.text: "samādhibalena karmajaṃ jīvitāvedhaṃ nirvartyāyuḥ saṃskārādhiṣṭhānajam, āyurna vipākaḥ" iti kośakāraḥ | tatra kimuttaramiti ? na tatrāvaśyamuttaraṃ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 99)

children.text: ) vaktavyaṃ yasmānnaitatsūtre 'varati, vinaye na saṃdṛśyate, dharmatāṃ ca vilomayati | (
children.translated_text: because it does not accord with the sūtras, is not found in the <s>Vinaya</s>, and contradicts the nature of things.
(Jaini 100)
Therefore, like the words of a child, this should be disregarded.

body.translated_text: 'Through the power of concentration, having extended the karmically produced life-limit, the life-span is produced through the basis of volitions — life-span is not maturation' — thus the <s>Kośakāra</s> (<s>Vasubandhu</s>). What is the reply to that? It is not necessary to give a reply to that,

body.text: kathaṃ tāvatsūtre nāvatarati, vinaye na saṃdṛśyate ? sūtre hyaktam- "asthānamanavaka śo yatprahāṇahetorvā upakramahetorvā apakvaṃ paripācayet, paripakvaṃ vā anyena nayena nayet" iti vistaraḥ |
body.translated_text: How does it not accord with the sūtras and not appear in the <s>Vinaya</s>? For it is said in the sūtra: 'It is impossible, <s>Anavaka</s> — it cannot happen — that through an act of abandonment or through an act of injury, one could ripen what is unripened, or lead what is ripened by another route' — and so on in detail.

body.text: vinaye 'pi "niyatavedanīyaṃ triprakāraṃ karma sadevakenāpi lokena na śakyaṃ vyāvartayitum" iti parigrahaḥ |
body.translated_text: In the <s>Vinaya</s> too: 'Definitely-to-be-experienced threefold karma cannot be diverted even by the entire world with its gods' — this is the established [teaching].

body.text: abhidharme 'pi sarvāparimitamāyurākṣipyate | tasyāpakṣālāḥ kālasthānāntarāvasthānādiṣu niyamyante | ityevaṃ tāvadāgamādapetaṃ nottarārham |
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharma</s> too, all unlimited life-span is projected [by karma]. Its diminutions are fixed with respect to time, place, circumstances, and so forth. Thus, first of all, what departs from scripture is not worthy of a reply.

body.text: tathāpi tu yuktimaduttaramucyate | yadi bhagavān samādhibalena svecchayāpūrvaṃ sattvaṃ savijñānakaṃ sendriyamutpādayet, svātmano vā jīvitamanākṣiptaṃ prākkarmabhiryogabalenākṣipet, tato buddho bhagavānnārāyaṇīkṛtaḥ syāt apūrvasattvanirmāṇāt | sa ca kāruṇikatvānneva parinirvāyāt, śāsanasambhedasaṃdehāṃśca cchindyāt | tasmādvaitulikaśāstrapraveśadvāramārabdhaṃ tena bhadantenetyadhyupekṣametat |
body.translated_text: Nevertheless, a reasoned reply is given: If the Blessed One were to create through the power of concentration, by his own wish, a being with consciousness and faculties that never existed before, or were to project his own life-span that was not projected by prior karma through the force of yoga, then the Buddha Blessed One would be made into a <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> (God), because of creating new beings. And being compassionate, he would never enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and would cut through all doubts about the splitting of the teaching. Therefore, this is an opening into the <s>Vaitulika</s> (Mahāyānist) treatise that has been initiated by that venerable [<s>Vasubandhu</s>] — this should be disregarded.

body.text: atha kimāyuḥkṣayādeva maraṇaṃ bhavatyāhosvidanyathāpi ? prajñaptyāmuktam- "astyāyuḥkṣayānmaraṇaṃ na puṇyakṣayādibhiḥ? catuṣkoṭikaḥ | prathamā koṭiḥ- āyuviṃpākasya karmaṇaḥ paryādānāt | dvitīyā- bhogavipākasya | tṛtīyā- ubhayoḥ | turthī- viṣamāparihāreṇa |
body.translated_text: Now, does death occur only from the exhaustion of life-span, or also otherwise? It is said in the <s>Prajñapti</s>: 'Is there death from the exhaustion of life-span but not from the exhaustion of merit and the like?' [This forms] a four-cornered [inquiry]. First corner: from the exhaustion of the karma whose maturation is life-span. Second: from the exhaustion of [karma] whose maturation is enjoyment. Third: from both. Fourth: from failure to avoid adversity.

body.text: jñānaprasthāna uktam- "āyuḥ santatyupanibaddhaṃ vartata iti vaktavyam ? sakṛdutpannaṃ tiṣṭhatīti vaktavyam ? āha- kāmāvacarāṇāṃ sattvānāmasaṃjñisamāpattiṃ nirodhasamāpattiṃ vā samāpannānāṃ santatyupanibaddhaṃ vartata iti vaktavyam | samāpannānāṃ santatyupanibaddhaṃ vartata iti vaktavyam | samāpannānāṃ rūpārupyāvacarāṇāṃ ca sattvānāṃ sakṛdutpannaṃ tiṣṭhatīti vaktavyam ||"
body.translated_text: In the <s>Jñānaprasthāna</s> it is said: 'Should life-span be said to continue bound to the stream [of existence]? Should it be said to remain once arisen? Answer: For beings of the desire-realm who have not entered the attainment of non-perception or the cessation-attainment — it should be said to continue bound to the stream. For those who have entered [those attainments], and for beings of the form and formless realms — it should be said to remain once arisen.'

body.text: kaḥ punarasya bhāṣitasyārthaḥ ? yasyāśrayopaghātādupadhātastatsantatyadhīnatvāt prathamam | yasyāśrayopaghāta eva nāsti tadyathotpannāvasthānād dvitīyam | sāntarāyaṃ prathamaṃ nirantarāyaṃ dvitīyamiti kāśmīrāḥ | tasmādastyakālamṛtyuḥ |
body.translated_text: What then is the meaning of this statement? That [life-span] whose support is subject to damage, and which is dependent on the stream — [this is] the first [case]. That whose support has no damage at all, and which remains as produced — [this is] the second. 'The first has obstacles; the second is without obstacles' — thus the <s>Kāśmīras</s>. Therefore, untimely death (<s>akālamṛtyu</s>) exists.

body.text: sūtra uktam- "catvāra ātmabhāvapratilambhāḥ | astyātmabhāvapratilambho yatrātmasaṃcetanā krāmati na parasaṃcetanā" iti catuṣkoṭikaḥ | ātmasaṃcetanāvakrāmati kāmadhātau krīḍāpramoṣakāṇāṃ devānāṃ manaḥpradoṣakāṇāṃ ca devānām | teṣāṃ hi praharṣamanaḥpradoṣābhyāṃ tasmātsthānāccyutibhaṃvati, nānyathā | buddhānāṃ ceti vaktavyam, svayaṃmṛtyutvāt | parasaṃcetanaiva krāmati garbhāṇḍāgatānām | ubhayam- anyeṣāṃ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ prāyeṇa | nobhayam- sarveṣāmantarābhavikānāṃ rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāmekatīyānāṃ ca kāmāvacarāṇām | tadyathā nārakāṇāṃ ca darśanamārgamaitrīnirodhasamāpattisamāpannānāṃ rājarṣijinadūtajinādiṣṭaprabhṛtīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca caramabhavikānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mātustadgarbhāyāścakravartinaśca tadgarbhāyāḥ |"
body.translated_text: In the sūtra it is said: 'There are four modes of obtaining a personal existence (<s>ātmabhāvapratilambha</s>). There is obtaining a personal existence where one's own volition operates but not another's volition' — [this forms] a four-cornered [inquiry]. One's own volition operates in the desire-realm for the 'play-enjoying' gods and the 'mind-corrupting' gods. For through excessive joy and mental corruption, they fall from that state — not otherwise. And this must be said of Buddhas also, because of dying voluntarily. Another's volition alone operates for womb-born and egg-born beings. Both — for other desire-realm beings generally. Neither — for all intermediate-existence beings, form and formless realm beings, and certain desire-realm beings — namely: hell-beings, those who have entered the path of seeing, loving-kindness [meditation], or the cessation-attainment; royal sages, messengers of the Conqueror, those commissioned by the Conqueror, and the like; all beings in their final existence, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and the mother [bearing] their embryo; universal monarchs and the mother [bearing] their embryo.

body.text: vyākhyātaṃ jīvitendrim ||
body.translated_text: The life-faculty has been explained.

body.text: saṃskṛtalakṣaṇānīdānīṃ vyākhyāyiṣyante | tāni punaḥ kāni kiyanti veti ? tadupavyākhyāyate-
body.translated_text: Now the characteristics of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtalakṣaṇa</s>) will be explained. What are they, and how many? This is explained:

body.text: jātiḥ sthitirjarānāśaḥ saṃskṛtāṅkacaṣṭatuyī /
body.translated_text: Birth, duration, decay, and destruction — the group of four marks of the conditioned.

body.text: etāni khalu catvāri saṃskṛtalakṣaṇāni bhagavatābhidharme 'bhihitāni | etānyeva vineyaprayojanavaśāt sūtre sthityanyathātvamekīkṛtya trīṇyuktāni | gāthāyāṃ tvebhyo 'ṅgadvayaṃ sāmarthyādgamyamānamantarṇīya pradarśyate | sthitirhi dharmāyogamicchantī taddharmamupaguhyāvatiṣṭhate | sā ca tathā pravartamānā lokasya cittonnativiśeṣaṃ janayati | tato bhagavatānyathātvākhyayā (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 105)

children.text: ) jarayā sahoktā śrīriva kālakarṇyānubaddhā saṃvegānukūlā bhaviṣyatītyeṣo 'rthaviṣayo dṛśyate | tasmāccatvāri | itaśca-
children.translated_text: like prosperity accompanied by [its inevitable] misfortune, it will be conducive to spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>) — this purpose is evident. Therefore [there are] four. And moreover:

body.translated_text: Indeed, these four characteristics of the conditioned were stated by the Blessed One in the <s>Abhidharma</s>. These very same, according to the purposes of those to be trained, are stated as three in the sūtra by combining duration and alteration (<s>anyathātva</s>). But in verse [form], by concealing two aspects that are understood by implication from among these, [only two] are displayed. For duration, desiring the [continued] conjunction of a dharma, embraces that dharma and persists. And while so operating, it generates a special elevation of mind in the world. Therefore, when stated by the Blessed One together with alteration — i.e., decay — under the name 'anyathātva,'

body.text: catvāri sthitināstitve hetutvādyaprasiddhitaḥ // Abhidh-d_139 //
body.translated_text: Four — because from the non-existence of duration, the causal function and the like would not be established. (Abhidh-d 139)

body.text: yadi hi dharmasya sthitirna syāt, tasyātmanyavasthitasya hetvākhyaḥ śaktiprabhāvaviśeṣo na syāt | anityatāgrastasya ca notpaktiśaktirityataśca kriyāṃ na kuryāt | kriyābhāvātphalābhāvaḥ syāt | phalārthaścāyamārambhaḥ | tasmādāstikairnāstikapakṣaṃ vikṣipya sthitiḥ pratigṛhyata iti siddham ||
body.translated_text: For if a dharma had no duration, then — while abiding in its own nature — the distinctive power-capacity called 'cause' would not exist for it. And for one consumed by impermanence, the power of production would not [exist] — therefore it would not perform [its] function either. From the absence of function, there would be an absence of fruit. And this enterprise is for the sake of fruit. Therefore, by the realists (<s>āstika</s>), having cast away the nihilist (<s>nāstika</s>) position, duration is accepted — this is established.

body.text: catvārīti na siddhyanti jarābhāvāt | bhavatu sthitiḥ, jarā tu sarvathā na yujyate | katham ? uktaṃ hi-
body.translated_text: [But they say] four is not established — because of the non-existence of decay. Let duration be [accepted]; but decay is in no way tenable. How? For it is said:

children.translated_text: 'If [decay] is established while [the thing remains] the same — then [it is already] decayed [at the start]. If in alteration — then it is something else entirely.
Therefore, decay of a single entity is untenable.'

body.text: taṃ pratīdamucyate-
body.translated_text: In reply to that, this is said:

children.translated_text: Decay is established from the diminution of power.

body.text: unmiṣito hi dharmo jāyate hṛṣitaḥ phalamākṣipatīti | tasya yadi jarasā śaktirna vihanyeta sa dvitīyamapi phalamākṣipeta | na ca śaknotyākṣeptum | tasmādgamyate kaścijjarākhyaḥ śatruastaṃ jarjarīkṛtyopahṛtasāmarthyamanityatāpiśācyāḥ samarpayatīti yuktamuktam 'śaktihānerjarāsiddhiḥ'; iti | naitadyuktamuktaṃ pariṇāmadoṣaprasaṅgāt | evaṃ laghvācakṣāṇena bhavatā sāṃkhyīyaḥ pariṇāmo 'bhyupagato bhavati | nābhyupagataḥ, yasmāt-
body.translated_text: For a dharma arises in a manifest, vigorous [state] and projects its fruit. If its power were not impaired by decay, it would project a second fruit also. But it is unable to project [a second fruit]. Therefore, it is understood that some enemy called 'decay,' having shattered it and impaired its capacity, delivers it to the demoness of impermanence. Thus it is rightly said: 'Decay is established from the diminution of power.' [Objection:] This is not rightly said — because of the fault of [entailing] transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>). By speaking thus lightly, you have accepted the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [concept of] transformation. [Reply:] It is not accepted, because:

body.text: nānyatvāt pariṇāmitā /
body.translated_text: There is no transformation, because of [there being] difference.

body.text: anya eva hi no jarākhyo dharmo, anyaśca dharmī | sāṃkhyasya tvavasthitasya dharmiṇaḥ svātmabhūtasya dharmāntarasyotsargaḥ svātmabhūtasya cotpādaḥ pariṇāma iti |
body.translated_text: For the dharma called 'decay' is indeed different [from the substrate], and the substrate (<s>dharmin</s>) is different. But for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, the relinquishing of one property belonging to a persisting substrate's own self and the arising of another [property] belonging to its own self — that is transformation.

body.text: kathaṃ punaḥ kṣaṇikasya dharmasya śaktihānirbhavati ? evam- yasmādasyājahadātmakasya-
body.translated_text: How then can there be diminution of power for a momentary dharma? Thus — because, for this [dharma] which does not abandon its own nature:

body.text: ekakāritranāśābhyāṃ śaktihāniḥ prasiddhyati // Abhidh-d_140 //
body.translated_text: The diminution of power is established from performing a single function and from destruction. (Abhidh-d 140)

body.text: yena khalu dārḍhyenopeto yamekaṃ phalamākṣipate, yadi tenaiva yuktaḥ syād dvitīyamapyākṣipet | na cainaṃ śaktimantamanityatā hiṃsyāt | tasmād gamyate 'nyathībhūto 'yamanityatāvyāghrīmukhaṃ praviśati | ityekaṃ phalamākṣipya naśyatītyuktametat- 'ekakāritranāśābhyāṃ śaktihāniḥ prasiddhyati |'
body.translated_text: Indeed, if [a dharma], endowed with the very strength by which it projects a single fruit, were to remain equally endowed [with that strength], it would project a second [fruit] too. And impermanence would not harm it while it possesses [such] power. Therefore, it is understood that, having become altered, it enters the mouth of the tigress of impermanence. Thus, having projected a single fruit, it perishes — this is stated: 'The diminution of power is established from performing a single function and from destruction.'

body.text: na prasiddhyati, nirhetukatvādvināśasya | ye hyarthatmāno hetumantaste khalvanityā dṛṣṭāḥ | katham ? aṃkuravat | na vināśasya vināśo 'sti, tasmādahetukaḥ | kiñca, ye cārthātmānaḥ paścādbhavanti teṣāṃ pūrvaheturasti tadyathā bhasmano bījādisaṃyogaḥ | na ca vināśasya heturasti | tasmādasau na paścādbhavatīti | tatra yaduktaṃ jātasya sthityanyathātvamapekṣya vināśo bhavatīti tadayuktam | atra pratyavasthānam-
body.translated_text: is not established, because destruction is causeless. For those that are entities with causes are seen to be impermanent. How? Like a sprout. There is no destruction of destruction — therefore it is causeless. Furthermore, those entities that come into being later have a prior cause — for example, the conjunction of seed and so forth [is the cause] of ash. But destruction has no cause; therefore it does not come into being later. Regarding what was stated — that destruction occurs in dependence on the stability and alteration of what has arisen — that is incorrect. Here is the counter-position:

children.translated_text: Given that birth exists, because [destruction] depends on it; because of the destruction of the capacity of a substance;
from scripture and from reasoning — destruction too has a cause. (Abhidh-d 141)

body.text: saheturvināśa iti sthāpanā | kutaḥ ? 'sati janmani tadbhāvāt |'; uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "asmin satīdaṃ bhavati | yāvadavidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ |" sati cotpattimati vināśo bhavati | tasmātsahetukaḥ | yasya punarahetukastasya prāgapi janmanaḥ so 'stīti janmaiva na syāt, viruddhānāmanyataropapatteḥ | tayoravirodhādvā tadvyapadeśānupapattiratāddharmyaṃ ca saṃskārāṇāmiti |
body.translated_text: The thesis is established that destruction has a cause. From what? 'Given that birth exists, because [destruction] depends on it.' For the Blessed One stated: 'This existing, that comes to be; as far as: conditioned by ignorance are the formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>).' And destruction occurs when there is something that has arisen; therefore [destruction] has a cause. But for those [who say destruction] is causeless, [destruction] would exist even prior to birth — and then birth itself would not occur, because one of two contradictories [would apply]. Or, if the two are non-contradictory, the designation [of destruction] would be untenable — and that would mean the formations are eternal.

body.text: dharmanāstitvamātraṃ vināśa iti cet | na | tadastitvapūrvakatvāt | astitvapūrvakaṃ hi tannāstitvamiti tadapi sahetukam | nāsti kiñcittaditi cet | na | astitvavirodhānupapatteḥ | kiñca, bhāvavirodhitve satyabhāvasya bhavatāpatteḥ | avirodhitve bhāvanityatvaprasaṃgādubhayābhāve vāṅmātratvāt | kā caiṣā vāco yuktiḥ sati ca bhavati tadviśeṣyaścātadvirodhī (

children.translated_text: [Reference:] Jaini p. 108.

children.text: ) ca | na ca kiñcidityevaiṣā vācoyuktirasaṃbaddhā | nirarthikā caiṣā vācoyuktiḥ | ataste bhāvābhāvo vāgvastumātram | pratiṣedhasāmarthātpratiṣedhyo bhāvo 'stīti cet | nāsti | śaśaviṣāṇavacchabdo gaḍumātratvātpratiṣedhadvayārthānupapatteśca | kiñca, kāritramātranāśācca | viruddhapratyayasānnidhye kriyāmātraṃ hi nodeti, naśyati | tasmānnānarthavān vināśaśabdaḥ | kutaśca ? āgamādupapatteśca |
children.translated_text: and yet 'there is nothing'? This is incoherent verbal reasoning. And this is meaningless verbal reasoning. Therefore your [notion of] the non-existence of being is a mere verbal fiction. Objection: From the capacity of negation, the being that is negated exists. Reply: It does not exist — like the horn of a hare; because the word is mere sound; and because the meaning of both negation [and affirmation] is untenable. Furthermore, because of the destruction of mere capacity [for activity]. In the proximity of a contrary condition, mere activity does not arise — [it] perishes. Therefore the word 'destruction' is not meaningless. And from what else? From scripture and from reasoning.

body.translated_text: Objection: Destruction is merely the non-existence of a dharma. Reply: No — because it is preceded by existence. For that non-existence is preceded by existence — hence it too has a cause. Objection: There is nothing that is 'that' [which is destroyed]. Reply: No — because the contradiction of existence is untenable. Furthermore, if non-being (<s>abhāva</s>) were contradictory to being, then non-being would become a real entity (<s>bhavat</s>). If they are non-contradictory, there would be the consequence of the eternality of being; and if both are absent, it is mere words. And what kind of verbal reasoning is this — [to say] that [something] exists and arises, and that its qualifier is non-contradictory to it,

body.text: uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "utpannānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirodhāya" iti | tathoktam- "ihaikatīyaḥ prāṇātipātiko bhavati" iti vistaraḥ | tathā- "tisraḥ saṃvartanyo 'nalajalānilākhyā yābhiḥ krameṇa yāvacchubhakṛtsnā vinaśyante" iti | tathā- "jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇam" iti |
body.translated_text: For the Blessed One stated: 'For the cessation of arisen unwholesome dharmas.' And likewise: 'Here, a certain one is a killer of living beings' — and so forth in detail. And likewise: 'There are three destructions — called fire, water, and wind — by which, in succession, [everything] up to the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> [heavens] is destroyed.' And likewise: 'Conditioned by birth are old age and death.'

body.text: upapattirapi | janmano 'pyahetukatvaprasaṃgāt | yadi khalvasati sadbhāve 'pyahetuko vināśaḥ, janmāpyahetukaṃ bhavatviti | tatsamarthahetusāmagrīsannidhāne janmadarśanāt, tatsahetukatvamiti cet | na | tadvināśe tulyatvāttasyāpi samarthahetusāmagryantarasannidhānābhyupagamāt |
body.translated_text: And reasoning [supports this]: because causelessness would be equally entailed for birth. For if destruction were causeless even when there is an occurrence of being from non-being, then let birth too be causeless! Objection: Since birth is observed in the presence of a capable assemblage of causes, it [i.e., birth] has causes. Reply: No — because the same applies in the case of destruction too — since we acknowledge the presence of another capable assemblage of causes for that [destruction] as well.

body.text: vyākhyātāni lakṣaṇāni ||
body.translated_text: The characteristics have been explained.

body.text: nāmakāyādayo vaktavyāḥ | na khalu vaktavyāḥ | na hi te śabdādanye vidyante, svabhāvakriyābhāvāditi | tadupadarśanārthamidamārabhyate |
body.translated_text: The name-bodies (<s>nāmakāya</s>) and so forth must be stated. [Opponent:] They need not be stated, for they do not exist apart from sound — because of the absence of inherent nature and activity. To demonstrate this, the following is undertaken:

children.translated_text: Their birth depends on vocal speech and sound; their activity is the communication of their own meaning;
having the alternative names 'designation' (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and so forth — three [categories], name and the rest, are remembered. (Abhidh-d 142)

body.text: viprayuktāḥ khalu nāmādayaḥ saṃskāraskandhasaṃgṛhītāḥ | vāk tu rūpaskandhasaṃgṛhītā vāggīrniruktirityarthaḥ | te ca tadadhīnotpattayo niruktyadhīnārthapravṛttayaśca (

children.translated_text: [Reference:] Jaini p. 109.

children.text: ) jñānavadarthasya pratinidhisthānīyāḥ | niruktiḥ nāma saṃjñā | nārthānāmekasaṃjñatvāt | yathā tu cakṣurvijñānakāyādayaḥ pañcarūpādyāyattavṛttayaḥ, tadvatte 'pi 'vākchabdādhīnajanmānaḥ'; | ataścoktam- "vāṅ nāmni pravartate, nāmārthaṃ dyotayati |" iti | vācā saha kacaṭatapādayo jāyante tayā nidhīyanta iti | prativarṇānuvartinīnāṃ vācāṃ sāvayavatve 'pi sati tadabhidhānānupapattiriti cet | na | śabdabhedasaṃcayasya pratyayatve tadabhidhānasāmarthyopapatteḥ |
children.translated_text: They stand as representatives of meaning for knowledge. Articulation means designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>) — because things do not have a single designation. Just as the five consciousness-bodies [beginning with] the eye-consciousness have their operation dependent on the five forms and so forth, so too these [name-bodies] 'have their birth dependent on speech and sound.' And therefore it is stated: 'Speech operates in the name; the name illuminates the meaning.' With speech the [letters] ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa and so forth are born; by it they are deposited. Objection: Since speeches that follow each individual letter, even though possessing parts, cannot designate [an entire meaning]. Reply: No — because when the accumulation of distinct sounds is the condition, the capacity for that designation is tenable.

body.translated_text: Name and the rest are indeed forces dissociated from mind (<s>viprayukta</s>), included in the aggregate of formations (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>). But speech (<s>vāk</s>) is included in the form aggregate — speech, language, articulation — this is the meaning. And they have their arising dependent on that [speech], and their operation of communicating meaning is dependent on articulation.

body.text: kiñca, kriyayā ca tadastitvaṃ nirdhāryate | kā ca setyucyate | svārthapratyāyanaṃ kriyā | svaṃ svamarthaṃ pratyāyayatyapauruṣeyatvānnāmārthasaṃbandhasyaiṣa teṣāṃ kṛtāntaḥ |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, their existence is determined by [their] activity. And what is that [activity]? It is stated: 'The communication of one's own meaning is the activity.' It communicates its own particular meaning — because the relation of name and meaning is impersonal (<s>apauruṣeya</s>); this is their established conclusion.

body.text: te punarnāmasaṃjñādyaparanāmānaḥ |
body.translated_text: They further have the alternative names 'name-body,' 'designation,' and so forth.

body.text: tatra nāmaparyāyaḥ saṃjñākaraṇaṃ yathā ghaṭa iti |
body.translated_text: Therein, the synonym of 'name' is 'designation' (<s>saṃjñā</s>/<s>karaṇa</s>) — as for example 'pot' (<s>ghaṭa</s>).

body.text: padaparyāyo vākyam | yathā ghaṭo dṛśyata iti | yena kriyāguṇakālaviśeṣā gamyanta iti kvacit | "yāvadbhirarthavadbhiḥ padairvivakṣitārthaparipūrirbhavati tāvatāṃ samūhaḥ padam" ityābhidharmikāḥ |
body.translated_text: The synonym of 'word' (<s>pada</s>) is 'sentence' (<s>vākya</s>) — as for example 'The pot is seen.' By which the distinctions of action, quality, and time are understood, according to some. 'The aggregate of as many meaningful words as bring about the completion of the intended meaning — that is a word (<s>pada</s>)' — thus the <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s>.

body.text: vyañjanaparyāyo 'kṣaraṃ yathā ka ityetadakṣaraṃ niravayavamamūrtamapratighaṃ rūpalakṣaṇavimuktaṃ traikālikārthapratyāyanasamarthaṃ manovada pratihatagamanamiti |
body.translated_text: The synonym of 'syllable' (<s>vyañjana</s>) is 'letter' (<s>akṣara</s>) — as for example the letter 'ka.' This letter is partless, immaterial, non-resistant, free from the characteristic of form, capable of communicating objects of all three times, and [yet] its movement is obstructed like that of mind.

body.text: na, asiddhatvāt | na khalu vākchabdādanye nāmādayaḥ siddhyanti | vākchabda evārtheṣu saṃjñākartṛkṛtāvadhiḥ smṛtyā gṛhītāvayavasamudāyaḥ śroturarthaṃ pratyāyayatīti kimanyairnāmādibhiḥ parikalpitaiḥ ? tatredaṃ pratyavasthīyate-
body.translated_text: Reply: No — because [this is] unestablished. Name and the rest are not established apart from vocal speech-sound. Vocal speech-sound alone — with conventional boundaries established by a designation-maker — being an aggregate of parts grasped by memory — communicates the meaning to the hearer. What need then for other fabricated name-bodies and the rest? To this the counter-position is established:

body.text: anye nāmādayaḥ śabdādaprāptārthaprakāśanāt /
body.translated_text: Name and the rest are other than sound, because they illuminate meaning without reaching [it].

body.text: śabdo hiparamāṇusaṃcayaḥ | sa prāpyārthaṃ prakāśayet, pradīpavat | nājātadhvastasvargādideśasthānarthān prāptuṃ śaknoti | tasmātpratipadyasva na śabdo 'rthaṃ pratyāyatīti | itaśca kramayaugapadyapratyāyanāsaṃbhavāt | katham ? balvajavat | iha hi bahūni balvajadravyāṇi pratyekamasamarthāni saṃbhūya rajjvātmanāvasthitāni dārvādyākarṣaṇakriyāsāmarthyopetāni bhavanti | na caivaṃ vākyātmānaḥ śabdāḥ buddhyupagṛhotāvayavasamudāyasaṃkṣepāḥ kramalabdhajanmānaḥ pratyekamarthapratyāyanasamarthāḥ, nāpi saṃbhūya pratyāyayanti, saṃbhūyānavasthānād balvajavat | tasmātkramayaugapadyātpratyāyanāsaṃbhavānna śabdāḥ kañcidarthaṃ pratyāyayantīti siddham |
body.translated_text: Sound is an accumulation of atoms. It could illuminate meaning by reaching it, like a lamp. But it cannot reach meanings situated in unborn, destroyed, or heavenly and other locations. Therefore accept that sound does not communicate meaning! And further: because sequential and simultaneous communication is impossible. How? Like <s>balvaja</s>-grass. For here many <s>balvaja</s>-grass strands, each individually incapable, having come together and established in the form of a rope, become endowed with the capacity for the activity of pulling wood and the like. But sounds constituting a sentence — being aggregates of parts grasped by the intellect, having birth obtained sequentially — are not individually capable of communicating meaning, nor do they communicate [meaning] by coming together, because they do not persist together, like <s>balvaja</s>-grass. Therefore, because of the impossibility of communication either sequentially or simultaneously, it is established that sounds do not communicate any meaning.

body.text: itaśca, pratyāyyapratyāyakādisaṃbandhānupapatteḥ | katham ? pradīpavat | tadyathā pradīpastamasi ghaṭādipratyāyyapratyāyakaśaktiyukto ghaṭadarśanārthibhirupādīyate na ca kaścicchabdaḥ kasmiṃścidarthe kenacitsaṃbandhiviśeṣeṇa niyatavṛttiḥ, yastaṃ gṛhītvā pratyāyayemeti |
body.translated_text: And further: because the relationship of communicated-object and communicator and so forth is untenable. How? Like a lamp. Just as a lamp, possessing the power of being a communicator of communicated objects such as pots and so forth in darkness, is employed by those desiring to see a pot — but no sound has a fixed operation with respect to any object through any particular relational connection by which it could, having grasped that [meaning], communicate [it].

body.text: tatra tāvat | na pradīpasyeva pratyāyyapratyāyakasaṃbandho 'sti | akṛtasaṃketasyāpratyāyanāt | nāpi saṃyogākhyaḥ saṃbandho 'sti sadasatostadanupapatteḥ | guṇatvācceti kasmiścinna samavāyākhyaḥ | ata evākāśaguṇatvācceti kaścit | tasmātpratyāyyapratyāyanādisaṃbandhānupapatteḥ yadagadiṣma na śabdo 'rthaṃ pratyāyayatīti tatsamyagabhyadhāmeti |
body.translated_text: Therein: there is no relationship of communicated-and-communicator like that of a lamp — because one who has not made a convention does not communicate. Nor is there a relationship called 'conjunction' (<s>saṃyoga</s>) — because that is untenable between the existent and non-existent. Nor, according to some, is there [a relationship called] 'inherence' (<s>samavāya</s>) in anything — because [name] is a quality. And hence, according to some, because it is a quality of space. Therefore, because of the untenability of the relationship of communicated-and-communicator and so forth, what we stated — that sound does not communicate meaning — that we have correctly maintained.

body.text: sāmayikaḥ śabdo 'rthapratyāyanaliṅgamiti cet | na | sādhyatvādvitarkavicārādhīnajanmanaḥ śabdasya kramayaugapadyapratyāyanānupapatteśca | prativarṇaviṣayā smṛtiḥ pratyāyayatīti cet | na | tatsamānadoṣatvātpūrvapakṣotsargatvācca | saṃskāra iti cet | na | asiddhatvāduktottaratvācca | yādṛcchikasaṃvṛttiśabdamātrābhyupagame vakṣyamāṇadoṣaprasaṃgācceti |
body.translated_text: Objection: Sound is conventional, a sign of meaning-communication. Reply: No — because [it is] to be proved; because sound, whose birth depends on <s>vitarka</s> (conceptual thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (discursive thought), cannot sequentially or simultaneously communicate. Objection: Memory directed at each letter communicates. Reply: No — because of the same fault, and because of abandoning the prior thesis. Objection: [It is] a <s>saṃskāra</s> (formation). Reply: No — because of being unestablished, and because of the previously stated reply; and because, in accepting mere conventional (<s>sāṃvṛtika</s>) arbitrary words, the faults to be stated would follow.

body.text: kiṃ punarete nāmakāyādayo nityā āhosvidanityā iti ?
body.translated_text: Now, are these name-bodies and so forth permanent or impermanent?

children.translated_text: They are to be known as impermanent.

body.text: tu śabdo 'nityatvavādaviśeṣa | rtho hetuḥ | ka iti cet | so 'yamucyate-
body.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) indicates the particular [view of] the impermanence-thesis. The meaning is the reason. What [reason]? It is stated:

body.text: sāpekṣārthavibhāvanāt // Abhidh-d_143 //
body.translated_text: Because of their dependent illumination of meaning. (Abhidh-d 143)

body.text: katham ? jñānavat | tadyathā jñānaṃ cakṣurādīn hetūnapekṣyārthaṃ vibhāvayati tadvannāmādayo 'pi ghoṣādīn hetūnapekṣyārthaṃ pratyāyayanti | tasmātsāpekṣapratyāyanādanityā iti ||
body.translated_text: How? Like knowledge. Just as knowledge illuminates its object in dependence on causes such as the eye and so forth, so too name and the rest communicate meaning in dependence on causes such as vocal sound and so forth. Therefore, because of their dependent communication, they are impermanent.

body.text: yadi tarhi nāmādayo 'rthaṃ pratyāyayanti, tatkathamidaṃ sadbhirapyucyate- 'śabdo 'rthaṃ pratyāyayati'; iti ? tadatrābhidhīyate-
body.translated_text: If then name and the rest communicate meaning, how can it also be stated by the wise that 'sound communicates meaning'? To this it is stated:

children.translated_text: Sound, manifesting its own form, and the syllables and so forth, certainly —
communicates meaning — [thus] the wise speak by way of figurative attribution (<s>bhaktikalpanā</s>). (Abhidh-d 144)

body.text: āñjasā hi vāṅ nāmni pravartate nāmābhilapatotyarthaḥ | nāma tvarthaṃ dyotayatīti prativarṇānuvartino vāk khalu nāmābhilapanto svañca rūpamudbhāvayantī santānena pravartamānā guṇakalpanayārthaṃ pratyāyayatītyapadiśyate | na tvarthaḥ śabdavācyo dyotyo vā |
body.translated_text: For directly, speech operates in the name — meaning, [speech] articulates the name. But the name illuminates the meaning. Speeches that follow each letter, while articulating the name and manifesting their own form, operating in continuity — are figuratively said to communicate meaning. But meaning is not the expressible or the illuminable of sound [directly].

body.text: itaśca na śabdo 'rthaṃ pratyāyayati | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: And hence sound does not communicate meaning. Because:

body.text: paramāṇusvabhāvatvād ghoṣaikatvaṃ na yujyate /
body.translated_text: Because of its atomic nature, unity with vocal sounds is not tenable.

body.text: "edaitau kaṇṭhatālavyau" iti pratijñāyate | na caikasyāṇuvacanasya viśliṣṭasthānadvaye vṛttirupapadyate | paramāṇusaṃghātasya tūpapadyate | paramāṇavo 'pi pratyekaṃ na pratyāyayanti, digbhāgāstitvanāstitve tadabhāvācceti | samudāyo 'pi madhyasthairapratyāyanānumānādantadvayenāpi na pratyāyayatītyadhyavasīyate | (

children.translated_text: [Reference:] Jaini p. 112.

children.text: ) na cārthāntaraṃ samudāyibhyaḥ samudāyo 'sti | sa kathamarthaṃ pratyāyayiṣyatīti | atītavarṇasamudāyastvantyavarṇāpekṣo manobuddhyopagṛhītasvarūpaḥ saṃbandhinyarthe buddhimutpādayan pratyāyayatīti yuktarūpo vyapadeśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Nor is the aggregate an entity other than its constituents. How could it communicate meaning? But the aggregate of past letters, dependent on the final letter, its own form being grasped by the mental faculty — producing cognition in the related meaning — communicates; this is the appropriate designation.

body.translated_text: It is acknowledged: 'E and ai are guttural and palatal.' And the operation of a single atomic utterance in two separated places [of articulation] is untenable. But for an aggregate of atoms it is tenable. Atoms individually also do not communicate — because of the presence and absence of directional parts, [communication] is absent from them. And it is concluded by those who are neutral that the aggregate too does not communicate through either [of the two] — because of the inference from non-communication by those in the middle.

body.text: atra mīmāṃsakavaiyyākaraṇau pratyācakṣāte | nāsiddhatvāt | na khalu śabdasya paramāṇumayatvaṃ siddham | tasmādanuttarametat | tau pratyabhidhīyate |
body.translated_text: Here the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> and the grammarian object: [Your thesis is] not [valid] because of non-establishment. For the atomic nature of sound is not established. Therefore this [argument] is without reply. They are answered:

children.translated_text: Its identity [as atoms is established] from its being obstructable.

body.text: pratihanyate khalu śabdaḥ prākārabhittyādiṣu tasmātpratighātī śabda iti | na | asiddham | siddhasādhanādasiddheḥ | yatkhalu bhavatā pratighātitvenāprasiddhaṃ paramāṇumayatvaṃ sādhyata ityasadetat | tatredaṃ pratyavasthīyate |
body.translated_text: Sound is indeed obstructed at walls, ramparts, and so forth — therefore sound is obstructable. Reply: No — [this is] unestablished; unestablished because of proving what is already proven. For what you seek to prove — namely, atomic nature — is itself unproven as 'obstructability.' To this the counter-position is established:

body.text: tatsiddhirvaraṇādibhiḥ // Abhidh-d_145 //
body.translated_text: Its establishment [comes] from obstruction and so forth. (Abhidh-d 145)

body.text: ālāṅgalagrāhebhyaḥ siddhametadgarbhagṛhāntargatena pihite kavāṭe 'bhihanyamānāḥ paṭahāḥ dhmāpyamānāśca śaṃkhā na śrūyante | hūṇanāḍonirghoṣeṇa ca nagaraprākārāṇi pātyante | tasmātsiddhena jālmajenāsiddhasya sādhanamidamāviṣkriyate nāsiddheneti |
body.translated_text: From evidence of obstructions: when one is inside an inner room with the door shut, drums being struck and conches being blown are not heard. And by the blast of Hūṇa war-trumpets (<s>nāḍī</s>), city ramparts are brought down. Therefore this demonstration of the unestablished by means of what is established — [and not] by means of what is unestablished — is made clear by one of simple understanding.

body.text: yadapyucyate sphoṭaḥ śabdo dhvaniḥ śabdaguṇa iti tatrāpadiśyate-
body.translated_text: As to what is stated — that <s>sphoṭa</s> is sound, [and] that <s>dhvani</s> (audible sound) is a quality of sound — to this it is stated:

body.text: sphoṭākhyo nāparo ghoṣācchabdo nityaḥ prasiddhyati /
body.translated_text: No other sound called <s>sphoṭa</s>, apart from audible sound (<s>ghoṣa</s>), is established as permanent.

body.text: tasmāddhdhaniḥ śabdaḥ sphoṭa ityanarthāntaram | yathā hastaḥ karaḥ pāṇiriti lokaprasiddhametat | tasmāt-
body.translated_text: Therefore <s>dhvani</s>, <s>śabda</s>, and <s>sphoṭa</s> are not different things. Just as 'hand' (<s>hasta</s>), 'hand' (<s>kara</s>), and 'hand' (<s>pāṇi</s>) — this is well-known in the world. Therefore —

body.text: kramavṛtterna śabdena kaścidartho 'bhidhīyate // Abhidh-d_146 //
body.translated_text: no object is expressed by a word that operates in sequence. (Abhidh-d 146)

body.text: iti prāgāviṣkṛtametat | tanmā pramoṣīḥ ||
body.translated_text: This has already been revealed previously. Do not forget it.

body.text: yadapyucyate vaiyākaraṇaiḥ śabdo buddhinirgrāhya eṣa vaiśeṣikairapi śrotragrāhyaḥ, śabdasyānyatve 'pi ca śabdatvādayaḥ śrotreṇa gṛhyanta iti | tayoridamucyate-
body.translated_text: As for what the grammarians (<s>vaiyākaraṇa</s>) say — that sound is grasped by the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) — and the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> also [say] that it is grasped by the ear; and that even when sound itself is different, soundness (<s>śabdatva</s>) and the like are grasped by the ear — to both of them this is said:

children.text: na śrutyā śrūyate śabdastadanyā ca gatiḥ śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: Sound is not heard by hearing; and no other function of hearing [exists] —
whoever says this would make himself a laughing-stock among the learned. (Abhidh-d 147)

body.text: iti | tasmātpratītapadārthako loke dhvaniḥ śabdaḥ | tataścānye nāmādayaḥ sarvārthaviṣayā iti sthāpanā |
body.translated_text: Therefore, a sound (<s>dhvani</s>) that is a conventionally understood referent in the world is [what is called] <s>śabda</s> (word/sound). And other [entities] such as names (<s>nāma</s>) and the like, which have all things as their objects, are different from that — this is the position.

body.text: pratidyotyaṃ yathāyogaṃ niyatāniyatāśca te /
body.translated_text: They illuminate their referents as appropriate, and are of fixed and unfixed [connection] —
