body.text: tatra ya āryayā niruktyā nirucyante dvādaśāyatanaviṣayāste niyatābhidheyasaṃbandhāḥ, laukikyāśca kecinniyatābhidheyā nirucyante | ubhaye 'pyete kṛtasaṃketasyārthaṃ pratyāyayanti | ye tu yathecchaṃ pitrādibhiḥ kriyante nāmakāyādibhiste hyaniyatā yadṛcchikā ityucyante | tadyathā ḍitthaḍavitthādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, those that are etymologized by the noble (<s>ārya</s>) etymology (<s>nirukti</s>) — having as their scope the twelve <s>āyatanas</s> — have a fixed connection with their referent. And some worldly [words] too are etymologized with a fixed referent. Both of these communicate meaning to one who has [learned] the convention. But those name-groups (<s>nāmakāya</s>) and the like that are created at will by parents and others — they are unfixed, called 'accidental' (<s>yādṛcchika</s>). For example, '<s>Ḍittha</s>,' '<s>Ḍavittha</s>,' and so forth.

body.text: prathamāstu buddhotpāda eva pravartante nānyadeti | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "tathāgatānāmutpādānnāmapadavyañjanakāyānāmutpādo bhavati" ityetasmāt-
body.translated_text: But the primary [words] come into operation only upon the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>, not otherwise. For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'From the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the arising of name-groups, word-groups, and syllable-groups occurs.' Therefore —

body.text: niyatodbhāvanād buddhaḥ sarvajña iti gamyate // Abhidh-d_148 //
body.translated_text: from the invariable manifestation [of words], the <s>Buddha</s> is understood to be omniscient. (Abhidh-d 148)

body.text: ye hyapaurūṣeyā dhātvāyatanaskandhādyavadyotakāste prathamaṃ buddhaviṣayā eva | tadavabodhācca bhagavānsarvajña ityabhidhīyate | te punarete-
body.translated_text: For those [words] that are non-personal (<s>apauruṣeya</s>), illuminating <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, <s>skandhas</s>, and the like — they are first within the domain of the <s>Buddha</s> alone. And because of his comprehension of them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> is called omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>). These, furthermore —

body.text: sattvākhyāḥ kāmarūpāptā niṣyandāvyākṛtāstathā /
body.translated_text: are designated as 'belonging to sentient beings' (<s>sattvākhya</s>), [found] in the desire and form realms, outflow-resultant (<s>niṣyanda</s>), and unobstructed-indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) —

body.text: sattvākhyā hyete | yaśca dyotayati sa taiḥ samanvāgataḥ | na yo dyotyate | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 114)
They belong to the desire and form realms, because their birth depends on vocal sound. They are outflow-resultant (<s>naiṣyandika</s>) and unobstructed-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>).

body.translated_text: for these are designated as 'belonging to sentient beings.' And the one who illuminates [meaning] is endowed with them, not the one who is illuminated.

body.text: yathā caite nāmādayaḥ
body.translated_text: And just as these names and the like [are such],

body.text: tathaiva ca vipākaśca sābhāgyaṃ prāptayo dvidhā // Abhidh-d_149 //
body.translated_text: so too maturation (<s>vipāka</s>), fortunateness (<s>sābhāgya</s>), and acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>) are twofold. (Abhidh-d 149)

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau dvitīyasyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the third section (<s>pāda</s>) of the second chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the second chapter.

body.text: tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Third chapter.

body.text: caturthapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: Fourth section.

body.text: ................ | dvitīyaṃ dvitīyasyāḥ | tṛtīyaṃ tṛtīyasyāḥ | vāyusaṃvartanyāścaturthadhyānaṃ śīrṣamiti |
body.translated_text: ................ The second [destruction cycle belongs] to the second [<s>dhyāna</s>]. The third to the third. The summit of the wind-destruction (<s>vāyusaṃvartanī</s>) is the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: atrāha- caturthadhyāne saṃvartanī kasmānna bhavati ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Here one asks: Why does no destruction-cycle occur in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>? This is stated:

children.translated_text: Because of the absence of calamities (<s>upadrava</s>) called 'belonging to sentient beings' — in the fourth [<s>dhyāna</s>] there is none, according to the <s>sūtras</s>.
From the destruction of the abode of equanimity, whence permanence? (Abhidh-d 150)

body.text: caturthe khalu dhyāne bāhyādhyātmikā apakṣālā na vidyante tasmānna saṃvartano utpādyate | prathame hi dhyāne vitarkavicāra vagnikalpāvapakṣālabhūtau vidyete | dvitīye prītirapkalpā cetopahāriṇī | tṛtīye dhyāne āśvāsapraśvāsā (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 116)

children.text: ) vāyvātmakāḥ | ityato yasyāṃ dhyānasamāpattau yathābhūto 'pakṣālastathābhūtena bāhyena vināśaḥ | caturthe tu bāhyo 'pakṣālo na pravartata iti nāsti saṃvartanī | nityaṃ tarhi caturthadhyānaṃ prāpyam | kasmāt ? 'vimānasya samatvasya'; karmakṣayena'pradhvaṃsāt'; iti ||
children.translated_text: being of the nature of wind. Thus, in whichever <s>dhyāna</s>-attainment there exists a particular internal calamity, destruction occurs by an external [element] of corresponding nature. But in the fourth [<s>dhyāna</s>], no external calamity operates; hence there is no destruction-cycle. Then should the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> be permanent? Why? 'Of the abode of equanimity' — 'from destruction' by the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>.

body.translated_text: Indeed, in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, no external or internal calamities (<s>apakṣāla</s>) exist; therefore no destruction-cycle is produced. For in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, applied and sustained thought (<s>vitarka-vicāra</s>), being of the nature of fire, exist as calamities. In the second, joy (<s>prīti</s>), of the nature of water, overwhelms the mind. In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, inhalation and exhalation (<s>āśvāsa-praśvāsa</s>),

body.text: kathaṃ punaretāḥ saṃvartanyaḥ kayā vānupūrvyā bhavanti ? taducyate | nirantaraṃ tāvat-
body.translated_text: But how do these destruction-cycles [occur], and in what sequence? This is stated. First, without interruption —

children.translated_text: seven [cycles] by fire, one by water; when the seven-fold [cycle] is completed, again
seven-fold [cycles] by fire, then one wind-destruction. (Abhidh-d 151)

body.text: sapta saṃvartanyastejobhiḥ bhavanti | aṣṭhamo 'pām | evaṃ saptako bhavati | tasmin saptake 'tikrānte punastejasā saptakaḥ | tasminnapyatikrānte vāyusaṃvartanyaikayā nāśo bhavati | sā tu nityaṃ tejasaḥ saptakapṛṣṭhe vāyusaṃvartanī bhavati | ta ete piṇḍena bhavanti ṣaṭpañcāśat tejaḥsaṃvartanyaḥ, saptāpsaṃvartanyaḥ, ekā vāyusaṃvartanī ||
body.translated_text: Seven destruction-cycles occur by fire. The eighth is by water. Thus a seven-fold [set] occurs. When that seven-fold [set] is exceeded, again a seven-fold [set] by fire. When that too is exceeded, destruction occurs by one wind-destruction. And that [wind-destruction] always occurs after the seven-fold fire [set]. In total, these amount to: fifty-six fire-destructions, seven water-destructions, and one wind-destruction.

body.text: kiṃ punastatra kāraṇaṃ yatpaścādvāyursavartanyekaiva bhavati ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: But what is the reason that there is only one wind-destruction at the end? This is stated:

children.translated_text: After one fire-seven-fold [set], one purifying [water-destruction] — what comes next?
Because of the determination of lifespan, the lifespan of the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> [gods] increases accordingly. (Abhidh-d 152)

body.text: evaṃ ca kṛtvā prajñaptibhāṣyamanulomitaṃ bhavati- "catuḥṣaṣṭhiḥkalpāḥ śubhakṛtsnānāṃ devanāmāyuṣpramāṇam" iti ||
body.translated_text: And having done thus, the <s>Prajñaptibhāṣya</s> is in accord: 'Sixty-four <s>kalpas</s> is the measure of the lifespan of the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods.'

body.text: atha kasmāt pṛthivīsaṃvartanī na bhavati ? tadatra kāraṇamucyate-
body.translated_text: Now why is there no earth-destruction (<s>pṛthivīsaṃvartanī</s>)? The reason is stated here:

children.translated_text: Because of similarity with the faults of wind, bile, and phlegm (<s>vāta-pitta-śleṣma</s>), those [elements] destroy those [beings];
because of [the analogy with] the internal [elements] — by similarity — no earth-destruction is accepted. (Abhidh-d 153)

body.text: yathā khalu vātapittaśleṣmabhistribhiḥ sattvānāṃ marmacchedaḥ pṛthivīdhātutvalakṣaṇo bhavati tadvadagnijalavāyubhirbhūrūtsādyate | kiñca, ete tadvināśakāḥ .............tannāśāya pravṛttatvāt | kiñca, 'ādhyātmiketi sārūpyācca'; | yathā cādhyātmikyastrisraścittasya tayorbhavanti vitarkavicāraprītyucchvāsapraśvāsalakṣaṇaistathā bāhyā apyupadravā vahnyambhovāyuprakopalakṣaṇā bhavantīti ||
body.translated_text: Just as by the three [humors] — wind (<s>vāta</s>), bile (<s>pitta</s>), and phlegm (<s>śleṣma</s>) — the destruction of beings' vital points occurs, which has the characteristic of the earth-element — so the earth is destroyed by fire, water, and wind. Moreover, these are their destroyers, ............. because they operate for that destruction. Moreover, 'because of similarity with the internal' — just as the three internal [humors] of consciousness have the characteristics of applied thought and sustained thought (<s>vitarka-vicāra</s>), joy (<s>prīti</s>), and inhalation-exhalation (<s>ucchvāsa-praśvāsa</s>), so too the external calamities have the characteristics of the eruption of fire, water, and wind.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau tṛtīyasyādhyāyasyacaturthaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the fourth section (<s>pāda</s>) of the third chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the third chapter.

body.text: caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Fourth chapter.

body.text: prathamaḥ pādaḥ |
body.translated_text: First section.

body.text: atha yaduktaṃ "sattvakarmadvidhākhyena pūritaṃ vāyumaṇḍalam" ityetaducyatām | kāni tāni kiyanti vā karmāṇītyataḥ karmāṇi prastūyante |
body.translated_text: Now, as was stated: 'The wind-circle (<s>vāyumaṇḍala</s>) is filled by the two-fold designation of beings' <s>karma</s>' — let that be explained. What are those <s>karmas</s>, and how many are there? Therefore, <s>karmas</s> are set forth:

children.translated_text: Of [those <s>dharmas</s>] that are the causes of the arising of beings, that bring about misfortune and fortune (<s>vipat-saṃpad</s>),
that are the agents of the world's variety — <s>karma</s> (action) is accepted as the cause. (Abhidh-d 154)

body.text: dṛśyate khalu sattvānāṃ hīnamadhyopkṛṣṭajātiparigrahāyāmāśrayabhogādisampadvipattiśca | yacca dvividhasya lokasya vicitratā tatra karmāṇi hetuḥ | atasteṣāṃ tattvāni vakṣyāmi | yadapyuktaṃ kāni kiyanti veti tadupavyākhyāyate ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, among beings there is seen the acquisition of low, middling, and high birth, as well as fortune and misfortune of physical constitution, possessions, and the like. And for the variety of the twofold world [of beings and their vessel-world], <s>karmas</s> are the cause. Therefore I shall state their true nature. As to the question 'what and how many?' — that is now explained.

body.text: sūtre dve karmaṇī nidiśyoktam- "dve karmaṇī cetanā karma cetayitvā ca" iti | tāni punastrīṇyuktāni | katham ?
body.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s>, two <s>karmas</s> are indicated: '<s>Cetanā</s> (volition) is <s>karma</s>, and [action] after having willed (<s>cetayitvā</s>).' But these are again said to be three. How?

children.text: kāyikaṃ vāṅmayaṃ caiva cetanākhyaṃ ca mānasam /
children.translated_text: Bodily (<s>kāyika</s>), verbal (<s>vāṅmaya</s>), and that called volition (<s>cetanā</s>), which is mental —
these are the <s>karmas</s>; they are the cause of the world, not God (<s>Īśvara</s>) and the like. (Abhidh-d 155)

body.text: etāni khalu trīṇi karmāṇi śubhāśubhāni dvividhasyāpi sattvabhājanalokasya hitāhitanimittānyutpattau ca sampattau ca vaicitryasya ca kāraṇam | neśvarakālapuruṣapradhānādayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, these three <s>karmas</s>, wholesome and unwholesome, are the cause of benefit and harm, and of the variety in the arising and fortune of both worlds — the world of sentient beings (<s>sattvaloka</s>) and the vessel-world (<s>bhājanaloka</s>). Not God (<s>Īśvara</s>), Time (<s>Kāla</s>), Primordial Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>), Primordial Matter (<s>Pradhāna</s>), and the like.

body.text: tatra tāvadyathā neśvaraḥ kāraṇaṃ tathā pūrvamullikhitam, idānīṃ tu vispaṣṭataramāviṣkriyate-
body.translated_text: Therein, first, how God is not the cause — this was outlined previously; now it is revealed more clearly:

body.text: vaiśvarūpyātkramotpādāttadvadanyatprasaṅgataḥ /
body.translated_text: Because of the variety [of effects], because of sequential arising, because of the absurd consequence that other [unwanted effects] would [follow] likewise —

body.text: yadi khalveko nityaśceśvaro lokasyotpattisthitipralayakāraṇaṃ syāt, tena khalu kāraṇānuvidhāyitvātkāryasyaitat trayaṃ viruddhaṃ yugapat syāt | na caitad dṛṣṭamiṣṭaṃ vetyasadetat | kiñca lokaścāpyavicitraḥ syāt | yugapaccotpadyeta nagnaḥ kapālapāṇiśca paryaṭettadicchānuvidhāyī ca syāt | na caitadevam | tasmānneśvaraḥ kāraṇam |
body.translated_text: if indeed a single, eternal God were the cause of the world's arising, persistence, and dissolution, then — since the effect conforms to its cause — these three contradictory [phases] would occur simultaneously. And this is neither seen nor accepted — hence it is unfounded. Moreover, the world would also be without variety. And it would arise simultaneously, and one would walk about naked, skull in hand, and be subject to his whims. But this is not so. Therefore, God is not the cause.

body.text: grāmādyadhipativiśeṣotkarṣāvasthānādīśvaraprasiddhiriti cet | na | grāmādhikṛtādiha paratantratvānityatvakāryāntaraśaktivighātādidarśanāt, gomayapiṇḍopamasūtrokteśca |
body.translated_text: Objection: The status of God is established from the observation of the ascending degrees of superiority among rulers of villages and the like. Reply: No — because among village-administrators and the like, we observe dependence on others, impermanence, obstruction of power for other tasks, and so forth; and because of the <s>sūtra</s>-statement comparing [them] to balls of cow-dung.

body.text: bhāgavatāditannindādarśanācca | bhāgavatādyā hi maheśvaraṃ nindyanto dṛśyante | māheśvarāśca viṣṇumiti |
body.translated_text: And because we see the censure of that [God] by the <s>Bhāgavatas</s> and others. For the <s>Bhāgavatas</s> and others are seen censuring <s>Maheśvara</s>; and the <s>Māheśvaras</s> [censure] <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.text: kāraṇasāpekṣaṃ tapaḥsāmarthyādutpādayatīti cet | tatrāpadiśyate |
body.translated_text: Objection: [God], being dependent on [auxiliary] causes, creates through the power of austerity (<s>tapas</s>). To that, we reply:

body.text: nānyāpekṣā tapoyogo pakṣahānyādidoṣataḥ // Abhidh-d_156 //
body.translated_text: The dependence on others and the application of austerity [entail] faults such as the loss of the thesis and the like. (Abhidh-d 156)

body.text: yadi khalu sahakārikāraṇāpekṣaḥ tapobalalabdhyaiśvaryaśca lokaṃ sṛjati kumbhakārabaddhaṭādīn | na | cevaṃ sati pūrvapakṣotsargaḥ kṛto bhavati | yaduktaṃ nityaścaikaśca svatantraḥ kāraṇamiti taddhīnam | tapobalasāmarthyābhyupagame cānityatvaṃ pāratantryaṃ cābhyupagataṃ bhavati | tadabhyupagamāccānaiśvaryamiti | etena kālapuruṣapradhānādikāraṇaparigrahāḥ pratyūḍhā veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: If indeed, being dependent on auxiliary causes and [endowed with] sovereignty obtained through the power of austerity, [God] creates the world — like a potter, brick-layer, and the like — no, for in that case, the original thesis has been abandoned. What was stated — that [God is] eternal, single, and independent as a cause — that is deficient. And in accepting the power of austerity, impermanence and dependence are thereby accepted. And from accepting dependence, non-sovereignty [follows]. By this, the adoption of Time (<s>Kāla</s>), Primordial Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>), Primordial Matter (<s>Pradhāna</s>), and the like as causes should be understood as refuted.

body.text: yadi khalu karma kāraṇaṃ neśvarādayaḥ kathaṃ tarhi lokastatkāraṇaparigrahaṃ karotīti ? atra brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> is indeed the cause and not God and the like, then how is it that the world adopts the acceptance of those as causes? Here we say:

children.translated_text: The power of <s>karmas</s> is recognized through [concepts such as] fate (<s>vidhi</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), planetary influence (<s>graha</s>), and the like;

children.text: yato 'tasteṣu tācchabdyaṃ gauṇyā vṛttyā prayujyate // Abhidh-d_157 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the terminology of those [concepts] is applied to <s>karmas</s> in a secondary sense (<s>gauṇī vṛtti</s>). (Abhidh-d 157)
As is stated:
'Fate, ordinance, destiny, inherent nature, time, planetary influence, God, <s>karma</s>, divine dispensation,
merits, fortune, the workings of death — these are synonymous names for what was previously done.'

body.text: kiñca, yataśca
body.translated_text: Moreover, since

children.translated_text: 'Planetary conjunction, movement of the arm, dreams, full pots, and the like —
these indicate to men the attainment of livelihood from their own <s>karma</s>'

body.text: ityato 'pi teṣu tācchabdyaṃ prayujyata iti ||
body.translated_text: — therefore too, the terminology of those [concepts] is applied [to <s>karma</s>].

body.text: kathaṃ punareṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ vyavasthānam ? yadyāśrayataḥ, sarveṣāṃ kāyāśritatvādekatvam | svabhāvataścet, vākkarmaivaikaṃ prāptam | samutthānataścet, manaḥkarmaikaṃ prāptam | sarveṣāṃ manasotthāpitatvāt | tribhirapīti vaibhāṣikāḥ ||
body.translated_text: But how is the classification of these three <s>karmas</s> established? If by basis (<s>āśraya</s>) — since all are based on the body, there would be only one. If by intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — only vocal <s>karma</s> would be obtained as one [type]. If by origination (<s>samutthāna</s>) — only mental <s>karma</s> would be obtained as one [type], since all are produced by the mind. [The answer is:] by all three — say the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>.

body.text: te punarete prathame dve karmaṇī pratyekaṃ dviprabhede | katham ? tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: These first two <s>karmas</s> are each of two subdivisions. How? This is explained:

children.translated_text: The first two are informative (<s>vijñapti</s>) and non-informative (<s>avijñapti</s>) —

body.text: kāyakarma khalu kāyavijñaptiḥ kāyāvijñaptiśca | vākkarmāpi vāgvijñaptirvāgavijñaptiśca | tṛtīyaṃ tu karma-
body.translated_text: bodily <s>karma</s> is indeed bodily informative action (<s>kāyavijñapti</s>) and bodily non-informative action (<s>kāyāvijñapti</s>). Vocal <s>karma</s> too is vocal informative action (<s>vāgvijñapti</s>) and vocal non-informative action (<s>vāgavijñapti</s>). But the third <s>karma</s> —

body.text: cetanā mānasī kriyā // Abhidh-d_158 //
body.translated_text: volition (<s>cetanā</s>) is mental action (<s>mānasī kriyā</s>). (Abhidh-d 158)

body.text: uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "cetanā karma cetayitvā |" tatpunastridhoktam- "kāyakarma vākkarma manaskarma ca" iti |
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: '<s>Cetanā</s> is <s>karma</s>; [and action] after having willed (<s>cetayitvā</s>).' And that has been stated as threefold: 'Bodily <s>karma</s>, vocal <s>karma</s>, and mental <s>karma</s>.'

body.text: kiṃ svabhāvaṃ punaridaṃ kāyakarma kiṃ tāvatkāyasvabhāvam ? yathā vākkarma (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 122)
is of the nature of speech — or is it different from the body, as mental <s>karma</s> is different from the mind? This he states: ..............

body.translated_text: What is the intrinsic nature of this bodily <s>karma</s>? First, is it of the nature of the body? Just as vocal <s>karma</s>

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau caturthādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ
body.translated_text: End of the first section (<s>pāda</s>) of the fourth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: caturthādhyāye
body.translated_text: Fourth chapter,

body.text: dvitīyapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: second section.

body.text: ..................parābhavantītyapadiśyate |
body.translated_text: .................. it is explained that they are defeated.

children.translated_text: Just as food burnt by excessive fire, and a vessel that is over-processed —
so is the morality (<s>śīla</s>) of one with wrong views, whose self is wounded by deceit (<s>śāṭhya</s>), jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), and the like. (Abhidh-d 159)
One endowed with right view on the conventional level [has] monkhood (<s>bhikṣutva</s>) in the ultimate sense;

children.text: ekasampattu saṃvṛtyā dvayābhāve dvidhāpi na // Abhidh-d_160 //
children.translated_text: with [only] one attainment, [one is a monk] conventionally; in the absence of both, [one is] not [a monk] in either way. (Abhidh-d 160)

body.text: dṛṣṭisampadviśuddhā khalu śaīlasampat 'bhikṣutvaṃ paramārthataḥ | anyataravikalastu saṃvṛtyā bhikṣurbhavati | dvyaṅgavikalastu nāpi saṃvṛtyā nāni paramārthata iti |
body.translated_text: Morality (<s>śīla</s>) that is purified by the attainment of right view is '<s>bhikṣutva</s> (monkhood) in the ultimate sense.' But one who lacks one of the two limbs is a monk (<s>bhikṣu</s>) only conventionally. One who lacks both limbs is neither conventionally nor ultimately [a monk].

body.text: yadi khalu vinā saṃvareṇāṣṭau nikāyā na vyavasthāpyante kathaṃ tarhi (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 124)

children.text: ) bhagavatoktaiḥ- "ekadeśakārī, pradeśakārī, yadbhūyaskārī, paripūrṇakārī" ityatrāpyayamartho dṛśyate ? kaścitkhalvakāryaikadeśaviratikṣamo bhavati | kaścidyāvatsamagradauḥśīlyaviratikṣamaḥ | ityato bhagavānakāryaikadeśaviratyāpyupāsakatvaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) by the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s words: 'one who practices partially, one who practices in parts, one who practices mostly, one who practices completely' — is this meaning also seen here? Someone indeed is capable of abstaining from only a part of misconduct; someone is capable of abstaining from [even] complete immorality. Therefore, the <s>Bhagavat</s> teaches that even through abstention from a part of misconduct, one can attain the status of a lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>) (
[page reference: Jaini 125]

children.text: ) śāsti | na hi sarvaśīlavikalaḥ kaściccharaṇagamanecchāmātrakeṇopāsako bhavati ṣaḍaṅgoṣadhaikadvyaṅgavaikalyopayogavaditi |
children.translated_text: ). For no one who is deficient in all precepts becomes a lay follower merely by the wish for going to refuge — like the usefulness of a six-limbed medicine even when lacking one or two limbs.

body.translated_text: If indeed the eight assemblies (<s>nikāya</s>) cannot be established without restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>), then how

body.text: atha yaduktam- "buddhaṃ dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchati" iti tatka ete buddhādayaḥ ? tadidamabhidhīyate-
body.translated_text: Now, regarding what was said — 'one goes for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>' — who are these, beginning with the <s>Buddha</s>? This is stated:

children.translated_text: With reference to the knowledge free from obstruction, the primary designation '<s>Buddha</s>' [is made];

children.text: tadāśraye phale cāpi vijñeyā guṇakalpanā // Abhidh-d_161 //
children.translated_text: and with reference to its support and to [its] fruit, the derivative designation should be known. (Abhidh-d 161)

body.text: dvividhaḥ khalu buddhaḥ saṃvṛtyā paramārthataśca | tatra paramārthato yathoktaṃ śāstre- "yo buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchati kimasau śaraṇaṃ gacchati ? tānevāsau buddhakārakānaśaikṣāndharmāñcharaṇaṃ gacchati | te hi buddhaśabdapravṛttinimittacihnam |" iti | tebhyo 'pi nirāvaraṇaṃ jñānaṃ pradhānaṃ sarvajña iti lokaprasiddha eṣa tāvat pāramārthiko buddhaḥ | saṃvṛtyāpi 'tadāśraye'; dvātriśatā lakṣaṇairaśītyā cānuvyañjanairvirājite rūpakāye 'pi buddhākhyeti | tatphale ca balavaiśāradyamahākaruṇādiṣu buddhoktiriti |
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> is indeed twofold: conventionally and in the ultimate sense. Of these, in the ultimate sense, as stated in the treatise: 'One who goes for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s> — what does he go to for refuge? He goes for refuge to those very <s>dharmas</s> that are the makers of the <s>Buddha</s> — the <s>aśaikṣa</s> (adept-level) <s>dharmas</s>. For they are the mark and sign that are the basis for the application of the word <s>Buddha</s>.' Among these, the unobstructed knowledge (<s>nirāvaraṇa jñāna</s>) is the principal — [the one called] 'omniscient' (<s>sarvajña</s>), well-known in the world. This is the ultimate <s>Buddha</s>. Conventionally too, 'with reference to its support' — even with reference to the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>) adorned with the thirty-two marks and eighty minor signs, the designation '<s>Buddha</s>' [is applied]. And with reference to its fruit — with reference to the powers (<s>bala</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and the like, the designation '<s>Buddha</s>' [is applied].

children.translated_text: Because of [its] permanence, because of [its] being auspicious, and because of the removal of all misfortune —
by the primary designation, <s>Dharma</s> likewise is said to be <s>nirvāṇa</s>. (Abhidh-d 162)

body.text: nityāvikṛtasvalakṣaṇadhāraṇāttatprāptānāṃ cātyantadhāraṇe nirvāṇaṃ pāramārthiko dharmaḥ | guṇakalpanathā tu pratyekabuddhabodhisattvasantāniko mārgaḥ | trīṇi ca piṭakāni dharmo nirvāṇaprāpakatvāt ||
body.translated_text: Because it supports the eternal, unmodified intrinsic characteristic, and because of the ultimate support of those who have attained it — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is the ultimate <s>Dharma</s>. By the derivative designation, however, [<s>Dharma</s> refers to] the path in the continuum of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> or a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And the three <s>piṭakas</s> (baskets of scripture) are also <s>Dharma</s>, because they lead to <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: āryāḥ śiṣyaguṇāḥ saṃghastathaiva paramārthataḥ /
body.translated_text: The noble ones, the qualities of the disciples — the <s>Saṃgha</s>, likewise in the ultimate sense:

body.text: navānāmaśaikṣāṇāmaṣṭādaśānāṃ ca śaikṣāṇāṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ santāne yo mārgaḥ sa pāramārthikaḥ saṃgha ityucyate | saṃvṛtyā tu pṛthagjanakalyāṇakabhikṣusaṃgha ityapadiśyate |
body.translated_text: the path in the continuum of the nine <s>aśaikṣas</s> (adepts) and the eighteen <s>śaikṣas</s> (learners), who are disciples — that is called the ultimate <s>Saṃgha</s>. Conventionally, however, it is designated as the <s>saṃgha</s> of virtuous ordinary-person <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: etānyo yāti śaraṇaṃ sa yāti śaraṇatrayam // Abhidh-d_163 //
body.translated_text: One who goes for refuge to these goes to the threefold refuge. (Abhidh-d 163)

body.text: etānyathoktalakṣaṇān buddhadharmasaṃdhān śaraṇaṃ gacchati 'yo yāti śaraṇatrayam'; iti ||
body.translated_text: One who goes for refuge to these — the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s> having the characteristics as stated — 'goes to the threefold refuge.'

body.text: kiṃ svabhāvāni punaḥ śaraṇagamanāni ? vāgvijñaptitatsamutthadharmasvabhāvāni ||
body.translated_text: What is the intrinsic nature of the going-for-refuge? Its intrinsic nature is vocal informative action (<s>vāgvijñapti</s>) and the <s>dharmas</s> arisen from that.

body.text: kaḥ punaḥ śaraṇārthaḥ ? trāṇārthaḥ śaraṇārthaḥ | tadāśrayeṇa sarvaduḥkhātyantavimokṣāt | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: What then is the meaning of 'refuge' (<s>śaraṇa</s>)? The meaning of 'refuge' is 'protection' (<s>trāṇa</s>). Because, by relying on that, there is ultimate liberation from all suffering. For the <s>Bhagavat</s> has said:

children.translated_text: 'Many go for refuge to mountains, forests,
gardens, and sacred trees — humans threatened by fear.
But this is not the best refuge; this is not the supreme refuge;
by resorting to this refuge, one is not freed from all suffering.

children.text: yastu buddhaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca saṃghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: But one who has gone for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>,
when one sees the Four Noble Truths with insight —
suffering, the origination of suffering, the transcendence of suffering,
and the Noble Eightfold Path, the secure path leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s> —

body.text:
etaddhi śaraṇaṃ śreṣṭhametaccharaṇamuttamam |
etaccharaṇamāgamya sarvaduḥkhātpramucyate ||" iti |
body.translated_text: this indeed is the best refuge; this is the supreme refuge; by resorting to this refuge, one is freed from all suffering.'

body.text: ata eva śaraṇagamanāni sarvasaṃvarasamādāneṣu dvārabhūtāni, dṛṣṭisaṃpannasya teṣāṃ prarohāt |
body.translated_text: For this very reason, the goings-for-refuge are the gateways to all undertakings of restraint (<s>saṃvara-samādāna</s>), because of their sprouting in one who is endowed with right view (<s>dṛṣṭisaṃpanna</s>).

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ kāmamithyācārādevopāsakasya viratiḥ śikṣāpadeṣu vyavasthāpitā na sarvasmādabrahmacaryāt ? anyebhyaśca prakṛtisāvadyebhyo mṛṣāvāda eva śikṣāpadeṣu vyavasthāpyate, na pāruṣyādi ? sarvebhyaśca pratipakṣapaṇasāvadyebhyaḥ madyapānādeva viratiḥ śikṣāpadaṃ vyavasthāpitam ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: But what is the reason that abstention from sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>) alone is established among the training rules for a lay follower, and not from all non-celibacy (<s>abrahmacaryā</s>)? And from among the other naturally blameworthy acts, why is false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>) alone established among the training rules, and not harsh speech and the like? And from among all acts blameworthy by prohibition (<s>pratikṣepaṇa-sāvadya</s>), why is abstention from intoxicant-drinking alone established as a training rule? To that it is said:

body.text: mithyācāraḥ satāṃ garhyātparatrākaraṇāptitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Sexual misconduct, because it is censured by the virtuous, and because through non-commission one obtains [benefit] in the next life;

body.text: pāpiṣṭhatvānmṛṣāvādo madyapānaṃ smṛtikṣayātū // Abhidh-d_164 //
body.translated_text: false speech, because of being the most sinful; and intoxicant-drinking, because of the destruction of mindfulness. (Abhidh-d 164)

body.text: kāmamithyācāro hi loke 'tyarthaṃ garhitaḥ | pareṣāṃ dāropaghātādāpāyikatvācca | na tathābrahmacaryam | sukarā ca gṛhasthasya kāmamithyācāravi ratiḥ, duṣkarā tvabrahmacaryāt | āryaścākaraṇasaṃvaraṃ kāmamithyācārādeva janmāntarito 'pi labhate na tvabrahmacaryāt |
body.translated_text: For sexual misconduct is extremely censured in the world; and because of the violation of others' wives, it leads to lower realms (<s>āpāyika</s>). Non-celibacy is not so [censured]. And abstention from sexual misconduct is easy for a householder, whereas abstention from all non-celibacy is difficult. And a noble one obtains the restraint of non-commission from sexual misconduct even when separated by intervening lives, but not from non-celibacy.

body.text: mṛṣāvādo 'pi bhagavatā pāpiṣṭhatvādrāhulamuddiṣya paramenādareṇoktaḥ- "yasya rāhula mṛṣāvāde nāsti lajjā nāsti kaukṛtyaṃ nāhaṃ tasya kiñcidakaraṇīyaṃ vadāmi" iti |
body.translated_text: False speech too was declared by the <s>Bhagavat</s> with supreme care, addressing <s>Rāhula</s>, because of its being the most sinful: 'For one who, <s>Rāhula</s>, has no shame and no regret regarding false speech, I declare there is nothing that such a one would not do.'

body.text: madyapāne 'pi smṛtilopo bhavati, sarvaśikṣāpadakṣobho bhavatītyataḥ pratikṣepaṇasāvadyamapi sanmadyapānaṃ kuśāgreṇāpi bhagavatā nābhyanujñātam ||
body.translated_text: Regarding intoxicant-drinking too, loss of mindfulness occurs, and disruption of all training rules occurs; therefore, even though blameworthy only by prohibition, intoxicant-drinking was not sanctioned by the <s>Bhagavat</s> even to the slightest degree.

body.text: idamidānīmucyatām | ya ete trayaḥ prātimokṣadhyānānāsravasaṃvarāḥ kimeṣāṃ yata eko labhyate tataḥ śeṣā apīti ? brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: Now let this be stated. There are these three restraints — <s>prātimokṣa</s> (individual liberation), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>anāsrava</s> (outflow-free). From where one obtains one, does one also obtain the others? We say:

body.text: sarvebhyo vartamānebhyo dvividhebhyo 'pi kāmajaḥ /
body.translated_text: The desire-realm [restraint arises] from all present [skandhas], from both types;

body.text: prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ khalu sarvebhyo maulaprayogapṛṣṭhebhyo vartamānebhyaḥ skandhāyatanadhātubhyaḥ sattvādhiṣṭhānapravattatvāt, nātītānāgatebhyasteṣāmasattvasaṃkhyātatvāllabhyate | 'dvividhebhyo 'pi'; sattvāsattvākhyebhyaḥ, prakṛtipratikṣepaṇasāvadyebhyaśca |
body.translated_text: the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint is indeed obtained from all present fundamental, preparatory, and subsequent [paths], and from the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s>, because it is established upon a sentient being-basis. It is not obtained from past and future [ones], because those are not counted as sentient-being [based]. 'From both types' — from those designated as sentient and non-sentient, and from those naturally and prohibitionally blameworthy.

body.text: trikālebhyastu maulebhyo labhyete bhāvanāmayau // Abhidh-d_165 //
body.translated_text: But the cultivation-born [restraints] are obtained from fundamental [karma-paths] of all three times. (Abhidh-d 165)

body.text: etau hi maulebhya eva karmapathebhyo labhyete na prayogapṛṣṭhebhyo nāpi prajñaptisāvadyebhyaḥ, sarvakālebhyaśca skandhāyatanadhātubhyo labhyete 'tītānāgatebhyo 'pi |
body.translated_text: For these two [dhyāna and anāsrava restraints] are obtained from fundamental karma-paths only, not from preparatory or subsequent [paths], nor from those blameworthy only by designation. And they are obtained from <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s> of all times — from past and future ones as well.

body.text: catuṣkoṭikā cātra bhavati | "santi te skandhāyatanadhātavo yebhyaḥ prātimokṣasaṃvaro labhyate na dhyānānāsravasaṃvarau" iti vistaraḥ | prathamā koṭiḥ- pratyutpannebhyaḥ sāmantakapṛṣṭhebhyaḥ pratikṣepaṇasāvadyācca | dvitīyāatītānāgatebhyo maulebhyaḥ karmapathebhyaḥ | tṛtīyā- pratyutpannebhyaḥ maulebhyaḥ karmapathebhyaḥ | caturthī- atītānāgatebhyaḥ sāmantakapṛṣṭhebhya iti ||
body.translated_text: And here there is a fourfold classification: 'there are those <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s> from which the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint is obtained but not the <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>anāsrava</s> restraints' — thus in detail. The first case: from present preparatory and subsequent [paths], and from the prohibitionally blameworthy. The second: from past and future fundamental karma-paths. The third: from present fundamental karma-paths. The fourth: from past and future preparatory and subsequent [paths].

body.text: kiṃ punarimau saṃvarāsaṃvarau sarvasattvebhya eva labhyete ? sarvāṅgebhyaḥ sarvakāraṇaiśca ? athāsti kaścidbhedaḥ ? tatra tāvadavaśyaṃ labhyate-
body.translated_text: Now, are restraint and non-restraint obtained from all beings, from all limbs, and by all causes? Or is there some distinction? Regarding this, what is necessarily obtained:

children.translated_text: Restraint [is obtained] from all classes of beings, but [it may differ] by limbs and causes;

children.text: sarvebhyo saṃvarāṅgebhyaḥ sattvebhyaśca na kāraṇaiḥ // Abhidh-d_166 //
children.translated_text: from all limbs of restraint and from [all] beings — but not [always] by [all] causes. (Abhidh-d 166)

body.text: sarvasattvebhyaḥ khalu saṃvaro labhyate na kebhyaścit | aṅgebhyastu vibhāṣā kaścitsarvebhyo labhyate bhikṣusaṃvaraḥ | kaściccaturbhyaḥ | tato 'nyaḥ | karmapathā hi saṃvarābhyāṅgāni | kāraṇairapi kenacitparyāyeṇa sarvaiḥ, kenacidekena |
body.translated_text: Restraint is indeed obtained from all beings, not from just some. But as for limbs, there is an alternative: some [restraint] is obtained from all [limbs] — the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint; some from [only] four [limbs]; and others differently. For the karma-paths are the limbs of the restraints. And by causes: in one way by all [causes], in another by just one.

body.text: kathaṃ tāvatsarvairyadyalobhādveṣāmohāḥ kāraṇānīṣyante ? kathamekena yadi mṛdumadhyādhimātrāṇi cittāni kāraṇānīṣyante ? paścimena paryāyeṇa niyamocyate | asti saṃvarasthāyo sarvasattveṣu saṃvṛto na sarvāṅgairna sarvakāraṇairyo mṛdunā cittena madhyenādhimātreṇa vā upāsakopavāsaśrāmaṇerasaṃvaraṃ samādatte | asti sarvasattveṣu saṃvṛtaḥ sarvāṅgaiśca, na tu sarvakāraṇairyo mṛdunā cittena madhyenādhimātreṇa vā bhikṣusaṃvaraṃ samādatte | asti sarvasattveṣu sarvāṅgaiḥ sarvakāraṇaiśca yastrividhena cittena trīnsaṃvarān samādatte | asti sarvasattveṣu sarvakāraṇaiśca na tu sarvāṅgairya upāsakopavāsaśrāmaṇerasavarānmṛdumadhyādhimātraiścittaiḥ samādatte | yastu na sarvasattveṣu syādīdṛśo nāsti yasmātsarvasattvānugatakalyāṇāśaye sthitaḥ saṃvaraṃ pratilabhate nānyathā, pāpāśayasyānuparatatvāt |
body.translated_text: How [is it] from all? If non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion are considered the causes. How by one? If mild, moderate, and intense mental states are considered the causes. The rule is stated according to the latter way. There is a person restrained toward all beings who is not restrained by all limbs nor by all causes — one who, with a mild, moderate, or intense mind, undertakes the restraint of a lay follower, one-day fast, or novice. There is one restrained toward all beings and by all limbs, but not by all causes — one who, with a mild, moderate, or intense mind, undertakes the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint. There is one [restrained] toward all beings, by all limbs, and by all causes — one who, with all three types of mind, undertakes all three restraints. There is one [restrained] toward all beings and by all causes, but not by all limbs — one who undertakes the lay follower, one-day fast, and novice restraints with mild, moderate, and intense minds. But one who would not be [restrained] toward all beings — such a one does not exist, because one obtains restraint [only] when established in a benevolent intention toward all beings, not otherwise, since one with a malevolent intention has not desisted [from harm].

body.text: pañcaniyamān kurvan prātimokṣasaṃvaraṃ labhate | sattvāṅgadeśakālasamayamiyamāḥ- amuṣmātsattvādviramāmīti sattvaniyamaḥ | amuṣmādaṅgādityaṅganiyamaḥ | amuṣmindeśa iti deśaniyamaḥ | māsādyāvaditi kālaniyamaḥ | anyatra yuddhāditi samayaniyamaḥ | sucaritamātraṃ tu tatsyādevaṃ gṛhṇato na saṃvaraḥ |
body.translated_text: One who makes five restrictions obtains the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint: [restrictions by] being, limb, place, time, and occasion. 'I will abstain from this being' — this is the being-restriction. 'From this limb [of misconduct]' — the limb-restriction. 'In this place' — the place-restriction. 'For a month and so forth' — the time-restriction. 'Except in war and the like' — the occasion-restriction. But if one grasps [the precepts] in this way, that would be merely good conduct, not [full] restraint.

body.text: kathamaśakyebhyaḥ saṃvaralābhaḥ ? sarvasattvajīvitānupaghātādhyāśayenābhyupagamāt | uktaṃ yathā saṃvaro labhyate ||
body.translated_text: How can there be obtaining of restraint from [harming] beings that are beyond one's capacity? Because of the commitment made with an intention of non-injury toward the life of all beings. Thus it has been stated how restraint is obtained.

body.text: asaṃvaro 'pi sarvasattvebhyaḥ sarvakarmapathebhyaśca na tu sarvakāraṇaiḥ, yugapanmṛdvādicittābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: Non-restraint too [is obtained] from all beings and from all karma-paths, but not by all causes, because of the impossibility of simultaneous mild and other mental states.

body.text: ke punarasāṃvarikāḥ ? aurabhrikāḥ kaukkuṭikāḥ saukarikāḥ śākuntikā (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 131]

children.text: ) mātsikā mṛgalubdhakāścaurāḥ vadhyaghātakā bandhanapālakā nāgabandhāśvapākā vāgurikāśca | rājāno daṇḍanetāro vyāvahārikāśca nīticalitā asāvarikāḥ | asaṃvare bhavāḥ, asaṃvaro vā eṣāṃ vidyata ityasāṃvarikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) fishermen, deer-hunters, thieves, executioners, prison-wardens, elephant-trappers, <s>caṇḍālas</s> (outcastes), and netters. Kings, judges, and lawyers who have deviated from justice are also non-restrained ones. Those who exist in non-restraint, or those for whom non-restraint exists — [these are] the non-restrained ones.

body.translated_text: Who then are the non-restrained ones (<s>asāṃvarika</s>)? Sheep-butchers, poultry-keepers, pig-slaughterers, bird-catchers, (

body.text: uktamidaṃ yebhyaḥ asaṃvaro labhyate | kathaṃ tu tallābha iti noktaṃ tadā rabhyate-
body.translated_text: It has been stated from what [sources] non-restraint is obtained. But how it is obtained was not stated; that is now undertaken:

children.translated_text: Non-restraint is obtained by action; it [is also obtained] by commitment;
and the non-informative [component] of others [is obtained] by distinction of field, limb, and the like. (Abhidh-d 167)

body.text: dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmasaṃvaro labhyate | kriyayābhyupagamena vā | kriyayā tatkulīnatatkarmābhyupagamāt | atatkulīnairvayamapyanayā jīvikayā jīviṣyāma iti | śeṣāvijñaptilābhastu kṣetrāṅgaviśeṣāditi | kṣetraṃ vā tadrūpaṃ bhavati yathārāmādipranānamātreṇāvijñaptirutpadyate | yathaupadhikeṣu puṇyakriyāvastuṣu | ādareṇa vā samādatte | buddhamavanditvā na bhokṣya iti | māsārdhamāsabhaktāni vā nityaṃ kariṣyāmītyevamādi | ādareṇa vā tadrūpeṇa kriyāmīhate kuśalāmakuśalāṃ vā yato 'syā vijñaptirutpadyate |
body.translated_text: Non-restraint is obtained by two causes: by action and by commitment. By action — through belonging to that family and committing to that occupation. Those not born in that family [undertake it through:] 'We too shall live by this livelihood.' The obtaining of the remaining non-informative [component], however, is from distinction of field and limbs. The 'field' may be of such a nature that merely from bowing down at a garden and the like, a non-informative [action] arises — as in the case of meritorious bases of action that involve material support. Or one undertakes [something] with care: 'Having not worshipped the <s>Buddha</s>, I shall not eat'; or 'I shall give food regularly for a month or half-month' — and so forth. Or with such care, one undertakes a wholesome or unwholesome activity from which a non-informative [action] arises.

body.text: uktametadyathā saṃvarāsaṃvarāṇāṃ pratilambhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus has been stated how restraint and non-restraint are obtained.

body.text: tyāga idānīṃ vaktavyaḥ | tatra tāvat-
body.translated_text: Now the relinquishment [of restraint] must be stated. To begin:

children.translated_text: The relinquishment of the desire-realm restraint [occurs] through renunciation of the training rules and the like;
some say through a <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) offense — [the text says] 'not so,' because of improper reasoning. (Abhidh-d 168)

body.text: kāmāptasyāṣṭaprakārasaṃvarasya pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaistyāgaḥ | śikṣānikṣepaṇanikāyasabhāgatyāgobhayavyañjanotpādakuśalasamucchedebhyo niśātyayenāṣṭamasya | tānyetānyabhisamasya pañca bhavanti |
body.translated_text: The relinquishment of the eightfold restraint belonging to the desire realm [occurs] by five causes: renunciation of the training rules, loss of class-homogeneity, arising of both sex-characteristics, severance of the wholesome root, and — for the eighth [type, the one-day fast] — by the passing of the night. Taking these together, they are five.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇamebhistyāgo bhavati ? samādānaviruddhavijñaptyutpādādāśrayatyāgādāśrayakopanānnidānacchedāttāvadevākṣepācca |
body.translated_text: What is the reason that relinquishment occurs through these? Because of the arising of an informative action (<s>vijñapti</s>) opposed to the undertaking; because of the loss of the support [body]; because of the corruption of the support; because of the severance of the causal basis; and because of the projection being limited to just that [duration].

body.text: anye punarāhuḥ- caturṇāṃ patanīyānāmanyatamena bhikṣuśrāmaṇerasaṃvaratyāgaḥ |" 'tanna'; iti, 'ayogataḥ'; |
body.translated_text: Others, however, say: 'the <s>bhikṣu</s> and novice restraints are relinquished through one of the four <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) offenses.' '[The text says] not so' — 'because of improper reasoning.'

body.text: kaḥ punarayogaḥ ?
body.translated_text: What then is the improper reasoning?

body.text: ayogo nāṃśuvidhvaṃsātpaṭadravyaṃ vinaśyati /
body.translated_text: The improper reasoning is that cloth-substance is not destroyed by the destruction of [its] threads;

body.text: na hyavayavanāśādavayavivināśo bhavati | avayavirūpaśca prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ | tasyāvayavakṣobhācchidratvaṃ bhavati mālinyaṃ ca | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā- "duḥśīlo bhavati pāpadharmā |"
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] For from the destruction of parts, the destruction of the whole does not follow. And the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint is of the nature of form — of the whole. From the disturbance of its parts, there is breach (<s>chidratva</s>) and defilement. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'He becomes one of bad morality, of evil ways.'

body.text: sūtravirodhādayuktamiti cedatropadiśanti-
body.translated_text: [Objection:] If [you say] this is improper because of contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s> — to this they reply:

body.text: sūtre dhvaṃsoktiranyārthā yatherṣyāśaṭhanādiṣu // Abhidh-d_169 //
body.translated_text: The statement of destruction in the <s>sūtra</s> is intended in another sense, as in [the cases of] envy, deceptiveness, and so forth. (Abhidh-d 169)

body.text: bhagavatātra "abhikṣurbhavati" iti śāsanasthityarthaṃ durvṛttavineyāvasādanārthaṃ coktam | yathā- "īrṣyiko bhavati matsarī śaṭho māyāvī mithyādṛṣṭirityevamādidoṣayuktaḥ kaśambakajātīyaḥ pāpabhikṣurnirvāsayitavyaḥ |" na ca cittāvidūṣaṇādabhikṣutvaṃ bhavati vineyaśāsanārthatattvavidbhirityuktam | tadvadatrāpi draṣṭavyamiti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The <s>Bhagavān</s>'s statement 'he becomes a non-monk' was made for the purpose of the stability of the Teaching and for the purpose of humiliating the ill-behaved trainee. Just as: 'One who is envious, avaricious, deceptive, hypocritical, holding wrong views, and so forth — such a wicked monk, like a <s>kaśambaka</s> plant, should be expelled.' But one does not become a non-monk without the corruption of mind — so say those who know the truth regarding the purpose of disciplining trainees. The same should be seen here too.

body.text: tasmātpūrvoktalakṣaṇa eva bhikṣurna yathāha kośakāraḥ |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, a monk is [defined] by the very characteristic stated previously — not as the <s>Kośa</s>-author states.

body.text: saddharmāntarddhito 'nye 'nye nāpūrvāpratilambhataḥ /
body.translated_text: Others [say that restraint is lost] at the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s> — [but] not from non-production of something unprecedented.

body.text: anye punarbrūvate- saddharmāntardhāne 'pi saṃvaratyāgo bhavati | tattu naivam | yasmādapūrvastadā notpadyate | utpannastu yathoktai reva kāraṇairvinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Others state that even at the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the abandonment of restraint occurs. But that is not so. Because at that time, something unprecedented is not produced. But what has been produced is destroyed by the very causes already stated.

body.text: atha dhyānānāsravasaṃvarayostyāgaḥ katham ? tadidamapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: Now, how is the abandonment of <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraint [to be understood]? This is indicated:

body.text: bhūsaṃcāreṇa hānyā ca tyajyate dhyānajaṃ śubham // Abhidh-d_170 //
body.translated_text: The wholesome [restraint] born of <s>dhyāna</s> is abandoned through change of ground (<s>bhūmisaṃcāra</s>) and through decline (<s>hāni</s>). (Abhidh-d 170)

body.text: sarvameva khalu dhyānāptaṃ kuśalaṃ dvyābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ tyajyate | upapattitto vā bhūmisaṃcārādardhvaṃ vādho vā | parihāṇito vā | samāpatternikāyasabhāgatyāgācceti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] All wholesome [restraint] obtained through <s>dhyāna</s> is abandoned by two causes: through change of ground — by rebirth either upward or downward; or through decline (<s>parihāṇi</s>) — from the attainment, [resulting in] the abandonment of class-homogeneity.

body.text: tathārūpyāptamāryantu phalāptyakṣavihānibhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Likewise, that obtained in the formless [realm] by the noble one, [is abandoned] through fruit-attainment, faculty-decline, and deterioration.

body.text: yathaiva rūpāptaṃ kuśalaṃ bhūmisaṃcārahānibhyāṃ tyajyate tathaivārūpyāptam | āryaṃ tu kuśalaṃ tribhiḥ kāraṇastyajyate | phalaprāptitaḥ pūrvako mārgastyajyate | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 135)

children.text: ) akṣottāpanena mṛdvindriyamārgaḥ | parihāṇita uttaro mārgaḥ | phalaṃ phalaviśiṣṭo vā | evaṃ tāvatsaṃvarastyajyate |
children.translated_text: ) Through faculty-weakening (<s>akṣottāpana</s>) — the path of weak faculties [replaces the sharp]. Through decline — the higher path [is lost]. [What is abandoned is] the fruit, or that which is distinguished by the fruit. Thus restraint is abandoned.

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Just as the wholesome obtained in the form [realm] is abandoned through change of ground and decline, so too that obtained in the formless [realm]. But the noble wholesome [path] is abandoned by three causes: through attainment of the fruit — the earlier path is abandoned. (

body.text: asaṃvaro damaprāptirjīvitotsarjanā dibhiḥ // Abhidh-d_171 //
body.translated_text: Non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>) [is cut off] through the attainment of discipline (<s>dama</s>), through the relinquishing of life, and the like. (Abhidh-d 171)

body.text: tribhiḥ kāraṇairasaṃvaracchedaḥ | saṃvaraprāptitaḥ | yadi saṃvaraṃ samāpadyate dhyānasaṃvaraṃ vā pratilabhate hetupratyayabalenasamādhilābhāttenāsaṃvarastyājyate | pratidvandvabalīyastvāt | maraṇena cāśrayatyāgāt | dvivyañjanotpādena cāśrayavikopanāt | śastrajalatyāge 'pyakaraṇāśayataḥ saṃvaramantareṇāsaṃvaracchedo nāsti | nidānaparivarjanena pravṛddharogānivṛttivat ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Non-restraint is cut off by three causes. Through attainment of restraint — if one undertakes restraint, or obtains <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint, or gains concentration through the power of causal conditions — by that, non-restraint is abandoned, because the antidote is more powerful. Through death — because the support [i.e., the body] is relinquished. Through the arising of both [male and female] sex-organs — because the support is disrupted. Even in the case of relinquishing weapons or water [i.e., through taking vows], without restraint, non-restraint is not cut off merely through the intention of non-performance — like an aggravated disease that does not abate merely through avoidance of its cause.

body.text: atha saṃvarāsaṃvaravinirmuktā kathamavijñaptistyajyate ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now how is <s>avijñapti</s> (non-informative [matter]) that is neither restraint nor non-restraint abandoned? To that it is said:

body.text: cittavegādivicchedairavijñaptistu madhyamā /
body.translated_text: The intermediate <s>avijñapti</s> [is cut off] through the cessation of mental impulse and so forth.

body.text: yena khalvasau prasādakleśavegenāvijñaptirākṣiptā tasya vicchedātsāpi vicchidyate, kumbhakāracakragativat | samādānatyāgādapi vicchidyate | kriyāvicchedādapi vicchidyate | caityavihārakṣetrāderapyarthasya vicchedādvicchidyate | āyuṣo 'pi kuśalamūlānāmapi vicchedādvicchidyate |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The <s>avijñapti</s> that was projected by the force of the impulse of faith or of affliction — through the cessation of that [force], it too ceases, like the motion of a potter's wheel. It is also cut off through the abandonment of the undertaking. It is also cut off through the cessation of the activity. It is also cut off through the cessation of the purpose — of the shrine, monastery, field, and so forth. It is also cut off through the cessation of lifespan and through the cutting off of wholesome roots.

body.text: kāmāptaṃ kuśalaṃ nāma tribhirmūlacchidādibhiḥ // Abhidh-d_172 //
body.translated_text: The wholesome [dharma] obtained in the desire [realm] — called [such] — [is abandoned] by three [causes], beginning with the cutting of roots. (Abhidh-d 172)

body.text: kāmāvacaraṃ punaḥ kuśalamarūpasvabhāvaṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ tyajyate | kuśalamūlasamucchedāt, rūpārūpyadhātūpapattitaśca |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The desire-realm wholesome of immaterial nature is abandoned by two causes: through the cutting off of wholesome roots, and through rebirth in the form and formless realms.

body.text: pratipakṣodayātkliṣṭaṃ tridhātvāptaṃ vihīyate /
body.translated_text: The afflicted [dharma], obtained in [any of] the three realms, is destroyed through the arising of its antidote.

body.text: kliṣṭaṃ tvarūpasvabhāvaṃ sarvameva pratipakṣodayādvihīyate | yasyopakleśaprakārasya yaḥ prahāṇamārgaḥ, tenāsau saparivāraḥ parityajyate | nānyathā ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] All the afflicted [dharmas] of immaterial nature are destroyed through the arising of their antidote. Whichever path of abandonment corresponds to whichever type of secondary affliction — by that [path], it is abandoned together with its retinue. Not otherwise.

body.text: atha keṣāṃ sattvānāmasaṃvaro bhavati keṣāṃ saṃvaraḥ ? tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: Now, which beings have non-restraint and which have restraint? This is indicated:

body.text: sarve kāmeṣu rūpe dvāveko 'rūpiṣu lābhataḥ // Abhidh-d_173 //
body.translated_text: All [have both] in the desire [realm]; two in the form [realm]; one in the formless [realm], from obtainment. (Abhidh-d 173)

body.text: kāmeṣu khalu sarvaśaṇḍhapaṇḍakādīni hitvā kurūṃśca hitvā | devānāmapi saṃvaraḥ | ityato gatidvaye saṃvarāsaṃvarau vidyete | nānyatreti ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the desire [realm], indeed all [have both restraint and non-restraint] — excluding eunuchs, hermaphrodites, and so forth, and excluding the <s>Kurus</s>. Gods too have restraint. Therefore, in two destinies [human and divine], restraint and non-restraint are found — not elsewhere.

body.text: karmādhikārādidānīṃ sū troktoddiṣṭānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nirdeśaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ | uktaṃ hi sūtre- "trīṇi karmāṇi kuśalamakuśalamavyākṛtaṃ ca |" teṣāṃ lakṣaṇamidamucyate-
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] From the topic of <s>karma</s>, we shall now give an exposition of the types of <s>karma</s> as taught in the <s>sūtras</s>. For it is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are three <s>karmas</s>: wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>), and indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>).' Their characteristics are stated as follows:

children.translated_text: That <s>karma</s> which gives a desired result — that is declared wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>).
Unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>) is the opposite; indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) is otherwise [than both]. (Abhidh-d 174)

body.text: yatkhalviṣṭavipākaṃ nirvāṇaprāpakaṃ ca duḥkhaparitrāṇāt, tatkālamatyantaṃ vā, tatkuśalam | niruktirapīyam | niravadyadevamanuṣyastrīrūpanirvartanācchikṣitacitrakararūpanirvartanavat | kuśalamiva kuśalamaupamiko 'yaṃ śabdaniveśaḥ | tadyathā śikṣitaḥ puruṣaḥ kuśānakṣatahasto lunāti sa kuśala iti nirucyate, tadvadanyāmapi kriyāmavikṛtāṃ saṃpādayan kuśala (

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 137)
) 'Unwholesome is the opposite' — like a camel or an owl [which are inauspicious]. 'Indeterminate is otherwise' — because it produces the result of neither [wholesome nor unwholesome].

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] That which has a desired result and which leads to <s>nirvāṇa</s> — through deliverance from suffering, whether temporarily or ultimately — that is wholesome. The etymology too [supports this]: from the production of blameless forms of gods, humans, and women — like the production of forms by a trained artist. [The word] '<s>kuśala</s>' is used figuratively, by analogy. Just as a trained person who cuts <s>kuśa</s> grass without cutting his hand is called '<s>kuśala</s>' (skillful), so too one who accomplishes any other action without distortion is called '<s>kuśala</s>.' (

body.text: anyānyapi trīṇi karmāṇyuktāni | puṇyamapuṇyamānejyaṃ ca | tatra tāvat
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Three other types of <s>karma</s> are also stated: meritorious (<s>puṇya</s>), demeritorious (<s>apuṇya</s>), and imperturbable (<s>ānejya</s>). Therein, now:

children.translated_text: The first — that obtained in the desire [realm] — is merit (<s>puṇya</s>); demerit (<s>apuṇya</s>) is of unwholesome nature;
that belonging to the higher grounds is imperturbable (<s>ānejya</s>), because it does not waver with respect to its result. (Abhidh-d 175)

body.text: kāmāvacaraṃ hi kuśalaṃ karma puṇyamakuśalamapuṇyamityucyate | ūrdhvabhūmikamānejyam |'; tadūrdhvaṃ dhātudvaye śubhaṃ karmānejyamityucyate | kasmātpunaretadānejyamityuktam ? 'vipākaṃ pratyanejanāt |'; kāmāvacaraṃ hi karma vipākaṃ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 138)

children.text: ) prati kampate lavaṇopamasūtraṇyāyena | katham ? avyavasthānāt | anyagatikamapi hyanyasyāṃ gatau vipacyate | tadanyadevanaikāyikaṃ cānyatra devanikāye | yadeva hi pramāṇabalavarṇasukhabhogādisaṃvartanīyaṃ karma deveṣu vipacyeta tadeva kadācidanyapratyayavaśānmanuṣyatiryakpreteṣu vipacyate | karmajāticodaneyaṃ bhagavato vivakṣitā na dravyacodaneti |
children.translated_text: ) according to the principle of the <s>Lavaṇopama-sūtra</s>. How? Because of instability. For even <s>karma</s> belonging to one destiny can ripen in another destiny. And even that which belongs to one class of gods can [ripen] in another class. For the very <s>karma</s> that would produce measure, strength, color, happiness, enjoyment, and the like among the gods — that same [karma] sometimes, due to the power of other conditions, ripens among humans, animals, and hungry ghosts. [The <s>Bhagavān</s>'s] intended meaning is a challenge to the type of <s>karma</s>, not a challenge to the substance.

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Wholesome <s>karma</s> of the desire-realm is called 'merit' (<s>puṇya</s>); unwholesome is called 'demerit.' 'That belonging to the higher grounds is imperturbable.' The wholesome <s>karma</s> above [the desire-realm], in the two higher realms, is called 'imperturbable.' Why then is it called 'imperturbable'? 'Because it does not waver with respect to its result.' For desire-realm <s>karma</s> wavers with respect to its result (

body.text: atrāha | nanu ca trīṇi dhyānāni señjitānyuktāni bhagavatā- "yadatra vitarkitaṃ vicāritamidamatrāryā iñjitamityāhuḥ" ityevamādi ? samādhyapakṣālāṃsteṣāṃ sandhāyaivamuktam | ānejyānyapi tu tānyuktānyānejyasūtre, ānejyasaṃpreyagāminīṃ pratipadamārabhya ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here one objects: 'But are not the three [lower] <s>dhyānas</s> said by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to be subject to disturbance: "Whatever is thought and reflected upon here — the noble ones call this disturbance"?' This was said with reference to the defects of those concentrations. But they are also called 'imperturbable' in the <s>Ānejya-sūtra</s>, in reference to the practice leading to the imperturbable.

body.text: punaranyāni trīṇi karmāṇyuktāni- "sukhavedanīyaṃ duḥkhavedanīyaṃ, aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyaṃ ca |" tatra
body.translated_text: Furthermore, three other types of <s>karma</s> are stated: 'to be experienced as pleasure, to be experienced as suffering, and to be experienced as neither-suffering-nor-pleasure.' Therein:

children.translated_text: Wholesome <s>karma</s> is to be experienced as pleasure, from the <s>dhyānas</s> below the fourth;
to be experienced as equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) elsewhere; unwholesome [karma] is to be experienced as suffering. (Abhidh-d 176)

body.text: tatra śubhaṃ karma yāvattṛtīye dhyāne sukhavedyamityucyate | etāvatī khalu bhūmiḥ sukhāyā vedanāyāḥ | tadeva caturthadhyānātprabhṛtyupekṣāvedanīyamityucyate | akuśalaṃ tu karma duḥkhavedanīyamityucyate |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Wholesome <s>karma</s> up to the third <s>dhyāna</s> is said to be experienced as pleasure. For this is the extent of the ground of pleasurable feeling. That same [karma], from the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> onward, is said to be experienced as equanimity-feeling. But unwholesome <s>karma</s> is said to be experienced as suffering.

body.text: kiṃ punarvedanaiva vipākaḥ ? netyāha | prādhāniko 'yaṃ rnirdeśaḥ | sacatuskandhasambhāraṃ hi sukhamabhipretam | dārṣṭāntikānāṃ tu sukhaiva vedanā vipākaḥ cetanaiva ca karma | ābhidhārmikānāṃ tu pañcaskandho vipākahetuḥ pañcaskandhāśca vipāka iti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] But is feeling alone the result? No, he says. This is a statement of what is primary. For the pleasure intended is that which has the accompaniment of four aggregates. But for the <s>Dārṣṭāntikas</s>, pleasure-feeling alone is the result, and volition (<s>cetanā</s>) alone is <s>karma</s>. For the <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s>, however, the five aggregates are the causal basis of result, and the five aggregates are also the result.

body.text: kathaṃ punaravedanāsvabhāvaṃ karma sukhavedanīyamityucyate ? sukhāyā vedanāyā hitaṃ sukhavedanīyam | sukhāsyā vedanīyo vipāka iti vā |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] How then is <s>karma</s> that is not of the nature of feeling said to be 'experienced as pleasure'? [It is called so] because it is beneficial (<s>hita</s>) for pleasurable feeling — 'to be experienced as pleasure.' Or: its experiential result (<s>vedanīya vipāka</s>) is pleasure.

body.text: kiṃ punaraduḥkhāsukhā vedanā caturthadhyānādadho na vidyate ? na khalu na vidyate | kiṃ tarhi?
body.translated_text: But does the neither-suffering-nor-pleasure feeling not exist below the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>? Indeed it does exist. But then:

children.translated_text: Below [the fourth dhyāna] too there is moderate <s>karma</s>; in the last <s>dhyāna</s> too, because of <s>nirvāṇa</s>,
because of the desire for simultaneous triple result, and because of the result of the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> [ground]. (Abhidh-d 177)

body.text: aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyaṃ khalu karma caturthadhyānādadho 'pyasti tṛtīye dvitīye prathame ca dhyāne | parinirvṛte upekṣāyāṃ ca sthitaḥ parinirvāti | kiñca, 'yugapat trivipākeṣṭeḥ |'; uktaṃ hi- "syāt trayāṇāṃ karmaṇāmapūrvācaramo vipāko vipacyeta | syātsukhavedanīyasya rūpaṃ, duḥkhavedanīyasya cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ, aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyasya cittaviprayuktāḥ" iti | ato 'pyastyadhastādaduḥkhāsukhavedanīyaṃ karma | kiñca, 'dhyānāntaravipākataḥ |'; nahi dhyānāntare upekṣāmantareṇa vipāko 'nyā vedanā vipacyate | tatra sukhaduḥkhayorabhāvāt ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Karma</s> to be experienced as neither-suffering-nor-pleasure indeed exists below the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> — in the third, second, and first <s>dhyānas</s> too. One who has entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, abiding in equanimity, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Furthermore, 'because of the desire for simultaneous triple result' — for it is said: 'It is possible that the unprecedented final result of three <s>karmas</s> may ripen [simultaneously]: the form may be [the result] of [karma] to be experienced as pleasure, the mind and mental factors [may be the result] of [karma] to be experienced as suffering, and the [dharmas] disjoined from mind [may be the result] of [karma] to be experienced as neither-suffering-nor-pleasure.' From this too, <s>karma</s> to be experienced as neither-suffering-nor-pleasure exists below [the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>]. Furthermore, 'because of the result of the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> [ground]' — for in the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> [ground], no result other than equanimity-feeling ripens, because suffering and pleasure are absent there.

body.text: punaścaturvidhaṃ karma dṛṣṭavedyādibhedataḥ /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>karma</s> is fourfold, from the distinction of to-be-experienced-in-this-life and so forth.

body.text: tadetatkarma samāsato dvividhaṃ, niyatavedanīyamaniyatavedanīyaṃ ca | tatra niyatavedanīyaṃ trividham | dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyamupapadyavedanīyamaparaparyāyavedanīyaṃ ca- ityetat trividhaṃ karma niyatavedanīyam | caturthamaniyatavedanīyam |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This <s>karma</s>, in summary, is twofold: with determinate result (<s>niyatavedanīya</s>) and with indeterminate result (<s>aniyatavedanīya</s>). The determinate is threefold: to be experienced in this very life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmavedanīya</s>), to be experienced at rebirth (<s>upapadyavedanīya</s>), and to be experienced in a subsequent [life] (<s>aparaparyāyavedanīya</s>) — this threefold <s>karma</s> has determinate result. The fourth has indeterminate result.

body.text: tatra dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ yatraiva janmani kṛtaṃ tatraiva vipacyate | upapadyavedanīyaṃ yad dvitīye janmani | aparaparyāyavedanīyaṃ tasmātpareṇa |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The to-be-experienced-in-this-life ripens in the very birth in which it was performed. The to-be-experienced-at-rebirth ripens in the second birth. The to-be-experienced-subsequently, after that.

body.text: ataḥ punaścaturvidhātkarmaṇaḥ katamena janmākṣipyate?
body.translated_text: From this fourfold <s>karma</s>, by which one is birth projected?

body.text: janmanastribhirākṣepo dṛṣṭadharmāhvayādṛte // Abhidh-d_178 //
body.translated_text: Birth is projected by three [types of karma], excluding [karma] called 'to be experienced in this life.' (Abhidh-d 178)

body.text: na khalu dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyena karmaṇā nikāyasabhāga ākṣipyate ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Class-homogeneity (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>) is not projected by <s>karma</s> to be experienced in this life.

body.text: atha kasmindhātau kasyāṃ vāṃ gatau katividhaṃ karmākṣipyate ?
body.translated_text: Now, in which realm and in which destiny is what kind of <s>karma</s> projected?

children.translated_text: And the projection of all four [types of karma] exists everywhere, except for the hells;
because in those [hells], wholesome [karma] does not ripen, since its desired fruit is absent there. (Abhidh-d 179)

body.text: sarveṣu khalu triṣu dhātuṣu sarvāsu ca pañcasu gatiṣu caturṇāmapi karmaṇāmākṣepaḥ kuśalānāmakuśalānāṃ ca | narakānvarjayitvā | narakeṣu hi dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ kuśalaṃ nākṣipyate | tatreṣṭavipākābhāvādanyat trividhamākṣipyate | kiñca,
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] In all three realms and in all five destinies, the projection of all four types of <s>karma</s> exists — both wholesome and unwholesome — except for the hells. For in the hells, wholesome [karma] to be experienced in this life does not project, because there is no desired result there. The other three types do project. Furthermore,

children.translated_text: One who has become dispassionate toward [a ground] does not perform <s>karma</s> to-be-experienced-at-rebirth there, [if that] ordinary person
is stable [in dispassion]; nor does a noble one, [even if] unstable, [perform karma] to-be-experienced-subsequently in the two — the summit of existence and its root. (Abhidh-d 180)

body.text: yataḥ khalu bhūmerviraktaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ sa ca sthiro bhavatyaparihāṇadharmā sa tatropapadyavedyaṃ karma nākṣipati | trividhamanyatkaroti | āryapudgalastu vītarāgo na ca parihāṇadharmā tatropapadyavedyamaparaparyāyavedanīyaṃ ca karma na karoti | na hyasau bhavyaḥ punaradharimaṃ bhūmimāyātum | aniyataṃ tu kuryād dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ yatropapannaḥ kāmadhātau bhavāgre ca | parihāṇadharmāpi tvāryaḥ kāmadhātau vītarāgaḥ, bhavāgrādvā, tayorupapadyāparaparyāyavedanīyaṃ karmābhavyaḥ kartum | kiṃ kāraṇam ? phalāddhyasau parihīṇo bhavati | na cāsti phalaparihīṇasya kālakriyeti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] An ordinary person who has become dispassionate toward a ground and is stable — not subject to decline — does not project <s>karma</s> to be experienced at rebirth there. He performs the other three types. But a noble person (<s>ārya</s>) who has become dispassionate and is not subject to decline does not perform <s>karma</s> to be experienced at rebirth or to be experienced subsequently there. For he is not capable of returning to that lower ground. But he may perform indeterminate [karma] and [karma] to be experienced in this life, where he is reborn — in the desire-realm and at the summit of existence. However, even a noble one subject to decline, [if] dispassionate toward the desire-realm or the summit of existence, is incapable of performing <s>karma</s> to be experienced at rebirth or subsequently in those two [places]. What is the reason? Because he has fallen from the fruit; and there is no death for one who has fallen from the fruit.

body.text: atha kimantarābhavikaḥ karmākṣipati nākṣipati ? ākṣipatītyāha | (

children.translated_text: [Reference:] Jaini p. 143.

children.text: ) tatra kāmāvacaro 'ntarābhavaḥ dvāviṃśatividhaṃ karmākṣipati | pañca garbhāvasthāḥ kalalārbudaghanapeśīpraśākhāvasthāḥ | pañca jātāvasthāḥ | bālyakaumārayuvamadhyamasthavirāvasthāḥ | tā etā niyatāniyatabhedena viṃśatirākṣipyante, ekanikāyatvāt | ata evāntarābhavavedanīyaṃ karma noktam | upapadyavedanīyenaiva tasyākṣepāt ||
children.translated_text: Therein, the intermediate existence of the desire-realm projects karma of twenty-two kinds. Five are embryonic stages: the <s>kalala</s>, <s>arbuda</s>, <s>ghana</s>, <s>peśī</s>, and <s>praśākhā</s> stages. Five are post-birth stages: infancy, youth, young adulthood, middle age, and old age. These ten, by the division of determined and undetermined, make twenty that are projected — because of being of one class [with the intermediate existence]. For this very reason, karma to-be-experienced-in-the-intermediate-existence is not mentioned [separately] — because its projection is by the karma-to-be-experienced-at-birth itself.

body.translated_text: Now, does the intermediate-existence being (<s>antarābhavika</s>) project karma, or does it not project? It does project, he says.

body.text: kīdṛśaṃ punaḥ karma niyataṃ bhavatyaniyataṃ vā ?
body.translated_text: What kind of karma, further, is determined (<s>niyata</s>) and what undetermined (<s>aniyata</s>)?

children.translated_text: Karma that is performed with an intense or violent mind, that is practiced repeatedly,

children.text: satkṣetre kriyate yacca phalaṃ tasya niyamyate // Abhidh-d_181 //
children.translated_text: or that is done in a [worthy] field — the fruit of that is determined. (Abhidh-d 181)

body.text: yadi karma raudreṇa tīvrakleśānugatena cittena kṛtaṃ bhavati, yacca ghanaśraddhāsalilābhyukṣitena kriyate, yacca mṛdvapyabhīkṣṇaṃ niṣevyate, yacca kiñcidguṇavati kṣetre kriyate śubhamaśubhaṃ vā phalaṃ tasya karmaṇo niyamyate ||
body.translated_text: If karma is done with a violent mind pervaded by intense affliction, or if done with [a mind] moistened by the waters of deep faith, or if even mild [karma is] practiced repeatedly, or if something is done in a field possessing some quality — whether wholesome or unwholesome — the fruit of that karma is determined.

body.text: atha dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ karma kīdṛśamityucyate-
body.translated_text: Now, what is karma-to-be-experienced-in-this-very-life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmavedanīya</s>)? It is stated:

children.translated_text: Due to the distinction of field and intention, the fruit ripens immediately;
and for one emerged from cessation [attainment] and so forth, immediate temporal fruit-production [occurs]. (Abhidh-d 182)

body.text: tatra kṣetraviśeṣādyathā da(?) kṣajātakādiṣu | āśayaviśeṣādyathā bakalāta(?) syokṣanirmocanādiṣu |
body.translated_text: Therein, [an example] of distinction of field — as in the <s>Jātaka</s> stories and so forth. [An example] of distinction of intention — as in the cases of [the story of] washing an ox, liberation, and so forth.

body.text: kīdṛśe punastat kṣetre viśiṣṭaṃ bhavati yatra dṛṣṭe dharme vipāko vipacyate ? buddhapramukhastāvadbhikṣusaṃgho | 'nirodhavyutthitādau ca sadyaḥ kālaphalakriyā |'; pañcasu ca pudgaleṣu kṛtaṃ nirodhasamāpattya raṇāmaitrīdarśanamārgādarhatphalādvyutthiteṣu kārāpakārā dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaphalā bhavanti | nirodhasamāpatteḥ khalu vyutthitaḥ parāṃ śāntiṃ labhate | nirvāṇasadṛśadharmānubhavanāt | araṇāvyutthitasyāpyapramāṇasattvahitādhyāśayapravṛttā santatirvartate | evaṃ maitrīvyutthitasya | strautaāpannasyāpi nirmalajñānalābhāt | arhato 'pi sarvakleśaprahāṇānnirmalā vartante ||
body.translated_text: In what kind of field, further, is [the karma] distinguished such that maturation ripens in this very life? First, the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> headed by the Buddha. 'And for one emerged from cessation and so forth, immediate temporal fruit-production.' For the five persons — one emerged from the cessation-attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>), from <s>araṇā</s> (non-hostility meditation), from <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), from the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>), or from the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> — acts of benefit and harm become karma-to-be-experienced-in-this-very-life. One emerged from cessation-attainment indeed attains supreme peace — because of experiencing dharmas similar to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. For one emerged from <s>araṇā</s> too, the continuum operates with an intention directed at the welfare of immeasurable beings. Likewise for one emerged from loving-kindness. For the stream-enterer too, because of attaining undefiled knowledge. And for the <s>Arhat</s> too, because of the abandonment of all afflictions, [their continuums] operate in a purified [state].

body.text: niyatavipākasya ca karmaṇaḥ śubhāśubhasya yā bhūmistadatyantavairāgyāttatkarma dṛṣṭe dharme vipacyata ityataḥ
body.translated_text: And for karma of determined maturation, whether wholesome or unwholesome — whose level that is — through complete dispassion from that [level], that karma ripens in this very life. Therefore:

children.translated_text: Because of non-re-arising in that level,

body.text: dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ bhavati | kīdṛśaṃ punaretatkarma ?
body.translated_text: it becomes included as karma-to-be-experienced-in-this-very-life. What kind of karma is this?

body.text: vipākaniyataṃ ca yat /
body.translated_text: And that which is determined as to maturation —

body.text: taccaitatkarma vipākaniyataṃ draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: that karma should be seen as determined regarding maturation.

children.translated_text: And that should be known as having visible fruit —

body.text: dṛṣṭe dharme khalu tasya vipāko vipacyate | kataratpunaretat ?
body.translated_text: its maturation ripens in this very life. Which one is this?

body.text: karmādaḥ paripūrakam // Abhidh-d_183 //
body.translated_text: This karma is the completing one, not the projecting one. (Abhidh-d 183)

body.text: nākṣepakamiti ||
body.translated_text: Not the projecting one.

body.text: vipākaḥ khalu vedanāpradhāna ityata idaṃ vicāryate | syātkarmaṇaścaitasikyeva vedanā vipāko na kāyikī ? syātkāyikyeva na caitasikī syādityāha-
body.translated_text: Since maturation is principally feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), this is now examined: Is the feeling that is the maturation of karma only mental (<s>caitasikī</s>) and not bodily (<s>kāyikī</s>)? Or only bodily and not mental? He says:

children.translated_text: For wholesome [karma] without <s>vicāra</s> (discursive thought), only mental feeling

children.text: vipākaḥ kāyikī tviṣṭā duḥkhavedyasya karmaṇaḥ // Abhidh-d_184 //
children.translated_text: is the maturation; but bodily [feeling] is the desirable [maturation] of karma experienced as suffering. (Abhidh-d 184)

body.text: kuśalaṃ khalvavicāraṃ karma dhyānāntarātprabhṛti yāvadbhavāgram | tasyāvicārasya kuśalasya karmaṇaścaitasikyeva vedanā vipākaḥ | kasmānna kāyikī ? tasyāḥ avaśyaṃ savitarkavicāratvāt | kāyikyeva tvaśubhasya duḥkhavedanāyasya kāyikyeva vedanā vipākaḥ | kasmānna caitasikī ? caitasikaṃ hi daurmanasyaṃ na vipākaḥ |
body.translated_text: Wholesome karma without <s>vicāra</s> [begins] from the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> up to the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). For that <s>vicāra</s>-free wholesome karma, only mental feeling is the maturation. Why not bodily? Because that [bodily feeling] necessarily involves <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>. But for unwholesome [karma] experienced as suffering-feeling, only bodily feeling is the maturation. Why not mental? Because mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) is not a maturation.

body.text: yattarhi karmavaśātsattvānāṃ cittakṣepaḥ tatsaṃprayuktā vedanā kathaṃ na vipākaḥ ? na hi tatra cittaṃ karmaṇo vipākaḥ | kiṃ tarhi ? yo mahābhūtātāṃ prakopaḥ sa vipākaḥ | tatastajjātaṃ cittaṃ vipākaśabdenopacaryate ||
body.translated_text: But when, due to the force of karma, there is mental derangement (<s>cittakṣepa</s>) in beings — how is the feeling associated with that not a maturation? In that case, the mind is not the maturation of karma. What then? The disturbance of the great elements — that is the maturation. From that, the mind born from it is figuratively designated by the word 'maturation.'

body.text: punaścaturvidhaṃ karmoktam- "asti karma kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇavipākam | asti śuklaṃ śuklavipākam | asti karma kṛṣṇaśuklaṃ kṛṣṇaśuklavipākam | astyakṛṣṇamaśuklamavipākaṃ karma karmakṣayāya saṃvartate'; iti | tatra
body.translated_text: And fourfold karma has been stated: 'There is karma that is black with black maturation; there is white with white maturation; there is karma that is black-and-white with black-and-white maturation; there is karma neither black nor white, without maturation, that leads to the destruction of karma.' Therein:

children.translated_text: Unwholesome with maturation is black; wholesome born in the form[-realm] with maturation is white;

children.text: śubhāśubhaṃ dvidhā kāme nirmalaṃ tatprahāṇakṛt // Abhidh-d_185 //
children.translated_text: the wholesome-and-unwholesome is twofold in the desire-realm; the undefiled [karma] effects the abandonment of those. (Abhidh-d 185)

body.text: aśubhaṃ khalu karma ekāntena kṛṣṇaṃ kliṣṭatvāt | kṛṣṇavipākaṃ cāmanojñavipākatvāt | rūpāptantu śubhamekāntena śuklam, akuśalenāvyavakīrṇatvāt | śuklavipākaṃ ca manojñavipākatvāt |
body.translated_text: Unwholesome karma is exclusively black — because of being afflicted. And it has black maturation — because of having unpleasant maturation. But wholesome [karma] attained in the form-realm is exclusively white — because of not being mixed with the unwholesome. And it has white maturation — because of having pleasant maturation.

body.text: ārūpyāptaṃ kasmānnocyate ? yatra hi dvividho 'sti vipākaḥ- antarābhavikaścopapattibhavikaśca; trividhasya ca kāyavāṅmanaskarmaṇastatraivoktamiti |
body.translated_text: Why is [karma] attained in the formless realm not mentioned? Because maturation is of two kinds there — intermediate-existence and birth-existence — and because the threefold karma of body, speech, and mind has been stated only there.

body.text: "kāmāptaṃ śuklaṃ kuṣṇaśuklamakuśalavyavakīrṇatvāt, kṛṣṇaśuklavipākaṃ vyavakīrṇavipākatvāt |" santānata etadvyavasthāpitaṃ na svabhāvato na hyevaṃjātīyakamevaṃ karmāsti vipāko vā yatkṛṣṇaṃ ca syācchuklaṃ ca, anyonyavirodhāt | nanu caivamakuśalasyāpi karmaṇaḥ kuśalavyavakīrṇatvātkṛṣṇaśuklatvaṃ prāpnoti ? nāvaśyamakuśalaṃ kuśalena vyavakīryate | kāmadhātau tvasya balavatvātkuśalantu vyavakīryate durbalatvāditi |
