body.translated_text: '[Karma] attained in the desire-realm is white-and-black — because of being mixed with the unwholesome; it has black-and-white maturation — because of having mixed maturation.' This is established by way of the continuum, not by nature — for there does not exist a karma or maturation of such a type that is both black and white, because of mutual contradiction. Objection: But in this case, unwholesome karma too, being mixed with wholesome, would be black-and-white! Reply: Unwholesome [karma] is not necessarily mixed with wholesome. In the desire-realm, however, because of its [the unwholesome's] strength, it is the wholesome that gets mixed — because of its weakness.

body.text: anāsravaṃ karmaiṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ kṣayāya prahāṇāya saṃvartate | taddhyakṛṣṇamakliṣṭatvādaśuklaṃ vipākaśuklatābhāvāt | ābhiprāyiko 'pyeṣa śuklaśabdaḥ | uktaṃ tu bhagavatā mahatyāṃ śūnyatāyāmaśaikṣadharmānārabhya- (

children.translated_text: [Reference:] Jaini p. 147.

children.text: ) "ime te ānanda, dharmā ekāntaśuklā ekāntānavadyāḥ" iti | śāstre ca- "śukladharmāḥ katame ? kuśalā dharmā anivṛtāvyākṛtāśca |" iti | avipākaṃ dhātvapatitatvāt pravṛttivirodhācca |
children.translated_text: 'These, <s>Ānanda</s>, are dharmas exclusively white, exclusively blameless.' And in the treatise: 'What are white dharmas? Wholesome dharmas and unobstructed indeterminate ones.' It is without maturation — because of not falling within the realms, and because of conflict with continued existence.

body.translated_text: Undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) karma leads to the destruction, the abandonment, of these three kinds of karma. For it is non-black — because of being unafflicted; and non-white — because of the absence of the 'white' [quality] of maturation. This use of the word 'white' is figurative. But the Blessed One stated in the Great Emptiness [discourse], beginning with the non-learner's dharmas:

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ sarvamanāsravaṃ karma sarvasyāsya trividhasya karmaṇaḥ kṣayāya saṃvartate ? netyucyate | kiṃ tarhi ?
body.translated_text: Now, does all undefiled karma lead to the destruction of all this threefold karma? No, it is said. What then?

children.translated_text: Four [sets of] volitions (<s>cetanā</s>) on the seeing-path at [the moment of] seeing; and on the cultivation-path,
the uninterrupted paths in the desire-realm — this karma effects the destruction of the black. (Abhidh-d 186)

children.text: navame cetanā yā tu sā kṛṣṇākṛṣṇayāghātinī /
children.translated_text: But the volition on the ninth [path] destroys both black and non-black;

children.text: antānantaryamārgasthā dhyāne dhyāne sitasya tu // Abhidh-d_187 //
children.translated_text: that standing on the last uninterrupted path in each <s>dhyāna</s> [destroys] the white. (Abhidh-d 187)

body.text: tatra darśanamārge tāvaccatasṛṣu dharmajñānakṣāntiṣu kāmavairāgye cāṣṭāsvānantaryamārgeṣu yā cetanā dvādaśaprakārā sā kṛṣṇasya karmaṇaḥ prahāṇakārī | kāmavairāgyānantaryamārgeṇāvaseyā cetanā sā kṛṣṇaśuklakarmakṣayakārī | dhyāne dhyāne tvānantaryamārge paścime yā cetanā caturvidhā sā śuklakarmāpahantrī |
body.translated_text: On the path of seeing: the volitions in the four <s>dharmajñānakṣāntis</s> (dharma-knowledge-patiences) and in the eight uninterrupted paths of desire-realm dispassion — those twelve kinds of volition effect the abandonment of black karma. The volition to be determined by the uninterrupted path of desire-realm dispassion — that effects the destruction of black-and-white karma. But in each <s>dhyāna</s>, the volition on the last uninterrupted path — those four kinds — destroys white karma.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇamantyenaivānantaryamārgeṇa kuśalasya karmaṇaḥ prahāṇaṃ nānyena ? na hi tasya svabhāvaprahāṇaṃ prahīṇasyāpi saṃmukhībhāvāt | kiṃ tarhi ? tadālambanakleśaprahāṇāt | ato yāvadeko 'pi tadālambanaḥ kleśaprakāro (

children.translated_text: [Reference:] Jaini p. 148.

children.text: ) 'sti tāvadasya prahāṇaṃ nopalabhyate | taccaitadasat | prahīṇaṃ hi tat, na tu vihīnam | ataḥ samudācaratīti | gatametat ||
children.translated_text: exists, its abandonment is not obtained. But this is incorrect — for it is abandoned, not [merely] absent; hence it can still occur. This topic is concluded.

body.translated_text: But what is the reason that the abandonment of wholesome karma is by the last uninterrupted path alone and not by another? For there is no abandonment of its own nature [here] — since even what is abandoned can become present again. What then? Through the abandonment of the affliction that takes it as its object. Therefore, as long as even one type of affliction taking that as its object

body.text: sūtra uktam- "trīṇi duścaritāni | kāyaduścaritaṃ vāṅmanoduścaritam | evaṃ sucaritāni" iti | teṣāṃ kaḥ svabhāvaḥ ? tatra tāvat-
body.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s> it is stated: 'There are three kinds of bad conduct: bodily bad conduct, vocal bad conduct, and mental bad conduct. Likewise good conduct.' What is their intrinsic nature? Therein:

body.text: kāyādyakuśalaṃ karma sarvaṃ duścaritaṃ matam /
body.translated_text: All unwholesome karma of body and so forth is regarded as bad conduct (<s>duścarita</s>).

body.text: sarvamiti sasāmantakamaulapṛṣṭhamityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'All' means including the preparatory and subsequent [phases], plus the principal and accessory — this is the meaning.

body.text: abhidhyādīnyapi trīṇi manoduścaritatrayam // Abhidh-d_188 //
body.translated_text: The three beginning with covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) are also the triad of mental bad conduct. (Abhidh-d 188)

body.text: sarvamevākuśalaṃ kāyakarma kāyaduścaritam | evaṃ vāṅmanoduścaritam | akarmasvabhāvānyapi tvabhidhyādīni manoduścaritasvabhāvāni |
body.translated_text: All unwholesome bodily karma is bodily bad conduct. Likewise vocal and mental bad conduct. But covetousness and the rest, though not of the nature of karma, have the nature of mental bad conduct.

body.text: "abhidhyādaya eva karmasvabhāvāni" iti sthitibhāgīyāḥ | tacca na, karmakleśaikatvadoṣāt | sthitibhāgīyā nāma śākyāḥ sva(śva?) lāṃgūlikadvitīyanāmānaḥ | te khalvabhidhyādīni manaskarmasvabhāvānīcchanti | teṣāṃ (

children.translated_text: [Reference:] Jaini p. 149.

children.text: ) karmakleśaikatvasaṅkaraḥ prāpnoti | kośakāraḥ- "ko 'tra doṣaḥ" ? yadi kaścitkleśaḥ karmāpi syādvāyasaḥ sārasaḥ syāt | karmakleśānāṃ cātyantasvabhāvaprabhāvakriyāphalabhedabhinnānāmekatvaparikalpaiḥ sāṃkhyīyādidarśanamabhyupagataṃ syāt |
children.translated_text: the confusion of identity between karma and affliction would follow. The <s>Kośa</s>-author [says]: 'What fault is there?' If some affliction were also karma, a crow would be a crane. And by the fabrication of identity between karma and afflictions — which are entirely distinct in their nature, power, activity, and fruit — the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and similar views would be endorsed.

body.translated_text: 'Covetousness and the rest are of the very nature of karma' — [say] the <s>Sthitibhāgīyas</s>. But that is not [correct], because of the fault of identity between karma and affliction. The <s>Sthitibhāgīyas</s> are the <s>Śākyas</s>, also known by the second name 'dog-tail' [school]. They indeed hold that covetousness and the rest are of the nature of mental karma. For them,

body.text: 'api'; śabdātpunaratra sūtroktāstrayo vaṅkāstrayo doṣāstrayaḥ kaṣāyā ākṛṣyante | teṣāṃ punaridaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yathākrameṇa | śāṭhyajaṃ kāyakarma kāyavaṅka (

children.translated_text: [Reference:] Jaini p. 150.

children.text: ) ityucyate | kuṭilānvayatvāt | evaṃ śāṭhyajaṃ vāṅmanaskarma vāṅmanovaṅka ityucyate | dveṣajāḥ punasta eva trayo doṣā ityākhyāyante, cittapradoṣānvayatvāt | rāgajaṃ punaḥ kāyakarma kāyakaṣāya ityuktaṃ rañjanātmakatvāt | evaṃ vāṅmanaḥkaṣāyau draṣṭavyau | tāni punaḥ kuśalāni kāyavāṅmanaskarmāṇi trīṇi sucaritāni boddhavyāni | etānyeva trīṇi śauceyānyuktāni |
children.translated_text: because of following a crooked course. Likewise vocal and mental karma born of deceit are called 'vocal crookedness' and 'mental crookedness.' Those same three, when born of hatred, are designated 'faults' (<s>doṣa</s>) — because of following mental corruption. Bodily karma born of passion is called 'bodily impurity' (<s>kāyakaṣāya</s>) — because of having the nature of dyeing. Likewise vocal and mental impurities should be understood. The three wholesome bodily, vocal, and mental karmas should be understood as the three good conducts (<s>sucarita</s>). These same three are called the three 'purities' (<s>śauceya</s>).

body.translated_text: From the word 'also,' further the three 'crookednesses,' three 'faults,' and three 'impurities' stated in the <s>sūtra</s> are included. Their characteristics are as follows, in order: Bodily karma born of deceit is called 'bodily crookedness' (<s>kāyavaṅka</s>),

body.text: aśaikṣasantāne trīṇi mauneyānyucyante | tatra kāyasucaritaṃ kāyamauneyaṃ vāksucaritaṃ vāṅmauneyaṃ mana eva tu mithyāsaṃkalpoparamānmunirityākhyāyate | taduparamāddhi kāyavāgjalpoparamo bhavati | muneridaṃ mauneyamiti niruktiḥ | (

children.translated_text: [Reference:] Jaini p. 151.

children.text:
)
kasmātpunararhata eva mauneyāni ? tasya paramārthamunitvāt | sa khalu sarvakleśajalpoparamānmunirityucyate |
children.translated_text: Why are the silences only of an <s>Arhat</s>? Because he alone has ultimate sage-hood (<s>munitva</s>). For he is called a sage because of the cessation of all affliction-chatter.

body.translated_text: In the continuum of a non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), [they are called] the three 'silences' (<s>mauneya</s>). Therein, bodily good conduct is bodily silence; vocal good conduct is vocal silence; but because of the cessation of wrong resolve, [one is called] a <s>muni</s> (silent sage) with respect to mind. For from the cessation of that [wrong resolve], the cessation of bodily and vocal chatter follows. 'This is the silence (<s>mauneya</s>) of the sage (<s>muni</s>)' — this is the etymology.

body.text: eṣā punarmauneyaśauceyadeśanā mithyāmaunaśaucābhiyuktānadhikṛtyadeśiteti tadetatsaha mauneyaśauceyarnirdiṣyate ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, this teaching of silence and purity was taught with reference to those devoted to false silence and false purity — hence it is set forth together with silence and purity.

children.translated_text: The wholesome [conducts] — non-covetousness and so forth — are declared the triad of good conduct;

children.text: dvayaṃmaulamadaḥ karma mārgā daśa śubhāśubhāḥ // Abhidh-d_189 //
children.translated_text: the pair — the principal below — the ten paths are wholesome and unwholesome. (Abhidh-d 189)

body.text: dvayaṃ punaretatsucaritaduścaritākhyaṃ yanmaulaṃ te daśa śubhāścāśubhāśca karmapathā bhavanti prayogapṛṣṭhavarjyāḥ |
body.translated_text: This pair called good conduct and bad conduct — that which is 'principal' — those are the ten wholesome and unwholesome karma-paths, excluding the preparatory and subsequent [phases].

body.text: tatra kāyasucaritasya pradeśaḥ pṛyogapṛṣṭhākhyo madyādiviratidānejyādikaḥ | vāksucaritasya priyavacanādikaḥ | manaḥsucaritasya śubhā cetanā |
body.translated_text: Therein, the portion of bodily good conduct called preparatory and subsequent includes abstention from intoxicants, giving, sacrifice, and so forth. Of vocal good conduct — pleasant speech and so forth. Of mental good conduct — wholesome volition.

body.text: kāyaduścaritasyāpi pareṣāṃ jīvitabhogadārāpahāraprayogapṛṣṭhākhyaḥ | vāgduścaritasyāpyapriyavacanādyākhyaḥ | manoduścaritasyāpyakuśalaṃ manaskarmai..................steṣāṃ nātyaudārikatvāt |
body.translated_text: Of bodily bad conduct too — the [portion] called preparatory and subsequent [includes] the depriving of others' life, possessions, and wives. Of vocal bad conduct — unpleasant speech and so forth. Of mental bad conduct — unwholesome mental karma... because of their not being exceedingly gross.

body.text: yastu prāṇātipātādattādānakāmamithyācāraviratyākhyo maulaḥ sa kuśalaḥ karmapathaḥ, tasyaudārikatvena mahānuśaṃsatamaphalatvāt | yastu pareṣāṃ jīvitabhogaparadārāpahārakāyaparispandaḥ sa maulaḥ sa cākuśalaḥ karmapathaḥ | evaṃ yathāsaṃbhavamanyeṣāṃ draṣṭavyamiti ||
body.translated_text: But that which is the principal [phase] — the abstention called refraining from killing, taking what is not given, and sexual misconduct — that is the wholesome karma-path, because of its grossness being the fruit of the greatest benefit. But that which is the bodily movement of depriving others of life, possessions, and others' wives — that is the principal [phase], and that is the unwholesome karma-path. Likewise for the others, as applicable.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau caturthādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ |
body.translated_text: End of the second section of the fourth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: caturthādhyāye
body.translated_text: Fourth chapter,

body.text: tṛtīyapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: third section.

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | ye ete daśakarmapathā eṣāṃ kati vijñaptisvabhāvāḥ katyavijñaptisvabhāvāḥ katyubhayasvabhāvāḥ ?
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: Of these ten courses of action (<s>karmapatha</s>), how many are of the nature of informative action (<s>vijñapti</s>), how many of non-informative action (<s>avijñapti</s>), and how many of both natures?

body.text: tatrākuśalānāṃ tāvat-
body.translated_text: There, first regarding the unwholesome ones —

body.text: kāritāḥ ṣaḍavijñaptirdvyātmaikaste 'pi ṣaṭ kṛtāḥ /
body.translated_text: When instigated [by another], six are non-informative; one is of dual nature; those same six, when performed [oneself], are [also of dual nature]. (Abhidh-d 190)

body.text: tatra prāṇātipātādattādānamṛṣāvādapaiśūnyapāruṣyasaṃbhinnapralāpāḥ | ete nāvaśyaṃ vijñaptisvabhāvāḥ | pareṇa kārayato maulīvijñaptyabhāvāt | kāmamithyācārastu nityaṃ dvyātmakaḥ, tasya pareṇāśakyatvāt | te 'pi 'ṣaṭ kṛtāḥ'; yadā svayameva prāṇātipātādīn ṣaṭ karmapathān karoti tadā dvyātmāno bhavanti | vijñaptyavijñaptisvabhāvatvāt |
body.translated_text: There, killing (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>), taking what is not given (<s>adattādāna</s>), false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>), divisive speech (<s>paiśūnya</s>), harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>), and idle chatter (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>) — these are not necessarily of informative-action nature, because when one has another person carry [them] out, there is no principal informative action [on the instigator's part]. But sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>) is always of dual nature, because it cannot be done by another. Those same 'six, when performed [oneself]' — when one personally performs the six courses of action beginning with killing, then they are of dual nature, because they are of both informative and non-informative nature.

body.text: kuśalānāṃ punaḥ
body.translated_text: Regarding the wholesome ones, moreover —

body.text: śubhāḥ sapta dvidhā jñeyā ekadhaite samāhitāḥ // Abhidh-d_190 //
body.translated_text: The seven meritorious [paths] should be known as twofold; those [arising] from concentration are of one nature. (Abhidh-d 190)

body.text: sapta khalu rūpiṇaḥ kuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ dvidhā bhavanti | vijñaptyadhīnatvāt samāhitaśīlasya | dhyānānāsravasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītāstvavijñaptisvabhāvā eva | samāhitasya vijñaptyabhāvāt |
body.translated_text: Indeed, the seven wholesome courses of action that are material (<s>rūpin</s>) are twofold, because of depending on informative action for one in the state of concentration-morality (<s>samāhitaśīla</s>). But those included in the restraint of <s>dhyāna</s> and the outflow-free [path] are of non-informative nature alone, because there is no informative action for one in concentration.

body.text: yā sāmanteṣvavijñaptiḥ pṛṣṭheṣu tu viparyayaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the preparatory [stages] there is non-informative action; but in the subsequent [stages] it is the reverse.

body.text: sāmantakaḥ khalu yadā tīvreṇa paryavasthānena prayogamārabhate, prasādena vā ghanarasena tadā dvisvabhāvā | yadā mṛdunā tadā vijñaptireva | viparyayeṇa tu pṛṣṭheṣvavaśyamavijñaptiḥ | yadi punaḥ karmapathaṃ kṛtvā punastatravānuceṣṭate syādvijñaptirapīti | tīvreṇa tu prahāreṇa jīvitādvyaparopayati | tatra yā vijñaptistatkṣaṇikā cāvijñaptiḥ sa maulaḥ karmapathaḥ | dvābhyāṃ hi kāraṇābhyāṃ prāṇātipātāvadyena spṛśyate | prayogataḥ phalaparipūritaśca | tata ūrdhvamavijñaptikṣaṇāḥ pṛṣṭhībhavanti | yāvaddhataṃ paśuṃ kṛṣṇāti śodhayati vikrīṇāti pacati khādati kīrtayati | yadi tāvadasya vijñaptikṣaṇā api pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavanti | evamanyeṣvapi yathāsaṃbhavaṃ yojyam |
body.translated_text: In the preparatory stage (<s>sāmantaka</s>), indeed, when one undertakes the preliminary action with intense mental affliction (<s>paryavasthāna</s>), or with deep faith (<s>prasāda</s>), then they are of dual nature. When with mild [intensity], then it is informative action alone. In the subsequent stages (<s>pṛṣṭha</s>), conversely, there is necessarily non-informative action. But if, after completing a course of action, one again engages in related activity, there may also be informative action. However, when one deprives [another] of life with an intense blow — the informative action at that moment, together with the non-informative action of that instant, constitutes the principal course of action (<s>maula karmapathaḥ</s>). For one is touched by the offense of killing for two reasons: through the preparatory action, and through the completion of the result. From that [moment] onward, the moments of non-informative action become 'subsequent' [stages] — as long as one drags away the slain animal, cleans it, sells it, cooks it, eats it, or boasts about it. If indeed those moments of informative action also constitute the subsequent stage — thus, in other [courses of action] also, this should be applied as appropriate.

body.text: abhidhyādīnāṃ nāsti prayogo na pṛṣṭhaṃ saṃmukhībhāvamātrādeva karmapathāḥ |
body.translated_text: For covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) and the rest, there is no preparatory stage and no subsequent stage — they become courses of action merely from [their] coming face-to-face [with their object].

body.text: sūtre bhagavatoktam- "prāṇātipāto bhikṣavastrividhaḥ | lobhajo dveṣaja mohajaḥ, yāvanmithyādṛṣṭiḥ" iti | tatraiṣāṃ karmapathānāṃ keṣāñcillobhena niṣṭhā, keṣāñcid dveṣeṇa, keṣāñcinmohena | sarveṣāmapi
body.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s>, the Blessed One said: 'Killing, O monks, is threefold: born of greed, born of hatred, born of delusion — and so on up to wrong view.' Therein, of these courses of action, some are completed by greed, some by hatred, and some by delusion. But for all of them —

children.translated_text: the preparatory action arises from three roots.

body.text: prayogasteṣāmakuśalamūlatrayājjātaḥ | tatra lobhajaḥ prāṇātipātastaccharīrāvayavārthaṃ mṛgalubdhānāmaurabhrikamātsikaśākuntakādīnāṃ ca | dveṣajo yathā vairaniryātanārtham | mohajo yājñikānāṃ dharmabuddhyā rājñāṃ ca dharmapāṭhakaprāmāṇyāddhiṃsatām | pārasīkādīnāṃ ca dharmabuddhyā mātaraṃ pitaramabhighnatām |
body.translated_text: The preparatory action of those [courses of action] is born from the three unwholesome roots. There, killing born of greed [occurs] for the sake of body-parts [of the victim], as with deer-hunters, sheep-butchers, fishermen, bird-catchers, and the like. [Killing] born of hatred is for the purpose of revenge. [Killing] born of delusion [occurs] for sacrificers who kill with the notion of dharma, and for kings who kill on the authority of dharma-reciters, and for Persians and the like who strike their mother and father with the notion of dharma.

body.text: lobhajamadattādānaṃ yastenārthī taddharati | dveṣajaṃ vairaniryātanārtham | mohajaṃ yathā rājñāṃ dharmapāṭhakaprāmāṇyād dṛṣṭanigrahārtham | yathā ca duṣṭabrāhmaṇā āhuḥ- "sarvamidaṃ prajāpatinā brāhmaṇebhyo dattaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ daurbalyādvṛṣalāḥ paribhuñjante | tasmādapaharan brāhmaṇaḥ svamādatte svameva tu koṣṭhaṃ vaste svaṃ dadāti" iti |
body.translated_text: Taking what is not given born of greed — one who desires [the object] takes it. [That] born of hatred — for the purpose of revenge. [That] born of delusion — as when kings [confiscate] for the purpose of punishing the guilty, on the authority of dharma-reciters. And as wicked brahmins say: 'All this was given by <s>Prajāpati</s> to brahmins; through the weakness of brahmins, the low-born enjoy it. Therefore, a brahmin who takes [it back] is taking his own; he merely fills his own granary; he gives his own.'

body.text: lobhajaḥ kāmamithyācāraḥ paradārādiṣu tatsaṃrāgādabrahmacaryam | dveṣajo vairaniryātanārtham | mohajo yathā pārasīkānāṃ mātrādigamanam | gosave ca yajñe "upahā uadakaṃ cūṣayati, tṛṇāni cchinatti, upaiti mātaramupasvasāramupasagotrāmiti |"
body.translated_text: Sexual misconduct born of greed — unchaste conduct with others' wives and the like, due to passion for them. [That] born of hatred — for the purpose of revenge. [That] born of delusion — as with the Persians' intercourse with their mothers and the like. And in the cow-sacrifice (<s>gosava</s>): 'He sips water like a bull, cuts grass, approaches his mother, approaches his sister, approaches a woman of his clan.'

body.text: mṛṣāvādādayo lobhajā dveṣajāśca yathā pūrvamuktam | mohajo mṛṣāvādo yathāha-
body.translated_text: False speech and the rest born of greed and born of hatred are as previously stated. False speech born of delusion — as it is said:

body.text:
"na narmayuktamanṛtaṃ hinasti
na strīṣu rājanna vivāhakāle |
body.translated_text: 'A lie spoken in jest does not harm; nor [one spoken] regarding women, at weddings, O king;

body.text:
prāṇātyaye sarvadhanāpahāre
pañcānṛtānyāhurapātakāni ||" iti |
body.translated_text: nor [one spoken] when life is at stake, or when all wealth is being seized — these five lies, they say, are not sins.'

body.text: paiśūnyādayastu mithyādṛṣṭipravartitā mohajā yaśca vedādyasacchāstrapralāpaḥ |
body.translated_text: But divisive speech and the rest, when motivated by wrong view, are born of delusion — as is the idle prattle of the <s>Vedas</s> and other false treatises.

body.text: abhidhyādyāstrimūlajāḥ // Abhidh-d_191 //
body.translated_text: Covetousness and the rest are born of three roots. (Abhidh-d 191)

body.text: abhidhyādayastu lobhādanantarasaṃbhūtatvāt trimūlajāḥ |
body.translated_text: Covetousness and the rest, because of arising immediately after greed [and the other roots], are born of the three roots.

body.text: uktāḥ akuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ |
body.translated_text: The unwholesome courses of action have been stated.

body.text: kuśalāḥ prayogapṛṣṭhāśca kuśalatrayamūlajāḥ /
body.translated_text: The wholesome [courses], including preparatory and subsequent [stages], are born of the three wholesome roots.

body.text: kuśalānāṃ tu prayogaḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ ca trimūlottham | teṣāṃ kuśalacittasamutthitatvāt, tatra ca tadbhāvāt |
body.translated_text: The preparatory and subsequent [stages] of the wholesome ones are born of the three roots, because they arise from wholesome mind, and because those [three roots] exist therein.

body.text: kena punareṣāṃ karmapathānāṃ samāptirbhavati ? tadidamapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: By what, then, is the completion of these courses of action [determined]? That is now indicated:

body.text: dveṣeṇa vadhapāruṣyavyāpattīnāṃ samāpanam // Abhidh-d_192 //
body.translated_text: By hatred is the completion of killing, harsh speech, and malice. (Abhidh-d 192)

body.text: prāṇātipātapāruṣyavyāpādānāṃ khalu dveṣeṇa niṣṭhā bhavati | parityāgaparuṣacittasaṃmukhībhāvāt ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, the completion of killing, harsh speech, and malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>) occurs through hatred — because of the coming-face-to-face of a mind that is abandoning [compassion] and is harsh.

body.text: steyasyānyāṅganāyāterabhidhyāyāśca lobhataḥ /
body.translated_text: Of theft, adultery, and covetousness — through greed.

body.text: adattādānaparastrīgamanābhidhyānāṃ lobhena niṣṭhā |
body.translated_text: The completion of taking what is not given, going to another's wife, and covetousness is through greed.

children.translated_text: But of wrong view — through delusion.

body.text: mithyādṛṣṭeḥ khalu mohena samāptirbhavati | adhimātramūḍhābhihitāṃ niṣṭhāpayati |
body.translated_text: Indeed, the completion of wrong view occurs through delusion — one who is greatly deluded brings it to its final form.

body.text: tadanyeṣāṃ tribhirmatam // Abhidh-d_193 //
body.translated_text: Of the rest — through [all] three, it is held. (Abhidh-d 193)

body.text: ke punaranye ? mṛṣāvādapaiśunyasaṃbhinnapralāpāḥ | teṣāṃ tribhirapi niṣṭhā lobhena dveṣeṇa mohena vā ||
body.translated_text: What then are the rest? False speech, divisive speech, and idle chatter. Their completion is through all three — through greed, hatred, or delusion.

body.text: athaiṣāṃ caturṇāṃ kāṇḍānāṃ kimadhiṣṭhānam ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now, what is the basis (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of these four groups? That is stated:

children.translated_text: The basis of each of the four [groups] should be known respectively —

children.text: prāṇinaścātha bhogāśca nāmarūpaṃ ca nāma ca // Abhidh-d_194 //
children.translated_text: living beings, possessions, name-and-form, and names. (Abhidh-d 194)

body.text: tatra sattvādhiṣṭhānā vadhādayaḥ | bhogādhiṣṭhānāḥ parastrīgamanādayaḥ | nāmarūpādhiṣṭhānā mithyādṛṣṭiḥ | nāmakāyādhiṣṭhānā mṛṣāvādādayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: There, killing and the rest have living beings as their basis. Going to another's wife and the rest have possessions as their basis. Wrong view has name-and-form as its basis. False speech and the rest have the name-body (<s>nāmakāya</s>) as their basis.

body.text: kathaṃ punaḥ prāṇātipātaṃ svayaṃ kurvataḥ karmapatho bhavati kathaṃ yāvanmithyādṛṣṭiriti ? lakṣaṇaṃ karmapathānāṃ vaktavyam | tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: How then does a course of action come about for one who personally commits killing, and how [does it come about] up to wrong view? The definition of the courses of action must be stated. That is now commenced:

body.text: prāṇātipāto dhīpūrvamabhrāntyā paramāraṇam /
body.translated_text: Killing is the slaying of another, preceded by intention, without error.

body.text: yadi khalu haniṣyāmi hanmyenamiti saṃcintyābhrāntacittaḥ paraṃ jīvitādvyaparopayati, (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 157)

children.text: ) evaṃ prāṇātipāto bhavati | prāṇo vā vāyuḥ kāyacittāśrito vartate | tamatipātayatīti prāṇātipātaḥ |
children.translated_text: thus killing comes about. Or, <s>prāṇa</s> (breath/life-force) is the wind that abides dependent on body and mind. One who causes it to 'fall beyond' (<s>atipātayati</s>) — that is <s>prāṇātipāta</s> (killing).

body.translated_text: If indeed, having deliberately thought 'I shall kill him, I am killing him,' one with unerring mind deprives another of life,

body.text: na, anupapatteḥ | vināśānuṣaktā khalu saṃskārāḥ pratikṣaṇavinaśvarāścābhyupagamyante | teṣāmitthaṃbhūtānāṃ sthitiśaktikriyābhāve satyanāgatānāṃ ca tulyātulyajātīyānāṃ nirātmakatvāviśeṣe kena hantrā kimāpadyate ?
body.translated_text: No — because of impossibility. For conditioned formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are acknowledged as conjoined with destruction and as perishing every moment. For these being of such nature — in the absence of the power of duration and activity, and given the absence of any difference in selflessness between future [formations] whether of the same or different class — by what killer is what brought about?

body.text: atra sautrāntikāḥ parihāramāhuḥ- "na | pradīpanirvāpanaghaṇṭaśabdanirodhavattatsiddheḥ |"
body.translated_text: Here the <s>Sautrāntikas</s> offer a solution: 'No — because it is established [to be analogous] to the extinguishing of a lamp, the sound of a bell, and the cessation [of a series].'

body.text: na, samānatvāt | ayaṃ tvatra parihāraḥ- hanturhetusāmarthyopaghātakaraṇe satyanāgatasaṃskāraśaktikriyādhānavidhānavighnakaraṇāt prāṇātipātopapattiḥ | kasya punastajjīvitaṃ yastena viyojyate, te vā prāṇā iti ? prasiddhasya (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 158)

children.text: ) pudgalasya yo 'sāvevaṃ nāmaivaṃ gotra iti vistaraḥ |
children.translated_text: individual (<s>pudgala</s>) — one who is 'of such-and-such name, of such-and-such clan' — and so on in detail.

body.translated_text: No — because of being the same [problem]. But here the [correct] solution is this: When the killer's causal power inflicts damage, it obstructs the establishment and arrangement of the power and activity of future formations — therefore killing is tenable. But whose life is it from which one is separated, and what are those vital breaths? Of the well-known

body.text: abuddhipūrvādapi prāṇivadhātkarturadharmo bhavati yathāgnisparśāddāha iti nagnāṭāḥ | teṣāṃ paradāradarśanasparśane 'pyeṣa prasaṃgaḥ | tuṣṭaruṣṭanagnāṭavāhlīkanirgranthaśiroluñcane ca |
body.translated_text: Even from killing a living being without intention, demerit accrues to the agent — just as burning [results] from contact with fire — so [say] the naked ascetics (<s>nagnāṭa</s>). For them, the same absurd consequence [would apply] to merely seeing or touching another's wife. And also to the shaving of the head of a pleased or displeased naked ascetic, a <s>Vāhlīka</s>, or a <s>Nirgrantha</s>.

body.text: buddhipūrvātprāṇivadhāddharmo 'pi bhavatīti yājñikāḥ | katham viṣabhakṣaṇavat | tadyathā kiñcidviṣabhakṣaṇaṃ mantrapūrvaṃ hitāya bhavati | kiñcidahitāya yadamantrapūrvaṃ tadvaditi | na | galāmreḍanaśastranipātamantareṇa mantramātrakena paśuvadhasāmarthyādarśanāt | piṣṭamayacchāgā hutimātreṇa paśuvadhādiyajñadharmotpattyasāmarthyācca | kiñca, viṣasya māraṇajīvitaśaktidvayasāmarthyadarśanāt | tatra mantrapūrvakaṃ kiñcijjīvayati kiñciddurgatāriṣṭeṣu na jīvayati | amantrapūrvakamapi kiñcījjīvayati kiñcinna jīvayati | bhuktaviṣasyāpekṣikatvāt | kiñca, śabarādimantrāṇāṃ viṣamāraṇāśaktyupaghāte 'pi pāpapraṇāśanaśaktyadarśanāt | kiñca, hiṃsāhiṃsayordharmādharmasvālakṣaṇyāparityāgabhūtatvāt | juhotyādikriyāvyaṅgyo (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 160)

children.text: ) dharmaḥ iti cet | na | tadrūpāsiddhatvāt, abhivyaktyanupapatteśca | kriyāmātramapūrvamiti cet | na | kriyāyā nityatvānupapatterniruktyanupapatteśca ||
children.translated_text: no — because such a thing is not established, and because manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) is untenable. If [one says] 'the mere ritual activity is <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit)' — no — because the eternality of [ritual] activity is untenable, and because [its] etymology is untenable.

body.translated_text: From killing a living being with intention, merit also arises — so [say] the sacrificers (<s>yājñika</s>). How? Like the consumption of poison. Just as some consumption of poison, preceded by mantras, is beneficial, while some, without mantras, is harmful — so too [with killing], they say. No — because the efficacy of killing an animal by mantras alone, without cutting the throat or striking with a weapon, is not observed. And because the <s>yajña</s>-dharma cannot arise from killing an animal merely through an oblation of a dough-figurine goat. Moreover, because poison is observed to have both powers — of killing and of restoring life. In that case, some [poison] preceded by mantras restores life, and some in cases of dire calamity does not restore life. Even without mantras, some restores life and some does not — because the [effect of] consumed poison is relative. Moreover, because even when the mantras of <s>Śabaras</s> and the like destroy the killing-power of poison, the power to destroy sin is not observed. Moreover, because violence and non-violence, being dharma and adharma respectively, do not abandon their own intrinsic characteristics. If [one says] 'dharma is implied by the ritual activity of offering and the like' —

body.text: atyaktānyadhanādānamadattādānamucyate // Abhidh-d_195 //
body.translated_text: Taking the wealth of another that has not been relinquished is called taking what is not given (<s>adattādāna</s>). (Abhidh-d 195)

body.text: abhrāntyeti vartate | yadi balacauryabuddhyā paradravyaṃ svīkaroti ||
body.translated_text: 'Without error' still applies. When one appropriates another's property by force or stealth —

body.text: parastrīgamanaṃ kāmamithyācāro vikalpavān /
body.translated_text: Going to another's wife is sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>) — it has [many] varieties.

body.text: agamyagamanaṃ khalvapi kāmamithyācāraḥ | sa ca bahuprakāravikalpo bhavati | agamyāṃ gacchati mātaraṃ vā duhitaraṃ vā paraparigṛhītāṃ vā svāmapyanaṅge gacchatyadeśe ca | niyamasthāṃ vā | abhrāntyetyuktam |
body.translated_text: Going to one who should not be approached is indeed sexual misconduct. And it has many varieties of distinction: one goes to one's mother, or daughter, or one taken by another; or even to one's own [wife] in an improper orifice, or in an improper place; or to one observing a vow. 'Without error' was stated [as a condition].

body.text: arthajñāyānyathāvādo drohabuddhyā mṛṣāvacaḥ // Abhidh-d_196 //
body.translated_text: A statement contrary to what is known, with intent to deceive — that is false speech (<s>mṛṣāvacas</s>). (Abhidh-d 196)

body.text: vaktṛśrotṛbuddhyapekṣayā khalu mṛṣāvādo bhavati | yadi vaktārthānāmabhijño bhavati sa taṃ vigopya drohabuddhyānyathā brūte | śrotā ca tathaivāvagacchati | tadāsya mṛṣāvādaḥ kamapatho bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, false speech occurs with reference to the understanding of both speaker and listener. If the speaker is aware of the facts and, concealing them, speaks otherwise with intent to deceive, and the listener also understands accordingly — then his false speech constitutes a course of action.

body.text: ye khalvime māhakīmātṛsūtrā diṣvaṣṭāvanāryā vyavahārāḥ proktāḥ, aṣṭau cāryāḥ- "adṛṣṭe dṛṣṭavāditānāryo vyavahāraḥ | aśrute, amate, avijñāte, śrutamatavijñātavāditānāryo vyavahāraḥ | dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñāte cādṛṣṭādivāditānāryo vyavahāraḥ | viparyayeṇa tvaṣṭāvevāryā vyavahārāḥ |" teṣāṃ punaridaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vyākhyāyate-
body.translated_text: Now, those sixteen ignoble modes of conduct stated in the <s>Māhakī</s> and <s>Mātṛ</s> sūtras, and eight noble ones: 'Saying that one has seen what has not been seen is an ignoble mode of conduct. [Likewise with] what has not been heard, not been thought, not been cognized; and saying one has not seen, heard, thought, or cognized what has been seen, heard, thought, or cognized — that is an ignoble mode of conduct. The reverse constitutes the eight noble modes of conduct.' Now the definition of these is explained:

children.translated_text: What is grasped by sight, by hearing and the other [senses], by the mind —

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ mataṃ jñātamityuktaṃ tadyathākramam // Abhidh-d_197 //
children.translated_text: is called respectively the seen, the heard, the thought, and the known. (Abhidh-d 197)

body.text: yatkhalu cakṣuṣālocitaṃ cakṣurvijñānamanovijñānābhyāṃ cānubhūtaṃ taddṛṣṭamityucyate | yacchrotreṇa śrotramanovijñānābhyāṃ cānubhūtaṃ tacchrutam | yat tribhirghrāṇajihvākāyaistadvijñānamanovijñānaiścānubhūtaṃ tanmatamityucyate | teṣāṃ prāpyaviṣayagrāhitvāt, kabaḍiṃkārāhāraviṣayatvācca | tatreṣṭaparyāyavācī mataśabdaḥ | yatpunarmanovijñānenānubhūtaṃ tadvijñātaṃ tadadhyavasāye niścayaparisamāpteḥ |
body.translated_text: What is perceived by the eye-[faculty] and experienced through eye-consciousness and mental consciousness — that is called 'seen.' What is experienced through the ear, ear-consciousness, and mental consciousness — that is 'heard.' What is experienced through the three [faculties] — nose, tongue, and body — and their respective consciousnesses and mental consciousness — that is called 'thought' (<s>mata</s>), because those [faculties] apprehend objects through contact, and because they pertain to material nutriment (<s>kabaḍiṃkārāhāra</s>). In that context, the word <s>mata</s> is a synonym for 'desired' (<s>iṣṭa</s>). But what is experienced by mental consciousness alone — that is 'known' (<s>vijñāta</s>), because of the completion of ascertainment and determination.

body.text: gatametat | prakṛtamevānuvartatām ||
body.translated_text: This has been covered. Let the main topic be continued.

body.text: yaḥ kāyenānyathātvaṃ prāpayet, syānmṛṣāvādaḥ ? syāt | tadapadiśyate- syānna kāyena parākrameta prāṇātipātāvadyena ca spṛśyeta | syādvācā parākrameta syānna vācā parākrameta mṛṣāvādāvadyena ca spṛśyeta | syātkāyena parākrameta, syānna kāyena vācā parākrameta, ubhayāvadyena ca spṛśyeta | syādṛṣīṇāṃ manaḥpradoṣeṇa proṣadhanidarśanaṃ cātra iti |
body.translated_text: Could one who produces a change through the body be [guilty of] false speech? Yes. That is indicated: One may physically act and not be touched by the offense of false speech; or one may physically act and be touched by the offense of killing. One may act verbally; or one may not act verbally and yet be touched by the offense of false speech. One may act physically; or one may not act physically but act verbally, and be touched by the offense of both. There are also the examples of the <s>Ṛṣis</s> [communicating] through mental intent, and the <s>poṣadha</s> [ceremony] illustration applies here as well.

body.text: kathaṃ punarvijñaptyā vinā tatrāvijñaptiḥ kāmāvacarī karmapatho yokṣyate | sati hi cittaparispande mahābhūtatajjakāyaparispando 'vaśyaṃ bhāvīti kartavyo 'tra yatnaḥ |
body.translated_text: But how, without informative action (<s>vijñapti</s>), can a non-informative action (<s>avijñapti</s>) belonging to the desire realm constitute a course of action (<s>karmapatha</s>) there? For when there is a mental impulse, a movement of the great elements and the body born from them must necessarily follow — effort must be made here.

body.text: ukto mṛṣāvādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: False speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>) has been explained.

children.translated_text: Slander (<s>paiśunya</s>) is speech that causes division —

body.text: yatkhalu kliṣṭacittasya parabhedāya vacanamabhrāntyā tatpaiśunyamityucyate |
body.translated_text: whatever speech by one with a defiled mind, without error [of identification], aimed at dividing others — that is called slander (<s>paiśunya</s>).

body.text: pāruṣyaṃ tu yadapriyam /
body.translated_text: Harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>), however, is what is unpleasant —

body.text: abhrāntyā kliṣṭacittasya yadvacanaṃ tatpārūṣyamiti |
body.translated_text: whatever speech by one with a defiled mind, without error — that is harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>).

body.text: kliṣṭaṃ saṃbhinnalāpitvamanye gītakathādivat // Abhidh-d_198 //
body.translated_text: Defiled [speech constituting] idle chatter (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpitva</s>) — others [say it is] like singing, storytelling, and the like. (Abhidh-d 198)

body.text: kliṣṭaṃ khalu sarvaṃ vacanaṃ saṃbhinnapralāpitvam | yasya guṇasya bhāvād dravye śabdaniveśastabhidhāne tvatalau | kaścāsau guṇaḥ ? saṃbhinnapralāpa eva | sa yasyāsti sa saṃbhinnapralāpī | tadbhāvaḥ saṃbhinnapralāpitvam |
body.translated_text: Indeed, all defiled speech is idle chatter (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpitva</s>). The quality by whose presence the term (<s>śabda</s>) is applied to the substance — in the designation, with the suffixes '<s>ta</s>' and '<s>tva</s>' — and what is that quality? Idle chatter itself. One who possesses it is an idle chatterer. Its state is 'idle-chatter-ness.'

body.text: anye punarbruvate | yadetanmṛṣāvādāditribidhaṃ vacanaṃ tato yadanyatkliṣṭaṃ lapanagītanāṭyatīrthaśāstrādi tatsarvaṃ sabhinnapralāpaḥ ||
body.translated_text: But others say: whatever defiled talk other than the threefold speech of false speech and so forth — conversation, singing, drama, heretical treatises, and the like — all that is idle chatter.

children.translated_text: Covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) is craving for another's [possessions]; malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>) has sentient beings as its object —
arising from hatred; and wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) denies causes. (Abhidh-d 199)

body.text: abhidhyā tāvad dviṣataḥ spṛhā | aho bata yatpareṣāṃ tanmama syādityeṣā viṣayaprārthanā viṣamalobhākhyā abhidhyetyucyate |
body.translated_text: Covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) is, first, the craving of one who dislikes [one's own condition]: 'Oh, if only what belongs to others were mine!' — this desire for objects, called 'crooked greed' (<s>viṣamalobha</s>), is called covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>).

body.text: vyāpādaḥ khalvapi sattvaparityāgabudhyā pratighaḥ |
body.translated_text: Malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>) is indeed hostility (<s>pratigha</s>) with the intention of abandoning [the welfare of] sentient beings.

body.text: mithyādṛṣṭirapi hetuṃ vā phalaṃ vā kriyāṃ vā sadvā vastu nāśayataḥ yā dṛṣṭirmatirityevamādi sā mithyādṛṣṭirityucyate |
body.translated_text: Wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) is that view, opinion, and so forth, of one who denies cause, or fruit, or action, or a real entity — that is called wrong view.

body.text: tayā punarmithyādṛṣṭyā prakarṣaprāptayā navaprakārayā navaprakārāṇi kuśalamūlāni samucchidyante | bhāvanāheyakleśaprahāṇavat |
body.translated_text: By that wrong view, when it reaches its most intense degree, in nine modes, the nine kinds of wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) are cut off — like the abandonment of afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāheya</s>).

body.text: yattarhi śāstra uktam- "katamānyadhimātrāṇyakuśalamūlāni yairakuśalamūlaiḥ kuśalamūlāni samucchinatti ? kāmavairāgyaṃ cānuprāpnuvan yāni tatprathamata upalikhati ?" naiṣa doṣaḥ | akuśalamūlādhyāhṛtatvāt | mithyādṛṣṭesteṣveva tatkarmopacaryate | tadyathāgnireva grāmasya dagdhā caurāstu tasyādhyāhārakāstadvaditi |
body.translated_text: As for what is stated in the treatise: 'What are those exceedingly intense unwholesome roots by which one cuts off the wholesome roots? And those that one first outlines when approaching detachment from the desire realm?' — this is not a fault, because unwholesome roots are to be supplied [in the reading]. The action [of cutting off] is attributed to wrong view in relation to those very [unwholesome roots]. Just as fire alone is the burner of a village, but thieves are its suppliers — likewise.

body.text: kāmāvacarāṇyupapattilambhikānyeva ca samucchidyante, prāyogikebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ parihīṇatvāt |
body.translated_text: It is only the desire-realm birth-obtained [wholesome roots] that are cut off, since the practice-obtained ones have already declined before that.

body.text: evaṃ hyūktaṃ bhagavatā- "samanvāgato 'yaṃ puruṣaḥ kuśalairapi dharmairakuśalairapi dharmaiḥ" iti vistaraḥ | tatra samanvāgato 'yaṃ pudgalaḥ kuśalairapi dharmairaviśeṣeṇa dvividhaiḥ- prāyogikairupapattilābhikaiśca | te 'sya pudgalasya kuśalā dharmā antardhāsyanti, prāyogikāḥ anupūrvasamucchede, pūrvaṃ tadvihāneḥ | asti cāsya kuśalamūlamanusahagatamanupacchinnamupapattilābhikam | tadapyapareṇa samayena

children.translated_text: (Jaini 167)

children.text: ) sarveṇa sarvaṃ samucchetsyate | yasya samucchedātsamucchinnakuśalamūla iti saṃkhyāṃ gamiṣyatīti | ataḥ sarvākuśalamūlabhūtā mithyādṛṣṭiriti saugatāḥ |
children.translated_text: will be entirely, completely cut off. From whose cutting off, he will come to be reckoned as 'one whose wholesome roots are cut off.' Therefore, wrong view is the root of all that is unwholesome — so say the <s>Saugatās</s> (Buddhists).

body.translated_text: For thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'This person is endowed with both wholesome <s>dharmas</s> and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>' — and so forth in detail. Therein, this individual is endowed with wholesome <s>dharmas</s> without distinction, of two kinds — practice-obtained and birth-obtained. Those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> of this individual will disappear — the practice-obtained ones in the gradual cutting off, because of their prior decline. And there exists for him a wholesome root, accompanied by mental [activity], uncut, birth-obtained. That too, at a later time,

body.text: "sūkṣmaṃ kuśaladharmabījaṃ tasminnakuśale cetasyavasthitaṃ yataḥ punaḥ pratyayasāmagrīsannidhāne sati kuśalaṃ cittamutpadyate" iti kośakāraḥ |
body.translated_text: 'A subtle seed of wholesome <s>dharma</s> remains established in that unwholesome consciousness, from which, when the assemblage of conditions is present, a wholesome consciousness arises' — so says the author of the <s>Kośa</s>.

body.text: yuktyāgamavirodhāttanneti dīpakāraḥ |
body.translated_text: 'That is not so, because of contradiction with reasoning and scripture' — says the author of the <s>Dīpa</s>.

body.text: tatra yuktivirodhastāvadvijātīyāddhetorvijātīya phalānutpattidarśanādyavabījācchāliphalavadyoniśo manasikāraparataḥ sadghoṣābhyāṃ mithyādṛṣṭivacca | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 170)

children.text: ) cakṣūrūpābhyāṃ vijñānavaditi cet | na | sabhāgahetau sati cakṣūrūpayornimittakāraṇamātratvāt, dadhyutpattāvātañcanavat | kiñca, viruddhānāmanyataropapatteśca | na hi viruddhānāṃ sukhaduḥkhālokatamaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ caikatra saṃbhavadavasthānaṃ dṛṣṭam | nāpi parasparaṃ bījaphalābhisaṃbandhaḥ | kiñca, cittabījaikatvābhyupagamācca | akuśalameva hi cittaṃ bhavatāṃ bījamiṣṭam | tasya kuśale cittakṣaṇe viruddhakriye ca cittāntare bījaleśānupapattiḥ | (
children.translated_text: Objection: Like consciousness from eye and form [taken together]. Reply: No — because when the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>) exists, eye and form are merely instrumental causes (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>), like a sour agent in the production of curd. Moreover, because of the arising of one of two contradictories. For the simultaneous existence and persistence of contradictories — pleasure and pain, light and darkness, and so forth — is not seen in one [locus]. Nor is there a seed-fruit relationship between mutual contraries. Moreover, because of accepting the unity of consciousness and seed. For it is indeed unwholesome consciousness alone that you accept as the seed. In a wholesome moment of consciousness, and in another moment of consciousness of contradictory activity, the impossibility of even a trace of seed [is clear].
(Jaini 171)
And because this has been answered in detail. For the answer to this has been stated at length here. Let it be remembered.

body.translated_text: Therein, the contradiction with reasoning is first: because a result of a different kind is not seen to arise from a cause of a different kind — like a rice-fruit from a barley-seed; and from thorough attention (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>), [even when] dependent on another, from a good proclamation, and like wrong view itself.

body.text: āgamavirodho 'pi, "sarvaṃ sarveṇa cchetsya te" iti ...........cyamānaṃ bījamavasthitaṃ gaṃsyate | iti |
body.translated_text: The contradiction with scripture too: 'will cut off entirely, completely' — ........... the seed that is being [cut will] remain established. Thus.

body.text: vyākhyātāḥ salakṣaṇāḥ karmapathāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The courses of action (<s>karmapatha</s>), together with their characteristics, have been explained.

body.text: kaḥ punaḥ salakṣaṇaḥ karmapathārthaḥ ? karma ca karmaṇaśca cetanākhyasya panthāna iti karmapathāḥ | tatra sapta karma ca karmaṇaśca panthā iti karmapathāḥ, trayastvabhidhyādayaḥ karmaṇaḥ panthāno na karma | cetanā hi tat saṃprayogiṇī bhavati | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 172)

children.text: ) saṃprayuktātadvaśenagacchatyabhisaṃskarotītyarthaḥ | sā tu karmaiva na karmapathaḥ | na hyasau trayāṇāṃ vaśena vartate | idamucyate-
children.translated_text: Because [volition], being associated, proceeds under their influence and constructs [results] — this is the meaning. But that [volition] is <s>karma</s> itself, not a course of action (<s>karmapatha</s>). For it does not operate under the influence of those three. This is stated:

body.translated_text: What then is the meaning of 'course of action' (<s>karmapatha</s>), together with its characteristics? <s>Karma</s> (action) and the paths (<s>pantha</s>) of that <s>karma</s> called volition (<s>cetanā</s>) — these are 'courses of action.' Therein, the seven are both action and the path of action — hence 'courses of action.' But the three beginning with covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) are paths of action, not action [itself]. For the volition associated with them exists.

body.text: cetanā na kriyāmārgastaistu sattā pravartate /
body.translated_text: Volition (<s>cetanā</s>) is not a course of action; but an [unwholesome] being operates through those [three mental paths].

body.text: katibhiḥ punaḥ karmapathaiḥ sārdhaṃ cetanā yugapadutpannā vartate ? tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: With how many courses of action does volition (<s>cetanā</s>) simultaneously arise and operate? This is now commenced:

body.text: yugapadyāvadaṣṭābhiraśubhaiścetanaiḥ saha // Abhidh-d_200 //
body.translated_text: Simultaneously, with up to eight unwholesome [courses of action], together with the volitions. (Abhidh-d 200)

body.text: ekena tāvatsaha vartate | vinānyenābhidhyādisaṃmukhībhāve akliṣṭacetaso vā tatprayogeṇa rūpiṇāmanyatamaniṣṭhāgamane |
body.translated_text: With one, first, it operates together — when, apart from any [other course], covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) and the like are faced; or when, for one with undefiled mind, through the effort [of another], one of the material [courses of action] reaches completion.

body.text: dvābhyāṃ saha vartate | vyāpannacittasya prāṇivadye | abhidhyāviṣṭasya cādattādāne kāmamithyācāre saṃbhinnapralāpe vā |
body.translated_text: With two it operates together — in the killing of a living being by one with a malicious mind; or in stealing, sexual misconduct, or idle chatter by one possessed by covetousness.

body.text: tribhiḥ saha | vyāpannacittasya parakīyaprāṇimāraṇāpaharaṇe yugapat | abhidhyāviṣṭasya tatprayogeṇa rūpidvayaniṣṭhāgamane tribhireva |
body.translated_text: With three together — simultaneously in the killing and stealing of another's creature by one with a malicious mind; or for one possessed by covetousness, through his effort, when two material [courses] reach completion — with exactly three.

body.text: caturbhiḥ saha vartate | bhedābhiprāyasya nandanavacane paruṣavacane vā | tatra hi mānasa eko bhavati vācikāstrayaḥ | abhidhyādigatasya vā tatprayoge 'nyatrayaniṣṭhāgamane |
body.translated_text: With four it operates together — in the joyful speech or harsh speech of one intending to cause division. For therein, one is mental and three are vocal. Or for one engaged in covetousness and the like, through his effort, when any three [courses] reach completion.

body.text: evaṃ pañcaṣaṭsaptabhiryojyam |
body.translated_text: Similarly, with five, six, and seven should be applied.

body.text: aṣṭābhiḥ saha vartate | ṣaṭsu prayogaṃ kṛtvā pare saṃpreṣaṇena svayaṃ kāmamithyācāraṃ kurvataḥ samaniṣṭhāgamane | evaṃ tāvadakuśalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: With eight it operates together — when one who has set in motion the effort for six [courses], while personally committing sexual misconduct through the dispatching of another, and [all] reach completion simultaneously. Thus is the unwholesome [explained].

body.text: śubhaistu daśabhiryāvatsārdhaṃ naikāṣṭapañcabhiḥ /
body.translated_text: But with wholesome [courses], up to ten together, but not with one, eight, or five.

body.text: śubhaiḥ khalu karmapathairyāvaddaśabhiḥ saha vartata ityutsṛṣṭiḥ | tadapavādoyam- 'naikāṣṭapañcabhiḥ'; | na khalvekena pañcabhiraṣṭābhirvā saha vartate |
body.translated_text: With wholesome courses of action, up to ten together [volition] operates — this is the general rule. The exception is: 'not with one, eight, or five.' It does not operate together with one, five, or eight.

body.text: tatra dvābhyāṃ saha vartate | kuśaleṣu pañcasu vijñāneṣu sthitasyārūpyasamāpattisaṃgṛhīte ca kṣayānutpādajñānasaṃprayuktāvijñānaṃ tatsaṃprayuktā ca prajñānadṛṣṭiriti |
body.translated_text: With two it operates together — for one established in the five wholesome consciousnesses, and in [a consciousness] included in a formless-realm attainment, the non-informative action associated with the knowledge of exhaustion (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>), and the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) that is not a 'view' associated with it.

body.text: tribhiḥ saha vartate | samyagdṛṣṭisaṃprayukte manovijñāne | yatra saṃvaro nāsti |
body.translated_text: With three together — in a mental consciousness associated with right view, where there is no restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>).

body.text: caturbhirakuśalāvyākṛtacittasyopāsakasya śrāmaṇerasaṃvarasamādāne |
body.translated_text: With four — for a lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>) or novice (<s>śrāmaṇera</s>) with unwholesome or indeterminate consciousness, at the undertaking of restraint.

body.text: ṣaḍbhiḥ kuśaleṣu pañcasu vijñāneṣu tatsamādāne |
body.translated_text: With six — in the five wholesome consciousnesses at the undertaking of that [restraint].

body.text: saptabhiḥ kuśale manovijñāne tatsamādāna eva | akuśalāvyākṛtacittasya ca bhikṣusaṃvarasamādāne |
body.translated_text: With seven — in wholesome mental consciousness at the very undertaking of that [restraint]; and for one with unwholesome or indeterminate consciousness at the undertaking of full monastic restraint (<s>bhikṣusaṃvara</s>).

body.text: navabhiḥ kuśaleṣu pañcasu vijñāneṣu tatsamādāne, kṣayānutpādajñānasaṃprayukte ca manovijñāne tasminneva ca dhyānasaṃgṛhīte |
body.translated_text: With nine — in the five wholesome consciousnesses at the undertaking of that [restraint], and in a mental consciousness associated with the knowledge of exhaustion and non-arising, which is included in that very <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: daśabhistato 'nyatra kuśale manovijñāne bhikṣusaṃvarasamādāna eva | sarvā ca dhyānānāsravasaṃvarasamāvartinī cetanānyatra kṣayānutpādajñānābhyām | saṃvaranirmuktena tvekenāpi saha syādanyacittasyaikāṅgaviratisamādāne | pañcāṣṭābhirapi syāt | kuśalamanovijñānasya dvipañcāṅgasamādāne yugapat |
body.translated_text: With ten — in a wholesome mental consciousness other than [that associated with] the knowledge of exhaustion and non-arising, at the very undertaking of full monastic restraint. And every volition that operates within <s>dhyāna</s> and undefiled restraint, other than the knowledge of exhaustion and non-arising. But with one also it could [operate] — for one with a different [type of] consciousness at the undertaking of a single-limbed abstinence, free from [full] restraint. With five and eight too it could [operate] — for a wholesome mental consciousness at the simultaneous undertaking of two-limbed or five-limbed [restraints].

body.text: kasyāṃ punargatau kati kuśalāścākuśalāśca karmapathāḥ saṃmukhībhāvataḥ samanvāgato vā santīti ?
body.translated_text: In which destiny (<s>gati</s>), how many wholesome and unwholesome courses of action exist, from the perspective of coming face-to-face or from the perspective of endowment (<s>samanvāgama</s>)?

body.text: vilāpadveṣapāruṣyāṇyuṣanti narake dvidhā // Abhidh-d_201 //
body.translated_text: Idle chatter, malice, and harsh speech exist in hell in both ways. (Abhidh-d 201)

body.text: ete trayaḥ saṃbhinnapralāpapārūṣyavyāpādā nārake saṃmukhībhāva taḥ samanvāgamataśca vidyante |
body.translated_text: These three — idle chatter (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>), harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>), and malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>) — exist for a hell-being both from the perspective of coming face-to-face and from the perspective of endowment.

body.text: tadvadeva matābhidhyā mithyādṛṣṭistathaiva ca /
body.translated_text: Likewise, covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) is held [to exist there]; and wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) similarly.

body.text: kecitkhalu bruvate- abhidhyā mithyādṛṣṭiścāpi dvābhyāṃ prakārābhyāṃ vidyete |
body.translated_text: Some indeed say: covetousness and wrong view too exist in both ways.

body.text: anye punarāhuḥ- samanvāgamata evābhidhyāmithyādṛṣṭī vidyete | rañjanīyavastvabhāvāt, karmaphalapratyakṣatvācca |
body.translated_text: But others say: covetousness and wrong view exist only from the perspective of endowment — because of the absence of delightful objects [in hell], and because of the directness of karmic fruits [there].

body.text: taccaitadakāraṇam | tatra tāvattṛṣṇāvidyādhimātratamatvāditi pūrvamapākṣikaḥ |
body.translated_text: But this is without reason. For to begin with, because craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) are exceedingly intense [there] — the earlier [view] of the opponent.

body.text: abhidhyāditrayaṃ tadvatkurau pralapanaṃ dvidhā // Abhidh-d_202 //
body.translated_text: The triad of covetousness and the like likewise [exists] in <s>Kuru</s>; idle chatter in both ways. (Abhidh-d 202)

body.text: kurau khalvevameva trayo 'bhidhyāvyāpādamithyādṛṣṭayaḥ |
body.translated_text: In <s>Kuru</s>, the three — covetousness, malice, and wrong view — [exist] in this same manner.

body.text: anye punarāhuḥ- samānvāgamata eva na saṃmukhībhāvataḥ amamāparigrahatvāt, snigdhasantānatvādāghātavastvabhāvādapāpāśayatvācca ||
body.translated_text: But others say: [in <s>Kuru</s>] only from the perspective of endowment, not from the perspective of coming face-to-face — because there is no concept of 'mine,' because the mental continuum is gentle, because of the absence of objects of aggression, and because of non-evil dispositions.

children.translated_text: But the ten unwholesome [courses of action exist] elsewhere [i.e., outside hell and Kuru] —

body.text: narakottarakurubhyāṃ kāmadhātau dvābhyāṃ prakārābhyāṃ daśāśubhā vidyante |
body.translated_text: apart from hell and <s>Uttarakuru</s>, in the desire realm, in the ten unwholesome [courses of action] exist in both ways.

body.text: sarvatra kuśalāstrayaḥ /
body.translated_text: The wholesome [courses of action] — three — everywhere.

body.text: śubhāstu 'trayaḥ'; | trayo 'nabhidhyāvyāpādasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ sarvatra traidhātuke pañcasvapi gatiṣu dvābhyāṃ prakārābhyāṃ santīti |
body.translated_text: But the wholesome are 'three' — the three of non-covetousness (<s>anabhidhyā</s>), non-malice (<s>avyāpāda</s>), and right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) exist everywhere, in all three realms and in all five destinies, in both ways.

body.text: ārūpyāryāsaṃjñināṃ ca rūpiṇaḥ sapta lābhataḥ // Abhidh-d_203 //
body.translated_text: For noble ones (<s>ārya</s>) in the formless realm and for unconscious beings (<s>asaṃjñin</s>), the seven material [courses exist] from [the perspective of] acquisition. (Abhidh-d 203)

body.text: ārūpyeṣu khalvāryāṇāmevātītānāgatenānāsravasaṃvareṇa samanvāgamo 'styasaṃjñināṃ ca | dhyānasaṃvareṇa yāvadbhūbhyāśrayaṃ hyanāsravaśīlamārya utpāditanirodhitaṃ kṛtvā ārūpyeṣūpapanno bhavati tenātītena samanvāgato bhavati | ṣaḍbhūbhyāśrayeṇānāgatenāpi, na tu saṃmukhībhāvataḥ, ārūpyāṇāṃ catuskandhātmakatvādasaṃjñisattvānāṃ cācittakatvāt | bhūtacittapratibaddho hi tatsaṃvarasaṃmukhībhāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the formless realms, noble ones (<s>ārya</s>) alone have endowment with past and future undefiled restraint; and unconscious beings (<s>asaṃjñin</s>) too [have endowment] with <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint. For however many levels of the undefiled morality a noble one has produced and ceased, having been reborn in the formless realms, he is endowed with that past [restraint]. And with undefiled [restraint] based on six levels as future [too] — but not from the perspective of coming face-to-face, because formless realms consist of four aggregates only, and because unconscious beings are without consciousness. For the coming face-to-face with that restraint depends on an actual consciousness.

body.text: kurūnsanarakānhitvā sarvatrānyatra te dvidhā /
body.translated_text: Excluding <s>Kuru</s> and the hells, in all other [destinies], those [seven] exist in both ways.

body.text: kurūn hitvā narakāṃśca | anyatra gatau saṃmukhībhāvato hyete sapta kuśalāḥ karmapathā vidyante | saṃvaranirmuktā eva tu tiryakpreteṣu | saṃvarasaṃgṛhītā eva rūpadhātāvanyatrobhayathā |
body.translated_text: Excluding <s>Kuru</s> and the hells — in other destinies, these seven wholesome courses of action exist from the perspective of coming face-to-face. But among animals and hungry ghosts, only those free from [full] restraint. Only those included in restraint in the form realm. In other [cases], in both ways.

body.text: te khalvete dvividhā karmapathāḥ
body.translated_text: These courses of action are indeed of two kinds —

body.text: sarve vipākaniṣyandādhipatyaphaladā daśa // Abhidh-d_204 //
body.translated_text: all ten give maturation-fruit (<s>vipāka</s>), outflow-fruit (<s>niṣyanda</s>), and dominant-fruit (<s>adhipatya</s>). (Abhidh-d 204)

body.text: tatrākuśalaiḥ sarvairāsevitairbhāvitairbahulīkṛtairnarakeṣūpapadyate tadeṣāṃ vipākaphalam | saceditthatvamāgacchati sa manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatām, prāṇātipātenālpāyuṣko bhavati | adattādānena bhogavyasanī | kāmamithyācāreṇa sapatnadāraḥ | mṛṣāvādenābhyākhyānabahulaḥ | paiśūnyenādṛḍhamitraḥ | pāruṣyeṇāmanojñaśabdaśrāvī | saṃbhinnapralāpenānādeyavākyaḥ | abhidhyayā tīvrarāgaḥ | vyāpādena tīvradveṣaḥ | mithyādṛṣṭyā tīvramohaḥ | itīdameṣāṃ niṣyandaphalam |
body.translated_text: Therein, through all unwholesome [courses], when cultivated, developed, and made much of, one is reborn in the hells — this is their maturation-fruit (<s>vipākaphala</s>). If one nonetheless attains [human birth], coming to human status: through killing (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>), one has a short life; through stealing (<s>adattādāna</s>), loss of wealth; through sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>), a rival spouse; through false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>), much false accusation; through slander (<s>paiśunya</s>), unsteady friends; through harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>), hearing unpleasant sounds; through idle chatter (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>), one's words are not heeded; through covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>), intense passion; through malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>), intense hatred; through wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), intense delusion. This is their outflow-fruit (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>).

body.text: prāṇātipātenātyāsevitena bāhyā bhāvā alpaujaskā bhavanti | adattādānena parīttaphalā alpasasyā aśanibahulāḥ | kāmamithyācāreṇa rajo 'vakīrṇāḥ | mṛṣāvādena durgandhāḥ | paiśūnyenotkūlanikūlāḥ | pāruṣyeṇa duḥsparśāḥ kaṇḍukaprāyāśca | saṃbhinnapralāpena viṣamapariṇāmāḥ | abhidhyayā pacitaphalāḥ | vyāpādena kaṭukarmaphalāḥ | mithyādṛṣṭyā bījādapakṛṣṭaphalā aphalā vā | idameṣāmādhipatyaphalam |
body.translated_text: Through frequently committed killing of living beings, external things become of diminished vitality. Through taking what is not given, [they become] of meager fruit, of scanty crops, and full of thunderbolts. Through sexual misconduct, [they become] covered with dust. Through false speech, [they become] foul-smelling. Through slander, [they become] uneven and hilly. Through harsh speech, [they become] rough to the touch and mostly thorny. Through idle chatter, [they are] of irregular maturation. Through covetousness, [they bear] cooked-over fruit. Through malice, [they bear] bitter and pungent fruit. Through wrong view, [they bear] fruit inferior to the seed, or no fruit. This is their dominant fruit (<s>ādhipatyaphala</s>).

body.text: tatpunaretat
body.translated_text: Furthermore, this [threefold analysis]:

children.translated_text: From the conjunction with suffering, [there is] suffering; from killing, short life;
from destruction of vitality, diminished vigor — this is the threefold fruit of that [karma]. (Abhidh-d 205)

body.text: yattena parasya duḥkhā vedanā janitā tatonarakeṣūpapadyate | yadiṣṭaṃ jīvitamupacchinnaṃ tato 'lpāyuḥ | yattejo nāśitaṃ tena bāhyā bhāvāḥ kṛśaujasaḥ | evamanyeṣāmapi yojyam |
body.translated_text: Because a painful feeling was produced in another by that [act], one is reborn in the hells. Because a cherished life was cut short, one has a short lifespan. Because vitality was destroyed, external things are of diminished vigor. In the same way, one should apply [this analysis] to the other [karma-paths] as well.

body.text: kuśalānāmapi karmapathānāmevameva tatphalatrayaṃ viparyayeṇa lakṣayitavyam | prāṇivadhaviratyā sevitayā deveṣūpapadyate | saceditthatvamāgacchati manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāṃ dīrghāyurbhavati | tadādhipatyenaiva bāhyā bhāvā mahojaso bhavantīti | sarvaṃ viparyayeṇa draṣṭavyam ||
body.translated_text: For wholesome karma-paths too, the threefold fruit should be discerned in the opposite way. Through the practice of abstention from killing living beings, one is reborn among the gods. If one attains human birth, one is long-lived in that class-homogeneity of humans. By the dominance of that very [abstention], external things become of great vitality. Everything should be understood in the opposite [way].

body.text: atra pūrvaṃ yāni pañca phalānyuktāni teṣāṃ kataratkarma katibhiḥ phalaiḥ saphalam ?
body.translated_text: Here, regarding the five fruits that were stated earlier, which <s>karma</s> is fruitful through how many fruits?

children.translated_text: On the unobstructed path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), <s>karma</s> bears fruit through five fruits;
but for the impure noble [path], through four — likewise for other wholesome and unwholesome [karmas]. (Abhidh-d 206)

body.text: prahāṇamārge samale pañcabhiḥ phalaiḥ karma saphalaṃ bhavati | tulyā adhikā api tasya paścādutpannāḥ sadaśā dharmā niṣyandaphalam | vipākaphalaṃ svabhūminiyato vipākaḥ | visaṃyogaphalaṃ yatkleśaprahāṇam | puruṣakāraphalaṃ ye tadbalasamutpannā dharmāḥ | na tathā sahabhuvaḥ | yaccānantarotpanno vimuktimārgaḥ, yaccānāgataṃ bhāvyate, yacca tatprahāṇaṃ tadbalena hi tatprāptyupattiḥ | adhipatiphalaṃ svabhāvādanye sarvasaṃskārāḥ pūrvotpanna varjjā iti draṣṭavyam | prahāṇamapi tanmārgasyādhipatiphalaṃ yujyate | tadādhipatyena tatsākṣātkaraṇādityanye | yattu nirmalaprahāṇamārge karma taccaturbhiḥ phalaiḥ saphalaṃ vipākaphalaṃ muktvā | 'tadvadanyacchubhāśubham |'; anyadapi sāsravaṃ yacchubhāśubham, yacca prahāṇamārgādanyatkuśalasāsravaṃ karmaṃ yaccākuśalaṃ tadapi caturbhireva phalaiḥ saphalaṃ visaṃyogaphalaṃ tyaktvā ||
body.translated_text: On the path of abandonment, <s>karma</s> that is impure bears fruit through five fruits. Its subsequently arisen <s>dharmas</s> of equal and superior [quality] are the outflow-fruit (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>). The maturation-fruit (<s>vipākaphala</s>) is the maturation determined by its own plane. The separation-fruit (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>) is the abandonment of defilements. The person-effort-fruit (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>) consists of <s>dharmas</s> that arose from its power. Not so for co-arisen [dharmas]. And the liberation-path that arose immediately after, and what is future that is to be cultivated, and the abandonment [of defilements] — for by that power the acquisition of that [abandonment] arises. The dominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>) should be seen as all conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) other than its own nature, excluding those that arose earlier. Abandonment too is rightly the dominant fruit of that path. [Some say:] because of the dominance of that [path], there is the direct realization of that — so say others. But for <s>karma</s> on the pure, stainless path of abandonment, it bears fruit through four fruits, excluding the maturation-fruit. 'Likewise for other wholesome and unwholesome [karmas]' — other with-outflow [karmas], whether wholesome or unwholesome, and wholesome with-outflow <s>karma</s> other than the path of abandonment, and unwholesome [karma] — these too bear fruit through exactly four fruits, excluding the separation-fruit.

body.text: tato 'nyannirmalaṃ jñeyaṃ tribhiravyākṛtaṃ tathā /
body.translated_text: Other than that, the pure [karma] should be known as [bearing] three [fruits]; likewise the indeterminate. (Abhidh-d 207)

body.text: śeṣaṃ punaranāsravaṃ yatprahāṇamārgādanyat, yaccāvyākṛtaṃ tattribhirvipākavisaṃyogaphalaṃ muktvā |
body.translated_text: The remaining outflow-free [karma] other than the path of abandonment, and the indeterminate [karma] — [these bear fruit through] three, excluding the maturation-fruit and the separation-fruit.

body.text: phalaṃ śubhasya catvāri dve trīṇi ca śubhādayaḥ // Abhidh-d_207 //
body.translated_text: The fruits of the wholesome are four; [those of] the unwholesome and the rest are two, three, and [more].

body.text: kuśalasya karmaṇaḥ kuśalā dharmāścatvāri phalāni vipākaphalaṃ hitvā | akuśalā dve puruṣakārādhipatiphale | avyākṛtāstrīṇi niṣyandavisaṃyogaphale hitvā ||
body.translated_text: Of wholesome <s>karma</s>, wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are four fruits, excluding the maturation-fruit. Unwholesome [dharmas are] two — the person-effort-fruit and the dominant fruit. Indeterminate [dharmas are] three, excluding the outflow-fruit and the separation-fruit.

body.text: śubhādyāstvaśubhasya dve trīṇi catvāri ca kramāt /
body.translated_text: Of the unwholesome [karma], the wholesome and the rest [are] two, three, and four, respectively.

body.text: akuśalasya karmaṇaḥ kuśalā dharmā dve puruṣakārādhipatiphale | akuśalāstrīṇi vipākavisaṃyogaphale hitvā | avyākṛtāścatvāri visaṃyogaphalaṃ hitvā | avyākṛtamapi hyakuśalānāṃ niṣyandaphalamasti | yathā kāmāvacare satkāyāntargrāhadṛṣṭī | sarveṣāṃ duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyānāṃ samudayadarśanaprahātavyānāṃ ca sarvatragānām |
body.translated_text: Of unwholesome <s>karma</s>, wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are two — the person-effort-fruit and the dominant fruit. Unwholesome [dharmas are] three, excluding the maturation-fruit and the separation-fruit. Indeterminate [dharmas are] four, excluding the separation-fruit. For the indeterminate can also be the outflow-fruit of unwholesome [karmas] — such as the views of the self-existent body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and extreme views (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>) in the desire realm; [these arise from] all the universally operative [defilements] to be abandoned by seeing suffering and seeing origination.

body.text: avyākṛtasya te tu dve trīṇi trīṇi śubhādayaḥ // Abhidh-d_208 //
body.translated_text: Of the indeterminate [karma], those [dharmas] are two, three, and three — the wholesome and the rest. (Abhidh-d 208)

body.text: avyākṛtasya karmaṇaḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ dve puruṣakārādhipatiphale | akuśalāstrīṇi visaṃyogaphale hitvā | avyākṛtasya tānyeva trīṇi ||
body.translated_text: Of indeterminate <s>karma</s>, wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are two — the person-effort-fruit and the dominant fruit. Unwholesome [dharmas are] three, excluding the separation-fruit. Of the indeterminate, [they are] those same three.

children.translated_text: For the past [karma], all [dharmas of all three times yield] four [fruits]; for the present, the same for the future;
the present [dharmas yield] two [to present karma]; and for the unborn [dharmas] of the unborn [karma], three. (Abhidh-d 209)

body.text: tatra 'sarve'; iti traikālikāḥ | atītasya karmaṇo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannā dharmāścatvāri phalāni visaṃyogamapāsya | pratyutpannasyāpi karmaṇo 'nāgatā dharmāścatvāri phalānyetānyeva | vartamānāstu dharmā vartamānasya karmaṇaḥ dve puruṣakārādhipatiphale | ajātasya tvajātā dharmāstrīṇi phalāni niṣyandavisaṃyogaphale hitvā ||
body.translated_text: 'All' refers to [dharmas] of all three times. Of past <s>karma</s>, past, future, and present <s>dharmas</s> [yield] four fruits, excluding the separation-fruit. Of present <s>karma</s> too, future <s>dharmas</s> [yield] these same four fruits. But present <s>dharmas</s> of present <s>karma</s> [yield] two — the person-effort-fruit and the dominant fruit. But unborn <s>dharmas</s> of unborn <s>karma</s> [yield] three fruits, excluding the outflow-fruit and the separation-fruit.

body.text: catvāryekabhuvo dve vā trīṇi cāparabhūmikāḥ /
body.translated_text: Of the same plane, four or two; of another plane, three.

body.text: svabhūmikā dharmāḥ karmaṇo yathāsaṃbhavaṃ catvāri phalāni visaṃyogaphalaṃ hitvā | anyabhūmikā dharmāḥ te cedanāsravāstrīṇi, vipākavisaṃyogaphale hitvā | niṣyandaphalaṃ hyadhātupatitānāmanyabhūmikaṃ na vāryate | sāsravāśced dve, puruṣakārādhipatiphale |
body.translated_text: <s>Dharmas</s> of one's own plane [yield] four fruits of <s>karma</s>, as applicable, excluding the separation-fruit. <s>Dharmas</s> of another plane — if they are outflow-free, three, excluding the maturation-fruit and the separation-fruit. For the outflow-fruit of those that have fallen into [a different] realm is not excluded as being of another plane. If with-outflow, two — the person-effort-fruit and the dominant fruit.

body.text: śaikṣādyāstrīṇi śaikṣasya ta evāśaikṣakarmaṇaḥ // Abhidh-d_210 //
body.translated_text: The learner and the rest [yield] three [to] learner [karma]; those same [yield fruits] of adept karma. (Abhidh-d 210)

body.text: śaikṣasya karmaṇaḥ śaikṣā dharmāstrīṇi phalāni, vipākavisaṃyogaphale (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 181]

children.text: ) hitvā | aśaikṣā apyevam | naivaśaikṣānāśaikṣāstrīṇyeva niṣyandavipākaphale hitvā ||
children.translated_text: ). Adept [dharmas yield] likewise. Neither-learner-nor-adept [dharmas yield] exactly three, excluding the outflow-fruit and the maturation-fruit.

body.translated_text: Of learner <s>karma</s>, learner <s>dharmas</s> [yield] three fruits, excluding the maturation-fruit and the separation-fruit (

body.text: aśaikṣasya tu karmaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: But of adept <s>karma</s>:

children.text:
ekaṃ trīṇi dvayaṃ caiva śaikṣādyāḥ paścimasya tu /
dve dve pañca yathāsaṃkhyaṃ
children.translated_text: one, three, and two — the learner and the rest of the last; but two, two, and five, respectively.

body.text: aśaikṣasya khalu karmaṇaḥ śaikṣā dharmā ekamadhipatiphalam, aśaikṣāstrīṇi vipākāvisaṃyogaphale hitvā | naivaśaikṣānāśaṃkṣā dve puruṣakārādhipatiphale | naivaśaikṣānāśaikṣāṇāṃ punaḥ śaikṣā dharmā dve puruṣākārādhipatiphale | evamaśaikṣāḥ | naivaśaikṣānāśaikṣāḥ pañcaphalāni |
body.translated_text: Of adept <s>karma</s>, learner <s>dharmas</s> [yield] one — the dominant fruit. Adept [dharmas yield] three, excluding the maturation-fruit and the separation-fruit. Neither-learner-nor-adept [dharmas yield] two — the person-effort-fruit and the dominant fruit. And of neither-learner-nor-adept [karma], learner <s>dharmas</s> [yield] two — the person-effort-fruit and the dominant fruit. Adept [dharmas yield] likewise. Neither-learner-nor-adept [dharmas yield] five fruits.

body.text: dṛggheyasya tu karmaṇaḥ // Abhidh-d_211 //
body.translated_text: Of <s>karma</s> to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaheya</s>) — (Abhidh-d 211)

body.text: trīṇi catvāri caikaṃ ca dṛṣṭiheyādayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
body.translated_text: three, four, and one — the [dharmas] to be abandoned by seeing and the rest, it is declared.

body.text: darśanaheyasya khalu karmaṇaḥ darśanaheyā dharmāstrīṇi phalāni, vipākavisaṃyogaphale hitvā | bhāvanāheyāścatvāri, visaṃyogaphalaṃ hitvā | apraheyā ekamadhipatiphalam |
body.translated_text: Of <s>karma</s> to be abandoned by seeing, <s>dharmas</s> to be abandoned by seeing [yield] three fruits, excluding the maturation-fruit and the separation-fruit. Those to be abandoned by cultivation [yield] four, excluding the separation-fruit. Those not to be abandoned [yield] one — the dominant fruit.

body.text: te tvabhyāsapraheyasya dve catvāri tridhā matāḥ // Abhidh-d_212 //
body.translated_text: Those [dharmas] of <s>karma</s> to be abandoned by cultivation are considered [to yield] two, four, and three. (Abhidh-d 212)

body.text: kramādekadvicatvāri te tvaheyasya karmaṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: In order: one, two, and four — those of <s>karma</s> not to be abandoned.

body.text: bhāvanāheyasya khalu karmaṇo darśanaheyā dharmāḥ dve, puruṣakārādhipatiphale | bhāvanāheyāścatvāri visaṃyogaphalaṃ hitvā | apraheyāstrīṇi, vipākaniṣyandaphale hitvā | apraheyasya tu karmaṇo darśanaprahātavyā dharmā ekamadhipatiphalam | bhāvanāheyā dve, puruṣakārādhipatiphale | apraheyāścatvāri vipākaphalaṃ hitvā ||
body.translated_text: Of <s>karma</s> to be abandoned by cultivation, <s>dharmas</s> to be abandoned by seeing [yield] two — the person-effort-fruit and the dominant fruit. Those to be abandoned by cultivation [yield] four, excluding the separation-fruit. Those not to be abandoned [yield] three, excluding the maturation-fruit and the outflow-fruit. But of <s>karma</s> not to be abandoned, <s>dharmas</s> to be abandoned by seeing [yield] one — the dominant fruit. Those to be abandoned by cultivation [yield] two — the person-effort-fruit and the dominant fruit. Those not to be abandoned [yield] four, excluding the maturation-fruit.

body.text: atha kimekaṃ karmaikaṃ janmākṣipati, athānekam ? tadādarśyate-
body.translated_text: Now, does a single <s>karma</s> project a single birth, or do many? This is shown:

body.text: ekenākṣipyatejanma bhūribhiḥ paripūryate // Abhidh-d_213 //
body.translated_text: A single [karma] projects a birth; many [karmas] complete it. (Abhidh-d 213)

body.text: ekena khalu karmaṇā sakalamekaṃ janmākṣipyate | bahubhistu paripūryate | tadyathā citrakara ekayā vartyā katsnaṃ rūpamākṣipati, bahvībhiḥ paripūrayati tadvaditi |
body.translated_text: By a single <s>karma</s>, a complete single birth is projected. But it is completed by many [karmas]. Just as a painter projects the entire figure with a single stroke, and fills it in with many [strokes] — so too.

body.text: atha yaduktaṃ bhagavatā- "karmasvako 'yaṃ bhikṣavo lokaḥ" iti | tatkeyaṃ karmasvakatā nāma ? tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: Now, regarding the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s statement: 'This world, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, has <s>karma</s> as its own possession.' What then is this '<s>karma</s>-own-possession' (<s>karmasvakatā</s>)? This is now undertaken:

children.translated_text: Whatever wholesome or evil [karma], past, that gives fruit —

children.text: svaṃ kāyavāṅmanaskarma sā karmasvakatā matā // Abhidh-d_214 //
children.translated_text: one's own bodily, verbal, and mental <s>karma</s> — that is considered '<s>karma</s>-own-possession.' (Abhidh-d 214)

body.text: yatkhalu kāyavāṅmanaskarma svayaṃ kṛtaṃ kuśalākuśalamabhyatītaṃ dadatphalaṃ sā karmasvakatā draṣṭavyā ||
body.translated_text: The bodily, verbal, and mental <s>karma</s> that one has personally performed, whether wholesome or unwholesome, that is past and gives fruit — that should be seen as <s>karma</s>-own-possession.

body.text: kathaṃ punaḥ pratikṣaṇabhidureṣu saṃskāreṣu parasparākṛtasaṅketeṣu satsu, asati ca nitye kartari bhoktari ca karmasvakatābhidhīyate ? tadatra pratisamādhīyate-
body.translated_text: But how, when conditioned things perish at every moment, when there is no mutually established convention among them, and when there is no permanent agent or experiencer, is <s>karma</s>-own-possession spoken of? To this, the response:

children.translated_text: Conventionally, in the continuum of aggregates, because action and fruit are observed,

children.text: kartṛtā bhoktṛtā coktā niṣiddhā śāśvatasya tu // Abhidh-d_215 //
children.translated_text: agency and experiencer-hood are spoken of; but [both] are prohibited for the eternal [self]. (Abhidh-d 215)

body.text: svātmābhyudayaviśeṣārthaḥ khalu karmārabhyate | kaścidahaṃ viśiṣṭajñānavijñānasaukhyarūpakāntilāvaṇyasauṣṭhavayuktaṃ janma pratilabheyeti | śāśvate tvātmani niṣkriye pūrvapaścādviśeṣābhāvāt kartṛtvaṃ cātyantāpadhvastayuktividhānam | skandhasantāne tu viśiṣṭaskandhāntarotpattau satyāṃ bījajalābhiṣekādyanugrahād viśiṣṭaphalotpattivaditi | pūrvamevāviṣkṛtametaditi ||
body.translated_text: For <s>karma</s> is undertaken for the purpose of one's own benefit and distinction. Someone [thinks:] 'May I obtain a birth endowed with distinguished knowledge, consciousness, happiness, form, beauty, charm, and grace.' But for an eternal, inactive self, because there is no distinction between before and after, agency would be a method with its logic completely refuted.
