But in the continuum of aggregates, when the arising of a distinguished [set of] subsequent aggregates occurs, it is like the arising of a distinguished fruit through the assistance of seed, water, and irrigation — this was previously disclosed.

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam |
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated:

body.text: syātkarmasvakatā nāsti tasya ceti catuṣkikā /
body.translated_text: There is <s>karma</s>-own-possession but not of that [karma] — [this is] the fourfold classification.

body.text: syātkhalu karmasvakatā nāpi ca tasya karmaṇo vipāke 'vasthita iti catuṣkoṭikā |
body.translated_text: There may be <s>karma</s>-own-possession, yet one is not situated in the maturation of that <s>karma</s> — [this is] the fourfold classification.

body.text: prathamā tatphalasthasya vihānāttasya karmaṇaḥ // Abhidh-d_216 //
body.translated_text: The first [case]: for one situated in the fruit of that [karma], through the destruction of that <s>karma</s>. (Abhidh-d 216)

body.text: yadi tasya karmaṇaḥ phale 'vasthitastacca karma vihīnaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: If one is situated in the fruit of that <s>karma</s>, and that <s>karma</s> has been exhausted.

children.translated_text: The second: for one situated in the fruit of that [karma], and still connected with that <s>karma</s>;
the third: for one endowed with both; the fourth: for one without either. (Abhidh-d 217)

body.text: syātkarmasvakatā nāpi tatphalaṃ vedayiṣyati /
body.translated_text: There may be <s>karma</s>-own-possession, yet one will not experience that fruit.

body.text: dvitīyā catuṣkoṭikā | tatra prathamā koṭiḥ-
body.translated_text: [This is] the second fourfold classification. Of that, the first case:

body.text: tatphalāvasthitasyādyā jñeyā taccarame phale // Abhidh-d_218 //
body.translated_text: For one situated in the fruit of that [karma] — the first — this should be known as [applying] to the last fruit. (Abhidh-d 218)

children.translated_text: The second: for one whose [karma] will certainly ripen, [but who is] not situated in its maturation;

children.text: tṛtīyā dvayasadbhāvā caturthī tūbhayaṃ vinā // Abhidh-d_219 //
children.translated_text: the third: from the existence of both; the fourth: without both. (Abhidh-d 219)

body.text: tṛtīyā catuṣkoṭikā-
body.translated_text: The third fourfold classification:

body.text: syātkarmaṇānvitaścaiva no ca tatphalavedanam /
body.translated_text: One may be connected with <s>karma</s> and yet not experience its fruit.

body.text: syātkhalu karmaṇā samanvāgato na ca tasya karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ vedayate | catuṣkoṭikā |
body.translated_text: One may indeed be possessed of <s>karma</s>, yet not experience the fruit of that <s>karma</s>. [This is] the fourfold classification.

body.text: ādyā dattavipākena niruddhānāgatādinā // Abhidh-d_220 //
body.translated_text: The first [case]: with a [karma] whose maturation has been given, [that is] ceased, future, and so forth. (Abhidh-d 220)

children.translated_text: The second: with a <s>karma</s> that is exhausted but will certainly ripen.

children.text: tṛtīyā dvayamuktasya caturthī tu dvayādṛte // Abhidh-d_221 //
children.translated_text: The third: for one freed from both; the fourth: without both. (Abhidh-d 221)

body.text: atha yadidaṃ śāstre yogavihitamayogavihitaṃ ca karmoktaṃ tasya kiṃ lakṣaṇam ? tadabhidhīyate-
body.translated_text: Now, regarding what is stated in the treatise as <s>karma</s> prescribed by [proper] method (<s>yogavihita</s>) and not prescribed by [proper] method (<s>ayogavihita</s>) — what is their definition? This is stated:

children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> not prescribed by [proper] method is that contaminated by defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) and secondary defilements (<s>upakleśa</s>);
and that which deviates from training rules, comportment, and the like — so say some of the learned. (Abhidh-d 222)

body.text: yatkiñcitkhalu kliṣṭaṃ kāyavāṅmanaskarma kleśopakleśadūṣitaṃ sarvaṃ tadayogavihitama, ayoniśomanaskārasamutthāpitatvāt | anye punarbruvate- yatkhalu śikṣāvyapetaṃ yathā gantavyaṃ sthātavyamityevamādi, yattu liṅgavacanahīnamasaṃbaddhaṃ nirarthakaṃ ca vākkarma tadayogavihitam | vidhibhraṣṭatvāditi | viparyayādyogavihitaṃ draṣṭavyamiti ||
body.translated_text: Whatever defiled bodily, verbal, and mental <s>karma</s>, contaminated by defilements and secondary defilements — all that is not prescribed by [proper] method, because it is produced by improper mental engagement (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>). Others, however, say: that which deviates from the training rules, such as how to walk, how to stand, and the like; and verbal <s>karma</s> that lacks proper form of expression, is incoherent, and meaningless — that is not prescribed by [proper] method, because it deviates from the prescribed form. By the opposite [of these], one should understand [what is] prescribed by [proper] method.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau caturthasyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the commentary called <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>, [this is] the third quarter (<s>pāda</s>) of the fourth chapter.

body.text: caturthādhyāye
body.translated_text: In the fourth chapter,

body.text: caturthapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: the fourth quarter.

body.text: athaitāṃ paramagambhīrāṃ duravabodhāṃ prakṛtipuruṣeśvarādikudarśanatimirotsādanakarīṃ karmasvakatāṃ kaḥ svayamabhisaṃbuddhya lokānugrahāya pradarśayatīti ? brūmaḥ | puruṣaḥ tu so bodhisattvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, who is it that, having himself fully comprehended this supremely profound and difficult-to-understand <s>karma</s>-own-possession — which dispels the darkness of wrong views such as [those regarding] primordial nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), person (<s>puruṣa</s>), lord (<s>īśvara</s>), and the like — demonstrates it for the benefit of the world? We say: that person is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: sa punaḥ kiṃ cittotpādātprabhṛti bodhisattvo bhavati ? atha lākṣaṇikakarmākṣepeṇa, āhosviccaramabhavika iti ? ata idaṃ prastūyate-
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] From what point does he become a <s>Bodhisattva</s>? Is it from the first arising of the [awakening] mind? Or from the projection of the <s>karma</s> that produces the [bodily] marks? Or from the last existence? Therefore this is taken up:

children.translated_text: From where does one become a <s>Bodhisattva</s>? From the point when, with irreversible mind,
he binds on the armor of awakening (<s>bodhisannāha</s>), having accepted the welfare of the world. (Abhidh-d 223)

body.text: yataḥ prabhṛti kalyāṇamitraṃ bhagavantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhamāpadya tadupadarśitadakṣiṇamārgaḥ yoniśo manasikārādhiṣṭhitabuddhiḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokamatrāṇamaśaraṇamaparāyaṇaṃ pañcagatimahāvarte jātijarāvyādhimaraṇādiduḥkhakṣārāmbhasi, karmarākṣasādhiṣṭhitatīre, pāpamitrakumbhīrānubaddhabele, rūpādiviṣayavikalpapavanoddhatatṛṣṇātaraṅge, mohakarṇadhāraparibhrāmitabuddhinauke saṃsāramahāsamudre nimagnamavalokya kṛpāviṣṭacetāstadabhyuddharaṇāya vīryabāhumabhiprasārya, avivartyaṃ cittamevamutpādayati- (

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 186)

children.text: ) avidyāndhaḥkāropahatabuddhinayano 'yaṃ lokaḥ sa mayā samyagdṛṣṭiprabhāvabhāsitena śīlasaṃkrameṇottārayitavyaḥ | pratighabhujaṅgadaṃṣṭrā viṣadūṣito 'yaṃ lokaḥ sa mayā maitryāgadena praśamitavyaḥ | tṛṣṇāpiśācīlalitābhibhūtamatirayaṃ lokaḥ sa mayā śamathabalena tṛṣṇānirodhasukhaṃ lambhayitavyaḥ | parāmarśabhūtagrahāviṣṭo 'yaṃ lokaḥ sa mayā vimokṣasukhasvastyayanena nirbhayamamṛtapadaṃ praveśayitavyaḥ | mānagiriśikharādhirūḍhabuddhirayaṃ lokaḥ sa mayā karmasvakatājñānavajreṇa mānagirīnvicūrṇya praśāntamānamadāmarśaśāntipade sthāpayitavyaḥ | vicikitsākathaṃkathībhāvaśalyaviddhahṛdayo 'yaṃ lokaḥ sa mayā pratītyasamutpādapravicayaśalākayā kāṅkṣāśalyamutpāṭyāmṛtarasaṃ pāyayitavyaḥ | jarāvyādhimaraṇamakaradaṃṣṭrāntargato 'yaṃ lokaḥ sa mayā sarvānarthaviyuktaṃ nirvṛtisukhaṃ prāpayitavyaḥ | śraddhādiguṇadhanadaridro 'yaṃ lokaḥ sa mayā bodhyaṅgaratnakhacite mahati guṇaiśvaryapade sanniveśayitavyaḥ | ityetasmādavivartyād bodhicittotpādātprabhṛti baudhisattvo vaktavya ityācāryakam ||
children.translated_text: 'This world, whose vision-eye of intellect is afflicted by the darkness of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) — it must be saved by me, crossing [them] over by the bridge of morality (<s>śīla</s>), illuminated by the radiance of right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>). This world, poisoned by the fang-venom of the serpent of hostility (<s>pratigha</s>) — it must be pacified by me with the medicine of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>). This world, whose intellect is overpowered by the seductive play of the she-demon of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) — by the power of tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>), the happiness of the cessation of craving must be bestowed by me. This world, possessed by the demon-grasp of clinging (<s>parāmarśa</s>) — it must be led by me, without fear, into the immortal state (<s>amṛtapada</s>), through the auspicious ceremony of the happiness of liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>). This world, whose intellect has climbed the mountain-peak of conceit (<s>māna</s>) — the mountains of conceit must be pulverized by me with the thunderbolt of the knowledge that one's actions are one's own (<s>karmasvaka</s>), and [they must be] established in the peaceful state where the intoxication and arrogance of conceit are quelled. This world, whose heart is pierced by the arrow of doubt and perplexity (<s>vicikitsā</s>) — the arrow of doubt must be extracted by me with the probe of the analysis of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), and the nectar-juice must be administered. This world, caught within the jaws of the sea-monster (<s>makara</s>) of aging, disease, and death — the happiness of cessation (<s>nirvṛti</s>), free from all misfortune, must be attained by me [for them]. This world, impoverished in the wealth of qualities such as faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) — it must be established by me in the great state of the sovereignty of qualities, studded with the jewels of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>).' From this irreversible arising of the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) onward, he should be called a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — this is the teaching of the masters.

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] From the point when, having come upon a good spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) — the <s>Bhagavān</s>, a Perfectly and Fully Awakened One — and having been shown by him the right path, with intellect established through proper attention (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>), [he sees] the entire world — without protector, without refuge, without final resort — in the great whirlpool of the five destinies, in the corrosive waters of suffering — birth, aging, disease, death, and the rest — on shores haunted by the demons of <s>karma</s>, in the depths pursued by the crocodiles of evil companions, with waves of craving tossed by the wind of conceptual proliferation regarding objects of form and the rest, with the boat of intellect whirled about by the helmsman of delusion — [seeing the world] sunk in this great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, his mind pervaded by compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>), for the sake of lifting [them] out, extending the arm of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), he produces this irreversible mind: (

body.text: yattarhi śāstra uktam- "bodhisattvaḥ kutaḥ prabhṛti ? yato lakṣaṇavaipākyaṃ karma karoti" iti | naiṣa doṣaḥ | yasmādasau-
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] As for what is stated in the treatise: 'From what point is one a <s>Bodhisattva</s>? From when one performs the <s>karma</s> that produces the [bodily] marks' — this is not a fault. Because that one —

children.translated_text: when he performs the <s>karma</s> producing the [bodily] marks, not subject to the lower destinies (<s>apāya</s>),
of great family, with intact sense-faculties, delighting in the gathering of his own assembly, (Abhidh-d 224)

body.text: pumāñjātismaro vāgmī prajñāvīryakriyānvitaḥ /
body.translated_text: a male, remembering past lives, eloquent, endowed with wisdom, vigor, and action —

body.text: yadā khalvayaṃ puruṣatvajātismaratvādiṣu padasthāneṣu niyatībhato bhavati-
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] When this [being] has become fixed in the positions of manhood, memory of past lives, and the rest —

body.text: tadā devamanuṣyāṇāmabhivyaktiṃ nigacchati // Abhidh-d_225 //
body.translated_text: then he becomes manifest to gods and humans. (Abhidh-d 225)

body.text: ato jñānaprasthāne 'smādavadheḥ prabhṛti bodhisattvaḥ anenābhiprāyeṇa paṭhitaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, in the <s>Jñānaprasthāna</s>, from this marker onward, he is recited as '<s>Bodhisattva</s>' — with this intention.

children.translated_text: For he, through three incalculable [aeons] (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>), accumulates the ocean of qualities of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>;

children.text: pracinoti tadādhāraṃ kāyaṃ kalpaśatena tu // Abhidh-d_226 //
children.translated_text: but the body that supports it, through a hundred aeons. (Abhidh-d 226)
Endowed with the thirty-two marks, radiant with the eighty minor characteristics —

children.text: dviṣatāmapi yaṃ dṛṣṭvā manaḥ sadyaḥ prasīdati // Abhidh-d_227 //
children.translated_text: seeing which, even the minds of enemies are immediately gladdened. (Abhidh-d 227)

body.text: eṣā khalu dharmatā yattribhiḥ kalpāsaṃkhyeyairanirastaśraddhāśīlaśrutatyāgaprajñādiguṇadhanaiśvaryaprayogānāṃ bhagavatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ puruṣottamānāṃ dharmakāyacaraṇaparisamāptirbhavati | kalpaśatena khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpānāṃ pratyekabuddhānām | ṣaṣṭhyā kalpaiḥ prajñāvatāmagryāṇām | catvāriṃśadbhiḥ ṛddhimacchreṣṭhānām | viṃśatibhiḥ kalpaiḥ śrutadharapravarāṇāṃ dharmakāyacaraṇaparipūrirbhavati |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This indeed is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>): that through three incalculable aeons of effort — with the wealth-sovereignty of qualities such as faith, morality, learning, generosity, and wisdom undiminished — the completion of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> conduct occurs for the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, the Perfectly and Fully Awakened Ones, the supreme among beings. Through a hundred aeons for <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> of the rhinoceros-horn type. Through sixty aeons for the foremost of those endowed with wisdom. Through forty for the best of those endowed with supernatural power. Through twenty aeons, the fulfillment of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> conduct occurs for the foremost among those who retain [the teachings] through learning.

body.text: yatpunarjanmaśarīraṃ bhagavatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ bodherāśrayabhūtaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ khacitamaśītyānuvyañjanairvirājitam, yatkhalu dṛṣṭvā svavikalpasamutthitapratighadūṣitabuddhīnāmapi (

children.translated_text: (Jaini, p. 188)
) even [those] of <s>Māra</s>'s faction and of the non-Buddhist teachers — even their minds are gladdened.

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] As for the birth-body of the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, the Perfectly and Fully Awakened Ones — the support of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — studded with the thirty-two marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) and adorned with the eighty minor characteristics (<s>anuvyañjana</s>) — seeing which, even [the minds] of those whose intellect is corrupted by hostility arisen from their own conceptual proliferation — (

body.text: kāni punastāni dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni ? kāni vāśītyanuvyañjanāni ? tadidaṃ pradarśyate-
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] What then are these thirty-two marks of a great being? And what are the eighty minor characteristics? This is now shown:

body.text: tatra tāvadamūni dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni-
body.translated_text: Now, these are the thirty-two marks of a great being:

body.text: buddhā hi bhagavantaḥ samamahītalākramaṇāt supratiṣṭhitapādāḥ || 1 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, have well-established feet, because they step evenly on the ground surface. (1)

body.text: sahasrārasanābhikasanemikasarvākāraparipūrṇacakrāṅkitapāṇipādatvāccakrāṅkahastapādāḥ || 2 ||
body.translated_text: They have wheel-marked hands and feet, because their palms and soles are marked with wheels complete in all features — with a thousand spokes, a hub, and a rim. (2)

body.text: āyatahastapādāṅgulitvāddīrghāṅgulayaḥ || 3 ||
body.translated_text: They have long fingers, because their fingers on hands and feet are elongated. (3)

body.text: dīrghāyatatvādāyatapārṣṇipādāḥ || 4 ||
body.translated_text: They have broad-heeled feet, because [the heels] are long and extended. (4)

body.text: tūlapicutaruṇasukumāropamakomalakaracaraṇatvānmṛdutaruṇapāṇipādāḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: They have soft, tender palms and soles, because their hands and feet are tender and delicate like cotton-down and fresh [sprouts]. (5)

body.text: abhitāmrāṣṭāpadavicitratanujālāvanaddhatvādabhijātahaṃsarājavajjālāvanaddhapādāḥ || 6 ||
body.translated_text: Their feet are web-joined — like a noble royal swan — because they are netted with a fine web of coppery-red, varied, eight-sided [design]. (6)

body.text: uccaiḥ sujātagulphatvāducchaṅkucaraṇāḥ || 7 ||
body.translated_text: They have high-raised ankles, because their anklebones are well-formed and elevated. (7)

body.text: anupūrvopacitavṛttataragarbhaiṇeyamṛgajaṅghatvādaiṇeyajaṅghāḥ || 8 ||
body.translated_text: They have antelope-like legs, because their calves are gradually filled, round, and shaped like the belly of an antelope deer. (8)

body.text: prāṃśubāhutvādanavanatakāyajānumaṇḍalasparśinaḥ || 9 ||
body.translated_text: They can touch their knees without bending, because their arms are long and reach the kneecaps of the unbent body. (9)

body.text: paramābhirūpanirgūḍhapuruṣanimittatvādabhijātahastyaśvājāneyavatkośagatavastiguhyāḥ || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Their male organ is sheathed — like a noble elephant, horse, or thoroughbred — because their sign of manhood is supremely well-formed and concealed. (10)

body.text: kāyavyāmasamāyāmatvānnyagrodhaparimaṇḍalāḥ || 11 ||
body.translated_text: They are proportioned like a <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree, because the height and span of their body are equal. (11)

body.text: anupūrvordhvamukhajātatvādūrdhvāṅgaromāṇaḥ || 12 ||
body.translated_text: Their body-hairs grow upward, because each [hair] grows individually upward. (12)

body.text: suvibhaktādvitīyanīlajātaromatvādekaikābhinīlapradakṣiṇāvartaromāṇaḥ || 13 ||
body.translated_text: Each body-hair curls clockwise, separately dark-blue in color, because the hairs are well-distributed and of matchless dark-blue birth. (13)

body.text: uttaptahāṭakasannibhadṛgvyāmamātraprabhāvabhāsanāt suvarṇavarṇāḥ || 14 ||
body.translated_text: They are golden-hued, because the luster of their refined gold-like radiance illuminates [the area of] a fathom around. (14)

body.text: suparikarmīkṛtarajatajātarūpaślakṣṇacchavitvādrajomalānupakleśanācca sūkṣmacchavayaḥ || 15 ||
body.translated_text: They have fine skin, because their complexion is smooth like well-polished silver-gold, and because dust and impurity do not adhere [to it]. (15)

body.text: samupacitahastapādāṃsagrīvatvātsaptotsadakāyāḥ || 16 ||
body.translated_text: They have the body of seven prominences, because their hands, feet, shoulders, and neck are well-formed and prominent. (16)

body.text: kāñcanaśilātalaślakṣṇopacitoraskandhāccitāntarāṃsāḥ || 17 ||
body.translated_text: The area between their shoulders is filled, because their chest and shoulders are smooth and prominent like a golden rock-surface. (17)

body.text: siṃhavadvistīrṇasaṃhatordhvāṅgatvātsiṃhapūrvārdhakāyāḥ || 18 ||
body.translated_text: They have the forequarters of a lion, because [their torso] is broad, compact, and upright like a lion's. (18)

body.text: avakropacitadaśatālasamucchritatvād bṛhadṛjugātrāḥ || 19 ||
body.translated_text: They have tall and straight bodies, because they are towering without curvature, measuring ten arm-spans in height. (19)

body.text: samantopacitamāṃsanirgūḍhajatrudeśatvātsusaṃvṛttaskandhāḥ || 20 ||
body.translated_text: They have well-rounded shoulders, because the shoulder-region is concealed by evenly accumulated flesh. (20)

body.text: adhastādupariṣṭācca samadantaviṃśatitvāccatvāriṃśaddantāḥ || 21 ||
body.translated_text: They have forty teeth, because they have twenty above and twenty below, equal [on both sides]. (21)

body.text: anunnatāvanatasamapramāṇatvātsamadantāḥ || 22 ||
body.translated_text: They have even teeth, because [the teeth] are not raised, not sunken, and of equal measure. (22)

body.text: nirantarāvasthitatvādaviraladantāḥ || 23 ||
body.translated_text: They have teeth without gaps, because [the teeth] stand without intervals. (23)

body.text: kundenduśaṅkhāvabhedasitatvācchakladantāḥ || 24 ||
body.translated_text: They have brilliant white teeth, because they are white like jasmine, moonlight, and conch-shell without blemish. (24)

body.text: ślakṣṇavṛttopacitadarśanīyamahāhanutvātsiṃhahanavaḥ || 25 ||
body.translated_text: They have lion-jaws, because the jawbone is smooth, round, prominent, and well-proportioned and large. (25)

body.text: vātapittaśleṣmānabhibhūtarasaharaṇirasārasapravibhāvanāsadṛśavijñānatvādrasanarasāgraprāptāḥ || 26 ||
body.translated_text: They have the supreme sense of taste, because their faculty of tasting discerns the distribution of flavor-essences, not overcome by wind, bile, or phlegm — like an unequaled cognition [for flavor]. (26)

body.text: vistīrṇapeśalatvājjihvāyāḥ sarvamukhamaṇḍalapraticchādanātprabhūtatanujihvāḥ || 27 ||
body.translated_text: They have a broad, thin tongue — because the tongue, being expansive and delicate, covers the entire face-surface. (27)

body.text: gambhīravalguhṛdayaṅgamavispaṣṭaśravaṇīyapañcāṅgopetasvaratvādbrahmasvarāḥ || 28 ||
body.translated_text: They have a <s>Brahmā</s>-voice, because their voice is deep, pleasing, heart-touching, clear, audible, and endowed with five qualities. (28)

body.text: kalaviṅkamanojñabhāṣiṇo dundubhisvaranirghoṣāḥ || 29 ||
body.translated_text: They speak with the sweet voice of a <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird, [having] the resonance of a celestial drum. (29)

body.text: śuklakṛṣṇapradeśānupakliṣṭalohitarājyavinaddhanīlotpalasamānavarṇatvādabhinīlanetrāḥ || 30 ||
body.translated_text: They have dark-blue eyes, because the color of their [irises] matches a blue lotus — the white and black regions being unafflicted and bound with a streak of red. (30)

body.text: adharordhvāvasthitānāṃ samyagavanatāsaṃluḍitadīrghatvādakṣipakṣmāṇāṃ gopakṣmāṇaḥ || 31 ||
body.translated_text: They have eyelashes like a cow's — because the lashes, properly situated above and below, are straight, unmatted, unshaken, and long. (31)

body.text: vṛttaparimaṇḍalasamānupūrvopacitadarśanīyāsthivajrajātamūrdhatvāduṣṇīṣālaṅkṛtaśirasaḥ śaṅkhāvadātapradakṣiṇāvartorṇāvidyotitabhrūvinatatvādūrṇāṅkitamukhāḥ || 32 ||
body.translated_text: Their heads are adorned with a cranial protuberance (<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>), because the crown of the head is round, proportioned, gradually prominent, handsome, and of adamantine bone-structure. Their faces are marked with the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the eyebrows), because the space between the brows is illumined by a shining <s>ūrṇā</s> — conch-white and curling clockwise. (32)

body.text: etāni dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmiti ||
body.translated_text: These are the thirty-two marks of a great being of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>.

body.text: aśītyanuvyañjanānyapyucyante | buddhā hi bhagavantaḥ apṛthupramāṇamṛdutāmratuṅgasnigdhanakhāḥ || 1 ||
body.translated_text: The eighty minor characteristics are also stated. The <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, have nails that are not broad, soft, coppery, elevated, and smooth. (1)

body.text: vṛttanirantarānupūrvopacitāṅgulayaḥ || 2 ||
body.translated_text: They have round, unbroken, gradually tapering fingers. (2)

body.text: nirgranthinirgūḍhālpatanuśirāpratānāḥ || 3 ||
body.translated_text: They have vein-networks that are knotless, concealed, and slender, with thin spreading. (3)

body.text: nirgūḍhasamātīkṣṇagulphāḥ || 4 ||
body.translated_text: They have ankles that are concealed, even, and sharp. (4)

body.text: aviṣamāvakraraktasnigdhapādāḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: Their feet are level, not crooked, red, and smooth. (5)

body.text: mṛgapatidviradavṛṣabhahaṃsarājapradakṣiṇāvartacārugatayaḥ || 6 ||
body.translated_text: Their gait is beautiful, clockwise-turning — like a king of deer, elephants, bulls, or royal swans. (6)

body.text: alomasāśleṣasamapramāṇobhayajaṅghāḥ || 7 ||
body.translated_text: Both shins are hairless, unclinging, and of equal measure. (7)

body.text: suvṛtasamasaṃhatanirgūḍhajānavaḥ || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Their knees are well-rounded, even, compact, and concealed. (8)

body.text: kadalīskandhopamapīnanibiḍāviṣamānupūrvopacitacārūravaḥ || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Their thighs are shapely — like plantain trunks — full, dense, even, gradually tapering, and beautiful. (9)

body.text: ardhacandrākṛtivistīrṇasamunnatāpagataromavakṣāṇaḥ || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Their hips are shaped like a half-moon — broad, prominent, and hairless. (10)

body.text: ślakṣṇasusaṃhatacaturastranābhyāyatakukundarasundarakaṭīdeśāḥ || 11 ||
body.translated_text: The region of the waist, navel, and belly is smooth, well-compacted, rectangular, elongated, and beautiful. (11)

body.text: gambhīrācchidraraktapradakṣiṇāvartanābhayaḥ || 12 ||
body.translated_text: Their navels are deep, clear, red, and clockwise-turning. (12)

body.text: ślakṣṇālomaśāślathānukramakṣāmodarāḥ || 13 ||
body.translated_text: Their abdomens are smooth, hairless, without folds, and progressively slender. (13)

body.text: anābhugnānibhugnasuvattapaṣṭhakukṣayaḥ || 14 ||
body.translated_text: Their flanks and sides are unbent, well-rounded, and level. (14)

body.text: samavatīrṇopacitanātidīrghaślakṣṇapārśvāḥ || 15 ||
body.translated_text: Their sides are evenly descending, well-formed, not too long, and smooth. (15)

body.text: animnopacitahrasvavajrasaṃsthānopapannasūkṣmadīrghalekhāṅkitādṛśyārithasandhicārupṛṣṭhāḥ || 16 ||
body.translated_text: Their backs are beautiful, with joints invisible — not sunken, well-formed, short, of adamantine structure, delicately inscribed with fine long lines. (16)

body.text: vistīrṇopacitadṛḍhasandhihṛdayāḥ || 17 ||
body.translated_text: Their hearts are broad, well-formed, and with firm joints. (17)

body.text: aviṣamonnatavistīrṇorasaḥ || 18 ||
body.translated_text: Their chests are level, elevated, and broad. (18)

body.text: anatisthūlonnataśaṅkhāvartanibhasūkṣmalekhāparikṣiptasamaraktastanāḥ || 19 ||
body.translated_text: Their nipples are even, red, not too thick, elevated — inscribed with fine lines like a conch-whorl, and set apart. (19)

body.text: hṛdayaviprakṛṣṭadeśajātatvādvistīrṇastanāntarāḥ || 20 ||
body.translated_text: The space between the nipples is wide, because [the nipples] are born far from the heart-region. (20)

body.text: māṃsopacitānativistīrṇatvādunnatakakṣāḥ || 21 ||
body.translated_text: Their armpits are raised because of fleshy fullness, not too wide. (21)

body.text: sthūladṛḍhasubaddhanimagnasamākṣakāḥ || 22 ||
body.translated_text: Their collarbones are thick, firm, well-bound, and sunken, with level hollows. (22)

body.text: aślakṣṇapṛthumāṃsanimagnāviṣamapramāṇasphijaḥ || 23 ||
body.translated_text: Their buttocks are fleshy, not rough, thick, and sunken — not uneven in measure. (23)

body.text: karikaranibhanirgūḍhasandhipīnakaṭhinaślakṣṇasamabāhavaḥ || 24 ||
body.translated_text: Their arms are like an elephant's trunk — with concealed joints, full, hard, smooth, and even. (24)

body.text: vartitaślakṣṇaromaśasiṃhopamadṛḍhaprakoṣṭhāḥ || 25 ||
body.translated_text: Their forearms are rounded, smooth, hairy, and firm like a lion's. (25)

body.text: samatāmradīrghapāṇayaḥ || 26 ||
body.translated_text: Their palms are even, coppery, and long. (26)

body.text: gambhīrācchidrāsaṃkīrṇavakrāyatasnigdhatanutāmrapāṇilekhāḥ || 27 ||
body.translated_text: Their palm-lines are deep, clear, uncrowded, not crooked, elongated, smooth, thin, and coppery. (27)

body.text: sūkṣmayamalīkṛtādhyākulāraktāṅguliparvāṇaḥ || 28 ||
body.translated_text: Their finger-joints are fine, paired, not confused, and reddish. (28)

body.text: anāmikāparvādhikapramāṇakanīnikāṅgulayaḥ || 29 ||
body.translated_text: Their little fingers are of greater measure than the ring-finger joint. (29)

body.text: anatibahutanumṛdusnigdhasubaddhamūlasamaromāṇaḥ || 30 ||
body.translated_text: Their body-hairs are not too many, thin, soft, smooth, well-rooted, and even. (30)

body.text: snigdhāsaṃkucitānupahatasāracchavayaḥ || 31 ||
body.translated_text: Their complexion is smooth, uncontracted, and unmarred — of essential [quality]. (31)

body.text: śotoṣṇasparśāvyakacchavīva varṇāḥ || 32 ||
body.translated_text: Their skin-color is like one unaffected by the touch of cold and heat. (32)

body.text: sthiranibiḍānatisthūlānatikṛśamāṃsāḥ || 33 ||
body.translated_text: Their flesh is firm, dense, not too thick, and not too thin. (33)

body.text: javāpuṣpābhitāmrasvacchasnigdhamadhuracandanagandhirudhirāḥ || 34 ||
body.translated_text: Their blood is like <s>javā</s> (hibiscus) flowers — coppery, clear, smooth, sweet, and fragrant with sandalwood. (34)

body.text: māṃsopagūḍhasthūladṛḍhasuśirāsthikāḥ || 35 ||
body.translated_text: Their bones are covered with flesh, thick, firm, and well-channeled. (35)

body.text: nāgagranthyavasthitanirgūḍhāsthisandhayaḥ || 36 ||
body.translated_text: Their bone-joints are established like knots of a <s>nāga</s> (serpent) and are concealed. (36)

body.text: vajravadabhedyaśarīratvātsusaṃhananāḥ |37 ||
body.translated_text: Their bodies are well-knit, because [their] bodies are like adamant — unbreakable. (37)

body.text: cārusuvibhaktāṅgapratyaṅgāḥ || 38 ||
body.translated_text: Their limbs and sub-limbs are beautiful and well-proportioned. (38)

body.text: anupūrvopacitasuparimṛṣṭasukumārādīptasvacchaśarīrāḥ || 39 ||
body.translated_text: Their bodies are gradually tapering, well-refined, delicate, radiant, and clear. (39)

body.text: nirmaśakatilakālapilyāḥ || 40 ||
body.translated_text: They are free from freckles, moles, and dark spots. (40)

body.text: jarādaurbalyakṛtāpagatavalayaḥ || 41 ||
body.translated_text: They are free from wrinkles caused by aging and weakness. (41)

body.text: siṃhaśayyānuṣṭhānavyapagatakāyavikṣepāḥ || 42 ||
body.translated_text: They are free from bodily restlessness, due to the practice of the lion-posture. (42)

body.text: svedamalānupakliṣṭaśucisaumyacchāyāḥ || 43 ||
body.translated_text: Their shadow is pure and pleasing, unafflicted by sweat and dirt. (43)

body.text: jvalanamaṇimahauṣadhiśaśāṅkasavitṛsamatejasaḥ || 44 ||
body.translated_text: Their radiance is equal to that of a blazing gem, a great healing herb, the moon, and the sun. (44)

body.text: mahīdharavaragurutvopetāḥ || 45 ||
body.translated_text: They are endowed with the weight of a great mountain-peak. (45)

body.text: ṛtusukhakālindikasukhasaṃsparṣāḥ || 46 ||
body.translated_text: Their touch is as pleasant as seasonal comfort and the [waters of the] <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) river. (46)

body.text: madhuramṛdusurabhikusumacandanasamānaromakūpagandhāḥ || 47 ||
body.translated_text: Their pore-fragrance is like sweet, soft, fragrant flowers and sandalwood. (47)

body.text: abhinavanīlotpalatulyasārvakālikamukhagandhāḥ || 48 ||
body.translated_text: Their face-fragrance at all times is equal to a fresh blue lotus. (48)

body.text: adbhutamṛdudīrghasnigdhapiṇḍitavyapagataśabdaniśvāsāḥ || 49 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] voices are wondrous, soft, prolonged, smooth, full, clear, and [their] breathing is free from [harsh] sounds. (49)

body.text:
anaśanakadannāśanātaṅkāttu vipariṇāmānuparatadharmadeśanābhirapyasañjitasvarabhedāḥ
|| 50 ||
body.translated_text: Even through fasting, eating poor food, illness, and the cessation of dharma-teaching due to transformation, they do not suffer deterioration of voice. (50)

body.text: nātisaṃkucitavidāritaraktāsyāḥ || 51 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] mouths are neither excessively contracted, nor gaping, nor reddened. (51)

body.text: śucisamācārāḥ || 52 ||
body.translated_text: They are of pure conduct. (52)

body.text: deśastha ttaptavispaṣṭaparipūrṇavyañjanāḥ || 53 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] syllables are placed in the proper region, clear, distinct, complete, and well-articulated. (53)

body.text: samantaprāsādikatvādasecanakadarśanāḥ || 54 ||
body.translated_text: Because of being universally pleasing, they are of captivating appearance. (54)

body.text: anatihrasvānatidīrghavṛttopacitatrivalivibhūṣitakambugrīvāḥ || 55 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] necks are neither too short nor too long, round, well-proportioned, adorned with three folds, [shaped like] a conch. (55)

body.text: samapramāṇadṛḍhāvakrahrasvavipulacibukāḥ || 56 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] chins are of even proportion, firm, slightly receding, short, and broad. (56)

body.text: bimbaphalātāmranātyāyatasamasnigdharucirauṣṭhāḥ || 57 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] lips are [red] like <s>bimba</s>-fruit, coppery, not overly extended, even, smooth, and beautiful. (57)

body.text: bandhūkapuṣpopamaślakṣṇadaśanamāṃsāḥ || 58 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] gums are like <s>bandhūka</s> flowers, smooth. (58)

body.text: śucisnigdhaspaṣṭaracanākṣīṇadantāḥ || 59 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] teeth are clean, smooth, clear in arrangement, and unworn. (59)

body.text: anupūrvavṛttasnigdhatīkṣṇasamasitadaṃṣṭrāḥ || 60 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] canine teeth are in proper sequence, round, smooth, sharp, even, and white. (60)

body.text: saprayojanadakṣiṇadantaraśmipradarśitamuhūrtasmitāḥ || 61 ||
body.translated_text: [They show] a momentary smile with a purpose, [displaying] rays of light from the right-side teeth. (61)

body.text: apamalamṛdutāmrasnigdhajihvāḥ || 62 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] tongues are spotless, soft, coppery, and smooth. (62)

body.text: nityoṣṇaślakṣṇamāṃsajālagajatālusamavarṇatālavaḥ || 63 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] palates are always warm, smooth, fleshy, webbed, [shaped like] an elephant's palate, and of even color. (63)

body.text: dhuroccāyatasaṃgatatuṅganāsāḥ || 64 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] noses are prominent, tall, well-joined, and elevated. (64)

body.text: aghanamṛdudṛḍhamūlasnigdhatanunīlakuṇḍalitasmaśruvaḥ || 65 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] beards are not dense, soft, firm-rooted, smooth, thin, dark, and curly. (65)

body.text: anunnatātīkṣṇamāṃsalamārṣṭipiṇḍitagaṇḍāḥ || 66 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] cheeks are not protruding, not sharp, fleshy, clean, full, and rounded. (66)

body.text: ādarśasamopacitāślatharucirakapolāḥ || 67 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] cheekbones are mirror-like, well-filled, firm, and beautiful. (67)

body.text: pīnāyatasamānopahatacārukarṇāḥ || 68 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] ears are full, extended, even, undamaged, and lovely. (68)

body.text: lalāṭakarṇagaṇḍasandhiśleṣānimnapūrṇacandrākṛtiśaṅkhāḥ || 69 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] temples — at the juncture of forehead, ears, and cheeks — are neither depressed [nor protruding], full, and of moon-like conch shape. (69)

body.text: viśālāyatasnigdhamadhuraprasannasamanetrāḥ || 70 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] eyes are wide, extended, smooth, sweet, clear, and even. (70)

body.text: prahasitāñcitāgrapakṣmāṇaḥ || 71 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] eyelashes are curved upward at the tips, like those of one smiling. (71)

body.text: somyabhrājiṣṇusthiravisandhidṛṣṭayaḥ || 72 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] gaze is gentle, radiant, steady, and without breaks. (72)

body.text: aparimitabalatvādapagatonmeṣanimeṣāḥ || 73 ||
body.translated_text: Because of unlimited power, they are free from blinking. (73)

body.text: dīrghāsitaślakṣṇānupūrvavartitasnigdhatanubhruvaḥ || 74 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] eyebrows are long, dark, smooth, in proper sequence, well-formed, smooth, and thin. (74)

body.text: kāñcanapaṭṭaślakṣṇārdhacandrākṛtivipulalalāṭāḥ || 75 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] foreheads are smooth like a golden plate, broad, of half-moon shape. (75)

body.text: paripūrṇacandramaṇḍalasamavadanāḥ || 76 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] faces are like a full moon-disc, even. (76)

body.text: ekaghanavajrasaṃhataśiraskapālāḥ || 77 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] skull-bones are like a single, compact, and diamond-hard [mass]. (77)

body.text: suparipūrṇacchatrākṛtiśirasaḥ || 78 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] heads are beautifully rounded, of parasol-like shape. (78)

body.text: ślakṣṇacitāsaṃluḍitapalitadoṣāpanatabhramarābhasnigdhamṛdusubaddhamūlasurabhisvastikanandyāvartākṛtikeśaracanāḥ || 79 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] hair is smooth, dense, unwithered, free from the fault of graying, dark as a black bee, lustrous, soft, well-rooted, fragrant, and arranged in <s>svastika</s> and <s>nandyāvarta</s> patterns. (79)

body.text: sasurāsuramanujādilokānavalokitamūrdhānaḥ || 80 ||
body.translated_text: [Their] heads are not [fully] seen even by the world including gods, <s>asuras</s>, and humans. (80)

body.text: atha tadādyaṃ bodhicittaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dāḍharyeṇa kathamiva draṣṭavyam ? naitallaukikena vastunopapādayituṃ śakyam | kasmāt ? yataḥ
body.translated_text: Now, how should that initial awakening-mind (<s>bodhicitta</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> be viewed with regard to its firmness? This cannot be illustrated by any worldly thing. Why? Because:

children.translated_text: By the wind at the end of an aeon, <s>Meru</s> [is destroyed]; by fire, the ocean;

children.text: vajreṇa dhvasyate vajramavikāri tu tanmanaḥ // Abhidh-d_228 //
children.translated_text: by a thunderbolt, a diamond is shattered — but that mind remains unaltered. (Abhidh-d 228)

body.text: kiṃ paryāpannam, katarat, kati prakāram, kiṃ purassaram, kasminvā kāle ko vā tadutpādayati ? ityetadapadiśyate -
body.translated_text: In what is it included, which [mind] is it, how many kinds does it have, what precedes it, at what time, and who generates it? This is now indicated:

children.translated_text: It belongs to the desire-realm, is born of the sixth [consciousness], is threefold; compassion and faith precede it in succession;

children.text: buddhotpāde naraḥ strī vā tadādyaṃ cittamaśnute // Abhidh-d_229 //
children.translated_text: at the arising of a Buddha, a man or woman attains that initial mind. (Abhidh-d 229)

body.text: tatkhalu bodhicittamādyaṃ kāmadhātuparyāpannameva | ṣaṣṭhajaṃ manodhātujamityarthaḥ | triprakāramupapattilābhikaṃ śrutamayaṃ cintāmayaṃ ceti | kṛpāpurassareṇa śraddhābahulena ca manaskāreṇa saṃprayuktam | buddhotpāda eva nāsati buddhaśāsane | manuṣyo vā strī votpādayati nānya iti |
body.translated_text: That initial awakening-mind indeed belongs only to the desire-realm. 'Born of the sixth' means born of the <s>manodhātu</s> (mind-element). It is of three kinds: that obtained at birth (<s>upapatilābhika</s>), that which arises from learning (<s>śrutamaya</s>), and that which arises from reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>). It is associated with attention preceded by compassion and abundant in faith. [It arises] only at the arising of a Buddha, not when there is no Buddha's teaching. A human male or female generates it — no other [being].

body.text: tasyāsya bodhibījasthānīyasya cittaratnasya sarvadhātugativyāpibuddhatvamahāvṛkṣāṅkurābhivṛddhaye bhūmijalasekādihetupratyayasthānīyān prajñādicaturadhiṣṭhānaparivārānpāramitādyānguṇānvakṣyamāṇasvarūpānbodhisattvaḥ krameṇābhyasyati |
body.translated_text: For the growth of the great tree-sprout of Buddhahood, which pervades all realms and destinies, from this jewel-mind that stands as the seed of awakening — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gradually cultivates the qualities such as the <s>pāramitās</s> and others (whose nature will be described), together with their retinue of the four bases (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) beginning with wisdom, which serve as the conditions of soil, water-sprinkling, and the like.

body.text: kathaṃ punaḥ krameṇa dānādipāramitānāṃ paripūrirbhavati ? tatra tāvat-
body.translated_text: How then does the gradual perfection of the <s>pāramitās</s> beginning with giving occur? First, regarding that —

body.text: sarvebhyaḥ sarvadā sarvaṃ vadato dānapūraṇam /
body.translated_text: Giving everything to everyone at all times — that is the completion of generosity.

body.text: prathame khalvasaṃkhyeye vartamāno bodhisattvaḥ na sarvasmai nāpi sarvaṃ na sarvadā dadāti | dvitīye sarvasmai sarvadā natu sarvam | tṛtīye sarvai sarvasmai sarvadā ca prayacchati | iyatā dānapāramitā paripūrṇā bhavati |
body.translated_text: In the first incalculable [aeon], while still practicing, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not give to everyone, nor everything, nor at all times. In the second, [he gives] to everyone and at all times, but not everything. In the third, he gives everything to everyone at all times. By this much, the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) is completed.

body.text: maraṇe 'pi damātyāgaḥ śīlasyotkṛṣṭirucyate // Abhidh-d_230 //
body.translated_text: Not abandoning self-discipline even in death is declared to be the excellence of morality. (Abhidh-d 230)

body.text: yadā punaḥ prāṇaparityāgenāpi prāṇātipātādiśikṣāpadaṃ na kṣobhayati, iyatā śīlapāramitā paripūrṇā veditavyā | krauñcādirājaduhitābhikṣudṛṣṭāntāścātrodāhāryāḥ |
body.translated_text: When, moreover, even at the cost of [his] life, he does not violate the training-rules (<s>śikṣāpada</s>) beginning with abstaining from killing — by this much, the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) should be understood as completed. The examples of the <s>Krauñca</s>-[bird], the king's daughter, and the monk should be cited here.

body.text: vīryasya tiṣyasaṃstutyā dhiyo vajropamātparam /
body.translated_text: For vigor — by the praise of [Buddha] <s>Tiṣya</s>; for wisdom — from beyond the diamond-like [concentration].

body.text: bhagavantaṃ khalu tiṣyaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ ekayā gāthayā ekapādena sthitvā saptāhamabhiṣṭhuvataḥ śākyamunervīyapāramitā paripūrṇā nava ca kalpāḥ pratyudāvartitāḥ |
body.translated_text: Indeed, when <s>Śākyamuni</s> praised the Blessed One <s>Tiṣya</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, standing on one foot, with a single verse for seven days — his perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) was completed, and nine aeons were turned back.

body.text: prajñāpāramitāyāstu vajropamātsamādherurdhvaṃ kṣayajñāne paripūrirbhavati |
body.translated_text: But the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) is completed in the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) above the diamond-like concentration (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>).

body.text: 'sarvāsāṃ tu kṣayajñāne paripūrirvidhīyate'; // Abhidh-d_231 //
body.translated_text: 'But the completion of all [perfections] is ordained in the knowledge of destruction.' (Abhidh-d 231)

body.text:
ityāgamaḥ |
atra punaḥ "kṣāntidhyānapāramite śīlaprajñāparivāratvānnārthāntaram" iti vaibhāṣikāḥ | vinayadharavaibhāṣikāstu vinaye catasraḥ pāramitāḥ paṭhanti |
body.translated_text: Thus is the scriptural authority. Here, moreover, the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> [say]: 'The perfections of patience and meditation (<s>kṣāntidhyānapāramitā</s>), being attendants of morality and wisdom, are not separate [perfections].' But the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> who are Vinaya-holders recite four <s>pāramitās</s> in the <s>Vinaya</s>.

body.text: atra punaḥ kecid buddhavacane bahiṣkṛtabuddhayaḥ prāhuḥ- "na hi piṭakatraye bhagavatā bodhisattvamārga upadiṣṭaḥ |" ta evaṃ vyāhartavyāḥ | bhrāntā hyatra bhavantaḥ | yasmāt
body.translated_text: Here, moreover, certain ones whose understanding of the Buddha's word is excluded say: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> path was not taught by the Blessed One in the three baskets (<s>piṭakatraya</s>).' They should be addressed thus: 'You are indeed confused in this matter.' Because:

children.translated_text: The three bases of merit, the teaching of the means of their attainment, and the like;
likewise the four bases (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), the teaching of the seven true dharmas; (Abhidh-d 232)
the seven applications (<s>yoga</s>), the three aggregates [of training] (<s>skandha</s>), the three trainings (<s>triśikṣā</s>), and the like are taught;
likewise, four <s>pāramitās</s> are also stated in the <s>Vinaya</s>. (Abhidh-d 233)

body.text: bodhipakṣyāśca kaṇṭhoktāḥ saptatriṃśatsvayaṃbhuvā /
body.translated_text: The thirty-seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>) are expressly stated by the Self-Arisen One (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>);

body.text: hetavaḥ sarvabodhināṃ trividhā mṛdutādibhiḥ // Abhidh-d_234 //
body.translated_text: the causes of all [types of] awakening are threefold, by [the distinction of] mild and the rest. (Abhidh-d 234)

children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no path to awakening other than the three baskets of <s>sūtras</s> and the rest.
Whoever here says otherwise would be one who speaks <s>Māra</s>'s words. (Abhidh-d 235)

body.text: uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "yadbhikṣavaḥ sūtrenāvatarati, vinayena dṛśyate, dharmatāṃ ca vilomayati nedaṃ śāstuḥ śāsanam" iti kṛṣṇāpadeśaḥ | śuklāpadeśoviparyayeṇa | yatkhalu sūtraṃ bhagavatā buddhena bhāṣitaṃ taccaturṣvāgameṣu sthaviramahākāśyapasthavirānandādibhiḥ saṃgītikartṛbhirūddānagāthābhirnibaddhaṃ tadeva grāhyam | gatametat |
body.translated_text: For the Blessed One said: 'Monks, what does not accord with the <s>sūtra</s>, is not found in the <s>Vinaya</s>, and contradicts the nature of dharmas — this is not the Teacher's teaching' — this is the 'dark indication.' The 'bright indication' is the reverse. What was spoken by the Blessed One, the Buddha, as <s>sūtra</s> — that alone, which was codified with <s>uddāna</s> (summary) verses by the compilers of the councils, the elders <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, and others, in the four <s>Āgamas</s>, should be accepted. This has been covered.

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | katameṣāṃ kalpānāmasaṃkhyeyatrayeṇa buddhatvaṃ prāpyate ?
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: Through how many sets of three incalculable aeons is Buddhahood attained?

body.text: kalpānāṃ mahatāmetadasaṃkhyeyatrayaṃ matam /
body.translated_text: This set of three incalculable [aeons] is held to be of great aeons.

body.text: kalpānāṃ yadi saṃkhyā na vidyate kathaṃ tarhi trayamiti nirdhāryate ? na khalu saṃkhyā na vidyate | kiṃ tarhi ?
body.translated_text: If there is no number of aeons, how then is the triad determined? It is not that there is no number. What then?

body.text: sthānāntaramasaṃkhyākhyamadaḥsaṃkhyopari sthitam // Abhidh-d_236 //
body.translated_text: There is a numerical place called '<s>asaṃkhya</s>' (incalculable), situated above [the number designated by] that many calculations. (Abhidh-d 236)

body.text: sthānāntaraviśeṣasya khalvetannāmāsaṃkhyeyamiti | na tu na saṃkhyā vidyata ityetadvivakṣitam |
body.translated_text: Indeed, '<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>' is the name of a particular numerical place. It is not intended to mean that no number exists.

body.text: atha yaṃ śākyamunirbhagavānsamyaksaṃbuddho bodhisattvacaryāyāmeṣu triṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu kiyatāṃ buddhānāṃ paryupāsāṃ cakre ? tadatra varṇayanti | prathame 'saṃkhyeye pañcasaptatisahasrāṇi | dvitīye ṣaṭsaptatim | tṛtīye saptasaptatim |
body.translated_text: Now, during the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice of <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Blessed One, the Perfectly Awakened One, through these three incalculable [aeons], how many Buddhas did he attend upon? This they describe: In the first incalculable [aeon], seventy-five thousand. In the second, seventy-six thousand. In the third, seventy-seven thousand.

body.text: kasya punaḥ kalpāsaṃkhyeyasyāvasāne katamo buddho babhūva ? atrāpi varṇayanti | ratnaśikhini samyaksaṃbuddhe prathamo 'saṃkhyeyaḥ samāptaḥ | bhagavati dīpaṅkare dvitīyaḥ | bhagavati vipaśyini tṛtīyaḥ samāptaḥ |
body.translated_text: At the end of which incalculable aeon did which Buddha appear? This too they describe: At [the time of] the Perfectly Awakened <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the first incalculable [aeon] was completed. Under the Blessed <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>, the second. Under the Blessed <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the third was completed.

body.text: kasminpunaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhe buddhatve prathamaṃ cittamutpāditam ? śākyamunī | śākyamunirnāma prathamasyāsaṃkhyeyasyādau babhūva yatra bhagavatā bhārgavabhūtena sukhodakenāṅgaparicaryābhirupasthānaṃ kṛtvā prathamaṃ bodhicittamutpāditamahamapyevaṃ prakāro bhūyāsamiti |
body.translated_text: Under which Perfectly Awakened One was the first awakening-mind generated? [Under] <s>Śākyamuni</s>. [A Buddha named] <s>Śākyamuni</s> appeared at the beginning of the first incalculable [aeon], under whom the Blessed One — who was then the [brahmin] <s>Bhārgava</s> — having attended upon him with warm water and the service of [massaging his] limbs, generated the first awakening-mind: 'May I too become one of such a kind.'

body.text: prabhāseturājani tadeva punardraḍhimānamāpāditamiti ||
body.translated_text: Under [the Buddha] <s>Prabhāsa</s> in the [city of] <s>Rāja</s>, that very [resolve] was further strengthened.

body.text: kasminpunaḥ kāle buddhā bhagavanto buddhādityāḥ prādurbhavanti ? tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: Now, at what time do the Blessed Ones, the sun-like Buddhas, appear? That is now commenced:

children.translated_text: The arising of Conquerors occurs in the [period of] decline, down to [a lifespan of] one hundred years;
of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> in both [periods]; of universal monarchs (<s>cakravartins</s>) in the [period of] increase. (Abhidh-d 237)

body.text: kalpāpakarṣe khalu buddhānāmutpattirbhavati | utkarṣe cāpakarṣe ca pratyekajinānām | utkarṣa eva cakravartinām ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, the arising of Buddhas occurs during the decline of an aeon. [The arising] of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> occurs in both the increase and the decline. [The arising] of universal monarchs occurs only during the increase.

body.text: cakravartināṃ punarayaṃ niyamaḥ-
body.translated_text: For universal monarchs, moreover, there is this restriction:

body.text: nādho 'śītisahasrāyostatsamutpattiriṣyate /
body.translated_text: Their arising is not accepted [when the lifespan is] below eighty thousand [years].

body.text: aśītibarṣasahasrāyurbhyaścakravartināmūrdhvamutpattirbhavati nādha iti |
body.translated_text: [When the lifespan is] eighty thousand years and above, the arising of universal monarchs occurs — not below that.

body.text: te hemarūpyatāmrāyaścakrāḥ puṇyaprabhāvataḥ // Abhidh-d_238 //
body.translated_text: They [have] wheels of gold, silver, copper — through the power of merit. (Abhidh-d 238)

body.text: caturvidhāḥ khalu cakravartinaḥ- sauvarṇacakrāḥ, rūpyacakrāḥ, tāmracakrāḥ, lohitacakrāśca svapuṇyaprakarṣāditi | yathākramaṃ caite catustridvyekadvīpeśvarāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, universal monarchs are fourfold: those with a golden wheel, those with a silver wheel, those with a copper wheel, and those with an iron wheel — due to the superior degree of their own merit. And these are, respectively, lords of four, three, two, and one continent.

body.text: atha yaduktam- 'tasmānna bodhimārgo 'nyaḥ sūtrādipiṭakatrayāt |'; iti | yadi tarhi mārgabhedo nāsti buddhapratyekabuddhaśrāvakānāṃ phalabhedenāpi tarhi na bhavitavyam | naiṣa doṣaḥ | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Now, regarding what was stated — 'There is no path to awakening other than the three baskets of <s>sūtras</s> and the rest' — if there is no difference in the path of Buddhas, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s>, then there should be no difference in fruit either. This is no fault. Because:

children.translated_text: Even though the means of accomplishment is the same, the difference [in fruit] arises from the difference of faculties and the like —
like the difference in the fruit of giving by two mothers who seek [respectively] worldly existence and liberation. (Abhidh-d 239)

body.text: yāvatkhalu kaścidguṇaḥ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya bhagavatā deśito vinirmuktidvayaprāptihetubhūtaḥ sarvo 'sau piṭakatrayānuvartī | tatpunarvimuktidvayaṃ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 204)

children.text: ) tribhiḥ pudgalaiḥ prāpyate | bhagavatā samyaksaṃbuddhena pratyekajinenāryaśrāvakeṇa ca | teṣāṃ punastulye bodhivartmani patitānāmindriyapraṇidhānāvaraṇabhedādbhedaḥ | tadyathā dvayormātrostulyaṃ vastu tulye kṣetre pratipādayatoścetanāviśeṣādatulyaṃ (
children.translated_text: is attained by three [types of] persons: the Blessed One, the Perfectly Awakened Buddha; the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>; and the noble <s>Śrāvaka</s>. For these, though fallen on the same path to awakening, the difference arises from the difference in faculties, aspirations (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), and obscurations (<s>āvaraṇa</s>). Just as, for two mothers giving the same thing in the same field, there is an unequal
(Jaini 205)

children.text: ) phalaṃ bhavati, tadvaduttamārthaṃ prārthayamānānāṃ trayāṇāmapi pudgalānāṃ praṇidhānendriyasatataghananirantarabhāvanāprayogapaṭutvābhyāsādiviśeṣāttulye 'pi mārge patitānāṃ kaścitphalaviśeṣo bhavati |
children.translated_text: fruit due to the difference in their volition — so too, for the three types of persons who aspire to the supreme goal, though they have fallen on the same path, there is some difference in fruit due to differences in aspiration, faculty-intensity, continuous dense uninterrupted cultivation, effort, skill of practice, and the like.

body.translated_text: Indeed, whatever quality the Blessed One taught after fully awakening to perfect enlightenment, which serves as the cause for attaining the two kinds of liberation — all of that follows the three baskets. That twofold liberation, moreover,

body.text: itaśca
body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: Through the predominance of cultivating compassion, [there is the Buddha]; of one's own realization and [its] mind, likewise;
of realization through another, and of the teacher — that difference is accordingly ordained. (Abhidh-d 240)

body.text: tatra bhagavato buddhasya karuṇābhāvanā codrekena vartate bhagavānbuddhaḥ | svasaṃviccintā ca pratyekabuddhasyādhikyena vartate | parasaṃvitparato ghoṣaśca śrāvakasya | kiñca, parato ghoṣamantareṇāpi carame janmani suyoniśomanaskārabalena hetupratyayaphalāvabodhopalambhāt, hetupratyayabalairaśeṣapranaṣṭaṃ niśreyasaṃ mārgaṃ prathamamadhigamya paratropadeśādityevamādi ||
body.translated_text: There, the Blessed Buddha's cultivation of compassion operates with predominance — [hence he is] the Blessed Buddha. The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>'s self-realization (<s>svasaṃvid</s>) and [personal] contemplation operate with predominance. For the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, realization from another and [hearing] the teacher's voice [are predominant]. Moreover, even without hearing another's voice, in the final birth, through the power of thorough proper attention (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>), one comprehends cause, condition, and fruit — [yet] having first attained the supreme path of welfare through the power of causes and conditions [with the complete destruction of all defilements], and then instructing others — thus and so on.

body.text: atha tulyāyāṃ vimuktau sthitānāṃ trayāṇāmabhisametṛṇāṃ ko viśeṣaḥ ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now, for the three who have directly realized, who abide in the same liberation — what is the distinction? That is stated:

children.translated_text: The greatness of the Teacher, arising from cause, truth, and fruit, is threefold —
Even when liberation is equal [for all three — <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and Buddhas], because of the attainment of enlightenment by the three — (Abhidh-d 241)

body.text: tatra hetukṛtaṃ tāvadbhagavato buddhasya mahattvaṃ triṣu kalpāsaṃkhyeyeṣu sūtravinayābhidharmālokena vineyajanamanograheṣvajñānatimirotsādanāt | svabhāvakṛtamapi balavaiśāradyasmṛtyupasthānamahākaruṇādisvarūpatvāt | phalakṛtamapi (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 208)
because of the establishment of his unimpeded teaching in the worlds including the gods, and because of his victory over the four <s>Māras</s>.

body.translated_text: In that regard, first, the greatness of the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> produced by cause [consists in] the dispelling of the darkness of ignorance through the light of <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Abhidharma</s> for the mental receptivity of beings to be trained, over three incalculable aeons. [His greatness] produced by intrinsic nature [is] because of having as his essential nature the powers (<s>bala</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and the rest. [His greatness] produced by fruit [is]

body.text: atha yadetatsarvasattvaprativiśiṣṭaṃ puruṣottamasya janmaśarīraṃ tatkimaniyatakālākṣepam, āhosvinniyatakālākṣepamiti ? tadabhidhīyate-
body.translated_text: Now, regarding this birth-body of the Supreme Person (<s>puruṣottama</s>), which is distinguished from all beings — is it projected at an indeterminate time, or at a determinate time? That is stated:

body.text: buddhasya saṃmukhīnasya bauddhamākṣipyate vapuḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha's</s> body is projected when he is face-to-face [with a previous <s>Buddha</s>].

body.text: nānyasminkāle | cintāmayena jñānena viśiṣṭatamatvāt | tatra punaḥ-
body.translated_text: Not at any other time — because the wisdom born of contemplation (<s>cintāmaya jñāna</s>) is then most distinguished. Furthermore, regarding that:

body.text: saikapuṇyaśatodbhūtamekaikaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ muneḥ // Abhidh-d_242 //
body.translated_text: Each mark of the Sage arises from a hundred merits. (Abhidh-d 242)

body.text: tatra pañcāśaccetanāḥ prayogabhūtāḥ pañcāśatpṛṣṭhabhūtāḥ, ekayā tallakṣaṇamākṣipati ||
body.translated_text: Therein, fifty volitions (<s>cetanās</s>) are the preparatory [phase] and fifty are the subsequent [phase]; by one [additional volition] that mark is projected.

body.text: tā punaḥ pañcāśaccetanāḥ katamāḥ ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now what are those fifty volitions? That is stated:

body.text: yathākarmapathāstadvatpuṇyāditrayamiṣyate /
body.translated_text: Just as the courses of action, so the three — merit and the rest — are held. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: pratikarmapathaṃ pañca, maulakarmapathapariśuddhiḥ sāmantakasyavitarkānupaghātaḥ smṛtyanuparigrahaḥ, nirvāṇapariṇāmanaṃ ca | tāḥ sarvāstadālamvanāḥ pañcāśatprayogabhūtāḥ | pṛṣṭhe 'pyetāvatya eva |
body.translated_text: Per course of action there are five: purification of the principal course of action, non-affliction by <s>vitarka</s> (discursive thought) in the preparatory [stage], maintenance of mindfulness, and dedication toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. All of these, having that [mark] as their object, are the fifty preparatory [volitions]. In the subsequent [phase] also, there are exactly this many.

body.text: anye tu bruvate- buddhā dviśarīrādhiṣṭhānāḥ | janmaśarīrādhiṣṭhānāḥ, dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇālambanāḥ | dharmaśarīrādhiṣṭhānāścāṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhaguṇālambanāḥ sāmantakapṛṣṭhasaṃgṛhītāḥ |
body.translated_text: Others, however, say: <s>Buddhas</s> have two bodies as their basis — the birth-body (<s>janmaśarīra</s>) basis, having the thirty-two marks of a great person as their object; and the dharma-body (<s>dharmaśarīra</s>) basis, having the eighteen special <s>Buddha</s>-qualities as their object, included in the preparatory and subsequent [phases].

body.text: anye punarāhuḥ- prāṇivadhaviraticetanā mṛdumadhyādhimātrādhimātrataratamabhedāddevamanuṣyeṣu yojyā |
body.translated_text: Yet others say: The volition of abstaining from killing, through the gradation of mild, middling, intense, more intense, and most intense, is to be applied to gods and humans [respectively].

body.text: kecinmantrayante- dvidhā samudrāścatvāro dvīpāḥ ṣoḍaśanarakāḥ, tiryakpretau ṣaṭkāmāvacarāviṃśatīrūpārūpyāḥ devāḥ | etānsarvān bhagavān karuṇāyate |
body.translated_text: Some maintain: There are two oceans, four continents, sixteen hells, the animal realm and the hungry ghost realm, six desire-realm [heavens], and twenty form and formless gods. The Blessed One has compassion for all of these.

body.text: evantu varṇayanti- sannikṛṣṭaṃ bodhisattvaṃ sthāpayitvā yatsarvasattvānāṃ bhogaiśvaryādhipatyaphalamiyadekasya puṇyasya pramāṇam ||
body.translated_text: And they describe it thus: Setting aside the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is close [to Buddhahood], whatever is the fruit of enjoyment, sovereignty, and dominion of all beings — that is the measure of one [such] merit.

body.text: atha yaduktam- 'dānapāramitā'; iti | tatra kaḥ samāsaḥ kiṃ sādhano vā dānaśabdaḥ, ko vā svabhāvo dānasya iti ? tadapadiśyate | dānasya pāramitāyā niścayabuddhiḥ sā dānapāramitā | evaṃ śeṣāsvapi vācyam |
body.translated_text: Now, regarding what was said — '<s>dānapāramitā</s>' (perfection of giving) — what is the compound analysis there? What is the denotation of the word '<s>dāna</s>' (giving)? Or what is the essential nature of giving? That is indicated. The definitive understanding of the <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) of <s>dāna</s> (giving) is <s>dānapāramitā</s>. The same should be said for the remaining [perfections] as well.

body.text: yatpunarucyate- 'kiṃ sādhano vāyaṃ dānaśabdaḥ, ko vā dānasya svabhāvaḥ'; iti tatrāpadiśyate-
body.translated_text: Regarding the further question — 'What is the denotation of the word <s>dāna</s>, or what is the essential nature of giving?' — that is now indicated:

body.text: dānaṃ hi dīyate yena svaparārthādyapekṣayā // Abhidh-d_243 //
body.translated_text: Giving is that by which something is given, with regard to one's own benefit, another's benefit, and so forth. (Abhidh-d 243)

body.text: kāyādikarma tattattvamavijñaptiḥ kvacitpunaḥ /
body.translated_text: The action of body and the rest is its nature; in some cases, it is <s>avijñapti</s> (unmanifest form).

body.text: karaṇasādhano 'yaṃ dānaśabda | dīyate teneti dānaṃ mānavat | hastādiṣu tarhi dānaprasaṃgaḥ | astu tarhi karmasādhano dīyate taditi dānam | suvarṇādiṣu dānaprasaṃgaḥ | bhavatu ko doṣaḥ | vipākaphalābhāvaḥ, suvarṇādīnāmavyākṛtatvāt | bhavatu tarhi karaṇasādhana eva | nanūktaṃ hastādiṣu prasaṃgaḥ ? naiṣa doṣaḥ | kuśalakarmatrayaparigrahāt | spardhāyaśoguptisevādivyudāsārthamidamārabhyate | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 211)

children.text: ) 'svaparārthādyapekṣayā'- svātmaparārthānugrahādyapekṣayā | svātmānugrahāya parānugrahāya ubhayānugrahāya |ādiśabdāt pūjākāmyayā ceti | svabhāvo 'pi 'kāyādikarmāvijñaptiḥ'; | kvacitpunaḥ kāyavāṅmanaḥ karma | sasaṃprayogaṃ saparivāraṃ cātra manaskarma dṛṣṭavyam | tatpunaretaddānam-
children.translated_text: 'With regard to one's own benefit, another's benefit, and so forth' — with regard to benefiting oneself, benefiting others, and benefiting both. The word 'and so forth' includes: for the purpose of worship. The essential nature is also 'action of body and the rest, and <s>avijñapti</s>.' In some cases, it is the action of body, speech, and mind. Here, mental action should be understood as including its associated [mental factors] and its retinue. Furthermore, this giving —

body.translated_text: This word '<s>dāna</s>' has the instrument as its derivation — 'that by which one gives is <s>dāna</s>' — like the word <s>māna</s> (measure). Then there would be the absurd consequence that hands and the like are '<s>dāna</s>.' Let it then have the action as its derivation — 'what is given is <s>dāna</s>.' Then there would be the absurd consequence that gold and the like are '<s>dāna</s>.' So be it — what is the fault? The absence of maturation-fruit, since gold and the like are morally indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>). Let it then indeed have the instrument as its derivation. But was it not said that there is the absurd consequence regarding hands and the like? This is not a fault — because of the inclusion within the three wholesome actions. To exclude rivalry, shame, concealment, service, and the like, this [definition] is undertaken.

body.text: prādhānyānmuninā proktaṃ mahābhogaphalaṃ hi tat // Abhidh-d_244 //
body.translated_text: was declared by the Sage as pre-eminent, because its fruit is great enjoyment. (Abhidh-d 244)

body.text: svargāvapargahetutve 'pi prādhānyānmahābhogatāyāṃ tadviniyogaḥ | tatpunaretaddānam-
body.translated_text: Even though [giving] is a cause of heaven and liberation, because of pre-eminence, its application is for great enjoyment. Furthermore, this giving —

children.translated_text: Some give for the accomplishment of their own, others', or both purposes; (Abhidh-d 245)
others for following virtuous conduct, and some not for both purposes.

body.text: dvābhyāṃ khalu kāraṇābhyāṃ svānyātmahitacikīrṣuśca, ubhayahitapratipannaśca sa evaṃguṇayuktaṃ dānaṃ dadāti | ātmanaśca kuśalamūlopacayārthaṃ parasya cendriyamahābhūtopacayārtham | tatra svahitāyaiva yathā pṛthagjanaḥ parinirvate bhagavati caityāya dadāti parārthameva yathā arhan saṃghāya dadāti, na ceṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ bhavati | ubhayārthaṃ yadavītarāgaḥ saṃghāya dadāti | nobhayārthaṃ yadarhaṃścaityāya dadāti tacca na dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ bhavati kevalaṃ tu satpuruṣapraśastamārgāvasthānapradarśanārtham ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, for two reasons — desiring one's own welfare and being established in the welfare of both — one endowed with such qualities gives. For the accumulation of wholesome roots for oneself, and for the accumulation of sense-faculties and great elements for the other. Therein, for one's own welfare alone — as when an ordinary person gives to a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) after the Blessed One has passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>. For another's welfare alone — as when an <s>Arhat</s> gives to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and that does not become [karma] to be experienced in this very life. For both purposes — when one not yet free from passion gives to the <s>Saṃgha</s>. For neither purpose — when an <s>Arhat</s> gives to a <s>caitya</s>, and that does not become [karma] to be experienced in this very life — but merely for the purpose of demonstrating adherence to the path praised by noble persons.

body.text: tatpunaretaddānaṃ kathaṃ phalato viśiṣyate ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now, how is this giving distinguished in terms of its fruit? That is stated:

body.text: dātṛvastvādivaiśiṣṭyāttatphalātiśayaḥ smṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text: The excellence of its fruit is held to be due to the distinction of the giver, the gift, and the recipient. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: tatra kathaṃ dātṛviśeṣaḥ kathaṃ vastuviśeṣaḥ kathaṃ kṣetraviśeṣaḥ ?
body.translated_text: Therein, how is the giver distinguished? How is the gift distinguished? How is the recipient (<s>kṣetra</s>, field) distinguished?

body.text: śraddhādibhirguṇairdātā datte 'taḥ satkriyādibhiḥ // Abhidh-d_246 //
body.translated_text: The giver gives endowed with qualities such as faith and the rest, and with respect and the like. (Abhidh-d 246)

body.text: yadā dātā hetuphalasaṃbandhaniścaye śraddadhāno dadāti śīlavān kalyāṇadharmā buddhavacanabahuśrutaśca bhavati nirmatsarī muktahastaśca bhavati nirvāṇānuśaṃsaḥ satkṛtya svahastaṃ kālena parānanupahatya dadāti, sa khalu
body.translated_text: When the giver gives with faith in the connection between cause and fruit, is endowed with moral discipline, possesses wholesome qualities, has learned much of the <s>Buddha's</s> word, is free from jealousy, is open-handed, has <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as his reward, gives respectfully, with his own hand, at the proper time, and without harming others — he indeed

body.text: satkārādiguṇopetaṃ phalaṃ tasmādavāpnute /
body.translated_text: obtains fruit endowed with qualities such as respect and the rest.

body.text: ataḥ satkṛtya dānātsatkāralābhī bhavati | svahastadānādudāreṣu bhogaparibhogeṣu ruciṃ labhate | kāladānātkālabhogāna labhate | parānupaghātādanācchedyāṃllabhate nirapakṣālamanyādibhirasādhāraṇān | etāvaddātā viśiṣyate |
body.translated_text: Therefore, from giving with respect, one obtains respect. From giving with one's own hand, one obtains enjoyment of excellent pleasures. From giving at the proper time, one obtains enjoyments at the right time. From giving without harming others, one obtains [wealth] that cannot be taken away, unshared, and free from hostility and the like. This is how the giver is distinguished.

body.text: kathaṃ vastu ?
body.translated_text: How is the gift [distinguished]?

body.text: vastu varṇādisaṃpannaṃ saurūpyādi phalapradam // Abhidh-d_247 //
body.translated_text: A gift endowed with [excellent] color and the rest yields beauty and similar fruits. (Abhidh-d 247)

body.text: yadi vastu varṇagandharasasparśasampannaṃ bhavati tadā viśiṣyate | tataḥ surupitvaṃ yaśasvitā priyatā sukumāratvaṃ sukhasparśāṅgatā bhavati yathākramam | evaṃ vastu viśiṣṭa bhavati ||
body.translated_text: If the gift is endowed with excellent color, smell, taste, and touch, then it is distinguished. From that, one obtains beauty, fame, belovedness, delicacy, and a body pleasant to touch, respectively. Thus the gift becomes distinguished.

body.text: guṇaduḥkhopakārākhyardharmaiḥ kṣetraṃ viśiṣyate /
body.translated_text: The recipient (<s>kṣetra</s>) is distinguished by qualities, suffering, and helpfulness. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: guṇādhikaṃ kṣetraṃ bhavati | tiryañcamupādāya yāvanmanuṣyāṇāṃ guṇāstaratamakrameṇa yāvadbuddhasya | yathoktam- "tiryagyonigatāya dānaṃ datvā śataguṇo vipākaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyaḥ syāt | duḥśīlāya manuṣyabhūtāya datvā sahasraguṇaḥ |" duḥkhaviśeṣātkṣetraṃ viśiṣyate | yathaupadhikeṣu puṇyakriyāvastuṣu | "glānāya dānaṃ glānopasthāya kāyadānaṃ śītalikāvardalikādiṣu (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 213)

children.text: ) ca dānam" iti vistaraḥ | upakāritvaviśeṣāt | yathā mātāpitroranyeṣāṃ copakāriṇāṃ ye aṭavīdurgakāntāre bhūtavyasanebhyo nistārayanti |
children.translated_text: and so on in detail. By distinction in helpfulness — as with one's mother and father, and other benefactors who rescue one from wilderness, difficulties, desolate regions, and calamities of beings.

body.translated_text: A recipient distinguished by qualities [produces greater merit] — from animals up to humans, qualities [increase] in ascending order, up to the <s>Buddha</s>. As stated: 'Having given a gift to an animal, a hundredfold maturation is to be expected. Having given to a morally deficient human, a thousandfold.' A recipient is distinguished by [degree of] suffering — as in the merit-making bases connected with physical endowment: 'a gift to the sick, bodily service to the sick, and a gift in cold spells, headaches, and the like' —

body.text: yaduktam- 'cetanāviśeṣātphalaviśeṣaḥ'; iti | atha kathaṃ cetanāyāḥ viśeṣo bhavati ? brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: It was said: 'The distinction of fruit [comes] from the distinction of volition.' Now, how does the distinction of volition arise? We say:

body.text: āśayādi mṛdutvādermṛdutvādīni karmaṇaḥ // Abhidh-d_248 //
body.translated_text: From the mildness and the rest of intention and so forth, [come] the mildness and the rest of action. (Abhidh-d 248)

body.text: paṇyāṃ khalu kāraṇānāṃ mṛdutvādiviśeṣātkarma viśiṣyate | āśayacetanāprayogādhiṣṭhānakṣetrapṛṣṭhānāṃ mṛdutvādeḥ karmaviśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Indeed, from the distinction of mildness and the rest among five causes, action becomes distinguished. The distinction of action [arises] from the mildness and the rest of intention (<s>āśaya</s>), volition (<s>cetanā</s>), effort (<s>prayoga</s>), basis (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), field (<s>kṣetra</s>), and subsequent [phase] (<s>pṛṣṭha</s>).

body.text: tatrāśayābhiprāyaḥ yathā- evaṃ caivaṃ ca kuryāṃ kariṣyāmīti vā cetanāyā karmapathaṃ samākṣipati | prayogastadadhiṣṭhānaṃ kāyavākkarma | adhiṣṭhānaṃ karmapathaḥ | kṣetraṃ yasmai vastu pratipādyate | pṛṣṭhaṃ nāma yatkṛtvā punaḥ sakṛdasakṛdvānukaroti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, intention (<s>āśaya</s>) is the mental resolve — such as 'I shall do thus and thus' or 'I will do it.' By the volition, one initiates the course of action. The effort is its basis — the action of body and speech. The basis (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) is the course of action. The field (<s>kṣetra</s>) is the person to whom the gift is given. The subsequent [phase] (<s>pṛṣṭha</s>) is when, having done [something], one does it again, once or repeatedly.

body.text: yaduktam- 'āryebhyo dānamaprameyaphalam'; iti | atha kimanāryebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ prameyam ? netyāha-
body.translated_text: It was said: 'A gift to the Noble Ones (<s>Āryas</s>) yields immeasurable fruit.' Now, is [the fruit of gifts] to all non-noble persons measurable? No — he says:

children.translated_text: To one who teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, to an ignorant person, to one's father, to one's mother, and to a sick person —
a gift to a <s>Bodhisattva</s> and [a gift in] another existence is immeasurable. (Abhidh-d 249)

body.text: ebhyaḥ pañcabhyaḥ pṛthagjanebhyo 'pi dānamaprameyaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: To these five ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjanas</s>) also, giving yields immeasurable [fruit].

body.text: atha kasya kasmai datvā dānamagryaphalaṃ bhavati ? tadabhidhīyate-
body.translated_text: Now, whose gift to whom yields the supreme fruit? That is stated:

children.translated_text: Whatever gift a <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives, and also the eighth [type] by another — (Abhidh-d 250)
that is declared by the wise as supreme, as well as [a gift] from an <s>Arhat</s> to an <s>Arhat</s>.

body.text: yatkhalu bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattvahitādhyāśayeṇa dānaṃ dadāti tadagryamuttamārthaphalatvāt bhagavatāṣṭau khalu dānānyuktāni sūtre "āsādya dānam | bhayadānam | adāt me dānam | dāsyati me dānam | dattapūrvaṃ me pitṛbhirdānam | dadāti svargārtham | kītyartham | yāvaduttāmārthasya prāptaye dadātyetadagryam | yacca traidhātukavītarāgo 'rhannarhate dadāti dānamidamagryam" iti |
body.translated_text: When indeed a <s>Bodhisattva</s> gives with the intention of benefiting all beings, that is supreme, because its fruit is the highest aim. The Blessed One has stated eight [types of] giving in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'giving after approaching; giving out of fear; giving [thinking] "he gave to me"; giving [thinking] "he will give to me"; giving [thinking] "my ancestors used to give"; giving for the sake of heaven; giving for the sake of fame; up to giving for the attainment of the highest aim — this is supreme. And when an <s>Arhat</s> who is free from passion in the three realms gives to an <s>Arhat</s> — this gift is supreme.'

body.text: sūtra uktam- "sāṃcetanikasyāhaṃ karmaṇaḥ kṛtopacitasya nāpratisaṃvedyaphala vadāmi" iti | atha kimidaṃ kṛtamupacitaṃ vā ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: It is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'I do not say that intentional action, performed and accumulated, [bears] no fruit to be experienced.' Now, what is this 'performed' (<s>kṛta</s>) and 'accumulated' (<s>upacita</s>)? That is stated:

children.translated_text: What is initiated after deliberation, strengthened by completion and the rest, (Abhidh-d 251)
and free from its antidote — that action is considered 'accumulated.'

body.text: tatra saṃpradhāryākṣiptaṃ nābuddhipūrvaṃ yadṛcchayā yacca kṛtvā paripūrikābhiścetanābhiḥ paripūritaṃ bhavati | pṛṣṭhataśca dṛḍhīkṛtaṃ bhavayi | niṣkaukṛtyādipratipakṣaṃ ca bhavati | tatkarmopacitamucyate ||
body.translated_text: Therein, 'initiated after deliberation' means not [done] without awareness or accidentally. And when, having performed [it], it is completed by subsequent volitions of fulfillment, and strengthened subsequently, and free from the antidote of remorse and the like — that action is called 'accumulated.'

body.text: kathaṃ caittādiṣvasati pratigṛhītari puṇyopajātirbhavati ? brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: How does merit arise with respect to <s>caityas</s> (shrines) and the like when there is no recipient? We say:

children.translated_text: With respect to <s>caityas</s>, shrine-worship, and the like, looking to one's own quality of relinquishment, (Abhidh-d 252)
even without a recipient, there is fruit — like dwelling in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>).

body.text: tadyathā maitrīvihāriṇo maharṣayo na ca lokaṃ sukhena yojayantyatha cāparimitaṃ puṇyaṃ pratigṛhṇantyevaṃ caityādiṣu tadguṇādhimuktivaśena svacittaprasādādeva puṇyaprasūtimicchanti ||
body.translated_text: Just as the great <s>Ṛṣis</s> who dwell in loving-kindness do not [actually] endow the world with happiness, yet they receive immeasurable merit — similarly, with respect to <s>caityas</s> and the like, through conviction in those [<s>Buddha</s>-]qualities, one expects the generation of merit from the mere purification of one's own mind.

body.text: sūtra uktam- "dve dāne | dharmadānamāmiṣadānaṃ ca |" tatrāmiṣadānamuktam | dharmadānamucyate-
body.translated_text: It is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'There are two [kinds of] giving — the gift of <s>Dharma</s> and the gift of material things.' Therein, the gift of material things has been explained. The gift of <s>Dharma</s> is now stated:

children.translated_text: The essential nature of <s>Dharma</s>-giving is speech; its object is name-bodies and the like. (Abhidh-d 253)
Because of being morally indeterminate in nature, name-bodies and the like are not [<s>Dharma</s>-giving] — just as food and drink are not [material] giving.

body.text: yathaiva kuśalatvāt trikarmasvabhāvamāmiṣadānaṃ nānnapānam | suvarṇādisvabhāvaṃ tat, avyākṛtatvāt | tadvadvācaḥ kuśalatvāddharmadānaṃ vāksvabhāvam | na nāmakāyādisvabhāvam ||
body.translated_text: Just as material giving, being wholesome, has the nature of the three actions [of body, speech, and mind], and is not [of] the nature of food, drink, gold, and the like — because those are morally indeterminate — similarly, because of the wholesomeness of speech, <s>Dharma</s>-giving has the nature of speech, not the nature of name-bodies and the like.

body.text: uktaṃ dānamayaṃ puṇyakriyādivastu | śīlamayamārabhyate |
body.translated_text: The merit-making basis consisting of giving has been stated. The [basis] consisting of moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>) is now commenced.

body.text: śīlaṃ śubhamayaṃ rūpaṃ vyākhyātaṃ tatprabhedataḥ /
body.translated_text: Moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>) is wholesome form (<s>rūpa</s>), and it has been explained according to its divisions. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: kuśalameva rūpaṃ śīlamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu | tatpunarvijñaptyavijñaptirūpam | avijñaptirūpamapi triprabhedaṃ prātimokṣadhyānānāsravasaṃgṛhītam | tadapivyākhyātaṃ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 216)

children.text: ) vistaraśaḥ | etadapi śīlamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu mahābhogatāphalaṃ mokṣaphalaṃ ca, praṇidhipariṇāmanaviśeṣāt |
children.translated_text: in detail. This merit-making basis of moral discipline also has the fruit of great enjoyment and the fruit of liberation, due to the distinction of aspiration and dedication.

body.translated_text: Only wholesome form constitutes the merit-making basis of moral discipline. That, furthermore, consists of manifest (<s>vijñapti</s>) and unmanifest (<s>avijñapti</s>) form. The unmanifest form also has three divisions — included in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>, <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and the uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>) [types]. That also has been explained

body.text: śāstre tu tappradhānatvātproktaṃ svargopapattaye // Abhidh-d_254 //
body.translated_text: But in the <s>Śāstra</s>, because of its pre-eminence [in that regard], it is declared [to lead] to heavenly rebirth. (Abhidh-d 254)

body.text: tatpunaretacchīlaṃ viśuddhaṃ cāviśuddhaṃ ca bhavati | tatra viśuddham
body.translated_text: This morality (<s>śīla</s>), moreover, is both purified and unpurified. Therein, purified [morality is]:

children.translated_text: that which is not corrupted by faults such as immorality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>), unwholesome roots, and the like,
