and which is a factor of the pacification of their counterparts — that is called purified (<s>śuddha</s>) here. (Abhidh-d 255)

body.text: yatkhalu śīlaṃ dauḥśīlyena na vidūṣitaṃ prāṇātipātādināṣṭaprakāreṇa, tatsamutthāpakaiśca kleśopakleśairmithyādṛṣṭyādibhiranupahatam, kleśopakleśavipakṣaiśca smṛtyupasthānādibhiḥ parigṛhetam, nirvāṇapariṇāmitaṃ ca na saṃsārabījabhūtaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: Whatever morality is not corrupted by immorality in the eight forms beginning with killing (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>), and is not damaged by the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>) that originate them — such as wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) and the like — and is embraced by the counterparts of afflictions and secondary afflictions, such as the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) and the like, and is directed toward <s>nirvāṇa</s> — it does not become a seed of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: pañcabhiḥ kāraṇairityanye | maulaiḥ karmapathairviśuddham, sāmantakairviśuddham, vitarkairanupahatam, smṛtyānuparigṛhītam, nirvāṇābhimukha ceti tadviśuddhaśīlamiṣyate | tadviparyayādaviśuddhaṃ veditavyam |
body.translated_text: Others [say it is purified] by five causes: purified by the fundamental courses of action (<s>karmapatha</s>); purified by the adjacent [precepts]; undamaged by applied thoughts (<s>vitarka</s>); embraced by mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>); and directed toward <s>nirvāṇa</s> — that is accepted as purified morality. By the opposite of that, unpurified [morality] should be understood.

body.text: vyākhyātaṃ śīlamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu ||
body.translated_text: The morality-based (<s>śīlamaya</s>) basis of meritorious action (<s>puṇyakriyāvastu</s>) has been explained.

body.text: bhāvanāmayamucyate-
body.translated_text: The meditation-based (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>) [basis] is now stated:

body.text: puṇyaṃ samāhitaṃ tvatra bhāvanā cittabhāvanāt /
body.translated_text: But merit that is concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>) here is called meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), because of the cultivation of consciousness.

body.text: yatsamādhisvabhāvaṃ samāhitaṃ puṇyaṃ tadbhāvanetyucyate | kasmāt ? (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 217)

children.text: ) cittabhāvanāt | yathā tailaṃ puṣpaiścampakādibhirvāsitaṃ tanmayi bhavati tatsamādhisaṃprayuktaistatsahabhūkaiśca dharmaiścittaṃ bhāvitaṃ vāsitamityucyate, tanmayīkaraṇāt | na caivamasamāhitamiti | samāhitameva cittaṃ bhāvanāmayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu maitryādiguṇasaṃprayuktaṃ draṣṭavyam |
children.translated_text: Because of the cultivation of consciousness. Just as oil perfumed with campaka and other flowers becomes imbued with them, so consciousness, cultivated — perfumed — by <s>dharmas</s> associated with <s>samādhi</s> and co-existing with it, is said to be 'cultivated,' because of being made to be imbued [with them]. But not so the unconcentrated [consciousness]. Only concentrated consciousness should be regarded as the meditation-based basis of meritorious action, when associated with qualities such as loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and the like.

body.translated_text: That concentrated merit whose nature is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is called <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation). Why?

body.text: kathaṃ punaretatpuṇyakriyāvastu mantavyam ? kiṃ puṇyaṃ kriyā ca vastu ca puṇyakriyāvastu, samāhāralakṣaṇo 'yaṃ dvandvaḥ samāso 'tha puṇyakriyayorvastu puṇyakriyāvastu ? atha puṇyakriyāyā vastu puṇyakriyāvastviti ? yathā na doṣastathāstu | kathaṃ ca na doṣaḥ ? tatra tāvat | kāyavākkarmasvabhāvatvāt tridhā kuśalatvātpuṇyam | karmātmakatvātkriyā | tatsamutthāpikāyāścetanāyā adhiṣṭhānātvādvastu | yā tatsamutthāpikā cetanā sā puṇyaṃ ca kriyā ca, tatsahabhuvo dharmāḥ puṇyameva | śīlamayaṃ tu kāyavākkarmaiveti tridhā bhavati | bhāvanāmayaṃ maitro puṇyaṃ ca puṇyakriyāśca vastu | tatsaṃprayuktāyāścetanāyā maitryadhiṣṭhānenābhisaṃskārāṇāṃ maitrīsahabhūcetanā śīlaṃ ca puṇyakriyā ca | anye tatsahabhuvaḥ puṇyameveti |
body.translated_text: But how should this basis of meritorious action (<s>puṇyakriyāvastu</s>) be understood? Is it merit (<s>puṇya</s>) and action (<s>kriyā</s>) and substance (<s>vastu</s>) — a <s>puṇyakriyāvastu</s> [as a <s>dvandva</s> compound], this being a coordinative compound of collective nature? Or is it the substance (<s>vastu</s>) of merit and action — <s>puṇyakriyāvastu</s>? Or is it the substance (<s>vastu</s>) of meritorious action (<s>puṇyakriyā</s>) — <s>puṇyakriyāvastu</s>? Let it be as there is no fault. And how is there no fault? First: because of being of the nature of bodily and vocal action, [it is] merit (<s>puṇya</s>), being wholesome in three ways. Because of being of the nature of action (<s>karma</s>), [it is] action (<s>kriyā</s>). Because of being the basis (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the volition (<s>cetanā</s>) that originates it, [it is] substance (<s>vastu</s>). The volition that originates it is both merit and action; the <s>dharmas</s> co-existing with it are merit only. The morality-based [basis] is indeed bodily and vocal action — thus it is threefold. The meditation-based [basis]: loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) is merit, meritorious action, and substance. The volition associated with it, through the superintendence of loving-kindness, [performs] constructions — the volition co-existing with loving-kindness is both morality and meritorious action. The other co-existing [<s>dharmas</s>] are merit only.

body.text: tatpunaretadbhāvanāmayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu sarvaṃ tatsarvahetutve 'pi sati
body.translated_text: This meditation-based basis of meritorious action, although all [wholesome <s>dharmas</s>] serve as causes of all [results], nevertheless —

body.text: pradhānyādapavargāya taduktaṃ sarvadarśinā // Abhidh-d_256 //
body.translated_text: because of its primacy, it is stated by the all-seeing one [<s>Buddha</s>] to be for liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). (Abhidh-d 256)

body.text: uttamārthaprāptaye khalvāsannatamo heturbhāvaneti kṛtvā bhagavatā bhāvanāmayameva kuśalamūlaṃ visaṃyogāya vidhiyuktamuktam | puṇyakriyāvastubhedena triprakāraṃ śubham |
body.translated_text: Because meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) is the cause closest to the attainment of the supreme goal, therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated that the meditation-based wholesome root alone, when properly applied, is for complete liberation (<s>visaṃyoga</s>). The wholesome [<s>dharma</s>] is threefold according to the division of bases of meritorious action (<s>puṇyakriyāvastu</s>).

body.text: punaranyena prakāratrayeṇa śubhabhedo vyākhyāyate-
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the division of the wholesome is explained by another triad:

children.translated_text: That which is conducive to merit (<s>puṇyabhāgīya</s>), conducive to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedha</s>) —
in this teaching, in brief, the wholesome root is accepted as threefold. (Abhidh-d 257)

body.text: puṇyabhāgīyaṃ yena devamanuṣyopapattibījaṃ pratigṛhṇāti maheśākhyaiśca kulamahābhogarūpyacakravartiśakrapuṣpaketubrahmatvādīnāṃ prāptaye phalamākṣipati | mokṣabhāgīyaṃ yenāvikampya mokṣāśayāvasthānādavaśyaṃ parinirvāṇadharmā bhavati | nirvedhabhāgīyamūṣmagatamūṣmaṃ caturvidham ||
body.translated_text: That which is conducive to merit (<s>puṇyabhāgīya</s>) — by which one grasps the seed of rebirth as a god or human, and attracts the fruit for the attainment of what is called great sovereignty — such as [high] family, great wealth, beauty, universal sovereignty (<s>cakravartin</s>), [the status of] <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Puṣpaketu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the like. That which is conducive to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>) — by which, being unshakable in the disposition toward liberation, one necessarily attains the nature of complete <s>nirvāṇa</s>. That which is conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) — the 'heat' stage (<s>ūṣmagata</s>) and so forth, fourfold.

body.text: atha yadidaṃ loka ucyate lipimudrāgaṇanāsaṃkhyeti eṣāṃ kaḥ svabhāvaḥ ? ucyate-
body.translated_text: Now, what is said in the world — 'writing' (<s>lipi</s>), 'seal' (<s>mudrā</s>), 'enumeration' (<s>gaṇanā</s>), 'calculation' (<s>saṃkhyā</s>) — what is the intrinsic nature of these? It is stated:

children.translated_text: Writing (<s>lipi</s>), seal (<s>mudrā</s>), and enumeration (<s>gaṇanā</s>) have the characteristic of bodily and vocal action;
calculation (<s>saṃkhyā</s>) should be known as having the nature of mental action. (Abhidh-d 258)

body.text: tatra tāvallipimudre yogapravartitaṃ kāyakarmasamutthānamiti pañcaskandhātmikā lipiḥ | yena tu karmaṇākṣarāṇi nirvartyante tatkarma lipirityucyate | nāma yatkhanyate dantaviṣāṇasuvarṇādiṣu sā mudrā | natu yena karmaṇā khanyate tatkarmocyate | kāvyamapi yogapravartitaṃ vākkarmasamutthānaṃ pañcaskandhāḥ | saṃkhyāpi yogapravartitaṃ manaskarma | yanmanasā saṃkalitaṃ dharmāṇāṃ sā tu saparivārā catuskandhasvabhāveti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, first, writing and seal: writing (<s>lipi</s>), originating from bodily action set in motion by application (<s>yoga</s>), consists of the five aggregates. But the action by which letters (<s>akṣara</s>) are produced — that action is called writing. The mark (<s>nāma</s>) carved on ivory, horn, gold, and the like — that is a seal (<s>mudrā</s>). But the action by which it is carved — that action is spoken of [as seal]. Poetry (<s>kāvya</s>) too, originating from vocal action set in motion by application, consists of the five aggregates. Calculation (<s>saṃkhyā</s>) too is mental action set in motion by application — what is computed by the mind regarding <s>dharmas</s> — but with its accompaniments, it is of the nature of four aggregates.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau caturthādhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the fourth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Fifth chapter.

body.text: prathamaḥ pādaḥ
body.translated_text: First section.

body.text: uktāni karmāṇa | atha yadayaṃ lokaḥ pañcagati cakrāvartaparivartanimittāni karmāṇyācinoti, kāryāṇi cotsṛjyākāryakarmakārī bhavati, dakṣiṇaṃ ca mārgaṃ hitvā vāmaṃ vartmāśrayati, paramapraśāntaṃ ca paraṃ brahmāpāsyānekaduḥkhopadravanīḍabhūte saṃsāre janma pratipadyate tatra ko heturityabhidhīyate-
body.translated_text: Actions (<s>karma</s>) have been stated. Now, this world accumulates actions that are the causes of the turning of the wheel of the five destinies (<s>pañcagati</s>), and abandoning what should be done, engages in forbidden actions, and leaving the right path, follows the left path, and forsaking the supremely peaceful, supreme <s>Brahman</s>, undergoes birth in <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is a nest of manifold sufferings and calamities — what is the cause of this? This is stated:

children.translated_text: The world is inclined toward the forbidden and subject to suffering, under the power of which —
I shall describe those afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) that are the bonds of existence (<s>bhavasaṃbandha</s>), beginning with passion (<s>rāga</s>). (Abhidh-d 259)

body.text: te punaḥ kleśāḥ
body.translated_text: Those afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), furthermore —

children.translated_text: through special [terms] arising from the activities produced by their own powers,
having assumed general designations, are referred to as 'latent dispositions' (<s>anuśaya</s>) and so forth. (Abhidh-d 260)

body.text: tatra tāvatsāmānyasaṃjñā svakriyānirjātāḥ kliśnantīti kleśāḥ anuśerata (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 220)

children.text: ) ityanuśayāḥ | ābhavāgramupādāya yāvadavīciṃ stravanti srāvayanti ca cittasantatimityāsravāḥ | āsravāniti pañcalakṣaṇānatra saṃyojantīti saṃyojanāni | granthayantīti granthāḥ | yojayantīti yogāḥ | apaharantītyoghāḥ | upādadata ityupādānānyeṣāṃ sāmānyanāma kleśa iti ||
children.translated_text: — hence 'latent dispositions' (<s>anuśaya</s>). From the summit of existence down to <s>Avīci</s>, they flow (<s>stravanti</s>) and cause the mental continuum to flow — hence 'influxes' (<s>āsrava</s>). They bind sentient beings to the five-characteristic [conditioned existence] — hence 'fetters' (<s>saṃyojana</s>). They knot — hence 'knots' (<s>grantha</s>). They yoke — hence 'yokes' (<s>yoga</s>). They carry away — hence 'floods' (<s>ogha</s>). They grasp — hence 'attachments' (<s>upādāna</s>). Their common name is 'affliction' (<s>kleśa</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, first, the general designations, arising from their own activities: they afflict (<s>kliśnanti</s>) — hence 'afflictions' (<s>kleśa</s>); they lie latent (<s>anuśerate</s>)

body.text: tatra ke kiyanto vānuśayāḥ ? tadavadyotyate-
body.translated_text: Therein, what and how many are the latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>)? This is revealed:

children.translated_text: Passion (<s>rāga</s>), hostility (<s>pratigha</s>), delusion (<s>saṃmoha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), doubt (<s>kāṅkṣā</s>), and wrong views (<s>kudṛṣṭi</s>) —
these six latent dispositions are declared to be the obstacles to the door of the good. (Abhidh-d 261)

body.text: ete khalu ṣaḍanuśayāḥ saṃsārapravṛttihetavaḥ śreyomārgavivandhinaśca śāstra uktāḥ | teṣāṃ niruktiḥ santānānugatā ityanuśayāḥ dhātrocailamalavat | anubadhnantīti vānuśayāḥ, khavarajalacaravat | ta ete vṛttitaśca draṣṭavyāḥ, hiṅgvādibhakṣaṇavat | phalataśca pārāvatabhujaṅgasūkarajanmāpātanavat | pudgalataśca nandāṅgulimālasunakṣatrādivat ||
body.translated_text: These six latent dispositions are stated in the treatise as the causes of the continuance of <s>saṃsāra</s> and as obstacles to the path of the good. Their etymology: 'following the continuum' — hence <s>anuśaya</s>, like garment-dirt on oil-cloth. Or, 'they bind continuously' — hence <s>anuśaya</s>, like [parasites on] aquatic creatures. And they should be seen from the perspective of activity — like eating <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) and the like; and from the perspective of fruit — like falling into birth as a pigeon, snake, or boar; and from the perspective of persons — like <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Aṅgulimāla</s>, <s>Sunakṣatra</s>, and so forth.

body.text: atha rāgādayo 'nuśayāḥ kathaṃ draṣṭavyāḥ ? kiṃ rāgādaya evānuśayāḥ, āhosvidrāgādīnāmanuśayāḥ ? kiñcātaḥ | rāgādaya evānuśayāścetsūtravirodhaḥ- (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 221)

children.text: ) "ihaikatyo na kāmarāgaparyavasthitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharatyutpannasya kāmarāgaparyavasthānasyottaranissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | tasya tatkāmarāgaparyavasthānaṃ sthāmaśaḥ samyaksusaṃvahataṃ sānuśayaṃ prahīyate" iti | rāgādīnāmanuśayā iti cedviprayuktānuśayaprasaṅgādabhidharmavirodhaḥ- "kāmarāgānuśayastribhirindriyaissaprayuktaḥ" iti | karmadhāraya eva parigṛhyate na ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa iti vaibhāṣikāḥ | nanu coktaṃ sūtravirodha iti | sānuśayaṃ sānubandhamityarthaḥ | aupacāriko vā sūtre 'nuśayaśabdaḥ (
children.translated_text: 'Here a certain one, without dwelling much with consciousness overwhelmed by desire-passion (<s>kāmarāga</s>), does not know as it truly is the escape from the arisen overwhelm of desire-passion. His overwhelm of desire-passion, firmly well-established, together with latent disposition (<s>sānuśaya</s>), is abandoned' — thus. If [one says] the latent dispositions belong to passion and the like, then because of the consequence of latent dispositions being dissociated [from consciousness], there would be a contradiction with the <s>Abhidharma</s>: 'The latent disposition of desire-passion is associated with three faculties.' The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> accept the <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional) compound, not the genitive compound. But was not the <s>sūtra</s>-contradiction stated? '<s>Sānuśaya</s>' means 'with its binding' (<s>sānubandha</s>). Or the term <s>anuśaya</s> in the <s>sūtra</s> is metaphorical,
(Jaini 222)

children.text: ) prāptau yathā duḥkho 'gniriti | lākṣaṇikastvabhidharme kleśa evānuśayaḥ | tasmāsaṃprayuktā evānuśayāḥ |
children.translated_text: applied to acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>), like 'fire is painful.' But in the <s>Abhidharma</s>, it is used in the primary sense (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>) — the affliction itself is the latent disposition. Therefore, the latent dispositions are indeed associated [with consciousness].

body.translated_text: Now, how should these latent dispositions beginning with passion (<s>rāga</s>) be viewed? Are passion and the like themselves the latent dispositions, or are the latent dispositions [something belonging] to passion and the like? What follows from this? If passion and the like are themselves the latent dispositions, there is a contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text: "evaṃ tu sādhu yathā dārṣṭāntikānām" iti kośakāraḥ | kathaṃ ca dārṣṭāntikānām ? "kāmarāgasyānuśayaḥ kāmarāgānuśayaḥ | na cānuśayaḥ saṃprayukto na viprayuktaḥ; tasyādravyāntaratvāt | supto hi kleśo 'nuśayaityucyate | prabuddhaḥ paryavasthānam | kā ca tasya prasuptiḥ ? asaṃmukhībhūtasya bījabhāvānubandhaḥ | kaḥ praboadhaḥ ? saṃmukhībhāvaḥ | ko 'yaṃ vījabhāvo nāma ? ātmabhāvasya kleśajā kleśotpādakaśaktiḥ, yathā cāṅkurādīnāṃ śāliphalajā (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 223)
that can produce the rice-fruit.'

body.translated_text: 'It is better as the <s>Dārṣṭāntikas</s> have it' — says the author of the <s>Kośa</s>. And how do the <s>Dārṣṭāntikas</s> [hold]? 'The latent disposition of desire-passion is the desire-passion-latent-disposition. And the latent disposition is neither associated nor dissociated [from consciousness], because it is not a separate substance. For the affliction when dormant is called a latent disposition (<s>anuśaya</s>); when awakened, it is an outburst (<s>paryavasthāna</s>). And what is its dormancy? The binding in seed-form (<s>bījabhāva</s>) when not coming face to face [with its object]. What is its awakening? Coming face to face. And what is this so-called seed-state? A power in one's personal existence, born from the affliction, that can produce the affliction, just as for sprouts and the like, a power born from the rice-fruit

body.text: yattarhi sūtra eva kleśo 'nuśaya uktaḥ ṣaṭṣaṭke- "so 'sya bhavati sukhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ rāgānuśayaḥ" iti ? bhavatīti vacanādadoṣaḥ | nāso tadaivānuśayaḥ | kadā tarhi ? yadā prasupto bhavati | | hetau vā phalopacāra eṣaḥ" iti |
body.translated_text: But then, in the <s>sūtra</s> itself, the affliction is called a latent disposition, in the 'Six Sets' (<s>ṣaṭṣaṭka</s>): 'He has, in regard to pleasant feeling, the latent disposition of passion (<s>rāgānuśaya</s>).' Because of the word 'has' (<s>bhavati</s>), there is no fault. He is not thereby a latent disposition at that very moment. When then? When he becomes dormant. 'Or this is a metaphorical use of the effect for the cause.'

body.text: tadetatsautrāntikairantargataṃ buddhavacananītiśravaṇakausīdyamāvirbhāvyate | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 225)

children.text: ) katham ? uktottaratvāt | uktamatra karmacintāyāmuttaraṃ tattvasaptatau ca | tatsmaryatām | mā pramoṣīḥ |
children.translated_text: How? Because this has been answered. The answer has been stated here in the 'Investigation of Action' and in the <s>Tattvasaptatī</s>. Let it be remembered. Do not forget it.

body.translated_text: This [position] of the <s>Sautrāntikas</s>, internalized [within them], reveals their laziness in hearing the correct understanding of the <s>Buddha</s>'s word.

body.text: punaścāpadiśyate | sautrāntikaparikalpite pratibījakalpe cittaśaktibījabhāvanāpakṣe nivṛttyuttaramanyānanyatvādidoṣāt | nānyānanya iti bījavāsanāvasthāne cittavināśābhyupagame ca madhyamāpratipatsiddhiriti cet | na | cittasvabhāvaśaktikriyābhāve tadantadvayāsiddhau madhyamāpratidanupapatteḥ khapuṣpamayadaṇḍavat |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, it is pointed out: regarding the <s>Sautrāntika</s>-conceived seed-theory, in the position of consciousness-power-seed-cultivation, there is the fault of identity-or-difference and so forth, from which there is no escape. Objection: Neither identity nor difference — the establishment of the <s>Madhyamā pratipat</s> (middle path) comes from accepting the seed-impression state and the destruction of consciousness. Reply: No — because in the absence of the intrinsic nature of consciousness, its power, and its activity, and in the non-establishment of those two extremes for it, the middle path is untenable — like a staff made of sky-flowers.

body.text: te punaḥ
body.translated_text: Those [latent dispositions], furthermore —

children.translated_text: are held to be seven by the division of passion and aversion; remembered as ten by the division of views;
and should be known as ninety-eight by the division of realm (<s>dhātu</s>), aspect (<s>ākāra</s>), and the like. (Abhidh-d 262)

body.text: tatra kāyarāgabhavarāgabhedaṃ purastādvakṣyate | dṛṣṭibhedo 'pi satkāyadṛṣṭyādibhedena pañcadhā | rāgabhedaṃ ca dvidhā vakṣyāmaḥ | te punarete sarva evānuśayā yathāsaṃbhavaṃ dhātvākāraprakārabhedenāṣṭānavatirbhavanti |
body.translated_text: Therein, the division into desire-passion (<s>kāmarāga</s>) and existence-passion (<s>bhavarāga</s>) will be explained later. The division of views too is fivefold, by the division into the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the like. And we shall also explain the twofold division of passion. All these latent dispositions, according to their applicability, become ninety-eight by the division of realm, aspect, and mode.

body.text: tatra kecitpaṇḍitā darśayanti | dhātubhedena kāmāvacarāḥ ṣaḍtriṃśaddarśanabhāvanāheyāḥ | dvātriṃśaddarśanaheyāḥ | rūpāvacarā ekatriṃśadubhayaheyāḥ, aṣṭāviṃśatirdarśanaheyāḥ pañca pratighavarjyāḥ | evamārūpyāvacarāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, some learned ones show: by the division of realm, those belonging to the desire realm are thirty-six — to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaheya</s>) and by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāheya</s>). Thirty-two are to be abandoned by seeing. Those belonging to the form realm are thirty-one, [abandonable] by both — twenty-eight to be abandoned by seeing, minus the five [of] hostility (<s>pratigha</s>). Likewise for those belonging to the formless realm.

body.text: tatra kathaṃ kāmāvacarāḥ ṣaḍtriṃśadbhavanti ? darśanabhāvanāheyaprakāranaiyamyabhedāt | dṛṣṭīnāmapidhātvākāraprakārabhedāt ṣaḍtriṃśatvam | pratighasya dhātunaiyamyāt pañcatvam | vayaṃ punareṣāṃ bhedaṃ ślokānugatameva darśayiṣyāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: How do those belonging to the desire realm become thirty-six? By the fixed division of the modes of being to be abandoned by seeing and by cultivation. And the thirty-six-ness of views [arises] from the division of realm, aspect, and mode. The five-ness of hostility is from the fixed [assignment] to the [desire] realm. We, however, shall show their division following the verses.

body.text: tatra katyeṣāmaṣṭānavateranuśayāṇāṃ duḥkhadarśanaheyāḥ kati yāvadbhāvanāheyāḥ ? tatra kāmadhātau tāvat | pratiduḥkhādisatyaṃ yathākramaṃ daśa sapta saptāṣṭau duḥkhādidarśanaheyā dvātriṃśatkāmadhātau bhavanti | teṣu teṣāṃ vipratipatteḥ | evaṃ rūpārūpyadhātvorabhyuhya vaktavyam ||
body.translated_text: Therein, of these ninety-eight latent dispositions, how many are to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering (<s>duḥkhadarśanaheya</s>), and how many up to those to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāheya</s>)? First, in the desire realm: for each truth of suffering and so forth, in order, ten, seven, seven, and eight are to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and so forth — making thirty-two in the desire realm. Because of the opposition [of the latent dispositions] to each [truth]. For the form and formless realms, one should state [the numbers] by inference.

children.translated_text: Desire-passion (<s>kāmarāga</s>) and that called existence-[passion] (<s>bhava</s>) — passion (<s>rāga</s>) is divided in two —
chiefly because of operating externally [and internally], and from the division of internal operation and the like. (Abhidh-d 263)

body.text: yathākramam | ukto rāgabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: In order. The division of passion has been stated.

body.text: dṛṣṭibhedo nirdiśyate-
body.translated_text: The division of views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) is enumerated:

children.translated_text: The view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the grasping of the two extremes (<s>antadvayagrāha</s>), wrong view (<s>mithyādarśana</s>) itself,
the view of [holding wrong] views and rites (<s>dṛṣṭi-śīla-vrata-āmarśa</s>) — these are the five views. (Abhidh-d 264)

body.text: te punarete prabhidyamānā dhātuprakārākārabhedenāṣṭānavatirbhavanti | ṣaṭtriṃśatkāmāvacarāḥ | ekatriṃśadrūpāvacarāḥ | ekatriṃśadārūpyāvacarāḥ | darśanabhāvanāheyaprakāranaiyamyāt ||
kati punarebhyaḥ kāmadhātau darśanaheyāḥ kati yāvadbhāvanāheyāḥ ? tadavadyotyate-
sarve 'pi daśeha kāmadhātau duḥkhe vipratipannatvādduḥkhadarśanaheyāḥ |
sapta hetvīkṣaṇakṣayāḥ /
ebhyo daśabhyaḥ satkāyāntargrāhadṛṣṭiśīlavrataparāmarśatrayaṃ hitvā |
eta eva
aṣṭau mārgekṣaṇakṣayāḥ // Abhidh-d_265 //
satkāyāntargrāhadṛṣṭī hitvā | te 'pi phalabhūteṣu skandheṣu vipratipannatvādduḥkhadarśanaheyaiva |
te darśanaprahātavyāsteṣāṃ caturṇāṃ rāgādīnāṃ yasmādālambanamatastatprahāṇātteṣāmapi (

children.text: ) prahāṇaṃ stambhanipātādupastambhanipātanavat | ye tu rāgādayaścatvāraḥ svalakṣaṇakleśāste bhāvanāprahātavyā draṣṭavyā rāgapratighamānāvidyāḥ ||

body.text: atra punaḥ
pratikalpavaśotpatterdṛṣṭikāṅkṣe tu dṛkkṣaye /
avidyamāne khalu vastunyete skandheṣu viparītasaṃdehākāragrahaṇaṃ kṛtvā pravartete | tasmādete darśanaheye cetoddhāṭanamātreṇa sāradravyāstitvasaṃdehāpagamavat |
rūpepyevaṃ tathārūpye pratighānuśayādṛte // Abhidh-d_267 //
yathā kāmadhātau proktāḥ, rūpārūpyadhātvorapyevaṃ draṣṭavyāḥ | pratighānuśayaṃ varjayitvā | tatra hi śamathasnigdhasantānatvātpratighanimittābhāvācca pratighānuśayo nāsti |

tatra satkāyāntargrāhadṛṣṭī ekaprakāre duḥkhadarśanamātraheyatvāt | mithyādṛṣṭidṛṣṭiparāmarśavicikitsāḥ pratyekaṃ catuṣprakārāḥ, catussatyadarśanaheyatvāt | śīlavrataparāmarśo dviprakāro duḥkhamārgadarśanaheyatvāt | rāgādayaḥ pañcaprakārāḥ, catussatyadarśanabhāvanāheyatvāt | ta ete kāmadhātau ṣaṭtriṃśadbhavanti | rūpadhātāvekatriṃśadārūpyadhātāvekatriṃśaditi samastā daśanabhāvanāheyā aṣṭānavatirbhavanti | tebhyaḥ punaraṣṭāśīti darśanaprahātavyāḥ | daśa bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ ||
atha ya ete 'ṣṭāśītiranuśayā darśanaprahātavyāḥ kimete darśanamārgeṇaiva prahīyante ? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi ?
bhavāgre kṣāntiheyā ye dṛggheyā eva te matāḥ /
te hyekāntenānvayakṣāntivadhyāḥ |
jñānavadhyāstu ye tasminnabhyāsenaiva tatkṣayaḥ // Abhidh-d_268 //

evamanyāsvapi bhūmiṣu ye 'nuśayā jñānavadhyāsta āryāṇāṃ pṛthagjanānāṃ ca bhāvanāmārgeṇaiva prahīyante | śeṣāstūbhayathā | yathāyogaṃ śeṣāsu khalu bhūmiṣu yathāsaṃbhavaṃ dharmānvayakṣāntibadhyā anuśayā āryāṇāṃ darśanaheyāḥ, pṛthagjanānāṃ ca bhāvanāheyā iti boddhavyam ||
atha yā imāḥ pañca dṛṣṭayo dhātvākāraprakārabhedena ṣaṭtriṃśaddhā bhinnāstāsāṃ pratyekaṃ kaḥ svabhāvaḥ ? tadārabhyate -

children.text: ahaṃ mameti yā dṛṣṭirasau satkāyadṛk smṛtā /

body.text: hetubalasāmarthyādasacchāstraśravaṇācca pṛthagjanasyāhaṃ mamemi pañcasūpādānaskandheṣu ya ātmagrāhaḥ sā satkāyadṛṣṭirityucyate | sati sīdati vā kāye dṛṣṭirviparītākārā satkāyadṛṣṭiriti nirvacanam | saiṣātmātmīyākārabhedāddviprakārā | punaḥ pañcaskandhālambanāḥ pañcātmadṛṣṭayo bhavanti | (

children.text: ) pañcadaśātmīyadṛṣṭayaḥ | tāḥ samastā viṃśatikoṭikā satkāyadṛṣṭiriti vyākhyāyate |

body.text: tayorgṛhītasya viparyāsenātmākhyasyāsadvastuno 'satpuruṣasaṃsargānnityatvagrāho vā nityatvagrāheṇa vā sāntargrāhadṛṣṭiriti ||
phalahetvapavādo yaḥ sā mithyādṛṣṭirucyate /
phalahetugrahaṇe vastukriyāgrahaṇaṃ pratyetavyam | anena śāstraproktayā mithyādṛṣṭeḥ sākalyena grahaṇaṃ pratyetavyam |
jñeyo dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ hīnavastūttamagrahaḥ // Abhidh-d_270 //
ahetāvapathe caiva taddhi śīlavratāhvayaḥ /

sarvaṃ khalu sāsravaṃ vastu hīnārhatvāddhīnam | ādigrahaṇaśabdasya cātra lopo draṣṭavyaḥ | dṛṣṭyādiparāmarśo dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ | catasro dṛṣṭīḥ pratyavaraṃ ca vastvagrato gṛhṇāti kathamagryeyaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ ? yeyamātmadṛṣṭiḥ- ātmānamahaṃ pūjayiṣyāmi vāsudevo 'tra pūjito bhaviṣyatīti hīnapuruṣaṃpañcopādānaskandhātmakamagrataḥ pratipadyate | nāsti dattaṃ yathāsukhaṃ pravartiṣyata ityevamādiḥ |

akāraṇe kumārge ca kāraṇamārgagrahaṇaṃ śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ | tadyathā prakṛtīśvarapuruṣādihetukaṃ pañcopādānaskandhātmakaṃ na tṛṣṇāhetukamityakāraṇe kāraṇadarśanam | kumārgaṃ cāgnijalapraveśādau prakṛtipuruṣāntarajñānādau ca svargāpavargahetutvam |

śīlaṃ tvatrāgnihotrānuṣṭhānaṃ pratijuhotyādyāstistro 'ntaraṅgakriyāḥ, paśvālambhanādyāḥ bahiraṅgāḥ, tadubhayasya yāvajjīvamanuṣṭhānaṃ śīlam | yathoktam- "jarāmaryaṃ vaitatsatraṃ yadagnihotraṃ juhoti" iti |
vratam- āgneyamagniparicaraṇaṃ śaukramāpo hi ṣṭhādyanuṣṭhānam apāṃ śukradaivatyatvāt | vārhaspatyaupaniṣadagodānīyaṃ jaṭāvatāraṇam | athavā govratādīni vratānyebhiḥ śudhyate mucyata ityāhuḥ |

trayīdharmāṇasta eva te hariharahiraṇyagarbhādayo na kāraṇamupādānaskandhātmakatvāt | na ca nityāḥ, na cāgryā ityetadvistareṇāviṣkṛtam | paśvālambhanāgnijalapraveśādayaśca na svargāpavargaheturdānaśīlabhāvanānāṃ taddhetutvāt | ityato viparītadarśanametacchīlavrataparāmarśākhyamiti ||
yadi tarhi puruṣeśvarādikāraṇadvāreṇa śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ pravartate, prāptastarhi samudayadarśanaprahātavyaḥ ? naitadasti | yasmādasau
duḥkhabhrāntyapathādānāttadṛṣṭyutsārya eva saḥ // Abhidh-d_271 //
duḥkhabhūteṣūpādānaskandheṣu hariharahiraṇyagarbhādiṣvakāraṇeṣu buddhyā bhrāntaḥ | tasmādyatraiva bhrāntastatraivāviparītadarśanatprahīyate | kāpathe ca (

children.text: ) satpathabuddhyā bhrānta iti samyaksvamārgadarśanātprahīyate | iti siddhaṃ dvidarśanaheyaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ |

body.text: yadā khalvasya dharmeṣu dharmamātrabuddhirutpannā bhavatyanityāḥ, duḥkhāḥ, śūnyāḥ, anātmānaśca dharmā iti tadaiva satkāyadṛṣṭyavacchedo bhavati, tatpravartitā cāntargrāhadṛṣṭiḥ, tatropāttasyā api samudghāta iti | tatra dharmadarśanamanityādyanyatamākāraṃ yasmādduḥkhābhisamayamātrādbhavatyata etad dṛṣṭidvayaṃ dukhadarśanaheyameveti siddham ||
atha ya ete catvāro viparyāsāḥ- "anitye nityam" evamādayaste kiṃ svabhāvāḥ ? tadārabhyate-
tatra tavat | dṛṣṭiparāmarśātsukhaśuciviparyāsau prakalpyete | satkāyadṛṣṭerātmadṛṣṭiviparyāsaḥ, antargrāhadṛṣṭyardhātnityaviparyāsaḥ prakalpyata (

children.text: ) iti | nanu satkāyadṛṣṭerardhātprāpnoti ? na | dṛṣṭyantaratvāt | śāśvatadṛṣṭerucchedadṛṣṭirdṛṣṭyantaram | puruṣameva tu svatantraṃ kartāraṃ vaśinamātmavādī manyamāno mamedamityabhyupagacchati tasmādātmadṛṣṭirevāsau | yadi ca mametyetad dṛṣṭyantaraṃ syānmayā mahyamityevamādyapi dṛṣṭyantaraṃ syāt | tasmādahaṃkāraparyāyā evaite draṣṭavyāḥ |

body.text: nanu ca sarve kleśā viparyāsāḥ viparītapravṛtatvāt ? tatkimucyate catvāra iti ? naiṣa doṣaḥ | yasmāt

viparītato nitīraṇātsamāropādekāntaviparyāsācca | na hyetadanyeṣāṃ kleśānāṃ samastamasti | mithyādṛṣṭyucchedadṛṣṭī yadyapi nitīrayataḥ, ekāntaviparyaste ca, na tu samāropike dravyanāśapravṛttatvāt | śīlavrataparāmarśo naikāntaviparītaḥ kāmavairāgyādisaṃbhavāt | anye kleśā na santīrakāḥ | iti catvāra eva |

nanu ca sūtra uktam- "ānitye nityamiti saṃjñāviparyāsaḥ, cittaviparyāso dṛṣṭiviparyāsa evaṃ yāvadātmani" iti dvādaśa bhavanti | naiṣa doṣaḥ | nahi saṃjñācitte nitīrake | tasmāccaturṣveva dṛṣṭisvabhāveṣu viparyāsoktiḥ | 'dṛgvaśāt cittasaṃjñayoḥ'; taduktiriti | saṃjñā hi lokakāryavyavahārapatitā darśanavaśādviparyastamālambananimittamudgṛhṇāti | cittaṃ ca tadvaśānuvartīti tayoreva grahaṇam | loke 'pi viparyastasaṃjño viparyastacittaścocyate na viparyastavedano viparyastacetana iti ||
atha kiṃ dṛṣṭyanuśayavat mānānuśayasyāpi kaścidbhedo 'sti ? vidyata ityāha | kathamityādarśyate-

tadasya ślokasya saṃkṣepavistāravyākhyāprabhedo 'yamādaryate | tatra tāvatkarmasvakatāsāmarthyasaṃmugdhasya yena kenacidvastunā cittasyonnatirmānaḥ | pratidyamānaḥ saptadhā bhavati mānaḥ, atimānaḥ, mānātimānaḥ, asmimānaḥ, abhimānaḥ, ūnamānaḥ, mithyāmānaśca | eteṣāṃ prapañco yathā prakaraṇeṣu |

nanu punarjñānaprasthāne navamānavidhā uktāstadyathā- "śreyānahamasmīti mānavidhā | sadṛśo 'hamasmīti taddṛṣṭisaṃniśritaiva mānavidhā | sadṛśāddhīno 'hamasmīti mānavidhā | asti me śreyānasti me sadṛśo 'sti me hīnaḥ, nāsti me śreyo nāsti me sadṛśo nāsti me hīnaḥ" iti |
body.translated_text: But are not nine modes of conceit stated in the <s>Jñānaprasthāna</s>, namely: 'The mode of conceit [that thinks] "I am superior" — the mode of conceit [that thinks] "I am equal," which is based on that very [self-]view — the mode of conceit [that thinks] "I am inferior to an equal" — "there is one superior to me," "there is one equal to me," "there is one inferior to me," "there is none superior to me," "there is none equal to me," "there is none inferior to me"'?

body.text: tatra śreyānahamasmīti satkāyadṛṣṭisanniśritā atimānavidhā | sadṛśo 'hamasmīti taddṛṣṭisanniśritaiva mānavidhā | hīno 'hamasmīti taddṛṣṭisanniśritaivonamānavidhā | asti me śreyānityūnamānavidhā | asti me sadṛśa iti mānavidhā | asti me māna iti mānātimānavidhā | nāsti me śreyāniti mānavidhā | nāsti me sadṛśa ityatimānavidhā | nāsti me hīna ityūnamānavidhā | iti evametā navamānavidhāstribhyo mānebhyo vyavasthāpyante mānāmimānonamānebhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: There, 'I am superior' is a mode of overweening conceit (<s>atimāna</s>) based on the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). 'I am equal' is a mode of [ordinary] conceit (<s>māna</s>) based on that very view. 'I am inferior' is a mode of self-deprecating conceit (<s>ūnamāna</s>) based on that very view. 'There is one superior to me' is a mode of self-deprecating conceit. 'There is one equal to me' is a mode of [ordinary] conceit. 'There is one inferior to me' is a mode of conceit-over-conceit (<s>mānātimāna</s>). 'There is none superior to me' is a mode of [ordinary] conceit. 'There is none equal to me' is a mode of overweening conceit. 'There is none inferior to me' is a mode of self-deprecating conceit. Thus these nine modes of conceit are established from three conceits: conceit (<s>māna</s>), overweening conceit (<s>atimāna</s>), and self-deprecating conceit (<s>ūnamāna</s>).

body.text: ta ete saptamānāḥ sarve 'pi darśanabhāvanāheyāḥ sthavirakṣemakasūtrokteḥ- "asti me eṣu pañcasūpādānaskandheṣvasmīti māno 'prahīṇaḥ" iti ||
body.translated_text: These seven conceits are all to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśana</s>) and by cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — as stated in the <s>sūtra</s> of the Elder <s>Kṣemaka</s>: 'In these five aggregates of clinging, there is an unabandoned conceit "I am."'

body.text: kiṃ punaryadbhāvanāheyamaprahīṇaṃ sarvaṃ tadāryasya samudācarati ? netyāha | prahīṇamapi hi kiñcitsamudācarati | tadyathā śraddhādīni pañcendriyāṇi middhaṃ duḥkhendriyaṃ cakṣurādyaṣṭakaṃ ceti | aprahīṇamapi khalu kiñcinna samudācarati | tadyathā
body.translated_text: But does everything that is to be abandoned by cultivation and is unabandoned actually manifest for a noble one? No, he says. For even some that has been abandoned may manifest — such as the five faculties of faith and the like, torpor (<s>middha</s>), the suffering-faculty, and the eight [elements] beginning with the eye. And some that is unabandoned may not manifest — namely:

children.translated_text: Mental afflictions [leading to] killing and the like, remorse, unwholesome modes [of conceit],

children.text: vibhavecchā ca nāryasya jāyante hetvabhāvataḥ // Abhidh-d_276 //
children.translated_text: and the desire for annihilation — these do not arise for a noble one, because of the absence of their cause. (Abhidh-d 276)

body.text: yena khalu kleśaparyavasthānena saṃcitya prāṇivadhādattādānakāmamithyācāramṛṣāvādānadhyāpadyetaitadvadhādyaprahīṇamapi na samudācarati bhāvanāheyatvāt | kaukṛtyaṃ cākuśalaṃ na samudācarati | mānavidhāśca nava na samudācaranti | vibhavatṛṣṇāpi bhāvanāprahātavyāpi satī na samudācarati | 'ca'śabdādbhavatṛṣṇāyāśca kaścitpradeśaḥ | aho vatāhamairāvaṇaḥ syāṃ nāgarājā aho vatāhamasurendraḥ syāṃ vaimacitrādiḥ | aho vatāhamuttareṣu kuruṣu janma labheyetyevamādi |
body.translated_text: That afflictive mental engulfment (<s>kleśaparyavasthāna</s>) by which one would deliberately commit killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, or false speech — this, though unabandoned concerning killing and the like, does not manifest, because it is to be abandoned by cultivation. Unwholesome remorse (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) too does not manifest. The nine modes of conceit do not manifest. The craving for annihilation (<s>vibhavatṛṣṇā</s>), though to be abandoned by cultivation and still present, does not manifest. By the word 'and,' a certain portion of the craving for existence (<s>bhavatṛṣṇā</s>) [is also included] — such as: 'Oh, would that I were <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, the king of elephants! Oh, would that I were <s>Vaimacitra</s> and the like, the lord of <s>Asuras</s>! Oh, would that I were born in <s>Uttarakuru</s>!' — and so forth.

body.text: kiṃ punaratra kāraṇaṃ yadete 'prahīṇāḥ khalvapi santo nāryasya samudācaranti ? śūnyatāyāḥ subhāvitatvātkarmaphalasaṃbandhayukteśca viditatvāt, dṛṣṭipuṣṭatvācca ||
body.translated_text: What then is the reason that these, though unabandoned, do not manifest for a noble one? Because emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) has been well cultivated [by them], because the connection of action and fruit has been understood through reasoning, and because [these defilements] are nourished by [wrong] views.

body.text: tatra mānavidhā asmimānaśca satkāyadṛṣṭipuṣṭāḥ | vadhādiparyavasthānaṃ mithyādṛṣṭipuṣṭam | vibhavatṛṣṇocchedadṛṣṭipuṣṭā | bhavatṛṣṇāpradeśaḥ śāśvatadṛṣṭipuṣṭaḥ | iti vidhādayastatpoṣakakleśābhāvādāryasya notsahante santānamadhyāroḍhum | kaukṛtyamapi cākuśalamavītarāgasyāryasyāprahīṇaṃ na cāsya tatsaṃbhavati cikitsāsamutthitatvāditi ||
body.translated_text: There, the modes of conceit and the 'I am' conceit are nourished by the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). The mental afflictions concerning killing and the like are nourished by wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>). The craving for annihilation is nourished by the view of annihilation (<s>ucchedadṛṣṭi</s>). The portion of the craving for existence is nourished by the view of eternalism (<s>śāśvatadṛṣṭi</s>). Thus the modes [of conceit] and the rest, in the absence of the defilements that nourish them, are unable to mount upon the continuum of a noble one. Unwholesome remorse too — though unabandoned for a noble one not yet free from passion — does not arise for him, because it arises from [moral] doubt.

body.text: athānuśayāḥ sarvatragāḥ kasmātkleśanikāyā vyavasthāpyante ? tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: Now, why are the universal (<s>sarvatraga</s>) latent defilements (<s>anuśaya</s>) established as defilement-groups? That is now commenced:

body.text: duḥkhātsamudayāccaiva sarvagānāṃ vyavasthitiḥ /
body.translated_text: The establishment of the universals is from [the truths of] suffering and origination.

body.text: duḥkhasamudayadarśanaprahātavyāḥ khalvanuśayāḥ sarvagāḥ | yasmāt
body.translated_text: Indeed, the universal latent defilements are those to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and origination. Because:

body.text: taddṛṣṭiheyajātīnāṃ sarvāsāṃ dvipadasthiteḥ // Abhidh-d_277 //
body.translated_text: Of those classes to be abandoned by seeing those [two truths], [their] establishment is in both bases. (Abhidh-d 277)

body.text: dvayoḥ khalu nikāyayoḥ duḥkhasamudayākhyayostaddarśanaheyāṇāṃ vakṣyamāṇānāṃ kleśānāmubhayatra labdhapratiṣṭhatvāt ||
body.translated_text: Because the defilements — to be stated — that are to be abandoned by seeing those two, namely suffering and origination, have their establishment in both groups.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ sarve duḥkhasamudayaheyāḥ na heyāḥ sarvatragāḥ ? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi ?
body.translated_text: But are all [defilements] to be abandoned by [seeing] suffering and origination universal? No, he says. What then?

children.translated_text: Doubt, the five views, ignorance mixed with them, and also [ignorance] alone —
seven are universal from suffering; from the origination, four from those [same ones]. (Abhidh-d 278)

body.text: saptadṛṣṭayo dve vicikitse tābhiśca saṃyuktāvidyā āveṇikī ca (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 240)

children.text: ) dviprakārā ityekādaśānuśayā dhātau dhātau svadhātubhūmisarvatragā jñeyāḥ | sakalasvadhātubhūmyālambanatvāt | ete ca paripiṇḍya trayastriṃśatsarvatragā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: of two types — [thus] eleven latent defilements in each realm are to be known as universal throughout their own realm and level, because they have as their object the entirety of their own realm and level. These, when aggregated, become thirty-three universals.

body.translated_text: The seven views, the two doubts, the ignorance associated with them, and also the distinctive (<s>āveṇikī</s>) [ignorance]

body.text: ete punaḥ sarvatragāḥ
body.translated_text: These universals, moreover —

body.text: dravyato daśa caikaśca nāmnā sapta tu te matāḥ /
body.translated_text: are by substance eleven, but by name they are considered seven.

body.text: tisṛṇāmapyavidyānāṃ dvayośca vicikitsayorekanāmatvāt |
body.translated_text: Because the three ignorances and the two doubts [each] share a single name.

body.text: atha kasmādrāgapratighamānā na sarvatragāḥ ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now, why are passion (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), and conceit (<s>māna</s>) not universal? That is stated:

body.text: rāgapratighamānāstu paricchedapravartinaḥ // Abhidh-d_279 //
body.translated_text: But passion, aversion, and conceit operate within limited [domains]. (Abhidh-d 279)

body.text: ete khalu svalakṣaṇakleśāḥ pratikleśamanavayavaṃ cālambyotpadyate | tasmānna sarvagāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, these are defilements with specific characteristics — each defilement arises taking as its object an indivisible [portion of the object]. Therefore, they are not universal.

body.text: vicikitsādyāstu
body.translated_text: But doubt and the rest —

children.translated_text: Because of operating in different modes, [they have] the nature of pervading all of their own level at once.
Because of taking as object other realms, the previously stated ones alone are universal. (Abhidh-d 280)

body.text: atra punaḥ
body.translated_text: Here, moreover —

body.text: navordhvadhātukāsteṣāmādyā dṛṣṭidvayādṛte /
body.translated_text: Nine are of the upper realms; of those, the first [group is established] except for two views.

body.text: satkāyāntargrāhadṛṣṭī hitvānye nava visabhāgadhātusarvatragāḥ |
body.translated_text: Excluding the views of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the view of [extreme] grasping (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), the other nine are universal across dissimilar realms.

body.text: kiṃ punaranuśayā eva sarvatragāḥ ? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi ?
body.translated_text: But are only latent defilements universal? No, he says. What then?

body.text: teṣāṃ sahabhuvo dharmāḥ prāptivarjyāśca sarvagāḥ // Abhidh-d_281 //
body.translated_text: The dharmas co-arising with them, excluding [the factor of] acquisition, are also universal. (Abhidh-d 281)

body.text: ye sarvatragānuśayasahabhuvo vedanādayo dharmāḥ, jātyādayaśca te 'pi sarvatragāstadekaphalatvāt ||
body.translated_text: The dharmas co-arising with the universal latent defilements — feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) and the like, and birth (<s>jāti</s>) and the like — are also universal, because they share a single fruit [with those defilements].

body.text: teṣāṃ punaraṣṭānavatīnāmanuśayānāṃ kati sāsravālambanāḥ katyanāsravālambanāḥ ? tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: Of those ninety-eight latent defilements, how many have contaminated objects (<s>sāsravālambana</s>) and how many have uncontaminated objects (<s>anāsravālambana</s>)? That is now commenced:

children.translated_text: Doubt, wrong view, and the ignorance mixed with them, and also [ignorance] alone —
those to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path — these six have the immaculate as their object. (Abhidh-d 282)

body.text: nirodhamārgadarśanaheyā mithyādṛṣṭivicikitsā tatsaṃprayuktā cāvidyā sahāveṇikyāvidyayā | ityete dhātau dhātau ṣaḍanuśayā anāsravālambanāḥ | śeṣāḥ sāsravālambanāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Wrong view and doubt that are to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path, together with the ignorance associated with them, along with the distinctive ignorance — thus these six latent defilements in each realm have uncontaminated objects. The rest have contaminated objects.

body.text: athaite nirmalālambanāḥ kati katyuparamamālambyante, kati bhūmipratipakṣaṃ ca ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now, of these that have immaculate objects — how many take how many [types of] cessation as their object, and how many [are directed at] the path of which level as their counteragent? That is stated:

children.translated_text: The <s>nirvāṇa</s> of one's own level alone [is the object]; the path is of nine levels.
The object seen by each [set of defilements] is different from the others, because of being a cause, because of being a cause-state. (Abhidh-d 283)

body.text: svabhūminirodha eva nirodhālambanānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādīnāmālambanam | kāmāvacarāṇāṃ kāmāvacaranirodhaḥ | evaṃ yāvadbhavāgrabhūmikānāṃ bhavāgrasyaiva | mārgālambanānāṃ tu kāmāvacarāṇāṃ sarva eva svabhūmikāḥ kleśāḥ mārga ālambanam | yo 'pyasau rūpārūpyapratipakṣaḥ, rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāmapyaṣṭamūmikānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādīnāṃ navabhūmi- ko 'nvayajñānapakṣyo mārga ālambanaḥ | kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ mithyādṛṣṭyā nirodhaḥ paricchinna ālambyate, na mārgeṇa ? taducyate | 'hetutvāddhetubhāvataśca |'; mārgo hi parasparahetukaḥ, na tu nirodha ityasti viśeṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The object of wrong view and the rest that take cessation as their object is only the cessation of one's own level. For those of the desire-realm, the cessation of the desire-realm [is the object]; similarly, up to those of the level of the Summit of Existence, [the cessation] of the Summit of Existence alone [is the object]. But for those that take the path as their object: for [defilements] of the desire-realm, all defilements of one's own level constitute the path that serves as [their] object — including whatever [path] is the counteragent of the form and formless [realms]. For wrong view and the rest of the form and formless realms, which are of eight levels, the path of nine levels — belonging to the class of <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) — is the object. What then is the reason that cessation is taken as a delimited object by wrong view, but the path is not? That is stated: 'Because of being a cause, and because of the state of being a cause.' For the path is mutually causal, but cessation is not — therein lies the distinction.

body.text: atha kasmādrāgapratighamānā dṛṣṭiśīlavrataparāmarśo ca nānāsravālambanā iṣyante ? tatrāpadiṣyate-
body.translated_text: Now, why are passion, aversion, conceit, and the view of clinging to rules and rites not accepted as having uncontaminated objects? This is indicated:

children.translated_text: Not passion — because of [its] power and because of not being a cause; not aversion — because of [the object's] non-offensiveness;
not conceit — because of [the object's] extreme tranquility; not the other views — because of their [positive] nature. (Abhidh-d 284)

body.text: tatra rāgastāvadyadyanāsravālambanaḥ syānnirvāṇābhilāṣapravṛttatvātkuśaladharmacchandavat, na yogināṃ varjanīyaḥ syāt | dveṣo 'pyapakāravastunyutpadyate, mokṣastu sarvaduḥkhoparamādupakārī | māno 'pyapraśāntatvādunnatilakṣaṇaḥ, nirmalāstu dharmāstadapaghātinaḥ | parāmarśī ca yadyanāsravālambanau syātāṃ samyagdṛṣṭitvaṃ pratipadyeyātām | tasmātpūrvoktā evānuśayā nirmalagocarāḥ ||
body.translated_text: There, first, if passion had an uncontaminated object — since it would be directed toward the longing for <s>nirvāṇa</s>, like desire for wholesome dharmas, it would not need to be abandoned by yogins. Aversion too arises regarding an object that is harmful, but liberation, being beneficial through the cessation of all suffering, [is not harmful]. Conceit too has the mark of arrogance due to [mental] restlessness, but immaculate dharmas counteract that. And if the two views of clinging [to rules and rites] had uncontaminated objects, they would amount to right view. Therefore, only the previously stated latent defilements have immaculate objects.

body.text: athaiteṣāmaṣṭānavateranuśayānāṃ katyālambanato 'nuśerate kati saṃprayogataḥ ?
body.translated_text: Now, of these ninety-eight latent defilements, how many lie latent by [way of their] object (<s>ālambana</s>) and how many by [way of] association (<s>saṃprayoga</s>)?

children.translated_text: A universal latent defilement lies latent throughout the entirety [of its] own realm and level, by [way of its] object.
A non-universal one [lies latent in] its own level and its own group by object. (Abhidh-d 285)

body.text: dvividhāḥ khalu sarvagāḥ | svadhātubhūmisarvagāḥ, visabhāgadhātubhūmisarvagāśca | asarvagā api dvividhāḥ | sāsravālambanāḥ, anāsravālambanāśca | tatra te ye 'nuśayāḥ svadhātubhūmisarvatragāste sakalāmeva pañcaprakārāṃ svadhātubhūmimālambanato 'nuśerate | ye tvasarvatragāḥ sāsravālambanāste svabhūmau svanikāyamālambanato 'nuśerate | duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyāḥ duḥkhadarśana prahātavyameva nikāyaṃ yāvadbhāvanāprahātavyā bhāvanāprahātavyameveti ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, the universals are of two kinds: those universal throughout their own realm and level, and those universal across dissimilar realms and levels. The non-universals are also of two kinds: those with contaminated objects, and those with uncontaminated objects. There, those latent defilements that are universal throughout their own realm and level lie latent throughout the entirety of the five categories of their own realm and level by way of object. But those that are non-universal and have contaminated objects lie latent in their own level and their own group by way of object — those to be abandoned by seeing suffering [lie latent in] the group to be abandoned by seeing suffering, and so on up to those to be abandoned by cultivation [lying latent in] the group to be abandoned by cultivation.

body.text: ālambanataśca
body.translated_text: And by way of object —

body.text: asvīkārādvipakṣatvānnordhvabhūmārgagocaraḥ /
body.translated_text: they do not have the path of a higher level or the uncontaminated as their domain, because of non-appropriation and because of being an adversary.

body.text: ālambanato 'nuśerata iti vartate | kiṃ kāraṇam ? anyabhūmikasyānāsravasya ca vastunaḥ 'asvīkārādvipakṣatvā'cca | ātmadṛṣṭitṛṣṇābhyāṃ hi svīkṛte vastunyanuśayo 'nuśayitumutsahate | anāsrave tu vastunyūrdhvabhūmike ca pravṛttireva satkāyadṛṣṭitṛṣṇayornāstīti na tatrānuśerate |
body.translated_text: 'Lie latent by way of object' is still the governing [clause]. For what reason? Because of the 'non-appropriation' of objects of other levels and of uncontaminated [objects], 'and because of being an adversary.' For a latent defilement is able to lie latent in an object that has been appropriated through the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). But with respect to uncontaminated and higher-level objects, the view of the existing body and craving simply do not operate — therefore [defilements] do not lie latent in those.

body.text: saṃprayogiṇi tu svasminnahīne saṃprayogataḥ // Abhidh-d_286 //
body.translated_text: But by way of association — in [those dharmas] associated with it and not inferior. (Abhidh-d 286)

body.text: anuśerata ityadhikṛtam | yo yena dharmeṇānuśayaḥ saṃprayuktaḥ sa tasminsaṃprayogiṇi saṃprayogato 'nuśerate yāvadaprahīṇo bhavatīti 'tu'; śabdo viśinaṣṭi | tataścedamapi siddhaṃ bhavati- anāsravālambanā visabhāgadhātubhūmyālambanāśca saṃprayogata evānuśerate | sāsravālambanāḥ svabhūmāvālambanataḥ saṃprayogataśceti ||
body.translated_text: 'Lie latent' is the governing [verb]. Whatever dharma a latent defilement is associated with — it lies latent in that associated [dharma] by way of association, as long as it remains unabandoned — this is what the word 'but' distinguishes. And from this the following is also established: those with uncontaminated objects and those with dissimilar-realm objects lie latent only by way of association. Those with contaminated objects [lie latent] in their own level both by way of object and by way of association.

body.text: kutaḥ punarete 'nuśayā ucyante ? taducyate | prāgāviṣkṛtametatprasaṅgāgataṃ na tu sūtritamiti | tadidānīṃ sūtragataṃ pradarśyate |
body.translated_text: But why are they called <s>anuśayas</s> (latent defilements)? That is stated. This was previously disclosed when it came up incidentally, but was not [formally] stated as a <s>sūtra</s>-teaching. Now what appears in the <s>sūtra</s> is shown:

children.translated_text: By the analogies of a wet-nurse, cloth, and stain; and by the pattern of sky-dwellers and water-dwellers —
because they lie latent, therefore they are called <s>anuśayas</s> (latent defilements). (Abhidh-d 287)

body.text: itaśca,
body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: Because they lie latent through modes such as the 'pleasant' and the rest, in objects as subtle as atoms and moments —
therefore they are considered <s>anuśayas</s>. (Abhidh-d 288)

body.text: tatra rāgastāvadiṣṭākāreṇa khaṇḍakṣīrabhakṣaṇavat | dveṣastvaniṣṭākāreṇa kāñjikakodravaudanabhakṣaṇavadityevamādi | paramāṇuṣu kṣaṇeṣu ca sūkṣmeṣvekeṣvapyanuśerata ityanuśayāḥ | niruktanyāyena pūrvaṃ vā prāptimutsṛjya paścātsamudācārato 'nuśerata ityanuśayāḥ | anyat pūrvameva vyākhyātamiti ||
body.translated_text: There, first, passion lies latent through the mode of 'pleasant,' like the eating of sweetened milk. But aversion [lies latent] through the mode of 'unpleasant,' like the eating of sour <s>kāñjika</s>-gruel and <s>kodrava</s>-rice — and so on in this manner. They lie latent even in atoms and moments as subtle as individual [units] — therefore [they are called] <s>anuśayas</s>. Or, by the method of etymology: having first relinquished [overt] possession (<s>prāpti</s>), they subsequently lie latent through [renewed] manifestation — therefore [they are called] <s>anuśayas</s>. The rest has been explained previously.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau pañcamasyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the first section (<s>pāda</s>) of the fifth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: pañcamādhyāye
body.translated_text: Fifth chapter,

body.text: dvitīyapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: second section.

body.text: athaiṣāmaṣṭānavateranuśayānāṃ katyakuśalāḥ katyavyākṛtāḥ ? tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: Now, of these ninety-eight latent defilements, how many are unwholesome and how many are indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>)? That is now commenced:

children.translated_text: The first pair of views in the desire[-realm] is considered obscured-indeterminate (<s>nivṛtāvyākṛta</s>).

children.text: dhātudvaye tu sarve 'pi nivṛtāvyākṛtā malāḥ // Abhidh-d_289 //
children.translated_text: But in the two [upper] realms, all defilements are obscured-indeterminate. (Abhidh-d 289)

body.text: kāmadhātau tāvat | satkāyāntargrāhadṛṣṭī tatsaṃprayuktāvidye nivṛtāvyākṛte | satkāyadṛṣṭistāvaddānaśīlabhāvanābhiraviruddhatvātkuśalamūlasamucchedavairodhikatvācca nākuśalā | viparītākāratvānna kuśalā | tṛṣṇāvadakuśaleti cet | na | tṛṣṇāprakarṣe sarvākāryapravṛttidarśanā t | antargrāhadṛṣṭirapi janmocchedapravṛttatvānnirvāṇavirodhinī saṃvegānukūlā ceti nākuśalā | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā- "yeyaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ sarvaṃ me na kṣamata itīyaṃ dṛṣṭirasaṃrāgāya na saṃrāgāya" iti | tathoktam- idamagryaṃ bāhyakānāṃ dṛṣṭikṛtānāṃ yaduta no ca syānna ca me syānna bhaviṣyāmi na me bhaviṣyati" iti | rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 246)

children.text: ) 'sarve 'pi nivṛtāvyākṛtā malāḥ |'; samādhisamāpattyupahatatvāt na śaknuvanti nivartayitum | kuśalāstu dharmā avyābādhaphalatvādvipākaṃ janayitumutsahante ||
children.translated_text: 'all defilements are morally indeterminate-with-obstruction' — because, being impaired by <s>samādhi</s> and meditative attainment, they are unable to cause turning away [from virtue]. But wholesome dharmas, because their fruit is non-affliction, are capable of producing maturation.

body.translated_text: First, in the desire realm: the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the extreme view (<s>antargrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), and the ignorance associated with them are morally indeterminate-with-obstruction (<s>nivṛtāvyākṛta</s>). The view of the existing body, being non-contradictory with giving, moral discipline, and meditation, and because it contradicts the cutting off of wholesome roots, is not unwholesome. Because it apprehends in a distorted manner, it is not wholesome. If one says 'it is unwholesome like craving' — no, because in the intensification of craving, engagement in all [kinds of] wrongdoing is observed. The extreme view (<s>antargrāhadṛṣṭi</s>) also, because it operates toward the cutting off of births, is opposed to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, yet is conducive to spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>) — therefore it is not unwholesome. As the Blessed One said: 'That view which holds "nothing is acceptable to me" — this view is for non-attachment, not for attachment.' Similarly it is said: 'This is the highest of the views of outsiders based on views — namely, "I shall not be, [what is] mine shall not be; I shall not exist, [what is] mine shall not exist."' In the form and formless realms,

children.translated_text: The remaining ones in the desire realm are unwholesome. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: satkāyāntargrāhadṛṣṭitatsaṃprayuktāvidyāvarjitāḥ kleśāḥ kāmadhātāvakuśalāḥ, savyābādhaphalanirvartakatvāt |
body.translated_text: The <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) in the desire realm, excluding the view of the existing body, the extreme view, and the ignorance associated with them, are unwholesome — because they produce a result that involves affliction.

body.text: ebhyaḥ punaḥ katyakuśalamūlāni kati neti ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now, of these, how many are unwholesome roots and how many are not? That is stated:

children.translated_text: From attachment, aversion, and delusion — (Abhidh-d continuation)
there are only three unwholesome roots, by the conjunction of five reasons. (Abhidh-d 290)

body.text: ye dharmā akuśalāścākuśalamūlaṃ ca darśanabhāvanāheyāśca pañcaprakārāśca ṣaḍvijñānakāyikāśca ta evākuśalamūlānīṣyante ||
body.translated_text: Those dharmas that are unwholesome and are unwholesome roots, and are to be abandoned by the path of seeing and the path of meditation, and are of five kinds, and belong to the six consciousness-groups — those alone are held to be the unwholesome roots.

body.text: kiṃ punaryathākuśalāni anuśayānāṃ mūlāni santyevamavyākṛtānāmapi santīti ?
body.translated_text: Now, just as there are roots of the unwholesome among the latent tendencies (<s>anuśayas</s>), are there also [roots] of the morally indeterminate? He says:

children.translated_text: Of the twofold indeterminate also, there are three roots, equal to them — (Abhidh-d 291)

children.text: avidyā dhīśca tṛṣṇā ca na kāṅkṣāmānadṛṣṭayaḥ // Abhidh-d_291 //
children.translated_text: ignorance, wisdom, and craving — but not doubt, pride, or views.

body.text: "trīṇi khalvavyākṛtamūlāni, avyākṛtāvidyā tṛṣṇā prajñā" iti kāśmīrāḥ | hetvartho hi mūlārthaḥ | anivṛtāvyākṛtā ca prajñā hetutvena vartata ityasāvapyavyākṛtamūlam | vicikitsā nāvyākṛtamalam | na ca mānaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Kāśmīras</s> [say]: 'There are indeed three indeterminate roots — indeterminate ignorance, craving, and wisdom.' For the meaning of 'root' is the meaning of 'cause.' And indeterminate wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) functions as a cause — therefore it too is an indeterminate root. Doubt is not an indeterminate defilement. Nor is pride.

body.text: calatvādūrdhvavṛttitvādavyāpitvādyathākramam /
body.translated_text: Because of instability, upward operation, and non-pervasiveness, respectively. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: calā hi vicikitsā pratiṣṭhārthaścamūlārthaḥ | ūrdhvavṛttirunnatalakṣaṇo mānaḥ, adhogamanavṛttīni ca mūlāni | na caitau kleśau ṣaḍvijñānakāyikau | tasmādavyāpitvānna mūleṣu vyavasthāpyete |
body.translated_text: For doubt is unstable, and the meaning of 'root' is the meaning of 'firm standing.' Pride has the characteristic of elevation, operating upward, while roots have the function of going downward. And these two afflictions do not belong to the six consciousness-groups. Therefore, because of non-pervasiveness, they are not established among the roots.

body.text: avyākṛtāḥ tṛṣṇādṛṣṭimānāvidyā iti bahirdeśīyakāḥ, dhyāyisūtrokteḥ | trayo hi dhyāyinaḥ- tṛṣṇādṛṣṭimānottaradhyāyibhedāt | sarve ca te 'vidyāvaśādbhavantīti catvāryeva iti |
body.translated_text: The outsiders [say]: 'The indeterminate [roots] are craving, views, pride, and ignorance' — because of the statement in the <s>Dhyāyisūtra</s>. For there are three [types of] meditators — differentiated as those dominated by craving, by views, and by pride. And since all of these arise through the power of ignorance, there are just four — thus [they say].

body.text: etacca na te | kasmāt ?
body.translated_text: But this is not [correct]. Why?

body.text: sūtrasyārthāparijñānādaheturdhyāyicodanāt // Abhidh-d_292 //
body.translated_text: Because of misunderstanding the meaning of the <s>Sūtra</s>, and because the instruction regarding meditators is not a cause [for determining roots]. (Abhidh-d 292)

body.text: na khalveṣā dhyāyitritvacodanāvyākṛtamūlanirdeśaparā | kiṃ parā tarhyeṣā ? yogināṃ vipattidhyānādhimokṣavyāvṛttipareti pūrvoktameva sādhuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, this instruction regarding three types of meditators is not intended as an indication of indeterminate roots. What then is its purpose? It is intended for turning [meditators] away from the meditation on failure and their [various] convictions — therefore what was stated previously is correct.

body.text: atha yāni sūtre caturdaśāvyākṛtavastūnyuktāni, kiṃ tāni kuśalākuśalapakṣāvyākaraṇādavyākṛtavastūni ? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi ? sthāpanīyatvāt |
body.translated_text: Now, regarding the fourteen indeterminate matters (<s>avyākṛtavastūni</s>) stated in the <s>Sūtra</s> — are they indeterminate matters because they are not declared as belonging to the wholesome or unwholesome class? No, he says. What then? Because they are to be set aside (<s>sthāpanīya</s>).

children.translated_text: The Best of Speakers declared four [types of] answering questions, (Abhidh-d 293)

children.text: śiṣyāṇāṃ vādaśikṣārthaṃ sthitīnāṃ ca catuṣṭayīm // Abhidh-d_293 //
children.translated_text: and a tetrad of positions, for the purpose of training disciples in debate.

body.text: trīṇi khalu kathāvastūnyārabhya catvāri vyākaraṇānyāvabudhya catasraśca sthitīravagamya vigṛhya sabhāyāṃ pañcabhiravayavaiḥ svapakṣaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya vādaḥ karaṇīyo nāto 'nyathā ityatra viniścayāt ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, having undertaken three topics of discussion, having understood the four [types of] answers, and having comprehended the four positions, one should conduct debate in an assembly by establishing one's own thesis with five members [of a syllogism] — not otherwise — such is the determination here.

body.text: kāni punastāni catvāri vyākaraṇāni ? kāśca tāścatasraḥ sthitayaḥ ? tadavadyotyate-
body.translated_text: Now, what are those four [types of] answers? And what are those four positions? That is elucidated:

children.translated_text: The categorical answer, the analytical answer, the counter-question answer, and the one to be set aside — (Abhidh-d 294)
like death, birth, superiority, and the [question about] <s>jīva</s> and substance being the same or different, and so forth.

body.text: tatraikāṃśavyākaraṇam- kiṃ yaḥ kaścijjāyate sarvosau mriyate? omiti vācyam | atha yaḥ kaścinmriyate sarvosau jāyata iti ? vibhajya vyākartavyam- kṣīṇāsravo na jāyate 'nyaḥ sarvoṃ jāyate | kiṃ manuṣyo viśiṣṭo 'tha hīna iti ? paripṛcchya vyākartavyam- kānadhikṛtya pṛcchasi ? devāṃstiryagādīnvā ? yadi devānārabhya hīna iti vācyam | atha tiraścaḥ śreṣṭha iti vyākartavyam | kimanyaḥ skandhebhyaḥ puruṣo vānanya iti ? eṣa praśnaḥ sthāpanīyaḥ, sadasatoranyānanyatvavyākaraṇāyogāt, khapuṣpasaugandhyadaurgandhyavyākaraṇavat ||
body.translated_text: Therein, a categorical answer: 'Does everyone who is born necessarily die?' — 'Yes' is to be said. 'But does everyone who dies necessarily get reborn?' — This is to be answered analytically: 'One whose outflows are destroyed (<s>kṣīṇāsrava</s>) is not reborn; everyone else is reborn.' 'Is a human being superior or inferior?' — This is to be answered by counter-question: 'With respect to whom are you asking? Gods, animals, and the like?' If asking with reference to gods, [the answer is] 'inferior.' If with reference to animals, 'superior' is to be answered. 'Is the person (<s>puruṣa</s>) the same as or different from the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>)?' — This question is to be set aside, because answering sameness or difference of the existent and non-existent is impossible — like answering whether a sky-flower has a pleasant or unpleasant fragrance.

body.text: sthitayaścatasro nirdiśyante |
body.translated_text: The four positions are now indicated:

children.translated_text: One is called 'standing on grounds,' another is called 'on suppositions,' (Abhidh-d 295)
another is called 'on procedure,' and another is designated 'standing on knowledge.'

body.text: kaściddhi vādī sthānāsthāne saṃbhavāsaṃbhavākhye saṃtiṣṭhate kaścinna saṃtiṣṭhate | prathamaḥ kathyaḥ, dvitīyastvakathyaḥ | parikalpe saṃtiṣṭhate, yaḥ parikalpite dṛṣṭānte dārṣṭāntikārthe prasādhake saṃtiṣṭhate, sa ca kathyo yo na santiṣṭhate so 'kathyaḥ | evaṃ pratipadi jñānavāditāyāṃ yaḥ santiṣṭhate sa kathyate | yastu na saṃtiṣṭhate sa durmatirakathyate |
body.translated_text: For a debater either stands firm on grounds — called 'possibility and impossibility' — or does not stand firm. The first is [fit to be] debated with; the second, however, is not [fit to be] debated with. [One who] stands firm on supposition — who stands firm on the supposed illustration, the illustrated meaning, and the proof — he is [fit to be] debated with; one who does not stand firm is not [fit to be] debated with. Similarly, regarding procedure and standing on knowledge — one who stands firm is to be debated with; but one who does not stand firm is a dull-witted person not [fit to be] debated with.

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | atha kenānuśayena kasminvastuni saṃyuktaḥ ? tatra tāvadvastu kṣetravastvādipañcaprakāram | tadiha saṃyogavastvadhikṛtaṃ veditavyam | tad dvividhamāśrayālambananaiyamyena prakāranaiyamyena ca |
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: By which latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>) is [a person] bound with respect to which object? There, first, the object is of five kinds — field-object and the rest. Here, the binding-object is to be understood. That is twofold: by the determination of basis and object (<s>āśrayālambana</s>), and by the determination of type (<s>prakāra</s>).

body.text: tatrāśrayālambananaiyamyena tāvaccakṣurvijñānakāyikairanuśayaiḥ, rūpeṣvālambanataḥ saṃyuktaḥ | tatsaṃprayukteṣu saṃprayogataḥ | te ca manodharmāyatane | evaṃ yāvatkāyavijñānikairyathāviṣayamālambanataḥ, tatsaṃprayukteṣu saṃprayogataḥ | manovijñānakāyikairdvādaśasvāyataneṣvālambanataḥ | saṃprayukteṣu saṃprayogataḥ | ityāśrayālambananiyamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, first by the determination of basis and object: by latent tendencies belonging to the eye-consciousness group, one is bound with respect to forms as objects. With respect to those associated [dharmas], by association. And they are in the mental-dharma sense-base. Similarly, up to the body-consciousness group — bound by object according to their respective domains; with respect to their associated [dharmas], by association. By those belonging to the mental consciousness group, bound by object with respect to [all] twelve sense-bases. With respect to their associated [dharmas], by association. This is the determination by basis and object.

body.text: prakāranaiyamyena tu duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaiḥ sarvatragaiḥ pañcasu nikāyeṣvālambanataḥ saṃyuktaḥ | tatsaṃprayukteṣu saṃprayogataḥ | asarvatragaistu svanaikāyikeṣvālambanataḥ | saṃprayukteṣu saṃprayogataḥ | ityevaṃ sarvatra yathāsaṃbhavaṃ vaktavyam ||
body.translated_text: By the determination of type: by those [afflictions] to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering that are universal (<s>sarvatraga</s>), one is bound by object in [all] five classes [of dharmas to be abandoned]. With respect to those associated [dharmas], by association. But by the non-universal ones, bound by object only in those of one's own class. With respect to their associated [dharmas], by association. Thus everywhere, this is to be stated according to possibility.

body.text: athedānīmatītānāgatapratyutpannanaiyamyena kaḥ pudgalaḥ kasminvastuni katamenānuśayena saṃyuktaḥ ? tadidamudbhāvyate-
body.translated_text: Now, by the determination of past, future, and present — which person is bound by which latent tendency with respect to which object? That is elucidated:

children.translated_text: By pride, aversion, and attachment — [those that are] present and have engaged in action — (Abhidh-d 296)
wherever [they have] arisen and are not abandoned, one is bound with respect to that object.

body.text: ete hi mānapratigharāgāḥ svalakṣaṇakleśāḥ sadvastuviṣayatvāt | sāmānyalakṣaṇakleśāstu dṛṣṭivicikitsādyāḥ | ata ete mānādayo 'tītāḥ pratyutpannāśca yasminvastunyutpannā na ca prahīṇāstasminvastuni taiḥ saṃprayukto veditavyaḥ | nahyete sarvasya sarvatrotpadyante svalakṣaṇakleśatvāt ||
body.translated_text: For these — pride, aversion, and attachment — are afflictions with specific characteristics, because they have existing objects as their domain. But afflictions with general characteristics are views, doubt, and the like. Therefore, these [specific ones] — pride and the rest — whether past or present, wherever they have arisen and have not been abandoned, one should be known as bound by them with respect to that object. For these do not arise in everyone everywhere, because they are afflictions with specific characteristics.

children.translated_text: By these [same afflictions that are] unarisen and mental, [one is bound] everywhere; by other unarisen ones [that are] of one's own time-period, (Abhidh-d 297)
and by the remaining unarisen ones likewise — the continuum of aggregates is bound.

body.text: yathā prahīṇā iti vartate | yasya khalu yo 'tītaḥ kleśaprakāraḥ prahīṇo 'nāgato 'pi | ato ye mānarāgadayo nāgatā na prahīṇāstaiḥ sarvasmiṃstraiyadhvike vastuni saṃyuktaḥ | tadālambanānāmutpattisaṃbhavānmānasānāṃ ca traiyadhvaviṣayatvāt | ato 'nyai rāgādibhiranāgatairanāgata eva vastuni saṃyukto 'tītairatīta eva pratyutpannaiḥ pratyutpanna eva | mānasebhyo hyanye pañcavijñānakāyikāḥ | tataḥ siddhaṃ bhavatyatītapratyutpannairapi mānasairasvādhvike 'pi vastunyaprahīṇaiḥ saṃyuktaḥ syānna ca kevalaṃ mānasairevānāgatairebhiḥ sarvatra | kiṃ tarhi ? pañcavijñānakāyikairapi | anutpattidharmikaistu pañcavijñānakāyikaiḥ sarvatra traiyadhvikairvastuni saṃyuktaḥ, tadviṣayasyātītānāgatapratyutpannatvāt | sāmānyakleśaistu dṛṣṭivicikitsāvidyākhyaistraiyadhvikairapi sarvasmiṃstraiyadhvike vastuni saṃyuktaḥ, teṣāṃ sāmānyakleśatvādyāvadaprahīṇā ityanuvartate |
body.translated_text: 'As [they are] not abandoned' — this [qualification] continues [from above]. Of whomsoever, whichever past type of affliction is abandoned, the future [one] is also [abandoned]. Therefore, by those unarisen [afflictions] — pride, attachment, and the rest — that are not abandoned, one is bound with respect to all objects across the three times. Because the arising of those whose object is that is possible, and because mental [afflictions] have objects across the three times. By other [afflictions such as] attachment and the rest that are future, one is bound only with respect to future objects; by past ones, only with respect to past [objects]; by present ones, only with respect to present [objects]. For apart from mental [afflictions], there are [afflictions] belonging to the five sensory consciousness groups. Hence it is established that one would be bound by past and present mental [afflictions] too, that are not abandoned, with respect to objects not of their own time-period — and not only by future mental ones everywhere. What then? By those belonging to the five sensory consciousness groups as well. But by [afflictions] belonging to the five sensory consciousness groups that will never arise, one is bound everywhere with respect to objects across the three times — because their object can be past, future, or present. By afflictions with general characteristics — called views, doubt, and ignorance — even those across the three times, one is bound with respect to all objects across the three times, because they are afflictions with general characteristics — 'as long as [they are] not abandoned' continues.

body.text: kathaṃ punargamyate 'tītādiṣu vastuṣu rāgādaya utpadyante taiśca tatra saṃyukto bhavatīti ? sūtrādeva hi | bhagavatoktam- "trayaśchandarāgasthānīyā dharmāḥ | atītāśchandarāgasthānīyā dharmāḥ, anāgatapratyutpannāḥ | atītāṃśchandarāgasthānīyāndharmānpratītyotpadyate cchandaḥ | utpanne cchande saṃprayuktastairdharmairvaktavyo (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 254)

children.text: ) na visaṃyuktaḥ |" tathā- "yasmin rūpe 'tītānāgatapratyutpanne utpadyate 'nunayo vā pratigho vā |" ityevamādi |
children.translated_text: not dissociated [from them].' Similarly: 'With respect to which form — past, future, or present — there arises satisfaction or aversion' — and so forth.

body.translated_text: How then is it understood that attachment and the rest arise with respect to past and other objects, and that one is bound by them therein? From the <s>Sūtra</s> itself. The Blessed One said: 'There are three classes of dharmas that are grounds for desire-and-attachment: past dharmas that are grounds for desire-and-attachment, and future and present ones. With respect to past dharmas that are grounds for desire-and-attachment, desire arises. When desire has arisen, one is to be said to be bound by association with those dharmas,

body.text: kaḥ punaratra saṃyujyate ? yadā śūnyāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ, nityena dhruveṇa śāśvatenāvipariṇāmadharmeṇātmanātmīyena vā ? yathoktam- "asti karmāsti vipākaḥ kārakastu nopalabhyate ya imāṃśca skandhān pratinikṣipyānyān skandhān pratisaṃdadhātītyanyatra dharmasaṃketāt" iti vistaraḥ |
body.translated_text: But who is it that is bound here? When all conditioned formations are empty of a permanent, stable, eternal, unchanging self or anything belonging to a self? As stated: 'There is action, there is maturation, but no agent is found who casts off these aggregates and takes up other aggregates — except through the conventional designation of dharmas' — and so on in detail.

body.text: tatra pratisamādhānam- 'saṃyuktā skandhasantatiḥ |'; skandhasantatau hi skandhalakṣaṇasantānaikatvābhimānāt, saṃṣṛtyā sattvasaṃjñaptirityadoṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The resolution there is: 'The continuum of aggregates is bound.' For in the continuum of aggregates, due to the conceit of identity of the continuum with the characteristics of aggregates, there is the conventional designation 'being' through transmigration — thus there is no fault.

body.text: trayātpunaretasmāt-
body.translated_text: Furthermore, of these three —

body.text: dvayamevātra niṣpannaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tūpacārataḥ /
body.translated_text: only two are truly existent here; the third is by figurative usage. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: vastusaṃyo nākhyaṃ dvayaṃ paramārthato vidyate sattvākhyastu tṛtīyo 'rthaḥ saṃvṛtyā vidyata iti |
body.translated_text: Two — called 'object' and 'bondage' — exist ultimately. But the third meaning — called 'being' — exists only conventionally.

body.text: kutaḥ punaretad dvayaṃ paramārthato vidyate ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: How then is it [known] that these two exist ultimately? That is stated:

body.text: sadasaddhetutā yasmānmadhyasthaiśca parigrahāt // Abhidh-d_298 //
body.translated_text: Because [they function as] causes of good and bad, and because of acceptance by the impartial. (Abhidh-d 298)

body.text: śubhāśubhaphalaṃ karmanaiyamyād guṇadoṣaphalaniyamyatā | kiñca, 'madhyasthaiśca parigrahāt |'; madhyasthā ucyante vītakleśāḥ | taiḥ śubhaṃ ca śubhato 'śubhaṃ cāśubhataḥ, guṇāśca guṇataḥ doṣāśca doṣataḥ parigṛhītaḥ | tatphalaṃ ceṣṭamiṣṭataḥ parigṛhītamaniṣṭaṃ cāniṣṭataḥ | iti siddhaṃ dvayaṃ pariniṣpannaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tūpacārata iti |
body.translated_text: Because of the determination of wholesome and unwholesome action [leading to their respective] fruits, there is the determination of [specific] fruits of merit and demerit. Moreover, 'because of acceptance by the impartial' — the impartial are said to be those free from afflictions. By them, the wholesome is accepted as wholesome and the unwholesome as unwholesome; merit as merit and demerit as demerit. And the desired fruit is accepted as desired, and the undesired as undesired. Thus it is established that two are truly existent, and the third is by figurative usage.

body.text: yuktaṃ tāvadidam | yadidaṃ pratyuktaṃ vastuhetupratyayātpratītyotpannaṃ paramārthato vidyate pratyātmavedanīyatvāt, tadālambanāśca rāgādayaḥ dravyataḥ santīti | yatpunaridamuktamatītānāgate vastuni traiyadhvikairanuśayaiḥ saṃyukta iti tadetatsāhasamāhopuruṣikamātram | kaḥ punaretadatītānāgatādi dravyato 'bhivāñcchatītyāhābhidhārmikāḥ ||
body.translated_text: This much is reasonable — namely, the response that objects arising from causes and conditions through dependent origination exist ultimately, because they are personally experienced; and that attachment and the rest, having those as objects, exist substantially. But the statement that one is bound by latent tendencies across the three times with respect to past and future objects — this is merely bold presumption. 'But who would desire this — that past and future [objects] exist substantially?' — say the <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s>.

body.text: catvāraḥ khalviha pravacane vādinaḥ | katame catvāraḥ ? tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: There are indeed four [schools of] disputants in this teaching. Which four? That is indicated:

children.translated_text: Everything exists; a part exists; nothing at all exists —
and the indeterminate-existence proponent — these four disputants are known. (Abhidh-d 299)

body.text: tatra sarvāstivādasyādhvatrayamasti sa dhruvatrayamiti | vibhajyavādinastu dārṣṭāntikasya ca pradeśo vartamānādhvasaṃjñakaḥ | vaitulikasya ayogaśūnyatāvādinaḥ (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 258]

children.text: ) sarvaṃ nāstīti | paudgalikasyāpi avyākṛtavastuvādinaḥ pudgalo 'pi dravyato 'stīti |
children.translated_text: ), nothing at all exists. And for the <s>Pudgalavādin</s> too, the proponent of an indeterminate entity, the <s>pudgala</s> (person) also exists as a substance.

body.translated_text: Therein, for the <s>Sarvāstivādin</s>, the three time-periods exist — he is [the proponent of] the three permanences. But for the <s>Vibhajyavādin</s> and the <s>Dārṣṭāntika</s>, a part — namely, that designated as the present time-period [exists]. For the <s>Vaitulika</s>, the proponent of the emptiness of non-connection (

body.text: atra punaḥ
body.translated_text: Here, furthermore:

children.text: ebhyo yaḥ prathamo vādī bhajate sādhutāmasau /
children.translated_text: Among these, the first disputant attains excellence;
but the others, proud of mere reasoning, are excluded from [valid] logic and scripture. (Abhidh-d 300)

body.text: yaḥ khalveṣa prathamo vādī sarvāstivādākhyaḥ, eṣa khalu yuktyāgamopapannābhidhāyitvātsadvādī | tadanye bādino dārṣṭāntikavaitulikapaudgalikāḥ na yuktyāgamābhidhāyinaḥ, tarkābhimāninaste | mithyāvāditvādete lokāyatikavaināśikanagnāṭapakṣe (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 259]
