). Therefore, 'I shall demonstrate that everything exists in all [time-periods].'

body.translated_text: Indeed, this first disputant called <s>Sarvāstivāda</s> is a true proponent, because he speaks in accordance with [valid] logic and scripture. The others — the <s>Dārṣṭāntika</s>, <s>Vaitulika</s>, and <s>Pudgalavādin</s> — do not speak in accordance with logic and scripture; they are proud of mere reasoning. Because they hold wrong views, they should be classified in the camp of <s>Lokāyatikas</s> (materialists), <s>Vaināśikas</s> (nihilists), and naked ascetics (<s>Nagnāṭakas</s>) (

body.text: kaḥ punarayaṃ sarvāstivādī sādhutāṃ bhajate ? tadidamavadyotyate | eṣa khalu vādī
body.translated_text: Now, who is this <s>Sarvāstivādin</s> who attains excellence? That is now elucidated. This disputant indeed —

children.translated_text: accepts the three time-periods and, by function, the three permanences;
therefore the <s>Sarvāstivāda</s> is said [to be] the first [school], and it is fourfold. (Abhidh-d 301)

body.text: khalveṣa sarvāstivādaścaturdhā bhedaṃ pratipannaḥ | katham ? tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: Indeed, this <s>Sarvāstivāda</s> has undergone a fourfold division. How? That is now commenced:

children.translated_text: Two [are called] the 'difference-of-nature' and the 'difference-of-characteristic'; another is the 'difference-of-state';
and another is the 'difference-in-every-respect' — the third is [preferred], because of [sound] reasoning. (Abhidh-d 302)

body.text: tatra bhāvānyathiko bhadantadharmatrātaḥ | sa hyevamāha- dharmasyādhvasu pravartamānasyānāgatādibhāvamātramanyathā bhavati | na dravyānyathātvam | yathā suvarṇasya kaṭakādisaṃsthānāntareṇa kriyamāṇasya pūrvasaṃsthānanāśe suvarṇanāśaḥ | kṣīrasya vā dadhitvena pariṇamato yathā rasavīryavipākaparityāgo na varṇasyeti | tadeṣa vārṣagaṇyapakṣabhajamānatvāttadvargya eva draṣṭavyaḥ | yasmāt eṣo 'vasthitasya dravyasya jātilakṣaṇasya samudāyarūpasya vānyathānyathāvasthānalakṣaṇaṃ pariṇāmamicchati |
body.translated_text: Therein, the proponent of difference-of-nature is the venerable <s>Dharmatrāta</s>. He indeed says thus: when a <s>dharma</s> traverses the time-periods, only its mode of being — such as being future and so forth — becomes different, not its substantial nature. Just as when gold is fashioned into a bracelet and other forms, the destruction of the former shape does not [entail] the destruction of the gold; or just as when milk transforms into yogurt, the flavor, potency, and maturation are abandoned but not the color. But this [view] should be regarded as belonging to the <s>Vārṣagaṇya</s> [Sāṃkhya] camp, because it subscribes to the <s>Vārṣagaṇya</s> position — since he accepts transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) characterized by the assuming of different states of what is a substantially established entity having a fixed generic characteristic or an aggregate-form.

body.text: lakṣaṇānyathiko bhadantaghoṣaka iha paśyatyatīto dharmo 'tītalakṣaṇena yukto 'nāgatapratyutpannalakṣaṇābhyāmaviyuktaḥ, evamanāgatapratyutpannāvapi | yathā puruṣaḥ (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 260]

children.text: ) ekasyāṃ striyāṃ rakto 'nyāsvaviraktaḥ | tadasyāpyadhvasaṃkaro bhavatyekasya dharmasya trilakṣaṇayogābhyupagamāt | eṣo 'pi puruṣakāraṇi(?)vāgurāyāṃ praveśayitavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) attached to one woman is not [thereby] free from passion toward the others. But for him too, confusion of time-periods arises, because he accepts the conjunction of a single <s>dharma</s> with three characteristics. He too should be driven into the snare of [the fallacy of] anthropomorphism (?).

body.translated_text: The proponent of difference-of-characteristic is the venerable <s>Ghoṣaka</s>. He holds: a past <s>dharma</s> is conjoined with the past characteristic [but] not dissociated from the future and present characteristics — and likewise for the future and present. Just as a man (

body.text: avasthānyathiko bhadantavasumitraḥ | sa khalvāha- dharmo 'dhvasu pravartamāno 'vasthāmavasthāṃ prāpyānyathānyathāstīti nirdiśyate | avasthāntaraviśeṣavikārātsvabhāvāparityāgācca | yathā nikṣepavartikaikāṅkavinyastaiketyucyate, saiva śatāṅke śataṃ sahasrāṅke sahasramiti |
body.translated_text: The proponent of difference-of-state is the venerable <s>Vasumitra</s>. He indeed says: a <s>dharma</s>, traversing the time-periods, is designated differently in different states when it reaches [each] state — because of the modification of a particular state, and because its intrinsic nature is not abandoned. Just as a single counting-piece, when placed on the ones column, is called 'one'; the same on the hundreds column [is called] 'a hundred'; and on the thousands column, 'a thousand.'

body.text: anyathānyathiko bhadantabuddhadevaḥ | sa brūte | dharmo 'dhvasu pravartamānaḥ pūrvāparamavekṣyānyathā cānyathā cocyate | naivāsya bhāvānyathātvaṃ bhavati dravyānyathātvaṃ vā | athaikā strī pūrvāparamapekṣya mātā cocyate duhitā ca | tadvaddharmo 'nāgatapratyutpannamapekṣyātīta ityucyate | tathetaro 'pītaradvayamapekṣyeti |
body.translated_text: The proponent of difference-in-every-respect is the venerable <s>Buddhadeva</s>. He says: a <s>dharma</s>, traversing the time-periods, is called different in different ways with reference to what precedes and what follows — but there is no difference of nature or difference of substance for it. Just as one woman is called 'mother' and 'daughter' with reference to what precedes and follows. Similarly, a <s>dharma</s> is called 'past' with reference to the future and the present, and likewise the others with reference to the other two.

body.text: asyāpyekasyātītasyādhvanaḥ pūrvottarakṣaṇadvayamapekṣyādhvatritvāpattidoṣaprasaṅgaḥ |
body.translated_text: For him too, there is the fault of arriving at a threefold time-period for a single past time-period, by having reference to its two moments — prior and subsequent.

body.text: tadebhyaścaturbhyaḥ sarvāstivādebhyastṛtīyaḥ sthaviravasumitraḥ pañcaviṃśatitattvanirāsī paramāṇusaṃcayavādonmāthīca | ityato 'sāveva yuktyāgamānusāritvādāptaḥ prāmāṇika ityadhyavaseyam |
body.translated_text: Now, among these four <s>Sarvāstivādins</s>, the third — the elder <s>Vasumitra</s> — refutes the twenty-five principles [of Sāṃkhya] and demolishes the doctrine of atomic aggregation. Therefore, because he alone follows logic and scripture, he should be recognized as authoritative and reliable.

body.text: bhadantabuddhadevo 'pi tīrthyapakṣyabhajamānatvānna parigṛhyate |
body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Buddhadeva</s> too is not accepted, because he subscribes to the position of the non-Buddhist schools.

body.text: bhadantaghoṣako 'pyadhvasaṃkaravāditvādekaikasyādhvano 'dhvatrayalakṣaṇabhāgbhavati |
body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ghoṣaka</s> too, because he holds the confusion of time-periods — [since] each individual time-period would partake of the characteristics of all three time-periods.

body.text: ityatastṛtīya evāpadoṣaḥ | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Therefore, the third alone is free from fault. Because —

children.translated_text: he desires the determination of the time-periods through function alone;
a [dharma] performing that [function] is the present time-period; with [function] done, past; with [function] undone, future. (Abhidh-d 303)

body.text: ye khalu bhagavatoktāḥ svabhāvasiddhāstraiyādhvikā dharmā atītānāgatapratyutpannāsteṣāmayamācāryaḥ kriyādvāreṇāvasthābhedamicchatyajahatsvarūpo hetusāmagrīsannidhānaprabodhitaśaktiḥ | kriyāvān hi saṃskāro vartamāna ityucyate | sa eva tyaktakriyo 'tīto 'nupāttakriyo 'nāgataḥ | ityevaṃ ca sati kālatrayasyaikādhikaraṇyamekādhiṣṭhānavyāpāraparicchedyatvaṃ copapannam | anyathaikadravyajātinimittābhāve vaiyadhikaraṇye sati kālatrayasaṃbandhābhāvaḥ prāpnuyāditi |
body.translated_text: Indeed, those <s>dharmas</s> of the three time-periods — past, future, and present — spoken of by the <s>Bhagavat</s>, whose intrinsic nature is established, this <s>Ācārya</s> accepts their distinction of states through the doorway of function, [as those] whose power has been awakened by the proximity of the aggregate of causes, without abandoning their own nature. For a conditioned thing (<s>saṃskāra</s>) possessing function is called 'present'; the same, having relinquished function, is 'past'; and not [yet] having taken up function, is 'future.' And when it is thus, the oneness of substratum of the three times, and [their] being delimited by a single foundation-activity, is established. Otherwise, in the absence of a single substance-class as ground, given their being of different substrata, the connection of the three times would be impossible.

body.text: atrāha codakaḥ- na, atītānāgatasyārthasya prajñaptyā vyapadeśasiddheḥ | na, paramārthadravyābhāve niradhiṣṭhānaprajñaptivyapadeśānupapatteḥ | vartamānāpekṣyastadvyapadeśa iti cet | na | vartamānasvarūpasthitiśaktikriyābhāve sattvānupapatteḥ, sadasatorapekṣāsaṃbandhābhāvācca | sattvalakṣaṇamidānīmeva dyotyate atītādīnāṃ padārthānām-
body.translated_text: Here the objector says: No — because the meaning of past and future is established by designation and conventional expression. [Reply:] No — because, in the absence of an ultimately real substance, it is impossible to have designation and conventional expression without a substrate. [Objection:] That expression is with reference to the present. [Reply:] No — because, in the absence of the power-activity of staying in one's own nature for the present [dharma alone], existence [of anything else] is impossible; and because, for what is existent and non-existent, the relation of mutual reference is absent. The characteristic of existence for entities such as past and future is now elucidated:

children.translated_text: That whose mark is perceived by the intellect — the knowable — is fourfold:
ultimately, conventionally, by both, and also by mutual reference. (Abhidh-d 304)

body.text: yasya khalvarthavastunaḥ svabhāvasiddhasvarūpasyāviparītākārayā dharmopalakṣaṇayā paricchinnaṃ lakṣaṇamupalakṣyate tatsaddravyamityucyate | tatpunaḥ sat pratibhidyamānaṃ caturvidhaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: Indeed, that entity whose intrinsic nature is established and whose characteristic is discerned by a cognition of undistorted aspect, serving as a mark of the <s>dharma</s>, is called 'real substance' (<s>saddravya</s>). That real [entity], when analyzed, becomes fourfold.

body.text: paramārthena yannityaṃ svabhāvena saṃgṛhītaṃ na kadācitsvamātmānaṃ jahāti, viśiṣṭajñānābhidhānāpauruṣeyaviṣayisaṃbandhaṃ tatparamārthasadityucyate |
body.translated_text: What is eternal by ultimate nature, grasped by its intrinsic nature, never abandoning its own self, [and] connected with a distinguished cognition, designation, and non-personal object-relation — that is called 'ultimately real' (<s>paramārthasat</s>).

body.text: yatpunaranekaparamārthasatyapṛṣṭhena byavahārārthaṃ prajñaptirūpatayā nirdiśyate tatsaṃvṛtisat | tadyathā dhaṭapaṭavanapugdalādikam |
body.translated_text: But that which, resting upon a multiplicity of ultimate truths, is indicated in conventional form for the purpose of ordinary usage — that is 'conventionally real' (<s>saṃvṛtisat</s>); such as a pot, cloth, forest, <s>pudgala</s> (person), and the like.

body.text: kiñcidubhayathā | tadyathā pṛthivyādi | kiñcitsattvā pekṣayā pitṛputraguruśiṣyakartṛkriyādi ||
body.translated_text: Some [things are real] in both ways — such as earth and the like. Some [are designated] with reference to living beings — such as father, son, teacher, pupil, agent, action, and the like.

body.text: atha yadidamuktaṃ dravyasanto 'tītānāgatādhvasthā dharmā iti tadāgamayuktyanabhidhānādabhidhānamātram | tasmādāgamayuktibhyāmupapādyo 'yamartha ityata idaṃ pratijñāyate-
body.translated_text: Now, the statement 'past and future <s>dharmas</s> existing in the time-periods are real substances' — since it is not established by scripture and logic, it is mere assertion. Therefore, this matter must be established by scripture and logic. Hence this is declared:

children.translated_text: The past and the unarisen are real, like the present, because of the <s>Buddha</s>'s statement;
and because of being objects of cognition, their reality is like the present. (Abhidh-d 305)

body.text: uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "asti bhikṣavo 'tītaṃ rūpaṃ nocedatītaṃ rūpaṃ abhaviṣyanneme sattvā atīte rūpe samarañjyantaḥ | yasmāttarhyastyatītaṃ rūpaṃ tasmādime sattvā atīte rūpe saṃrañjyante |" evamanāgatapratyutpannaṃ ceti vācyam | vibhaktipratirūpako 'yaṃ nipāta iti cet | na | vartamāne 'pi tatprasaṅgāt | kriyāvacanena cottarapadena pūrvasya kriyāvacanasyaiva padasya sāmānādhikaraṇyāt |
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bhagavat</s> has said: 'There is, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, past form. If past form did not exist, these beings would not become attached to past form. Because past form does exist, therefore these beings become attached to past form.' Similarly for the future and present — this should be stated. [Objection:] 'This particle is a substitute for a verbal inflection.' [Reply:] No — because the same consequence would apply to the present as well; and because, by the verbal expression in the latter compound, there is co-referentiality with the former [equally] verbal expression.

body.text: punaścoktaṃ bhagavatā- "rūpamanityamatītānāgatam, kaḥ punarvādaḥ pratyutpannasya ? evaṃdarśī śrutavānāryaśrāvako 'tīte rūpe 'napekṣo bhavatyanāgataṃ rūpaṃ nābhinandati | pratyutpannasya rūpasya nirvide virāgāya nirodhāya pratipanno bhavati | atītaṃ cedrūpaṃ nābhaviṣyanna śrutavānāryaśrāvako 'tīte rūpe 'napekṣo 'bhaviṣyat; yasmāttarhyastyatītaṃ rūpaṃ tasmācchrutavānāryaśrāvakaḥ atīte rūpe 'napekṣo bhavati" iti vistaraḥ |
body.translated_text: And again the <s>Bhagavat</s> has said: 'Form is impermanent — past and future. What need to speak of the present? Seeing thus, the learned noble disciple (<s>Āryaśrāvaka</s>) is indifferent toward past form, does not delight in future form, and is established on the path toward revulsion, dispassion, and cessation with regard to present form. If past form did not exist, the learned noble disciple would not be indifferent toward past form. Because past form does exist, therefore the learned noble disciple is indifferent toward past form' — and so on in detail.

body.text: tathoktam- yacchāriputra karmābhyatītaṃ kṣīṇaṃniruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ tadastīti | taccet karma śāriputra nābhaviṣyannehaikatīyastaddhetoḥ tatpratyayādapāya durgativinipātaṃ kāyasya bhedānnarakeṣūpapatsyate" iti vistaraḥ | (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 266]

children.text: ) tadāhitacittabhāvanāṃ sandhāya vacanādadoṣa iti cet | na | uktottaratvāt | uktottaro hyeṣa vādaḥ | kiṃ tilapīḍakavatpunarāvartase ?
children.translated_text: ) [Objection:] 'That statement is with reference to the mental cultivation previously deposited, so there is no fault.' [Reply:] No — because this objection has already been answered. This objection has indeed been answered. Why do you return to it again like an oil-presser [going round and round]?

body.translated_text: Likewise it is said: 'That <s>karma</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, which is past, exhausted, ceased, gone, and transformed — that exists. If that <s>karma</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, did not exist, then certain ones, on account of that cause and condition, upon the dissolution of the body, would [not] be reborn in the lower realms, evil destinies, and hells' — and so on in detail. (

body.text: kiñca, bhāvanābhāvyamānacittayoḥ svarūpaśaktikriyānupapatteḥ puṣṭavāsitatailavat, anyānanyatvādivakṣyamāṇadoṣācca |
body.translated_text: Moreover, because the power-activity of the intrinsic nature of both the cultivation and the mind being cultivated is impossible — like oil that has been pressed and scented — and because of the faults regarding identity, difference, and so forth that will be stated,

body.text: paramārthaśūnyatāsūtrādasaditi cet | na | tadarthāparijñānāt | tata evānāgatādyastitvasiddheśca | tatraitat syāt- paramārthaśūnyatā sūtre bhagavatā (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 267]

children.text: ) vispaṣṭamanāgatādināstitvaṃ pradarśitam | tatra hyaktam- "cakṣurūtpadyamānaṃ na kutaścidāgacchati, nirudhyamānaṃ na kvacitsaṃnicayaṃ gacchati" iti vistaraḥ | atītānāgatasadbhāve cāgatigatidoṣābhyupagamaḥ prāpnotīti |
children.translated_text: ) clearly demonstrated the non-existence of the future and the rest. For there it is said: 'The eye, when arising, does not come from anywhere; when ceasing, it does not go to any storehouse' — and so on in detail. And if past and future [dharmas] were real, the fault of [their] coming and going would have to be accepted.

body.translated_text: [Objection:] From the <s>Paramārthaśūnyatā Sūtra</s>, [past and future] do not exist. [Reply:] No — because of not having fully understood the meaning of that [sūtra]; and because from that very [sūtra], the existence of the future and the rest is established. One might think: in the <s>Paramārthaśūnyatā Sūtra</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s> (

body.text: etacca na | kutaḥ ? sūtrārthāparijñānāt | ata evānāgatādyastitvasiddheśca |
body.translated_text: But this is not so. Why? Because of not having fully understood the meaning of the sūtra; and because from that very [sūtra], the existence of the future and the rest is established.

body.text: sūtrasya tāvadayamarthaḥ | yaduktam- "cakṣurutpadyamānaṃ na kutaścidāgacchati, nirudhyamānaṃ na kvacitsaṃnicayaṃ gacchati" iti tadvedoktavādavidhipratiṣedhārthaṃ sāṃkhyamatavyudāsārthaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: The meaning of the sūtra, to begin with, is this: the statement 'the eye, when arising, does not come from anywhere; when ceasing, it does not go to any storehouse' — that is for the purpose of [refuting] the Vedic injunctions and prohibitions as stated in the <s>Vedas</s>, and for the purpose of removing the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine.

body.text: vede hyaktam- "pañcatvamāpadyamānasya cakṣurādityādāgataṃ punastatraiva prativigacchati | śrotramākāśam | ghrāṇaṃ pṛthivīm | jihvā āpaḥ | kāyo vāyum | manaḥ salilaṃ somamityarthaḥ |" tatpratiṣedhārthaṃ bhagavānavocat- "cakṣurutpadyamānaṃ na kutaścidāgacchati" iti vistaraḥ |
body.translated_text: For in the <s>Vedas</s> it is said: 'For one who is dying, the eye, having come from the sun, returns to that very [sun]; the ear to space; the nose to earth; the tongue to water; the body to wind; the mind to the waters, to <s>Soma</s> — this is the meaning.' To refute that, the <s>Bhagavat</s> declared: 'The eye, when arising, does not come from anywhere' — and so on in detail.

body.text: sāṃkhyāḥ khalvapyācakṣate- "cakṣuṣpradhānādāgacchati tatraiva ca punarvigacchati" iti | tannirāsārtha ca bhagavānavocat- "cakṣarutpadyamānaṃ na kutaścidāgacchati |" adeśapradeśasthāḥ khalvanāgatātītaparamāṇvavijñaptisaṃjñitā dharmāḥ iti tadāgamanagamanānupapattiḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> too indeed say: 'The eye comes from <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and returns to that very [source].' To refute that too, the <s>Bhagavat</s> declared: 'The eye, when arising, does not come from anywhere.' Indeed, those <s>dharmas</s> designated as future, past, atomic, and non-manifest are without a [specific spatial] location or place — hence it is impossible for them to come or go.

body.text: kastarhi vākyārtha |- "abhūtvā bhavati | bhūtvā ca prativigacchati" iti ? dvividhaṃ hi cakṣurdravyasadeva paramārthasato yadaprabuddhamubhayam(?) | anyatprabuddhamanu(- ddhamu ?)pāttakriyam | pūrvaṃ taddhetūnpratītya kriyāmupādatte prabudhyata ityarthaḥ | upāttakriyaṃ ca dvitīyam | taddhi kriyāmujjhatprativigacchatītyuktaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: What then is the meaning of the statement: 'Not having existed, it comes to be; and having been, it passes away'? For the eye is twofold, being a real substance: one whose both [aspects] (?) are unawakened — [its] intrinsic nature and power; the other is awakened, having taken up function. The first, relying on its causes, takes up function and awakens — this is the meaning. And the second, having taken up function, relinquishes that function and passes away — thus it is said.

body.text: sāṃkhyamataniṣedhārthaṃ vā | sāṃkhyānāṃ khalvekaṃ kāraṇaṃ nityaṃ svāṃ jātimajahattena tena vikāraviśeṣātmanā bhūtvā bhūtvānyenānyena kāryaviśeṣātmanā pariṇamatīti | tatpratiṣedhārthaṃ bhagavānavocat- "cakṣurutpadyamānaṃ na kutaścidāgacchati nirudhyamānaṃ na kvacitsaṃnicayaṃ gacchati" iti | cakṣurabhūtvā vartamāne 'dhvani kṣaṇamātraṃ kriyārūpamādaya tyaktvā punaradarśanaṃ gacchati |
body.translated_text: Or, for the purpose of refuting the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position. Indeed, according to the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, a single cause, permanent, without abandoning its own genus, having become [something] of a particular modification-nature, transforms into one and then another particular effect-nature. To refute that, the Blessed One declared: 'The eye, when arising, does not come from anywhere; when ceasing, it does not go to any accumulation.' The eye, having not existed previously, takes on a momentary activity-form in the present time-period, then abandons [it] and again becomes invisible.

body.text: kiñcānyat, ata evānāgatāstitvasiddheḥ | yaduktamasminneva sūtre cakṣurutpadyamānaṃ na kutaścidāgacchati" ityatraitadādarśitam | sadidaṃ cakṣurantaraṅgabahiraṅgakāraṇasāmagrīsannidhānopādhivaśena kriyāmupādadānaṃ na kutaścidāgacchati | kutaḥ punastatsattvamiti cet | mukhyasattāviṣṭe kartari śānacovidhānānnirudhyamānavaditi | tasmād durvihitavetāḍotthānavat sautrāntikaiḥ svapakṣopaghātāya sūtrametadāśrīyate |
body.translated_text: Moreover, from precisely this the existence of the future is established. What was stated in this very <s>sūtra</s> — 'The eye, when arising, does not come from anywhere' — here this has been shown: this eye, existing, taking on activity through the proximity-condition of the assemblage of internal and external causes, does not come from anywhere. But how is its existence [established]? Because the suffix '-āna' (śānac) is prescribed for an agent endowed with primary existence, like [in the form] 'ceasing.' Therefore, this <s>sūtra</s> is relied upon by the <s>Sautrāntikas</s> to the destruction of their own position, like rising after a poorly delivered blow.

body.text: evaṃ tāvadāgamātsiddhamadhvatrayāstitvam |
body.translated_text: Thus, to this extent, the existence of the three times is established from scripture.

body.text: yuktito 'pi- 'dhīnāmagocaratvācca tatsattvaṃ vartamānavat |'; tadākārayā khalu buddhyā yasyārthasya svasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ paricchidyate, yaśca buddhoktanāmakāyadharmakāyābhyāmabhidyotyate sa paramārthato vidyate | katham ? vartamānacakṣūrūpādivat | jñānajñeyābhidhānābhidheyasaṃbandhaḥ khalvakṛtakaiti śiṣṭāḥ pratipadyante ||
body.translated_text: Also by reasoning: 'Because they are not beyond the scope of cognition, their existence is like that of the present.' (Abhidh-d) Indeed, when an object's own-characteristic and general-characteristic are discerned by a cognition having that form, and when it is illuminated by the <s>Buddha's</s> name-body and <s>Dharmakāya</s>, it exists in the ultimate sense. How? Like present eye, form, and the rest. The learned recognize that the relation between knowledge and knowable, designation and designatum, is uncreated.

body.text: asadālambanāpi buddhirastīti cet | atrāpadiśyate-
body.translated_text: If [one objects that] cognition having a non-existent object also exists — to that it is pointed out:

body.text: nāsadālambanā buddhirāgamādupapattitaḥ /
body.translated_text: There is no cognition having a non-existent object, from both scripture and reasoning. (Abhidh-d 306)

body.text: āgamastāvat- "cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpaṃ cotpadyate cakṣurvijñānaṃ yāvanmanaḥ pratītya dharmāṃścotpadyate manovijñānam | etāvaccaitatsarvamasti" ityuktaṃ bhagavatā | tatra manovijñānaṃ traiyadhvikāsaṃskṛtadharmaviṣayāyama, pañcavijñānakāyāḥ pratyutpannapañcaviṣayālambanāḥ | na tu kvacidasadālambanamuktaṃ nāpi tadastīti tadviṣayabuddhyabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: As for scripture — the Blessed One said: 'Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises; up to: dependent on the mind and <s>dharmas</s>, mind-consciousness arises. All this exists to just this extent.' Therein, mind-consciousness has the three-temporal and unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> as its domain; the five classes of consciousness have present objects of the five senses as their support. But nowhere is cognition having a non-existent object stated, nor does it exist — hence there is no cognition having that as its object.

body.text: tathoktam- "yaduta loke nāsti tadahaṃ drakṣyāmi" iti vistaraḥ |

children.translated_text: Jaini_270

children.text:
)
tathā- "trayāṇāṃ sannipātaḥ sparśaḥ | sahajātā vedanā" iti vistaraḥ | etenābhidhānābhidheyasaṃbandhaḥ pratyuktaḥ | tadevaṃ sati sūtre 'sminmadhyamāpratipatpradarśitā | yaduta- kenacitprakāreṇa śūnyāḥ saṃskārāḥ mithyāparikalpitena puruṣālayavijñānābhūtaparikalpādinā | kenacidaśūnyāḥ, yaduta- svalakṣaṇasāmānyalakṣaṇābhyāmiti | yathā kātyāyana sūtre- "lokasamudayaṃ jñātvā yā loke nāsti tā sā na bhavati | lokanirodhaṃ jñātvā yā loke 'sti tā sā na bhavati itīmau dvāvantau parityajya madhyamayā pratipadā tathāgato dharmaṃ deśayati |" na caitad dva yamastināstitvākhyamekādhikaraṇaṃ virodhādupapadyate na ca niradhiṣṭhānam | nāpi khapuṣpaśūnyādhiṣṭhitam |
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'The meeting of the three is contact. Co-born is feeling' — and so forth in detail. By this, the relation of designation and designatum is answered. This being so, in this <s>sūtra</s> the middle path is demonstrated. Namely: in some respect, <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned things) are empty — of what is falsely imagined, such as <s>puruṣa</s> (person), <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness), <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (unreal imagination), and the like. In some respect they are non-empty — namely, of their own-characteristic and general-characteristic. As in the <s>Kātyāyana Sūtra</s>: 'Having known the arising of the world, whatever "non-existence" there is in the world, that does not obtain for him. Having known the cessation of the world, whatever "existence" there is in the world, that does not obtain for him. Avoiding these two extremes, the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> by the middle path.' And this dual [assertion] called 'exists' and 'does not exist' is not possible with a single substratum, due to contradiction; nor is it without a substratum; nor is it based on [mere] emptiness like a sky-flower.

body.translated_text: Thus it is stated: 'That which indeed does not exist in the world, that I shall see' — and so forth in detail.

body.text: yuktirapi | jñānajñeyābhidhānābhidheyasaṃbandhasyākṛtakatvāt | nāstiśaśaviṣāṇamityasya jñānasyābhidhānasya cāsadviṣayatvamiti cet | tatra brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: Reasoning also [supports this]: because the relation between knowledge and knowable, designation and designatum, is uncreated. If [one says] the cognition and designation 'a hare's horn does not exist' have a non-existent object — to that we say:

body.text: anyāpekṣye 'tha saṃbandhaprtiṣedho 'śvaśṛṅgayoḥ // Abhidh-d_306 //
body.translated_text: The negation of connection between horse and horn is with reference to something else. (Abhidh-d 306)

body.text: yo 'yaṃ nāsti śaśaviṣāṇādipratiṣedho 'sya tarhi kiṃ pratiṣedhyam ? yadyasadālambanā buddhirnāstyabhidhānaṃ vā nirabhedheyamiti ? atrāpadiśyate | 'anyāpekṣye 'tha saṃbandhapratiṣedhaḥ |'; kāryakāraṇādistrividhaḥ saṃbandho 'tra goviṣāṇādiṣu pūrvadṛṣṭaḥ śaśaviṣāṇādiṣu pratiṣiddhyate | śaśaśiromātrakākāśadhātusaṃbandhadarśanādyadi śaśaśirasyapi viṣāṇama viṣyattadvadevopalapsyata | na copalabhyate | tasmātsaṃbandhāntarāpekṣaṃ śaśaviṣāṇaśabdagaḍumātraṃ nañā saṃbandhyantarasaṃbandhabuddhyapekṣeṇāvadyotyate, na tu kiñcidabhidhānamabhidheyaṃ vā pratiṣedhyātmanā śrīyata iti siddhaṃ sarvā buddhiḥ sadviṣayeti |
body.translated_text: This negation 'a hare's horn does not exist' — what then is being negated? Is it that cognition having a non-existent object does not exist, or that designation has no designatum? To that it is pointed out: 'The negation of connection is with reference to something else.' The threefold connection — of cause and effect and so forth — previously seen in cow's horns and the like, is here negated with respect to hare's horns and the like. Because one has seen the connection of merely the hare's head with the space-element, if on the hare's head too there were a horn, it would be perceived just like [a cow's horn]. But it is not perceived. Therefore, dependent on another connection, the mere word-sound 'hare's horn' is expressed by the negative particle with reference to cognition of connection with something else; but nothing — neither designation nor designatum — is apprehended as having the nature of what is negated. Thus it is established that all cognition has an existent object.

body.text: etenājātaṃ dhvastaṃ ca goviṣāṇaṃ pratyuktam | gośiromātramākāśadhātuveṣṭitaṃ dṛṣṭvā janiṣyate dhvastaṃ vā goviṣāṇamiti draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: By this, an unborn or destroyed cow's horn is also answered. One should understand it as: having seen the mere cow's head enveloped by the space-element, [one thinks] 'a cow's horn will arise' or 'a cow's horn has been destroyed.'

body.text: trayodaśāyatanapratiṣedhabuddhiviṣayād astitvādasadālambanā buddhirastīti cet | na | bhagavataiva vāgvastumātrametaditi nirṇītatvāt | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā hastatālopame sūtre- "etāvatsarvaṃ yaduta cakṣū rūpaṃ ca yāvanmano dharmāṃśca | yaḥ kaścidetad dvaya pratyākhyāyānyad dvayaṃ jñeyamabhidheyaṃ vā (

children.translated_text: Jaini_272

children.text: ) kalpayet vāgvastumātramevāsya syāt | pṛṣṭo vā na saṃprajānīyāduttare vā saṃmohamāpadyeta | yathāpi tadaviṣayatvāt |" iti |
children.translated_text: that would be a mere verbal matter for him. Being questioned, he would not understand; moreover, he would fall into confusion. Why? Because it is beyond his scope.'

body.translated_text: If [one says] there is cognition having a non-existent object, because the cognition negating the thirteenth <s>āyatana</s> (sense-base) has existence as its object — no. Because the Blessed One himself has determined this to be a mere verbal matter. For the Blessed One said in the <s>Hastatālopama Sūtra</s>: 'All this is just this much, namely: eye and forms, up to mind and <s>dharmas</s>. Whoever, rejecting this pair, would imagine another pair [that is] knowable or expressible,

body.text: kiñca, astiśaśaviṣāṇābhidhānābhidheyavannāstyuktirapi vāgvastumātraṃ viṣāṇākhyābhidheyārthasaṃbandhavihīnam | etena ṣaṣṭhaḥ skandhaḥ pratyuktaḥ | kiñca, pañcaskandhaviṣayaviparītajñānapratiṣedhāt | alātacakrabuddhipratiṣedhavat, dvicandrabuddhipratiṣedhavacca | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "ye kecidātmeti samanupaśyantaḥ samanupaśyanti sarve ta imāneva pañcopādānaskandhānsamanupaśyantaḥ samanupaśyanti" iti skandhaviṣaye caiṣā nityātmadravyabhrāntirityavadyotyate |
body.translated_text: Moreover, just as the statement 'hare's horn' is a mere verbal matter devoid of connection with a designatum called 'horn,' so too is the statement 'does not exist.' By this, a sixth <s>skandha</s> is refuted. Furthermore, because cognition that is contrary to the domain of the five <s>skandhas</s> is negated — like the negation of the cognition of a fire-brand circle, and like the negation of the cognition of a double moon. For the Blessed One said: 'All those who perceive a self, they all perceive these very five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging)' — and this indicates that the delusion of permanence, self, and substance pertains to the domain of the <s>skandhas</s>.

body.text: kiñca, nañaḥ sadasatpratiṣedhyaviṣayatvānupapatteśca | santaṃ tāvadarthaṃ na pratiṣeddhum samarthaḥ | yadi hi santamarthaṃ śaknuyātpratiṣeddhuṃ na rājāno hastyaśvaṃ bibhṛyurna santi dasyava ityevaṃ brūyuḥ | ityukte dasyūnāmabhāvaḥ syāt | na caitadasti | athāsantaṃ pratiṣedhayati, tenābhāvapratiṣedhādbhāva eva syāditi | tasmānnaño na goviṣāṇādiḥ nāpi śaśaviṣāṇādiḥ pratiṣidhyate | kiṃ tarhi | śaśākāśadhātusaṃbandhabuddhyapekṣeṇa goviṣāṇādidravyāsaṃbandhabuddhayo 'vadyotyante | siddhā sadālambanaiva buddhiḥ | evamanyatrāpi |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, because the negative particle cannot have either an existent or non-existent thing as its object of negation. It cannot negate an existing thing — for if it could negate an existing thing, kings would not maintain elephants and horses; they would [simply] say 'robbers do not exist,' and thereby robbers would cease to exist. But this is not the case. And if it negates a non-existent [thing], then by negating absence, existence alone would follow. Therefore, the negative particle negates neither cow's horns and the like nor hare's horns and the like. What then? With reference to the cognition of the non-connection of hare with space-element, the cognitions of non-connection with substances such as cow's horns and the like are expressed. Thus it is established that cognition has only existent objects. Likewise in other cases.

children.translated_text: When a thing such as form and the rest has perished, cognition arises with regard to what truly exists. (Abhidh-d 307)
That [cognition] is the non-existent-form of cognition — like the <s>Śāstṛ's</s> (Teacher's) [knowledge of] others' minds.

body.text: rūpādau khalvapivastunyabhyatīte satyeva buddhirutpadyate | na hyasadālambanā buddhirutpadyate | sadālambanā buddhirastītyupapāditam | na ca no dravyaṃ vinaśyatītyuktam | yadetada rūpādidravyaṃ pūrvānubhūtaṃ tadeva tatsmṛtyā gṛhyata ityupariṣṭādapi sādhayiṣyāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: When indeed a thing such as form and the rest that has passed away, cognition arises with regard to what truly exists. For cognition having a non-existent object does not arise. It has been demonstrated that cognition has an existent object. And we have not said that the substance perishes. That very substance of form and the rest, previously experienced, is grasped by memory of it — this we shall also establish further on.

body.text: yā tarhi niruddhadevadattānusmṛtirdhaṭānusmṛtirvā sā kathaṃ jāyate ? atītānāga tayordevadattaghaṭaprajñaptyupādānayoriti | atra brūmaḥ | sāpi khalu sāvidyāsyāsadākārotpadyate sthāṇvādau puruṣādibuddhivat | niravidyasya tu śāstustattvākārā bhavati rūpādidharmamātrabuddhireva | (

children.translated_text: Jaini_273

children.text: ) tadyathā paracittavidaḥ svalakṣaṇākārā buddhirutpadyate | tatsāmarthyopādhivaśenānyathāpi jānīte | tadvattatsāmarthyeṇa bhāvinīṃ bhūtāṃ ca saṃjñāṃ rūpādiṣu devadattaghaṭalakṣaṇāṃ pratipadyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Just as for one who knows others' minds, cognition arises with the form of the own-characteristic [of the other's mind]; by the force of its capacity-condition, he also knows [it] in another way. Similarly, by that very capacity, one apprehends designations — future and past — regarding forms and the like, designations characterized by '<s>Devadatta</s>' and 'pot.'

body.translated_text: Now, how does the recollection of a deceased <s>Devadatta</s> or the recollection of a [destroyed] pot arise? [If one says:] because the past and future <s>Devadatta</s> and pot are the basis of designation — to that we say: that [cognition] too arises with the form of a non-existent [appearance] due to ignorance, like the cognition of a person and the like in a post and the like. But for the non-ignorant Teacher, it has the form of reality — it is merely the cognition of <s>dharmas</s> such as form and the like.

body.text: itaśca sadatītānāgatam-
body.translated_text: Also from this, the past and future exist —

body.text: harṣotpādabhayodvegasmṛtyutpattyaṅgabhāvataḥ /
body.translated_text: Because of the arising of joy, dread, memory, and constituent-status: (Abhidh-d)

body.text: atītānāgataṃ hi mitramamitraṃ vā manasi kṛtvā harṣotpādabhayādayo 'bhyupajāyante | te cānimittā na bhavitumarhanti | katham ? vartamānavat | | tadyathā sati vartamāne mitre 'mitre vā harṣabhayādayo bhavanti nāsatīti tadvat |
body.translated_text: For having mentally attended to a past or future friend or enemy, joy, dread, and the like arise. And these cannot be without a basis. How? Like the present. Just as when a present friend or enemy exists, joy, fear, and the like occur, but not when [one] does not exist — likewise [with past and future objects].

body.text: kiñca,
body.translated_text: Moreover,

body.text: sāṅgasya śaktyabhivyakteḥ sadīpaghaṭarūpavat // Abhidh-d_308 //
body.translated_text: Because of the manifestation of potency in what has constituents — like the form of a pot [seen by] lamplight. (Abhidh-d 308)

body.text: vidyamānasya khalvanāgatasya vastuno 'tītapratyutpannasahakārikāraṇasāmagrīgṛhītasya śaktimātramāvirbhavati | katham ? 'sadīpaghaṭarūpavat |'; tadyathā tamasi vidyamānasya ghaṭarūpasya svātmodbhāvanaśaktiḥ pradīpādikāraṇasāmagrīsannidhāne sati bhavati tadvaditi | itaścāstyanāgatam ||
body.translated_text: Of an existing future thing, grasped by the assemblage of cooperative causes both past and present, merely potency becomes manifest. How? 'Like the form of a pot [seen by] lamplight.' Just as the self-manifesting potency of the form of a pot existing in darkness comes about when the assemblage of causes such as a lamp and the like is present — likewise. And also from this, the future exists.

body.text: janīhākartṛ sādhyatvātpañcabhāvavikāravat /
body.translated_text: Birth [applied] to the non-existent agent is to be established — like the five modifications of being. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: tadyathā asti vipariṇamate vardhate kṣīyate vinaśyatīti sati mukhyasattāviṣṭe kartari ete pañca bhāvavikārā bhavanti | tadvajjāyata ityayamapi ṣaṣṭhaḥ bhāvavikāraḥ sati mukhyāviṣṭe kartari bhavitumarhatīti | kiñca jāyamānatā sattā naśyatā nāsāmānādhikaraṇye satyananyatāpattisaṅkaradoṣaprasaṅgāt | vaiyadhikaraṇyābhyupagame saṃbandhābhāvādekatra tadvyapadeśānupapattiḥ | kiñca, jāyamānatādikriyābhāve 'stitvāyogāt | katham ? śaśaviṣāṇavaditi | upacārasatteti cet | na | mukhyasattāyāṃ satyāmupacārasadbhāvāt, vakṣyamāṇadoṣācca |
body.translated_text: Just as 'exists, transforms, grows, diminishes, perishes' — these five modifications of being occur when there is an agent endowed with primary existence — likewise 'is born,' this sixth modification of being, should be possible when there is an agent endowed with primary [existence]. Moreover, if birth-ness, existence, and perishing-ness were not co-referential and yet [treated as] non-different, the fault of confusion would follow; and if they are admitted to be in different substrata, then due to the absence of connection, the designation of one [predicate] with respect to the other would be impossible. Furthermore, in the absence of activities such as birth-ness and the like, existence would be impossible. How? Like a hare's horn. If [one says it has] metaphorical existence — no. Because metaphorical existence [is possible only] when primary existence obtains, and because of the faults to be stated.

body.text: itaścāsti-
body.translated_text: And from this too, [the future] exists —

body.text: sataḥ kriyāṅgatādṛṣṭervikāryaprāpyakarmavat // Abhidh-d_309 //
body.translated_text: Because activity is seen in what exists as a constituent — like transformable and reachable objects of action. (Abhidh-d 309)

body.text: tadyathā vikārye karmaṇi sati karaṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kāśātkaṭī karoti | prāpye ca karmaṇi sati grāmaṃ gacchati devadattaḥ sūryaṃ ca paśyatīti gamanadṛśikriye sati karmaṇi bhavataḥ | tadvannirvartye 'pi karmaṇi mukhyadravyāstitve sati devadattakartṛkā ghaṭakriyopapadyata iti ||
body.translated_text: Just as when there is a transformable object of action, an instrument is seen — [as in] 'one makes a mat from grass' — and when there is a reachable object of action — [as in] '<s>Devadatta</s> goes to the village' and 'sees the sun' — the activities of going and seeing occur when the object of action exists. Similarly, when there is an object of action that is to be produced, and primary substantial existence obtains, the activity of <s>Devadatta</s> as agent producing a pot is possible.

body.text: sāṃkhyaḥ paśyati- vidyamānameva jāyate | tadyathā kṣīre vidyamānaṃ dadhi, kāryakāraṇayorekatvāt | taṃ pratyapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: The <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [philosopher] holds: what already exists is what is born. Just as curd exists in milk, because of the identity of cause and effect. To him it is pointed out:

body.text: dvitīyaṃ janma jātasya vastuno nopapadyate /
body.translated_text: A second birth of an already-born thing is not possible. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: yadi khalu kṣīre dadhyādayo vikārāḥ santi bīje cāṅkurādayaḥ śukraśoṇite ca kalalādayaḥ, teṣāṃ jātānāṃ kṣīrādivajjanma punarna yujyate | yathā ca na yujyate tathā pūrvamevāviṣkṛtam |
body.translated_text: If indeed modifications such as curd and the like exist in milk, and sprouts and the like in seeds, and <s>kalala</s> (embryonic form) and the like in semen and blood, then for those already-born [things], birth again — like [birth] from milk and the like — is not possible. And the way in which it is not possible has been previously revealed.

body.text: vaiśeṣiko manyate- kapāleṣvavidyamānaṃ ghaṭadravyaṃ tantuṣu cāvidyamānaṃ paṭadravyaṃ kapālatantusaṃyogādutpadyate | gauṇyā ca kalpanayā viprakṛtā(ṣṭā ?)vasthāviṣayā janikartṛ sattā vyapadiśyata iti | asyāpyavayavidravyaṃ sahāvayavaiḥ pūrvameva vihitottaram | yatpunaruktamupacārasattayā janikartopadiśyata ityatra brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> holds: pot-substance, not existing in the potsherds, and cloth-substance, not existing in the threads, arises from the conjunction of potsherds and threads. And by metaphorical usage, existence in a transformed state is designated as the agent of birth. For him too, the composite substance together with its parts has already been dealt with above. As for what was said — that by metaphorical existence the agent of birth is designated — to that we say:

body.text: mukhyasattā guṇābhāvādgauṇī sattā na vidyate // Abhidh-d_310 //
body.translated_text: In the absence of primary existence, which is the basis [of metaphor], metaphorical existence does not obtain. (Abhidh-d 310)

body.text: na hi mukhyasattāyāṃ guṇābhāve 'vayavābhāve vā kāraṇeṣu prāgutpattyabhāve vā kāryasattopacāro yujyate ||
body.translated_text: For in the absence of primary existence in the causes — that is, in the absence of [inherent] parts, or prior to origination — the metaphorical attribution of existence to the effect is not possible.

body.text: kasmāt ?
body.translated_text: Why?

body.text: sādharmye sati tadvṛttervyāhāraṃ madhuroktivat /
body.translated_text: Because activity follows from that [existence], when there is similarity — like the expression 'sweet speech.' (Abhidh-d)

body.text: tadyathā madhuravāgdevadatta iti vāci mādhuryaguṇayuktasya guḍadravyasya madhuno vā sādharmyamabhilaṣaṇīyatā vidyate ityato vāci mādhuryaśabdaḥ prayujyate | kanyāmukhe ca candrakāntisādṛśyaṃ dṛṣṭvā candraśabdaḥ prayujyate | vāhīke ca jāḍyasādharmyādgośabdaḥ prayujyate- gaurayaṃ vāhīka ityevamādi | na ca tathā kaścidaguṇāvayavagandho 'pi tantuṣu tatsaṃyoge vā prāgutpattyabhāve nirātmanaḥ kāryasyāstīti | na ca kāryaṃ kiñcidīṣatkṛtamupapadyate | niṣṭhāsattaikakālābhyupagamāt | prāgavyapadeśyaṃ vastumātraṃ viprakṛtaṃ jāyata iti cet | na | uktottaratvāt | mama tu candrakoṭīprakāśalakṣaṇo dṛṣṭānto vidyate |
body.translated_text: Just as [in the expression] 'sweet-speaking <s>Devadatta</s>' — the word 'sweetness' (<s>mādhurya</s>) is applied to speech because there is a similarity with the sweetness-quality of the substance <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) or honey in terms of desirability. And seeing a resemblance to the moon's radiance in a maiden's face, the word 'moon' is applied. And for a <s>Vāhlīka</s>, because of a resemblance to dullness, the word 'cow' is applied — as in 'this <s>Vāhlīka</s> is a cow' — and so on. But there is not even a trace of such a quality-component in the threads or in their conjunction prior to the arising [of the cloth], since the effect has no self. Nor does any effect arise as partially produced — because one accepts that it exists [only] at the moment of completion, at a single time. If [one says] 'a mere thing, prior [to completion] inexpressible, arises in a raw state' — no, because this has already been answered. But I have an illustration characterized by the light of a trillion moons:

body.text: āviṣṭaliṅgamukhyasya janmeṣṭaṃ dārakādivat // Abhidh-d_311 //
body.translated_text: The birth of the primary [entity], which has entered into [manifest] form, is accepted — like a boy and the like. (Abhidh-d 311)

body.text: ayaṃ hi janirabhiniṣkramaṇādivacano nāsatprādurbhāvavacanaḥ | katham ? 'dārakādivat'; | tadyathā dārako mukhyasattāviṣṭo mātṛkukṣerniṣkramaṇe jāyata ityucyate | tadvadatrāpīti |
body.translated_text: For this [word] 'birth' (<s>jani</s>) means 'emergence' and the like, not 'coming into being from non-existence.' How? 'Like a boy and the like.' Just as a boy, who already exists as a primary entity, is said to be 'born' upon emergence from the mother's womb — similarly here also.

body.text: dārṣṭāntikaḥ khalu brūte- kāraṇaśaktiṣu nirātmakajanikartrupacāraḥ pravartate | taṃ prati brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: The <s>Dārṣṭāntika</s> indeed says: 'The figurative usage of a selfless producer operates with respect to the powers of causes.' To him we say:

children.translated_text: 'The sky would bloom with sky-flowers, and frogs would have matted hair,

children.text: svabhāvo yadi bhāvanāṃ prāgabhūtvā samudbhavet // Abhidh-d_312 //
children.translated_text: if the intrinsic nature of things were to arise having previously not existed.' (Abhidh-d 312)

body.text: na hyasataḥ kasyacicchaśaviṣāṇāderutpādo bhavati nairātmyāviśeṣasarvāsadutpattiprasaṅgāt | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 275)

children.text: ) taddhetukānāṃ ca jāyamānajātanaśyatkāleṣvātmāstitvasthitaśaktīnāmanupapatteḥ | kāraṇānāṃ ca kāryātmakatvāt prāgutpatterasattvam, asattvādanupapattidoṣāpattiḥ | kutaśca nābhāvo bhāvībhavati ? sthitiśaktikriyāyogāt ||
children.translated_text: And because the existence, stable power, and duration of those caused [by factors] is untenable at the times of being-born, being-born, and perishing. And because causes, being of the nature of the effect, are non-existent prior to arising — from non-existence, the fault of impossibility follows. And why does non-existence not become existent? Because of the impossibility of the functioning of the power of duration.

body.translated_text: For there is no arising of what is non-existent — of a hare's horn and the like — because of the absurd consequence that everything non-existent would arise, given the absence of any difference in selflessness.

body.text: kathamayoga iti cet | tadāviṣkriyate-
body.translated_text: If [one asks] 'how is it impossible?' — that is now made clear:

children.translated_text: 'Tell me, dear one, how does a thing attain thingness through dependence,

children.text: vada somya kathaṃ yāti pratītyā vastu vastutām // Abhidh-d_313 //
children.translated_text: when dharmas arise conjoined with destruction and devoid of the power of duration?' (Abhidh-d 313)

body.text: iha khalu bhavatāmahetuko vināśaḥ sarvotpattimatāṃ nityasaṃnihitaḥ | tasmiṃśca sati janmasthitiśaktikriyā na vidyante, virodhāt | tāsvasatīṣu kāraṇamapi caiva vinaṣṭam | tadasminnasati kiṃ pratītya asannirātmakaṃ vastu vastutāṃ yātītyācakṣva | kathaṃ te kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ vopapadyate ? satāṃ hi saṃjñāsaṃjñijñānajñeyakriyākāraṇahetuphalādīnāmanyonyāpekṣaprajñapteḥ | atha tavābhāvo na kaścidasti bhāvavirodhī, kathaṃ tarhi sa bhāvo naṣṭa ityucyate ? tasmādbhavato vāṅmātrametat, mama tu vidyamānayorevopakāryupakārakabhāvo yuktaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here indeed, for you [<s>Sautrāntikas</s>], causeless destruction is perpetually present for everything that has arisen. And when that [destruction] exists, the functioning of birth, duration, and power does not exist — because of contradiction. When those do not exist, the cause too has perished. So tell me — when this [cause] does not exist, depending on what does a non-existent, selfless thing attain thingness? How is your effect or cause tenable? For the designations of existing things — cognition, what-is-cognized, knower, what-is-known, action, cause, effect, and the like — are mutually dependent. Now, if for you there is no non-existence opposed to existence, how then can one say that an existent thing has 'perished'? Therefore, your [position] is mere words. But for me, the relationship of benefited and benefactor is reasonable only between two existing things.

body.text: yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Because:

children.translated_text: 'In the world, mutual assistance is observed only between existing things;
likewise mutual harm — not of hare's horns and serpent's feet.' (Abhidh-d 314)

body.text: anugrahopaghātayośca kāryakāraṇasaṃbandhopacāraśca satoreva bhavatītyāstanandhayebhyaḥ prasiddhametat, nāsatoḥ na ca sadasatoriti ||
body.translated_text: And the figurative usage of the cause-effect relationship belongs only to what exists, with respect to both assistance and harm — this is well-known even to the dull, not [as applying] to two non-existents, nor to an existent and a non-existent.

body.text: vaitulikaḥ kalpayati-
body.translated_text: The <s>Vaitulika</s> (Mādhyamika) imagines:

body.text: yatpratītyasamutpannaṃ tatsvabhāvānna vidyate /
body.translated_text: 'Whatever is dependently arisen does not exist by its own nature.'

body.text: yatkhalu nisvabhāvaṃ nirātmakaṃ hetūnpratītya jāyate tasya khalu svabhāvo nāsti | na hi tatkāraṇeṣu pratyekamavasthitaṃ nāpi bhāgaśo nāpyanyatra kvacit | nāpi hetusamudāye tadrūpābhāvāt | yacca na kvacidasti tatkatamena svabhāvenotpatsyata iti nāsti svabhāvaḥ | yasya ca nāsti svabhāvaḥ tatkathamastītyucyate ? tasmādalātacakravannisvabhāvatvāt sarvadharmā nirātmāna iti |
body.translated_text: What is indeed without own-nature, selfless, and arises depending on causes — its own-nature does not exist. For it is not found in each cause individually, nor partially, nor anywhere else. Nor in the assemblage of causes, because its form is absent there. And what does not exist anywhere — by what own-nature would it arise? Therefore, there is no own-nature. And what has no own-nature — how can it be said to 'exist'? Therefore, like a whirling firebrand-circle, all dharmas are selfless because they lack own-nature.

body.text: taṃ pratyapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: To him, the reply is given:

body.text: na vidyate svabhāvādyadvidyate tattato 'nyathā // Abhidh-d_315 //
body.translated_text: 'What does not exist by its own nature — that which does not exist — is otherwise than that.' (Abhidh-d 315)

body.text: brahmodyametat- yatpratītyasamutpannaṃ tatsaṃvṛtyātmanā vidyate vanasaṃghādivat | yatparamārthato vidyate taraya pratītyāvasthāśaktimūrtikriyādimātramutpadyata iti ||
body.translated_text: This is a riddle: What is dependently arisen exists by its conventional self (<s>saṃvṛtyātman</s>), like a forest-assemblage. What exists ultimately — for that, the condition of having merely the arising of state, power, form, and activity through dependence [is what is meant].

body.text: tasya tarhi hetavo vidyamānasya kamupakāraṃ kurvantīti ? atrābhidhīyate | na khalu dravyasvabhāvāstitvaṃ prati kañcidupakāraṃ kurvanti | na ca svabhāvasyāpekṣya prajñaptiḥ | kiṃ tarhi ?
body.translated_text: What benefit, then, do causes provide to it, which exists [already]? Here it is stated: Causes do not indeed provide any benefit toward the existence of [the thing's] own substantial nature (<s>dravyasvabhāva</s>). Nor is the designation dependent on own-nature. What then?

children.translated_text: 'Causes produce merely the state [of activity] for a thing that exists —
like ministers [producing] kingship for a prince who already possesses a self.' (Abhidh-d 316)

body.text: tadyathābhijātasya rājaputrasya vidyamānasya mantriṇaḥ sabalasamudayāḥ parigrahānugrahamātreṇopakurvanto rājatvaṃ kurvantyevamanāgatasya vastunaḥ sato hetupratyayāḥ sametya lakṣaṇamātraṃ vartamānākhyamaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kurvantītyavaboddhavyam ||
body.translated_text: Just as the ministers, together with their assembled forces, by merely sheltering and supporting a well-born prince who already exists, produce kingship for him — so too, the causes and conditions, coming together for a future thing that exists, should be understood as producing merely the characteristic called 'present-state,' [which is] the sovereignty and dominion [of the thing].

body.text: anye punarvarṇayanti-
body.translated_text: Others, however, explain:

children.translated_text: 'When the assemblage of conditions exists for dharmas, a power arises —
like [what happens] in the perception of massed atoms as a self [i.e., a unitary object].' (Abhidh-d 317)

body.text: yathā khalu paramāṇusaṃcayaścakṣuṣā gṛhyate, pratyekaṃ paramāṇavo na gṛhyante, tathā kāraṇasāmagrye sati dharmāṇāṃ kriyāsāmarthyamupajāyata iti draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: Just as an accumulation of atoms is apprehended by the eye, while individual atoms are not apprehended — so too, when the assemblage of conditions exists, the power of activity arises for dharmas — thus it should be seen.

body.text: bhadantakumāralātaḥ paśyati- vātāyanapraviṣṭasyāntaḥpārśvadvaye 'pi truṭayaḥ santi | raśmigatasya tu darśanamasya truṭe raśmipārśvagāstvanumeyāḥ | etena vyākhyātaṃ dharmāṇāmadhvayordvayorastitvam | prāpya jñānātiśayaṃ munayaḥ paśyanti, tāstu dhīrhi trikajā ||
body.translated_text: The Venerable <s>Kumāralāta</s> holds: A ray of light entering through a window — there are gaps on both inner sides. What is in the path of the ray is seen; but [what is in] the gap beside the ray is inferred. By this is explained the existence of dharmas in two of the three times. Having attained the excellence of knowledge, the sages see [this]; but that vision is born of the three [sources of knowledge].

body.text: yastu manyate 'tītaṃ karmābhāvībhavatyanāgataṃ ca na vidyate taṃ pratyapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: Now, to one who thinks 'past action becomes non-existent, and the future does not exist' — the reply is given:

children.translated_text: 'For one whose past action is non-existent — a non-existent [action] producing a future non-existent fruit —
clearly, a barren woman's son is born to him from the son of an intermediate being.' (Abhidh-d 318)

body.text: na hi bhavato vartamānakālāstitvamupapadyate, atītānāgatahetuphalābhāvāt, vandhyāvyantaraputrajanmavat ||
body.translated_text: For the existence of the present time is untenable for you, because of the non-existence of past and future cause and fruit — like the birth of a son from a barren woman or an intermediate being.

body.text: atra pratyavatiṣṭhante dārṣṭāntikāḥ- na brūmaḥ sarvathātītaṃ na vidyate | kiṃ tarhi ? dravyātmanā na vidyate prajñaptyātmanā tu saditi | tatra pratisamādhīyate-
body.translated_text: Here the <s>Dārṣṭāntikas</s> take their stand: 'We do not say that the past does not exist in every respect. What then? It does not exist as a substance (<s>dravyātman</s>), but it is existent as a designation (<s>prajñaptyātman</s>).' To this, the response is:

children.translated_text: 'Because of the absence of the characteristic [described as] merely a name-indicator, and because of the establishment of [things being] marked as substantially real (<s>dravyasatya</s>) —
the future and past do not have designative reality (<s>prajñaptisatyatā</s>).' (Abhidh-d 319)

body.text: sopādānaṃ hi sarvaṃ prajñaptisat | na ca vartamānamupādānamupapadyate | anāgatābhyatītasya tasmānnirupādānasya prajñaptyabhāvādasadetat |
body.translated_text: For everything that is designatively real depends on a basis (<s>upādāna</s>). And a present basis is not tenable [for past and future things]. Therefore, for the future and past, which are without a basis, because of the absence of designation — they are non-existent.

body.text: yadi tarhyanāgataṃ cakṣurādidravyaṃ vidyate kasmānna paśyati na dṛśyate na vijānāti ? na vyaktaṃ kāritrābhāvāditi ||
body.translated_text: If, then, the future substance of the eye and the like exists, why does it not see, is not seen, and does not cognize? Clearly, because of the absence of functional activity (<s>kāritra</s>) — is it not so?

body.text: tadatra kośakāraḥ praśnayati-
body.translated_text: Here the <s>Kośakāra</s> (<s>Vasubandhu</s>) poses the question:

children.translated_text: 'What is the obstacle?'

body.text: yadi cakṣurvidyate kiṃ na paśyati ? vayaṃ brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: If the eye exists, why does it not see? We say:

children.translated_text: 'The deficiency of a component.'

body.text: dṛṣṭaṃ hi pradīpādyaṅgavaikalye vartamānasyāpi cakṣuṣo rūpādarśanam |
body.translated_text: For it is observed that even a present eye does not see form when there is a deficiency of components such as a lamp and the like.

body.text: sa pratyācaṣṭe- sarvasya sadāstitve kuto 'ṅgavaikalyam ? vayamācakṣmahe-
body.translated_text: He replies: 'If everything exists at all times, how can there be a deficiency of a component?' We state:

body.text: na tatsarvāstitā sadā /
body.translated_text: 'Not everything exists at all times in that [required] way.'

body.text: traiyadhvikāni khalvatrāṅgāni vivakṣitāni | tatra keṣāñcidasāṃnidhyaṃ bhavati tadvaikalyātkāritraṃ na karotīti |
body.translated_text: What is meant here is the components belonging to the three times. Of those, some are not proximately present — therefore, due to their deficiency, [the eye] does not perform its function.

body.text: sa pratyācaṣṭe-
body.translated_text: He replies:

children.translated_text: 'How then —'

body.text: kiṃ lakṣaṇātkāritraṃ tato vā dravyāt, kimanyadāhosvidananyaditi ? tatra vayaṃ prativadmaḥ-
body.translated_text: 'Is functional activity the same as or different from the characteristic or from the substance itself?' — To this, we reply:

children.translated_text: 'Let the wise listen!'

body.text: chātrāsanamadhyāsya na hi sarvajñapravacanagāmbhīryaṃ sadevakenāpi lokena śakyaṃ tarkamātreṇāvaboddhum | yasmātsomya-
body.translated_text: Sitting on a student's seat, one cannot comprehend the profundity of the Omniscient One's teaching by mere reasoning, even with the entire world including its gods. Because, dear one:

body.text: durbodhā khalu dharmatā // Abhidh-d_320 //
body.translated_text: 'The nature of dharmas is indeed difficult to comprehend.' (Abhidh-d 320)

body.text: tathāpi tu śrūyatām ||
body.translated_text: Nevertheless, listen!

children.translated_text: 'Through arrival at the present time-period, through the taking up of the components of the assemblage —
the projection of a fruit by one that has obtained power — this is called functional activity.' (Abhidh-d 321)

body.text: anāgatasya khalu dharmasya vartamānādhvasaṃpātādantaraṅgavahiraṅgasāmagryāṅgaparigrahāt labdhasāmarthyasya dharmasya yaḥ phalākṣepastatkāritramityucyate | sā ca vartamānakālā vṛttiḥ kāritramityākhyāyate | tatra yo brūte 'nanyatkāritramiti tasya dravyasvabhāvaparityāgaḥ prasajyate ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, for a future dharma, through arrival at the present time-period and through the taking up of the components of the internal and external assemblage — the projection of a fruit by a dharma that has obtained capacity — this is called functional activity (<s>kāritra</s>). And that operation belonging to the present time is designated as 'functional activity.' There, whoever says 'functional activity is not different [from the substance]' — for him, the abandonment of [the thing's] own substantial nature would follow.

body.text: śāstre tu khalu-
body.translated_text: But in the treatise indeed:

children.translated_text: 'Present-ness is not [the thing's] form; nor is past-ness or future-ness.
Therefore, not through the passage through times is the self of form considered to become otherwise.' (Abhidh-d 322)

body.text: yadi dravyātmano nānyathātvaṃ kiṃ tarhi hetūn pratītya jāyate ? brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: If the substantial self does not become otherwise, what then arises depending on causes? We say:

children.translated_text: 'A certain state arises for a thing that exists,

children.text: tathā śaktistathā velā tathā sattā tathā kriyā // Abhidh-d_323 //
children.translated_text: likewise power, likewise time, likewise existence, likewise activity.' (Abhidh-d 323)

body.text: tatrāvasthāśaktipracayakriyāpekṣā dravyavaśā śaktiḥ kriyāpekṣākṛtaṃ sāmarthyam | kriyānāgataphalā | dravyavṛttirvelā kālo vartamānākhyaḥ | mūrtiḥ paramāṇupracayaviśeṣaḥ | sattā prabodhākhyaṃ prajñaptisatyam | iti sarvametadantaraṅgabahiraṅgakāraṇasāmagrīsannidhānāpekṣāsaktasvarūpam ||
body.translated_text: There, 'state' (<s>avasthā</s>) is dependent on power, accumulation, and activity — [all] under the control of the substance. 'Power' (<s>śakti</s>) is the capacity dependent on activity — what has been wrought. 'Activity' (<s>kriyā</s>) has its fruit in the future. 'Time' (<s>velā</s>) is the operation of the substance, the time called 'present.' 'Form' (<s>mūrti</s>) is the particular accumulation of atoms. 'Existence' (<s>sattā</s>) is the designative reality called 'awakeness.' Thus all of this has a self-nature that is dependent on the proximate presence of the assemblage of internal and external conditions.

body.text: atra sarvāstivādavibhraṣṭirvaituliko nirāha- vayamapi trīn svabhāvān kalpayiṣyāmaḥ | tasmai prativaktavyam-
body.translated_text: Here, a <s>Vaitulika</s> (Mādhyamika) who has fallen away from the <s>Sarvāstivāda</s> says: 'We too shall posit three intrinsic natures.' To him, one should reply:

children.translated_text: 'The world is pervaded by fabrications that delight the minds of fools;

children.text: yastu vidvanmanogrāhī parikalpaḥ sa durlabhaḥ // Abhidh-d_324 //
children.translated_text: but a fabrication that captivates the minds of the wise — that is rare.' (Abhidh-d 324)

body.text: te khalvete bhavatkalpitāstrayaḥ svabhāvāḥ pūrvameva pratyūḍhāḥ | evamanye 'pyasatparikalpāḥ protsārayitavyāḥ | ityetadaparamadhvasaṃmohāṅkanāsthānaṃ kośakārakasyeti |
body.translated_text: Those three intrinsic natures fabricated by you have already been refuted. Thus other false fabrications should also be dismissed. This much serves as the basis for marking [<s>Vasubandhu</s>] the <s>Kośakāra</s>'s confusion about time-periods (<s>adhva</s>).

body.text: gatametatprāsaṅgikaṃ prakaraṇam | śāstramevānuvartatām ||
body.translated_text: This incidental topic is finished. Let the treatise itself continue.

body.text: vyākhyātamidaṃ yasminvastuni yaiḥ kleśairyadavasthairyaḥ saṃyuktaḥ | idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | yadvastvaprahīṇaṃ saṃyuktaḥ sa tasminvastuni ? yasmi vā vastuni saṃyukto 'prahīṇaṃ tasya tadvastu ? yattāvadvastvaprahīṇaṃ saṃyuktaḥ sa tasminvastuni | syādvastuni saṃyukto na ca tadvastvaprahīṇaṃ yathā tāvaddarśanamārge |
body.translated_text: This has been explained: by which afflictions, in what state, one is connected with which object. Now this must be stated: Is one who has [the object as] an unabandoned thing connected with it? Or is a thing with respect to which one is connected unabandoned for him? First, regarding a thing that is unabandoned — one is connected with it. [But] it may be that one is connected with a thing, yet that thing is not unabandoned [for him] — as, for example, on the path of seeing:

body.text: anyasarvatragairbaddhaḥ prahīṇe duḥkhadṛkkṣaye /
body.translated_text: One bound by the universals of another [truth] — in what is abandoned by seeing suffering —

body.text: duḥkhajñāne utpanne samudayajñāne cānutpanne duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaṃ vastu prahīṇaṃ bhavati | tasminprahīṇe 'pi samudayadarśanaprahātavyo 'prahīṇaḥ, tadālambanaiḥ sarvatragaiḥ saṃyuktaḥ |
body.translated_text: when the knowledge of suffering has arisen and the knowledge of origination has not yet arisen, the thing to be abandoned by seeing suffering is abandoned. Even when that is abandoned, [one remains] connected with what is to be abandoned by seeing origination — [being] not yet abandoned — through the universal [defilements] that take that [abandoned thing] as their object.

body.text: bhāvanāmārge 'pi-
body.translated_text: Even on the path of cultivation —

body.text: prahīṇe prākprakāre 'pi śeṣaistadavalambibhiḥ // Abhidh-d_325 //
body.translated_text: even when a prior type [of defilement] is abandoned, [one remains connected] by the remainder that cling to it. (Abhidh-d 325)

body.text: navānāṃ prakārāṇāṃ yo yaḥ prakāraḥ pūrva prahīṇastasminprahīṇe 'pi śeṣaistadavalambibhiḥ kleśaiḥ saṃyukto vijñātavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Of the nine types [of defilement], whichever type is first abandoned — even when that is abandoned, one should be known as connected [with it] through the remaining afflictions that cling to it.

body.text: atha kasminvastuni katyanuśayā anuśerate ? atra cālambananiyama eva tāvaddarśayitavyaḥ | katamo dharmaḥ katamasya vijñānasyālambanam ? tata eva tadvispaṣṭaṃ gamyate- amuṣminvastuni iyanto 'nuśayā anuśerata iti | tadidamabhidharmagahvaraṃ pratāyate-
body.translated_text: Now, in which object do how many latent defilements lie latent? Here, the restriction of object must first be shown: Which dharma is the object of which consciousness? From that alone, this will become clear — namely, that in such-and-such an object, this many latent defilements lie latent. This <s>Abhidharma</s> thicket is now laid open —

children.translated_text: Dharmas are to be known as sixteen, each having the nature of three realms of existence, (Abhidh-d 326)

children.text: pañcadhā nirmalāścaiva vijñānāni tathaiva ca // Abhidh-d_326 //
children.translated_text: and fivefold uncontaminated ones, and consciousnesses likewise.

body.text: dharmāstāvat kāmarūpārūpyadhātuṣu pratyekaṃ pañcaprakārā duḥkhādidarśanaheyā apraheyāśca nirmalā iti ṣoḍaśa bhavanti | evaṃ vijñānāni draṣṭavyāni ||
body.translated_text: First, dharmas: in the desire, form, and formless realms, each has five types — to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and the rest, not to be abandoned, and uncontaminated — making sixteen. Consciousnesses are to be viewed in the same way.

body.text: tatra tāvadābhidhārmiko 'nyaiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ-
body.translated_text: Therein, first, when an <s>Ābhidhārmika</s> is questioned by others —

children.translated_text: He should determine [the answer] in terms of elements (<s>dhātus</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), truths, and types, (Abhidh-d 327)
when questioned about dharma-collections, consciousnesses, knowledges, and latent tendencies.

body.text: dharmasaṃgrahavijñāne vā pṛṣṭo dhātvāyatanaskandheṣu pātayitvā lakṣayet | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 284)

children.text: ) jñāneṣu pṛṣṭaḥ satyeṣu pātayitvā lakṣayet | anuśayeṣu pṛṣṭaḥ prakāreṣu pātayitvā nirdiśet | evamasaṃmūḍho vyākarotīti ||
children.translated_text: When questioned about knowledges, one should determine by placing [them] into the truths. When questioned about latent tendencies, one should indicate by placing [them] into the types. Thus, one who is unconfused answers.

body.translated_text: When questioned about dharma-collections or consciousness, one should determine [the answer] by placing [them] into elements, sense-bases, and aggregates.

body.text: tatra tāvat | vijñāneṣu ṣoḍaśadharmāścodyante | kasya vijñānasya katame dharmā gocarā iti ? tadāviṣkriyate-
body.translated_text: Therein, first: among the consciousnesses, the sixteen dharmas are brought up [as questions]. Which dharmas are the objects of which consciousness? That is disclosed:

children.translated_text: Those to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and its origin, those belonging to the desire realm, and those [destroyed] by the exhaustion of meditation — (Abhidh-d 328)
together with those of one's own three [classes], one form-realm class, the passionless ones — these are the domain of [certain] consciousnesses.

body.text: kāmāvacarāḥ khalu duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāprahātavyā dharmāḥ pratyekaṃ pañcānāṃ vijñānānāṃ gocarībhavanti | katameṣāṃ pañcānām ? sveṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ kāmāvacarasya duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyasya vijñānasyālambanam | samudayadarśanaprahātavyasya sarvatragasaṃprayuktasya | bhāvanāprahātavyasya kuśalasya | ekasya ca rūpāptasya bhāvanāprahātavyasya kuśalasyānāsravasya ceti | evaṃ samudayadarśanabhāvanāprahātavyāvapi vaktavyau ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, dharmas of the desire realm to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and the seeing of origination, and by meditation, become the objects of five consciousnesses each. Of which five? Of one's own three — the consciousness to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering in the desire realm is its object; that to be abandoned by the seeing of origination when associated with the universal [defilements]; that to be abandoned by meditation which is wholesome. And of one class belonging to the form realm — to be abandoned by meditation, which is wholesome and uncontaminated. Thus, those to be abandoned by the seeing of origination and by meditation are also to be stated [similarly].

body.text: eta eva trayo dharmāḥ
body.translated_text: These same three dharmas —

body.text: ātmīyādhastrayaikordhvanirmalānāṃ tu rūpajāḥ /
body.translated_text: are objects of their own, the lower three, one upper, and the uncontaminated ones — those born of the form [realm].

body.text: rupāvacaro hi duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyo dharmaḥ aṣṭānāṃ vijñānānāmālambanam | svakatrayasyādharatrayasyordhvaikasyāmalasya ca | svadhātukasya trayasya pūrvavat | adharadhātukasya tu kāmāvacarayorduḥkhasamudayadarśanaprahātavyavisabhāgadhātvālambanayoḥ | bhāvanāprahātavyasya ca kuśalasya ūrdhvaikasyārūpyāvacarasya bhāvanāprahātavyasya kuśalasyānāsravasya ca | evaṃ samudayadarśanabhāvanāprahātavyau vācyau |
body.translated_text: For a dharma of the form realm to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering is the object of eight consciousnesses: its own three, the lower three, one upper, and the uncontaminated. Of its own realm's three, as before. Of the lower realm — those of the desire realm to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and the seeing of origination, having objects in a dissimilar realm; and that to be abandoned by meditation which is wholesome. Of the one upper — the formless realm's [consciousness] to be abandoned by meditation that is wholesome and uncontaminated. Thus, those to be abandoned by the seeing of origination and by meditation are also to be stated.

body.text: ārūpyāptāstridhātvāptatrikanirmalagocarāḥ // Abhidh-d_329 //
body.translated_text: Those belonging to the formless realm are the domain of ten [consciousnesses] — those belonging to three realms, each three, and the uncontaminated. (Abhidh-d 329)

body.text: ārūpyāvacarāsta eva trayo dharmāḥ, daśānāṃ vijñānānāmālambanam | traidhātukānāṃ pratyekaṃ trayāṇām, eṣāmevānāsravasya ca | ityevaṃ tāvat traidhātukāḥ duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyābhāvanāheyāśca dharmā uktāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Those same three dharmas of the formless realm are the objects of ten consciousnesses — three of each of the three realms [making nine], and the uncontaminated. Thus, the dharmas of the three realms that are to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, the seeing of origination, and by meditation have been stated.

body.text: sarve svādhikavijñeyāḥ samaniryāṇadṛkkṣayāḥ /
body.translated_text: All [those to be abandoned by] the seeing of cessation and the path [are objects] of their own plus additional consciousnesses. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: sarva eva traidhātukāḥ nirodhamārgadarśanaheyāḥ svanaikāyikādhikacittagocarā vijñātavyāḥ | kāmāvacaro hi nirodhadarśanaprahātavyo dharmo duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyādivat pañcānāṃ vijñānānāmālambanam | svanaikāyikasya cānirodhadarśanaprahātavyasyeti ṣaṇṇām | evaṃ mārgadarśanaprahātavyo 'pi veditavyaḥ | rūpāvacarau nirodhamārgadarśanaprahātavyau pūrvavadaṣṭānāṃ vijñānānāṃ pratyekamālambanaṃ svanaikāyikasya cādhikasyeti navānām | evamārūpyāvacarau pūrvavaddaśānāṃ svanaikāyikasya cādhikasyetyekādaśānāmālambanaṃ bhavataḥ | uktāḥ pañcadaśadharmāḥ |
body.translated_text: All dharmas of the three realms to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation and the seeing of the path are to be known as objects of their own plus additional consciousnesses. For a dharma of the desire realm to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation is the object of five consciousnesses — like that to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering — plus that of its own class which is not to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation, making six. The same is to be understood for that to be abandoned by the seeing of the path. Those of the form realm to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation and the seeing of the path, as before, are each the object of eight consciousnesses plus that of their own class which is additional, making nine. Similarly, those of the formless realm, as before, are the object of ten [consciousnesses] plus that of their own class which is additional, making eleven. The fifteen dharmas have been stated.

body.text: niṣkleśāstribhavāptāntyatrayanirmalagocarāḥ // Abhidh-d_330 //
body.translated_text: The uncontaminated ones are objects of the last three of those belonging to the three realms, and of the uncontaminated. (Abhidh-d 330)

body.text: traidhātukānāṃ pañcānāṃ prakārāṇāṃ pratyekaṃ ye 'ntyāstrayaḥ prakārā nirodhamārgadarśanabhāvanāheyākhyāḥ, teṣāṃ navānāmanāsravasya ceti | evamanāsravā dharmā daśānāṃ vijñānānāmālambanaṃ bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: Of the five types in each of the three realms, the last three types — called [those to be abandoned by] the seeing of cessation, the seeing of the path, and meditation — and the uncontaminated [making ten]. Thus, uncontaminated dharmas become the objects of ten consciousnesses.

body.text: punaraṣyeṣa evārthapiṇḍaḥ ślokenāvadyotyate-
body.translated_text: Again, this same summary of meaning is elucidated by a verse:

children.translated_text: That belonging to the desire realm is the domain of five; that belonging to the form realm, of eight; (Abhidh-d 331)

children.text: ārupyāptaṃ daśānāṃ tu daśānāmeva cāmalam // Abhidh-d_331 //
children.translated_text: that belonging to the formless realm, of ten; and the uncontaminated, also of ten.

body.text: duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāheyānuśayasaṃprayuktaṃ vijñānaṃ traidhātukamanāsravaṃ ca pañcāṣṭadaśadaśavijñānagocaram | evameṣāṃ ṣoḍaśānāṃ dharmāṇāmetāni ṣoḍaśacittāni traidhātukāni pañcaprakārāṇyanāsravaṃ ca vyavasthāpyānuśayakāryaṃ yojayitavyam |
body.translated_text: Consciousness associated with latent tendencies to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, origination, and by meditation in the three realms, and the uncontaminated — [being] the domain of five, eight, ten, and ten [consciousnesses respectively]. Thus, having established these sixteen dharmas and these sixteen consciousnesses of the three realms of five types each and the uncontaminated, the function of the latent tendencies is to be applied.

body.text: tatra tāvatkāmāvacaraduḥkhadarśanaprahātavyā dharmā daśānuśayāḥ, tatsaṃprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ salakṣaṇānulakṣaṇāḥ aprāptiprāptiprāptayaḥ | ete dharmā viṣayaḥ pañcānāṃ vijñānānām, duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyasya sarvasya vijñānasya, samudayadarśanaheyasya sarvatragasaṃprayuktasya, bhāvanāheyasya kuśalasyākliṣṭasya, dvividhasya kuśalasāsravasyāvyākṛtasya ca, rūpāvacarasyākliṣṭasya kuśalasāsravasya, akliṣṭasyāvyākṛtasya ca kuśalasyoṣmagatādivimokṣāpramāṇādisaṃprayuktasya | avyākṛtasya tu vipākajasya manobhaumasya sukhasaumanasyopekṣāsaṃprayuktasyānāsravasya ca duḥkhadharmajñānasamudayadharmajñānatatkṣāntisaṃprayuktasya vijñānasya |
body.translated_text: Therein, first: the dharmas to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering in the desire realm [include] the ten latent tendencies (<s>anuśayas</s>), the mind and mental factors (<s>cittacaitasika</s>) associated with them, together with their characteristics and subsidiary characteristics, [and] the non-possessions, possessions, and acquisitions. These dharmas are the objects of five consciousnesses: [1] that of all consciousness to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, [2] that to be abandoned by the seeing of origination associated with the universals, [3] that to be abandoned by meditation which is wholesome and unafflicted, [4] that of twofold type — wholesome-with-outflows and indeterminate, [5] that of the form realm — unafflicted, wholesome-with-outflows, and indeterminate — [including] wholesome [consciousness] associated with the warmth stage, liberations, immeasurables, and the rest; and indeterminate maturation-born consciousness of the mental-ground [type], associated with pleasure, mental pleasure, and equanimity; and uncontaminated [consciousness] associated with the knowledges of suffering-dharma and origination-dharma, and the corresponding <s>kṣāntis</s> (patient acceptances).

body.text: tatrānāsrave vijñāne na kecidanuśayā anuśerate | sāsrave tu tatra tāvat-
body.translated_text: Therein, in uncontaminated consciousness, no latent tendencies whatsoever lie dormant. But in consciousness with outflows — first there:

children.translated_text: In consciousness belonging to the desire realm and the upper [realms] directed toward dharmas, three of its own realm (Abhidh-d 332)
and those of the form realm to be abandoned by meditation, together with the universals, lie dormant.

body.text: kāmāptaduḥkhadarśanaprahātavye vijñāne kāmāvacarā duḥkhasamudayabhāvanāheyāḥ sarve 'nuśerate | rūpāvacare tvakliṣṭe kāmāvacaradharma gocarā eva rūpāvacarāḥ sarvatragāḥ, bhāvanāheyāścānuśerate ||
body.translated_text: In consciousness of the desire realm to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, all desire-realm [latent tendencies] to be abandoned by [the seeing of] suffering, origination, and meditation lie dormant. But in unafflicted form-realm [consciousness] having desire-realm dharmas as its object, only form-realm universals and those to be abandoned by meditation lie dormant.

children.text: catvāraḥ parivṛtte sve rūpāptāḥ khalvapi trayaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the 'turned' [consciousness of] one's own [realm], four [classes of] the form realm, indeed three as well; (Abhidh-d 333)
and formless realm ones together with the universals and those [destroyed by] exhaustion through meditation.

body.text: parivṛtte tu khalvālambanālambane vijñāna ityarthaḥ | pūrvakāḥ kāmāvacararūpāvacarā yathoktāḥ | kenādhikībhavanti ? kāmāvacarastāvaccaturtho nikāyo mārgadarśanaprahātavyaḥ | kathaṃ kṛtvā ? yattadduḥkhasamudayajñānaṃ tatkṣāntisaṃprayuktaṃ vijñānaṃ kāmāvacaraduḥkhadarśanaheyadharmālambanam | tatkhalvālambanaṃ mārgadarśanaheyamithyādṛṣṭivicikitsāvidyāsaṃprayuktasya vijñānasya | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 287)

children.text: ) tasminvijñāne te 'nāsravālambanāḥ saṃprayogato 'nuśerate | sāsravālambanāḥ ālambanataḥ | evaṃ kāmāvacarāścatvāro nikāyā bhavanti |
children.translated_text: In that consciousness, those whose object is uncontaminated lie dormant by association; those whose object has outflows, by objectification. Thus, there are four classes of the desire realm.

body.translated_text: 'Turned' means in consciousness whose object is the object [of the preceding one] — that is the meaning. The previous desire-realm and form-realm ones are as stated. What is additional? In the desire realm first, the fourth class — to be abandoned by the seeing of the path. How so?
