That consciousness associated with the knowledge of suffering-dharma and origination-dharma and the corresponding <s>kṣāntis</s>, which has desire-realm dharmas-to-be-abandoned-by-the-seeing-of-suffering as its object — that indeed is the object of consciousness associated with wrong view, doubt, and ignorance to be abandoned by the seeing of the path.

body.text: rūpāvacare vijñāne sarvatragasaṃprayukte tvasarvatragālambate(?) | evaṃ rūpāvacarāstrayo nikāyā bhavanti | tasya tu caturthadhyānabhaumasyākliṣṭasya vijñānasya kāmadhātvālambanasyoṣmagatavimokṣāpramāṇā śubhādisaṃprayuktasyopekṣopavicārasaṃyuktasya vijñānasyālambanam | tatpunarākāśānantyāyatanasāmantakena kuśalenālambyate | atastatrārūpyāḥ sarvatragā bhāvanāheyāścānuśerate | uktaṃ duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyam |
body.translated_text: In form-realm consciousness associated with universals but having non-universal objects — thus there are three classes of the form realm. Of that [consciousness] belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground, unafflicted, having the desire realm as its object, associated with the warmth stage, liberations, immeasurables, purities, and the rest, and associated with equanimity and with subtle investigation — that consciousness becomes the object [of the consciousness] of the preliminary stage (<s>sāmantaka</s>) of the sphere of infinite space which is wholesome. Therefore, formless-realm universals and those to be abandoned by meditation lie dormant therein. The [case of consciousness] to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering has been stated.

body.text: tadvadeva dvitīye 'pi pañcame 'pi tathaiva ca /
body.translated_text: Likewise in the second [class] and in the fifth as well. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: evaṃ samudayadarśanabhāvanāprahātavyayorapi vijñānayorthathoktayordraṣṭavyam | ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ | duḥkhe duḥkhadarśanaheyāḥ sarve, samudayasarvatragāśca | samudaye tu samudayadarśanaheyāḥ sarve, duḥkhadarśanaheyāśca sarvatragāḥ | anyatsarvaṃ samānam |
body.translated_text: Thus, in the [consciousnesses] to be abandoned by the seeing of origination and by meditation as well, [the situation] is to be viewed as stated. But here is the distinction: In [the case of consciousness to be abandoned by the seeing of] suffering, all those to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, and the origination-universals [lie dormant]. But in [the case of consciousness to be abandoned by the seeing of] origination, all those to be abandoned by the seeing of origination, and the suffering-seeing-universals [lie dormant]. Everything else is the same.

body.text: sāsravālambanāḥ sve ca tṛtīye 'pyanuśerate // Abhidh-d_334 //
body.translated_text: Those whose object has outflows also lie dormant in their own and in the third [class]. (Abhidh-d 334)

body.text: nirodhadarśanaprahātavyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vijñānam | tatrāpyete ca trayo nirodhadarśanaheyāśca sāsravālambanāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The third consciousness is that to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation. In that too, these three [classes] and those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation whose object has outflows [lie dormant].

body.text: parivṛtte tu kāmāptāḥ saṃskṛtārthāvalambinaḥ /
body.translated_text: But in the 'turned' [consciousness], those of the desire realm that apprehend conditioned objects — (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: parivṛtte tu vijñāne kāmāvacarāścatvāro nikāyāḥ, nirodhadarśanaheyālambanāśca sāsravālambanāḥ | ye hyanāsravālambanāste nirvāṇālambane vijñāne 'nuśerate, na vijñānālambane |
body.translated_text: in the 'turned' consciousness, the four classes of the desire realm, and the cessation-seeing ones whose object has outflows [lie dormant]. For those whose object is uncontaminated lie dormant in consciousness whose object is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, not in consciousness whose object is [another] consciousness.

children.translated_text: The rest is to be stated as before — (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: pūrve catvāro nikāyāḥ, duḥkhasamudayamārgabhāvanāheyāścānuśerata ityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: the previous four classes — to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, origination, the path, and by meditation — lie dormant — that is the meaning.

body.text: caturthe 'pi tṛtīyavat // Abhidh-d_335 //
body.translated_text: In the fourth [class] also, as in the third. (Abhidh-d 335)

body.text: caturthe 'pi khalu mārgadarśanaheye vijñāne kāmāvacarāstrayo mārgadarśanaheyāśca sāsravālambanā rūpāvacarāḥ savatragā bhāvanāheyāśca ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, in consciousness to be abandoned by the seeing of the path as well, the three classes of the desire realm, and those to be abandoned by the seeing of the path whose object has outflows, and the form-realm universals and those to be abandoned by meditation [lie dormant].

body.text: parivṛtte tu kāmāptāścatvāro 'nyatra pūrvavat /
body.translated_text: But in the 'turned' [consciousness], four of the desire realm, and the rest as before. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: parivṛtte tu khalu vijñāne kāmāvacarāścatvāro nirodhadarśanaheyaṃ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 288)

children.text: ) muktvā | rūpāvacarāstrayo duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāheyāḥ | ārūpyāḥ sarvatragāḥ bhāvanāheyāśca | samāptaṃ kāmāvacaraṃ vijñānam ||
children.translated_text: excluding those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation. Three of the form realm — to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, origination, and meditation. And formless-realm universals and those to be abandoned by meditation. The desire-realm consciousness is complete.

body.translated_text: But indeed in the 'turned' consciousness, four classes of the desire realm —

body.text: rūpāpte prathame 'dhastāt trayaḥ sve khalvapi trayaḥ // Abhidh-d_336 //
body.translated_text: In the first [consciousness] of the form realm, three from below and three of its own indeed; (Abhidh-d 336)

body.text: ārūpyāḥ sarvagāḥ sārdhaṃ bhāvanāpathasaṃkṣayaiḥ /
body.translated_text: and formless-realm universals together with those [destroyed by] exhaustion through the path of meditation.

body.text: rūpāvacare prathame khalu vijñāne kāmāvacarāstrayo duḥkhasamudayavisabhāgadhātvālambanāḥ saṃprayogataḥ | asarvatragāstvālambanato bhāvanāheyāśca sve ca trayaḥ | eta evārūpyāḥ sarvatragā bhāvanāheyāśca |
body.translated_text: In the first consciousness of the form realm indeed: three of the desire realm — those to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and origination having objects in a dissimilar realm, by association; the non-universals by objectification; and those to be abandoned by meditation. And of its own, three — these same [classes]. The formless-realm universals and those to be abandoned by meditation [are the same].

children.translated_text: In the 'turned' [consciousness], three from below, (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāheyāḥ |
body.translated_text: to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, origination, and by meditation;

body.text: catvāraśca svadhātutaḥ // Abhidh-d_337 //
body.translated_text: and four from one's own realm. (Abhidh-d 337)

body.text: mārgadarśanaheyāśca duḥkhasamudayānvayajñānakṣāntisaṃprayukte vijñāne ||
body.translated_text: And those to be abandoned by the seeing of the path — in consciousness associated with the <s>kṣāntis</s> and knowledges of suffering-subsequent-knowledge and origination-subsequent-knowledge.

body.text: ārūpyāptāśca catvāro nikāyā anuśerate /
body.translated_text: And four classes of the formless realm lie dormant. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: duḥkhasamudayayoḥ mārgadarśanamithyādṛṣṭyādisaṃprayuktacittālambanatvāt |
body.translated_text: Because [that consciousness] is the object of consciousness associated with wrong view and the like to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and origination [in the formless realm].

body.text: tadvadeva dvitīye 'pi pañcame 'pi tathaiva ca // Abhidh-d_338 //
body.translated_text: Likewise in the second [class] and in the fifth as well. (Abhidh-d 338)

body.text: dvitīye 'pi khalu kāmāvacararūpāvacarāstrayo duḥkhasamudayabhāvanāheyāḥ | ārūpyāḥ sarvagā bhāvanāheyāśca ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, in the second [consciousness of the form realm] as well, three of the desire realm and form realm — to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, origination, and meditation. Formless-realm universals and those to be abandoned by meditation [likewise].

body.text: sāsravālambanāḥ sve ca tṛtīye 'pyanuśerate /
body.translated_text: Those whose object has outflows also lie dormant in their own and in the third. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: yathā nirdiṣṭa iti |
body.translated_text: As indicated.

body.text: parivṛtte tu rūpāptāḥ saṃskṛtārthāvalambinaḥ // Abhidh-d_339 //
body.translated_text: But in the 'turned' [consciousness], those of the form realm that apprehend conditioned objects. (Abhidh-d 339)

body.text: nirodhadarśanaheyā asaṃskṛtālambanān muktvā ||
body.translated_text: Excluding those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation whose object is unconditioned.

body.text: anyattu pūrvavajjñeyaṃ caturthe 'pi tṛtīyavat /
body.translated_text: The rest is to be known as before; in the fourth also, as in the third. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: kāmāvacarāḥ trayo duḥkhasamudayabhāvanāheyākhyāḥ, ārūpyāvacarāścatvāraḥ, nirodhākhyaṃ muktvā | 'caturthe 'pi'; mārgadarśanaheye 'tṛtīyavat'; draṣṭavyam | yathā tṛtīye sāsravālambanāḥ svanaikāyikā adhikībhavanti, tathā caturthe 'pi sve sāsravālambanā adhikībhavanti |
body.translated_text: Three of the desire realm — called to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, origination, and meditation; and four of the formless realm — excluding those called [to be abandoned by the seeing of] cessation. 'In the fourth also' — to be abandoned by the seeing of the path — 'as in the third' is to be viewed. Just as in the third, those of one's own class whose object has outflows become additional — so in the fourth also, those of one's own [class] whose object has outflows become additional.

children.translated_text: In the 'turned' [consciousness], as in the third — (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: catvāro duḥkhasamudayamārgadarśanabhāvanāheyākhyāḥ rūpāvacarāḥ, kāmāvacarāsrayaḥ, ārūpyāvacarāścatvāro nirodhadarśanaheyaṃ muktvā | mārgācca trayaḥ | samāptaṃ rūpāvacaram |
body.translated_text: four of the form realm — called to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, origination, the path, and meditation; three of the desire realm; and four of the formless realm excluding those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation. And from the path, three. The form realm is complete.

body.text: ārūpyādye nibodhayet // Abhidh-d_340 //
body.translated_text: In the first of the formless realm, one should understand — (Abhidh-d 340)

body.text: sve trayaḥ kāmadhātvāptā rūpāptāśca trayastrayaḥ /
body.translated_text: In one's own [realm], three are obtained from the desire realm, and three groups of three are obtained from the form realm.

body.text: sve trayo duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāheyāḥ kāmāptāḥ eta eva | rūpāptāśca eta eva trayaḥ |
body.translated_text: In one's own [realm], the three — to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, the seeing of origination, and by cultivation — are obtained from the desire realm: those very [three]. And the same three are obtained from the form realm.

body.text: rūpāptavatparāvṛtte dvitīye pañcame tathā // Abhidh-d_341 //
body.translated_text: Like those obtained from the form realm, in the reversed [object], in the second and fifth [consciousnesses] likewise. (Abhidh-d 341)

body.text: parāvṛtte 'pi trayo nirodhamārgadarśanaheyau hitvā | rūpyārūpyāścatvāro nirodhadarśanaheyaṃ muktvā ||
body.translated_text: In the reversed [object] also, three [classes bind], excluding those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation and of the path. For the form and formless [realms], four [classes bind], excluding those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation.

body.text: yathā prathame dvitīye pañcame ca,
body.translated_text: As in the first, second, and fifth [consciousnesses],

body.text: tṛtīye khalvapi sve ca sāsravārthāvalambinaḥ /
body.translated_text: in the third also, [those that are] one's own and have objects that are with-outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>),

body.text: tṛtīye 'pi khalveta eva 'sve ca sāsravārthāvalambinaḥ'; |
body.translated_text: in the third also, these very [classes bind that are] 'one's own and have objects that are with-outflows';

body.text: parāvṛtte svadhātvāptāḥ saṃskṛtārthāvalambinaḥ // Abhidh-d_342 //
body.translated_text: in the reversed [object], those obtained from one's own realm [that] have conditioned objects. (Abhidh-d 342)

body.text: parāvṛtte khalu sarve '; 'rūpyāvacarā asaṃskṛtālambanānmuktvā ||
body.translated_text: In the reversed [object] indeed, all [bind]; 'excluding those belonging to the form-realm that have unconditioned objects.'

body.text: anyattvādyavadākhyeyaṃ caturthe 'pi tṛtīyavat /
body.translated_text: The rest should be stated in the same way for the fourth, as for the third.

body.text: kāmāvacararūpāvacarāḥ pūrvavadākhyātavyāḥ | 'caturthe 'pi tṛtīyavat |'; sve sāsravālambanāstvatrādhikī bhavanti |
body.translated_text: Those belonging to the desire realm and form realm should be stated as before. 'In the fourth also, as in the third'; in one's own [realm], those with outflow-objects are additionally [present] here.

body.text: ādyavattu parāvṛtte vijñāne nirdiśed budhaḥ // Abhidh-d_343 //
body.translated_text: But in the reversed [object], the wise one should state regarding consciousness as in the first. (Abhidh-d 343)

body.text: parāvṛtte khalu vijñāne ādyavatkāmāvacarāstrayaḥ, nirodhamārgadṛggheyau hitvā | rūpāvacarāścatvāraḥ, nirodhadarśanaheyaṃ muktvā | aprahātavyadharmālambane vijñāne nirodhamārgadarśanaheyānāsravālambanasaṃprayukte | tatra traidhātukāstrayo 'nuśerate | ālambanālambanaṃ tu duḥkhasamudayamārgadarśanabhāvanāheyeta nikāyenālambate | nirodhadarśanaheyena ca sāsravālambanenālambyate | tatra saṃskṛtālambanāścatvāro nikāyāḥ, nirodhālambanaṃ muktvā | te hi nirvāṇālambane vijñāne nānuśerate, vijñānālambane tu ||
body.translated_text: In the reversed consciousness indeed, the desire-realm [classes] are three, as in the first, excluding those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation and of the path. The form-realm [classes] are four, excluding those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation. In a consciousness whose object is the object of a <s>dharma</s> not to be abandoned, which is associated with an undefiled [state] to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation and of the path — therein, latent tendencies belonging to all three realms, of three classes, lie latent. But the object-of-the-object is apprehended by the class [of latent tendencies] to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, origination, the path, and by cultivation. And it is apprehended by a with-outflow [object] to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation. Therein, those with conditioned objects are four classes, excluding those with cessation as their object. For those [latent tendencies] do not lie latent in a consciousness whose object is <s>nirvāṇa</s>, but they do in one whose object is consciousness.

body.text: samāptāni ṣoḍaśacittāni | teṣu cānuśayanidaśaḥ kṛtaḥ | adhunā cakṣurindriyādīnāṃ vaktavyaḥ | so 'yamupadiśyate-
body.translated_text: The sixteen [types of] consciousness are completed. And in them, the exposition of binding by latent tendencies has been made. Now the [binding with respect to] the eye-faculty and so forth must be stated. That is taught:

children.translated_text: The class to be abandoned by the path of cultivation, together with the universal ones, (Abhidh-d 344)
lies latent in the eye-faculty — [those] obtained from two realms, and the formless-realm [ones also]. (Abhidh-d 344)

body.text: cakṣurindriye khalu bhāvanāheyāḥ sarvatragāścānuśayāḥ kāmāvacararūpāvacarā anuśerate | evaṃ yāvatkāyendriye cakṣurdhātau rūpadhātau cakṣurvijñānadhātau yāvadvistareṇa kāyavijñānadhātau yāvadrūpaskandhe vācyam ||
body.translated_text: In the eye-faculty indeed, the latent tendencies to be abandoned by cultivation and the universal ones, belonging to the desire realm and form realm, lie latent. Likewise up to the body-faculty, the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and so on in detail up to the body-consciousness-element, and up to the form-aggregate — this should be stated.

body.text: adhunā cakṣurindriyālambane vijñāne vaktavyāḥ-
body.translated_text: Now, [the latent tendencies] in a consciousness whose object is the eye-faculty are to be stated:

children.translated_text: The classes obtained from the desire and form [realms], in regard to the eye-faculty as object, (Abhidh-d 345)
to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, [seeing of] cause, seeing, and cultivation — three groups of three. (Abhidh-d 345)

body.text: ārūpyā bhāvanāheyāḥ sarvagāścānuśerate /
body.translated_text: Those from the formless realm, to be abandoned by cultivation, and the universal ones, lie latent. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: cakṣurindriyālambane khalu vijñāne kāmāvacararūpāvacarāḥ duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāprahātavyāḥ, ārūpyāvacarāśca bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ, sarvatragāścānuśerate |
body.translated_text: In a consciousness whose object is the eye-faculty indeed, those belonging to the desire realm and form realm, to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, the seeing of origination, and by cultivation, and those belonging to the formless realm to be abandoned by cultivation, and the universal ones — lie latent.

body.text: parivṛtte tu catvāraḥ samadṛkkṣayavarjitāḥ // Abhidh-d_346 //
body.translated_text: But in the reversed [object], four [classes], excluding those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation, lie latent. (Abhidh-d 346)

body.text: cakṣurindriyālambanālambane tu vijñāne catvāro nikāyā anuśerate | nirodhadarśanaheyaṃ hitvā | taddhi cakṣurindriyālambanaṃ vijñānaṃ sarvatra saṃprayuktam | tadapyālambanaṃ sarvatragāṇām | evaṃ trayaḥ parāvṛtte |
body.translated_text: In a consciousness that has as its object the object of the eye-faculty, four classes of latent tendencies lie latent, excluding those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation. For that consciousness whose object is the eye-faculty is associated everywhere [with conditioned objects]. That too is the object of the universal ones. Likewise, three [classes bind] in the reversed [object].

body.text: dviṣparāvṛtte tu cakṣurindriyaṃ khalvālambanaṃ duḥkhasamudayadharmajñānakṣāntisaṃprayuktasya cittasya | tatpunarālambanaṃ kāmāvacaramārgadarśanaprahātavyam | mithyādṛṣṭivicikitsāvidyātatsaṃprayuktānāṃ vijñānānām | teṣu vijñāneṣvanāsravālambanāḥ saṃprayogataḥ, sāsravālambanāstvālambanato 'nuśerate | evaṃ caturtho nikāyo vardhate mārgadarśanaheyaḥ | tadevaṃ sati kāmāvacarāścatvāraḥ, ārūpyāvacarāścatvāraḥ, sarve 'bhisamasya traidhātukāścatvāro bhavanti |
body.translated_text: In the twice-reversed [object]: the eye-faculty is indeed the object of a consciousness associated with the <s>duḥkha-samudaya-dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the cognition of the dharma of suffering and origination). That [consciousness] is again the object of [latent tendencies] to be abandoned by the seeing of the desire-realm path — namely, the consciousnesses associated with wrong view, doubt, ignorance, and their accompaniments. In those consciousnesses, the undefiled-object [latent tendencies bind] by association, and the with-outflow-object ones [bind] by object. Thus the fourth class increases — those to be abandoned by the seeing of the path. This being so, there are four [classes] from the desire realm, four from the formless realm, and combining all, four [classes] from all three realms.

body.text: ākāśānantyāyatanasya khalu kuśalasya cakṣurindriyamālambanam | tatrārūpyāḥ sarvatragā bhāvanāheyāścānuśerate | tatrāpi sarvatragasaṃprayukte cetasi asarvatragā vardhanta iti trayo bhavanti | duḥkhasamudayālambanajñānakṣāntisaṃprayuktasya ca vijñānasya cakṣurindriyamālambanam | tadārupyamārgadarśanaprahātavyasya mithyādaṣṭyādisaṃprayukttasya vijñānasyālambanam | tatra te 'nāsravālambanāḥ saṃprayogataḥ, sāsravālambanāḥ ālambanataḥ | evamārūpyāvacarā api catvāro nikāyā bhavantīti ||
body.translated_text: The wholesome [consciousness] of the <s>Ākāśānantyāyatana</s> (Sphere of Infinite Space) has the eye-faculty as its object. Therein, the formless-realm universal ones and those to be abandoned by cultivation lie latent. Therein too, in the consciousness associated with the universal ones, the non-universal ones increase, making three [classes]. And the consciousness associated with the <s>duḥkha-samudaya-ālambanajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the cognition of suffering and origination as object) has the eye-faculty as its object. That is the object of a consciousness associated with wrong view and so forth, to be abandoned by the seeing of the formless-realm path. Therein, the undefiled-object [latent tendencies bind] by association, and the with-outflow-object ones by object. Thus the formless-realm [classes] also become four.

children.text: duḥkhendriye tu kāmāptaḥ svaireva saha sarvagaiḥ /
children.translated_text: In the suffering-faculty (<s>duḥkhendriya</s>), those obtained from the desire realm, together with one's own and the universal ones, (Abhidh-d 347)

children.text: tadgocare tu vijñāne nikāyā anuśerate // Abhidh-d_347 //
children.translated_text: in a consciousness whose object is that, the classes of latent tendencies lie latent. (Abhidh-d 347)
Those obtained from the desire realm are three [classes]; from the form [realm], the universal and cultivation-to-be-abandoned ones, (Abhidh-d continuation)

children.text: paravṛtte tu catvāraḥ kāmāptā anuśerate // Abhidh-d_348 //
children.translated_text: but in the reversed [object], four obtained from the desire realm lie latent. (Abhidh-d 348)
Three from the form realm and the last [formless realm] — to be abandoned by cultivation and the universal ones; (Abhidh-d 349)
all [classes], and in the twice-reversed [object], four lie latent. (Abhidh-d 349)
In the pleasure-faculty (<s>sukhendriya</s>), in its object-consciousness, and in its domain also, (Abhidh-d 350)
those obtained from the desire realm and so forth, according to applicability, and the universal ones, lie latent. (Abhidh-d 350)

body.text: tatra tāvat | sukhendriyaṃ saptavidham | kāmāvacaraṃ bhāvanāprahātavyam, rūpāvacaraṃ pañcaprakāram, anāsravaṃ ceti | tadetatsamāsato dvādaśavidhasya vijñānasyālambanaṃ bhavati | kāmāvacarasya catuṣprakārasya anyatra nirodhadarśanaheyāt, rūpāvacarasya pañcaprakārasya, ārūpyāvacarasya dviprakārasya mārgadarśanabhāvanāheyasya anāsravasya ca | idaṃ dvādaśavidhaṃ sukhendriyālambanaṃ vijñānam | tatra yathāyogaṃ kāmāvacarāścatvāro nikāyāḥ rūpāvacarāḥ saṃskṛtāvalambanāḥ, ārūpyāvacarau dvau nikāyau, sarvatragāścānuśayā anuśerata iti |
body.translated_text: Therein, to begin with: the pleasure-faculty is sevenfold — belonging to the desire realm and to be abandoned by cultivation; belonging to the form realm in five modes; and undefiled. This, in summary, becomes the object of twelve types of consciousness: four types from the desire realm excluding those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation; five types from the form realm; two types from the formless realm — those to be abandoned by the seeing of the path and by cultivation; and the undefiled. These are the twelve types of consciousness having the pleasure-faculty as object. Therein, according to applicability, four classes from the desire realm, the form-realm [classes] with conditioned objects, two classes from the formless realm, and the universal latent tendencies lie latent.

body.text: tatpunaḥ sukhendriyālambanaṃ vijñānaṃ yasya cittasyālambanaṃ taccittaṃ sukhendriyā lambanālambanam | tasmin katyanuśayānuśerate ? tatkhalu sukhendriyālambanaṃ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 292)

children.text: ) dvādaśavidhaṃ cittaṃ katamasya vijñānasyālambanam ? tasyaiva ca dvādaśavidhasyārūpyāvacarasya ca bhūyo dviprakārasya duḥkhasamudayadarśana prahātavyasya | idaṃ caturdaśavidhaṃ sukhendriyālambanaṃ vijñānam | tatrārūpyāvacarau duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyau vardhayitvā kāmāvacarā ārūpyāvacarāśca catvāro nikāyāḥ, rūpāvacarāśca saṃskṛtālambanā anuśayānuśerata iti 'yathāyoga'- vacanāt, 'api'śabdācca draṣṭavyam ||
children.translated_text: ) — of which consciousness is that the object? Of those same twelve types, and additionally of two more types from the formless realm — those to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and origination. These make fourteen types of consciousness having the pleasure-faculty as object. Therein, adding the two formless-realm [classes] to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and origination, four classes from the desire realm and four from the formless realm, and from the form realm those with conditioned objects, lie latent — as should be understood from the phrase 'according to applicability' and the word 'also.'

body.translated_text: Furthermore, the consciousness having the pleasure-faculty as its object is itself the object of some consciousness — that consciousness is the object-of-the-object of the pleasure-faculty. In that, how many latent tendencies lie latent? The twelve types of consciousness having the pleasure-faculty as object (

children.translated_text: All [latent tendencies] comprised in the three realms [lie latent] in the mental faculty (<s>manendriya</s>); (Abhidh-d 351)
in a consciousness whose object is that, those having all conditioned [dharmas] as their domain [lie latent]. (Abhidh-d 351)

body.text: manaindriye khalu sarvatraidhātukāḥ ye 'pi te nirvāṇālambanāste 'pi saṃprayogataḥ | manaindriyālambanaṃ khalu vijñānaṃ saṃskṛtālambanam | atastatra saṃskṛtālambanāste 'nuśayā anuśerate |
body.translated_text: In the mental faculty indeed, all [latent tendencies] belonging to the three realms [lie latent] — even those with <s>nirvāṇa</s> as their object, by association. The consciousness having the mental faculty as its object has conditioned objects. Therefore, therein, those latent tendencies with conditioned objects lie latent.

children.translated_text: Only those with conditioned objects lie latent in the reversed [object]; (Abhidh-d 352)

children.text: viśeṣo dviḥparāvṛttau vidyate 'tra na kaścana // Abhidh-d_352 //
children.translated_text: there is no difference whatsoever in the twice-reversed [object] here. (Abhidh-d 352)

body.text: pūrvanītyā vātra parivṛtte 'nuśayakāryaṃ boddhavyam | dviṣparāvṛtte 'pyatra na kaścidviśeṣa iti draṣṭavyam ||
body.translated_text: By the method established earlier, the function of latent-tendency-binding in the reversed [object] should be understood here also. In the twice-reversed [object] too, there is no difference here — this should be noted.

body.text: adhunā ṣoḍaśānāṃ cittānāṃ kasya cittasya samanantaraṃ kati cittānyutpadyanta ityupadiśyate |
body.translated_text: Now it is taught: of these sixteen [types of] consciousness, immediately after which consciousness do how many consciousnesses arise?

children.translated_text: From the consciousness to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and so forth, for one in the desire realm, (Abhidh-d 353)

children.text: bhavatyanantaraṃ ṣaḍ vā tasyorddhvaṃ pañca pañca vā // Abhidh-d_353 //
children.translated_text: six consciousnesses arise immediately after it, or five above it, or five. (Abhidh-d 353)

body.text: kāmadhātūpapannasya duḥkhadarśanaheyādeścittādanantaraṃ svabhūmikāni pañca, ṣaṣṭhaṃ ca bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ prathamadhyānasāmantakāt | sa yadā kāmadhātoścyutvā rūpadhātāvupapadyate tasya tatratyāni pañca bhavanti | evamārūpyeṣūpapadyamānasyārūpyāṇi pañca bhavantīti ||
body.translated_text: For one born in the desire realm, immediately after the consciousness to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, five [consciousnesses arise] from one's own level, and a sixth — to be abandoned by cultivation — from the threshold of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. When he, departing from the desire realm, is reborn in the form realm, five [consciousnesses] belonging to that [realm] arise. Likewise, for one being reborn in the formless realms, five formless [consciousnesses] arise.

children.translated_text: But for one born in the form realm, one should state the consciousnesses: (Abhidh-d 354)

children.text: ekaṃ vā pañca vā ṣaḍ vā sapta vā yadi vā daśa // Abhidh-d_354 //
children.translated_text: one, or five, or six, or seven, or ten. (Abhidh-d 354)

body.text: tatra 'ekam'; vītarāgasyoparisāmantakādbhāvanāmayam | 'ṣaḍ'; vītarāgasya kāmāvacaraṃ bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ prathamadhyānaphalam | 'pañca'; svabhaumāni | 'sapta vā'; uparisāmantakādbhāvanāprahātavyaṃ kuśalaṃ sāsravam | 'daśa vā'; rūpebhyaḥ pracyutasya kāmarūpeṣūpapadyamānasyeti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, 'one' — for one free from passion, the cultivation-produced [consciousness] from the upper threshold. 'Six' — for one free from passion, the desire-realm cultivation-to-be-abandoned consciousness, the emanation-consciousness, and the fruit of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. 'Five' — those of one's own level. 'Or seven' — the cultivation-to-be-abandoned wholesome with-outflow [consciousness] from the upper threshold. 'Or ten' — for one departing from the form [realm] and being reborn in the desire and form [realms].

children.translated_text: For one born in the formless realm, one should note these consciousnesses: (Abhidh-d 355)
five belonging to one's own realm only; at the time of death, ten from elsewhere. (Abhidh-d 355)

body.text: rūpakāmeṣūpapadyamānasya tatratyāni daśa bhavanti | svāni pañca pañcānyataḥ | gatametat ||
body.translated_text: For one being reborn in the form and desire [realms], ten [consciousnesses] belonging to those [realms] arise — five of one's own and five from elsewhere. This has been explained.

body.text: idānīṃ vaktavyam | atha yadidaṃ sānuśayaṃ cittamuktaṃ tatkatham ? ityatrābhidhīyate-
body.translated_text: Now it must be stated: As for what was said — 'consciousness with latent tendencies' (<s>sānuśaya citta</s>) — how is that? In response to this it is said:

children.translated_text: Consciousness is regarded as 'with latent tendencies' because of companionship and because of binding by latent tendencies; (Abhidh-d 356)
in two ways for the defiled, in one way alone for the undefiled — thus it is designated. (Abhidh-d 356)

body.text: dvābhyāṃ khalu prakārābhyāṃ cittaṃ sānuśayamucyate | sācivyabhāvenānuśāyitvena ca | tatra kliṣṭaṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ sānuśayaṃ yadaprahīṇakleśam | akliṣṭaṃ punarekadhā sācivyabhāvanaiveti | tatra kliṣṭaṃ cittamanuśayaiḥ saṃprayuktairaprahīṇaiḥ sānuśayaṃ tadālambanaiścāprahīṇaiḥ |
body.translated_text: By two modes indeed is consciousness called 'with latent tendencies' — by the mode of companionship and by the mode of binding. Therein, defiled [consciousness] is 'with latent tendencies' by both causes — that whose afflictions are not abandoned. But undefiled [consciousness] is [so] in one way only — by the mode of companionship alone. Therein, defiled consciousness is 'with latent tendencies' through associated latent tendencies that are not abandoned, and through [latent tendencies having it as] object that are not abandoned.

body.text: kathamiha yo 'nuśayo yena cittena saṃprayuktaḥ sa khalvaprahīṇastasmiṃścitte 'nuśete ? yāvaddhi tadanuśayānuprāptiviśeṣeṇa sā cittasantatiravaṣṭabdhā cādhiṣṭhitā ca bhavati, niṣyandaphalasya cānāgatasya tasyāṃ cittasantatau sabhāgaheturutpattaye kṛtāspado bhavati, tāvadasāvanuśayastaśmiṃścetasyanuśeta ityucyate | tasya punaḥ kleśāśīviṣasya prāptidraṃṣṭrāvabhaṅge kṛte vidyamāno 'pi san kleśastasmiṃścetasyanarthānutpādanāt sannapi saṃprayogataḥ nānuśeta ityucyate | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 294)

children.text: ) nityaṃ ca tadālambanato kāritrākaraṇāt, tasminnālambane mārgavidūṣaṇākāradūṣite ālambanato 'pi nānuśeta ityucyate | na tu kadācinmuñjeśīkāvaduddhṛtya śakyate tasmāt kleśaḥ cittātpṛthakkartuṃ nirnāśayituṃ vā svālambanādvā vimukhīkartum | uktaṃ hi- "yo dharmo yasya dharmasyālambanaṃ kadācitsa dharmastasya dharmasya nālambanam ? āha- na kadācit" iti | atastaccittaṃ sahāyabhāvena sānuśayaṃ sahāyabhāvasyāparityāgāt | na tvanuśayabhāvena sānuśayaṃ tatrānarthānutpādanāt |
children.translated_text: ) And because it perpetually does not perform its function with respect to that object, when that object has been spoiled by the aspect of the path's corruption [of its attractive character], it is said not to lie latent by object either. But at no time can the affliction be extracted from consciousness like a reed from its sheath, or separated from it, or destroyed, or turned away from its object. For it has been said: 'A <s>dharma</s> that is the object of a [particular] <s>dharma</s> — is there ever a time when that <s>dharma</s> is not the object of that <s>dharma</s>? The answer: never.' Therefore, that consciousness is 'with latent tendencies' by way of companionship, because companionship is not relinquished. But it is not 'with latent tendencies' by way of [actual] latent-tendency-binding, because of not producing harm therein.

body.translated_text: How is it that a latent tendency associated with a given consciousness, being not yet abandoned, lies latent in that consciousness? As long as, through the specific acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>) of that latent tendency, that mental continuum is held and maintained, and [as long as] for the future outflow-fruit, the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>) has its ground established for arising in that mental continuum — for that long, that latent tendency is said to lie latent in that consciousness. But when the fang of acquisition of that affliction-serpent is broken, then even though the affliction still exists, because it does not produce harm in that consciousness, it is said not to lie latent by association even though it exists. (

body.text: kataratpunaścittaṃ sānuśayam ? traidhātukaṃ pratyekaṃ pañcaprakāram | punaḥ pratyekaṃ dvidhā bhidyate | sarvatragāsarvatragasāsravā nāsravālambanakliṣṭākliṣṭabhedaiḥ |
body.translated_text: Which consciousness, then, is 'with latent tendencies'? That belonging to each of the three realms is fivefold. Furthermore, each is divided in two — by the distinctions of universal and non-universal, with-outflow and without-outflow object, and defiled and undefiled.

body.text: tatra duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktam | tayā ca satkāyadṛṣṭyā tatsaṃprayuktayā cāvidyayā sahāyabhāvena cānuśayāne ca sānuśayam | śeṣaiḥ svanikāyikaiḥ samudayadarśanaprahātavyaiśca sarvatragairanuśayabhāvenaiva | śeṣarnobhayathā | evaṃ sarvaiḥ duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaṃḥ samudayadarśanaprahātavyaiśca saṃprayuktaṃ cittaṃ yathāyogamabhyūhitavyam |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is to be abandoned by seeing suffering, [when] associated with <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existent body) — by that <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and by the ignorance associated with it, [the mind] is latent both in the manner of companionship and of underlying tendency. By the remaining [defilements] of its own class and by the universally operative ones to be abandoned by seeing origination, it is latent only in the manner of underlying tendency. By the rest, it is not [latent] in either way. Thus, the mind associated with what is to be abandoned by seeing suffering and by seeing origination should be inferred according to its applicability.

body.text: nirodhadarśanaprahātavyaṃ mithyādṛṣṭisaṃprayuktam | tathaiva tatsaṃprayuktayā cāvidyayobhayathā | śeṣaiḥ svānikāyikasāsravālambanaiḥ sarvatragaiścānuśayabhāvenaiva | svānikāyikānāsravālambanaistadanyaiśca nobhayathā | evamanyairnirodhadarśanaprahātavyaiḥ mārgadarśanaprahātavyaiśca yathāsaṃbhavaṃ vaktavyam |
body.translated_text: What is to be abandoned by seeing cessation, [when] associated with wrong view — likewise by the ignorance associated with it, in both ways. By the remaining [defilements] of its own class that have contaminated objects and by the universally operative ones, only in the manner of underlying tendency. By [those of] its own class with uncontaminated objects and by others, not in either way. Similarly, what is to be abandoned by seeing cessation and by seeing the path should be stated as applicable.

body.text: bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ rāgasaṃprayuktam | tenaiva tatsaṃprayuktayā cāvidyayobhayathā | śeṣairbhāvanāprahātavyaiḥ sarvatragaiścānuśayairbhāvanairvā | anyairnobhayathā | evamanyadbhāvanāheyasaṃprayuktamapi yathāyogaṃ vācyam |
body.translated_text: What is to be abandoned by cultivation, [when] associated with attachment — by that very [attachment] and by the ignorance associated with it, in both ways. By the remaining [defilements] to be abandoned by cultivation and by the universally operative underlying tendencies, or by those of cultivation. By others, not in either way. Similarly, other [minds] associated with what is to be abandoned by cultivation should be stated as applicable.

body.text: akliṣṭantu svānikāyikaiḥ sarvatragaiścānuśayabhāvenaiva sānuśayamiti ||
body.translated_text: But the undefiled [mind] is latent only by [defilements of] its own class and by the universally operative ones, in the manner of underlying tendency alone.

body.text: kaḥ punareṣāmanuśayānāṃ pravṛttyanukramaḥ ? taducyate | mohastāvat sarvakleśāgraṇī, tasmātkleśapuroyāyinaḥ |
body.translated_text: What then is the order of arising of these underlying tendencies? That is stated. Delusion (<s>moha</s>) is indeed the leader of all defilements; therefore, it precedes the defilements:

children.translated_text: From delusion, the view of the self-existent body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>); from that, the extreme view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>);
from that, doubt (<s>kāṅkṣā</s>); from that, wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>); from that, adherence to rites and rules (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>); from that, [wrong] views. (Abhidh-d 357)
Attachment (<s>rāga</s>) [arises] with respect to one's own view; pride (<s>māna</s>) likewise; hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) extends to what is other.
This order of these [defilements] should be known as [established] from the preponderance of [their] arising. (Abhidh-d 358)

body.text: iha tāvad bālasya pañcopādānaskandhātmake duḥkhe saṃmugdhasya phalabhūtān pañcopādānaskandhānajānataḥ satkāyadṛṣṭirūpajāyate | sattvajīvapudgalātmagrāhayogena | tato 'sya tacchāśvatocchedāntagrāhalakṣaṇāntagrāhadṛṣṭiḥ | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- yadi tāvadayaṃ nityo 'vikārī puruṣaḥ kiṃ dharmeṇa yaḥ sukhena nānugṛhyate, duḥkhena vā notpīḍyate | athāyamucchedadharmānityastathāpi kiṃ dharmeṇeti vicārayataḥ kāṅkṣotpadyate | kāṅkṣāpravṛddhyā mithyādarśanamāvahati | tadakāraṇe kāraṇābhiniveśānnihīnaṃ cāgrato grahaṇāt śīlavratadṛṣṭiparāmarśāvākarṣati | tato 'sya 'rāgaḥ svadṛśi mānaśca dveṣo 'nyatra pratāyate |'; tasya khalu mithyādarśanabhūtagrahāvedha śādaśreyasi śreyobuddhyā pravṛttasyānagre cāgryabuddhyabhiniviṣṭasya svapakṣe rāgo bhavati parapakṣe ca dveṣaḥ pravartate | ityataḥ tat 'jñeyaḥ pravṛttibāhulyādevameṣāmanukramaḥ'; ||
body.translated_text: Here, to begin with, when an ignorant person is bewildered regarding suffering consisting of the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging), not knowing the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> that are the fruit, <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> arises — through the grasping of a being, a living soul, a person, and a self. From that, the <s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s> (extreme view), characterized by grasping at eternalism or annihilationism, [arises] for him. He thinks: 'If this person is eternal and unchanging, what is the use of <s>Dharma</s>, since he is neither benefited by happiness nor afflicted by suffering? But if he is subject to annihilation and impermanent, then too what is the use of <s>Dharma</s>?' — for one deliberating thus, doubt arises. Through the growth of doubt, wrong view is brought about. Through adherence to what is not a cause as a cause, and through grasping what is inferior as superior, it draws in the views of adherence to rites and rules and adherence to [wrong] views. Then for him, 'attachment arises with respect to one's own view, and pride, while hatred extends to what is other.' For one who, pierced by the grasping of wrong view as truth, engages in what is not the highest good with the conviction that it is the highest good, and who adheres to what is not supreme with the conviction that it is supreme — attachment arises toward his own faction, and hatred operates toward the other faction. Therefore, 'this order of these [defilements] should be known as [established] from the preponderance of [their] arising.'

body.text: vayaṃ tu paśyāmaḥ
body.translated_text: But we hold:

body.text: sadasanmitrayogāttu tadvṛttyaniyamo mataḥ /
body.translated_text: From association with good and bad friends, the non-fixity of their arising is held.

body.text: kalyāṇamitrapāpamitrasaṃsargāddhi prāyeṇa śraddhādīnāṃ guṇānāmeṣāṃ ca kleśānāṃ samudācārapravṛttiḥ ācāryāṇāmabhimateti | sa punareṣaḥ-
body.translated_text: For through association with virtuous friends and evil friends, there is, for the most part, the active arising of qualities such as faith and the rest, and of these defilements — this is the position of the <s>Ācāryas</s>. And this [defilement] —

body.text: kleśa utpadyate kaścitsaṃpūrṇaiḥ kāraṇaistribhiḥ // Abhidh-d_359 //
body.translated_text: a certain defilement arises with the three causes complete; (Abhidh-d 359)

body.text: hetuprayogaviṣayabalaiḥ kaścit tribhirutpadyate | kaścid dvābhyāmiti | (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 296]

children.text: ) tatra hetubalaṃ sabhāgasarvatragādihetubhāvanāgatotpattaye vartamānaprāptyutsarge meghikādinidarśanāt | prayogabalamapyayoniśo manaskārādisaṃnidhānam | pratyayabalamaparijñātaviṣayābhāsagamanaṃ nidarśanamarhatparihāṇisūtramiti ||
children.translated_text: ) Therein, the force of the seed — for what has arisen through the cultivation of homogeneous and universally operative causes, [there is arising] through the release of present acquisition, as illustrated by the case of <s>Meghika</s> and the like. The force of application is also the proximity of improper mental engagement (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>) and the like. The force of the condition is the encountering of an object whose [nature] has not been fully comprehended — the illustration is the <s>Arhat</s>-retrogression sūtra.

body.translated_text: by the forces of seed, application, and object, some arise with [all] three; some with two. (

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the commentary called <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>,

body.text: pañcamasyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [this is] the second quarter (<s>pāda</s>) of the fifth chapter.

body.text: pañcamādhyāye
body.translated_text: In the fifth chapter,

body.text: tṛtīyapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: the third quarter.

body.text: atha ya ime bhagavatā traya āsravā ākhyātāḥ- "kāmāsravo bhavāsravo 'vidyāsravaśca |" eṣāṃ kaḥ svabhāvaḥ ? tadidamārabhyate-
body.translated_text: Now, regarding the three outflows (<s>āsravas</s>) declared by the <s>Bhagavat</s> — 'the outflow of desire (<s>kāmāsrava</s>), the outflow of existence (<s>bhavāsrava</s>), and the outflow of ignorance (<s>avidyāsrava</s>)' — what is their intrinsic nature? That is now commenced:

children.text: vyavidyāḥ sakalāḥ kleśāḥ kāme kāmāsravo mataḥ /
children.translated_text: Excluding ignorance, all defilements in the desire [realm] are considered the outflow of desire;
and excluding torpor and restlessness, those above [are] the outflow of existence, because of [their] sameness. (Abhidh-d 360)

body.text: sarve hyete samānā nivṛtāvyākṛtatvādantarmukhapravṛttatvācca |
body.translated_text: For all these are the same, being of the nature of obscured-indeterminate, and because of their inward-directed operation.

body.text: avidyākhyastu mūlatvādavidyā sārvadhātukī /
body.translated_text: But that called 'ignorance' — because of being the root, ignorance belongs to all realms.

body.text: avidyā khalu saṃsāramūlam | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ |" tathā- "yāḥ kāścana durgatayo 'smilloke paratra ca |
body.translated_text: Ignorance is indeed the root of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). For the <s>Bhagavat</s> has said: 'Conditioned by ignorance are the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations).' Likewise: 'Whatever evil destinies there are in this world and the next,

body.text: sarvāstā avidyāmūlikāḥ " iti |
body.translated_text: all of them have ignorance as their root.'

body.text: tatra tāvatkāmāsravaḥ ekacatvāriṃśad dravyāṇi | rāgapratighamānāḥ pratyekaṃ pañcaprakāratvāt pañcadaśa bhavanti | vicikitsāḥ catasraḥ | dṛṣṭayo dvādaśa | daśa paryavasthānāni | ityetānyekacatvāriṃśad dravyāṇa kāmāsrava ityākhyāyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, the outflow of desire [comprises] forty-one substances. Attachment, aversion, and pride, being each of five kinds, amount to fifteen. Doubts are four. Views are twelve. Envelopments (<s>paryavasthānas</s>) are ten. These forty-one substances are called the outflow of desire.

body.text: bhavāsravaḥ catuṣpañcāśad dravyāṇi | rāgamānau viṃśatiḥ | aṣṭau vicikitsāḥ | caturviṃśati dṛṣṭayo 'vidyāṃ hitvā | dve ca paryavasthāne styānauddhatyākhye, paratantratvāt |
body.translated_text: The outflow of existence [comprises] fifty-four substances. Attachment and pride are twenty. Doubts are eight. Views are twenty-four, excluding ignorance. And two envelopments called torpor (<s>styāna</s>) and restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), because of being dependent [on both form and formless realms].

body.text: avidyāsravaḥ pañcadaśadravyāni | tāni piṇḍenāṣṭottaraṃ dravyaśatamāsravāṇāṃ svabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: The outflow of ignorance [comprises] fifteen substances. In total, the intrinsic nature of the outflows is one hundred and eight substances.

body.text: tathaughayogā dṛgvarjjaṃ tatpṛthaktvantu pāṭavāt // Abhidh-d_361 //
body.translated_text: Likewise for floods (<s>oghas</s>) and yokes (<s>yogas</s>), excluding views — their separation being due to [the views'] acuity. (Abhidh-d 361)

body.text: kāmāsrava eva khalu kāmaughaḥ kāmayogaśca | dṛṣṭī varjayitvā | dṛṣṭayastu paṭutvātpṛthagogheṣu yogeṣu ca vyavasthāpyante | haraṇaśleṣaṇakāryapradhānabhūtā hi dṛṣṭayaḥ | yathā hi sarve kleśāḥ dṛṣṭivarjyāḥ, apaharanti śleṣayanti ca (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 299]

children.text: ) tathaivaikākinyo 'pi dṛṣṭaya iti | tadevaṃ sati kāmaugha ekānnatriṃśat dravyāṇi | rāgapratighamānāḥ pañcadaśa | vicikitsāścatasraḥ | daśa paryavasthānānīti |
children.translated_text: ) so too do views alone. That being so, the flood of desire [comprises] twenty-nine substances: attachment, aversion, and pride are fifteen; doubts are four; envelopments are ten.

body.translated_text: The outflow of desire is indeed the flood of desire and the yoke of desire — excluding views. But views, because of their acuity, are established separately among floods and yokes. For views are pre-eminent in performing the functions of carrying away and binding. Just as all defilements excluding views carry away and bind, (

body.text: bhavaugho 'ṣṭāviṃśatirdravyāṇi | rāgamānā viṃśatiḥ | vicikitsā aṣṭau | dṛṣṭyoghaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśad dravyāṇi | avidyaughaḥ pañcadaśadravyāṇi | evameva yogā draṣṭavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The flood of existence is twenty-eight substances: attachment and pride are twenty; doubts are eight. The flood of views is thirty-six substances. The flood of ignorance is fifteen substances. The yokes should be seen in exactly the same way.

children.text: sāvidyā dve upādāne yathāktau dve tu dṛṅmaye /
children.translated_text: With ignorance, two clingings (<s>upādānas</s>); two as stated are view-based;
the four [have] one [comprising] the last [among them], from [their] dependence on wrong path and the like. (Abhidh-d 362)

body.text: śeṣāstraidhātukāstvantye sātmabhāvapravṛttitaḥ /
body.translated_text: The remaining [clingings] belong to all three realms; the last, because of its operation with respect to [one's] personal existence.

body.text: tatra kāmayoga eva sahāvidyayā kāmopādānaṃ catustriṃśad dravyāṇi | rāgapratighamānāvidyā viṃśatiḥ | vicikitsāścatasraḥ | daśaparyavasthānāni |
body.translated_text: Therein, the yoke of desire together with ignorance is the clinging to desire (<s>kāmopādāna</s>) — thirty-four substances: attachment, aversion, pride, and ignorance are twenty; doubts are four; envelopments are ten.

body.text: bhavayoga eva sahāvidyayā ātmavādopādānam, aṣṭātriṃśad dravyāṇi | rāgamānāvidyāstriṃśat | vicikitsā aṣṭau |
body.translated_text: The yoke of existence together with ignorance is the clinging to a self-doctrine (<s>ātmavādopādāna</s>) — thirty-eight substances: attachment, pride, and ignorance are thirty; doubts are eight.

body.text: dṛṣṭiyogācchīlavrataṃ niṣkṛṣya dṛṣṭyupādānaṃ triśad dravyāṇi | śīlavratopādānaṃ ṣaḍdravyāṇi | kasmātpunaretad dṛṣṭibhyo niṣkṛṣṭam ? 'kumārgādisamāśrayāt |'; mārgapratidvandvabhūtaṃ hyetadubhayapakṣavipralabhbhakaṃ ca | gṛhiṇo 'pi hyanena vipralabdhāḥ anaśanādibhiḥ svargamārgasaṃjñayā | pravrajitā apīṣṭaviṣayavivarjane śuddhipratyāgamanāditi |
body.translated_text: From the yoke of views, extracting adherence to rites and rules, the clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭyupādāna</s>) [comprises] thirty substances. The clinging to rites and rules (<s>śīlavratopādāna</s>) [comprises] six substances. Why then is this extracted separately from the [other] views? 'From [their] dependence on wrong path and the like.' For this [clinging to rites and rules] is the direct adversary of the path and deceives both sides. For householders too are deceived by it through fasting and the like, thinking these are the path to heaven. And renunciants too [are deceived, thinking] that there is purification through abstention from desired objects.

body.text: 'śeṣāstraidhātukāḥ |'; dṛṣṭayo dṛṣṭyupādānam | traidhātukāśca śīlavrataparāmarśāḥ parāmarśopādānam | kāmāsravastu ekadhātukaḥ | bhavāsravastu dvidhātukaḥ | tasmādeva tat 'antyam'; dvayaṃ sārvadhātukameva | 'ātmabhāvapravṛttitaḥ |'; ātmabhāvālambanapravṛttaṃ khalvetaditi |
body.translated_text: 'The remaining [clingings] belong to all three realms.' Views [constitute] the clinging to views. And the adherences to rites and rules belonging to all three realms [constitute] the clinging to adherence. But the outflow of desire belongs to one realm. The outflow of existence belongs to two realms. Therefore, 'the last' two [clingings] belong to all realms. 'Because of its operation with respect to personal existence' — because it operates with personal existence as its object.

body.text: te khalvete anuśayāḥ
body.translated_text: Now, those underlying tendencies —

body.text: saṃyojanādibhiḥ śabdairdarśitāḥ pañcadhā punaḥ // Abhidh-d_363 //
body.translated_text: are shown by terms such as 'fetter' (<s>saṃyojana</s>) and the rest in five ways. (Abhidh-d 363)

body.text: saṃyojanabandhanānuśayopakleśaparyavasthānabhedena pañcadhā bhittvoktāḥ |
body.translated_text: [They are] spoken of as divided fivefold by the distinctions of fetter (<s>saṃyojana</s>), bond (<s>bandhana</s>), underlying tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>), secondary defilement (<s>upakleśa</s>), and envelopment (<s>paryavasthāna</s>).

children.translated_text: Nine fetters are [taught] here, together with jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) and miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>);
from commonality of substance-count, two fetters are [formed from] the views. (Abhidh-d 364)
The remaining [five] underlying tendencies

body.text: nava khalu sayojanāni sūtra uktāni- anunayapratighamānāvidyādṛṣṭiparāmarśavicikitserṣyāmātsaryasaṃyojanāni |
body.translated_text: — nine fetters are indeed stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: the fetters of attachment (<s>anunaya</s>), aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), adherence (<s>parāmarśa</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), and miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>).

body.text: tatrānunayasaṃyojanaṃ traidhātuko rāgaḥ | evamanyāni yathāyogaṃ vaktavyāni | dṛṣṭisaṃyojanaṃ tisro dṛṣṭayaḥ parāmarśasaṃyojanaṃ dve dṛṣṭī |
body.translated_text: Therein, the fetter of attachment is attachment belonging to all three realms. The others likewise should be stated as applicable. The fetter of view [comprises] three views; the fetter of adherence [comprises] two views.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ saṃyojaneṣu tisro dṛṣṭayo dṛṣṭisaṃyojanaṃ pṛthaguktam ? dve punardṛṣṭī parāmarśasaṃyojanaṃ pṛthagiti ? taducyate- 'dravyāmarṣaṇasāmānyād dṛśaḥ saṃyojanadvayam |'; aṣṭādaśadravyāṇi khalu tisro dṛṣṭayaḥ | aṣṭādaśaiva dve parāmarśadṛṣṭī | dvayośca nāmasāmānyam | tasmādetad dvayamekaṃ saṃyojanamuktamiti |
body.translated_text: What then is the reason that among the fetters, three views are called the fetter of view separately, and two views are called the fetter of adherence separately? That is stated: 'From commonality of substance-count, two fetters are [formed from] the views.' Indeed, three views [comprise] eighteen substances. The two adherence-views also [comprise] exactly eighteen. And the two [groupings] share commonality of name. Therefore, this pair is stated as one fetter.

body.text: punarapyanyatra bhagavānsaṃyojanam
body.translated_text: Moreover, elsewhere the <s>Bhagavat</s> [taught] the fetter

children.translated_text: as fivefold and fivefold again —
declaring lower-part (<s>avarabhāgīya</s>) and upper-part (<s>ūrdhvabhāgīya</s>) [fetters]. (Abhidh-d 365)

body.text: ādyantye dve dṛśau kāṅkṣākāmacchando dvireva yaḥ /
body.translated_text: The first and last [of the five lower] are two views; doubt; desire-realm attachment [which appears] twice indeed.

body.text: tatra pañca saṃyojanānyavarabhāgīyāni | tadyathā- satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ śīlavrataparāmarśo vicikitsā kāmacchando vyāpāda iti | ete hi kāmadhātuhitatvādavarabhāgīyā ityucyante | avarā hi kāmadhātūretāni ca tadanuguṇāni | yasmāt
body.translated_text: Therein, five fetters are lower-part [fetters], namely: <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existent body), <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (adherence to rites and rules), <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt), <s>kāmacchanda</s> (desire for sense-pleasures), and <s>vyāpāda</s> (ill-will). For these are conducive to the desire realm and are therefore called lower-part [fetters]. For the desire realm is 'lower,' and these are in conformity with it. Because —

body.text: dvābhyāṃ kāmānatikrāntiḥ punarānayanaṃ tribhiḥ // Abhidh-d_366 //
body.translated_text: by two [fetters], one does not transcend desire; by three, [even after] transcending, one returns. (Abhidh-d 366)

body.text: kāmacchandavyāpādābhyāṃ kāmadhātuṃ nātikrāmati | satkāyadṛṣṭyādibhistribhiratikrānto 'pi punarāvartate dauvārikānucarasādharmyāt |
body.translated_text: By desire and ill-will, one does not transcend the desire realm. By the three beginning with <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, even after transcending, one returns — like a gatekeeper and a retainer.

body.text: anye punarāhuḥ- tribhiḥ sattvāvaratāṃ nātikrāmati pṛthagjanatvam, dvābhyāṃ dhātvavaratāṃ kāmadhātumiti |
body.translated_text: Others, however, say: by three, one does not transcend the lower state of [being] an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>); by two, one does not transcend the lower state of the desire realm.

body.text: yadā khalu strotaāpannasya paryādāya trisaṃyojanaprahāṇe ṣaṭ kleśāḥ prahīṇāḥ kimarthaṃ tisro dṛṣṭīrapahāya trayamevāha satkāyadṛṣṭiṃ śīlavrataparāmarśaṃ vicikitsāṃ ca ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: When indeed, for the <s>Srotaāpanna</s> (stream-enterer), six defilements are abandoned through the exhaustive abandonment of the three fetters — why does [the <s>Bhagavat</s>] mention only three, setting aside the three [other] views: <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>, and <s>vicikitsā</s>? That is stated:

children.translated_text: Because of stating the function of what is to be abandoned by seeing [which operates] through two, one, and [more] views;
although all are to be abandoned by seeing, these three are cited — because of grasping the principal among what is to be abandoned by seeing. (Abhidh-d 367)

body.text: pravartakagrahaṇe khalu pravartyamapi gahītaṃ bhavati pradīpālokavat | tatra satkāyadṛṣṭyā tatpravartitāntagrāhadṛṣṭirgṛhītā | śīlavrataparāmarśeṇa dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ pravartitaḥ | vicikitsayā mithyādṛṣṭiḥ pravartitā | ato hetugrahaṇātkāryagrahaṇaṃ veditavyam |
body.translated_text: For in grasping the instigator, what is instigated is also grasped — like a lamp and its light. Therein, by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, the <s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s> (extreme view) instigated by it is grasped. By <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>, <s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s> (adherence to views) is instigated. By doubt, wrong view is instigated. Therefore, from grasping the cause, the grasping of the effect should be understood.

body.text: athavā trividhā kleśāḥ- ekaprakārāḥ, dviprakārāḥ, catuṣprakārāśca | tatra satkāyadṛṣṭyā ekaprakārā gṛhītāḥ | śīlavrataparāmarśena dviprakārāḥ | vicikitsayā catuṣprakārāḥ gṛhītā bhavantīti ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively, defilements are threefold: of one kind, of two kinds, and of four kinds. Therein, by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, those of one kind are grasped. By <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>, those of two kinds. By doubt, those of four kinds are grasped.

body.text: vayaṃ brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: We say:

children.translated_text: Because of being the cause of all misfortune, because of being the adversary of the path,
and because of being contrary to true assertion — [thus is] the teaching of the three fetters. (Abhidh-d 368)

body.text: satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ khalu sarvānarthamalānāṃ kleśasya ca bhavatrayasya ca mūlam | atastayotkhātayā sarvānarthavṛkṣasyotsādanaṃ bhavati | mārgasya ca sadbhūtasya pratyarthibhūtaḥ kumārgāvalambī śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ | tena prahīṇena sanmārgeṇa mokṣapurapraveśo bhavati | samyagdṛṣṭyādimārgapratipattipratibandhabhūtā ca vicikitsā | (

children.translated_text: Jaini_304

children.text: ) tayā prahīṇayā samyagdṛṣṭisaṃkalpapuraḥsaro mārgo nirvibandhaḥ pravartate | ityaṣṭāśītyanuśayaprahāṇe 'pi sati trayāṇāmeva grahaṇam |
children.translated_text: When it is abandoned, the path led by right view and right intention proceeds without obstruction. Thus, even though eighty-eight <s>anuśayas</s> (latent afflictions) are abandoned, only three are mentioned.

body.translated_text: <s>Satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the perishable collection) is indeed the root of all afflictions, which are the stain of all misfortune, and of the three [modes of] existence. Therefore, by its uprooting, the tree of all misfortune is eradicated. And <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (clinging to rules and rituals), being the adversary of the true path, clings to a false path. When it is abandoned, entry into the city of liberation occurs through the true path. And <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt) is the obstruction to the practice of the path beginning with right view.

body.text: vaibhāṣāḥ punaḥ paśyanti- mokṣāntarāyāḥ trayodbhāvanāḥ | yathā khalu trayo 'ntarāyā mārgagamane bhavantyagantukāmatānyamārgagrahaṇaṃ mārgabahutvasaṃdehācca mārgagamanāpratipattiḥ | evaṃ mokṣagamane trayo 'ntarāyā bhavanti | satkāyadṛṣṭyā mokṣāduttrāsaṃ gatasyāgantukāmatā bhavati | śīlavrataparāmarśenānyamārgagrahaṇāt mārgavibhrāntiḥ | vicikitsā mārgasaṃśaye sati mārgāpratipattirityeṣāṃ mokṣagamanāntarāyāṇāṃ prahāṇaṃ strotaāpannasya dyotayadbhagavānkleśatrayasyaiva grahaṇamakārṣīditi ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>, however, hold this view: three [afflictions] are to be enumerated as obstacles to liberation. Just as there are three obstacles in traveling a road — unwillingness to go, taking a wrong road, and failure to proceed on the road due to doubt about which of many roads [to take] — similarly, there are three obstacles in the journey to liberation. Through <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, having become terrified of liberation, one becomes unwilling to go. Through <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>, by taking a wrong path, there is confusion about the path. <s>Vicikitsā</s> is failure to proceed on the path when there is doubt about the path. Thus, illuminating the abandonment of these obstacles to the journey to liberation for the stream-enterer, the Blessed One mentioned only these three afflictions.

body.text: yathā ca pañcavidhamavarabhāgīyaṃ saṃyojanamuktavāṃstathā pañcordhvabhāgīyānisaṃyojanānyākhyātavān sūtre |
body.translated_text: Just as he stated the fivefold lower-realm fetters, so too the Blessed One declared the five upper-realm fetters in the <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: dvau rūpārūpajau rāgau mānamohoddhavāstrayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Two [fetters of] passion born of the form and formless [realms], and three arising from conceit, delusion, and restlessness. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: pañca khalurdhvabhāgīyāni saṃyojanāni | tadyathā- rūparāgaḥ, ārūpyarāgaḥ, auddhatyam, māno 'vidyā ca | eṣāmaprahīṇānāṃ ūrdhvadhātudvayaṃ nātikrāmanti sattvāḥ | samāptaḥ saṃyojanādhikāraḥ |
body.translated_text: There are five upper-realm fetters. Namely: <s>rūparāga</s> (passion for the form realm), <s>ārūpyarāga</s> (passion for the formless realm), <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness), <s>māna</s> (conceit), and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). When these are not abandoned, beings do not transcend the two upper realms. The section on fetters is concluded.

body.text: bandhanānīdānīmucyante | trīṇi bandhanāni | rāgo bandhanaṃ dveṣo moho (

children.translated_text: Jaini_305

children.text: ) bandhanam | ebhistraidhātukāḥ sattvāḥ saṃsāracārake baddhāḥ yathāyogam | kasmātpunaretāni bandhanānītyuktāni ? taducyate-
children.translated_text: is a bond. By these, beings of the three realms are bound in the prison of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), each according to its application. Why then are these called bonds? That is stated:

body.translated_text: Now bonds (<s>bandhana</s>) are stated. There are three bonds: passion (<s>rāga</s>) is a bond, aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) is a bond, delusion (<s>moha</s>)

body.text: trivedanānuśāyitvād dṛḍhatvādbandhanatrayam // Abhidh-d_369 //
body.translated_text: The three bonds are so called because of underlying the three feelings and because of firmness. (Abhidh-d 369)

body.text: trivedanāvaśātkhalu bandhanatrayamuktam | tatra sukhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ rāgo 'nuśerate | duḥkhāyāṃ dveṣaḥ | aduḥkhāsukhāyāṃ mohaḥ | ete ca trayo mūlakleśāḥ ṣaḍvijñānabhaumāḥ pañcaprakārāḥ | tasmādete dṛḍhatvād bandhanaśabdenoktāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The three bonds are stated on account of the three feelings. Therein, passion underlies pleasant feeling; aversion underlies painful feeling; delusion underlies neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. And these three root afflictions pertain to the six classes of consciousness and are of five kinds. Therefore, because of their firmness, they are called by the term 'bonds.'

body.text: punaranye bhagavatā sūtre-
body.translated_text: Furthermore, others [are stated] by the Blessed One in the <s>sūtra</s> —

children.translated_text: Because they tie together two sides, four knots are proclaimed: (Abhidh-d 370)
<s>abhidhyā</s> (covetousness), likewise aversion, and the two [kinds of] clinging (<s>parāmarśa</s>).

body.text: tatra gṛhī abhidhyayā viṣayeṣu grathitastadvyāghātakartṛṣu vivādamārabhamāno dveṣeṇānubadhyate | pravrajitaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśagrathitastadapavādaśravaṇādidameva satyamiti satyābhiniveśaparāmarśena dṛṣṭiparāmarśākhyena badhyate | iti catvāro bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, a householder, knotted by covetousness to sense objects, and beginning to quarrel with those who obstruct [his enjoyment], is bound by aversion. A renunciant, knotted by <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (clinging to rules and rituals), upon hearing the repudiation of that [practice], is bound by <s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s> (clinging to views), called the clinging to 'this alone is the truth' (<s>satyābhiniveśaparāmarśa</s>). Thus there are four.

body.text: uktāḥ kleśāḥ |
body.translated_text: The afflictions have been stated.

children.translated_text: The subsidiary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>) should be known as hostility and the rest, as enumerated. (Abhidh-d 371)

children.text: sarve vā caitasāḥ kliṣṭāḥ saṃskāraskandhasaṃjñitāḥ // Abhidh-d_371 //
children.translated_text: Or, all defiled mental factors designated as belonging to the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of formations).

body.text: ye tāvatkhalu kleśā upakleśā api te cittopakleśanāt | iha tu paryavasthānakleśamalasaṃgṛhītāḥ kṣudrakavastukoddiṣṭā veditavyāḥ | ye 'pi cānye caitasikāḥ saṃskāraskandhasaṃgṛhītāḥ te 'pyupakleśā ityākhyāyante ||
body.translated_text: Those afflictions that are also subsidiary afflictions — they are so because they defile the mind. But here, those included among the envelopment-affliction-stains and enumerated in the <s>Kṣudrakavastu</s> should be understood. And whatever other mental factors are included in the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s>, they too are called subsidiary afflictions.

body.text: ke punaste kleśamalāḥ kāni vā paryavasthānāni ? tatra tāvat-
body.translated_text: Now, what are those defilement-stains and what are the envelopments? As for those —

body.text: mūlakleśamalāstvanye ṣaḍupakleśasaṃjñitāḥ /
body.translated_text: The stains of the root afflictions are six others, designated as subsidiary afflictions. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: ta ime ucyante-
body.translated_text: These are stated:

body.text: śāṭhyopanāhapradāśamāyāmadaviheṭhanāḥ // Abhidh-d_372 //
body.translated_text: Deceit (<s>śāṭhya</s>), rancor (<s>upanāha</s>), malice (<s>pradāśa</s>), guile (<s>māyā</s>), intoxication (<s>mada</s>), and cruelty (<s>viheṭhanā</s>). (Abhidh-d 372)

body.text: tatra cittakauṭilyaṃ śāṭhyaṃ cittasyānṛjutā vakrībhāvaḥ | upanāhaḥ pratighaniṣyando vairānubandhakṛdrandhrāvadhānatā | santoṣyamānasyāpyadharmadṛḍhagrāhitā pradāśaḥ | parābhisandhānāya mithyopadarśanakārī paravañcanāmāyā | cittasmayo madaḥ | saturūpakulabalabhogayauvanārogyaparijanasaṃpattisaṃrāgajaḥ pramādāspadaṃ vividhendriyavibhramotpādajanakaḥ | sattvavyāpādo vihiṃsā viheṭhanetyarthāntaram | uktāḥ ṣaṭ kleśamalāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, crookedness of mind is <s>śāṭhya</s> (deceit) — the non-straightness of mind, its becoming crooked. <s>Upanāha</s> (rancor) is the outflow of hostility (<s>pratigha</s>) — the watching for an opening with the making of enmity. <s>Pradāśa</s> (malice) is the rigid grasping of wrong even when being appeased. <s>Māyā</s> (guile) is the deception of others — making false appearances for the purpose of deceiving others. <s>Mada</s> (intoxication) is mental elation — born from attachment to prosperity in form, family, strength, wealth, youth, health, and retinue; it is the ground of heedlessness and the generator of various disturbances of the faculties. <s>Vihiṃsā</s> (cruelty) is malicious intent toward beings; <s>viheṭhanā</s> (harassment) is a synonym. The six defilement-stains have been stated.

body.text: daśa paryavasthānānyucyante |
body.translated_text: The ten envelopments (<s>paryavasthāna</s>) are stated.

children.translated_text: Concealment (<s>mrakṣa</s>), jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>), torpor (<s>styāna</s>), drowsiness (<s>middha</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), (Abhidh-d 373)

children.text: mātsaryaṃ kukṛtatvaṃ ca daśadhā paryavasthitiḥ // Abhidh-d_373 //
children.translated_text: avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>), and regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) — tenfold is the envelopment.

body.text: ete hyanubandhādārḍhyānnānuśayāḥ | na hyeṣāmanubandhadārḍhyamastyanuśayāstu dṛḍhānubandhāḥ | tasmādetāni kālāntaramātraṃ cittaparyavasthāpanāt paryavasthānānītyucyante |
body.translated_text: These are not <s>anuśayas</s> (latent afflictions), because they do not possess the firmness of being deep-rooted — for they do not have the firmness of being deep-rooted, whereas <s>anuśayas</s> are firmly deep-rooted. Therefore, these are called <s>paryavasthānas</s> (envelopments) because they envelop the mind for merely a period of time.

body.text: avadyaṃ chādayataḥ cittāpalepo mrakṣaḥ, cittaṃ mrakṣayatīti mrakṣaḥ | parasampattyamarṣaṇamīrṣyā | akāryaṃ kurvataḥ svātmānamavekṣyālajjanāhrīḥ | (

children.translated_text: Jaini_309

children.text: ) paramapekṣyālajjanānapatrāpyam | kāyākarmaṇyatā styānaṃ tandrīparyāyavacanam | kāyacittākarmaṇyatā middhaṃ cittābhisaṃkṣepaḥ svapnākhyaḥ, sa tu kliṣṭa eva paryavasthānam | cittāvyupaśāntirauddhatyam | parāpakāranimittodbhavo 'parityāgayogena caṇḍībhāvaḥ krodhaḥ | svavastunyāgraho mātsaryam, matto mā saredetaditi niruktiḥ | kukṛtabhāvaḥ kaukṛtyam | ityenāni daśa paryavasthānāni ||
children.translated_text: <s>Anapatrāpya</s> (lack of moral dread) is the lack of embarrassment having regard for others. <s>Styāna</s> (torpor) is the unfitness for work of the body, a synonym for languor. <s>Middha</s> (drowsiness) is the unfitness for work of body and mind — the contraction of mind called sleep; it, moreover, is only defiled as an envelopment. <s>Auddhatya</s> (restlessness) is the non-tranquility of mind. <s>Krodha</s> (anger) is the state of fierceness with non-relinquishment, arising from a cause of harm to others. <s>Mātsarya</s> (avarice) is the grasping of one's own possessions — its etymology is 'let not another take from me' (<s>matto mā saret</s>). <s>Kaukṛtya</s> (regret) is the state of having done wrongly. These are the ten envelopments.

body.translated_text: The mental adhesion of one who conceals a fault is <s>mrakṣa</s> (concealment) — it 'smears' (<s>mrakṣayati</s>) the mind, hence <s>mrakṣa</s>. <s>Īrṣyā</s> (jealousy) is intolerance of another's prosperity. <s>Āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness) is the lack of embarrassment, having examined oneself, when doing what should not be done.

body.text: athaiṣāmupakleśamalaparyavasthānānāṃ kaḥ kasya rāgādermūlakleśasya niṣyandaḥ ? tadidamārabhyate ||
body.translated_text: Now, which of these subsidiary affliction-stains and envelopments is the outflow of which root affliction — passion and the rest? That is now commenced.

body.text: ebhyo 'nunayaniṣyandā āhrīkyauddhatatādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Shamelessness, restlessness, and the rest are outflows of attachment among these. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: ime khalūpakleśāḥ rāganiṣyandāḥ | yaduta- ahrīkyauddhatyamadamātsaryakuhanālapanānaimittikatānaiṣpeśikatā lābhena lābhasya niścikīrṣatā pāpecchatā mahecchatecchasvitā kāmajñātijanapadavitarkapāpamitratādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: These subsidiary afflictions are outflows of passion (<s>rāga</s>). Namely: shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), intoxication (<s>mada</s>), avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>), <s>kuhanā</s> (hypocrisy), <s>lapanā</s> (flattery), <s>naimittikatā</s> (hinting), <s>naiṣpeṣikatā</s> (belittling), the desire to gain gain by gain, evil desire (<s>pāpecchatā</s>), great desire (<s>mahecchatā</s>), desire-longing, thoughts of relatives, thoughts of one's country, association with bad friends, and the like.

body.text: tatrāhrīkyānapatrāpyamadā vyākhyātalakṣaṇāḥ | lābhasatkārayaśolobhādabhūtaguṇadarśanārthamīryāpathavikalpakṛccaittaviśeṣaḥ kuhanā | lābhādyarthameva guṇapriyālapanakṛllapanā | upakaraṇārthitvanimittadarśanakṛccaittaviśeṣo naimittakatā | paraguṇavaddoṣavacananiṣpeṣaṇakṛdeva caitasiko naiṣpeṣikatā | labdhalābhakhyāpanenānyalābhaniścakīrṣaṇatā lābhena lābhasya niścikīrṣatā | parairabhūtaguṇasambhāvanecchā pāpecchatā | lābhasatkāraparivāraprārthanā mahecchatā |
body.translated_text: Therein, shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>), and intoxication (<s>mada</s>) have already-explained characteristics. <s>Kuhanā</s> (hypocrisy) is a special mental state that contrives deportment-modification for the purpose of displaying non-existent qualities, out of greed for gain, honor, and fame. <s>Lapanā</s> (flattery) is the contriving of charming speech praising qualities, also for the sake of gain and the rest. <s>Naimittikatā</s> (hinting) is a special mental state that contrives the display of signs indicating desire for requisites. <s>Naiṣpeṣikatā</s> (belittling) is a mental factor that contrives the crushing speech of attributing faults to one who possesses good qualities. The desire to gain gain by gain is the desire to procure another's gain by publicizing one's own gain. <s>Pāpecchatā</s> (evil desire) is the wish to be esteemed by others for non-existent qualities. <s>Mahecchatā</s> (great desire) is the craving for gain, honor, and retinue.

body.text: lobhātparairbhūtaguṇasambhāvanecchā icchasvitā | kāmarāgapratisaṃyukto vitarkaḥ kāmavitarkaḥ | jñātisnehaparītasya tadāvāhavivāhakṛṣivaṇigrājasevādīnāṃ gṛhasandhāraṇamupajīvanopāyānāṃ rājataskarādibhayapraśamanopāyānāṃ ca vitarkāṇāṃ vitarkaḥ jñātivitarkaḥ | paryāptajīvitopakaraṇāparituṣṭasya lokamitratā, chandarāgāpahṛtacetasasteṣāṃ janapadānāṃ bhūmiramaṇīyatāsubhikṣakṣematāpracuragorasekṣuvikāragodhūmaśālyādīnāṃ vitarkaṇājjanapadavitarkaḥ śīladṛṣṭyācāravipannānāṃ ratikṛtā saṃsevā pāpamitratā |
body.translated_text: <s>Icchasvitā</s> (desire-longing) is the wish, out of greed, to be esteemed by others for existent qualities. <s>Kāmavitarka</s> (thought of sensual desire) is thought conjoined with sensual passion. <s>Jñātivitarka</s> (thought of relatives) is the thought of one pervaded by affection for relatives — thoughts about their marriage arrangements, farming, trade, royal service, and other means of household maintenance, and means of averting dangers from kings, thieves, and the like. <s>Janapadavitarka</s> (thought of one's country) is the thought, of one dissatisfied despite having sufficient livelihood-requisites — due to friendship with the world, with the mind carried away by desire and passion — thinking about those countries' beautiful terrain, prosperity, safety, abundance of dairy products, sugarcane products, wheat, rice, and the like. <s>Pāpamitratā</s> (association with bad friends) is the companionship, made for delight, with those who are deficient in morality, views, and conduct.

body.text: mrakṣānapatrapāstyānamiddhādyā mohasaṃbhavāḥ // Abhidh-d_374 //
body.translated_text: Concealment (<s>mrakṣa</s>), lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>), torpor (<s>styāna</s>), drowsiness (<s>middha</s>), and the rest arise from delusion. (Abhidh-d 374)

body.text: tatra 'mrakṣānapatrapāstyānamiddhāḥ'; | 'ādi'grahaṇāllayaḥ, amanasikārodanādaratā, daurvacasyaṃ tandrī bhaktāsamatetyevamādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'concealment, lack of moral dread, torpor, drowsiness'; by the word 'and the rest' — depression (<s>laya</s>), inattention (<s>amanasikāra</s>), indifference (<s>anādaratā</s>), stubbornness (<s>daurvacasya</s>), languor (<s>tandrī</s>), imbalance in food (<s>bhaktāsamatā</s>), and the like.

body.text: tatra layonāma doṣaguṇatyāgārjanaṃ prati ātmaparibhavajaścittasaṃkocaḥ | kuśalāsamanvāhāra audāsīnyayogeṇāmanasikāraḥ | guṇeṣu guṇavatsu cābahumānavṛttiranādaratā | (

children.translated_text: Jaini_311

children.text: ) dharmānuśāstṛṣu sāsūyitapratimantrakṛddaurvacasyam | jṛmbhikodgamādakṣivartmastambhanidrāspadaḥ caittaviśeṣaḥ styānākhyā tandrī | kuśalapakṣānukūlabhojanasamatāprativedhaścetaso bhaktāsamatā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Daurvacasya</s> (stubbornness) is [the attitude] of making envious counter-replies toward instructors in the <s>Dharma</s>. <s>Tandrī</s> (languor) is a special mental state called torpor (<s>styāna</s>), which causes yawning, eyelid-heaviness, and is the basis of sleep. <s>Bhaktāsamatā</s> (imbalance in food) is the non-penetration of the mind by food favorable to the wholesome side, that is, the imbalance of mind regarding food.

body.translated_text: Therein, <s>laya</s> (depression) is the contraction of mind born from self-deprecation with respect to abandoning faults and cultivating virtues. <s>Amanasikāra</s> (inattention) is the non-application [of mind] through the practice of indifference. <s>Anādaratā</s> (indifference) is the attitude of not respecting virtues and those who possess virtues.

body.text: kaukṛtyaṃ vicikitsotthaṃ krodhādyā dveṣasambhavāḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Kaukṛtya</s> (regret) arises from doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>); anger (<s>krodha</s>) and the rest arise from aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>). (Abhidh-d)

body.text: kaukṛtyaṃ khalu yathoktalakṣaṇaṃ vicikitsāsamutthitam | krodhādyā dveṣaniṣyandāḥ | 'ādi'śabdādīrṣyākṣāntyupanāhapradāśasaṃrambhādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Kaukṛtya</s> with the characteristics as stated arises from doubt. Anger and the rest are outflows of aversion. By the word 'and the rest' — jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), impatience (<s>akṣānti</s>), rancor (<s>upanāha</s>), malice (<s>pradāśa</s>), hostility (<s>saṃrambha</s>), and the like.

body.text: tatrerṣyā pūrvoktalakṣaṇā | sahyāsahiṣṇutākṣāntiḥ | randhrāvadhānānivṛttirupanāhaḥ | saṃtoṣamānasyāpyadṛḍhagrāhitā pradāśaḥ | parānvimardiṣataḥ pāṇipādauṣṭhakapolaśarīrakampayonirbhrāntamanasaḥ kṣobhaḥ saṃrambhaḥ | nimittamātreṇa sātatyaviheṭhanakṛcchṛṅgī | nistanato 'bhīkṣṇavivādakṛtyaṃ stambhanatā | kāmyānviṣayānanusmarato rativiparītamanasaḥ pravṛttiraratiḥ | cittāpaiśalyamanārjavatā | vyāpādārtha prayukto vitarko vyāpādavitarkaḥ | vihiṃsāsaṃprayukto vitarkaḥ vihiṃsāvitarkaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>īrṣyā</s> (jealousy) has the previously stated characteristics. <s>Akṣānti</s> (impatience) is the inability to endure. <s>Upanāha</s> (rancor) is the non-cessation of watching for an opening. <s>Pradāśa</s> (malice) is the rigid grasping [of wrong] even when one's contentment is being addressed. <s>Saṃrambha</s> (hostility) is the agitation — the fierceness of one who wishes to crush others, with trembling of hands, feet, lips, cheeks, and body, and a bewildered mind. <s>Śṛṅgī</s> is one who, upon the slightest provocation, continuously harasses. <s>Stambhanatā</s> is obstinacy — the conduct of frequent quarreling by groaning. <s>Arati</s> (discontent) is the activity of a mind opposite to delight, recollecting desired objects. <s>Anārjavatā</s> (crookedness) is the lack of mental straightness. <s>Vyāpādavitarka</s> (thought of malice) is thought directed at the purpose of harm. <s>Vihiṃsāvitarka</s> (thought of cruelty) is thought conjoined with cruelty.

body.text: pramādastambhamārdva(?)kṣya māyāśāṭhyavijṛmbhikāḥ // Abhidh-d_375 //
body.translated_text: Heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>), stubbornness (<s>stambha</s>), softness(?) (<s>mārdvakṣya</s>), guile (<s>māyā</s>), deceit (<s>śāṭhya</s>), yawning (<s>vijṛmbhikā</s>), (Abhidh-d 375)

body.text: kāyaduṣṭhūlatādyāśca jñeyā vyāmiśrasambhavāḥ /
body.translated_text: physical unwieldiness (<s>kāyaduṣṭhūlatā</s>) and the rest — these should be known as arising from a mixture [of root afflictions].

body.text: tatra doṣapravaṇasya guṇānabhisaṃmukhyaṃ pramādaḥ | pūjārheṣvasaṃnatiḥ stambhaḥ | parānurodhātpāpānuvṛttikṛccaitto mārdvakṣyam(?) | parābhisandhānāya mithyopadarśanakṛccaitto māyā | cittakauṭilyaṃ śāṭhyam | kleśasamutthitaḥ kāyasyānamanavinamanakṛccaitto vijambhikā | kleśakṛtā vividhālambanasaṃjñā nānātvasaṃjñāḥ | ativīryabhaktāsamatānirjātakāyavaiṣamyābādhaḥ kāyadauṣṭhulyam | kalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ guṇeṣvananuśikṣā asabhāgānuvartanatā | kleśasamutthā parasampadvitarkaṇā, parodayapratisaṃyukto vitarkaḥ | ityevamādayo vyāmiśrasamutthitā draṣṭavyāḥ |
