body.translated_text: Therein, <s>pramāda</s> (heedlessness) is the non-turning toward virtues of one inclined toward faults. <s>Stambha</s> (stubbornness) is the failure to bow before those worthy of respect. <s>Mārdvakṣya</s> (?) is a mental factor that follows along in wrongdoing out of compliance with others. <s>Māyā</s> (guile) is a mental factor that contrives false appearances for the purpose of deceiving others. <s>Śāṭhya</s> (deceit) is crookedness of mind. <s>Vijṛmbhikā</s> (yawning) is a mental factor, arisen from afflictions, that causes the bending and stretching of the body. <s>Nānātvasaṃjñā</s> (perceptions of diversity) are perceptions of various objects arisen from afflictions. <s>Kāyadauṣṭhulya</s> (physical unwieldiness) is the bodily affliction-distress born from excessive effort, imbalance in food. Failure to learn the virtues of good friends, following the unlike — is <s>asabhāgānuvartanatā</s>. Thought, arisen from afflictions, reflecting on others' prosperity — thought connected with others' fortune — is also [mixed]. Thus these and others should be seen as arising from a mixture.

body.text: pradāśo dṛkparāmarśaniṣyandaḥ śaṭhatā dṛśaḥ // Abhidh-d_376 //
body.translated_text: <s>Pradāśa</s> (malice) is an outflow of <s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s> (clinging to views); <s>śāṭhya</s> (deceit) is [an outflow] of views. (Abhidh-d 376)

body.text: pūrvoktalakṣaṇaḥ pradāśaḥ parāmarśaniṣyandaḥ | śāṭhyaṃ dṛṣṭisamutthitamiti ||
body.translated_text: <s>Pradāśa</s> with the previously stated characteristics is an outflow of <s>parāmarśa</s> (clinging). <s>Śāṭhya</s> (deceit) arises from views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>).

body.text: atha kaḥ kleśaḥ kayā vedanayā saṃprayujyate ? tadidamārabhyate-
body.translated_text: Now, which affliction is associated with which feeling? That is now commenced:

body.text: saumanasyena rāgasya saṃprayogaḥ sukhena ca /
body.translated_text: Passion is associated with mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>) and with pleasure (<s>sukha</s>). (Abhidh-d 377)

body.text: rāgaḥ khalu sukhasaumanasyābhyāṃ saṃprayuktaḥ |
body.translated_text: Passion (<s>rāga</s>) is indeed associated with pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>).

body.text: dveṣasya daurmanasyena duḥkhena ca nigadyate // Abhidh-d_377 //
body.translated_text: The association of aversion with mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) and with suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) is stated. (Abhidh-d 377)

body.text: saṃyoga iti vartate | pratighaḥ khalu duḥkhadaurmanasyābhyāṃ saṃprayuktaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Association' is supplied [from the previous verse]. <s>Pratigha</s> (aversion) is indeed associated with suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) and mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>).

children.translated_text: Of delusion, with all [five feelings] —

body.text: mohasya tu pañcabhirapīndriyaiḥ saṃprayogaḥ |
body.translated_text: Delusion (<s>moha</s>) has association with all five faculties [of feeling].

body.text: vittibhyāṃ caitasībhyāmasaddṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text: And with the two mental feelings, [the case of] wrong view is dissimilar. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: mithyādṛṣṭirhi daurmanasyasaumanasyābhyāṃ saṃprayujyate, pāpakarmaṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇāṃ ca yathākramam |
body.translated_text: <s>Mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view) is indeed associated with mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) and mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>) — with respect to sinful actions and meritorious actions, respectively.

children.translated_text: And doubt (<s>kāṅkṣā</s>) with mental displeasure —

body.text: sāṃśayito hi niścayākāṅkṣī daurmanasyena saṃbadhyate |
body.translated_text: For one who doubts and craves certainty is bound by mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>).

body.text: śeṣāṇāṃ sumanastayā // Abhidh-d_378 //
body.translated_text: Of the remaining [afflictions], with mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>). (Abhidh-d 378)

body.text: śeṣāstvanuśayāḥ- catasro dṛṣṭayaḥ, mānaśca | harṣākāravṛttitvātsaumanasyena saṃprayuktāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The remaining latent tendencies are the four [other] views and pride. Because they operate in the mode of delight, they are associated with mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>).

children.translated_text: But with equanimity, [the association is] of all [latent tendencies]. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: sarve 'pyaviśeṣeṇānuśayā upekṣayā saṃprayujyante | pravāhacchedakāle khalu kleśānāmavaśyamupekṣā saṃmukhībhavati |
body.translated_text: All latent tendencies without distinction are associated with equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). For at the time of cutting the stream of afflictions, equanimity necessarily comes face-to-face [with them].

body.text: kāmāptānāmayaṃ vidhiḥ /
body.translated_text: This is the rule for those belonging to the desire realm. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: kāmāvacarāṇāṃ khalvanuśayānāmeṣa vidhiḥ draṣṭavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: This rule is to be viewed for the latent tendencies of the desire realm.

body.text: ito 'nyadhātujānāṃ tu pratibhūmyantaraṃ svakaiḥ // Abhidh-d_379 //
body.translated_text: But for those born in other realms, [the association is] with their own [feelings], differing by ground. (Abhidh-d 379)

body.text: yasyāṃ yasyāṃ bhūmau yāvantīndriyāṇi santi tatrāpi cāturvijñānakāyikāścāturvijñānakāyikairmanobhūmikā manobhūmikaireva yathāsaṃbhavam ||
body.translated_text: In whatever ground whatever faculties exist — there too, those belonging to the four consciousness-groups [are associated] with those of the four consciousness-groups, and those of the mental ground with those of the mental ground alone, according to possibility.

body.text: uktāḥ kleśānāmindriyasaṃprayogaḥ | upakleśānāmucyate-
body.translated_text: The association of afflictions with faculties has been stated. That of the secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśas</s>) is now stated:

children.translated_text: Envy with mental displeasure, and likewise remorse, anger, (Abhidh-d 380)
irritability, enmity, and likewise harmfulness.

body.text: daurmanasyena khalvīrṣyākaukṛtyakrodhapradāśopanāhavihiṃsāḥ saṃprayujyante ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), remorse (<s>kaukṛtya</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), irritability (<s>pradāśa</s>), enmity (<s>upanāha</s>), and harmfulness (<s>vihiṃsā</s>) are associated with mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>).

body.text: mātsaryaṃ daurmanasyena saumanasyena kasyacit /
body.translated_text: Miserliness [is associated] with mental displeasure, [but] for some, with mental pleasure. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: prārthyamāno hyaprayacchan parasya jahrīyamāno durmanāyate | kecitpunaḥ vyācakṣate- saumanasyena saṃprayujyate lobhānvayatvena harṣākāravartitvāt |
body.translated_text: For one who, being asked, does not give to another and feels ashamed — he feels mental displeasure. But some explain: it is associated with mental pleasure, because of following from greed and operating in the mode of delight.

body.text: dvābhyāṃ māyā tathā śāṭhyaṃ mrakṣo middhaṃ tathaiva ca // Abhidh-d_381 //
body.translated_text: Deceit, guile, and concealment, as well as torpor — with both. (Abhidh-d 381)

body.text: daurmanasyasaumanasyābhyāṃ māyāśāṭhyamiddhāni saṃprayujyante | kadāciddhi sumanāḥ paraṃ vañcayate | kadāciddurmanāḥ | evaṃ yāvatsvapīti ||
body.translated_text: Deceit (<s>māyā</s>), guile (<s>śāṭhya</s>), and torpor (<s>middha</s>) are associated with both mental displeasure and mental pleasure. For sometimes one deceives another while happy, and sometimes while unhappy. Similarly up to: one sleeps [in either state].

body.text: madastu sumanaḥskandhasukhābhyāṃ saṃprayujyate /
body.translated_text: But intoxication (<s>mada</s>) is associated with the aggregate of mental pleasure and bodily pleasure. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: tṛtīye dhyāne sukhenādhastātsaumanasyenordhvaṃ copekṣayā | 'tu'śabdasya viśeṣaṇatvādayaṃ viśeṣo labhyate |
body.translated_text: In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, with bodily pleasure (<s>sukha</s>); below that, with mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>); and above, with equanimity. Because the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) has a specifying function, this distinction is obtained.

body.text: āhrīkyamanapatrāpyaṃ styānauddhatye ca pañcabhiḥ // Abhidh-d_382 //
body.translated_text: Shamelessness, recklessness, and torpor and restlessness — with all five. (Abhidh-d 382)

body.text: pañcabhirapīndriyaiḥ āhrīkyānapatrāpyastyānauddhatyāni saṃprayujyante | eṣāṃ caturṇāṃ paryavasthānānāmakuśalamahābhūmikatvāt kleśamahābhaumikatvācca ||
body.translated_text: Shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), recklessness (<s>anapatrāpya</s>), torpor (<s>styāna</s>), and restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>) are associated with all five faculties [of feeling]. Because these four secondary afflictions are of the nature of unwholesome great-ground [factors] (<s>akuśalamahābhūmika</s>) and affliction-great-ground [factors] (<s>kleśamahābhaumika</s>).

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | ka eṣāṃ kiṃ prahātavyaḥ ? yāni tāvaddaśa paryavasthānāni tebhyaḥ-
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: Which of these is to be abandoned by what? Taking first the ten secondary afflictions (<s>paryavasthānas</s>) —

body.text: āhrīkyamanapatrāpyaṃ styānamiddhaṃ tathoddhavaḥ // Abhidh-d_383 //
body.translated_text: Shamelessness, recklessness, torpor, and likewise restlessness — (Abhidh-d 383)

body.text: ..........abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau pañcamādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: ..........End of the third quarter of the fifth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, the commentary called <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>.

body.text: ..........pañcamodhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: ..........The fifth chapter is complete.

body.text: ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: [Beginning of] the sixth chapter.

body.text:
prathamaḥ pādaḥ.....
..............rvaudārikam | atastutpūrvam | tato vedanāsmṛtyupasthānaṃ dvābhyāṃ sthūlataraṃ vedanāskandhavat | tataḥ cittasmṛtyupasthānaṃ rūpādiprativijñaptisvābhāvyātsulakṣam | dharmāstu saṃjñācetanādyā saṃprayuktāḥ, prāptyādayaḥ viprayuktāḥ, saṃskṛtāśca paramasūkṣmāstasmādante dharmasmṛtyupasthānam | ata evotpattikramopi tathaiva |
body.translated_text:
First quarter.....
..............is gross. Therefore that is first. Then the foundation of mindfulness on feelings — [it is] coarser than two [others], like the feeling-aggregate. Then the foundation of mindfulness on mind — because of being easily discernible through the cognition contrasting with form and the rest. But dharmas — the associated ones such as perception, volition, and the rest; the disjoined ones such as acquisition and the rest; and the conditioned ones — are supremely subtle; therefore the foundation of mindfulness on dharmas comes last. For this very reason, the order of arising is also the same.

body.text: prāyeṇa hi sattvāḥ rūpādyupabhogaratatvāt mokṣavimukhā bhavanti vedanābhinanditvāt, sā cābhinandanā cittasyādāntatvāt | taccādāntatvaṃ rāgādibhiḥ | śraddhādibhiśca dāntatvaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: For beings, generally, being attached to the enjoyment of form and the rest, are turned away from liberation; because of delighting in feeling — and that delight is due to the untamed mind; and that untamedness is due to attachment and the rest. By faith and the rest, tamedness comes about.

body.text: catuṣṭvamapi caturviparyāsapratipakṣatvāt | aśucau śucisaṃjñāviparyāsapratipakṣo hi kāyaparīkṣā | duḥkhe sukhasaṃjñāviparyāsapratipakṣo vedanāparīkṣā | anitye nityasaṃjñāviparyāsapratipakṣaścittaparīkṣā, cittasya laghuparivartitvāt | anātmanyātmasaṃjñāviparyāsapratipakṣo dharmaparīkṣā | dharmasmṛtyupasthānasya vaicitryādekātmasaṃjñāviparyāso nivartate | 'ādi'śabdāccaturāhārapañcaskandhapratipakṣatvādyathāyogam ||
body.translated_text: The fourfoldness is also because of being the antidote to the four perversions (<s>viparyāsas</s>). For the examination of the body is the antidote to the perversion of [perceiving] the pure in the impure. The examination of feeling is the antidote to the perversion of [perceiving] pleasure in suffering. The examination of mind is the antidote to the perversion of [perceiving] permanence in the impermanent — because the mind changes quickly. The examination of dharmas is the antidote to the perversion of [perceiving] self in what is not-self. Because of the diversity of the foundation of mindfulness on dharmas, the single perversion of self-perception is turned back. By the word 'and so forth' — [the fourfoldness is] also because of being the antidote to the four nutriments and the five aggregates, according to applicability.

body.text: sa tadānīṃ yogācāraḥ
body.translated_text: At that time, the yogic practitioner,

body.text: samastālambināntyena tānvettyadhruvatādibhiḥ /
body.translated_text: by the last [foundation] which has a combined object, knows them through impermanence and the rest. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: sambhinnālambanaṃ hi dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ tricatuṣpañcaskandhālambanatvāt | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 317)

children.text: ) pañcaskandhālambanameva tu sāmānyālambanamiti nirdiśyate | tena tu catvāryapi smṛtyupasthānānyabhisamasyānityato duḥkhataḥ śūnyato 'nātmataśceti caturbhirākāraiḥ pratyavekṣate | tataḥ punaryogī kāyaṃ paramāṇusaṃghātakṣaṇasantānabhedena prabhidya paramāṇuśaḥ kṣaṇaśaśca nirīkṣate | kalalādīnāṃ vā bījādyaśucyaṅgāni pṛthaṅmiśrībhūtāni ca yogī rūpāṇi nimitteṣu paśyati | tadūrdhvaṃ tasyānityatvādibhiḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇena yathāyogaṃ sarvadharmakajātīyatvādhimokṣe satyahaṃkāramamakāraviṣkambhanaprahāṇaṃ bhavati | tanprahāṇādrāgādayopi doṣāḥ śrutacintāmayābhyāṃ jñānābhyāṃ viṣkambhyante |
children.translated_text: But that which has five aggregates as its object is indicated as [the foundation] with a general object (<s>sāmānyālambana</s>). By that, he examines all four foundations of mindfulness through the four aspects: as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, and as not-self. Thereafter, the yogin further analyzes the body by dividing it into atoms, assemblages of atoms, and momentary continua, and examines it atom by atom and moment by moment. Or the yogin sees forms — the impure parts from the embryonic stage (<s>kalala</s>) onward, or from seeds and the rest — separately and mixed together, in their characteristics. Beyond that, through impermanence and the rest, by the general characteristic, according to applicability, when there is conviction of belonging to the class of all dharma-types, there occurs the suppression-abandonment of the conceits 'I' and 'mine.' From that abandonment, the faults of attachment and the rest are also suppressed by the knowledges born of learning and reflection.

body.translated_text: For the foundation of mindfulness on dharmas has a combined object (<s>sambhinnālambana</s>), because it has three, four, or five aggregates as its object.

body.text: katamena punaratra smṛtyupasthānena kleśātyantakṣayo bhavati ? brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text: By which foundation of mindfulness does the ultimate destruction of afflictions come about? We say:

body.text: kleśātyantakṣayo 'ntyena saṃbhinnālambanena vā // Abhidh-d_384 //
body.translated_text: The ultimate destruction of afflictions is by the last [foundation], or by [that with] the combined object. (Abhidh-d 384)

body.text: saṃsargasmṛtyupasthānena khalu 'saṃbhinnālambanena atyantakleśaprahāṇaṃ kriyate | 'vā'; śabdo vikalpārthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, by the conjoined foundation of mindfulness (<s>saṃsargasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) — 'with the combined object' — the ultimate abandonment of afflictions is accomplished. The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) is for the purpose of [indicating] an alternative.

body.text: yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Because —

body.text: asaṃbhinnārtha viṣayaṃ trayametad dvidheṣyate /
body.translated_text: These three, having objects of non-combined meaning, are considered twofold — (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: sāsravānāsravabhedāt | tataḥ punaḥ skandhānanityādinā
body.translated_text: due to the distinction of with-outflows and without-outflows. Then again, [examining] the aggregates through impermanence and the rest —

body.text: tasyaivaṃ paśyataḥ sākṣādudayavyayadarśanam // Abhidh-d_385 //
body.translated_text: For one thus observing, there directly arises the seeing of arising and passing away. (Abhidh-d 385)

body.text: skandheṣu jāyate paścāccakrabhramarikādivat /
body.translated_text: In the aggregates, it subsequently arises — like a spinning wheel or top.

body.text: eṣā ca smṛtyupasthānakuśalamūlaniṣṭhā | tasya khalvanityākāramabhyasyataḥ sarvasaṃskāreṣu pratikṣaṇamudayavyayadarśanamutpadyate, 'cakrabhramarikādivadi'ti |
body.translated_text: And this is the culmination of the wholesome roots of the foundations of mindfulness. For one who practices the aspect of impermanence, with respect to all conditioned formations, the seeing of arising and passing away at every moment arises — 'like a spinning wheel or top.'

body.text: sa pratītyasamutpādaṃ skandhānāṃ pratyavekṣate // Abhidh-d_386 //
body.translated_text: He examines the dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) of the aggregates. (Abhidh-d 386)

body.text: tasya pratikṣaṇaṃ utpādavyayaṃ paśyataḥ evaṃ bhavati- kathaṃ caite saṃskārāḥ santānena pravartante nocchidyante | sa pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyati traiyadhvikānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ hetuphalasambandhaniyamāvasthitānām | tataḥ punaḥ pratītyasamutpādam ||
body.translated_text: For one seeing the arising and passing away at every moment, thus it occurs to him: 'How do these conditioned formations continue in a stream and are not cut off?' He sees the dependent origination of conditioned formations across the three times, established in the determinate relation of cause and effect. Then again, [he examines] the dependent origination —

children.translated_text: Having placed it in the truths, someone then examines it. (Abhidh-d continuation)
Having understood its impermanence and suffering, then further — (Abhidh-d 387)

body.text: ekaikamaṅgaṃ satyeṣu pātayitvānityato duḥkhataśca pratyavekṣya
body.translated_text: having placed each member into the truths and examined [them] as impermanent and as suffering,

children.translated_text: seeing [them] as without an agent, without striving, and as arising dependent on conditions, (Abhidh-d 388)
he cultivates the aspect of truth — 'not-self' — in all [dharmas].

body.text: tatra svatantrakartṛvirahitvācchūnyānpaśyati svavaśena vinā sahakāribhiḥ pratyayaiḥ kriyākaraṇāt, parādhīnajanmatvāccānātmānaṃ paśyati 'dṛṣṭvā sarveṣvanātmeti tattvākāraṃ niṣevate'; ||
body.translated_text: Therein, seeing [dharmas] as empty because of the absence of an independent agent — because actions are performed not by their own power but by cooperative conditions — and seeing them as not-self because of being born dependent on others — 'seeing [them] as without an agent, as without striving in all, he cultivates the aspect of truth — not-self.'

body.text: tadabhyasyataḥ
body.translated_text: For one practicing that,

body.text: anadhiṣṭhātṛkatvaṃ ca pāratantryaṃ ca paśyataḥ /
body.translated_text: seeing the absence of a controller and the dependence on others — (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: na hyatra kaścitpuruṣo vā parameṣṭhī veśvaraḥ svatantraścaikaśca vidyate, paratantrajanmaprasarā eva sarvasaṃskārāḥ svasāmānyalakṣaṇādhiṣṭhitasvabhāvāḥ, iti parīkṣyamāṇasya
body.translated_text: for there is no person here, nor a supreme being, nor a Lord who is independent and singular; all conditioned formations merely proceed with birth dependent on others, having natures established in their own particular and general characteristics — thus for one examining,

body.text: sarvadharmeṣu nairātmye sthirā buddhiḥ pravartate // Abhidh-d_389 //
body.translated_text: a firm understanding of selflessness arises with respect to all dharmas. (Abhidh-d 389)

body.text: yathoktam-
body.translated_text: As stated:

children.translated_text: 'When one sees with wisdom that all dharmas are not-self,
then one becomes disenchanted with suffering — this is the path to purification.'

body.text: atha kasmādiha śūnyākāro na deśitaḥ ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now why is the emptiness aspect (<s>śūnyākāra</s>) not taught here? That is stated:

children.translated_text: Because [dharmas] are not empty of their own nature, the dharma-seals have been proclaimed. (Abhidh-d 390)

children.text: taduktyā ca taduktatvācchūnyākāro na deśitaḥ // Abhidh-d_390 //
children.translated_text: And because by stating that [not-self], this [emptiness] is also stated — the emptiness aspect is not taught.

body.text: na khalu saṃskārāḥ svabhāvena śūnyāḥ pṛthivyaptejovāyuprabhṛtīnāṃ kāṭhinyādilakṣaṇasya dhṛtyādikriyāyāśca pratyakṣatvāt | rāgādīnāṃ doṣāṇāṃ śraddhādīnāṃ ca guṇānāṃ cittamālyaśuddhikaraṇasāmarthyāt | teṣāṃ ca sāmarthyaṃ yathā dravyāṇāṃ harītakīcitrakadantīprabhṛtīnāṃ rasavīryavipākaprabhāvādidarśanāta sasvabhāvaprabhāvāḥ sarvadharmāḥ dharmamudrāyāśca 'śūnyākāro'; noktaḥ | tasmādihāpi nocyate | athavātaduktyā ca tadukteḥ |'; anātmākāroktyā ca śūnyatāpyuktā bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, conditioned formations are not empty of their own nature — because the characteristics of hardness and the like of earth, water, fire, and wind, and their functions of supporting and the rest, are directly perceived; because of the capacity of faults such as attachment and the rest, and qualities such as faith and the rest, to pollute and purify the mind [respectively]. And their capacity is [understood] just as the efficacy of substances like <s>harītakī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and the like is seen through their taste, potency, post-digestive effect, and special power — [so] all dharmas have their own nature and power. And the emptiness aspect is not stated in the dharma-seal. Therefore it is not stated here either. Or: 'because by stating that, this is stated' — by stating the not-self aspect, emptiness too is stated.

body.text: tadevaṃ nairātmye sthiramatiḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, having a firm understanding of selflessness,

children.translated_text: he constantly examines the elements and the rest through the doors of class, collection, and the like, (Abhidh-d 391)
by their particular and general marks, as appropriate.

body.text: dhātvāyatanaskandheṣu svasāmānyalakṣaṇaparicchinneṣu
body.translated_text: With the elements, sense-bases, and aggregates being delimited by their particular and general characteristics —

children.translated_text: then, for him, with respect to the intrinsic natures and so forth of each aggregate, truly, (Abhidh-d 392)
skill in the seven stations gradually arises thereafter.

body.text: "rūpaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti rūpasamudayaṃ rūpanirodhaṃ rūpanirodhagāminīṃ pratipadaṃ rūpasyāsvādaṃ rūpasyādīnavaṃ rūpasya niḥsaraṇamevaṃ yāvadvijñānasya |" uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- 'saptasthāne kuśalo bhikṣuḥ trividhārthopaparīkṣī kṣipramevāsravakṣayaṃ karoti" iti ||
body.translated_text: 'He truly knows form, the origination of form, the cessation of form, the path leading to the cessation of form, the gratification of form, the danger of form, and the escape from form — and so on up to consciousness.' For the Blessed One said: 'A monk skilled in seven stations and examining meaning in three ways quickly accomplishes the destruction of the outflows.'

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau ṣaṣṭhasyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the first quarter of the sixth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, the commentary called <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>.

body.text: ṣaṣṭhādhyāye
body.translated_text: In the sixth chapter,

body.text: dvitīyapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: second quarter.

body.text: tasyedānīṃ yoginaḥ smṛtyupasthānādiṣu kuśalamūleṣu dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ jñeyaṃ satyākāravyavasthānenānucitaśrutacintāmayākārasamudācāranyāyena
body.translated_text: Now, for that yogin, in the wholesome roots of the foundations of mindfulness and the rest, having previously seen the knowable [truths] through the arrangement of the aspects of the truths, by the method of the functioning of aspects [produced by] learning and reflection that have been practiced —

children.translated_text: for one churning, gradually, the fire-stick of the truth of suffering, (Abhidh-d 393)
with faith and energy as companions, seeking the fire of true knowledge —
then there arises knowledge that has fallen upon the aspects, that determines pacification, (Abhidh-d 394)
that is born of meditation, called 'warmth' (<s>ūṣman</s>), together with its accompaniments.

body.text: tatkhalūṣmagataṃ prakarṣitatvāt ṣoḍaśākāram, pratisatyaṃ caturākāratvāt, sāmānyaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ bhaviṣyasyāryamārgāgnernimittabhūtaṃ dhūmāgnivat | tasmiṃśca labdhe śamaḥ pratyāsannībhavati | atastat 'śamaniyāmakaṃ bhāvanāmayam'; iti | dhyānasaṃvarāśritasamādhibalena dṛḍhībhāvāccittaṃ bhāvayati campakapuṣpatilatailavaditi | 'sānuvartakaṃ'; ca pañcaskandhasvabhāvaṃ nairātmyabuddhiparitoṣāccānuskandhaśaḥ prasāda utpadyate- skandhamātrakamevedaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭervastubhūtaṃ nātrātmāstyātmīyaṃ vā ||
body.translated_text: That warmth-stage (<s>ūṣmagata</s>), being intensified, has sixteen aspects — four aspects per truth — and is the general foundation of mindfulness on dharmas, serving as the sign of the future noble path-fire, like smoke to fire. And when that is obtained, pacification (<s>śama</s>) comes near. Therefore it is 'determining pacification, born of meditation.' Through the power of <s>samādhi</s> based on the meditation-restraint (<s>dhyānasaṃvara</s>), because of becoming firm, it cultivates the mind — like <s>campaka</s> flowers, creepers, and sesame oil. 'Together with its accompaniments' — having the nature of the five aggregates; and because of the satisfaction of the understanding of selflessness, confidence arises aggregate by aggregate: 'This is merely aggregates — the object of the view of the existing body — there is no self here nor anything belonging to a self.'

children.translated_text: Then, likewise, the summits (<s>mūrdhānas</s>) — which damage wrong view, (Abhidh-d 395)
which, because of greater capacity than the warmth [stage], increase faith in the [Three] Jewels.

body.text: tadūrdhvaṃ tato mūrdhānastathaiva ṣoḍaśākārāḥ | teṣāṃ punarayaṃ viśeṣaḥ |

children.translated_text: (Jaini 322)

children.text: ) mithyādṛṣṭiśaktyupaghātitvam, tadupaghātāt kuśalamūlāni na samucchindanti | ūṣmabhyo 'dhiko viśeṣaḥ ratnatrayaśraddhāvivardhinaśca | teṣu khalvadhimātreṇa buddhādiṣu ratneṣu triṣvākārataḥ prasādo 'bhivardhate, na skandhaśaḥ, prāgevoṣmagateṣu tadbuddhiparitoṣāt | mūrdhasū..............
children.translated_text: the capacity to damage wrong view — from that damage, wholesome roots are not cut off. Greater distinction than the warmth [stage], and increasing faith in the Three Jewels. In them, indeed, with intensity, confidence in the form of aspects increases with regard to the three Jewels — <s>Buddha</s> and the rest — not aggregate by aggregate, as formerly in the warmth stages, from satisfaction of that understanding. In the summits..............

body.translated_text: Beyond that come the summits — likewise with sixteen aspects. But their distinction is this:

body.text: ........netvasminnubhayatrāpi paścimā // Abhidh-d_396 //
body.translated_text: ........in this, in both cases, the last [stage] — (Abhidh-d 396)

body.text: vinyāse vivardhane caiva dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ pratyutpannaṃ tadeva cānāgataṃ bhāvyate ||
body.translated_text: In the placing and developing [stages], the <s>dharma</s>-foundation of mindfulness (<s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) is present, and those very same [four] are cultivated as future.

body.text: bhāvyate skandhadṛktvādau na tannirvāṇadarśinaḥ /
body.translated_text: It is cultivated for one who sees aggregates and the like in their arising — not for one who sees their cessation (<s>nirvāṇa</s>).

body.text: na khalu skandhoparamadarśinaḥ skandhamatirbhāvyate |
body.translated_text: For one who sees the cessation of the aggregates, the contemplation of the aggregates is not cultivated.

body.text: ākārāṃstulyajātīyān sarvatrātra tu nirdiśet // Abhidh-d_397 //
body.translated_text: But the aspects of similar type should be indicated everywhere here. (Abhidh-d 397)

body.text: yādṛśāḥ pratyutpannāstādṛśā evānāgatā bhāvyante ||
body.translated_text: The future ones cultivated are of the same kind as the present ones.

children.translated_text: In the developing [stage], one of the present ones should be seen as arising from those [four] —
one of the four is present in the developing [stage]. (Abhidh-d 398)
But the future ones are cultivated — certainly all four here.
At the end, in liberation, all the unarisen future ones come face-to-face, [being] complete. (Abhidh-d 399)

body.text: nirodhe tu pratyutpannaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ catvāri tvanāgatāni bhāvyante ||
body.translated_text: But in [the seeing of] cessation, the <s>dharma</s>-foundation of mindfulness is present; however, all four future ones are cultivated.

body.text: ākārāḥ khalu sarvepi bhāvyante gotralābhataḥ /
body.translated_text: Indeed, all the aspects are cultivated from the attainment of the lineage (<s>gotra</s>).

body.text: gotrāṇi khalu labdhāni nirodhasatyato 'tra ṣoḍaśāpyākārā bhāvyante |
body.translated_text: When the lineages have been attained through the truth of cessation, here all sixteen aspects are cultivated.

body.text: gotralābhe tu vijñeyā sabhāgākārabhāvanā // Abhidh-d_400 //
body.translated_text: But in the attainment of the lineage, the cultivation of aspects of the same class should be known. (Abhidh-d 400)

body.text: prathamayoḥ satyayoḥ gotrāṇi ālambanāni | tenātra na visabhāgākārabhāvanā ||
body.translated_text: For the first two truths, the lineages [serve as] objects. Therefore, the cultivation of dissimilar-class aspects does not [occur] here.

children.translated_text: Everywhere in the scattering [stage], in the summit's cessation-scattering and increase —
the four called '<s>dharma</s>' [foundations of mindfulness] come face-to-face, being future. (Abhidh-d 401)

body.text: mūrdhākāravinyāse 'nirodhākiraṇaidhane'; ca dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ pratyutpannam, catvāryanāgatāni bhāvyante ||
body.translated_text: In the summit's aspect-placing stage, and 'in the cessation-scattering and increase,' the <s>dharma</s>-foundation of mindfulness is present; all four future ones are cultivated.

children.translated_text: All aspects there are cultivated from the attainment of the lineage.
One of all [foundations of mindfulness] arises; in the developing of the three truths — (Abhidh-d 402)
the four future ones are cultivated there with certainty.

children.text: ākārāḥ sakalā jñeyāḥ kṣāntivinyasane śṛṇu // Abhidh-d_403 //
children.translated_text: All aspects should be known — listen regarding the placing of the patient-acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>). (Abhidh-d 403)
Everywhere, the last [one] has arisen; the four are future.
All aspects there are cultivated — and also the future ones. (Abhidh-d 404)
In the present supreme dharmas (<s>agradharma</s>), the foundation of mindfulness called '<s>dharma</s>'
is present; but the four future ones are cultivated with certainty in those. (Abhidh-d 405)
The four aspects are [cultivated] — because of being similar to the path of seeing.
As in the heat-scattering [stage], so too it should be seen in the path of seeing. (Abhidh-d 406)
One should indicate the last — the <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge of the path) — as present.
Four [foundations of mindfulness are] future; likewise, the cultivation of the sixteen aspects. (Abhidh-d 407)
And above that too, for a noble one, in the arising of all unprecedented qualities —

children.text: śrutacintāmayaṃ hitvā sūkṣmasūkṣmaṃ vyapohya ca // Abhidh-d_408 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned what arises from learning and reflection, and having removed even the most subtle — (Abhidh-d 408)

body.text: evaṃ tāvadāryasya smṛtyupasthānabhāvanā draṣṭavyā ||
body.translated_text: thus, the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness for a noble one should be seen in this way.

children.translated_text: But for an ordinary person (<s>bāla</s>), at the beginning of the path, through the conquerings of four levels —
one of those arises as present; the four are future. (Abhidh-d 409)
On the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), all are unarisen in the last [foundation of mindfulness]; all are future.
In the last <s>dhyāna</s>, in the eight paths beginning with the preparatory — as before. (Abhidh-d 410)
But in the ninth, one should know three — because of entering the basic level.
And in the preparatory effort of the threshold, four — or the last one may be [present]. (Abhidh-d 411)
In the divine eye, divine ear, and [other] superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), in the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) and the like, likewise —
the first comes face-to-face; the four are future. (Abhidh-d 412)
But in [the knowledge of] others' minds, the third [is present]; and four are future.
In [the knowledge of] past lives and the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the last [is present]; all are future. (Abhidh-d 413)
Of the formless liberations, one of three should be stated [as present];

children.text: saṃmukhe nāma jātāstu tisra eva vinirdiśet // Abhidh-d_414 //
children.translated_text: but when [it] comes face-to-face — the named ones that have arisen — one should indicate precisely three. (Abhidh-d 414)
But for the formless [liberations] and the totalities, one should cite the last as present;
stating precisely three as unarisen. (Abhidh-d 415)

children.text: āryasya khalu vairāgyaprayoge kṣepaṇe pi ca /
children.translated_text: For a noble one, in the effort of dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) and in the casting forth (<s>kṣepaṇa</s>) as well —
one of all arises as present; and four are future. (Abhidh-d 416)
On the uninterrupted path, all are unarisen in the last; all are future.

children.text: ṛdhyādau tu guṇāḥ sarvamanāryasyaiva nirdiśet // Abhidh-d_417 //
children.translated_text: But in miraculous powers and the like, all qualities should be indicated only for the non-noble. (Abhidh-d 417)
In the knowledge of past lives and the like — and in the analytical knowledge of dharmas (<s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s>),
likewise in the subsequent concentrations and the like; and in the covering-over (<s>āvaraṇā</s>) likewise; (Abhidh-d 418)
in the formless liberations and the like; likewise in the arising of subtle perception —
one of all arises as present; the four are future. (Abhidh-d 419)
But in the most subtle [state], one should state the last as present; three as future.
In brief, this cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness has been stated. (Abhidh-d 420)

body.text: nirvedhabhāgīyānadhikṛtya
body.translated_text: Now, taking up the penetrative factors (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) —

body.text: etannirvedhabhāgīyaṃ caturdhā bhāvanāmayam /
body.translated_text: This penetrative [factor] is fourfold, [and] arises from cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>).

body.text: paramārthadakṣiṇīyabhikṣusaṅghapraveśadvārabhūtatvāt bhāvanāmayaṃ na śrutamayaṃ cintāmayam | kutaḥ punarupapattiprātilambhikaṃ bhaviṣyatītyetacca sandhāya (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 328)

children.text: ) bhagavatoktam- "cyutau batemau mohapuruṣāvasmāddharmavinayādyatra nāmānayoḥ mohapuruṣayorūṣmagatamapi nāsti" iti | taccaitatsarvam
children.translated_text: the Blessed One said: 'Alas, these two confused men have fallen away from this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, where even the heat-stage (<s>ūṣmagata</s>) does not exist for these two confused men.' And all this —

body.translated_text: Because it serves as the gateway for entering the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks worthy of supreme offerings, it arises from cultivation — not from learning or reflection. Moreover, as to why [it cannot arise as] birth-obtained (<s>upapattiprātilambhika</s>) — with this in mind,

body.text: ṣaḍbhaumaṃ ṣoḍaśākāraṃ pañcaskandhā vināptibhiḥ // Abhidh-d_421 //
body.translated_text: is of six levels, of sixteen aspects, of five aggregates, excluding acquisitions (<s>prāpti</s>). (Abhidh-d 421)

body.text: 'ṣaḍbhaumaṃ'; darśanamārgavato, 'ṣoḍaśākāraṃ'; darśanamārgavat sānuparivartakaṃ | 'pañcaskandhaṃ vināptibhiḥ |'; prāptayaḥ khalu noṣmāgatādisvabhāvāḥ | tatsvābhāvye (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 329)

children.text: ) hi tāsāmāryasyoṣmagatādisaṃmukhībhāvaḥ syāt | na ceṣyate | satyadarśanasamaṅgino dṛṣṭasatyasya vā satyadarśanaprayogasaṃmukhībhāve prayojanābhāvāditi |
children.translated_text: indeed, there would be a coming-face-to-face with the heat-stage and the like for a noble one. And this is not accepted — because there is no purpose in the coming-face-to-face of [another] truth-seeing effort for one who possesses the seeing of truth, or for one who has already seen the truths.

body.translated_text: 'Of six levels' — like the path of seeing. 'Of sixteen aspects' — like the path of seeing, together with their accompaniments (<s>sānuparivartaka</s>). 'Of five aggregates, excluding acquisitions' — for the acquisitions are not of the nature of the heat-stage and the like. In their being so

body.text: āha | ke punaste ṣoḍaśākārāḥ yeṣāṃ bhāvanayā strotaāpanno bhavati ? taducyate | caturbhirākārairanityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmākāraiḥ duḥkhaṃ parīkṣate | tatra bodhisattvādṛte tṛṣṇācaritaḥ prāyo 'nityākāreṇa, kausīdyādhiko duḥkhākāreṇa, ātmīyadṛṣṭicaritaḥ śūnyākāreṇa, ātmadṛṣṭicarito 'nātmākāreṇa |
body.translated_text: He asks: Which are those sixteen aspects by whose cultivation one becomes a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>)? That is stated: By four aspects — the aspects of impermanent, suffering, empty, and non-self — one examines suffering. There, except for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, one whose conduct is dominated by craving [examines] chiefly by the aspect of impermanence; one dominated by laziness, by the aspect of suffering; one whose conduct is dominated by the view of 'mine,' by the aspect of emptiness; one whose conduct is dominated by the view of self, by the aspect of non-self.

body.text: hetusamudayaprabhavapratyayataḥ samudayam | hetutaḥ ahetudṛṣṭicaritaḥ | samudayataḥ ekakāraṇadṛṣṭicaritaḥ prabhavato nityakāraṇadṛṣṭicaritaḥ | pratyayato 'buddhipūrvakṛtadṛṣṭicaritaḥ |
body.translated_text: By [the aspects of] cause (<s>hetu</s>), origination (<s>samudaya</s>), arising (<s>prabhava</s>), and condition (<s>pratyaya</s>), [one examines] the origination [truth]. By 'cause' — one whose conduct is dominated by the view that there is no cause. By 'origination' — one whose conduct is dominated by the view of a single cause. By 'arising' — one whose conduct is dominated by the view of a permanent cause. By 'condition' — one whose conduct is dominated by the view that [things] are made without intelligence.

body.text: nirodhaśāntapraṇītaniḥsaraṇato nirodham | ebhiścaturbhirnirodhaḥ | nāsti mokṣa ityevaṃ dṛṣṭicarito nirodhataḥ śarīrādimata ityevaṃ caritaḥ śāntataḥ | viṣayasukhacaritaḥ praṇītataḥ | dhyānādisukhacarito niḥsaraṇataḥ |
body.translated_text: By [the aspects of] cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), peace (<s>śānta</s>), excellent (<s>praṇīta</s>), and escape (<s>niḥsaraṇa</s>), [one examines] cessation. [One examines] cessation by these four: by 'cessation' — one whose conduct is dominated by the view that liberation does not exist. By 'peace' — one whose conduct [holds] that the body and the like [constitute liberation]. By 'excellent' — one whose conduct is attached to sense-pleasures. By 'escape' — one whose conduct is attached to the pleasure of <s>dhyāna</s> and the like.

body.text: mārganyāyapratipannairyāṇikato mārgam | ebhiścaturbhirmārgaḥ | nāsti mokṣamārga ityevaṃ dṛṣṭicarito mārgataḥ | kaṣṭatapobhirityevaṃ dṛṣṭicarito nyāyataḥ | laukikavairāgyamārgacaritaḥ pratipattitaḥ | asakṛllaukikamārgaparihāṇiko nairyāṇikataḥ | ityevamādite(ke?) samaye vyabhicaraṇakāle tvekopi sarvaiḥ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 330)

children.text: ) parīkṣate | rogagaṇḍaśalyāghātākārādibhirna tu tairatyantaprahāṇamityataḥ ṣoḍaśaivāryākārā ityucyante | purastāccaitacchlokānugatamevopadarśayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: by the aspects of disease, boil, arrow, affliction, and the like. But because these [latter aspects] do not bring about complete abandonment, only sixteen are called the noble aspects. Moreover, this shall be demonstrated later, in accordance with the verses.

body.translated_text: By [the aspects of] path (<s>mārga</s>), method (<s>nyāya</s>), practice (<s>pratipanna</s>), and leading-out (<s>nairyāṇika</s>), [one examines] the path. [One examines] the path by these four: by 'path' — one whose conduct is dominated by the view that there is no path to liberation. By 'method' — one whose conduct [holds] 'through severe austerities.' By 'practice' — one whose conduct follows the worldly path of dispassion. By 'leading-out' — one who repeatedly falls away from the worldly path. Thus, at certain times — at the time of deviation — even by one [aspect], one examines all [truths]

body.text: nirvedhabhāgīyebhyaḥ punaḥ
body.translated_text: After the penetrative factors, moreover —

children.translated_text: 'subsequently, indeed, there is the penetration, which is called the noble path.'
'Because it is a definite penetration, therefore it is called <s>nirvedha</s> (penetration).' (Abhidh-d 422)

body.text: iti prāgāviṣkṛtametat ||
body.translated_text: This has been disclosed previously.

children.translated_text: Having the inclination toward <s>dharmajñāna</s> (cognition of the dharma) regarding suffering, the undefiled seeing of the dharma [arises].
Then, in that very [truth], the determination — the <s>dharmajñāna</s> (cognition of the dharma) — [arises] immediately after. (Abhidh-d 423)

body.text: laukikebhyaḥ khalvagradharmebhyo nirāsravā lokottarā dharmamātrekṣaṇadṛṣṭirutpadyate | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 332)
In the <s>Sūtra</s> it is stated: 'Immediately after the worldly supreme dharmas, one simultaneously enters the fixed course (<s>niyāma</s>);
(Jaini 333)

children.text: ) yadavakrāntau pṛthagjanabhūmiṃ samatikrāmati" iti | tadanantaraṃ duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ (
children.translated_text: upon entering which, one transcends the stage of an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>).' Immediately thereafter, the <s>dharmajñāna</s> (cognition of the dharma) regarding suffering
(Jaini 334)

children.text: ) niścayātmakam | kṣāntyā vā saṃyogaprāptiṃ chinatti jñānena visaṃyogaprāptimāvahatīti (
children.translated_text: arises, being of the nature of determination. Or, the distinction is: the patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>) cuts the conjunction-acquisition (<s>saṃyogaprāpti</s>), while the knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) brings about the disjunction-acquisition (<s>visaṃyogaprāpti</s>).
(Jaini 335)
This is the distinction.

body.translated_text: From the worldly supreme dharmas, there arises an outflow-free, supramundane seeing that observes the mere dharma.

body.text: evaṃ triṣvapi satyeṣu tathaivānvayadhīrdvidhā /
body.translated_text: Similarly, in all three [remaining] truths as well — the subsequent cognition (<s>anvayadhī</s>) is likewise twofold.

body.text: dvābhyāṃ dharmajñānakṣāntidharmajñānekṣaṇābhyāṃ samanantaraṃ rūpārūpyāvacare duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntyanvayajñānekṣaṇamutpadyate | evaṃ triṣvapi satyeṣu draṣṭavyam | atra punaḥ
body.translated_text: Immediately after the two — the patient acceptance of the cognition of the dharma and the seeing by cognition of the dharma — there arises the patient acceptance of subsequent cognition and the seeing by subsequent cognition, regarding suffering in the form and formless realms. Similarly, this should be seen for all three [remaining] truths as well. Here, moreover —

body.text: anantyāstatra dṛṅmārgāḥ jñeyāḥ pañcadaśakṣaṇāḥ // Abhidh-d_424 //
body.translated_text: the path of seeing, excluding the last, should be known as having fifteen moments. (Abhidh-d 424)

body.text: antyakṣaṇaṃ muktvā pañcadaśasvabhāvo darśanamārgaḥ yastvasau sthāpitaḥ sa khalu
body.translated_text: Excluding the last moment, the path of seeing has fifteen natures. But that [sixteenth moment] which was set aside —

body.text: kṣaṇo 'ntyo bhāvanāmārgāt phalameṣo 'rthasiddhitaḥ // Abhidh-d_425 //
body.translated_text: the last moment belongs to the path of cultivation; it is this [person's] fruit, established in meaning. (Abhidh-d 425)

body.text:
yogācāryasya khalvabhi...............
................... strotāśceti pañcabhavanti ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, for the practitioner of yoga ............ ............... thus there are five [types of stream-enterers].

body.text: atra punarya eṣa pañcamaḥ sa khalu
body.translated_text: Here, moreover, this fifth one indeed —

body.text: dhyānāni vyavakīryātaḥ pañcamastvakaniṣṭhagaḥ /
body.translated_text: passes through the <s>dhyānas</s> in alternation; but the fifth [goes] to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>.

body.text: śuddhāvāsopapattiḥ khalu dhyānavyavakiraṇaphalā |
body.translated_text: Rebirth in the pure abodes (<s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>) is indeed the fruit of alternating between <s>dhyānas</s>.

body.text: caturdhārūpyagāmyanyo dṛṣṭanirvāyako 'paraḥ // Abhidh-d_426 //
body.translated_text: One who goes to the formless [realm is] fourfold; another is one who attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> in this very life. (Abhidh-d 426)

body.text: ūrdhvagasyānāgāminaḥ pañcadhā bheda uktaḥ | ārūpyagāmī tu caturdhā nirdiśyate pūrvoktebhyaḥ antarāparinirvāyiṇamapāsya | ityete ṣaḍ bhavanti | dṛṣṭadharmanirvāyakaḥ saptama ihaiva janmani yaḥ parinirvāti ||
body.translated_text: The fivefold division of the <s>Anāgāmin</s> who goes upward has been stated. But the one who goes to the formless realm is indicated in four ways, excluding the <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the interval) from those stated above. Thus there are six. The one who attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> in this very life (<s>dṛṣṭadharma-nirvāyaka</s>) is the seventh — one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in this very birth.

body.text: punastridhā tridhā kṛtvā trīnato rūpagā nava /
body.translated_text: Again, making each of the three into three groups — therefore nine [types of] form-realm goers from [the original] three.

body.text: ete khalu rūpopagāḥ pañcānāgāminastrayo bhavanti | antaropapadyaparinirvāyiṇamū(nnū ?)rdhvastrotāśca | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 340)

children.text: ) dvitīyādyā hi trayo 'nāgāminaḥ sarva evopapadya parinirvāyiṇo bhavanti | anupapannānāṃ parinirvāṇāt | teṣāṃ pratyekaṃ tridhā bhedānnavānāgāmino bhavanti | kathamiti ? antarāparinirvāyiṇastāvadutpatata evādūraṃ gatvopapattyāsannībhūtasya ca parinirvāṇabhedāt | upapadyaparinirvāyiṇaḥ upapadya sābhisaṃskārānabhisaṃskārabhedādūrdhvastrotasaḥ plutādibhedāt |
children.translated_text: For the second and subsequent three <s>Anāgāmins</s> are all <s>upapadyaparinirvāyins</s> (those who attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth), because their <s>parinirvāṇa</s> occurs [only] upon being reborn. By dividing each of those into three, there are nine <s>Anāgāmins</s>. How? The <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> is [subdivided] by the distinction of: attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> just upon arising [in the intermediate existence], after going a short distance, and while approaching [the place of] rebirth. The <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> — by the distinction of [attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s>] upon rebirth, with effort (<s>sābhisaṃskāra</s>) and without effort (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>). The <s>ūrdhvasrotas</s> — by the distinction of leaping and the like.
Their further distinction should be known through the differences in <s>karma</s>, <s>kleśa</s> (afflictions), and <s>indriya</s> (faculties). (Abhidh-d 427)

body.translated_text: These five <s>Anāgāmins</s> who go to the form-realm become three [main types]: the <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> (interval-attainer), the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> (birth-attainer), and the <s>ūrdhvasrotas</s> (upward-streamer).

body.text: teṣāṃ punastrayāṇāṃ navānāṃ vā anāgāmināṃ karmakleśendriyabhedādyathāyogaṃ viśeṣo boddhavyaḥ | trayāṇāṃ tāvatkarmataḥ, abhinirvṛtyupapattyaparaparyāyavedanīyakarmopacitatvāt | kleśataḥ mṛdumadhyādhimātrakleśasamudācārāt | indriyato 'dhimātramadhyamṛdvindriyabhedāt ||
body.translated_text: The distinction of these three or nine <s>Anāgāmins</s> should be understood, as applicable, through the differences in <s>karma</s>, <s>kleśa</s>, and <s>indriya</s>. For the three [main types], first — through <s>karma</s>: because of the accumulation of <s>karma</s> to be experienced in the production-existence, the rebirth-existence, and a subsequent existence [respectively]. Through afflictions: because of the manifestation of mild, middling, and intense afflictions. Through faculties: because of the distinction of sharp, middling, and dull faculties.

body.text: yadi tarhi kleśendriyabhedānnavānāgāmino bhavanti, kathaṃ sūtre sapta satpuruṣagatayo deśitāḥ ? tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: If, then, there are nine <s>Anāgāmins</s> because of the distinctions of afflictions and faculties, how is it that seven destinations of good persons (<s>satpuruṣagati</s>) are taught in the <s>Sūtra</s>? This is indicated:

body.text: ṣaḍdhordhvastrotasā sārdhaṃ saptadhā sadgatirmatā /
body.translated_text: Together with the <s>ūrdhvasrotas</s> (upward-streamer), the destination of a good person is held to be sevenfold.

body.text: dvau khalvatrānāgāminau tridhā tridhā bhittvā ṣaḍdhā vyavasthāpitau |

children.translated_text: (Jaini 342)
But the third — the <s>ūrdhvasrotas</s> — is stated without subdivision, for the purpose of not causing confusion. Thus the destination of a good person is taught as sevenfold.

body.translated_text: The two <s>Anāgāmins</s> [antarā and upapadya], being divided threefold each, are established as sixfold.

body.text: kasmāt punaḥ strotaāpannasakṛdāgāminoḥ satpuruṣagatirna deśitā satpuruṣasūtroddeśe lakṣaṇepi sati taducyate-
body.translated_text: Why then is the destination of a good person not taught for the stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) and once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>) in the exposition of the <s>Satpuruṣasūtra</s>, even though they have the defining characteristics? That is stated:

body.text: sati vṛtteranairyāṇāduktaiṣāmeva sadgatiḥ // Abhidh-d_428 //
body.translated_text: Because of the existence of [rebirth-]activity and the non-finality [of their path], [only] the good destiny as stated belongs to these [Non-returners]. (Abhidh-d 428)

body.text: yasmādanāgāminaḥ satyeva vṛttirbhavati nāsatī | itarayostu kuśalākuśale vṛttiḥ | yasmāccānāgāmī yato gatastatra na punarāgacchati, tau tu gatāgatī kurvāte tasmāttasyaiva sā gatirdeśitā netarayoriti ||
body.translated_text: Because the Non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) has indeed existing [rebirth-]activity, not non-existing. The other two [Stream-enterer and Once-returner], however, have both wholesome and unwholesome [rebirth-]activity. And because the Non-returner, wherever he has gone, does not return again from there, while those two go back and forth — therefore that destiny is taught as belonging to him alone, not to the other two.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ parāvṛttajanmāpyanāgāmī satpuruṣagatau vyavasthāpitaḥ ? netyāha | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: But is even a Non-returner with reversed birth established in the destiny of the noble person? No, he says. Because —

body.text: parāvṛttabhavo hyāryo neha dhātvantaropagaḥ /
body.translated_text: a noble one with reversed existence does not here go to another realm; (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: rūpadhātau hi parāvṛttajanmanaḥ āryasya dhātvantaragamane 'sti saṃbhavaḥ | kāmadhātau tu parāvṛttajanmāryo na dhātvantaraṃ gacchati tatraiva janmani parinirvāṇāt |
body.translated_text: for a noble one with reversed birth in the form realm, there is a possibility of going to another realm. But a noble one with reversed birth in the desire realm does not go to another realm, because of attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in that very birth.

body.text: yaścaiṣa kāmadhātau parivṛttajanmārya uktaḥ
body.translated_text: And this noble one with reversed birth in the desire realm who has been mentioned —

body.text: eṣa cordhvagatiścaiva nākṣamaṃ cārahānibhāk // Abhidh-d_429 //
body.translated_text: this one and the one of upward destiny — neither [experiences] faculty-transfer nor decline toward <s>arhat</s>-ship. (Abhidh-d 429)

body.text: ūrdhvadhātūpapannaḥ ūrdhvagatirārya ityapi kṛtaṃ dvayorapyanayornāstīndriyasaṃcāro na parihāṇiḥ | janmāntaraparivāsenāryamārgasya santatau dṛḍhataraniveśāt, āśrayaviśeṣalābhādāryasya janmāntare rūpārūpyapraveśendriyasaṃcāraparihāṇayo na santi ||
body.translated_text: The noble one reborn in an upper realm, called 'one of upward destiny' — for both of these there is neither faculty-transfer nor decline. Because through the sojourn of another birth, the noble path becomes more firmly established in the continuum, and because of the attainment of a special basis — for a noble one in another birth, there is no faculty-transfer or decline through entry into the form or formless [realms].

body.text: atha yaduktaṃ dhyānavyavakiraṇāditi tatra katamaddhyānamādau vyavakīryate ?
body.translated_text: Now, as for what was said about '<s>dhyāna</s>-intermixture' (<s>dhyānavyavakiraṇa</s>) — which <s>dhyāna</s> is intermixed first?

body.text: antyakāmīryate pūrvaṃ siddhirdvikṣaṇamiśraṇāt /
body.translated_text: The last [fourth dhyāna] is intermixed first; perfection comes from the mixing of two moments. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: caturthe hi praśrabdhisukhotkaṭaḥ samādhiḥ sarvakarmaṇyo yatastatsaṃmukhībhāvāt, āśrayasyopacaye satyāmṛtābhivṛddhiḥ yena śaknoti dhyānāni vyavakaritum |
body.translated_text: For in the fourth [<s>dhyāna</s>], the <s>samādhi</s> in which tranquility-bliss (<s>praśrabdhisukha</s>) is predominant is serviceable for all activities, and because of coming face to face with that [samādhi], when there is an increase of the basis, there is an increase of the deathless (<s>amṛta</s>), by which one is able to intermix the <s>dhyānas</s>.

body.text: kathaṃ punardhyānāni vyakīryante ? ādau tāvadanāsravaṃ pravāhayuktaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyate | tasmādvyutthāya tadeva sāsravaṃ pravāhayuktaṃ samāpadyate | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 345)

children.text: ) punaśca tadutthitaḥ anāsravaṃ tathaiva sa tān pravāhānhrasitvā yāvatkṣaṇa dvaye tiṣṭhatītyeṣa prayogaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) And again, having emerged from that, [one enters] the undefiled [fourth <s>dhyāna</s>] in the same way — reducing those flows until one stands in [just] two moments — this is the practice.

body.translated_text: But how are the <s>dhyānas</s> intermixed? First, one enters the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> that is undefiled and flow-connected. Having emerged from that, one enters that same [fourth <s>dhyāna</s>] that is with-outflow and flow-connected. (

body.text: siddhistu kṣaṇadvayamisraṇāt | yadā tu śaknotyekenāsravakṣaṇānantaramekaṃ laukikaṃ saṃmukhīkartum, ekalaukikakṣaṇāntaraṃ caikamanāsravamayatnena, evamanāsravābhyāṃ sāsravasya miśrīkaraṇānniṣpannā bhavati dhyānavyavakiraṇā |
body.translated_text: Perfection, however, [comes] from the mixing of two moments. When one is able to bring one worldly moment face to face immediately after one undefiled moment, and one undefiled moment immediately after one worldly moment, effortlessly — thus, through the mixing of the with-outflow with two undefiled [moments], the <s>dhyāna</s>-intermixture is accomplished.

body.text: kimarthaṃ punardhyānavyavakiraṇam ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: For what purpose, however, is <s>dhyāna</s>-intermixture [practiced]? That is stated:

body.text: udbhavārthaṃ sukhārthaṃ ca kleśāśaṅkārthameva ca // Abhidh-d_430 //
body.translated_text: For the purpose of [higher] rebirth, for the purpose of bliss, and for the purpose of [allaying] fear of afflictions. (Abhidh-d 430)

body.text: tribhiḥ kāraṇairdhyānāni vyavakīryante | upapattyarthaṃ sukhavihārārthaṃ kleśaparihāṇibhīrutayā ca | tatra dṛṣṭiprāptaḥ upapattyabhilāṣasamāpattipriyatābhyām | śraddhādhimuktastu pūrvābhyāṃ ca kāraṇābhyāṃ kleśabhīrūtayā ca | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 346)

) An <s>arhat</s> whose liberation is not time-bound (<s>asamayavimukta</s>) [does so] for the purpose of blissful abiding in the present life. And one whose liberation is time-bound (<s>samayavimukta</s>) [does so] also out of fear of afflictions.

body.translated_text: For three reasons the <s>dhyānas</s> are intermixed: for the purpose of [favorable] rebirth, for the purpose of blissful abiding, and out of fear of decline from afflictions. Therein, one who has attained through [direct] seeing (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>) [does so] out of desire for rebirth and fondness for attainment. But one liberated through faith (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>) [does so] for the two previous reasons and also out of fear of afflictions. (

body.text: yaccaitadvyavakiraṇamuktam,
body.translated_text: As for this intermixture that was stated —

body.text: tatpāñcavidhyataḥ pañca śuddhāvāsabhuvaḥ smṛtāḥ /
body.translated_text: because of its fivefold [nature], five Pure Abode levels (<s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>) are remembered. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: taddhi caturthadhyānavyavakiraṇaṃ pañcaprakāraṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātratara madhimātratamabhedāt | ato hetupāñcavidhyāt phalamapi pañcavidhaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: For that fourth-<s>dhyāna</s> intermixture is fivefold, by the division into mild, medium, intense, more intense, and most intense. Therefore, because the cause is fivefold, the fruit also is fivefold.

body.text: etāḥ punaḥ śuddhāvāsabhūmayaḥ
body.translated_text: These Pure Abode levels, furthermore —

body.text: na jātu dṛṣṭapūrvāstāḥ sarvairapi pṛthagjanaiḥ // Abhidh-d_431 //
body.translated_text: have never been seen before by any ordinary persons whatsoever. (Abhidh-d 431)

body.text: bhavāgramupādāya brahmalokamindralokaṃ yāvadavīcimupādāya sarvabālapṛthagjanairadṛṣṭapūrvamanyatra śuddhāvāsebhya iti |
body.translated_text: From the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) to the <s>Brahma</s>-world, down to the <s>Indra</s>-world, and from <s>Avīci</s> upward — never before seen by all foolish ordinary persons, except for the Pure Abodes.

body.text: abhidharmapradīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau ṣaṣṭhasyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the second section of the sixth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: ṣaṣṭhādhyāye
body.translated_text: Sixth chapter,

body.text: tṛtīyapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: third section.

body.text: yo nirodhasamāpattimaśnute kāyasākṣyasau /
body.translated_text: He who attains the cessation-attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) is a body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣin</s>). (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: yaḥ khalu nirodhasamāpattilābhyanāgāmī sa kāyasākṣītyucyate | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 349)

children.text: ) nirvāṇasadṛśasya dharmasya kāyena sākṣātkaraṇāt | sa khalu dharmaḥ kāyāśrayeṇopajāyate | tatprāptilābhādapi nirodhalābhītyucyate |
children.translated_text: ) Because of the bodily direct realization of a <s>dharma</s> resembling <s>nirvāṇa</s>. That <s>dharma</s> indeed arises with the body as its basis. From the attainment of its acquisition, he is also called 'one who has attained cessation' (<s>nirodhalābhin</s>).

body.translated_text: The Non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) who has attained the cessation-attainment is called a body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣin</s>). (

body.text: bhavāgrāṣṭāṃśahā yāvadarhattvapratipannakaḥ // Abhidh-d_432 //
body.translated_text: From the summit of existence, an eight-aspect abandoner, up to one on the path to <s>arhat</s>-ship. (Abhidh-d 432)

body.text: prathamadhyānavairāgyādekaprakāramārabhya yāvadbhavāgrāṣṭaprakāraprahāṇādarhattvapratipannakodraṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Starting from detachment from the first <s>dhyāna</s> as one type, up to the abandonment of eight types [of afflictions] at the summit of existence — he should be seen as one on the path to <s>arhat</s>-ship.

body.text: yaścānantaryamārge 'ntye vajraupamyāhvayesthitaḥ /
body.translated_text: And he who stands on the final uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), called 'diamond-like' (<s>vajropama</s>) — (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: navamasyāpi bhāvāgrikasya prakārasya prahāṇāyānantaryamārge 'ntye 'ntyaphalapratipannakaḥ evāvagantavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: for the abandonment of the ninth type also, at the summit of existence, on the final uninterrupted path — he should be understood as one on the path to the final fruit.

body.text: tatphalārthaṃ kṣayajñānaṃ tadekālambanaṃ na vā // Abhidh-d_433 //
body.translated_text: The knowledge of exhaustion (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) [arising] for the purpose of its fruit — does it have the same object as that [vajropama samādhi] or not? (Abhidh-d 433)

body.text: tasya vajropamasya samādherbalādutthitaṃ tadbalotthamantyavimuktimārgākhyaṃ tena sahaikālambanaṃ bhavati na vā | kṣayajñānasya catuḥsatyālambanatvāt ||
body.translated_text: The [knowledge] that arises by the power of that diamond-like <s>samādhi</s>, born from its power, called the final liberation-path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>) — does it have the same single object as that [samādhi] or not? Because the knowledge of exhaustion (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) has the four truths as its object.

children.translated_text: Upon attaining that, he is a non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), an <s>arhat</s>, honored by the three worlds, (Abhidh-d 434)
completely disjoined from all afflictions, gone beyond the threefold training. (Abhidh-d 434)

body.text: sa khalu trayāṇāmāsravāṇāṃ niravaśeṣaprahāṇāttisṛṇāṃ ca śikṣāṇāṃ pāragamanāt sabrahmakasyāpi lokasya pūjāmarhatītyarhannirucyate ||
body.translated_text: He indeed, because of the complete abandonment without remainder of the three outflows (<s>āsrava</s>), and because of having gone beyond the three trainings (<s>śikṣā</s>) — he deserves the worship (<s>pūjā</s>) even of the world including <s>Brahmā</s>, therefore he is etymologically explained as <s>arhat</s> ('worthy one').

body.text: eṣāṃ punastrayāṇāṃ mārgāṇāṃ katamaḥ sāsravo katamo nirāsravaḥ ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Of these three paths, which is with-outflow and which is without-outflow? That is stated:

children.translated_text: The path called 'cultivation' (<s>bhāvanā</s>) is twofold, by the division of with-defilement and without-defilement; (Abhidh-d 435)
but the path called 'seeing' (<s>darśana</s>) should be known as entirely without-outflow. (Abhidh-d 435)
In sequential order, [the path] that is predominantly for those with and without detachment — (Abhidh-d continuation)
the one called 'non-learner' (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) too should be understood as always immaculate. (Abhidh-d 436)

body.text: katamatpunaḥ katamāṃ bhūmimatyeti ? tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: Which [path], furthermore, transcends which level? That is indicated:

body.text: bhavāgraṃ nirmalo 'tyeti........ // Abhidh-d_437 //
body.translated_text: The undefiled [path] transcends the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>)........ (Abhidh-d 437)

body.text: ..........tatra tāvadaśaikṣasya catvāri dhyānāni trīṇyārūpyāṇyanāgamyadhyānāntaraṃ ca | śaikṣasya tu ṣaḍārūpyatrayaṃ hitvā | kiṃ punaratra kāraṇam ?
body.translated_text: ..........Therein, to begin with, for the non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) there are four <s>dhyānas</s>, three formless [attainments], the access (<s>anāgamya</s>), and the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> [level]. But for the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), six — excluding the three formless [attainments]. What then is the reason here?

body.text: saviśeṣaṃ yatastyaktvā phalaṃ paramupāśnute /
body.translated_text: Because, abandoning [a path] that has a distinguishing fruit, one attains only the higher fruit. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: iha khalu yaḥ phalaviśiṣṭamārgasthaḥ indriyāṇi saṃcarati saphalaṃ phalaviśiṣṭaṃ ca mṛdvindriyamārgaṃ tyaktvā tīkṣṇendriyamārgasaṃgṛhītaṃ phalamātrameva pratilabhate | yaścāśaikṣaḥ ārūpyabhūmiṃ niḥśrityendriyāṇi saṃcarati niyatamanāgāmiphalaviśeṣamārgasthasya na cāstyanāgāmiphalamārūpyabhūmisaṃgṛhītam | ityetat kāraṇam |
body.translated_text: Here indeed, one who is on the path distinguished by [its] fruit transfers faculties — abandoning the path with mild faculties that has a fruit and is distinguished by that fruit, one attains only the fruit comprised in the path with sharp faculties. And a non-learner who transfers faculties based on the formless level — [such a person] is necessarily on the path distinguished by the fruit of Non-return, and there is no Non-return fruit comprised in the formless level. This is the reason.

body.text: yaduktaṃ bhagavatā- "kleśān prahāyeha hi yastu pañcāhāryadharmā paripūrṇaśaikṣaḥ" iti | kiyatā paripūrṇaśaikṣo bhavati ?
body.translated_text: As stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Having abandoned the afflictions here, one who is a complete learner with five unsurpassable <s>dharmas</s>' — by how much is one a complete learner?

body.text: śaikṣasya tribhirakṣādyairdvābhyāṃ saṃpūrṇaṃtārhataḥ // Abhidh-d_438 //
body.translated_text: For a learner, completeness is by three [factors] beginning with attainment; for the <s>arhat</s>, by two. (Abhidh-d 438)

body.text: śaikṣasya khalu tribhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ paripūrṇatā bhavati | samāpattīndriyaphalaiḥ | tadyathā dṛṣṭiprāptasya kāmasākṣiṇaḥ anyataravaikalyāttu na paripūrṇatā syātprāgeva sarvavaikalyāt | tadyathā kāmāvītarāgasya śraddhādhimuktasyaivaṃ tāvacchaikṣasya |
body.translated_text: For a learner indeed, completeness is by three causes: by attainments, faculties, and fruits. For example, for a seeing-attainer (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>) who is a desire-realm witness (<s>kāmasākṣin</s>) — but due to the deficiency of one of these, there would be incompleteness, much more so from the deficiency of all. For example, for one not free from desire-realm [passion] who is a faith-liberated one (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>) — thus for a learner.

body.text: aśaikṣasya dvābhyāmindriyasamāpattibhyām | tadyathobhayabhāgavimuktasya asamayavimuktasyeti ||
body.translated_text: For a non-learner, [completeness is] by two — faculties and attainments. For example, for one liberated both ways (<s>ubhayabhāgavimukta</s>), one whose liberation is not time-bound (<s>asamayavimukta</s>).

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau ṣaṣṭhasyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the third section of the sixth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: ṣaṣṭhādhyāye
body.translated_text: Sixth chapter,

body.text: caturthapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: fourth section.

body.text: laukikalokottaradarśanabhāvanāśaikṣāśaikṣamārgabhedenānekavidho mārga uktaḥ | sa tu
body.translated_text: The path has been stated as manifold, by the division of worldly, supramundane, seeing, cultivation, learner, and non-learner paths. But it —

children.translated_text: should be known, in summary, as the path being fourfold: (Abhidh-d 439)
the uninterrupted (<s>ānantarya</s>) and liberation (<s>vimukti</s>) [paths], characterized as commencement and elevation. (Abhidh-d 439)

body.text: tatra prayogamārgaḥ kuśalamūlaphalasyārambha ityarthaḥ | tasyānantaramānantaryamārgaḥ yena kleśāñjahāti | vimuktimārgo yaḥ tatpraheyāvaraṇavimukte (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 355)

) arises as the companion of the acquisition of disjunction (<s>visaṃyogaprāpti</s>). The distinction path (<s>viśeṣamārga</s>) is that which, above that, is characterized by ascending progress for the purpose of attaining other wholesome roots.

body.translated_text: Therein, the preparatory path (<s>prayogamārga</s>) means 'commencement of the fruit of wholesome roots.' Immediately after that is the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), by which one abandons afflictions. The liberation path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>) is that which, in the continuum freed from the obscuration to be abandoned by that [uninterrupted path], (

body.text: punarmārgo bhagavatā mokṣapurapratipādanāt pratipacchabdenoktaḥ "catasraḥ pratipadaḥ | asti pratipatsukhā dhandhābhijñā | asti sukhā kṣiprābhijñā | asti duḥkhā dhandhābhijñā | asti duḥkhā kṣiprābhijñā |" tāsāṃ punarindriyato bhūmitaśca vyavasthānaṃ tadidaṃ pradarśyate-
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the path was stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with the word 'practice' (<s>pratipat</s>), because it leads to the city of liberation: 'There are four practices. There is the practice that is pleasant and of slow understanding. There is the pleasant and of quick understanding. There is the painful and of slow understanding. There is the painful and of quick understanding.' Their determination by faculty and level — that is now shown:

children.translated_text: For one with sharp faculties, in the fundamental <s>dhyānas</s>, the practice is pleasant, (Abhidh-d 440)
of quick understanding; but for one with dull faculties, [it is] slow; in other [levels], the reverse. (Abhidh-d 440)

body.text: mauleṣu khalu caturṣu dhyāneṣu yo mārgaḥ sā sukhāpratipat | sā ca tīkṣṇendriyasya kṣiprābhijñā tatrāyatnavāhitvāt | nairyāṇavatsukhā tatrāyatnavāhitvāt śamathavidarśanayoḥ sāmyāt | tatraiva sā mṛdvindriyasya dhandhābhijñā | anyāsu tu pañcasu bhūmiṣvanāgamyadhyānāntarikārūpyatrayasaṃgṛhītāsvanaṅgaparigṛhītatvāt | śamathavidarśanānyūnatvāt anāgamyadhyānāntarikayorārūpyatraye (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 356)

children.text: ) cānāsravo mārgaḥ tīkṣṇendriyasya pratipat, duḥkhā kṣiprābhijñā | mṛdvindriyasya duḥkhā dhandhābhijñā |
children.translated_text: ) — the undefiled path for one with sharp faculties is a practice that is painful and of quick understanding. For one with dull faculties, [it is] painful and of slow understanding.

body.translated_text: In the four fundamental <s>dhyānas</s> indeed, the path constitutes a pleasant practice. And that, for one with sharp faculties, is of quick understanding, because of effortlessly leading [to realization] there, and because of the equality of calm (<s>śamatha</s>) and insight (<s>vidarśana</s>). In those same [dhyānas], for one with dull faculties, [it is] of slow understanding. But in the other five levels — comprised in the access (<s>anāgamya</s>), inter-<s>dhyāna</s>, and the three formless [attainments] — because they are not endowed with [all] limbs, and because of the deficiency of calm and insight in the access and inter-<s>dhyāna</s>, and in the three formless [attainments] (

body.text: kathaṃ punarāryamārgo duḥkho bhavati ? nāsau duḥkhātmakaḥ na duḥkhasaṃprayuktaḥ ? naiṣa doṣaḥ | yatnavāhitvābhisandhervivakṣitatvāt ||
body.translated_text: But how can the noble path be painful? Is it not non-painful in nature and not associated with pain? There is no fault here. Because the intention of 'requiring effort' is what is meant.

body.text: punarapyeṣa mārgo bodhipakṣyaśabdenocyate "saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 357)

children.text: ) catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni catvāri samyakprahāṇāni catvāro ṛddhipādāḥ pañcendriyāṇi pañca balāni saptabodhyaṅgānyaṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ" iti |
children.translated_text: ) Four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), four right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), five powers (<s>bala</s>), seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), and the eightfold path (<s>aṣṭāṅga mārga</s>).'

body.translated_text: Furthermore, this path is stated with the term 'factors of awakening' (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>): 'There are thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening. (

body.text: kā punariyaṃ bodhiḥ ?
body.translated_text: What, furthermore, is this <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)?

children.translated_text: The knowledge of exhaustion (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) is regarded as <s>bodhi</s>, and likewise the cognition of non-arising (<s>anutpādadhī</s>); (Abhidh-d 441)

children.text: daśa caikaśca tatpakṣyāḥ saptatriṃśattu nāmataḥ // Abhidh-d_441 //
children.translated_text: and those conducive to it are eleven [in substance], but thirty-seven by name. (Abhidh-d 441)

body.text: sā punareṣā bodhiḥ kṣayānutpādajñānarūpāsatī pudgalabhedena tridhā bhidyate | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 358)

children.text: ) tisro bodhayaḥ | buddhapratyekabuddhaśrāvakabodhayaḥ | uttamanirvāṇāṅgabhūtā taddhi tisṛṇāmapi bodhīnāṃ puruṣakāraphalaṃ tatprādhānyatvāt | mṛdumadhyādhimātrāḥ saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedabhinnā mahāyānam | mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedabhinnaṃ buddhapratyekabuddhaśrāvakayāna mityucyate |
children.translated_text: ) Three [types of] <s>bodhi</s>: the <s>bodhi</s> of a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and a <s>Śrāvaka</s>. Being the factor constituting the supreme <s>nirvāṇa</s> — for that is the fruit of personal effort (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>) for all three <s>bodhis</s>, because of its predominance. The thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening, differentiated by the divisions of mild, medium, and intense — the mild-medium-intense differentiation is the Great Vehicle (<s>Mahāyāna</s>); the mild-medium-intense differentiation constitutes the vehicles of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and <s>Śrāvaka</s> — so it is said.

body.translated_text: This <s>bodhi</s>, furthermore, being of the nature of the knowledge of exhaustion and non-arising (<s>kṣayānutpādajñāna</s>), is divided threefold according to the distinction of persons. (

body.text: tasyāḥ punastriprakārāyā bodheranukūladharmāḥ smṛtyupasthānādayaḥ 'saptatriṃśannāmataḥ'; | dravyatastvekādaśa | śraddhādīni pañca balāni prītiprasrabdhyupekṣāsamyaksaṃkalpavākkarmāntāśca ṣaḍiti | ata idamucyate-
body.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> favorable to that threefold <s>bodhi</s>, beginning with the foundations of mindfulness, are 'thirty-seven by name.' But in substance, [they are] eleven: the five powers beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), and six — joy (<s>prīti</s>), tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), right intention (<s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s>), right speech (<s>vāk</s>), and right action (<s>karmānta</s>). Therefore this is stated:

children.translated_text: The five faculties beginning with faith, together with equanimity, joy, and intention, (Abhidh-d 442)
together with tranquility, and two arising from form — the difference is merely in name. (Abhidh-d 442)
The powers are none other than the faculties; wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) alone is the foundation of mindfulness; (Abhidh-d 443)
effort (<s>vīrya</s>) is called right exertion (<s>samyakpradhāna</s>); the bases of supernatural power are mental stability (<s>manasthiti</s>). (Abhidh-d 443)

body.text: kathaṃ punarekaṃ vīryaṃ caturdhā nirdiśyate ? tadapadiśte-
body.translated_text: But how is the single [quality of] effort designated fourfold? That is indicated:

children.translated_text: Abandonment of faults, non-arising [of faults], arising of qualities, and increase [of qualities] — (Abhidh-d continuation)
That which accomplishes [each goal] at once — that is the fourfold right exertion. (Abhidh-d 444)

body.text: utpannānāṃ rāgādīnāṃ khalu doṣāṇāṃ prahāṇāyānutpannānāṃ cānutpādāya yadvīryam, guṇānāṃ ca smṛtyupasthānardhipādādīnāmanutpannānāmutpādāya, utpannānāṃ ca sthitaye yadvīryaṃ, tatprayojananiṣpattibhedāccatvāri samyakprahāṇāni bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: The effort for the abandonment of arisen faults such as passion and the rest, and for the non-arising of unarisen [faults]; and the effort for the arising of unarisen qualities such as <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundations of mindfulness), <s>ṛddhipāda</s> (bases of supernatural power), and the rest, and for the maintenance of arisen [qualities] — from the division of the accomplishment of these purposes, there are four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions).

children.translated_text: Desire (<s>chanda</s>), effort (<s>vyāyāma</s>), investigation (<s>mīmāṃsā</s>), and mind (<s>citta</s>) — drawn by these, the concentrations (Abhidh-d 445)
are the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), the sources of the accomplishment of qualities.

body.text: chandamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā yo niṣpadyate samādhiḥ sa chandasamādhiḥ | kuśalamūlacchandamūlakatvāt samādhyādiguṇaniṣpatteḥ, tasmādasau chandasamādhirityucyate | tatprabhavāḥ sarvā guṇardhayaḥ | evaṃ vīryaṃ cittaṃ mīmāṃsāmadhipatiṃ kṛtvā niṣpannaḥ samādhiḥ sa eṣa cchandavīryacittamīmāṃsāsamādhiścaturvidhaḥ | prahāṇasaṃskāraiḥ cchandavīryasmṛtibuddhiśraddhāprasrabdhicetanopekṣābhiḥ pratyekaṃ samanvāgataḥ sarvaguṇasamṛddhiniṣpādako bhavati chandavīryacittamīmāṃsāparigrahaḥ sāmarthyāt | kuśaladharmacchande hyasati kutastat prāptyārambhaḥ ? ārabdhepi ca vīrye yadi na tatpraguṇameva cittaṃ bhavati na kāryābhiniṣpattirbhavati | yathāraṇīmabhinirmathyāpyantarāyavyuparamo bhavati punaḥ śaityamāpadyate tadvaditi | vīryānuvṛttaye cittamadhipatimiṣyate | tatpravaṇepi citte yadi sūkṣmān samādhyupakleśānnopalakṣya parivarjayati yadi samādhyanuguṇān, guṇāṃstu sāmānyalakṣaṇaśaktikriyānuttamārthāṅgabhūtānupalakṣya, prajñayā nopacinoti tasyānyāyārabdhavīrye trayamapyetanna prayojananiṣpattaye bhavati | evaṃ chandavīryaśraddhāsmṛtibuddhiprasrabdhicetanopekṣākhyānāmaṣṭāṇāṃ prahāṇasaṃskārāṇāṃ samādhiparigrahasāmarthyaṃ yathāyogamavagantavyam ||
body.translated_text: The concentration that is accomplished by making desire (<s>chanda</s>) predominant is the desire-concentration. Because the accomplishment of qualities such as concentration and the rest has its root in desire, which is rooted in wholesome roots — therefore it is called the desire-concentration. All accomplishments of qualities arise from it. Similarly, the concentration accomplished by making effort (<s>vīrya</s>), mind (<s>citta</s>), and investigation (<s>mīmāṃsā</s>) predominant — this fourfold concentration is of desire, effort, mind, and investigation. Endowed with the abandonment-formations — desire, effort, mindfulness, wisdom, faith, tranquility, volition, and equanimity — in each case, it becomes the accomplisher of the prosperity of all qualities, through the power of being governed by desire, effort, mind, and investigation, respectively. For if there is no desire for wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, how can there be the beginning of effort toward their attainment? And even when effort has been initiated, if the mind is not favorably inclined toward it, the accomplishment of the task does not occur — just as when one rubs a fire-stick but interrupts [the effort], [the wood] becomes cold again — so mind is considered predominant for the continuation of effort. And even when the mind is inclined, if one does not discern and avoid the subtle subsidiary afflictions of concentration, and does not discern and cultivate by wisdom the qualities that are constituents of the highest aim — such as general-characteristic, power, and function — then for one whose effort is improperly initiated, even these three do not serve the accomplishment of the purpose. Thus, the capacity of the eight abandonment-formations — called desire, effort, faith, mindfulness, wisdom, tranquility, volition, and equanimity — to govern concentration should be understood according to their respective applications.

children.translated_text: The fivefold group of faculties beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) is taught because of sovereignty over the three [kinds of] awakening. (Abhidh-d 446)
That very [group] is called 'powers' (<s>bala</s>) because of not being overpowered.

body.text: śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñārūpāṇi khalu pañcendriyāṇi bodhipakṣyeṣu vyavasthāpyante | bodhitrayādhigame śraddhādīnāṃ pañcānāmaiśvaryādhikyāt, sarvabhūmīṣūpalabdheśca | eteṣāṃ cādhimātramadhyamṛdutaratamaviśeṣādarhatprabhṛtīnāṃ vyavasthānaṃ bhavati | tānyeva bodhipakṣyeṣvindriyāṇyuktāni, na cakṣurādīnyājñātavatendriyaparyavasānāni | eṣāmevaiśvaryarddhiliṅgatvāt | ihendrāḥ dvividhāḥ | citteśvarāśca dhaneśvarāaścetyataḥ indraliṅgamindriyamitikṛtvendriyāṇi | (

children.translated_text: Jaini_360
