children.text: ) yathā pṛthivīśvarāṇāṃ paṭṭādīni liṅgāni bhavanti yaiḥ pṛthivīśvaroyamiti prajñāyate | yathā ca pṛthivīśvarāḥ vibhūṣaṇopabhogaiḥ parijñāyante tathā citteśvarāṇāmāryadhanasamṛddhānāṃ ca śraddhādīni viṣkambhitaprahīṇavipakṣāṇi nirmalāni liṅgāni bhavanti |
children.translated_text: Just as rulers of the earth have insignia such as diadems and the like, by which one knows 'this is a ruler of the earth'; and just as rulers of the earth are recognized by their ornaments and enjoyments — similarly, for lords of mind who are endowed with the wealth of the Noble Ones (<s>Āryas</s>), the faculties beginning with faith, having suppressed or abandoned their opponents, are pure insignia.

body.translated_text: The five faculties having the form of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), effort (<s>vīrya</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) are established among the factors conducive to awakening. Because of the pre-eminence of the sovereignty of these five beginning with faith in the attainment of the three [kinds of] awakening, and because they are found on all grounds. And their gradation — of highest, middle, mild, and mildest degrees — is established for <s>Arhats</s> and the rest. Those very [dharmas] are called faculties among the factors conducive to awakening, not [the other faculties such as] the eye and the rest up to the faculty of final knowledge. Because these alone bear the mark of sovereignty and accomplishment. Here, '<s>indra</s>' is of two kinds: lords of mind and lords of wealth — hence faculties (<s>indriya</s>) have the mark of lordship (<s>indra</s>).

body.text: tatra tāvacchraddhāyāḥ svalakṣaṇaṃ buddhadharmasaṅghān sambhāvayataścittaṃ prasādamupayāti sadbhūtaguṇayogādapetadoṣatvācca, taddharmeṣu ca prasādātmakamevārthitvamutpadyate | pratītyasamutpādādīnāṃ vā yathābhūtapratyavekṣaṇāt karmaphalādiṣu tatra saṃbhāvanā bhavati | tathā ca saṃbhāvayato yaścetasaḥ prasādaḥ sā śraddhā nāma dharmaścittena saṃprayuktaḥ | yathādarśādau dharmasamūhe, dharmāntaramādarśaprasādādayaḥ, evamarūpiṇi cittādidharmasamudayā dharmāntaraṃ śraddhādayaḥ, cittasyāśrayabhāvāt prādhānyāt santānānuvṛtteśca cittavyapadeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the own-characteristic of <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) is: when one esteems the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>, the mind attains serene clarity, because of connection with true qualities and because of being free from faults; and with respect to those <s>dharmas</s>, an aspiration that is of the nature of serene clarity arises. Or, from contemplating <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) and the like as they truly are, conviction arises regarding <s>karma</s>-fruit and the rest. And that serene clarity of the mind of one who thus esteems — that <s>dharma</s> associated with mind is called faith. Just as in a collection of <s>dharmas</s> such as a mirror and the like, clarity and the rest are <s>dharmas</s> distinct [from the mirror]; similarly, in the formless collection of <s>dharmas</s> such as mind and the rest, faith and the rest are distinct <s>dharmas</s> — but because mind is the basis and predominant factor, and because it is continuous throughout the mental stream, it receives the designation 'mind.'

body.text: vīryaṃ nāma cetasobhyutsāhalakṣaṇaṃ prayojane vārthiśakyatāṃ saṃbhāvya vividhamīryata iti vīryam |
body.translated_text: <s>Vīrya</s> (effort) has the characteristic of mental enthusiasm — one exerts oneself in various ways, having esteemed the capacity for [achieving] the purpose, hence <s>vīrya</s>.

body.text: smṛtīndriyaṃ nāma kāyādiṣu prajñayopalakṣiteṣu yā khalvaviparītābhilapanā pratyabhijñānam, yenāvadhārite viṣayasaṃmoṣaścetasi na bhavati sa khalvasaṃmoṣaḥ smṛtīndriyam |
body.translated_text: The <s>smṛtīndriya</s> (faculty of mindfulness) is: when objects such as the body and the rest have been discerned by wisdom, that non-erroneous re-cognition, that recognition, by which, when the object has been determined, there is no loss [of it] in the mind — that non-forgetting is the faculty of mindfulness.

body.text: cetasa ekāgralakṣaṇaṃ samādhīndriyam | viṣayagrāhiviṣayiṇo dharmāstadekālambanaṃ cittamekāgramityucyate | vicitraviṣayapradyute hyanavasthite cetasi tattvāvadhāraṇaṃ na bhavati | yathā khalu vidrutajavanāśvārūḍhaḥ puruṣaḥ pratimukhamāgacchatāṃ dṛṣṭapūrvāṇāmapi manuṣyādīnāṃ na śaknoti vyaktimupalakṣayitumevamanekaviṣayapradrute laghuparivartini citte na kāyādiviṣayatattvopalakṣaṇā bhavati | yadā tu susārathineva samādhinaikasmin viṣaye ciraṃ cittamādhāryate tadā dharmatattvamupalakṣayati | tasmāt kuḍya iva raṅgasya śleṣaḥ samādhirālambane cittasyādhāraḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>samādhīndriya</s> (faculty of concentration) has the characteristic of one-pointedness of mind. When the <s>dharmas</s> — the subject that grasps the object — have a single object, the mind is called one-pointed. For when the mind is unstable, flashing toward various objects, the determination of reality does not occur. Just as a person mounted on a horse running at full speed cannot clearly discern the features even of previously-seen humans and the like coming toward him — similarly, when the mind races toward many objects and turns swiftly, there is no discernment of the reality of objects such as the body and the rest. But when the mind is held for a long time on a single object, like [a horse guided] by a good charioteer, by concentration — then it discerns the reality of <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore, like the adhesive [that holds] the dye on a wall, concentration is the support of the mind upon its object.

body.text: prajñendrisaṃ yat svasāmānyalakṣaṇamupalakṣayati | yacca kāyadīnāṃ tattvamabhimukhavadavasthitaṃ prāptamiva ślaṣṭamiva pṛṣṭha iva ca lakṣayati sopalakṣaṇāt (

children.translated_text: Jaini_361

children.text: ) prajñendriyam | yadyapi sarvacitteṣu yathāviṣaye pratyupalakṣaṇā vidyate na tu sā yathārthapravṛtteti na sendriyam |
children.translated_text: that is the faculty of wisdom, because of discernment with signs. Although in all cognitions there is some degree of discernment according to the object, that [discernment] does not operate in accordance with reality, hence it is not a faculty.

body.translated_text: The <s>prajñendriya</s> (faculty of wisdom) is what discerns the own-characteristic and general-characteristic. And that which perceives the reality of body and the rest as if standing face to face, as if attained, as if adhered to, as if traced —

body.text: etānyevendriyāṇi śraddhādīni yasmādyoginaḥ kleśasaṃgrāmāvatīrṇasya kleśānīkavijaye pradhānāṅgabhūtāni rājña iva hastyādayastasmādbalānītyucyante |
body.translated_text: These very faculties beginning with faith — since they are the principal constituents for the victory over the army of afflictions of the <s>yogin</s> who has descended into the battle with afflictions, like elephants and the rest for a king — are therefore called 'powers' (<s>bala</s>).

children.translated_text: The sevenfold group of factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) was taught by the Teacher for the purpose of awakening. (Abhidh-d 447)
And the last [member], wisdom, is so because of ultimate assistance.

body.text: samānepi bodhipākṣikatve viśeṣeṇaite saptadharmā bodhyaṅgāni bhavanti | bhāvanāmārge khalveteṣāṃ prādhānyaṃ dṛṣṭasatyasthānata eva | dharmopalakṣaṇopalakṣitasvarūpādiṣu guṇadoṣeṣu smṛtipramoṣadoṣāpanayanārthamādau smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgamuktam |
body.translated_text: Although equally being factors conducive to awakening, these seven <s>dharmas</s> are specifically the factors of awakening. On the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), their pre-eminence [is established] from the very stage of having seen the truths. In order to remove the fault of loss of mindfulness regarding qualities and faults whose own-nature and the rest have been discerned by the discernment of <s>dharmas</s>, first the <s>smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅga</s> (mindfulness factor of awakening) is stated.

body.text: hlādaḥ prasrabdhiḥ | rāgajādiparidāhaprataptacittaśarīrasya grīṣmārkaprataptasyeva śītodakahradāvagāhanādanāsravajñānasaṃmukhībhāvā dyat kāyacittaprahlādaḥ sa dharmaḥ prasrabdhiḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Prasrabdhi</s> (tranquility) is refreshment. For one whose mind and body are scorched by the burning of passion and the rest — like one scorched by the summer sun — the refreshment of body and mind that arises from coming face to face with outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) knowledge, as if entering a pool of cool water — that <s>dharma</s> is <s>prasrabdhi</s>.

body.text: upekṣā nāma rāgadveṣapakṣapātavipakṣeṇa yathābhūtajñeyamavekṣamānasya yaccittasamatānyatarapakṣābhisaṃskāravipakṣo nirvāṇāśayā sopekṣā bodhyaṅgamityucyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Upekṣā</s> (equanimity) is: when one examines the knowable as it truly is, with the antidote to partiality toward passion and aversion, the evenness of mind that is the antidote to the formation of either side, with the aspiration toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — that is called the equanimity factor of awakening.

body.text: atra punaḥ prītyādīni trīṇyapi kṛtāvaśeṣāṇi catvāri pūrvameva vyākhyātāni | teṣāṃ punaḥ saptānāṃ buddhirdharmapravicayalakṣaṇā bodhiśca bodhyaṅgaṃ ca | jñānaṃ hi bodhiḥ jñānaṃ ca prajñā śeṣāṇyaṅgānyeva ||
body.translated_text: Here, furthermore, three [factors] beginning with joy (<s>prīti</s>) and the remaining four have already been explained previously. Among those seven, wisdom (<s>buddhi</s>), having the characteristic of investigation of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmapravicaya</s>), is both awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) and a factor of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>). For knowledge is awakening, and knowledge is wisdom; the remaining [six] are factors only.

body.text: teṣāmapi ca
body.translated_text: And of those also —

body.text: prītiprasrabdhyupekṣāṇāmuktāddhetostadaṅgatā /
body.translated_text: Joy, tranquility, and equanimity have the status of factors for the reason stated. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: nirāmiṣaprītiprasrabdhyupekṣābhiḥ prīṇitendriyagrāmaḥ sukhamanudvigno bodhimadhigacchati | (

children.translated_text: Jaini_362
And the characteristics, specifications, and reasons stated for these — from those too comes their status as factors of awakening.

body.translated_text: Through non-material joy, tranquility, and equanimity, one whose faculties are delighted, who is happy and undisturbed, attains awakening.

body.text: saṃkalpādeścatuṣkasya patho jñeyānukūlyataḥ // Abhidh-d_448 //
body.translated_text: Because of conformity to the path as what is to be known, the fourfold [group] beginning with right intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) [has the status of factors]. (Abhidh-d 448)

body.text: aṅgateti vartate | samyaksaṃkalpasamyagvākkarmāntājīvānāṃ samyagdṛṣṭisamyagvyāyāmasamyaksmṛtisamyaksamādhīnāmiva mārgānukūlyādaṅgatvam ||
body.translated_text: 'Has the status of factors' is to be supplied. Right intention (<s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s>), right speech (<s>samyagvāk</s>), right action (<s>samyakkarmānta</s>), and right livelihood (<s>samyagājīva</s>) — like right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>), right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>), and right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>) — have the status of factors because of conformity to the path.

body.text: ayaṃ punarāryamārgasatattvapiṇḍārthaḥ-
body.translated_text: Now, the summary meaning of the truth of the Noble Path is this:

children.translated_text: Having the light of knowledge, the ground of subtle discrimination, accompanied by moral discipline, with mindfulness and effort as friends, (Abhidh-d 449)
concentration as the enjoyment of the supreme bliss of all states — this is the path that reaches the abode of twofold liberation.

body.text: prādhānyaṃ saptavargasya prārambhoṣmagatādiṣu /
body.translated_text: The pre-eminence of the seven groups begins with the heat stage (<s>ūṣmagata</s>) and the rest. (Abhidh-d 450)

body.text: atra punaḥ

children.translated_text: this should be understood in order, with respect to the paths of cultivation and seeing.

body.translated_text: Here, furthermore,

body.text: tatra smṛtyupasthānānyādikarmikāvasthāprabhāvitāni kāyādisvabhāvopalakṣaṇāt | samyakprahāṇānyūṣmagateṣu | tatra saṃsāranirvāṇayorādīnavānuśaṃsadarśane balavadvīryāśrayaṇāt saṃsārapāramuttarati | mūrdhāvasthāyāmṛddhipādāḥ prabhāvyante teṣu samādhibalalābhāccittanigrahe sati parihāṇyabhāvānna kadācid guṇadhanadaridro bhavati | indriyāṇi kṣāntiṣvapāyātyantanivṛttau tadādhipatyāt | balānyagradharmeṣu kleśānavamardanīyatvāt | bodhyaṅgānāṃ bhāvanāmārge prādhānyaṃ vāsīdaṇḍopamayā mārgabhāvanayā niravaśeṣakleśaprahāṇāt | navaprakāratayā vā malaprahāṇe sati bodherāsannībhāvāt | darśanamārge mārgāṅgāni darśanaheyakleśaprahāṇārthamāśu traidhātukātikramaṇotpādāt | ānupūrvīvyatikramastu deśanānukūlyāt ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) are effected in the beginner's stage, through the discernment of the own-nature of body and the rest. The <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions) [predominate] in the heat stage (<s>ūṣmagata</s>); there, through seeing the danger of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the benefit of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, by relying on powerful effort, one crosses beyond the far shore of <s>saṃsāra</s>. In the summit stage (<s>mūrdhan</s>), the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power) become effective; in those, through gaining the power of concentration and thereby restraining the mind, because there is no decline, one never becomes destitute of the wealth of qualities. The faculties (<s>indriya</s>) [predominate] in the patience stage (<s>kṣānti</s>), because of the absolute cessation of the lower destinies (<s>apāya</s>) through their sovereignty. The powers (<s>bala</s>) [predominate] in the supreme worldly <s>dharmas</s> (<s>agradharma</s>), because afflictions cannot overpower [them]. The pre-eminence of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) is on the path of cultivation, because of the complete abandonment of afflictions through the cultivation of the path likened to an adze and handle — or because of the proximity to awakening when the stains are abandoned in nine modes. On the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>), the path-factors (<s>mārgāṅga</s>) [predominate], because they arise for the swift transcendence of the three realms for the purpose of abandoning afflictions to be abandoned by seeing. The [apparent] transgression of order [in the presentation] is due to conformity with the teaching.

body.text: atha kasmāccaitasikadharmadharmibhūtaṃ cittaṃ bodhipakṣyeṣu na vyavasthāpitam ? (

children.translated_text: Jaini_363

And [why are] <s>dharmas</s> such as perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), volition (<s>cetanā</s>), attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), desire (<s>chanda</s>), and resolve (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) not established among the factors conducive to awakening? That is now explained:

body.translated_text: Now, why is mind (<s>citta</s>), which is the substrate of mental factors (<s>caitasikadharma</s>), not established among the factors conducive to awakening?

body.text: na cittaṃ rājakalpatvād guṇadoṣānuvartanāt /
body.translated_text: Mind [is not included] because of being like a king — because it follows both qualities and faults. (Abhidh-d 451)

body.text: rājasthānīyaṃ khalu cittaṃ tadbodhipakṣyairdharmairviśodhya mokṣasukhamupalabhyate | yathaiva ca guṇānuvarti cittaṃ tathaiva doṣānuvarti | yathoktam- "cittasaṃkleśātsattvā saṃkliṣyante | cittavyavadānahetośca viśuddhyante |" tasya rāgādayaḥ saṃkleśakarāḥ, śraddhādayo vyavadānādhāyinastasmāccittaṃ na vyavasthāpitam |
body.translated_text: Mind, being in the position of a king, is purified by the <s>dharmas</s> that are factors conducive to awakening, and thereby one obtains the happiness of liberation. And just as mind follows qualities, so too it follows faults. As stated: 'Through the defilement of mind, beings are defiled; through the purification of mind, they are purified.' Passion and the rest are its defilers; faith and the rest are its purifiers — therefore mind is not established [among the <s>bodhipakṣya</s> dharmas].

body.text: vyavahārānukūlyatvāt saṃjñā hyeteṣu neṣyate // Abhidh-d_451 //
body.translated_text: Perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) is not accepted among these, because of its conformity with conventional usage. (Abhidh-d 451)

body.text: prāyo hi vyavahārānupatitā saṃjñā bodhipakṣyāstvekāntena paramārthapakṣabhajamānāḥ ||
body.translated_text: For perception mostly pertains to conventional usage, whereas the factors conducive to awakening exclusively partake of the ultimate level.

body.text: vipākaphalanimnatvānmārgokteśca na cetanā /
body.translated_text: Volition (<s>cetanā</s>) [is not included] because of its inclination toward result of maturation, and because the path is stated [separately]. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: cetanā khalviṣṭāniṣṭavipākanirvartanatvāt mārgaśabdenābhidhānācca nocyate |
body.translated_text: Because volition brings about pleasant and unpleasant maturation-results, and because it is [already] denoted by the term 'path' — it is not stated [separately].

body.text: nāprādhānyānmanaskāro vidyāvidyāpravartanāt // Abhidh-d_452 //
body.translated_text: Attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) [is not included] because of non-pre-eminence, and because it drives both knowledge and ignorance. (Abhidh-d 452)

body.text: manaskāropi samyagdṛṣṭeraṅgabhūtatvādapradhānaṃ vidyāvidyāpravartanācca ||
body.translated_text: Attention too, being a constituent of right view and hence non-predominant, and because it drives both knowledge and ignorance, [is not included].

body.text: kriyārambhapradhānatvānna cchando vīryabṛṃhaṇāt /
body.translated_text: Desire (<s>chanda</s>) [is not included] because of the predominance of initiating action and because it nourishes effort. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: chandaḥ khalu kartukāmatārūpaḥ kriyārambhaḥ prabhāvyate | vīrya cānubṛṃhayati | tadvīryaṃ bodhipratilambhakartavyatāparisamāpterūrdhvaṃ yāvadanuvartate |
body.translated_text: Desire, having the form of wish-to-do, is effected as the initiation of action. And it nourishes effort. That effort continues onward until the completion of the task of attaining awakening.

body.text: nādhimokṣaḥ samāropānna sparśo daurvibhāvyataḥ // Abhidh-d_453 //
body.translated_text: Resolve (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) [is not included] because of superimposition; contact (<s>sparśa</s>) [is not included] because of difficulty of discernment. (Abhidh-d 453)

body.text: prāyeṇa khalvadhimokṣo 'dhimuktamanaskāreṣu vartate | sparśopi trisannipātamātravipratipatterduravadhāravṛttiḥ | tasmānnoktaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Resolve mostly operates in [states of] resolute attention. Contact too, being merely the meeting of three [factors], has a function difficult to determine due to the disparity [of views regarding it]. Therefore it is not stated.

body.text: nāryavaṃśa hryapatrāpyā aviśāradavṛttitaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Āryavaṃśas</s> (lineages of the Noble Ones), and <s>hrī</s> (shame) and <s>apatrāpya</s> (moral dread) [are not included] because of non-confident conduct. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: catvāraḥ khalvāryavaṃśāḥ hryapatrāpye ca | navapravrajitabhikṣuvadaviśāradavṛttitvānna bodhipakṣyāḥ |
body.translated_text: The four <s>Āryavaṃśas</s>, and <s>hrī</s> and <s>apatrāpya</s> — because of non-confident conduct like that of a newly ordained monk — are not factors conducive to awakening.

body.text: nāpramādaḥ parāṅgatvānnāvihiṃsāviheṭhanāt // Abhidh-d_454 //
body.translated_text: Not non-heedlessness, because of being extraneous; not non-harming, because of [opposing merely] annoyance. (Abhidh-d 454)

body.text: vīryabhāṇḍāgārikaḥ khalvapramādaḥ | avihiṃsā ca viheṭhanāmātrapratipakṣatvānnoktā ||
body.translated_text: Non-heedlessness (<s>apramāda</s>) is indeed the storehouse-keeper of energy. And non-harming (<s>avihiṃsā</s>) is not stated because it is merely the antidote to annoyance.

body.text: sattvādhiṣṭhānavṛttitvānna maitrīkaruṇādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Not loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and the rest, because of operating on the basis of sentient beings.

body.text: dharmādhiṣṭhānāḥ khalu bodhipakṣyāḥ maitryādayastvekāntena sattvādhiṣṭhānāḥ |
body.translated_text: The factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyas</s>) indeed have <s>dharmas</s> as their basis, whereas <s>maitrī</s> and the rest have exclusively sentient beings as their basis.

body.text: mārgāṅgākṣaikadeśatvānnāpyavetyaprasattayaḥ // Abhidh-d_455 //
body.translated_text: And not the confirmed confidences (<s>avetyaprasāda</s>), because of being a partial aspect of the path-factors and the faculties. (Abhidh-d 455)

body.text: avetyaprasādāḥ khalu mārgāṅgaikadeśasvabhāvatvādakṣaikadeśarūpatvācca na punarbodhipakṣyeṣūktāḥ |
body.translated_text: The confirmed confidences are not stated among the <s>bodhipakṣyas</s> because their intrinsic nature is a partial aspect of the path-factors and because they are a partial form of the faculties.

body.text: nādveṣaḥ śubhamūlebhyaḥ sattvagocarabhāvataḥ /
body.translated_text: Not non-hatred (<s>adveṣa</s>), [although it is one of] the wholesome roots, because of having sentient beings as its domain.

body.text: sattvādhiṣṭhānapravṛtto hi adveṣaḥ | tasmānna bodhipakṣyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Non-hatred (<s>adveṣa</s>) indeed operates on the basis of sentient beings. Therefore it is not a <s>bodhipakṣya</s>.

body.text: audāsīnyānna nirvāṇaṃ daviṣṭhyānna paradhvaniḥ // Abhidh-d_456 //
body.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> [is excluded] because of [its] indifference; the voice of another because of [its] remoteness. (Abhidh-d 456)

body.text: niṣkriyaṃ khalu nirvāṇaṃ kriyāvantastu bodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ | parato ghoṣaḥ khalvapi bodhipakṣyāṅgabhāvo bodherbahiraṅgabhāvādviprakṛṣyate | tasmāt saptatriṃśadeva dharmā bodhipakṣyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is indeed without activity, whereas the <s>bodhipakṣya</s> dharmas are possessed of activity. The voice of another (<s>parato ghoṣa</s>), although a factor of awakening, is excluded because of being an external factor of awakening. Therefore, exactly thirty-seven <s>dharmas</s> are the factors conducive to awakening.

body.text: kati punarbodhipakṣyāḥ sāsravāḥ katyanāsravāḥ ? tadidaṃ pradarśyate-
body.translated_text: How many of the <s>bodhipakṣyas</s> are with-outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>), and how many are without-outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>)? That is now shown:

children.translated_text: The awakening-factors (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>) are stainless, because of being closest to awakening.
The others are to be understood [as being] both with and without defilement. (Abhidh-d 457)

body.text: bodhyaṅgāni khalu bodherāsannatamatvādekāntānāsravāṇi | tadanye tu sāsravānāsravāḥ sarve hi kuśalā dharmā āryamārgāvāhakā nirvāṇāśayāśca | bodhitrayasaṃnikṛṣṭaviprakṛṣṭāṅgabhāvā bodhipakṣyā ityucyante | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 365]

children.text: ) "adhigato me paurāṇo mārgaḥ" iti vacanāt | śāstre tu bodhyaṅgopari ye paṭhyante samyagdṛṣṭyādayo dharmāste 'nāsravā iti ||
children.translated_text: ) 'I have found the ancient path' — from this statement. But in the <s>Śāstra</s> (treatise), those <s>dharmas</s> beginning with right view that are recited above the awakening-factors are without-outflows.

body.translated_text: The awakening-factors, because of being closest to awakening, are exclusively without-outflows. But the others are both with-outflows and without-outflows. For all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are conveyors to the noble path and have <s>nirvāṇa</s> as their aim. As proximate or remote factors of the threefold awakening, they are called '<s>bodhipakṣyas</s>.' For the <s>Bhagavat</s> has said: (

body.text: kasyāṃ punarbhūmau kiyanto bodhipakṣyā vidyante ?
body.translated_text: In which plane, then, are how many <s>bodhipakṣyas</s> found?

children.translated_text: In the first <s>dhyāna</s>, all [are found]; in the fundamental [dhyāna] and in the access (<s>anāgamya</s>), [all] minus joy (<s>prīti</s>);
in the second [dhyāna] too, minus [wrong] conception (<s>saṃkalpa</s>); and in the two [dhyānas after that], minus both of those. (Abhidh-d 458)
And minus the moral-discipline factors and those two, they should be seen in the three formless [attainments];
and minus all the awakening-factors, in the desire realm [they are] minus the awakening-factors. (Abhidh-d 459)

body.text: tatra tāvanmaule dhyāne sarvepi saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣyā vidyante | anāgamye tu prītivarjitāḥ | tatra prīterabhāvāt | vītarāgāvītarāgasādhāraṇaiṣā bhūmiriti nāsti prītiḥ | dvitīye tu dhyāne saṃkalpavarjitāḥ sarve vidyante | tṛtīyacaturthayostu dhyānayoḥ saṃkalpaprītivarjyāḥ pañcatriṃśat | 'ca'śabdād dhyānāntarepi pañcatriṃśat saṃkalpaprītivarjitāḥ | triṣvārūpyeṣu samyagvākkarmāntājīvaistribhiḥ prītisaṃkalpābhyāṃ ca | bhavāgrepi śīlāṅgatrayaprītisaṃkalpabodhyaṅgavarjitāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ | kāmadhātāvapi bodhyaṅgavarjitāstriṃśadvidyanta iti | ye punaranāstravāṇyeva mārgāṅgānīcchanti teṣāṃ tairapi varjitāḥ śeṣā bodhipakṣyā vidyanta iti | gatametat ||
body.translated_text: Therein, to begin with, in the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>, all thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣyas</s> are found. But in the access (<s>anāgamya</s>), minus joy — because joy is absent there; since this plane is common to those free from passion and those not free from passion, there is no joy. In the second <s>dhyāna</s>, all are found minus conception (<s>saṃkalpa</s>). But in the third and fourth <s>dhyānas</s>, thirty-five, minus conception and joy. By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), in the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> [intermediate stage] too, thirty-five, minus conception and joy. In the three formless [attainments], [they are] minus the three moral-discipline factors, joy, and conception. In the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) too, twenty-five, minus the three moral-discipline factors, joy, conception, and the awakening-factors. In the desire realm too, thirty are found, minus the awakening-factors. But for those who hold that the path-factors are exclusively without-outflows, the remaining <s>bodhipakṣyas</s> are found minus those [path-factors] as well. This has been covered.

body.text: idaṃ tu vaktavyam | bodhipākṣikādhikāre-
body.translated_text: But this must be stated. In the topic of <s>bodhipakṣyas</s> —

children.translated_text: those four firstnesses (<s>tatprathamatā</s>) therein are declared by the learned:
with respect to entering the certainty (<s>nyāmāvakrānti</s>), dispassion, attainment of fruit, and growth of the faculties. (Abhidh-d 460)

body.text: nyāmāvakrāntitatprathamatā, vairāgyatatprathamatā, phalaprāptitatprathamatā, irndriyāntaravivṛddhitatprathamatā tāsu khalvetāsu catasṛṣu tatprathamatāsu-
body.translated_text: The firstness of entering certainty, the firstness of dispassion, the firstness of attaining fruit, and the firstness of growth of a [different] faculty — in these four firstnesses —

children.translated_text: of the eight stainless path-factors, in each case,
in those [firstnesses], one should know the gain and non-gain of each across the time-periods, [with reference to] the nine bases. (Abhidh-d 461)

body.text: bodhipakṣyabhāvanāprayuktasyāvetyaprasādapratilambho 'vaśyambhāvītyato vaktavyaṃ kasmin satye dṛśyamāne kasyāvetyaprasādasya lābhaḥ ? tadidaṃ nirdiśyate-
body.translated_text: Since the obtaining of confirmed confidence (<s>avetyaprasāda</s>) is inevitable for one engaged in the cultivation of the <s>bodhipakṣyas</s>, it must be stated: upon seeing which truth is the confirmed confidence of which [type] obtained? That is now indicated:

children.translated_text: Upon comprehending three truths, the gain of the confidences in moral discipline and <s>Dharma</s>;
upon seeing the truth of the path, [the gain] of those pertaining to the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s> as well. (Abhidh-d 462)

body.text: duḥkhasatyamabhisamāgacchannāryakāntāni ca śīlāni pratilabhate dharme cāvetyaprasādaḥ | katarasmin dharme ? tasminneva duḥkhasatye | dharmamātramidaṃ sarvaṃ dvādaśāyatanamātramityarthaḥ | nātra kaścidekaḥ sarvabhedānvayī jātidravyākhyo dharmī vidyate | na cātra santi puruṣajīvapugdalā bhūtakoṭayaḥ śaśaviṣāṇakalpā nirātmāna iti | evaṃ samudayamabhisamāgacchato dvayoreva lābhaḥ | tadvinnirodhaṃ samāgacchato draṣṭavyam | mārgasatyekṣaṇe tu buddhe bhagavati prasādo labhyate tatsaṅghe ca | sadbhūtamārgākhyāyī bhagavānmārgajño mārgadeśikaḥ | yepi ca taṃ mārgaṃ pratipannāḥ śrāvakāḥ śaikṣāśaikṣāḥ puruṣavṛṣabhāḥ ye ca saptasaddharmādipradīpaprakāśitabuddhyāśayasā(?)ca bodhisattvasiṃhāḥ darśanamārgaguhādhyāsinaḥ teṣu ca prasādo bhavati dvyākāraśraddhāsvarūpaḥ | so 'yaṃ vistareṇocyate ||
body.translated_text: Upon comprehending the truth of suffering, one obtains the morals loved by the noble ones (<s>āryakānta śīla</s>) and confirmed confidence in the <s>Dharma</s>. In which <s>Dharma</s>? In that very truth of suffering. The meaning is: 'All this is merely <s>dharmas</s>, merely twelve <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases).' There is no single entity here, called by the terms 'genus' or 'substance,' that pervades all distinctions. Nor are there here persons, living souls, <s>pudgalas</s>, ultimate points — [all of which are] like a hare's horn; [all is] without a self. Thus, upon comprehending origination, one gains [confidence] in those two alone. Without those, upon comprehending cessation, it should be seen [analogously]. But upon seeing the truth of the path, confidence in the <s>Buddha Bhagavat</s> and in his <s>Saṃgha</s> is obtained. The <s>Bhagavat</s> is the one who declares the true path, the knower of the path, the guide of the path. And those disciples — learners and adepts, bulls among men — who have entered that path, and those <s>Bodhisattva</s>-lions dwelling in the cave of the path of seeing, whose understanding and aspiration are illuminated by the seven noble treasures and the like (?) — in them too confidence arises, having the nature of twofold faith. This is stated in detail.

children.translated_text: That faith whose object is the truths, apart from the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Saṃgha</s>, and the path —
that is the confirmed confidence in the <s>Dharma</s>, because of the effect of full conviction. (Abhidh-d 463)

body.text: sa punardharmo nirvāṇaṃ bodhisattvasantānikaśca mārgaḥ ||
body.translated_text: That <s>Dharma</s>, moreover, is <s>nirvāṇa</s> and the path in the continuum of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: kaḥ punareṣa buddhaḥ ko vā tatprasāda ityapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: Who then is this <s>Buddha</s>, and what is the confidence in him? That is indicated:

children.translated_text: Through the destruction of the darkness of the sleep of delusion, through the opening of the eye of wisdom by oneself —

children.text: buddho yastadguṇe śraddhā prasādaḥ sa jine mataḥ // Abhidh-d_464 //
children.translated_text: [one who is] awakened (<s>Buddha</s>); faith in his qualities — that is considered confidence in the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror). (Abhidh-d 464)

body.text: dviprakāro hi buddhaśabdasyārtho mukhyo gauṇaśca | tatrādyo buddhakārakā buddhasyāśaikṣā dharmāḥ | gauṇastu tadādhārepi śarīre tatphalabhūteṣu cāṣṭādaśasvāveṇikeṣu buddhaguṇeṣu buddhaśabdasādhutvaṃ pūrvameva pradarśitam ||
body.translated_text: The meaning of the word '<s>Buddha</s>' is indeed twofold: primary and secondary. Therein, the first [meaning] — the <s>aśaikṣa</s> (adept-level) <s>dharmas</s> that are the makers of the <s>Buddha</s>. The secondary [meaning] — even with reference to the body that is their support, and with reference to the eighteen distinctive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> that are the fruits thereof, the propriety of the word '<s>Buddha</s>' has been previously demonstrated.

children.translated_text: The source of the persons rich in the qualities of learners and adepts —
faith having their qualities as its object — that is the confidence pertaining to the <s>Saṃgha</s>. (Abhidh-d 465)

body.text: uktaṃ hi sūtre- "kati bhadanta loke dakṣiṇīyāḥ ? dvau gṛhapate śaikṣā aśaikṣāśca | tatrāṣṭādaśa śaikṣāḥ nava śaikṣāḥ |" iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: For it is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'How many, Venerable Sir, are worthy of offerings in the world? Two, O householder — learners and adepts. Therein, eighteen are learners and nine are adepts' — and so on in detail.

body.text: śīlānāṃ yattu vaimalyaṃ tatprasādastathaiva tu /
body.translated_text: And the purity of the moral precepts — that is the confidence therein; likewise,

body.text: kati punareṣāṃ dravyataḥ kati nāmataḥ ?
body.translated_text: how many of these are there by substance and how many by name?

body.text: dravyato dvayamevaitannāmatastu catuṣṭayam // Abhidh-d_466 //
body.translated_text: By substance, these are just two; but by name, they are four. (Abhidh-d 466)

body.text: śraddhā ratnatrayālambanabhedena tridhā bhitvāryakāntāni ca śīlānyekadhā kṛtvā tatrāpi vaimalyaprasādoktiḥ | yaddhi nirmalaṃ tat prasannamityucyate ||
body.translated_text: Faith, divided threefold by the distinction of having the Three Jewels as its object, and the noble-loved moral precepts, made one — therein too the expression of 'purity' and 'confidence' [is used]. For what is stainless is said to be 'clear' (<s>prasanna</s>).

body.text: idamidānīṃ vācyam | atha kasmātsamanvāgatopi śaikṣaḥ samyagjñānena samyagvimuktyā cāṣṭābhiraṅgaiḥ samanvāgataḥ śaikṣaḥ prātipada ityuktaṃ daśabhirarhan kṣīṇāsrava iti ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated. Why is the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), even though endowed with right knowledge and right liberation, said to be 'a practitioner endowed with eight factors,' while the <s>Arhat</s> with outflows destroyed is [said to be endowed with] ten? That is stated:

body.text: śaikṣasya bandhaśeṣatvādvimuktirnāṅgamiṣyate /
body.translated_text: Because for the learner, bondage remains, liberation is not considered a factor.

body.text: śaikṣasya vidyamānāpi anākāritvānnāṅgamucyate | satyāmapi hi tasyāṃ kleśabandhanabaddhaḥ śaikṣo na ca vimokṣo yujyate |
body.translated_text: Even though existing for the learner, it is not called a factor because of being non-operative. For even when it exists, the learner is bound by the bondage of defilements, and liberation is not appropriate [for him].

body.text: kā punariyaṃ vimuktiḥ katidhā ca ? tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: What then is this liberation, and of how many kinds? That is indicated:

body.text: mokṣādhimokṣarūpatvānnityānityatvato dvidhā // Abhidh-d_467 //
body.translated_text: Because of having the nature of release and firm resolve, and because of being permanent and impermanent — it is twofold. (Abhidh-d 467)

body.text: svarūpabhedādapi dvidhā prakārabhedādapīti | svabhāvabhedāt mokṣādhimokṣasvabhāvā | prakārabhedopi kṣarākṣarabhedāt, sāmayikī kāntākopyabhedādvā rāgavirāgāvidyāvirāgabhedācca ||
body.translated_text: It is twofold by distinction of intrinsic nature and also by distinction of type. By distinction of intrinsic nature, it has the nature of release (<s>mokṣa</s>) and firm resolve (<s>adhimokṣa</s>). By distinction of type too, from the distinction of perishable and imperishable; or from the distinction of temporary (<s>sāmayikī</s>), loved [by the noble ones] (<s>kāntā</s>), and immovable (<s>akopyā</s>); and also from the distinction of dispassion from attachment and dispassion from ignorance.

body.text: atha samyagjñānaṃ katamattaducyate-
body.translated_text: Now, which one is right knowledge? That is stated:

body.text: pūrvoktaiva hi yā bodhiḥ sā samyagjñānamucyate /
body.translated_text: That very awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) previously stated — that is called right knowledge.

body.text: kṣayānutpādajñāne bodhirityuktam | te eva samyagjñānaṃ veditavyam |
body.translated_text: The knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>) were stated as awakening. Those very [two] should be understood as right knowledge.

body.text: katarat punaścittaṃ vimucyate ? kiṃ jātaniruddhamathājātaniruddhamatha jātameva ?
body.translated_text: Which mind, then, is liberated? Is it one that has arisen and ceased, or one that has not [yet] arisen and not [yet] ceased, or one that has merely arisen?

body.text: mucyate 'nāgataṃ cittamaśaikṣaṃ kleśarodhataḥ // Abhidh-d_468 //
body.translated_text: The future mind is liberated — [specifically] the adept [mind] — because of the cessation of defilements. (Abhidh-d 468)

body.text: kaścit khalvāha- anāgataṃ khalu cittamutpādyamānaṃ vimucyate 'dhvavimuktyā sarvameva tvanāgataṃ vimucyate | kleśāvaraṇāt santānavimuktyā | tatpunaraśaikṣameva kleśopakleśaprāptivibandhāpagamāt | yadapi tadrūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktaṃ karmopapattiphalaṃ tadapyarhattvaprāptivibandhakaraṃ tacca sarvaṃ vajropamena prahīyata ityāvaraṇavigamāt sarvamevānāgatamaśaikṣaṃ cittaṃ vimucyate ||
body.translated_text: Someone indeed says: the future mind, when about to arise, is liberated — by the liberation of the time-period, all the future [mind] is liberated. By the liberation of the continuum — because of the obstruction of defilements. That, moreover, is exclusively the adept [mind], because of the removal of the bondage of the acquisition of defilements and secondary defilements. That which is also the maturation-fruit of <s>karma</s> connected with the form and formless [realms] — that too creates an obstruction to attaining <s>arhatship</s>; and all of that is abandoned by the vajra-like [concentration]. Therefore, because of the removal of obstruction, all future adept mind is liberated.

body.text: dharmā eva tu paramārthataḥ śikṣante | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: But it is <s>dharmas</s> themselves that, in the ultimate sense, undergo training. Because —

body.text: dharmavyāpārato loke dharmyapi vyāpṛto mataḥ /
body.translated_text: from the activity of <s>dharmas</s>, the possessor of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmin</s>) too is considered to be active in the world.

body.text: auṣṇyākhyasya dharmasyendhanādidahanavyāpāre satyagnerapi dharmiṇo vyāpāra ucyate | agninā kāṣṭhaṃ dagdhamityagnidahanavyāpāre ca devadattena dagdhosmītyupacaryate | tathā dharmāṇāṃ kleśaprahāṇaśikṣaṇe sati tatsambandhāpekṣayā bhikṣuraśaikṣa ityucyate |
body.translated_text: When the <s>dharma</s> called 'heat' has the activity of burning fuel and the like, the activity is attributed to fire, the possessor of that <s>dharma</s>. 'The wood was burned by fire' — and the activity of fire-burning is figuratively transferred: 'I was burned by <s>Devadatta</s>.' Similarly, when <s>dharmas</s> undergo the training of abandoning defilements, in dependence on the connection with those [dharmas], a monk is called 'adept' (<s>aśaikṣa</s>).

body.text: mārgastūpāttakāritro nirasyati tadāvṛtim // Abhidh-d_469 //
body.translated_text: But the path, having taken up function, dispels the obstruction of that [defilement]. (Abhidh-d 469)

body.text: 'tu'śabdānnirudhyamāna evetyarthaḥ, vartamānasya hi kriyābandhāt sāmarthyopapatteḥ |
body.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) means 'while ceasing' — for it is reasonable that capacity [arises] from the binding of activity to the present.

body.text: atha yeyamasaṃskṛtā vimuktiḥ ye ca trayo dhātavaḥ prahāṇadhātvādayaḥ, te tataḥ kimanye 'thānanye ? brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: Now, regarding the unconditioned liberation and the three elements — the element of abandonment (<s>prahāṇadhātu</s>) and the rest — are they the same or different [from liberation]? We say:

children.translated_text: That very eternal liberation — that is the three [elements]:

children.text: ākhyātā dhātavaḥ sūtre tridhā bhedo hyapekṣayā // Abhidh-d_470 //
children.translated_text: the elements are declared in the <s>Sūtra</s>; their threefold division is indeed by [difference of] reference. (Abhidh-d 470)

body.text: prajñaptiviśeṣāpekṣayā khalveṣāṃ traividhyamuktam | katham ?
body.translated_text: Their threefold nature is indeed stated with reference to a distinction of designation. How?

children.translated_text: Dispassion (<s>virāga</s>) is release from attachment; that called abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>) is the destruction of the others;
the element of cessation (<s>nirodhadhātu</s>) [is the cessation] of the other things that involve clinging. (Abhidh-d 471)

body.text: rāgaprahāṇaṃ khalu virāgadhāturityucyate | tadanyeṣāṃ kleśopakleśānāṃ prahāṇadhātuḥ | tadanyasya sopādānasya vastunaḥ nirodho nirodhadhāturākhyāyate ||
body.translated_text: The abandonment of attachment is called the element of dispassion (<s>virāgadhātu</s>). The abandonment of other defilements and secondary defilements is the element of abandonment (<s>prahāṇadhātu</s>). The cessation of other things that involve clinging is called the element of cessation (<s>nirodhadhātu</s>).

body.text: yena vastunā nirvidyate virajyate 'pi tena vastunā ? catuṣkoṭikaḥ praśnaḥ | katham ?
body.translated_text: Does one become disenchanted with the same thing from which one also becomes dispassionate? [This is] a fourfold question. How?

children.translated_text: A <s>yogin</s> becomes disenchanted by a cognition that has the objects of suffering and origination;
but one who is attached becomes dispassionate from that — thus [there is] a fourfold classification. (Abhidh-d 472)

body.text: duḥkhasamudayakṣāntibhiḥ tajjñānaiśca nirvidyate, nānyaiḥ | virajyate tu yaḥ saṃraktaḥ sa ca sarvairapi duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgakṣāntijñānairvirajyate yaiḥ kleśān prajahāti | evaṃ catuṣkoṭiko bhavati |
body.translated_text: One becomes disenchanted by the patient acceptances (<s>kṣāntis</s>) and knowledges (<s>jñānas</s>) pertaining to suffering and origination, not by others. But one who is attached — he becomes dispassionate by all the patient acceptances and knowledges pertaining to suffering, origination, cessation, and the path, by which he abandons defilements. Thus a fourfold [classification] arises.

body.text: tatra virvidyata evaṃ kāmavītarāgo niyāmamavakrāman duḥkhasamudayadharmakṣāntibhyāṃ taddharmajñānābhyāṃ ca pūrvaprahīṇatvānna kṣāntibhyāṃ jahātyapratipakṣatvānna jñānābhyāmato na virajyate | bhāvanāmārgepi prayogavimuktiviśeṣāt mārgasaṃgṛhītābhyāṃ duḥkhasamudayajñānābhyāṃ na virajyate vimuktatvānnirviddhavastvālambanatvāttu nirvidyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, one who has become disenchanted and is entering the certainty [of the path] as one free from passion in the desire realm — by the patient acceptances and cognitions pertaining to suffering and origination, because those have been previously abandoned, he does not abandon by the patient acceptances, because they are not the antidote; nor does he become dispassionate by the knowledges — therefore he does not become dispassionate. On the path of cultivation too, because of the distinction of the application and liberation [paths], he does not become dispassionate by the cognitions of suffering and origination included in the path; but because of having the object of what has been examined with disenchantment, he becomes disenchanted though already liberated.

body.text: dvitīyā koṭiḥ- virajyate evāvītarāgaḥ kāmebhyo niyāmamavakrāmannirodhamārgadharmānvayakṣāntibhiḥ bhāvanāmārge ca nirodhamārgajñānaistraidhātukādvairāgyaṃ gacchanna nirvidyate |
body.translated_text: The second alternative: One who is not yet free from passion toward sense-desires, entering the fixed course (<s>niyāma</s>), becomes dispassionate through the patient acceptances of cessation-dharma-cognition, cessation-subsequent-cognition, path-dharma-cognition, and path-subsequent-cognition, and on the path of meditation through cessation and path knowledges, attaining dispassion from the three realms — [such a one] does become dispassionate but does not become disenchanted.

body.text: prāmodyavastvālambanatvādubhayam | vītarāgaḥ kāmebhyo niyāmamavakrāman duḥkhasamudayadharmānvayakṣāntibhirbhāvanāmārge ca duḥkhasamudayajñānaistraidhātukādvairāgyaṃ gacchan |
body.translated_text: [The third alternative:] Both [disenchantment and dispassion arise] because of having objects that are grounds for joy. One free from passion toward sense-desires, entering the fixed course, through the patient acceptances of suffering-dharma-cognition, suffering-subsequent-cognition, origination-dharma-cognition, and origination-subsequent-cognition, and on the path of meditation through suffering and origination knowledges, attaining dispassion from the three realms —

body.text: nobhayam- kāmavītarāgo niyāmamavakrāmannirodhamārgadharmajñānakṣāntibhyāṃ taddharmajñānābhyāṃ ca bhāvanāmārge cānantaryamārgetarābhyāṃ nirodhamārgadharmajñānābhyām ||
body.translated_text: Neither [disenchantment nor dispassion]: One free from passion toward sense-desires, entering the fixed course, through the two patient acceptances of cessation-dharma-cognition and path-dharma-cognition, through the two corresponding dharma-knowledges, and on the path of meditation through cessation and path dharma-knowledges on the uninterrupted path and the [alternative] paths.

body.text: ya ete trayo dhātavastā eva tisraḥ saṃjñāḥ prahāṇavirāganirodhasaṃjñāḥ | vistareṇa tu
body.translated_text: These three realms are themselves the three perceptions — the perceptions of abandonment, dispassion, and cessation. In detail, however —

children.translated_text: The perceptions beginning with the perception of impermanence are ten; from them [arise] those beginning with [the perception of] the impure; (Abhidh-d 473)
three are the path-method, the path, and four — the last triad is the fruit.

body.text: aśubhasaṃjñā maraṇasaṃjñā sarvaloke 'nabhiratisaṃjñā | mārgaprayogastisṛbhirābhiruktaḥ | catasṛbhiśca mārgo 'nityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmasaṃjñābhiḥ | prahāṇavirāganirodhasaṃjñābhiḥ phalamākhyātamiti ||
body.translated_text: The perception of the impure, the perception of death, and the perception of non-delight in all the world — [these three are] declared as the application to the path. By the four — the perceptions of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self — the path [is indicated]. By the perceptions of abandonment, dispassion, and cessation — the fruit is declared.

body.text: kati punarāsāṃ sāsravāḥ katyanāsravāḥ ?
body.translated_text: Now, how many of these have outflows and how many are without outflows?

children.translated_text: The triad beginning with the perception of the impure should be known as having outflows. (Abhidh-d 474)

children.text: samalā nirmalāstvanyā bodhyā nava bhuvo 'malāḥ // Abhidh-d_474 //
children.translated_text: The with-defilement [perceptions] are with outflows; but the others are to be understood as uncontaminated, [present] in nine grounds.

body.text: aśubhā maraṇasarvalokānabhiratisaṃjñāstisraḥ samalāḥ | śeṣāstu sāsravānāsravāḥ, navabhūmikā anāsravā avaboddhavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The three perceptions of the impure, death, and non-delight in the world are with defilement. The rest are both with-outflows and without-outflows; the without-outflows ones are to be understood as [present] in nine grounds.

children.translated_text: In the eleven grounds, the last [perceptions] should be identified in the <s>dhyānas</s> and the rest; (Abhidh-d 475)

children.text: caturthī pañcamī ṣaṣṭhī vidyāt saptasu bhūmiṣu // Abhidh-d_475 //
children.translated_text: the fourth, fifth, and sixth should be known in seven grounds.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāṇaṃ vṛttau ṣaṣṭhasyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the fourth quarter of the sixth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, the commentary called <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>.

body.text: samāptaśca ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The sixth chapter is complete.

body.text: saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: [Beginning of] the seventh chapter.

body.text: prathamaḥ pādaḥ |
body.translated_text: First quarter.

body.text: atrāha | bhagavatoktastriskandho 'yaṃ mārgaḥ | tatra śīlaskandhaḥ karmādhyāye vistareṇa vyākhyātaḥ | samādhiskandho 'ṣṭame 'vyāye vyākhyāyiṣyate | prajñāskandha idānīṃ vyākhyātavyaḥ | so 'yamārabhya-
body.translated_text: Here he says: This path taught by the Blessed One comprises three aggregates [of training]. Therein, the aggregate of moral discipline (<s>śīlaskandha</s>) was explained in detail in the chapter on action. The aggregate of concentration (<s>samādhiskandha</s>) will be explained in the eighth chapter. The aggregate of wisdom (<s>prajñāskandha</s>) is now to be explained. That is commenced:

children.translated_text: This world, confused about reality, is bewildered regarding the truth of the knowable. (Abhidh-d 476)
I shall expound those knowledges, with elaboration of their nature and the rest.

body.text: kāni punastāni kiyanti veti ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: What are those [knowledges] and how many are they? That is stated:

children.translated_text: Setting aside class and substance, and with regard to the antidote and the rest, (Abhidh-d 477)
its division is declared to be tenfold, by names such as <s>dharmajñāna</s> (cognition of the dharma) and so forth.

body.text: jātyāśrayaṇe khalvekatraprasaṅgo dravyāśrayaṇe hyānantyaṃ taccāśakyaṃ vaktum | tasmādubhayametadupekṣya yayāpekṣyayā daśa bhavanti yacca teṣāṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ ca tatsarvaṃ vistareṇa vakṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, if relying on class, there would be the absurd consequence of being limited to one; if relying on substance, there would be infinity — and that cannot be expressed. Therefore, setting aside both, by that regard through which there are ten, and what are their particular and general characteristics — all that we shall explain in detail.

body.text: tatra tāvat-
body.translated_text: Therein, first —

children.translated_text: Two [are specified] by dharma and subsequent [cognitions]; and a tetrad by suffering and the rest. (Abhidh-d 478)
Two by conventional and other-mind [cognitions]; and a pair by destruction and non-arising.

body.text: dharmānvayajñāne khalu dharmānvayābhyāmeva viśeṣyete | duḥkhādīni tu catvāri svaviṣayaireva caturbhirāryasatyaiḥ viśeṣyante | saṃvṛtyā paracittena ca saṃvṛtiparacittajñāne viśeṣyete | kṣayeṇāpunarutpattyā ca kṣayānutpādajñānadvayaṃ viśiṣyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Dharmajñāna</s> (cognition of the dharma) and <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent cognition) are indeed specified by 'dharma' and 'subsequent' [respectively]. The four — suffering and the rest — are specified by their own objects, the four noble truths. The conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) and other-mind (<s>paracitta</s>) knowledges are specified by convention and other minds [respectively]. And the pair of destruction-knowledge (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and non-arising-knowledge (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>) is specified by destruction and non-rebirth.

body.text: athavā
body.translated_text: Or alternatively —

children.translated_text: By antidote, effort, intrinsic nature, aspects, objects, (Abhidh-d 479)
function, and accumulation — their arrangement is to be understood.

body.text: tatra kāmadhātuvipakṣapratipakṣo dharmajñānam | rūpārūpyāvacaravipakṣapratipakṣo 'nvayajñānam | prayogataḥ paracittajñānaṃ cittaṃ jñāsyāmīti tatprayogāt | svabhāvataḥ saṃvṛtijñānaṃ pipīlikādiṣvapi tadbhāvāt | satyākārairgocaraiścatvāri (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 375)

knowledges. By function: destruction-knowledge, because of the completion of function. By accumulation of causes: non-arising-knowledge, because of the accumulation of homogeneous causes by all uncontaminated knowledges.

body.translated_text: Therein, <s>dharmajñāna</s> is the antidote opposed to the adversary in the desire realm. <s>Anvayajñāna</s> is the antidote opposed to the adversary in the form and formless realms. By effort: other-mind knowledge [arises] from the effort 'I shall know [another's] mind.' By intrinsic nature: conventional knowledge, because it exists even in ants and the like. By the aspects of truth and objects: four

children.translated_text: For the purpose of removing confusion regarding realms, truths, objects, and minds, (Abhidh-d 480)

children.text: saṃmohasya nivṛttyarthaṃ tadbhedo daśadhaiva vā // Abhidh-d_480 //
children.translated_text: regarding arising, perishing, and non-rebirth — its division is tenfold alone.

body.text: tatra dhātusaṃmoho dvābhyāṃ dharmānvayajñānābhyāṃ nivartyate | satyasaṃmohaścaturbhiḥ duḥkhajñānādibhiḥ | arthasaṃmohaḥ saṃvṛtijñānena | cittasaṃmohaḥ paracittajñānena | jātisaṃmohaḥ kṣayajñānena | punarutpattisaṃmoho 'nutpādajñāneneti daśaiva jñānāni bhagavānavocat | nātibhūyāṃsi nālpīyāṃsīti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, confusion regarding realms is removed by the two — <s>dharmajñāna</s> and <s>anvayajñāna</s>. Confusion regarding truths — by the four beginning with suffering-knowledge. Confusion regarding objects — by conventional knowledge. Confusion regarding minds — by other-mind knowledge. Confusion regarding arising — by destruction-knowledge. Confusion regarding re-arising — by non-arising-knowledge. Thus the Blessed One taught exactly ten knowledges — neither more nor fewer.

body.text: atra punaḥ
body.translated_text: Here, moreover —

body.text: parijñātādyavagamaḥ duḥkhādau kṣayadhī phalam // Abhidh-d_481 //
body.translated_text: The understanding of 'fully known' and the rest is the fruit of the destruction-cognition regarding suffering and the rest. (Abhidh-d 481)

body.text: "dukhaṃ parijñātaṃ samudayo me prahīṇaḥ,................
body.translated_text: 'Suffering has been fully known, origination has been abandoned by me,...............

body.text: ..............miti vādavipakṣeṇa vā anārambhiṇāṃ saṃsāreṇaiva śuddhiriti vādavipakṣeṇa pratipadākāraḥ | laukikavairāgyamārgamārasaṃjñāvipakṣeṇa vā anātyantikavairāgyagamanavipralambhāt sarvatrābahumānavipakṣeṇa nairyāṇikākāraḥ ||
body.translated_text: ..............or, opposing the view that purification comes through <s>saṃsāra</s> alone without effort — the aspect of 'practice' [is taught]. Opposing the worldly path of dispassion, the perception of <s>Māra</s> — or, because of the deception of going to non-ultimate dispassion — opposing disrespect everywhere — the aspect of 'leading-out' [is taught].

body.text: athākāro nāma ka eṣa dharmaḥ | kiṃ vā tenākāryata iti ? tadubhayaṃ nirdiśyate-
body.translated_text: Now, what is this dharma called 'aspect' (<s>ākāra</s>)? Or, what is 'aspected' (<s>ākāryate</s>) by it? Both are indicated:

body.text: dhīrākāraḥ sadākāryaṃ sākārāstvavalambinaḥ // Abhidh-d_482 //
body.translated_text: Wisdom is the aspect; what exists is always aspected; those that are 'with-aspect' are apprehenders [of objects]. (Abhidh-d 482)

body.text: prajñā khalvākāra ityucyate | na tarhi prajñā sākārā bhavati dvayoḥ prajñayoḥ yaugapadyābhāvāt | tataśca na sarve caitasikāḥ sākārāḥ prāpnuvanti | na khalu brū maḥ prajñāsaṃprayogātsākārā vaikākārā vā | kiṃ tarhi ? svavṛttibhirākaraṇādālambanagrahaṇādityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is indeed called the 'aspect.' Then wisdom itself would not be 'with-aspect' — because two wisdoms cannot exist simultaneously. Consequently, not all mental factors would be 'with-aspect.' But we do not say [they are 'with-aspect'] because of association with wisdom, or [because they are] of a single aspect. What then? Because they aspect [objects] through their own activities — [that is,] because of grasping objects — that is the meaning.

body.text: kiṃ punastadākāryam ? sadākāryam | yatkiñcid dravyataḥ prajñaptito vā vidyate tadākāryate | cittacaittāstu sākārāḥ viṣayagrāhiṇa ityarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What, then, is 'aspected'? What exists is always aspected. Whatever exists, whether substantially or by designation — that is aspected. Mind and mental factors are 'with-aspect' — meaning they are apprehenders of objects.

body.text: kiṃ punarjñānaṃ kati smṛtyupasthānāni ?
body.translated_text: Now, knowledge — how many foundations of mindfulness [does it comprise]?

children.translated_text: Other-mind knowledge — three; cessation-cognition — the dharma-[foundation]; (Abhidh-d 483)
four foundations of mindfulness — the remaining knowledges are [so] held.

body.text: paracittajñānaṃ khalu trīṇi vedanācittadharmākhyāni | nirodhajñānaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānam | paracittanirodhajñānābhyāmanyāni jñānāni catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni ||
body.translated_text: Other-mind knowledge indeed [comprises] three [foundations] — called feeling, mind, and dharmas. Cessation-knowledge is [only] the foundation of mindfulness on dharmas. Other knowledges apart from other-mind and cessation knowledge [comprise] four foundations of mindfulness.

body.text: atha katamasya jñānasya kati jñānānyālambanam ?
body.translated_text: Now, how many knowledges are the object of which knowledge?

body.text: mārgadharmānvayajñānagocaro navaśo dhiyaḥ // Abhidh-d_484 //
body.translated_text: The domain of path, dharma, and subsequent knowledges is nine [knowledges] each. (Abhidh-d 484)

body.text: mārgadharmānvayajñānānāṃ pratyekaṃ navajñānānyālambanam | mārgajñānasya tāvatsaṃvṛtijñānaṃ hitvā | dharmajñānasyānvayajñānam | anvayajñānasya dharmajñānam |
body.translated_text: Each of path-knowledge, dharma-knowledge, and subsequent-knowledge has nine knowledges as its object. For path-knowledge — excluding conventional knowledge. For dharma-knowledge — [excluding] subsequent-knowledge. For subsequent-knowledge — [excluding] dharma-knowledge.

body.text: duḥkhahetudhiyordve dve
body.translated_text: For suffering and origination cognitions — two each. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: duḥkhasamudayajñānayoḥ saṃvṛtijñānaṃ sāsravaṃ ca paracittajñānamālambanam |
body.translated_text: Suffering-knowledge and origination-knowledge have as their objects: conventional knowledge and other-mind knowledge with outflows.

body.text: caturṇāṃ daśa
body.translated_text: For [the remaining] four — ten. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: saṃvṛtiparacittakṣayānutpādajñānānāṃ sarvāṇyeva daśajñānānyālambanam |
body.translated_text: For conventional, other-mind, destruction, and non-arising knowledges, all ten knowledges are their object.

body.text: nāparam ||
body.translated_text: Nothing beyond [ten]. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: nirodhajñānaṃ khalu naiva jñānālambanam ||
body.translated_text: Cessation-knowledge indeed has no knowledge as its object [because it takes the unconditioned Nirvāṇa as object].

body.text: punarapi daśadharmān sthāpayitvā kasya jñānasya kati dharmā viṣaya iti vācyam | katham ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Furthermore, having established ten dharmas, it must be stated: which knowledge has how many dharmas as its objects? How? That is stated:

children.translated_text: Dividing the five dharmas — those belonging to three realms, those of the nature of the path, and the permanent ones — (Abhidh-d 485)
into two each, for the purpose of instruction, one should show the domain of knowledge.

body.text: traidhātukān dharmān pratyekaṃ dvidhā kṛtvā saṃprayuktā viprayuktāśca, apratisaṃyuktāṃśca dvidhā kṛtvā saṃyuktaviprayuktabhedenaiva, asaṃskṛtamapi dvidhākṛtvā kuśalāvyākṛtabhedenaivaṃ kṛtvā daśa bhavanti |
body.translated_text: Dividing the dharmas of the three realms each into two — associated and disjoined — and dividing the non-conjoined ones also into two by the distinction of conjoined and disjoined, and dividing the unconditioned also into two by the distinction of wholesome and indeterminate — thus done, there are ten.

body.text: tatra tāvatsaṃvṛtijñānasya sarva eva daśadharmā viṣayaḥ | dharmajñānasya pañca (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 378)

children.text: ) kāmapratisaṃyuktānāsravāḥ saṃprayuktaviprayuktākuśalaṃ cāsaṃskṛtam | anvayajñānasya sapta rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktānāsravāḥ saṃprayuktaviprayuktakuśalaṃ cāsaṃskṛtam | paracittajñānasya trayaḥ kāmarūpapratisaṃyuktānāsravāsaṃprayuktā eva | duḥkhasamudayajñānayoḥ ṣaṭkāmarūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktāsaṃprayuktaviprayuktāḥ | nirodhajñānasyaiko 'saṃskṛtameva kuśalam | mārgajñānasya dvāvanāsravaḥ saṃprayukto viprayuktaśca | kṣayānutpādajñānayornava dharmā viṣayo 'saṃskṛtamavyākṛtaṃ muktvā ||
children.translated_text: the desire-realm conjoined, the uncontaminated — associated and disjoined — the unwholesome, and the unconditioned. For subsequent-knowledge — seven: the form and formless realm conjoined, the uncontaminated — associated and disjoined — the wholesome, and the unconditioned. For other-mind knowledge — three: the desire-realm and form-realm conjoined and the uncontaminated — associated only. For suffering and origination knowledges — six: the desire, form, and formless realm conjoined — associated, disjoined, and non-conjoined. For cessation-knowledge — one: only the unconditioned wholesome. For path-knowledge — two: the uncontaminated associated and disjoined. For destruction and non-arising knowledges — nine dharmas as objects, excluding the indeterminate unconditioned.

body.translated_text: Therein, first: all ten dharmas are the object of conventional knowledge. For dharma-knowledge — five:

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | kaḥ katibhirjñānaiḥ samanvāgataḥ ? sarvastāvatpṛthagjanaḥ saṃvṛtijñānenaiva | ayaṃ tu niyamaḥ-
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: Who possesses how many knowledges? Every ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) possesses only conventional knowledge. But this is the rule:

body.text: dṛṅmārge prathame jñāne tribhirjñānaiḥ samanvitaḥ /
body.translated_text: On the path of seeing, at the first knowledge, one possesses three knowledges. (Abhidh-d 486)

body.text: dvitīyakṣaṇe tribhiḥ saṃvṛtijñānaduḥkhajñānadharmajñānaiḥ |
body.translated_text: At the second moment — [one possesses] three: conventional knowledge, suffering-knowledge, and dharma-knowledge.

body.text: caturṣvekaikavṛddhyordhvaṃ virakto 'nyamano dhiyā // Abhidh-d_486 //
body.translated_text: In four [moments], with an increase of one each — above that, one free from passion [possesses] also other-mind knowledge. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: ataḥ paraṃ caturṣu cittakṣaṇeṣvekaikaṃ jñānaṃ vardhate | tadyathā duḥkhe 'nvayajñāne 'nvayajñānaṃ vardhate | samudayadharmajñāne samudayajñānam | nirodhadharmajñāne nirodhadharmajñānam | mārgadharmajñāne mārgadharmajñānaṃ vardhate | samudayanirodhamārgānvayajñāneṣu kṣāntiṣu ca nāstyapūrvajñānavṛddhiḥ | sarvatra tu vītarāgasya paracittajñānaṃ vardhata iti vācyam ||
body.translated_text: Thereafter, in four mind-moments, one knowledge increases each [time]. Namely: at the subsequent-cognition of suffering, subsequent-knowledge increases. At the dharma-cognition of origination, origination-knowledge [increases]. At the dharma-cognition of cessation, cessation-dharma-knowledge [increases]. At the dharma-cognition of the path, path-dharma-knowledge increases. At the subsequent-cognitions of origination, cessation, and path, and at the patient acceptances (<s>kṣāntis</s>), there is no increase of a new knowledge. But everywhere, for one already free from passion, other-mind knowledge increases — this should be stated.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau saptamasyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the first quarter of the seventh chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, the commentary called <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>.

body.text: saptamādhyāye
body.translated_text: In the seventh chapter,

body.text: dvitīyapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: second quarter.

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | kasyāṃ bhūmau kasyāṃ vāvasthāyāṃ kasya vā pudgalasya kati jñānāni bhāvyante ? tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: In which ground, or in which stage, or for which person, how many knowledges are cultivated? That is commenced:

children.translated_text: In dispassion from [the first] three <s>dhyānas</s> and the desire [realm], on the last path of liberation, (Abhidh-d 487)
and in the preparatory [path] for the principal <s>dhyānas</s> — the future cultivation is to be understood.
For an ordinary person, in the production of the foundations of mindfulness, <s>dhyānas</s>, and the rest, likewise (Abhidh-d 488)
on the preparatory and liberation paths — [the future cultivation] of conventional and other-mind knowledges.

body.text: bālasya khalvādyadhyānatrayavairāgye paścime vimuktimārge mauladhyānaprayogamārge ca smṛtyupasthānādikuśalamūlotpādane ca prayogavimuktimārge ca saṃvṛtijñānasya paracittajñānasya cānāgatabhāvanā veditavyā ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, for an ordinary person — in dispassion from the first three <s>dhyānas</s> and [the desire realm], on the last path of liberation, on the preparatory path for the principal <s>dhyānas</s>, in the production of wholesome roots of the foundations of mindfulness and the like, and on the preparatory and liberation paths — the future cultivation of conventional knowledge and other-mind knowledge is to be understood.

body.text: āryasya tu
body.translated_text: But for the noble one —

body.text: kṣāntijñānāni bhāvyante svajātīyāni dṛkpathe /
body.translated_text: On the path of seeing, the patient acceptances and knowledges of one's own class are cultivated. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: darśanamārge khalu yadyeva saṃmukhībhūtaṃ bhavati kṣāntirvā jñānaṃ vā tajjātīyamevānāgataṃ bhāvyate | nānyajātīyamanyaviṣayaṃ vā pṛthakkāryatvāt |
body.translated_text: Indeed, on the path of seeing, whichever comes face-to-face — whether a patient acceptance or a knowledge — only one of the same class that is future is cultivated, not one of a different class or different object, because their functions are separate.

body.text: sāṃvṛtaṃ cānvayajñāne duḥkhahetusamāhvaye // Abhidh-d_489 //
body.translated_text: And conventional [knowledge is cultivated] at the subsequent-cognitions of suffering and origination. (Abhidh-d 489)

body.text: saṃvṛtijñānaṃ khalu darśanamārge triṣu citteṣu duḥkhasamudayanirodhānvayajñānākhyeṣu bhāvyate | na dharmajñāneṣu, akṛtārthatvādālambanākāraparijayo hi nādyāpi parisamāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, conventional knowledge on the path of seeing is cultivated in three mind-moments — called the subsequent-cognitions of suffering, origination, and cessation. Not at the dharma-cognitions — because the task is not yet complete, for the familiarization with object and aspect is not yet accomplished.

body.text: kasmātpunaḥ saṃvṛtijñāna tatra bhāvanāṃ gacchati ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: But why does conventional knowledge undergo cultivation there? That is stated:

body.text: samānapratipakṣatvātteṣu mārgāyitatvataḥ /
body.translated_text: Because of being a similar antidote, and because [those moments] serve as path for it. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: yathaivānvayakṣāntijñānāni trīṇi tatprahātavyakleśapratipakṣaḥ, tathā tānyapi saṃvṛtijñānāni pratipakṣaḥ | tairapi tatra mārgāyitaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyāvasthāyām |
body.translated_text: Just as the three subsequent patient acceptances and knowledges (<s>anvayakṣāntijñāna</s>) are the counteragent of the afflictions to be abandoned by those [truths], so too those conventional knowledges (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>) are [their] counteragent. By those too, there was path-practice in the stage of the penetrative factors (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>).

body.text: ato 'bhisamayātyākhyaṃ tattrisatyāntalābhataḥ // Abhidh-d_490 //
body.translated_text: Therefore, it is designated as 'pertaining to full comprehension' (<s>abhisamaya</s>), because of its attainment at the end of the three truths. (Abhidh-d 490)

body.text: ata eva tadābhisamayāntikaṃ saṃvṛtijñānamityākhyāyate | dharmajñāneṣu khalu tadbhāvanāyāmabhisamayamadhyāni syuriti | taccaitadanutpattidharmakamapi saddharmatayā cintyate |
body.translated_text: For precisely this reason, that conventional knowledge is designated as 'pertaining to full comprehension.' For in the cultivation of the <s>dharmajñānas</s> (cognitions of the dharma), it would be in the midst of the full comprehension. And this, even though it is of the nature of non-arising, is considered as belonging to the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: kasmātpunastadanutpattidharmakameva ? śraddhādharmānusāryāśrayeṇa tadutpattipratibaddhatvāt | darśanamārge ca saṃmukhībhūte tannotpannam | tasmādanutpattikadharmameva bhāvanāṃ gacchati | tatpunaretatsaptabhūmikaṃ kāmāvacaraṃ darśanamārgasamānabhūmikaṃ ca | uktā darśanamārgabhāvanā ||
body.translated_text: Why, moreover, is it only of the nature of non-arising? Because its arising is dependent on the basis of one who follows through faith (<s>śraddhānusārin</s>), and when the path of seeing comes face-to-face, it has not arisen. Therefore, it is only of the non-arising nature that enters cultivation. This, moreover, is of seven levels, belongs to the desire realm, and is of the same level as the path of seeing. The cultivation of the path of seeing has been stated.

body.text: bhāvanāmārge vaktavyā |
body.translated_text: The path of cultivation is now to be stated.

body.text: mārgākhye tvanvayajñāne ṣaḍ bhāvyante 'tha sapta vā /
body.translated_text: In the subsequent knowledge of the path (<s>mārgānvayajñāna</s>), six or seven [knowledges] are cultivated.

body.text: ṣoḍaśetu vartamānānvayajñānacitte bhāvanāvartmanyavītarāgasya ṣaḍ bhāvyante | saṃvṛtiparacittakṣayānutpādajñānāni hitvā | vītarāgasya tu saptānāgatāni bhāvyante paracittajñānaṃ vardhayitvā |
body.translated_text: At the sixteenth [moment] — the present mental moment of the subsequent knowledge — on the path of cultivation, for one not yet free from passion, six [knowledges] are cultivated, excluding conventional knowledge, knowledge of others' minds, and the knowledges of exhaustion and non-arising. But for one already free from passion, seven future ones are cultivated, with the addition of the knowledge of others' minds.

body.text: ānantaryapathe corddhvaṃ bhāvyate nānyacittadhīḥ // Abhidh-d_491 //
body.translated_text: On the uninterrupted path and above, the knowledge of others' minds is not cultivated. (Abhidh-d 491)

body.text: sarāgasyāpi bhāvanāmārge tasmāt ṣoḍaśātkṣaṇādūrdhvaṃ yāvatkāme vīta rāgo bhavati tāvatsarveṣu prayogānantaryavimuktiviśeṣamārgeṣu sapta jñānāni bhāvyante | anyatra paracitakṣayānutpādajñānebhyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Even for one with passion, on the path of cultivation — from that sixteenth moment onward, as long as one becomes free from passion in the desire realm — in all the preparatory, uninterrupted, liberation, and distinction paths, seven knowledges are cultivated, except for the knowledges of others' minds, of exhaustion, and of non-arising.

children.translated_text: In the paths of abandonment and liberation — except for the liberation [path] of the last [stage] —
there is no cultivation of conventional [knowledge], because it is the counteragent of the Summit of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). (Abhidh-d 492)

body.text: dhyānacatuṣṭvārūpyatrayavairāgye pañcasvabhijñāsu, akopyāprativedhe ca vyavakīrṇabhāvite ca dhyāne | śaikṣasya sarveṣvānantaryavimuktimārgeṣu saptaiva jñānāni ............. |
body.translated_text: In the dispassion from the four <s>dhyānas</s> and the three formless [attainments], in the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), in the attainment of the immovable (<s>akopya</s>), and in the alternating cultivation of <s>dhyāna</s> — for a learner, in all the uninterrupted and liberation paths, seven knowledges alone .............

body.text: ........abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau saptamasyādhyāyasya dvitīyapādaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: ........ End of the second section of the seventh chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: saptamādhyāye
body.translated_text: Seventh chapter,

body.text: tṛtīyapādaḥ |.....
body.translated_text: third section. .....

body.text: .........sthānavastuhetuvipākaprativistarairboddhavyam | tatrātītānāgate pratyutpanne ca tadākṣeptākṣepavaicitryaṃ pratikarmasamādānaṃ (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 383)

children.text: ) bhavati | kiciddhi sahasā pratyayavaśātkriyate | kiñcid dṛṣṭacetasā | kiñcitpunaḥ samādāya kriyate tena karmaṇā mayā jīvitavyamiti | tathā dharmo 'yamadharmo veti samādāyāsamādāya karoti | sthānādipravibhāgataśca gāmbhīryaṃ boddhavyam | tatra sthānamāyatyutpattyāyattānāmavakāśakāraṇāt | heturapi yena hetunā kriyate | yathoktam- "vastu sthānādhikaraṇamucyate | sādhikaraṇaṃ vastu sthānam | tadyathā prāṇivadhakarmaṇaḥ svabhāvaḥ | sa ca prāṇī yasya cārthe vadhyate yayā pratyayasāmagryā sarvametadvastu sambhavati | kutaḥ ? sthānahetuvipākānāṃ pṛthagukteḥ | yasya khalvetat sthānaṃ yaccāsya sthānaṃ kriyate yasya tatkarma hetuḥ, yaddhetukaṃ ca tat, ayaṃ cāsya karmaṇo vipāko 'yamanyasya" iti | tadetadaṣṭajñānasvabhāvaṃ nirodhamārgajñāne hitvā ||
children.translated_text: occurs [in various ways]. For some [action] is done suddenly, under the influence of conditions. Some is done with a discerning mind. Some, moreover, is done by undertaking [the resolve]: 'By this action I shall live.' Likewise, [one acts] having undertaken [the thought] 'this is dharma, this is adharma,' or without undertaking [such thought]. And the profundity should be understood from the detailed division of ground and the like. There, 'ground' — because of providing the occasion for those whose arising depends on future birth. 'Cause' also — the cause by which [the action] is done. As stated: 'The object is called the ground and basis. A grounded object is the ground. For example, the intrinsic nature of the action of killing a living being — and that living being for whose sake [another] is killed, and the assemblage of conditions by which all this occurs. Why? Because of the separate statement of ground, cause, and maturation. For one for whom this is the ground, and that which is made into his ground — the <s>karma</s> that is its cause, and that of which it is the cause — this is the maturation of that <s>karma</s>, and that of another' — and so on. This has the nature of eight knowledges, excluding the knowledges of cessation and the path.

body.translated_text: ......... should be understood through the detailed exposition of ground, object, cause, and maturation. There, regarding the past, future, and present — the variety of its projection and non-projection, the undertaking of the action

children.translated_text: That which operates without obstruction regarding the intrinsic nature and the like of the <s>dhyānas</s> and so forth —
that, called the knowledge of <s>dhyāna</s> and so forth, is the power comprised of nine knowledges. (Abhidh-d 493)

body.text: dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpatti jñānabalaṃ khalu yatsaṃkleśavyavadānavyavasthānaviśuddhiṣu nivṛttipakṣe dhyānānāṃ vimokṣāṇāṃ samādhīnāṃ samāpattīnāṃ ca saṃkleśavyavadānavyavasthānaviśuddhiṣu yadbalamavyāhatam | tatra saṃkleśādicatuṣṭayaṃ hānaviśeṣasthitinirvedhabhāgīyaṃ sāsvādaśuddhakānāsravādibhedāt | tadetaddhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalaṃ navajñānātmakaṃ boddhavyam ||
body.translated_text: The power of knowledge of <s>dhyāna</s>, liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), and attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>) — regarding their defilement, purification, establishment, and complete purity — that unobstructed power, on the side of cessation, regarding defilement, purification, establishment, and complete purity of the <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, concentrations, and attainments. There, the fourfold [classification] of defilement and the like corresponds to decline, distinction, stability, and the penetrative factor, from the division of savored, pure, uncontaminated, and the like. This power of knowledge of <s>dhyāna</s>, liberations, concentrations, and attainments should be understood as having the nature of nine knowledges.

children.translated_text: That which operates in the discernment of the mildness and the like of beings' faculties —
the power of knowledge of the superior and inferior among faculties — that is comprised of nine cognitions. (Abhidh-d 494)

body.text: indriyaparāparajñānabalam yatsarvasattvānāṃ śreyaḥprāptiśaktitraividhye jñānamavyāhataṃ tadindriyaparāparajñānabalaṃ navajñānātmakaṃ nirodhajñānaṃ hitvā ||
body.translated_text: The power of knowledge of the superior and inferior among faculties — the unobstructed knowledge regarding the threefold [classification of] the capacity of all beings to attain the supreme — that power of knowledge of the superior and inferior among faculties has the nature of nine knowledges, excluding the knowledge of cessation.

children.translated_text: That which operates regarding the threefold [classification] of beings' predominant inclinations into inferior and the rest —
the power named 'knowledge of diverse dispositions' (<s>nānādhimukti</s>) — that too has nine [knowledges] as its nature. (Abhidh-d 495)

body.text: yatkhalu sarvasattvānāṃ hīnamadhyamottamādhimuktiṣvavyāhataṃ jñānaṃ tacca nānādhimuktijñānabalaṃ navajñānātmakameva nirodhajñānaṃ hitvā ||
body.translated_text: The unobstructed knowledge regarding the inferior, middling, and superior dispositions of all beings — that power of knowledge of diverse dispositions has the nature of nine knowledges alone, excluding the knowledge of cessation.

children.translated_text: That which, with reference to diverse elements (<s>dhātu</s>), operates for the benefit of beings —
comprised of nine knowledges, similarly — that is the power of knowledge of diverse elements. (Abhidh-d 496)

body.text: te punaḥ pūrvābhyāsavāsanādhātavaḥ pūrvajanmasu guṇadoṣavidyāśilpakarmābhyāsebhyo yā vāsanāstāḥ khalviha dhātavo viśeṣeṇa boddhavyāḥ | gotrārthenāvasthānāṃ ta evāśayā ityavagantavyāḥ, tadvaśāccaratītyucyate | uktaṃ ca bhagavatā- "dhātuśaḥ sattvāḥ saṃsyandante" iti ||
body.translated_text: Those elements (<s>dhātu</s>) — the latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) from habitual practice in previous lives — the latent impressions from the cultivation of virtues, faults, knowledge, arts, and actions in former births — these elements should be understood here particularly. In the sense of lineage (<s>gotra</s>), those same dispositions (<s>āśaya</s>) should be understood as the basis of [different] states, and one is said to 'conduct [oneself]' under their influence. As the Blessed One said: 'Beings flow together according to their elements.'

children.translated_text: That which knows the distinctions of destiny, dharma, and the noble [ones], through the distinction of conditions —
that is the power of knowledge called 'the practice leading everywhere' (<s>sarvatragāminī pratipat</s>), [comprised of] ten cognitions. (Abhidh-d 497)

body.text: yatkhalu sattvopapattinirvartakeṣu tatkṣayakareṣu ca dharmeṣu jñānamavyāhataṃ tatsarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabalam | bhavyaviśeṣauṣadhavad draṣṭavyam | mokṣabhavyānāṃ nānādhātūnāṃ sattvānāmanekadhātūnāṃ sarvakleśaprahāṇāyauṣadhaviśeṣavatsāmānyapratipakṣaviśeṣapratipakṣaṃ ca sarvatra jānīte gatihetuṃ cānena dhāturekasantāne yo yadgatacittastadvaśena tadavataraṇabhavyo 'bhavyaśca bhavati tatsarvaṃ yathāvatpratijānātīti sarvākārajñatāpyuktā bhavati | tadetat saphalamārgaprahāṇāddaśajñānātmakaṃ bhavati | kecittu kevalamārgagrahaṇānnavajñānātmakam ||
body.translated_text: The unobstructed knowledge regarding the dharmas that bring about beings' rebirth and those that bring about their cessation — that is the power of knowledge of the practice leading everywhere. It should be viewed like a special medicine for [curing] potent [diseases]. For beings of diverse elements who are capable of liberation, with diverse elements — for the abandonment of all afflictions, [the Buddha] knows everywhere both the general counteragent and the specific counteragent, like a special medicine. And by this [power] he knows, regarding a single continuum, which element — based on the mind that has gone where — makes one capable or incapable of entering that [state]. He knows all this as it truly is — thus omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) is also affirmed. This, because of the inclusion of the path that bears fruit, has the nature of ten knowledges.
