Some, however, [say it has] nine knowledges, because of the inclusion of the path alone.

children.translated_text: That which examines one's own and others' past births — the conventional knowledge —
the power of knowledge of the recollection of past births — that is held to include the [path] that bears fruit. (Abhidh-d 498)

body.text: svaparasantā nikānāmatītajanmaparamparāṇāṃ vicitrasukhaduḥkheṣu prāṇiṣvayamamuṣyakarmaṇo vipāko 'yamamuṣyasvapnanimittadhyāyimanasikāracihnārthāvadhāraṇavadanekavidhasambandhāvabodhavaśitvamasya sūcitaṃ bhavati | yathā khalu bhavyārthasūcakān svapnānanekaśo dṛṣṭvā tāṃścārthānabhiniṣpannān prāyaśaḥ sadṛśānapekṣya niścayo bhavati tadvaditi | yathā ca dhyāyināṃ manasikāreṣu dharmacihnānyutpadyante taiśca suvyakto dharmaparicchedo bhavati | tadvatsarvadharmeṣu mudrā bhagavato viditā | kiṃ punastatkarma vipākasambandhamudrāsviti ? tadetadbalaṃ saṃvṛtijñānātmakameva ||
body.translated_text: Regarding the succession of past births of one's own and others' continua — among beings with diverse happiness and suffering — 'this is the maturation of this one's action; this is the meaning ascertained through dreams, omens, meditative attention, and signs for that one' — the mastery of comprehending manifold connections of this kind has been indicated. Just as, having observed dreams that indicate future events on many occasions, and seeing those events come to pass mostly in a similar manner, one attains certainty — in that way. And just as for meditators, dharma-signs arise in their acts of attention, and through those, a clear discernment of dharmas occurs — similarly, the seals (<s>mudrā</s>) of all dharmas are known by the Blessed One. How much more so the seals of the connection between <s>karma</s> and maturation? This power has the nature of conventional knowledge alone.

children.translated_text: That knowledge which operates regarding the death and rebirth of beings, [extending to] other time-periods —
that is called the power of knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutyutpatti</s>), as stated before. (Abhidh-d 499)

body.text: divyacakṣurāśrayācca jñānātkarmaphalavaicitryacaritāvataraṇajñānaparapratyayo bhavati | pratyutpannaviṣayamapyevam | taddivyacakṣurāśrayajñānaṃ saha praṇidhijñānenāparānte prabhāvyate | tadetatsaṃvṛtijñānātmakameva ||
body.translated_text: And from the knowledge based on the divine eye, one obtains confirmation from others regarding the variety of <s>karma</s>-fruit and the entry into [various] modes of conduct. [This applies] to present objects as well. That knowledge based on the divine eye, together with the knowledge born of aspiration (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>), has its power in the future. This too has the nature of conventional knowledge alone.

body.text: āsravakṣayadhīsaṃjñaṃ ṣaḍjñānānyathavā daśa /
body.translated_text: The [power] called 'knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows' (<s>āsravakṣayajñāna</s>) is of six knowledges, or alternatively ten.

body.text: ata idānīṃ bhagavato vineyakāryaṃ kimavaśiṣṭam ? āsravakṣayaḥ | tasminyajjñānaṃ yasya yadā yairavataraṇadeśanāvidhibhirakṛcchreṇa saṃpadyate tadbhagavān sarvākāramanena jñānena vetti nānyaḥ kaścit | ato 'syaiva tadbalaṃ nānyasya | tatpunaretat ṣaḍjñānasvabhāvaṃ daśātmakaṃ vā | yadyāsravakṣaye jñānam, ṣaḍbhavanti | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 387)

children.text: ) paracittaduḥkhasamudayamārgajñānāni hitvā | atha sopāye kṣaye jñānaṃ darśanaṃ bhavati, daśajñānāni bhavanti |
children.translated_text: excluding the knowledges of others' minds, suffering, origination, and the path. But if the knowledge [extends to] the means for exhaustion, the seeing and [knowledge] — then there are ten knowledges.

body.translated_text: Now then, what task remains for the Blessed One regarding those to be trained? The exhaustion of outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>). Regarding that — the knowledge of who, when, and by what methods of entry and instruction [the exhaustion] is effortlessly accomplished — the Blessed One knows all this completely through this knowledge; no one else [does]. Therefore, this is his power alone, and not another's. This, moreover, has the nature of six knowledges, or of ten. If the knowledge is [only] regarding the exhaustion of outflows, there are six —

body.text: ukto daśabalasvabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: The intrinsic nature of the ten powers has been stated.

body.text: ākāraniyamo vaktavyaḥ | so 'yamucyate-
body.translated_text: The restriction of aspects must be stated. That is now stated:

body.text: ṣoḍaśākāramatrādyamanyaiścāpyuttaraṃ bhuvā // Abhidh-d_500 //
body.translated_text: The first [power] here has sixteen aspects; the rest too, above — with [different numbers of] levels. (Abhidh-d 500)

children.translated_text: The seventh is of sixteen aspects; a pair has undifferentiated aspects.

children.text: aṣṭākāraṃ dvitīyaṃ tu navajñānamayaṃ tu yat // Abhidh-d_501 //
children.translated_text: The second has eight aspects; but whatever is comprised of nine knowledges — (Abhidh-d 501)

body.text: tathāgatabalaṃ proktaṃ tajjñeyaṃ dvādaśākṛti /
body.translated_text: that <s>Tathāgata</s> power, it should be known, has twelve aspects.

body.text: sthānāsthānajñānabalaṃ ṣoḍaśabhirākāraiḥ pravartate | anyaiśca tannirmuktairāsravakṣayajñānabalamapi yadi sopāyaṃ kṣayaṃ vivakṣati tadapi ṣoḍaśākāram | atha kṣayamātraṃ tat, ṣaḍjñānamayairākāraiḥ sarvatragāminīṃ pratipajjñānabalaṃ saptamaṃ tadapi tathaiva ṣoḍaśākāram | dvayaṃ tu pūrvenivāsānusmṛticyutyupapattijñānabalamavibhaktākārabalam | dvitīyaṃ tu karmavipākajñānabalamaṣṭākāram | yattu samādhisamāpattijñānabalaṃ tasya navajñānasvabhāvaṃ taireva dvādaśabhirākāraiḥ pravartate | anyadyannoktaṃ tadabhyūhyam |
body.translated_text: The power of knowledge of ground and non-ground (<s>sthānāsthānajñāna</s>) operates with sixteen aspects. The power of knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows, as well — with those same other [aspects excluded]: if it intends the exhaustion together with its means, it too has sixteen aspects. But if [it intends] the exhaustion alone, [then it operates] with the aspects comprised of six knowledges. The seventh — the power of knowledge of the practice leading everywhere — that too likewise has sixteen aspects. The pair — the powers of knowledge of past-life recollection and of death-and-rebirth — are powers with undifferentiated aspects. The second — the power of knowledge of <s>karma</s> and maturation — has eight aspects. The power of knowledge of <s>dhyāna</s>, concentration, and attainment, which has the nature of nine knowledges, operates with those same twelve aspects. What else has not been stated should be inferred.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ kiṃ gocaram ?
body.translated_text: What, moreover, is the domain of each [power]?

body.text: sarvagocaramatrādyamantyaṃ śāntyavalambi vā // Abhidh-d_502 //
body.translated_text: The first has all [dharmas] as its domain; the last rests on peace (i.e., <s>nirvāṇa</s>), or [on all four truths]. (Abhidh-d 502)

body.text: sarvaviṣayaṃ sthānāsthānabalam | āsravakṣayajñānabalaṃ nirvāṇaviṣayaṃ vā catuḥsatyaviṣayaṃ vā ||
body.translated_text: The power of knowledge of ground and non-ground has all [dharmas] as its domain. The power of knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows has <s>nirvāṇa</s> as its domain, or the four truths [as its domain].

body.text: dvidhā hetubhavālambaṃ saptamaṃ satyagocaram /
body.translated_text: The [power of knowledge of] cause and existence as object is twofold; the seventh has the truths as its domain.

body.text: karmavipākajñānabalaṃ bhavaviṣayam | sarvatragāminī pratipatjñānabalaṃ catuḥsatyālambanam |
body.translated_text: The power of knowledge of <s>karma</s>-maturation has existence (<s>bhava</s>) as its domain. The power of knowledge of the practice leading everywhere has the four truths as its object.

body.text: atītādyaddhi dhātvarthamaṣṭamaṃ samudāhṛtam // Abhidh-d_503 //
body.translated_text: The eighth is said to pertain to the element (<s>dhātu</s>) — past and the like. (Abhidh-d 503)

body.text: pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānabalaṃ 'atītādyaddhi'; dhātugocaram ||
body.translated_text: The power of knowledge of past-life recollection has 'the past and the like' — that is, the elements — as its domain.

body.text: navamaṃ khalu rūpārthaṃ saṃskṛtālambyate param /
body.translated_text: The ninth pertains to form; the remaining [power] has conditioned [dharmas] as its object.

body.text: cyutyupapattijñānabalaṃ rūpāyatanaviṣayam anyadyadavaśiṣṭaṃ tatsaṃskṛtadharmagocaraṃ draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: The power of knowledge of death and rebirth has the form-base (<s>rūpāyatana</s>) as its domain. Whatever else remains — that should be seen as having conditioned dharmas as its domain.

body.text: atra punaḥ
body.translated_text: Here, moreover —

body.text: dvyapekṣo balaśabdo 'yaṃ balaṃ tvapratighātataḥ // Abhidh-d_504 //
body.translated_text: this word 'power' (<s>bala</s>) has a twofold reference; [it is] a power because of unobstructedness. (Abhidh-d 504)

body.text: parābhibhavāpekṣaśca sarvāpratighātitvena ca | yatkhalu apratihatasāmathya tadbalamityucyate | mānasaṃ balaṃ daśavidhaṃ bhagavato vyākhyātam ||
body.translated_text: With reference to overpowering others, and in [the sense of] being completely unobstructed — what possesses unobstructed capacity is called a 'power.' The tenfold mental power of the Blessed One has been explained.

body.text: kāyikamapyabhidhīyate-
body.translated_text: The physical [power] too is now stated:

body.text: sandhau sandhau ca buddhasya kāyenārāyaṇaṃ balam /
body.translated_text: In every joint of the Buddha's body, there is the power of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

body.text: spraṣṭavyamadhikaṃ tattu daśa hastyādisaptakāt // Abhidh-d_505 //
body.translated_text: That tangible [power] is ten times greater than [the power of] seven [groups] of elephants and the like. (Abhidh-d 505)

body.text: nārāyaṇaṃ nāma balamucyate | tacca bhagavato marmaṇi marmaṇi vidyate | nāgagranthiśaṅkalāśaṅkusandhayaśca yathākramaṃ buddhapratyekabuddhacakravartinaḥ |
body.translated_text: The power called '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' is [a unit of strength]. And that exists in every vital point of the Blessed One [of the Buddha]. The joints — of elephant-knot (<s>nāgagranthi</s>), chain-link (<s>śaṅkalā</s>), and hook (<s>śaṅku</s>) types — belong respectively to the Buddha, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and the universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>).

body.text: kiṃ pramāṇaṃ punastannārāyaṇaṃ balam ? yatkhalu daśānāmitarahastīnāṃ balaṃ tadekasya gandhahastinaḥ | evaṃ daśottaravṛttyā mahānagnapraskandivarāṅgacānūranārāyaṇānāṃ vācyam | airāvaṇasahasrasyetyanye | sa hi devodyānayātrāsamaye trayastriṃśacchirasamātmānamabhinirmāyātyadbhutavicitrodyānāyāyamānāni tāvantyeva devakulānyanekasahasraparivārāṇi bhūrjapatravadādāya gacchaḥyeṣa balasamudayastasya | evaṃ tu varṇayanti mānasabalavadanantaṃ kāyikamapi balaṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmiti | tatpunaḥ kāyikaṃ balaṃ spṛṣṭavyāyatanasaṃgṛhītam | gurutvena balasaṃgraho laghutvena daurbalyasyeti varṇayanti |
body.translated_text: What, moreover, is the measure of that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-strength? The strength of ten other elephants equals that of one rutting elephant. Thus, in a series of tenfold increases, the strength of great naked ascetics (<s>mahānagna</s>), cavalry chargers (<s>praskandin</s>), champions (<s>varāṅga</s>), wrestlers (<s>cānūra</s>), and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> should be stated. Others say: [the strength] of a thousand <s>Airāvaṇas</s>. For when attending the garden-festival of the gods, he creates himself with thirty-three heads, and as many divine families with retinues of many thousands, attending the most wondrous and marvelous garden, he takes them [all] up like birch-bark leaves and goes — this is the aggregate of his strength. But [others] describe it thus: like the mental strength, the physical strength of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, is also infinite. That physical strength, moreover, is comprised in the tangible sense-base (<s>spṛṣṭavyāyatana</s>). They describe the collection of strength as heaviness, and weakness as lightness.

children.translated_text: Because of having fully attained one's own and others' purposes — the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>); (Abhidh-d 506)

children.text: ādyantabalarūpe dve dve karma pratipaddhiyoḥ // Abhidh-d_506 //
children.translated_text: the first and last two are of the nature of strength, [the other] two concern action and practice-wisdom. (Abhidh-d 506)

body.text: sūtra uktam- "samyaksambuddhasya vata me sata ime dharmāstvayānabhisambuddhāḥ" iti vistaraḥ | atra hi prathamadvitīyābhyāṃ svārthasampadbhagavatodbhāvitā | pūrveṇa jñānasampat | dvitīyena prahāṇasampat | dvābhyāmanyābhyāṃ parārthasampadā darśitā vyavadānasaṃklelodbhāvanāt |
body.translated_text: It is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'Being indeed a Perfectly Awakened One, these <s>dharmas</s> were not fully awakened to by you' — and so on in detail. Herein, by the first two [fearlessnesses], the Blessed One's attainment of one's own purpose is revealed. By the first, the attainment of knowledge. By the second, the attainment of abandonment. By the other two, the attainment of others' purpose is shown, through revealing purification and defilement.

body.text: kataratpunarvaiśāradyaṃ kati jñānātmakam ? taducyate | sthānāsthānabalarūpamādyam | āsravakṣayajñānarūpaṃ dvitīyam | karmasvakajñānabalaṃ tṛtīyam | sarvatragāminīpratipatjñānabalaṃ caturthaṃ vaiśāradyam | tadyāvajjñānasvabhāvānyetāni valāni tāvatsvabhāvāni yathākramaṃ catvāri vaiśāradyāni boddhavyāni |
body.translated_text: Which fearlessness, moreover, is of the nature of how many knowledges? That is stated: The first is of the nature of the strength [of knowledge] of what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānabala</s>). The second is of the nature of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñāna</s>). The third is the strength of knowledge of one's own actions (<s>karmasvakajñānabala</s>). The fourth fearlessness is the strength of knowledge of the practice leading everywhere (<s>sarvatragāminīpratipatjñānabala</s>). Insofar as these strengths are of the nature of knowledge, to that extent the four fearlessnesses should be understood as having those respective natures.

body.text: sūtra uktam- "trīṇīmāni smṛtyupasthānāni yānyāryaḥ sevate" iti vistaraḥ | teṣāṃ punaridaṃ lakṣaṇam-
body.translated_text: It is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'There are these three foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) that the noble one cultivates' — and so on in detail. Their characteristic, moreover, is this:

children.translated_text: Dependent on the threefold excellence of listeners, the threefold foundation of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthiti</s>) — (Abhidh-d 507)
has the characteristics of recollection, composure, and clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>). (Abhidh-d 507)

body.text: śuśrūṣakāśuśrūṣakādibhedādvineyānāṃ traividhyena vyavasthānam | śuśrūṣakādivargatrayābhisandheḥ | svabhāvaḥ punaḥ smṛtiviśiṣṭasaṃprajanyatrayasvabhāvāni trīṇi smṛtyupasthānāni | smṛtiviśiṣṭasaṃprajanyato hi bhagavataḥ śuśrūṣamāṇāśuśraṣamāṇatadubhayayukteṣu vineyasamūheṣu nānando bhavatyāghāto vā ||
body.translated_text: Because of the threefold distinction of disciples — willing listeners, unwilling listeners, and so forth — the determination is threefold. Because of the intent toward the three groups of willing listeners and the like. The intrinsic nature, moreover: the three foundations of mindfulness are of the nature of the threefold clear comprehension distinguished by mindfulness. For through clear comprehension distinguished by mindfulness, the Blessed One experiences neither delight nor vexation toward groups of disciples who are attentive, inattentive, or a mixture of both.

body.text: mahākaruṇā punaḥ
body.translated_text: Great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), furthermore —

children.translated_text: because of being of the nature of conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>), because of following for a long time, (Abhidh-d 508)
because of operating equally everywhere, and the like — great compassion belongs to the <s>Buddha</s> alone. (Abhidh-d 508)

body.text: yadā śrāvakasyāpi karūṇā vidyate pratyekabuddhasyāpi kasmād buddhasyaiva mahākṛpetyucyate ? yasmādiyaṃ saṃvṛtijñānasvabhāvā śrāvakādīnāmadveṣasvabhāvā buddhasya ca dīrghakālānugatā sūkṣmānugatā sarvasattvasamagrahapravṛttā sarvatrānugatā ca dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇavidyotitaśarīrādhyāsinī daśabalaparigṛhītā ca | tasmād buddhasyaiva bhagavato mahākṛpetyucyate | uktā asādhāraṇaguṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: When even a <s>Śrāvaka</s> has compassion, and a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> also, why is it called great compassion only for the <s>Buddha</s>? Because this [compassion of the <s>Buddha</s>] is of the nature of conventional knowledge — whereas that of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others is of the nature of non-hatred — and because it has followed for a long time, followed in subtle form, operates in embracing all sentient beings, follows everywhere, resides in a body illuminated by the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>), and is supported by the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>). Therefore it is called great compassion of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, alone. The uncommon qualities have been stated.

body.text: śrāvakasādhāraṇā ucyante-
body.translated_text: The qualities shared with <s>Śrāvakas</s> are stated:

children.translated_text: <s>Araṇā</s> (non-contention), resolution-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>), and the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>); (Abhidh-d 509)

children.text: arhatsāntānikā hyete pañca tu prāntakoṭikāḥ // Abhidh-d_509 //
children.translated_text: these belong to the <s>arhat</s>'s continuum, but the five are 'final-extremity' [qualities]. (Abhidh-d 509)
The qualities common to others also, such as non-heedlessness (<s>apramāda</s>) and the like, (Abhidh-d 510)

children.text: eṣāṃ yathopadiṣṭānāṃ śṛṇu vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam // Abhidh-d_510 //
children.translated_text: of these as enumerated — listen, I shall state their characteristics. (Abhidh-d 510)

body.text: tatra tāvat |
body.translated_text: Therein, to begin with:

children.translated_text: <s>Araṇā</s> (non-contention) is conventional knowledge, based on the last <s>dhyāna</s> [fourth], for a person of good conduct; (Abhidh-d 511)
belonging to the continuum of a noble one, arisen, with a real basis, [and] seeing without stain. (Abhidh-d 511)

body.text: iha kaścidarhannakopyadharmā sarvakleśaprahāṇātparamāmṛtasukhamanubhavatyevaṃ cittamutpādayati- kathaṃ nāma pare 'pi ime santānālambanād kleśān notpādayeyuḥ kathañca tamaniṣṭaphalaṃ nānubhaveyuḥ | caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ vivṛddhikāṣṭhāgataṃ samāpadya tathā karoti yathāsya cāravihāragatasya santāne na kaścitkleśamutpādayati |
body.translated_text: Here, a certain <s>arhat</s> of unshakeable nature (<s>akopyadharmā</s>), having completely abandoned all afflictions, experiences the supreme bliss of the deathless. He generates the thought: 'How might others too not generate afflictions by taking my continuum as their object, and how might they not experience that undesirable fruit?' Having entered the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> that has reached its highest development, he acts in such a way that no one generates afflictions with respect to his continuum while he dwells in that mode of conduct.

children.translated_text: Resolution-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>) too is likewise, but apprehending all <s>dharmas</s>; (Abhidh-d 512)
it belongs to one of unshakeable nature, and the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) are declared likewise. (Abhidh-d 512)

body.text: praṇidhijñānamapi saṃvṛtijñānasvabhāvaṃ prāntakoṭika caturthadhyānalābhāt, arhadyadyatpraṇidhatte tattajjānīte praṇidhijñānasya sarvadharmālambanatvāt ||
body.translated_text: Resolution-knowledge too is of the nature of conventional knowledge, from the attainment of the final-extremity fourth <s>dhyāna</s>; whatever an <s>arhat</s> resolves, that he knows, because resolution-knowledge has all <s>dharmas</s> as its object.

body.text: pratisaṃvidaḥ khalvapi
body.translated_text: The analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) too —

children.translated_text: the first is the discriminator of non-confusion regarding the meaning connected with what is intended to be expressed; (Abhidh-d 513)
the second is that which manifests it, [and] should be known as investigating knowledge; (Abhidh-d 513)
the third concerns verbal formations (<s>śabdasaṃskāra</s>), destroying confusion about knowledge; (Abhidh-d 514)
the fourth is discourse in connected speech, oriented toward the production of <s>dhyāna</s> and the like. (Abhidh-d 514)

body.text: tatra dvādaśāṅgapravacanasaṃgṛhīteṣu vakṣyamāṇārthasambandhiṣu vivakṣiteṣu nāmakāyādiṣu yadavivartyaṃ jñānaṃ sā dharmapratisaṃvit | tadavadyotyeṣu paurūṣeyāpauruṣeyasambandheṣu parārthasaṃvṛtyartharāśiṣu yadavivartyaṃ jñānaṃ sārthapratisaṃvit | nāmakāyādivācaka eva vākchabdeṣvarūpadravyaliṅgasaṃkhyāsādhanakriyākālapuruṣo pagrahasambandhini yadavivartyaṃ jñānaṃ sā niruktipratisaṃvit | dharmārthaniruktiṣu dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattivaśitvasaṃprakhyāne yadavivartyaṃ jñānaṃ sā pratibhānapratisaṃvit |
body.translated_text: Therein, with respect to the intended name-bodies (<s>nāmakāya</s>) and so forth, connected with the meaning to be explained, comprised in the twelve-fold teaching (<s>dvādaśāṅgapravacana</s>) — the unwavering knowledge regarding them is the analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s>). With respect to the referents illuminated by those [dharmas] — the collections of conventional meaning connected with personal and impersonal [expressions], for the benefit of others — the unwavering knowledge is the analytical knowledge of meaning (<s>arthapratisaṃvid</s>). With respect to the vocal sounds that express the name-bodies and so forth — what is unwavering knowledge regarding the connection with form-substance, gender, number, case, action, tense, and person — that is the analytical knowledge of etymology (<s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s>). What is unwavering knowledge in the clear exposition of mastery over <s>dhyāna</s>, liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>), <s>samādhi</s>, and attainment, regarding <s>dharmas</s>, meaning, and etymology — that is the analytical knowledge of eloquence (<s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s>).

body.text: ta ete ṣaḍguṇāḥ prāntakoṭikamityucyante ||
body.translated_text: These six qualities are called 'final-extremity' [qualities].

body.text: kā kati bhūmikāḥ punarāsāṃ pratisaṃvidāṃ kā vā kati jñānamayī ? tadavadyotyate-
body.translated_text: How many levels do these analytical knowledges [span], and how many of them are of the nature of knowledge? That is elucidated:

body.text: arthākhyā khalu sarvatra ṣaḍjñānānyathavā nava /
body.translated_text: The one called 'meaning' (<s>artha</s>) [analytical knowledge] indeed [is found] everywhere, [consisting of] six knowledges, or alternatively nine. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: arthapratisaṃvit sarvāsu bhūmiṣu kāmadhātau yāvadbhavāgre navajñānasvabhāvā nirodhajñānaṃ varjayitvā ṣaḍjñānāni nirvāṇasyaiva paramārthatvāt, paracittaduḥkhasamudayamārgajñānāni varjayitvā |
body.translated_text: The analytical knowledge of meaning [is found] in all levels, from the desire realm up to the summit of existence, and is of the nature of nine knowledges — excluding the knowledge of cessation, [or] six knowledges — because <s>nirvāṇa</s> alone is the ultimate truth — excluding the knowledges of others' minds, suffering, origination, and the path.

body.text: pratibhānāhvayāpyevaṃ daśajñānamayī tvasau // Abhidh-d_515 //
body.translated_text: The one called 'eloquence' (<s>pratibhāna</s>) is likewise; but that consists of ten knowledges. (Abhidh-d 515)

body.text: pratibhānapratisaṃvidapi sarvāsu bhūmiṣu daśajñānamayī |
body.translated_text: The analytical knowledge of eloquence too [is found] in all levels, consisting of ten knowledges.

body.text: tatra
body.translated_text: Therein:

body.text: kāme dhyāneṣu dharmākhyā tadanyā tvādyakāmayoḥ /
body.translated_text: In the desire [realm] and <s>dhyānas</s>, [is found] the one called '<s>dharma</s>'; the other [i.e., etymology] in the first desire [realm] and [first dhyāna]. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: dharmapratisaṃvit kāmadhātau caturṣu dhyāneṣu niruktipratisaṃvit kāmadhātau prathame ca dhyāne |
body.translated_text: The analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> [is found] in the desire realm and in the four <s>dhyānas</s>. The analytical knowledge of etymology [is found] in the desire realm and in the first <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: saṃvṛtijñānamayyau tu dve ete pratisaṃvidau // Abhidh-d_516 //
body.translated_text: These two analytical knowledges consist of conventional knowledge. (Abhidh-d 516)

body.text: ubhe apyete saṃvṛtijñānasvabhāve dharmaniruktipratisaṃvidāviti ||
body.translated_text: Both of these — the analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> and the analytical knowledge of etymology — are of the nature of conventional knowledge.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau saptamasyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the third section of the seventh chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: saptamādhyāye
body.translated_text: Seventh chapter,

body.text: caturthapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: fourth section.

body.text: pṛthagjanasādhāraṇāḥ idānīmabhijñādayo guṇā vaktavyāḥ | ta ima ucyante-
body.translated_text: Now the qualities common to ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) — the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) and so forth — are to be stated. They are stated as follows:

children.translated_text: Regarding supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), [divine] hearing, others' minds, former [lives], death-and-rebirth, and exhaustion [of outflows] — (Abhidh-d 517)
direct realization through knowledge is a superknowledge; or it is sixfold wisdom on the path of liberation. (Abhidh-d 517)

body.text: jñānasākṣātkriyā khalu vimuktimārgasaṃgṛhītābhijñetyucyate | keṣāṃ punarguṇānāṃ jñānasākṣātkriyā ? tadapadiśyate | ṛddhipādadivyaśrotracetaḥ- paryāyapūrvenivāsānusmṛticyutyupapādāsravakṣayajñānānāṃ yā jñānasākṣātkriyā sābhijñā | abhijānātītyabhijñāyate vā tayeti abhijñā |
body.translated_text: Direct realization through knowledge comprised in the liberation path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>) is called a superknowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>). Of which qualities, then, is it a direct realization? That is indicated: the direct realization through knowledge of the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>), the knowledge of others' minds (<s>cetaḥparyāya</s>), the recollection of former lives (<s>pūrvenivāsānusmṛti</s>), the knowledge of death-and-rebirth (<s>cyutyupapāda</s>), and the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñāna</s>) — that is a superknowledge. One directly knows (<s>abhijānāti</s>), or it is that by which one directly knows — hence <s>abhijñā</s>.

body.text: kasmātpunarvimuktimārga evābhijñā śrāmaṇyaphalavat na ānantaryamārgasvabhāvāḥ ? paracittajñānasyānantaryamārgapratiṣedhādarhataścāsravakṣayānantaryamārgatyāge kasyacinnirabhijñatvaprasaṃgāt ||
body.translated_text: But why is the superknowledge only on the liberation path, like the fruits of the ascetic life (<s>śrāmaṇyaphala</s>), and not of the nature of the uninterrupted path? Because the knowledge of others' minds would be excluded from the uninterrupted path, and because if the uninterrupted path for the <s>arhat</s>'s exhaustion of outflows were relinquished, there would be the consequence of someone being without superknowledge.

body.text: āsāṃ punaḥ
body.translated_text: Of these, furthermore:

children.translated_text: four consist of conventional knowledge; the knowledge of [others'] minds consists of five knowledges; (Abhidh-d 518)
the superknowledge of exhaustion of all outflows consists of six knowledges, or alternatively ten. (Abhidh-d 518)

body.text: cetaḥparyāyāsravakṣayābhijñe hitvā | cetaḥparyāyābhijñā pañcajñānāni dharmānvayamārgasaṃvṛtiparacittajñānāni | āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā ṣaḍjñānāni daśa vā paracittaduḥkhasamudayamārgajñānāni hitvāathavā daśe'ti ||
body.translated_text: Excluding the knowledge of others' minds and the superknowledge of exhaustion of outflows: the superknowledge of [knowing] others' minds consists of five knowledges — <s>dharma</s>-knowledge, inferential knowledge (<s>anvaya</s>), path-knowledge, conventional knowledge, and knowledge of others' minds. The superknowledge of the direct realization of the knowledge of exhaustion of outflows consists of six knowledges, or ten — excluding the knowledges of others' minds, suffering, origination, and the path — or alternatively ten.

body.text: ṣaṣṭhī sarvatra pañcānyā maulīṣu dhyānabhūmiṣu /
body.translated_text: The sixth [superknowledge] is [found] everywhere; the other five in the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>-levels. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyā sarvāsu bhūmiṣu | śeṣā maulīṣu catasṛṣu dhyānabhūṣviti |
body.translated_text: The direct realization of the knowledge of exhaustion of outflows [is found] in all levels. The remaining [five superknowledges are found] in the four fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>-levels.

body.text: yatnavairāgyato labhyāḥ svabhūmyadharagocarāḥ // Abhidh-d_519 //
body.translated_text: They are obtained through effort and detachment, and have one's own level and lower [levels] as their domain. (Abhidh-d 519)

body.text: sarvāḥ abhijñāḥ yatnato labhyante vairāgyataśca | tatrānucitā yatnataḥ | ucitā vairāgyataḥ | janmāntarābhyastāḥ khalvabhijñā vairāgyato labhyante | vaiśeṣikyo yatnataḥ | 'svabhūmyadharagocarā'ścaitāḥ | ṛddhyā svabhūmiṃ gacchatyadharāṃ ca bhūmim | nirmitanirmāṇamapyevam | divyaśrotrābhijñayāpi svabhūmikamadhobhūmikaṃ ca śabdaṃ śṛṇoti | evaṃ paracittajñānaṃ pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānaṃ ca | cyutyupapādābhijñayā ca svādhobhūmiviṣayaṃ rūpaṃ jānāti ||
body.translated_text: All superknowledges are obtained through effort and through detachment. Therein, the unpracticed ones [are obtained] through effort; the practiced ones through detachment. Superknowledges practiced in former lives are obtained through detachment; special [superknowledges] through effort. And 'they have one's own level and lower levels as their domain': through supernatural power, one goes to one's own level and to lower levels. Created emanations likewise. Through the superknowledge of the divine ear too, one hears sounds of one's own level and of lower levels. Likewise the knowledge of others' minds and the recollection of former lives. And through the superknowledge of death-and-rebirth, one knows form pertaining to one's own and lower levels.

body.text: katamā punarāsāṃ kati smṛtyupasthānāni ?
body.translated_text: How many foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), moreover, belong to these [superknowledges]?

children.translated_text: The knowledge of others' minds is regarded as [comprising] three foundations of mindfulness; (Abhidh-d 520)
for the superknowledges of supernatural power, hearing, and [divine] eye — the first foundation of mindfulness. (Abhidh-d 520)

body.text: paracittābhijñā trīṇi smṛtyupasthānāni kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ hitvā | cittacaittālambanā khalveṣā | ṛddhiśrotracakṣurabhijñāḥ kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ rūpālambanatvāt | ṛddhiḥ khalu caturbāhyāyatanālambanā | divyaśrotracakṣuṣī yathākramaṃ śabdarūpāyatanālambane |
body.translated_text: The superknowledge of others' minds [comprises] three foundations of mindfulness, excluding the foundation of mindfulness of body. For this [superknowledge] has consciousness and mental factors as its object. The superknowledges of supernatural power, [divine] hearing, and [divine] eye have the foundation of mindfulness of body, because they have form as their object. Supernatural power indeed has the four external sense-bases as its object. The divine ear and eye have the sound and form sense-bases as their objects respectively.

body.text: kuśalādibhedena tu
body.translated_text: By the distinction of wholesome and so forth, however:

body.text: divyamavyākṛtaṃ śrotraṃ netraṃ cānyā śubhā matāḥ /
body.translated_text: The divine ear is morally indeterminate, and the [divine] eye too; the others are wholesome. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: divyaśrotracakṣuṣī kilāvyākṛte | tacca na | abhijñānāṃ vimuktimārgasvabhāvyāccakṣuḥśrotravijñānayoścāvikalpatvādvimuktijñānānutpattiḥ | caturṣu dhyāneṣu tu asti prajñāviśeṣaḥ svabhūmikabhūtaphalo yatsaṃmukhībhāvātsvabhūmikaphalameva cakṣuḥśrotraṃ saṃmukhībhāvaṃ gacchati | yattaccakṣuḥśrotravijñānayorāśrayī bhavati tasmānna tadvijñāne saṃprayuktā prajñābhijñeti |
body.translated_text: The divine ear and eye are indeed indeterminate. But that is not so — because superknowledges are of the nature of the liberation path, and because no liberation-knowledge arises for the eye- and ear-consciousnesses, since they are non-conceptual. In the four <s>dhyānas</s>, however, there is a special wisdom, the fruit of the great elements of one's own level, through the coming face to face with which the eye and ear [themselves] of one's own level come into actuality, which serve as the basis for those eye- and ear-consciousnesses. Therefore the wisdom associated with those [eye and ear] consciousnesses is not a superknowledge.

body.text: kathaṃ punaretayorabhijñāśabdaḥ ? taducyate-

children.translated_text: Being the fruit of a superknowledge, [they are called] superknowledge, through the wisdom of mental consciousness. (Abhidh-d 521)

body.translated_text: How then is the term 'superknowledge' applied to these [divine ear and eye]? That is stated:

body.text: abhijñāphalamatrābhijñāśabdenoktam | manovijñānasaṃprayuktayā tu prajñayābhijānātīti | saivābhijñā nirūpakatvāt |
body.translated_text: Being the fruit of a superknowledge — they are called by the term 'superknowledge.' But one directly knows through the wisdom associated with mental consciousness — that alone is the superknowledge, because it is the determining factor.

body.text: kati punarāsāṃ vidyā ?
body.translated_text: How many of these, moreover, are [classified as] knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>)?

children.translated_text: Three are regarded as knowledge, for the removal of confusion about the three times; (Abhidh-d 522)
one is by nature non-learner's [knowledge]; the [other] two from the arising of the non-learner's basis. (Abhidh-d 522)

body.text: pūrvanivāsacyutyupapādāsravakṣayajñānatatsākṣātkriyāstisraḥ khalvaśaikṣyo vidyā ucyante | kasmādetā eva ? eta eva tisro vidyāḥ yasmādābhiravidyātrayaṃ vinivartate | pūrvenivāsābhijñājñayāpūrvāntasaṃmohaḥ nivartate | cyutyupapādābhijñayā tvaparāntasaṃmoho nivartate | āsravakṣayābhijñayā madhyādhvasaṃmohaḥ |
body.translated_text: The direct realizations of the knowledge of former lives, death-and-rebirth, and exhaustion of outflows — these three are indeed called non-learner's knowledges (<s>vidyā</s>). Why these alone? Because it is by these three knowledges that the threefold ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is dispelled. By the superknowledge of former lives, confusion about the past is removed. By the superknowledge of death-and-rebirth, confusion about the future is removed. By the superknowledge of exhaustion of outflows, confusion about the present is removed.

body.text: yadyapi ca tisro 'pyaśaikṣāstathāpi 'ekā svabhāvato 'śaikṣī dve tvaśaikṣāśrayodayāt'; | antyā vāśaikṣī svabhāvataḥ santānataśca | ādye dve tvaśaikṣasantānādaśaikṣāvityucyante |
body.translated_text: Although all three are [states of] one beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), nevertheless 'one is beyond training by own-nature, but the two are called beyond training because of arising in the continuum of one beyond training.' The last [superknowledge] is beyond training both by own-nature and by continuum. The first two are called 'beyond training' because [they arise] in the continuum of one beyond training.

body.text: kati punarāsāṃ prātihāryāṇi ?
body.translated_text: Now, how many of these are miracles (<s>prātihārya</s>)?

children.translated_text: The miracle of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), [of reading] minds (<s>citta</s>), and [of the knowledge of] destruction of outflows (<s>kṣaya</s>) — the threefold miracle is held. (Abhidh-d 523)

children.text: harato dve kuśāstṛbhyo mārebhyo harate param // Abhidh-d_523 //
children.translated_text: Two [miracles] take away [disciples] from false teachers; the last takes away from <s>Māras</s>.

body.text: ṛddhyādeśanāprātihārye khalu kuśāstṛbhyaḥ kapilolūkākṣapādādibhyo vineyajanacittamapahṛtya buddhe bhagavati paramārthaśāstari saṃniyojayataḥ | anuśāsanāpratihāryaṃ mārebhyo 'pahṛtya sarvajñaṃ mārgadeśike pravare pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
body.translated_text: Through the miracles of supernatural power and mind-reading, the minds of disciples are taken away from false teachers such as <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Ulūka</s>, <s>Akṣapāda</s>, and the like, and yoked to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the supreme teacher of ultimate truth. The miracle of instruction takes away [beings] from the <s>Māras</s> and establishes [them] in the omniscient one, the supreme guide of the path.

body.text: kā punariyamṛddhiḥ ?
body.translated_text: Now, what is this supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>)?

children.translated_text: Concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) is called supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>); its fruit is eightfold mastery (<s>aiśvarya</s>). (Abhidh-d 524)
This [fruit] is twofold: locomotion and magical creation; locomotion is held to be threefold.

body.text: ṛddhiḥ khalu samādhirūpā tatphalatvāttu prātihāryamṛddhiratyuktaṃ sūtre | aṅgaparigṛhīte samādhau sati sarvametatprātihārya mṛddhyati | tasmātsamādhireva ṛddhiḥ | tasyāḥ phalamaṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryamaṇimādi |
body.translated_text: Supernatural power is of the nature of concentration; but because [the miraculous display] is its fruit, the miracle of supernatural power is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>. When concentration endowed with its constituents is present, all this miraculous [display] is accomplished (<s>ṛddhyati</s>). Therefore concentration itself is <s>ṛddhi</s>. Its fruit is eightfold mastery — <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the rest.

body.text: yacca sūtre 'padiṣṭamekānekayathecchitarūpāvasthānādistatpunaretamṛddhiphalaṃ dvividhaṃ gatiśca nirmāṇaṃ ca | gatirapi trividhā | tatra
body.translated_text: What is indicated in the <s>sūtra</s> — assuming one or many forms, appearing at will, and the rest — that fruit of supernatural power is twofold: locomotion (<s>gati</s>) and magical creation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>). Locomotion too is threefold. Therein,

children.translated_text: the locomotion of the Teacher (<s>Śāstṛ</s>) is mind-made (<s>manomayī</s>), proceeding from mere wish; (Abhidh-d 525)
for others it is accomplished by resolve (<s>adhimokṣa</s>); and then there is body-conveying [locomotion].

body.text: manojavāḥkhalu ṛddhirbuddhasyaiva | manasa iva javastasyāḥ | yāvatā kālena cakṣurvijñānaṃ nīlaṃ pratipadyate yāvatā kālena bhagavāñccharīreṇa sarvalokāntarāṇi vyāpnotyanantarddhiśarīrā hi buddhā bhagabanto 'nābhogena yathecchitābhiprāyasiddheḥ bhagavato buddhasya | śrāvakādīnāṃ punaḥ śarīravāhinī gatirbhavati yathā devānāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ vā | ādhimokṣikī ca dūramapyāsannamadhimucyāstagamanaṃ saṃpadyate | bāhuprasāraṇamātreṇa sumerumūrddhani prādurbhavati | vyākhyātaṃ samādhiphalam ||
body.translated_text: The mind-speed supernatural power belongs to the <s>Buddha</s> alone. Its speed is like that of mind. In the same time that eye-consciousness cognizes blue, the Blessed One pervades all world-intervals with his body — for the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, have bodies that are not separate from supernatural power, because the Blessed <s>Buddha's</s> intended aims are accomplished without effort. For <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others, however, there is body-conveying locomotion, like that of <s>devas</s> or birds. And through resolve (<s>ādhimokṣikī</s>), even what is far, resolving it to be near, one accomplishes the going — [or] by merely extending the arm, one appears on the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>. The fruit of concentration has been explained.

body.text: gamanaṃ nirmāṇamidānīṃ vaktavm | taddvividhaṃ kāmāvacaraṃ rūpāvacaraṃ ca | tatra tāvat-
body.translated_text: Now magical creation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) is to be stated. It is twofold: belonging to the desire realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) and belonging to the form realm (<s>rūpāvacara</s>). Therein, first:

children.translated_text: In the desire [realm], creation of form, smell, taste, and touch is accepted; (Abhidh-d 526)

children.text: rūpasparśau matau rūpe sveśarīre 'tha vā bahiḥ // Abhidh-d_526 //
children.translated_text: in the form [realm], form and touch are held [to be created]; [this is] in one's own body or externally.

body.text: kāmāvacaraṃ khalu bāhyamāyatanacatuṣṭayaṃ nirmīyate | nānyadīśvarakartṛtvavādābhyupagamaprasaṃgāt | rūpāvacaraṃ tvāyatanadvayaṃ tatra gandharasābhāvāt | tatpunaretat svaśarīre paraśarīre ca draṣṭavyam | etaccaturvidhaṃ nirmāṇaṃ kāmadhātāvevaṃ rūpadhātau draṣṭavyam | ityaṣṭavidhaṃ nirmāṇam |
body.translated_text: In the desire realm, the four external sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) are created — not [sense-bases] other than these, because that would entail the acceptance of the doctrine that <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is the creator. In the form realm, however, only two sense-bases [are created], because smell and taste are absent there. This, furthermore, should be seen in one's own body and in others' bodies. This fourfold creation in the desire realm and likewise in the form realm should be understood. Thus there is eightfold creation.

body.text: kiṃ khalu nirmāṇamabhijñayā nirmīyate ? kiṃ tarhi ?
body.translated_text: Now, is magical creation created by the superknowledge [itself]? Or what then?

children.translated_text: By the mind that is the fruit of the superknowledge; and those [creation-minds] are fourteen. (Abhidh-d 527)
The fruit of the first <s>dhyāna</s> [yields] two; then increasing by one for each higher ground.

body.text: prathamadhyānaphale khalu nirmāṇacitte kāmāvacaraṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ ca, dvitīyadhyānaphalāni trīṇi, tṛtīyadhyānaphalāni catvāri, caturthadhyānaphalāni pañca ||
body.translated_text: In the creation-mind that is the fruit of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, [there are minds] belonging to the desire realm and the ground of the first <s>dhyāna</s> — [making] two. The fruits of the second <s>dhyāna</s> are three; of the third <s>dhyāna</s>, four; of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, five.

body.text: kathaṃ punarnirmāṇacittāni labhyante ?
body.translated_text: Now, how are the creation-minds obtained?

children.translated_text: Their obtainment should be known as being like that of the <s>dhyānas</s>.

body.text: yathā khalu dhyānāni vairāgyata upapattitaḥ prayogataśca labhyante tathā nirmāṇacittāni |
body.translated_text: Just as the <s>dhyānas</s> are obtained through dispassion, through rebirth, and through practice — so too the creation-minds.

body.text: kathaṃ punastadutpadyate ?
body.translated_text: Now, how does it [the creation-mind] arise?

body.text: śuddhakācca svataśca tat /
body.translated_text: It arises from a pure [dhyāna] and from itself.

body.text: śuddhakād dhyānādanantaraṃ nirmāṇacittamutpādyate nirmāṇacittādeva vā nānyataḥ | tataḥ khalvapi nirmāṇacittādanantaraṃ śuddhakadhyānaṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ cotpadyate nānyat | sarvasya ca nirmitasya
body.translated_text: The creation-mind arises immediately after a pure (<s>śuddhaka</s>) <s>dhyāna</s>, or from a creation-mind itself — not from anything else. And from that creation-mind, immediately after, a pure <s>dhyāna</s> or a creation-mind arises — not anything else. And of everything created,

body.text: svabhūmenaiva nirmāṇamadhareṇāpi bhāṣaṇam // Abhidh-d_528 //
body.translated_text: creation is by [a mind of] its own ground; but speech is also by a lower [ground]. (Abhidh-d 528)

body.text: na khalvanyabhūmikaṃ nirmāṇamanyabhūmikena nirmāṇacittena nirmīyate | bhāṣaṇaṃ tu svabhaumenādharabhaumena ca | kāmadhātuprathamadhyānabhūmiko hi nirmitaḥ svabhūmikenaiva cittena bhāṣate | ūrdhvabhūmikāstu prathamadhyānabhūmikena, tatraiva vijñaptisamutthāpakacittasadbhāvāt ||
body.translated_text: A creation of one ground is not created by a creation-mind of another ground. But speech is by [a mind of] its own ground or a lower ground. For a creation belonging to the desire realm or the ground of the first <s>dhyāna</s> speaks only with a mind of its own ground. But those of higher grounds [speak] with a mind of the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, because only there does a mind capable of generating manifest action (<s>vijñapti</s>) exist.

body.text: kiṃ punarnirmitanirmātroḥ krameṇa vāgbhāṣaṇaṃ bhavatyatha yugapat ? taducyate-
body.translated_text: Now, do the created [beings] and the creator speak sequentially or simultaneously? That is stated:

body.text: nirmātraiva sahaiteṣāṃ bhāṣaṇaṃ sugatādṛte /
body.translated_text: Only the creator [speaks]; their speaking is simultaneous with his — except for the <s>Sugata</s> (the <s>Buddha</s>). (Abhidh-d)

body.text: uktaṃ hi
body.translated_text: For it is stated:

children.translated_text: 'When one speaks, all the created [beings] speak;

children.text: ekasya tūṣṇīṃ bhūtasya sarve tūṣṇīṃ bhavanti te || "
children.translated_text: when one falls silent, all of them fall silent.'

body.text: bhagavatastu icchātaḥ pūrvaṃ paścādyugapadvā nirmitā bhāṣante | teṣāṃ punaḥ
body.translated_text: But for the Blessed One, the created [beings] speak before, after, or simultaneously, according to his wish. And of those,

body.text: ekasya bruvataḥ sarve nirmitā bruvate samam // Abhidh-d_529 //
body.translated_text: when one speaks, all the created [beings] speak equally. (Abhidh-d 529)

body.text: adhiṣṭhāya tu nirmāṇaṃ bhāṣante 'nyena cetasā /
body.translated_text: But having established the creation, they speak with another mind.

body.text: 'adhiṣṭhāya tu nirmāṇaṃ'; saṃsthāpyetyarthaḥ | anyena cetasā vijñaptisamutpādakākhyena vācaṃ pravartayatītyato 'pi nāsti nirmāṇāntardhāno doṣaḥ | tatpunaretadadhiṣṭhānaṃ na kevalaṃ jīvata eva | kiṃ tarhi ?
body.translated_text: 'Having established the creation' — meaning having set it up — one activates speech with another mind, called the mind that generates manifest action. Therefore there is no fault of the creation disappearing. And that establishment [of creation] is not only for one who is living. Rather,

body.text: adhiṣṭhānaṃ mṛtasyāpi sthirasyaiva tu vastunaḥ // Abhidh-d_530 //
body.translated_text: establishment [is possible] even for one who has died, but only of a stable thing. (Abhidh-d 530)

body.text: āryamahākāśyapādhiṣṭhānena tadasthiśaṃkalāpasthānaśravaṇāt sthirasyāsthilakṣaṇasya na māṃsarudhirādīnāmasti ||
body.translated_text: Because we hear of the noble <s>Mahākāśyapa's</s> establishment of his bone-relics as [having the quality of] duration — [this pertains to] a stable thing characterized by bones, not to flesh, blood, and the like.

body.text: kiṃ punarekacittenaikaṃ nirmitaṃ nirmiṇotyatha bahūn ?
body.translated_text: Now, does one create one creation with one mind, or many?

body.text: ajayyekamanekena jayiṇastadviparyayaḥ /
body.translated_text: The unconquered, with many [minds creates] one; for the victorious, the reverse. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: ādyābhinirhārairbahubhirnirmāṇacittairekaṃ sopādānaṃ ca nirmitaṃ nirmiṇoti | (

children.translated_text: Jaini_403

children.text: ) rjitāyāṃ tvabhijñāyāṃ nirmāturicchayā bahūnapyekacittena nirūpādānamapi ca nirmiṇoti |
children.translated_text: But when the superknowledge has been mastered, according to the creator's wish, one creates even many [creations] with one mind, and even without material support.

body.translated_text: The beginner creates one creation, with material support, by means of many creation-mind efforts.

body.text: tatputaretannirmāṇacittaṃ dvividhaṃ bhāvanāmayamupapattiprātilambhikañca | tatra
body.translated_text: Furthermore, this creation-mind is twofold: born of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>) and acquired through birth (<s>upapattiprātilambhika</s>). Therein,

body.text: avyākṛtamabhijñotthaṃ upapattya tvayaṃ tridhā // Abhidh-d_531 //
body.translated_text: The [creation-mind] arising from superknowledge is morally indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>); but that [acquired] through birth is threefold. (Abhidh-d 531)

body.text: yatkhalu bhāvanāphalaṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ tadavyākṛtaṃ bhavati | upapattiprātilambhikaṃ tu kuśalādinā triprakāram | tadupapattiphalaṃ daśātiśayayuktam |
body.translated_text: The creation-mind that is the fruit of cultivation is morally indeterminate. But the one acquired through birth is of three kinds — wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), and so on. That fruit of birth is endowed with ten excellences.

children.translated_text: For <s>Arhats</s>, this mastery (<s>aiśvarya</s>) arises in ten ways, (Abhidh-d 532)
due to the conjunction with the knowledge of the destruction of all outflows and twofold liberation.

body.text: yadetatadaṇimādiśaikṣāntaṃ daśavidhamaiśvaryasukhaṃ tadatiśayayuktamarhatāmevopapadyate ||
body.translated_text: This tenfold mastery-bliss — from minuteness (<s>aṇimā</s>) up to the [state] beyond training (<s>śaikṣa</s>) — endowed with excellences, arises only for <s>Arhats</s>.

body.text: yadi tarhi trayāṇāmarhatāmetadaiśvaryaṃ samānamasti kastarhi viśeṣaḥ śāstṛśiṣyayoḥ ? tatredamupadiśyate-
body.translated_text: If then this mastery is equal for three [kinds of] <s>Arhats</s>, what then is the distinction between the Teacher and the disciples? To that, this is pointed out:

children.translated_text: Even when the mastery is equal in this respect, as stated, between the Teacher and the disciples, (Abhidh-d 533)
the Teacher's difference is supremely great — that has been previously stated.

body.text: daśabalādyāveṇikabuddhaguṇacintāyāṃ catuṣpratyayatā nadyuttaraṇe gandhahastya śvaśaśakadṛṣṭāntaiśca viśeṣāntaraṃ boddhavyamiti ||
body.translated_text: In the consideration of the <s>Buddha's</s> unique qualities such as the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>) and the rest, the fourfold causality, and through the similes of crossing a river with an elephant, a horse, a hare, and so forth — a further distinction should be understood.

body.text: abhidharmapradīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau saptamasyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmapradīpa</s>, in the <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s> commentary, the fourth section of the seventh chapter.

body.text: samāptaśca jñānavibhāgo nāma saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The seventh chapter, called the analysis of knowledge (<s>jñānavibhāga</s>), is concluded.

body.text: aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Chapter Eight.

body.text: prathamaḥ pādaḥ |
body.translated_text: First Section.

body.text: vyākhyātā hi vistaraśo vidarśanā | śamatha idānīṃ vaktavyaḥ | sa khalveṣa śamathaścaturthadhyānārūpyasaṃgṛhītaḥ | tatra tu
body.translated_text: The higher insight (<s>vidarśanā</s>) has been explained in detail. Now tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>) is to be stated. This tranquility is included in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and the formless [attainments]. Therein,

body.text: sāṅgā cittasthitirdhyānaṃ taccaturdhāṅgabhedataḥ /
body.translated_text: the stability of mind together with its constituents is <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation); that is fourfold by the division of constituents. (Abhidh-d 534)

body.text: śamathaḥ khalu sāṅgā kuśalā cittaikāgratā dhyānamityucyate | yasya khalu dharmasyāṅgaparigṛhītato(syo ?) drekāt cittacaittānyālambanāntaraṃ na pratipadyante sa dharmaścaitasikaḥ samādhirityākhyāyate | tadaṅgabhedena caturvidhamiti vakṣyāmaḥ | tasyāṃ punaścittasthitau
body.translated_text: Tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>) is wholesome one-pointedness of mind together with its constituents — this is called <s>dhyāna</s>. That <s>dharma</s> which is a mental factor, by the comprehension of which, having been grasped together with its constituents, mind and mental factors do not proceed to another object — that <s>dharma</s> is called <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). We shall state that it is fourfold by the division of its constituents. Now, regarding that stability of mind,

body.text: dhyānoktirāñjasī tatra bhāktī tatsahabhūṣvapi // Abhidh-d_534 //
body.translated_text: the direct designation '<s>dhyāna</s>' applies there; the figurative one applies also to those co-existent [dharmas]. (Abhidh-d 534)

body.text: samādhisvabhāvaṃ khalu paramārthena dhyānam | saparivāraṃ tu gṛhyamāṇaṃ pañcaskandhasbabhāvam | bhaktikalpanayā tatsahabhūṣvapi dharmeṣu tācchabdyam ||
body.translated_text: In the ultimate sense, <s>dhyāna</s> has the nature of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>). But when taken together with its retinue, it has the nature of the five <s>skandhas</s>. Through figurative usage, the term [<s>dhyāna</s>] also applies to the <s>dharmas</s> that co-exist with it.

body.text: saṃkṣepādiyamākhyātā dhyānajātiścaturvidhā /
body.translated_text: In brief, this class of <s>dhyāna</s> is stated as fourfold: (Abhidh-d 535)

body.text: prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ caturthamiti |
body.translated_text: the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the second, the third, and the fourth.

body.text: dravyabhedānahaṃ tasyāḥ pravakṣyāmi yathāgamam // Abhidh-d_535 //
body.translated_text: I shall now state the substance-divisions of that, according to scripture.

body.text: dravyabhedastu dhyānajāteścaturvidhāyāḥ samāpattijāteśca tāvatyā eva samāsena vakṣyāmi ||
body.translated_text: The substance-division of the fourfold class of <s>dhyāna</s> and of the equally [fourfold] class of attainment — I shall state in summary.

body.text: tatra tāvat |
body.translated_text: Therein, first:

children.translated_text: Together with the fourfold group of formless [attainments], the attainments are held to be eightfold. (Abhidh-d 536)
The <s>dhyāna</s> [attainment] is in four or five <s>skandhas</s>, functioning by classes, as stated.

body.text: pañcaskandheṣu vargībhūteṣu dhyānasamāpattiḥ prajñāpyate | catuḥpañceṣvārūpyasamāpattiriti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>dhyāna</s> attainment is designated as consisting of the five <s>skandhas</s> grouped together. The formless attainment is in four [or] five.

children.text: bhedena tu samāpattidravyāṇi daśa sapta ca /
children.translated_text: But by division, the substance-units of the attainments are seventeen. (Abhidh-d 537)
Together with the eight <s>sāmantakas</s> (preparatory stages), and also with the <s>dhyānāntarikā</s> (intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>).

body.text: aṣṭānāṃ khalu samāpattibhūmīnāmaṣṭānāmeva sāmantakadravyāṇāṃ tatpraveśopāyabhūtāni dhyānāntarikā ca prathamadhyānasaṃgṛhītā | etāni khalu saptadaśa yathāsthaulyaṃ bhidyamānāni saptadaśa bhavantītyata āha-
body.translated_text: Of the eight attainment-grounds, the eight substance-units of their preparatory stages — which serve as the means of entry into them — and the <s>dhyānāntarikā</s>, which belongs to the first <s>dhyāna</s> — these seventeen, when divided grossly, become seventeen. Therefore it is said:

body.text: tadbhedāḥ khalvime 'nyepi vakṣyante śāstracoditāḥ /
body.translated_text: These divisions and yet others, prompted by the <s>Śāstra</s>, will be stated. (Abhidh-d)

body.text: anye 'pi khalu samāpattibhedāstadantargatā eva sūtrābhidharmoditā vakṣyante |
body.translated_text: Other divisions of attainment, included within these very [seventeen], as stated in the <s>sūtras</s> and <s>Abhidharma</s>, will be stated.

body.text: buddhabuddhestu te sarve tattvenāyānti gocaram // Abhidh-d_538 //
body.translated_text: But all of them come within the scope of the <s>Buddha's</s> cognition in reality. (Abhidh-d 538)

body.text: bhagavāneba hi sarvaprathamadhyānasamāpattyādibhedeṣu, anantasvabhāvaprabhāvakriyāphaleṣvaparokṣabuddhivṛttiriti ||
body.translated_text: For the Blessed One alone has direct cognitive function regarding all the divisions of the first <s>dhyāna</s> attainment and the rest, which have infinite own-nature, power, function, and fruit.

body.text: ta ete dhyānārūpyāstriprakārāḥ katham ? tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: How are these <s>dhyānas</s> and formless [attainments] threefold? That is commenced:

children.translated_text: The root <s>dhyānas</s> are threefold by the division of savoring (<s>āsvāda</s>) and the rest. (Abhidh-d 539)

children.text: tathaiva traya ārūpyā bhavāgraṃ tu dvidhā matam // Abhidh-d_539 //
children.translated_text: Likewise the three [lower] formless [attainments]; but the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) is held to be twofold.

body.text: tatra maulāni tāvad dhyānāni traividhyānyāsvādanāsaṃprayuktaśuddhakānāsravabhedāt | evaṃ trayo maulā ārūpyāḥ | bhavāgraṃ tu nāstyanāsravam | kāmadhātorbhavāgrasya ca bhavamūlatvāt ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the root <s>dhyānas</s> first: they are threefold — by the division into savoring (<s>āsvādana</s>), disjoined-pure (<s>śuddhaka</s>), and outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>). Likewise the three root formless [attainments]. But the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) has no outflow-free [mode] — because the desire realm and the peak of existence are the root of [continued] existence.

children.text: sāmantāni dvidhā sapta prathamaṃ tu tridhā matam /
children.translated_text: The preparatory stages are twofold, seven [in number]; but the first is held to be threefold. (Abhidh-d 540)
The <s>dhyānāntarikā</s> (intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>) is likewise threefold; but [the preparatory stage that is] undefiled has a lower ground as its basis.

body.text: prathamadhyānasāmantaṃ hitvānyāni sapta sāmantāni dviprakārāṇyanyatrānāsravāt | prathamadhyānasāmantakaṃ tu triprakāram | kecittu āsvādanāsaṃprayuktaṃ necchanti | tadvad dhyānāntarikā tridheti vartate | yattatrākliṣṭaṃ tadadharāśrayaṃ dravyamiti ||
body.translated_text: Except for the first, the other seven preparatory stages (<s>sāmantaka</s>) are of two kinds — excluding the outflow-free. But the preparatory stage of the first <s>dhyāna</s> is of three kinds. Some, however, do not accept savoring-disjoined [as a type of the first preparatory stage]. 'Likewise the <s>dhyānāntarikā</s> is threefold' is to be supplied. That which is undefiled (<s>akliṣṭa</s>) therein has a lower ground as its substance-basis.

body.text: kiṃ punareṣāmāsvādanādisaṃprayuktānāṃ trayāṇāṃ lakṣaṇam ? ucyate-
body.translated_text: Now, what is the characteristic of the three — savoring-disjoined and the rest? It is stated:

children.translated_text: That which is accompanied by craving, like savoring, is held to be worldly and pure (<s>śuddhaka</s>). (Abhidh-d 541)
That which has been [applied to] the lower [realms] and is to be savored — [while] the outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) is beyond the world.

body.text: yatkhalu satṛṣṇaṃ tadāsvādanāsaṃprayuktamityucyate | tṛṣṇāyā āsvādaparyāyatvāt | yattu na saṃprayuktaṃ tadapi tṛṣṇāsahagatatvādāsvādavadityucyate tṛṣṇayaikaphalatvāt | yattu sāsravaṃ kuśalaṃ samāpattidravyaṃ tacchuddhakamākhyāyate | kleśamalāsaṃparkādalobhādiśukladharmayogācca |
body.translated_text: That which is accompanied by craving is called 'associated with relishing' (<s>āsvādanāsaṃprayukta</s>) — because craving is a synonym for relishing. That which is not associated [with craving] is also called 'as if relishing' because of being accompanied by craving, since it has the same fruit as craving. But that wholesome attainment-substance which has outflows is called 'pure' (<s>śuddhaka</s>) — because of non-contact with the defilement of afflictions, and because of its connection with white dharmas such as non-greed and the rest.

body.text: tadetacchuddhakaṃ tasyāsvādanāsaṃprayuktasyāsvādyam | tena hi tatsamanantarātītamāsvādyate | yenāsvādayati tamāpanno yadāsvādayati tasmādvyutthitaḥ | anyonyasaṃsargāddhi tṛṣṇāsamādhyornnāmanirvṛtiḥ | tṛṣṇāvaśātsamādherāsvāda nāma, samādhivaśāttṛṣṇāyāḥ dhyāna nāma, anyathā vipratiṣiddhaṃ syāt | na hi kaścittṛṣṇāṃ samāpadyate, na ca samādhināsvādayatoti | lokottaraṃ tu samāpattidravyamanāsravamityucyate ||
body.translated_text: This 'pure' [attainment] is what is relished by that 'associated with relishing' [attainment]. For by that [relishing attainment], the [pure attainment] which has just passed immediately before is relished. One who relishes has entered that [relishing attainment]; that which is relished — one has emerged from that [pure attainment]. For from the mutual contact of craving and <s>samādhi</s>, there is the designation 'delight.' Through the power of craving, the designation 'relishing' applies to <s>samādhi</s>; through the power of <s>samādhi</s>, the designation '<s>dhyāna</s>' applies to craving — otherwise there would be a contradiction. For no one 'enters' craving, nor does one 'relish' by means of <s>samādhi</s>. But the supramundane attainment-substance is uncontaminated and is called [simply] thus.

body.text: āsāṃ punaḥ samāpattīnāṃ dhyānānyevāṅgavarti nārūpyāḥ | kati punaḥ kasya dhyānasyāṅgāni ? tadidaṃ prastūyate-
body.translated_text: Of these attainments, moreover, only the <s>dhyānas</s> have limbs (<s>aṅgas</s>), not the formless [attainments]. Now, how many limbs does each <s>dhyāna</s> have? That is now introduced:

children.translated_text: In the first wholesome [<s>dhyāna</s>], there are five limbs: applied thought, mental subtlety, (Abhidh-d 542)

children.text: prītiḥ sukhaṃ samādhānaṃ kliṣṭaṃ sukhavivarjitam // Abhidh-d_542 //
children.translated_text: joy, pleasure, and one-pointedness. The afflicted [first <s>dhyāna</s>] is without pleasure.

body.text: prathame tāvacchubhe dhyāne pañcāṅgāni vitarkavicāraprītisaukhyasamādhayaḥ | kliṣṭe catvāri sukhaṃ hitvā ||
body.translated_text: In the first wholesome <s>dhyāna</s>, there are five limbs: applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>), sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>), joy (<s>prīti</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), and concentration (<s>samādhi</s>). In the afflicted [first <s>dhyāna</s>], four — excluding pleasure.

children.translated_text: With inner confidence, the limbs are pleasure, joy, and concentration — (Abhidh-d 543)

children.text: dvitīye 'ṅgāni catvāri kliṣṭe śraddhā sukhādṛte // Abhidh-d_543 //
children.translated_text: four limbs in the second [<s>dhyāna</s>]; in the afflicted, [there is] faith, excluding pleasure.

body.text: dvitīye kuśale dhyāne catvāryaṅgāni | ādhyātmasaṃprasādaḥ prītiḥ sukhaṃ cittaikāgratā ca kliṣṭe dve śraddhā sukhaṃ hitvā ||
body.translated_text: In the second wholesome <s>dhyāna</s>, there are four limbs: inner confidence (<s>ādhyātmasaṃprasāda</s>), joy (<s>prīti</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), and one-pointedness of mind. In the afflicted — two, excluding faith and pleasure.

children.text: tṛtīye pañcame prajñā smṛtyupekṣā sukhaṃ sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: In the third and fifth [dhyānas]: wisdom, mindfulness, equanimity, pleasure, and stability; (Abhidh-d 544)
but in the afflicted, the pair of limbs should be known as concentration and feeling-pleasure.

body.text: tṛtīye śubhe dhyāne upekṣā smṛtiḥ saṃprajñānaṃ sukhaṃ samādhiśca | kliṣṭe tu dve 'samādhirvedanāsukham'; ||
body.translated_text: In the third wholesome <s>dhyāna</s>: equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajñāna</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), and concentration. In the afflicted — two: 'concentration and feeling-pleasure.'

children.text: antye catvāryupekṣe dve samādhiḥ smṛtireva ca /
children.translated_text: In the last [<s>dhyāna</s>], four: two equanimities, concentration, and mindfulness. (Abhidh-d 545)

children.text: kliṣṭe dhyāne caturthe tu dve aṅge vedanā sthitiḥ // Abhidh-d_545 //
children.translated_text: But in the afflicted fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, two limbs: feeling and stability.

body.text: caturthe khalu dhyāne śubhe catvāryaṅgāni | aduḥkhāsukhāvedanā upekṣā ca smṛtipariśuddhiḥ samādhiśca | kliṣṭe tu dve vedanā sthitiśca ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, in the fourth wholesome <s>dhyāna</s>, there are four limbs: the feeling of neither-pain-nor-pleasure, equanimity, purity of mindfulness, and concentration. In the afflicted — two: feeling and stability.

body.text: kati punareṣāṃ dravyato bhavanti kati nāmataḥ ?
body.translated_text: Now, how many of these exist as substances and how many as names?

children.text: dravyātmanā daśaikaṃ ca nāmnā tvaṣṭau daśaiva ca /
children.translated_text: As substances, eleven; but as names, eighteen. (Abhidh-d 546)
These limbs are so stated; from this, a fourfold classification is taught.

body.text: dravyataḥ khalvekādaśa bhavanti | prathame dhyānāṅgāni pañca | dvitīye 'dhyātmasaṃprasādo vardhate | tṛtīye samādhivarjyāni vardhante | caturthe tvaduḥkhāsukhāvedaneti |
body.translated_text: Substantially, there are eleven. In the first <s>dhyāna</s>, five limbs. In the second, inner confidence increases [as a new substance]. In the third, [limbs] other than concentration increase. In the fourth, the feeling of neither-pain-nor-pleasure [is new].

body.text: nanu ca yat tṛtīye dhyāne sukhamuktaṃ tathā prathamadvitīyayoḥ..........
body.translated_text: But was not the pleasure stated in the third <s>dhyāna</s> the same as in the first and second?..........

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau aṣṭamasyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the first quarter of the eighth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, the commentary called <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>.

body.text: aṣṭamādhyāye
body.translated_text: In the eighth chapter,

body.text: dvitīyapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: second quarter.

children.translated_text: And of tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>) —
in the preliminary stages of <s>dhyāna</s> and in the formless [attainments], there is no [fixed] arrangement of limbs. (Abhidh-d 547)

body.text: dhyānasāmantakeṣu khalu vidarśanodṛktā śamatho nyūnaḥ | ārūpyeṣu sarvatra śamatho 'dhikavṛttirvipaśyanā nyūnatarā | vipaśya paśyato saṃjñāyāmiti vacanādaṅginyapi paścāduddeśo bhavati | tataḥ siddhaṃ vipaśyanāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, in the preliminary stages of <s>dhyāna</s>, insight (<s>vidarśanā</s>) predominates and tranquility is deficient. In all formless [attainments], tranquility has greater activity and insight is less. Since [the term] <s>vipaśyanā</s> is derived from 'perceiving in a special way' (<s>vipaśya paśyataḥ</s>), even the later enumeration refers to [what is] endowed with limbs. Therefore, [the formless attainments as] <s>vipaśyanā</s> are established.

body.text: yadā khalu catvāryapi dhyānāni vipākaṃ prati neñjante kasmāccaturthamevānejyamucyate ? tatrāpadiśyate-
body.translated_text: When indeed all four <s>dhyānas</s> do not waver with respect to maturation, why is only the fourth called 'immovable' (<s>ānejya</s>)? That is indicated:

children.translated_text: Because of the destruction of applied and sustained thought, because of the cessation of in-breathing and out-breathing, (Abhidh-d 548)
and because of the absence of feeling through equanimity — the last [<s>dhyāna</s>] is called 'immovable.'

body.text: trīṇi khalvapi dhyānāni señjitānyuktāni bhagavatā vitarkādyapakṣālayogāt | vitarkavicārāśvāsapraśvāsau sukhaduḥkhasaumanasyadaurmanasyānītyaṣṭāpakṣālāḥ | taiścaturthaṃ dhyānamakampyamityuktamabhidharme | vitarkavicāraprītisukhairakampanīyatvādānejyaṃ caturthamuktaṃ sūtre | ābhiprāyikaḥ sūtranirdeśo lākṣaṇikastvabhidharme | tathāhi "sukhaduḥkhayoḥ prahāṇātsaumanasyadaurmanasyayoścāstaṅgamāccaturthaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharati" ityuktam | abhidharme vitarkavicāraprītisukhānyeveñjitam ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, the Blessed One called even the [first] three <s>dhyānas</s> 'wavering' because of their connection with disturbing factors. Applied thought, sustained thought, in-breathing, out-breathing, pleasure, pain, mental pleasure, and mental displeasure — these are eight disturbing factors. By these, the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is called 'unshakable' in the <s>Abhidharma</s>. In the <s>Sūtra</s>, the fourth is called 'immovable' because of not being shakable by applied thought, sustained thought, joy, and pleasure. The <s>Sūtra</s> indication is intentional; that in the <s>Abhidharma</s> is according to characteristics. For thus it is said: 'With the abandonment of pleasure and pain, and the previous disappearance of mental pleasure and displeasure, one enters and dwells in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>.' In the <s>Abhidharma</s>, [only] applied thought, sustained thought, joy, and pleasure are the 'wavering.'

body.text: idamidānīṃ vaktavyam | iha dhyānasamāpattiṣu prathamadvitīyayordhyānayoḥ saumanasyamuktaṃ prītivacanāt | prītirhi saumanasyam | tṛtīye sukhaṃ caturthe upekṣā | tatkiṃmupapattidhyāneṣvapyeṣa eva vedanāniyamaḥ ? netyucyate | kiṃ tarhi ?
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: Here, in the <s>dhyāna</s>-attainments, in the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>, mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>) was stated, because of the mention of joy (<s>prīti</s>) — for joy is mental pleasure. In the third, [bodily] pleasure; in the fourth, equanimity. Is this same restriction of feeling [applicable] also in the rebirth-<s>dhyānas</s>? No, it is said. What then?

children.translated_text: In the first [rebirth-<s>dhyāna</s>]: joy, pleasure, and equanimity; in the second, excluding pleasure; (Abhidh-d 549)
pleasure and equanimity in the third; in the last, only equanimity is to be known.

body.text: prathamadhyānopapattau khalu tisro vedanāḥ | sukhaṃ trivijñānakāyikaṃ, saumanasyaṃ manobhaumamupekṣā caturvijñānakāyikī | dviṃtīyadhyānopapattau dve vedane saumanasyopekṣe manobhūmike | nātra sukhamasti pañcavijñānakāyābhāvāt | tṛtīyadhyānopapattau dve vedane manobhūmike | caturthadhyānopapattāvupekṣaiva vedanā vidyata iti ||
body.translated_text: In the rebirth in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, there are three feelings: pleasure belonging to the three [sensory] consciousness-groups, mental pleasure belonging to the mental ground, and equanimity belonging to the four consciousness-groups. In the rebirth in the second <s>dhyāna</s>, two feelings: mental pleasure and equanimity — both of the mental ground. There is no [bodily] pleasure there because of the absence of the five [sensory] consciousness-groups. In the rebirth in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, two feelings of the mental ground. In the rebirth in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, only equanimity as feeling exists.

body.text: nanu ca dvitīyādiṣu dhyāneṣu rūpaśabdaspraṣṭavyānāmupalabdhayaḥ santi vijñaptisamutthāpakaṃ ca cittam | tatkathaṃ tatra trivijñānakāyikā vedanā nāstītyucyate, vitarkavicārau ceti ? naiṣa doṣaḥ | svabhūmikapratiṣedhāt | kutastena tarhi rūpādayo vijñāyante ka yavijñaptiścotthāpyate ? tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: But in the second and subsequent <s>dhyānas</s>, there are perceptions of form, sound, and tangibles, and also mind that produces manifest [bodily] action (<s>vijñapti</s>). Then how can it be said that there is no feeling belonging to the three [sensory] consciousness-groups, and no applied and sustained thought? This is not a fault — because of the negation [applying only] to those of one's own ground. By what, then, are forms and the rest cognized and bodily action produced? That is indicated:

children.translated_text: Visual, auditory, and body-consciousness, and likewise [consciousness] that generates manifest [action] — (Abhidh-d 550)
whichever is in a ground without sustained thought — from the first [<s>dhyāna</s>], but that is indeterminate.

body.text: dvitīyadhyānopapannāḥ khalu rūpaśabdaspraṣṭavyānyupalipsavo jigamiṣavo prathamadhyānabhūmikāni cakṣuvijñānādīni trīṇi vijñānāni vijñaptisamutthāpakaṃ ca saṃmukhīkṛtya nirmāṇacittavadupalabhante spandante ceti | tatpunaḥ prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ cittamavyākṛtameva saṃmukhīkurvanti na kuśalaṃ nyūnenābahumānatvānna kliṣṭaṃ vītarāgatvāt | tadyathā kaścidīśvaro daridramitragṛhaṃ gataḥ | tenāsau suhṛdā sarvasvapradānenopanimantrito mitracittānuvartanayā hīnotkṛṣṭaṃ vastu hitvā yatkiñcid gṛhṇīte tadvaditi | vyākhyātasvarūpāṇi dhyānāni ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, those reborn in the second <s>dhyāna</s>, wishing to perceive form, sound, and tangibles, and wishing to move, bring face-to-face three consciousnesses — visual and the rest — belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, and consciousness that produces manifest [action], and perceive and move — like a creation-mind (<s>nirmāṇacitta</s>). They bring face-to-face that consciousness of the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground that is only indeterminate — not wholesome, because of disrespect for what is inferior; not afflicted, because of being free from passion. Just as a wealthy person who has gone to the house of a poor friend, being invited by that well-wishing friend with an offering of everything, out of compliance with the friend's intention, rejecting what is inferior or superior, takes whatever [is available] — so it is.

body.text: ārūpyāḥ vaktavyāḥ | tadārabhyate-
body.translated_text: The formless [attainments] are to be stated. That is commenced:

children.translated_text: One attracted by the apprehension of the sign of space is called [one who has attained] infinite space-perception. (Abhidh-d 551)
He is free from all form — the formless [attainment] designated as the sphere of infinite space.

body.text: anantākāśanimittodgrahaḥ tatsaṃjñāpravṛttinimittaṃ paścāttu catuḥskandhālambanāstadanyatamālambanā anyadharmālambanā vā manaskārāḥ saṃmukhībhāvaṃ gacchanti | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "sarvvaśo rupasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramātpratidhasaṃjñānāmastagamānnānātvasaṃjñānāmamanasikārādanantamākāśamānantyayāyatanamupasampadya viharati" iti |
body.translated_text: The apprehension of the sign of infinite space — the cause for the operation of that perception — but subsequently, mental activities that have four aggregates as their object, or one of those [aggregates], or some other dharma, come face-to-face. For the Blessed One said: 'By completely transcending perceptions of form, by the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, by not attending to perceptions of diversity, [thinking] "space is infinite," one enters and dwells in the sphere of infinite space.'

body.text: kaḥ punarāsāṃ tisṛṇāṃ rūpādisaṃjñānāṃ viśeṣaḥ ? prapañcarūpasaṃjñābhiratra viśeṣo boddhavyaḥ | tadasmādāgamādvividhādyā rūpārūpyaskandhāḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ | tatra samāpattilakṣaṇā cittānuparivartinā śīlena viyutā śeṣenopapatti lakṣaṇāt | ta eta ārūpyāḥ prathamārūpyasāmantakaṃ hitvā vibhūtarūpasaṃjñā bhavanti | prathamasāmantakaṃ tu caturthadhyānāvidūṣitavṛttitvādgāḍhabandha miti | atastadekaṃ na vibhūtarūpasaṃjñākhyaṃ labhate |
body.translated_text: Now what is the distinction among these three perceptions of form and the rest? The distinction here is to be understood through the elaborate perceptions of form. From this teaching, the various form and formless aggregates are included. Therein, those characterized by attainment, being disjoined from the morality that follows the mind, are [distinguished] from those characterized by rebirth. These formless [attainments], excluding the preliminary stage of the first formless [realm], are called 'free from the perception of form.' But the first preliminary stage, because its activity is not far removed from the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, is [considered] 'tightly bound.' Therefore that one alone does not receive the designation 'free from the perception of form.'

body.text: kathaṃ punarnirdhāryate nārūpyeṣu rūpamastīti ? āgamādyuktitaśca | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 413)

children.text: ) āgamastāvat- "sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramāt" ityāviṣkṛtamidam | anyadāptavacanam- "arūpiṇaḥ santi sattvāḥ" iti | īṣadrūpatvādarūpiṇonudarā kanyāvaditi cet | na | sarvaśa ityapadeśāt, niḥsaraṇokteśca | uktaṃ hi "rūpāṇāṃ niḥsaraṇamārūpyāḥ" iti | yathā hi "yat kiñcidabhisaṃskṛtamabhisaṃviditaṃ nirodhastasya niḥsaraṇam |" nirodhe khalu sarvasaṃskṛtaviyogo 'myupagamyate | na hi mūrtivigrahalakṣaṇo mokṣaḥ tatpravṛttinirodhitvāt |
children.translated_text: First, from scripture: 'By completely transcending perceptions of form' — this has been disclosed. Another authoritative statement: 'There are formless beings.' If [one objects] that they are 'formless' [only] in the sense of having very little form, like a slender young woman — no, because of the word 'completely' (<s>sarvaśaḥ</s>), and because of the statement about escape. For it is said: 'The escape from forms is the formless [realms].' Just as: 'Whatever is conditioned and experienced — cessation is its escape' — in cessation, separation from all conditioned [things] is acknowledged. For liberation is not characterized by having a material body; because it is the cessation of the operation of that [conditioned existence].

body.translated_text: But how is it determined that there is no form in the formless [realms]? From scripture and from reasoning.

body.text: yuktirapi | rūpāśrayādīnyavadhūya svodvegamukhena tadāśrayāddasyūpadrutatadviyuktadeśāśrayavat | uktastarhyārūpyebhyo rūpiṣūpapadyamānānāṃ rūpamutpadyate hetupratyayādhipatipratyayabalāt, nāmarūpasyānyonyahetutvācca | tatra sabhāgavipākahetvoreva tayorapyastitvāt kāraṇatvaṃ rūpapratyayena ca vijñānotpattidarśanāt, cittaviśeṣotpādāt mahābhūtendriyaprasādādirūpotpattidarśanāccānyonyahetutvasiddhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Reasoning also [supports this]: Having shaken off the basis of form and the rest through the door of one's own urgency [to be free], [one departs] from that basis — like [one who flees] from a region infested by bandits to a region free of them. It is said then that for those being reborn in form [realms] from the formless, form arises through the power of the projecting cause, the dominant condition, and because name-and-form are mutual causes. There, since both the homogeneous and maturation causes exist for both [name and form], causation [is established]; and because the arising of consciousness is seen from the condition of form, and because from the arising of a special [state of] mind the arising of form such as great elements and sense-faculties is observed — thus mutual causation is established.

body.text: uktaḥ prayogaprathamārupyaḥ | dvitīyo 'pyucyate-
body.translated_text: The first formless [attainment] with its application has been stated. The second is also stated:

body.text: tadvaccittavibhutvekṣī vijñānānantyalakṣaṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: Similarly, one who sees the pervasiveness of consciousness [attains] that characterized as infinite consciousness. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: ākāśānantyasaṃjñādveṣī tadālambanānantyavijñānādhimokṣābhimukhabuddhiranantaṃ vijñānānantyāyatanamupasampadya viharati | atrāpi paścāccatuḥskandhālambanāstadanyataskandhālambanā śāśvatadharmālambanāśca manaskārāḥ saṃmukhībhavanti | tadvikṣiptasaṃjñakaḥ
body.translated_text: One who is averse to the perception of infinite space, with a mind directed toward the conviction of infinite consciousness as its object, enters and dwells in the sphere of infinite consciousness, [thinking] 'consciousness is infinite.' Here too, subsequently, mental activities having four aggregates as their object, or one of those aggregates, or eternal dharmas as their object, come face-to-face. [He is one] whose perception is dispersed from that [previous attainment].

body.text: vijñānānantyadveṣī ca akiñcanyāhvayaḥ punaḥ // Abhidh-d_552 //
body.translated_text: And one averse to infinite consciousness [attains] that called 'nothingness.' (Abhidh-d 552)

body.text: sa khalu yogī vijñānānantyasaṃjñādveṣī tatrākiñcanasaṃjñitvādākiñcanyāyatanamupasampadya viharati | athavā nāsti kiñciṃdupekṣāprayoganiṣpattirākiñcanyāyatanamityucyate | anantākāraudārikadarśano hi tadviveke saṃjñāvimokṣaḥ pravartate | ata evākiñcanyāyatanaṃ paramopekṣetyucyate | yasmāttatrānantākārānabhisaṃcetanā cetaso 'nābhogatā saṃtiṣṭhate ||
body.translated_text: That yogin, being averse to the perception of infinite consciousness, because of having the perception of nothingness therein, enters and dwells in the sphere of nothingness.
