Or, the accomplishment of the practice of equanimity [thinking] 'there is nothing' is called the sphere of nothingness. For one who sees the infinite-aspect as gross, the perception-liberation operates in its separation. For this very reason, the sphere of nothingness is called 'supreme equanimity' — because therein the non-intentioning of the infinite-aspect, the effortlessness of mind, abides.

body.text: tadvittūcchedaśaṅkī ca na saṃjñāsaṃjñasaṃjñakaḥ /
body.translated_text: And one who fears the annihilation of that [consciousness attains that] designated as neither-perception-nor-non-perception. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: sa khalu saṃkṣiptāmapi vibhutvasaṃjñāṃ saṃjñāśalya iti kṛtvā tāmalpāmapi vispaṣṭaparicchinnarūpāṃ saṃjñāmutsṛjyocchedaśaṅkī ca vispaṣṭarūpāṃ satīṃ naivasaṃjñaṃ nāsaṃjñamupasampadyate | ato naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ samāpadyate | na saṃjñāveditanirodhaṃ nāpi vispaṣṭāṃ pūrvasamāpattisaṃjñām | sarvaiṣu cārūpyeṣu
body.translated_text: That one, regarding even the contracted perception of pervasiveness as a thorn of perception, abandoning even that slight but clearly defined perception — and fearing annihilation when the clearly defined [perception] exists — enters neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Therefore one enters the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception — not the cessation of perception and feeling, nor the clearly defined perception of the previous attainment. And in all formless [attainments] —

body.text: ādau tathā prayuktatvāt tatsaṃjñā vyapadiśyate // Abhidh-d_553 //
body.translated_text: because of being so applied at the beginning, that perception is designated [as the name of the attainment]. (Abhidh-d 553)

body.text: na tu tanmātrasaṃjñā evārūpyā ityāviṣkṛtametatpūrvameveti | vyākhyātāni maulānyaṣṭau samāpattidravyāṇi ||
body.translated_text: But the formless [attainments] are not [constituted by] that perception alone — this has been disclosed previously. The eight principal attainment-substances have been explained.

body.text: sāmantakānāṃ punarādidhyānasāmantakasyānāgamyākhyasya kiṃ rūpam ? tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: Of the preliminary stages, moreover — what is the nature of the preliminary stage of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, called <s>anāgamya</s> (the 'not-yet-attained')? That is indicated:

children.translated_text: That which has initial application (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained application (<s>vicāra</s>), which is dependent, which has accompaniment,
and the mind that has noble and non-noble aspects — that is called the access (<s>anāgamya</s>). (Abhidh-d 554)

body.text: yatkhalu prathamamauladhyānapraveśopāyacittaṃ savitarkaṃ savicāramupekṣāvedanāsaṃprayuktaṃ sānuparivartakaṃ...............
body.translated_text: Indeed, that mind which is a means of entering the first fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>, which has initial and sustained application, which is conjoined with equanimity-feeling, which has accompaniment...........

body.text: ......abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau aṣṭamasyādhyāyasya dvitīyapādaḥ || .......
body.translated_text: ......End of the second quarter of the eighth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, the commentary called <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>. .......

body.text: aṣṭamādhyāye
body.translated_text: In the eighth chapter,

body.text: tṛtīyapādaḥ | ......
body.translated_text: the third quarter. ......

body.text: ..........vyutkrāntakasamāpattiṃ, samāpadyante tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: ..........the leaping attainment (<s>vyutkrāntakasamāpatti</s>) — they attain [it]; that is now indicated:

children.translated_text: Four meditators are declared, from the examination of the four <s>dhyānas</s>;
[they are] perceivers of success-in-failure, and so on, [with stages of] decline and the rest. (Abhidh-d 555)

body.text: catvāro hi dhyāyino bhagavatoktāḥ | "teṣāmekaḥ samāpattau vipattisaṃjñī, dvitīyo vipattau sampattisaṃjñī, tṛtīyaḥ sampattau sampattisaṃjñī, caturtho vipattau vipattisaṃjñī" iti | ete hānasthitiviśeṣotkarṣadhyānabhedadarśanayogāt catvāro bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: Four meditators are indeed stated by the <s>Bhagavat</s>: 'Of these, one perceives failure in attainment; the second perceives success in failure; the third perceives success in success; the fourth perceives failure in failure.' These are four because of seeing the distinctions of decline, stability, distinction, and superior <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: kaḥ punarayaṃ dhyātā kāni vā dhyānadhyeyadhyānaphalāni ? tadāviṣkriyate-
body.translated_text: Who then is this meditator, and what are the meditation, the object of meditation, and the fruit of meditation? That is made clear:

body.text: dhyātā proktastathā dhyeyaṃ dhyānaṃ dhyānaphalaṃ tathā /
body.translated_text: The meditator is declared; likewise the object, the meditation, and the fruit of meditation.

body.text: sarvametaccatuṣṭayaṃ pūrvameva vistareṇābhihitam | bhavatastu
body.translated_text: All this fourfold [classification] has been previously stated in detail. But for you —

body.text: asiddheruktadoṣatvānnāstyātmādicatuṣṭayam // Abhidh-d_556 //
body.translated_text: because of non-establishment, and because the stated faults [apply] — there is no [such] fourfold [classification] of self and the rest. (Abhidh-d 556)

body.text: na hi tavaitaccatuṣṭayaṃ siddham aupaniṣadasāṃkhyavaiśeṣikādiparikalpitapramātṛpramāṇaprameyapramāṇaphalāni pūrvamevoktadoṣāṇi ||
body.translated_text: For this fourfold [classification] is not established for you — the knower, the means of knowledge, the knowable, and the fruit of knowledge as conceived by the <s>Aupaniṣada</s> (Vedāntin), <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>, and others — [these have] the faults already stated.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ karmānuṣṭhānānmokṣo bhavati, āhosvijjñānānuṣṭhānāditi ? tatra brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: Does liberation come about from the performance of action, or from the practice of knowledge? Regarding that, we say:

children.translated_text: Liberation [comes] from the performance of action and likewise from the practice of knowledge,
because activity [in both] exists, and because of the understanding of the true nature [of things]. (Abhidh-d 557)

body.text: trīṇi khalu karmāṇi | dānaśīlabhāvanākhyānyanuṣṭhāya daśa ca jñānāni dharmasvasāmānyalakṣaṇasaṃmohapratipakṣabhūtānyanuṣṭhāya paraṃ brahma prāpnoti nānyatheti | tadetadāviṣkriyate-
body.translated_text: There are indeed three actions — called giving (<s>dāna</s>), moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>), and meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — having practiced which, and having practiced the ten knowledges that are the antidote to confusion regarding the particular and general characteristics of <s>dharmas</s>, one attains the supreme <s>Brahman</s> (liberation) — not otherwise. That is now made clear:

body.text: karma tvatra dvidhā jñeyaṃ puṇyāpuṇyakriyākriye /
body.translated_text: Action here should be known as twofold: meritorious and non-meritorious activities.

body.text: tatra khalu
body.translated_text: Therein indeed —

body.text: puṇyakriyā tridhā proktā viratistadvidhoditā // Abhidh-d_558 //
body.translated_text: meritorious activity is declared threefold; abstinence is stated to be of that [same] kind. (Abhidh-d 558)

body.text: karmādicintāyām ||
body.translated_text: — in the reflection on <s>karma</s> and the rest.

children.translated_text: But knowledge should be known as the ultimate, as previously illustrated.
One who resorts to anything other than that chews on iron [i.e., wastes effort]. (Abhidh-d 559)

body.text: yastu manyate paśvādyālaṃbhanādibhiḥ karmabhiḥ bhoktṛbhogyāntaraparijñānādibhiśca mokṣo bhavati sa vaktavyaḥ 'khalīnaṃ carvayati |'; yasmāt
body.translated_text: One who thinks that liberation comes from actions such as binding animals and the like, and from the discernment of the difference between the experiencer and the experienced — to him it should be said: 'he chews on iron.' Because —

children.translated_text: killing, greed, falsehood, and the like, being directed toward harming others,
should be known as causes of lower realms and obstructors of the gateway to the highest good. (Abhidh-d 560)

body.text: hiṃsānṛtalobhādayo hi doṣāḥ kugatigamanahetavo na svargāpavargagamanopāyāḥ | śāstracoditā hiṃsā nādharma iti cet | na | śāstralakṣaṇāparijñānāt | katham ? yasmāt
body.translated_text: For faults such as harming, falsehood, greed, and the like are causes of going to evil destinies, not means of going to heaven and liberation. [Objection:] 'Harming enjoined by scripture is not <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).' [Reply:] No — because of not having fully understood the definition of scripture. How? Because —

children.translated_text: from enjoining what is in accord with reason, from protecting against suffering, from instructing [against] faults —
[a text] is called 'scripture' (<s>śāstra</s>); what is other than that should be known as the babbling of a madman. (Abhidh-d 561)

body.text: yatkhalu pramāṇatrayaviruddhārthaṃ vākyam, yacca pāpakebhyaḥ karmebhyaḥ kugatigamanahetubhyo nivāraṇena trāyate, yacca rāgadveṣamohānanuśāsti tadvākyaṃ (

children.translated_text: [page reference: Jaini 418]

children.text: ) śāstramityucyate | nānyaditi | tasmādanyadanāptavacanam | na | vedamantrāṇāṃ viṣopaśamanasāmarthyadarśanāt | pratyakṣaṃ hi pramāṇaṃ balīyastatpūrvake ca dve pramāṇe trayīdharmābhihite pramāṇamiti | tatredaṃ pratyucyate-
children.translated_text: ) is called 'scripture.' Not anything else. Therefore, anything else is the word of the unreliable. [Objection:] No — because the power of Vedic <s>mantras</s> to neutralize poison is observed. For direct perception is the strongest means of valid knowledge, and the two [other] means of knowledge that are based on it — [all of which] are taught in the three <s>Vedas</s> — are valid. To that, this is replied:

body.translated_text: Indeed, that speech which does not contradict the three means of valid knowledge, which protects by restraining from evil actions that are causes of going to evil destinies, and which instructs [against] attachment, hatred, and delusion — that speech (

children.translated_text: The power of Persian and other <s>mantras</s> to expel poison is seen in some cases,
but not in all — because of the non-prevention of ill omens and the like. (Abhidh-d 562)

body.text: dṛṣṭaṃ hi sāmarthyaṃ pārasīkaśabarakāpālikādimantrāṇāmapi na tu tairmantraiḥ pāpanāśo 'bhyupagabhyate bhavadbhiḥ, na ca sarvasya viṣamaṃ praśamayanti; tadgatāriṣṭādinā maraṇadarśanāt | yadi ca śāstracoditā hiṃsā mantrasāmarthyāddharmāṅgaṃ sampadyate kasmānna mantrasāmarthyādeva paśuṃ ghātayati ? kiṃ śastrapātanagalāmreḍakādyupakramānuṣṭhānena ? mantrasāmarthyādeva ca piṣṭakṛtapuroḍāśānāṃ svargagamanahetorapūrvasyābhivyaktirbhavatvalaṃ paśvādivadheneti | dṛṣṭaṃ ca mantrāṇāṃ viṣopaśamane sāmarthyaṃ na tu vināhārapānādibhiḥ kṣuttṛṣṇapraśamanādiṣu | evaṃ mantrāṇāṃ viṣopaśamane sāmarthyaṃ bhavatu | mā bhūtpāpavināśana iti |
body.translated_text: For the efficacy of <s>mantras</s> of Persians, <s>Śabaras</s>, <s>Kāpālikas</s>, and others is also observed — yet the destruction of evil is not accepted by you through those <s>mantras</s>, nor do they pacify all poison, because death through ill omens and the like connected with that [poison] is observed. And if harming enjoined by scripture becomes a component of <s>dharma</s> through the power of <s>mantras</s>, why does it not kill the animal by the power of the <s>mantra</s> alone? What is the need for procedures such as striking with a weapon, strangling, and the like? And let the manifestation of the <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit), which is the cause of going to heaven, occur by the power of the <s>mantra</s> alone for the sacrificial cakes made of flour — enough with the slaughter of animals and the like! And the efficacy of <s>mantras</s> is seen in neutralizing poison, but not in pacifying hunger and thirst without food, drink, and the like. Thus, let <s>mantras</s> have efficacy in neutralizing poison — but let them not have [the power of] destroying evil.

body.text: yadapyucyate bhavadbhiḥ | vaitānakarmānuṣṭhātāro brāhmaṇā eva mokṣavartmanyadhikriyante netare varṇā iti tadapi ḍimbhābhihitameva satāṃ pratibhāti | yasmāt |
body.translated_text: As for what you also say — that only <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who perform the <s>Vaitāna</s> (Vedic fire) rites are qualified on the path to liberation, and not the other classes — that too appears to the wise as mere childishness. Because —

children.translated_text: the mind is defiled by attachment and the rest, and purified by faith and the rest;
since [this applies] to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> as well, therefore only one endowed with qualities is liberated. (Abhidh-d 563)

body.text: tadyathauṣadhaṃ viśuddhakoṣṭhasyaivārogyaṃ janayati nolbanavātādidoṣasya | tasmādbhavyajātīyaḥ śraddhādiguṇaparibhāvitātmā kumbhakāro 'pi mokṣavartmanyadhikriyate | na caturvedo rāgadveṣamohādidoṣorarīkṛtacittabhūmiriti | alamatiprasaṅgena prakṛtameva prastūyatām | tadidamārabhyate-
body.translated_text: Just as medicine produces health only for one whose constitution is purified, not for one with excessive wind and other imbalances — therefore, even a potter of the right spiritual lineage, whose self is cultivated by qualities such as faith and the rest, is qualified on the path to liberation; but not a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> learned in the four <s>Vedas</s> whose mental ground is hardened by faults such as attachment, hatred, and delusion. Enough with this digression — let the main topic be resumed. That is now commenced:

children.translated_text: The pure [meditation] is fourfold — the decline-part and so forth, in order,
corresponding to lesser, equal, superior strength, and the stainless [path]. (Abhidh-d 564)

body.text: caturvidhaṃ khalu śuddhakaṃ hānabhāgīyaṃ sthitibhāgīyaṃ viśeṣabhāgīyaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyam evamārupyamanyatra bhavāgrāt | taddhi trividhaṃ viśeṣabhāgīyaṃ hitvā ||
body.translated_text: The pure (<s>śuddhaka</s>) [meditation] is indeed fourfold: the decline-part (<s>hānabhāgīya</s>), the stability-part (<s>sthitibhāgīya</s>), the distinction-part (<s>viśeṣabhāgīya</s>), and the penetration-part (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). Likewise for the formless [attainments], except for the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). For that is threefold, excluding the distinction-part.

body.text: kiṃ punareṣāṃ lakṣaṇam ?
body.translated_text: What then is their definition?

body.text: kleśasvoparimasthānanīrajaskānuvarti vā /
body.translated_text: [They are] conforming to the defilement of one's own or higher plane, or following the stainless [path].

body.text: yathākramaṃ khalu kleśotpattyanuguṇaṃ hānabhāgīyaṃ, svabhūmyanuguṇaṃ sthitibhāgīyamūrdhvabhūmyanuguṇaṃ viśeṣabhāgīyamanāsravānuguṇaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyam | tasmādanāsravamutpadyate |
body.translated_text: In order: that which conforms to the arising of defilements is the decline-part; that which conforms to one's own plane is the stability-part; that which conforms to the higher plane is the distinction-part; that which conforms to the outflow-free [path] is the penetration-part. From that, the outflow-free [state] arises.

body.text: athaiṣāṃ caturṇāṃ kati kasmādanantaramutpadyante ?
body.translated_text: Now, how many of these four arise immediately after which?

body.text: dve trīṇi trīṇi ca dve vā hānapakṣyādyanantaram // Abhidh-d_565 //
body.translated_text: Two, three, three, and two [arise] immediately after the decline-part and the rest. (Abhidh-d 565)

body.text: hānabhāgīyasya khalvanantaraṃ dve utpadyete hānasthitibhāgīye | sthitibhāgīyasya trīṇyanyatra nirvedhabhāgīyāt | viśeṣabhāgīyasyāpi trīṇyanyatra hānabhāgīyāt | nirvedhabhāgīyānantaraṃ tadevaikamiti ||
body.translated_text: Immediately after the decline-part, two arise — the decline-part and the stability-part. After the stability-part, three — excluding the penetration-part. After the distinction-part also, three — excluding the decline-part. Immediately after the penetration-part, that one alone.

body.text: vyutkrāntakasamāpattirarhato 'kopyadharmaṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: The leaping attainment (<s>vyutkrāntakasamāpatti</s>) belongs to the <s>Arhat</s> of the immovable type (<s>akopyadharman</s>).

body.text: sa khalveṣārhato 'kopyadharmaṇa eva niṣkleśatvātsamādhivaśitvācca | dṛṣṭiprāptasya yadyapi tīkṣṇendriyatvātsamādhau vaśitvaṃ na tu niṣkleśā santatiḥ | samayavimukto yadyapi niṣkleśo na tvasya samādhau vaśitvamiti |
body.translated_text: That [leaping attainment] indeed [belongs] to the <s>Arhat</s> of the immovable type alone, because of being free from defilements and because of mastery over <s>samādhi</s>. For one who has attained through insight (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>), although there is mastery over <s>samādhi</s> due to sharp faculties, the continuum is not free from defilements. For one liberated by occasion (<s>samayavimukta</s>), although free from defilements, there is no mastery over <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text: kathaṃ punariyamutpādyate ?
body.translated_text: How then is this [leaping attainment] produced?

body.text: tatprayogo dvidhā bhūmirgatvāgamyajigīṣayā // Abhidh-d_566 //
body.translated_text: Its practice is twofold: by the planes, having gone [in forward order] and desiring to conquer [in reverse]. (Abhidh-d 566)

children.translated_text: By the order of <s>dharma</s>-planes, the eight [attainments]; from the pure, the outflow-free;

children.text: śuddhakācca tṛtīyaṃ svaṃ niṣṭhā śuddhācca nirmalam // Abhidh-d_567 //
children.translated_text: and from the pure, the third [is] one's own [plane]; the conclusion [is] the stainless from the pure. (Abhidh-d 567)

body.text: 'gatve'tyanulomamaṣṭau bhūmīḥ samāpadya | 'āgamye'ti pratilome samāpadya | 'dvidhe'ti sāsravānāsravā | 'jigīṣaye'ti jayaṃ cikīrṣandharmabhūmyutkrameṇa jetukāmaḥ | śuddhakādanāsravaṃ 'śuddhakācca tṛtīyaṃ svaṃ |'; 'niṣṭhā'; tu śuddhādanāsravam | sa khalvevaṃ vijityānāsravāśca sapta paścātsāsravā prathamāddhyānātsāsravaṃ tṛtīyaṃ samāpadyate | tasmādākāśānantyāyatanaṃ tasmādākiñcanyāyatanamevaṃ punaḥ pratilomaṃ nirjityānāsravā apyekavilaṅghitā anulomaṃ pratilomaṃ ca samāpadyate | eṣa prayogo vyutkrāntasamāpatteḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Having gone' — in forward order, having attained the eight planes. 'Desiring to conquer' — in reverse order, having attained. 'Twofold' — with-outflows and without-outflows. 'Desiring to conquer' — wishing to win, desiring to conquer by the order of <s>dharma</s>-planes. From the pure, the outflow-free; 'and from the pure, the third is one's own.' The 'conclusion' is the outflow-free from the pure. Indeed, having conquered thus — the seven outflow-free [attainments] afterward, from the first <s>dhyāna</s> the with-outflow [one], one attains the third [dhyāna] as with-outflow; from that, the base of infinite space; from that, the base of nothingness — and thus, conquering again in reverse order, the outflow-free [ones] too, skipping one each [in forward and reverse], one attains [them]. This is the practice of the leaping attainment.

body.text: yadā tu prathamāḥ sāsravāḥ tṛtīyamanāsravaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyate tasmātsāsravamākāśānantyāyatanaṃ tasmādanāsravākiñcanyāyatanamevaṃ punaḥ pratilomam | tadā visabhāgatṛtīyadravyagamanādabhiniṣpannā bhavati | ativiprakṛṣṭatvānna caturthaṃ samāpadyate | tāṃ ca triṣu dvīpeṣu samāpadyate ||
body.translated_text: But when, from the first with-outflow [dhyāna], one attains the third <s>dhyāna</s> as outflow-free, from that the with-outflow base of infinite space, from that the outflow-free base of nothingness — and thus again in reverse — then, because of traversing the third [member of each pair] which is of a different class, it becomes fully accomplished. Because of being excessively distant, one does not attain the fourth [by skipping]. And one attains it in the three continents.

children.translated_text: The pure existences of the <s>dhyānas</s> and formless [attainments] are produced in one's own or higher [planes].
But one stationed at the peak of existence relies on the stainless [attainment] at the beginning of the access and elsewhere. (Abhidh-d 568)

body.text: bhavāgraṃ bhavāgre ca saṃmukhīkriyate | adhaśca yāvatkāmadhātorevaṃ śeṣāṇi svasyāṃ ca bhūmāvadhaśceti | ūrdhvo papanno nādharāṃ samāpattiṃ saṃmukhīkaroti vaiyarthyāt | na hi tatrānāsravo mārgo 'sti saṃsāramūlatvāt | na ca vinānāsraveṇa mārgeṇa tatratyāḥ kleśā hantuṃ śakyante | caitanyarūpaṃ puruṣamālambya tadvairāgyamiti cet | na | yuṣmatpuruṣasya kriyāvattve sattvānekatvaikatvopapatteḥ saṃsargidharmitvopapatteḥ buddhivaditi vijñānajñānopalabdhe ca..............................................ti ||
body.translated_text: The peak of existence is made to face the peak of existence itself. And downward, as far as the desire realm — thus the remaining [attainments are faced] in their own plane and below. One born above does not bring to face a lower attainment, because of its uselessness. For there is no outflow-free path there, because [the desire realm] is the root of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Nor can the defilements pertaining to that [realm] be destroyed without the outflow-free path. [Objection:] 'Dispassion from that [is achieved] by taking the conscious-form <s>Puruṣa</s> as object.' [Reply:] No — because, if your <s>Puruṣa</s> were active, the faults of [being either] one or many [with the body] would follow, and it would be a thing subject to association — like the intellect; and because consciousness and knowledge are already apprehended [without needing a separate <s>Puruṣa</s>].......

body.text: kasya punardhyānasya prāptyā kataradbhāvyate ? tadanukramyate-
body.translated_text: Upon attaining which <s>dhyāna</s> is which [attainment] cultivated? That is enumerated:

body.text: bālādyadhyānasaṃprāptau laukikasyaiva bhāvanā /
body.translated_text: Upon the initial attainment of <s>dhyāna</s> by a beginner, only the mundane is cultivated.

body.text: yadā khala pṛthagjanaḥ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ labhate tadāsyānāgataṃ laukikameva bhāvyate |
body.translated_text: When indeed an ordinary person first obtains the [first] <s>dhyāna</s>, then for him only the future mundane [dhyāna] is cultivated.

body.text: ūṣmādivarjye cālabdhe dhyānāntarasamudbhave // Abhidh-d_569 //
body.translated_text: And when one that excludes the warmth stages and the like is obtained, [it being] produced in the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> — (Abhidh-d 569)

body.text: caramabhavikasyoṣmādivarjite '.....................gikasvā(?)nucitam | tatra dhyānāntare prathamaṃ sāsravameva bhāvyate | ucite tu vairāgyalabdhatvānna bhāvyate | ūṣmagatādiṣu tu na bhāvyate | tānyeva dhyānāntarasaṃgṛhītāni bhāvyante prathamaṃ nānāgamyam ||
body.translated_text: for one in the last existence, in [a dhyāna] that excludes the warmth stages and the like, ......practiced [by oneself]. Therein, in the inter-<s>dhyāna</s>, only the with-outflow is cultivated first. But when practiced, because of having been obtained through dispassion, it is not cultivated. In the warmth stages and the rest, however, it is not cultivated — those very [stages] included in the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> are cultivated first, not the access (<s>anāgamya</s>).

body.text: vītarāgasya cālabdhe pūrvasāmantake tathā /
body.translated_text: And for one free from passion, when the access is not yet obtained, [it is] likewise for the preliminary [concentration].

body.text: vītarāgasyānāgamye 'pyalabdhe 'nucite prathamaṃ bhāvyate......................a nāgamyasaṃgṛhītāni bhāvyante na prathamāryamārgasādṛśyāt |
body.translated_text: For one free from passion, when the access too has not been obtained, when practiced, it is cultivated first..............[those stages] included in the access are cultivated, not [those of] the first noble path, because of their similarity.

body.text: viraktasya tu pūrvasya nirmalasyaiva bhāvanā // Abhidh-d_570 //
body.translated_text: But for one who is dispassionate with regard to the former [plane], only the stainless is cultivated. (Abhidh-d 570)

body.text: vītarāgasya tvāryasya prathamasyānāsravasyaiva bhāvanānyāme vā 'bhisamayāntikakṣaṇavarjyeṣu anāsravameva bhāvyate | śaikṣasya ca dvābhyāṃ kṣaṇābhyāmakṣavivardhane bhavāgre ca saptadaśasu .................. | evaṃ navaprakāratayākopyaprativedhe tatpṛṣṭhe ca yatkiñcidbhāvanāmayaṃ saṃmukhīkarotyalabdhaṃ tatrānāsravameva prathamaṃ bhāvyate nobhayabhāvanocyate ||
body.translated_text: But for a noble person who is free from passion, only the outflow-free of the first [dhyāna] is cultivated — or, in the certainty [of the path], excluding the moments near the culmination of direct realization, only the outflow-free is cultivated. And for the learner, at the two moments of faculty-growth, and at the peak of existence in the seventeen [moments].......... Thus, in nine ways, at the penetration of the immovable [type] and its aftermath, whatever meditation-born [attainment] is brought to face that has not yet been obtained — there, only the outflow-free is cultivated first; both states are not mentioned.

children.translated_text: In the path of certainty, at the subsequent-cognition, and at the learner's faculty-growth,
on the unobstructed path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), on the path of seeing — twelve moments. (Abhidh-d 571)
And in the dispassion from the peak of existence, excluding the destruction-knowledge,
For a noble one, in the dispassion from the desire realm, on the final liberation path —
in the three knowledges, in the three called the fixed course (<s>niyāma</s>), excluding the access (<s>anāgamya</s>) — (Abhidh-d 573)
for a learner with passion, in the development of faculties of the first three levels,
in the preparatory and liberation paths — for one whose [attainment] is born of the desire[-realm] up to the [first] <s>dhyāna</s> — (Abhidh-d 574)
in the attainment of the twofold <s>arhatship</s>, on the final liberation path,
and for detached learners — in the conquest of the other three levels, without distraction — (Abhidh-d 575)
the cultivation of both types [of dhyāna] —

body.text: ........................su sāsravānāsravasyāpi prathamasya dhyānasya bhāvanā bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: ........................ the cultivation of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, both with-outflow and without-outflow, occurs.

body.text: nobhayasya tu bhāvanām /
body.translated_text: But there is no cultivation of both [together] —

body.text: anāgamyāśraye nyāma tadbhāgīyodbhavādiṣu // Abhidh-d_576 //
body.translated_text: for one based on the access (<s>anāgamya</s>), in the fixed course, in the arising of the penetrative factors, and so forth. (Abhidh-d 576)

body.text: yadyanāgamyaṃ niḥśrito niyāmamavakrāmati, tasyānāgamyameva bhāvyate na tu prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ kiñcidapi bhāvyate | yadā khalvapyanāgamyānirvedhabhāgīyānyutpādayati................bhāvanayā bhāvyate na tu prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ darśanamārgasādṛśyādityāviṣkṛtametaditi ||
body.translated_text: If one enters the fixed course (<s>niyāma</s>) based on the access, only the access is cultivated — no part of the first <s>dhyāna</s> is cultivated. When indeed one produces the penetrative factors from the access ................ it is cultivated by cultivation, but the first <s>dhyāna</s> [is not cultivated], because of its similarity to the path of seeing — this has been disclosed.

children.translated_text: In the second and subsequent [<s>dhyānas</s>], by this very method, having inferred from reasoning —
the cultivation of the future should be known through knowledge of the <s>Abhidharma</s> method. (Abhidh-d 577)

body.text: dvitīyādiṣu khalvadhidhyāneṣvanayaiva prathamadhyānānāgatābhāvanānītyā tatra yuktimanusaratā yathātantrama............ |
body.translated_text: In the second and subsequent higher <s>dhyānas</s>, by this very method of non-cultivation of the future of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, one following the reasoning in each case ............

body.text: dhyānaṃ kasya kimālambanamityata idamanukramyate |
body.translated_text: Whose <s>dhyāna</s> has what as its object? — Therefore this is now set forth in order:

children.translated_text: The savored (<s>sāsvāda</s>) has its own existence as object; the pure <s>dhyāna</s> is all-seeing;
the wholesome basic formless [attainments] do not take the lower world as object. (Abhidh-d 578)

body.text: āsvādanāsraṃprayuktaḥ svabhūmikaṃ bhavamālambate sāsravaṃ vastvityarthaḥ | nādharāṃbhūmimālambate vītarāgatvānnottarāṃ tṛṣṇāparicchinnatvāt | nānāsravaṃ kuśalatvaprasaṅgāt | kuśalaṃ tu dhyānaṃ śuddhakamanāsravaṃ vā sarvālambanaṃ yatkiñcidasti saṃskṛtamasaṃskṛtaṃ vā | maulānāṃ tu kuśalārūpyāṇāmadhobhūmikaṃ ca sāsravaṃ vastu nālambanam | svabhūmyordhvabhūmyālambanatvāt | anāsravaṃ tvālambanam | sarvānvayajñānapakṣo na dharmajñānapakṣo nādhobhūminirodhaḥ | sāmantakānantaryamārgāṇāṃ tvadharābhūmirālambanam ||
body.translated_text: The savored, being associated with outflows, takes as its object the with-outflow existence of its own level — that is the meaning. It does not take a lower level as object, because of being free from passion [toward it]; nor a higher one, because [one's craving for it is] delimited by craving. Nor an uncontaminated [object], because of the absurd consequence that it would be wholesome. But the pure <s>dhyāna</s> — whether pure (<s>śuddhaka</s>) or uncontaminated — takes all objects whatsoever, whether conditioned or unconditioned. But for the basic wholesome formless [attainments], with-outflow objects of a lower level are not [their] object, because they take as object [only] their own level and higher levels. But uncontaminated [objects are their object] — all [those] belonging to the class of subsequent knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>), not to the class of <s>dharmajñāna</s>, and not cessation of a lower level. But for the uninterrupted paths of the threshold [concentrations], a lower level is the object.

body.text: eṣāñca punastrividhānāṃ dhyānārūpyāṇām
body.translated_text: And of these three types of <s>dhyānas</s> and formless [attainments] —

children.translated_text: by immaculate <s>dhyānas</s> and formless [attainments], the defilements of the mind are abandoned;
but [defilements] of a lower level are obtained even by the pure threshold [concentrations]. (Abhidh-d 579)

body.text: anāsraveṇaiva dhyānārūpyeṇa kleśāḥ prahīyante na kuśalena | kuta eva kliṣṭena ? vītarāgavannādhaḥ prahīyante tasyaiva tadapratipakṣatvāt, na svabhūmau (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 423)

because [the afflictions of one's own level] are even more distinguished [than the counteragent]; nor of a higher level. But afflictions are abandoned even by the pure threshold of the <s>dhyāna</s> and formless [attainments], because they are the counteragent of lower-level [afflictions].

body.translated_text: Afflictions are abandoned by the uncontaminated <s>dhyāna</s> and formless [attainment] alone — not by the wholesome [type]. Much less by the defiled [type]. Like one free from passion, [afflictions] of a lower level are not abandoned [by it], because that [lower-level meditation] is not a counteragent of those [afflictions]; nor [those] of one's own level,

body.text: punaśca | sarvaṃ samādhiṃ saṃkalayya trayaḥ samādhaya uktāḥ sūtre-
body.translated_text: Furthermore, combining all concentrations, three concentrations are stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>:

children.translated_text: Three concentrations are declared: with initial and sustained application, and so forth.

children.text: dhyānāntare sa cārodhaḥ sadvayo 'nyatra nirdvayaḥ // Abhidh-d_580 //
children.translated_text: In the inter-<s>dhyāna</s>, there is ascent; the dual [type exists] below; elsewhere, the non-dual. (Abhidh-d 580)

body.text: "savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ samādhiḥ avitarko vicāramātro 'vitarko 'vicāraḥ" iti | tatra dhyānāntaraṃ tāvadavitarko vicāramātraḥ | satatodhaḥ savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ samāviḥ | paratastvavitarko 'vicāraśca ||
body.translated_text: 'The concentration with initial application (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained application (<s>vicāra</s>), the [concentration] without initial application but with sustained application only, and the [concentration] without initial or sustained application' — thus [they are stated]. There, the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> is without initial application but with sustained application only. Below it, the concentration has both initial and sustained application. But above, it is without both initial and sustained application.

body.text: punaḥ
body.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.translated_text: another [set of] three, both with-outflow and without-outflow, of eleven levels —
the concentrations called emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and the rest, illuminating the noble aspects. (Abhidh-d 581)

body.text: śūnyatābhidheyaḥ samādhirapraṇihita animittaśca tṛtīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The concentration called 'emptiness' (<s>śūnyatā</s>), the 'signless' (<s>animitta</s>), and the third — the 'wishless' (<s>apraṇihita</s>).

body.text: katamaiḥ punareta āryākārāḥ..........................vat ṣoḍaśabhirākārairityatastrayo 'pyanityatādiṣoḍaśākāramatidyotāḥ(?) | pratyekaṃ tu
body.translated_text: Which noble aspects do these [illuminate]? ........................ like the sixteen aspects, therefore these three illuminate the sixteen aspects beginning with impermanence and the like. But individually —

children.translated_text: the wishless has ten aspects; of emptiness, two are held;
the signless operates with four aspects of the deathless. (Abhidh-d 582)

body.text: apraṇihitaḥ khalu samādhiranityaduḥkhākārābhyāṃ saṃprayuktaścaturbhiḥ samudayākāraiścaturbhiśca mārgākāraiḥ..............................tānātmākārābhyāṃ saṃprayuktaḥ | animittaḥ samādhirnirodhākāraiścaturbhirnirodhākārādibhiḥ saṃprayuktaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The wishless concentration (<s>apraṇihita</s>) is associated with the two aspects of impermanent and suffering, the four aspects of origination, and the four aspects of the path — .............................. [the emptiness concentration is] associated with the two aspects of empty and non-self. The signless concentration (<s>animitta</s>) is associated with the four aspects of cessation — the aspects beginning with cessation and the like.

children.translated_text: For the attainment of twofold liberation, the immaculate ones, moreover —
those very three are disclosed under the name 'liberation-face' (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>). (Abhidh-d 583)

body.text: rāgavirāgāccetovimuktiravidyāvirāgāt prajñāvimuktiḥ | tasya vimuktidvayasya.................āviṣkṛtāni | tatra śūnyatāyāḥ saṃprayuktaḥ samādhiḥ śūnyatāsamādhiḥ | na praṇidhatte bhavamityapraṇihitaḥ | daśanimittāpagamādanimittaṃ tadālambanasamādhiranimittaḥ || punaḥ
body.translated_text: Mind-liberation (<s>cetovimuktī</s>) is through dispassion from passion; wisdom-liberation (<s>prajñāvimuktī</s>) is through dispassion from ignorance. For that twofold liberation ................. are disclosed. There, the concentration associated with emptiness is the emptiness-concentration. [The concentration that] does not aspire toward [further] existence is the wishless. Due to the departure of the ten signs, [the object of] the signless — the concentration that takes that as its object is the signless. Furthermore —

body.text: trayo 'parasamādhyākhyā śūnyatāśūnyatādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: three more, called 'subsequent concentrations' — emptiness-of-emptiness and the like.

body.text: teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ samādhīnāmutsargopāyapradarśanārthaṃ śūnyatāśūnyatādayaḥ trayaḥ samādhayo 'bhidharmebhihitāḥ |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of showing the method of relinquishing those three concentrations, three concentrations called 'emptiness-of-emptiness' and the like are stated in the <s>Abhidharma</s>.

body.text: dvayamālambate 'śaikṣaṃ śūnyato 'nityatastathā // Abhidh-d_584 //
body.translated_text: From emptiness and from impermanence, [the first two] take a non-learner [concentration] as their object. (Abhidh-d 584)

body.text: kṣayamapratisaṃkhyākhyamantyo gṛhṇāti śāntataḥ /
body.translated_text: The last apprehends [analytically-]unobstructed cessation and non-analytical cessation, through [the aspect of] 'peaceful.'

body.text: śūnyatādyālambanatvāttannāma aśaikṣaṃ samādhiṃ dvāvaparasamādhī ālambete | śūnyatāśūnyatā aśaikṣaṃ śūnyatāsamādhimālambate śūnyākāreṇa | apraṇihitāpraṇihito 'pyaśaikṣamapraṇihitam anityākāreṇa | na duḥkhato na hetvādito 'nāsravasya atallakṣaṇatvāt | na mārgākārairdūṣaṇīyatvāt | animittānimittatvāt samādhiraśaikṣasyānimittasyāpratisaṃkhyānirodhamālambate | śāntākāreṇānāsravasya pratisaṃkhyānirodhābhāvāt | na nirodhapraṇītaniḥsaraṇākārairanityatānirodhasādhāraṇatvādavyākṛtatvādavisaṃyogācca |
body.translated_text: Because they take emptiness and the like as their object, they are so named. Two subsequent concentrations take a non-learner concentration as their object. Emptiness-of-emptiness takes the non-learner emptiness-concentration as its object, through the aspect of 'empty.' The wishless-of-the-wishless also takes the non-learner wishless [concentration] as its object, through the aspect of 'impermanent' — not through [the aspect of] 'suffering,' nor through 'cause' and the like, because the uncontaminated does not have those characteristics; nor through the path-aspects, because of [the concentration's nature of] being something to be relinquished. The signless-of-the-signless concentration takes as its object the non-analytical cessation (<s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) of the non-learner's signless [concentration], through the aspect of 'peaceful' — because there is no analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) for the uncontaminated; not through the aspects of cessation, excellent, or escape — because of commonality with impermanence and cessation, because of being morally indeterminate, and because of being non-disjunction.

body.text: te punarete samādhayaḥ
body.translated_text: These concentrations, moreover —

body.text: ekādaśabhuvaḥ sarve sāsravā nṛṣvakopinaḥ // Abhidh-d_585 //
body.translated_text: are all of eleven levels, with-outflow, and [arise] in humans for the immovable (<s>akopya</s>) [arhat]. (Abhidh-d 585)

body.text: tatra sāsravā āryamārgadveṣitvānmanuṣyeṣūtpādyante | akopyasyārhataḥ ekādaśabhuvaśca saptasāmantakāni hitvānyāsvekādaśasu bhūmiṣu kāmadhātvanāgamyadhyānāntaradhyānārūpyeṣu |
body.translated_text: There, being with-outflow, they are produced in humans because of being hostile to the noble path. [They belong to] the immovable <s>arhat</s>, and are of eleven levels — excluding the seven thresholds, in the other eleven levels: the desire realm, access, inter-<s>dhyāna</s>, [four] <s>dhyānas</s>, and [four] formless [attainments].

body.text: punaḥ
body.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.translated_text: the cultivation of concentration (<s>samādhibhāvanā</s>) — the first [type], the pure <s>dhyāna</s>, is for happiness;
for seeing — the divine eye and superknowledges are stated; for the analysis of wisdom — [these are] for the practitioner. (Abhidh-d 586)

body.text: "catasraḥ khalu samādhibhāvanāḥ | asti samādhibhāvanā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā dṛṣṭadharmavihārāya saṃvartate" iti vistaraḥ | kuśalaṃ khalu (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 426)

children.text: ) prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ śuddhakamanāsravaṃ vā dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāya samādhibhāvanā | tadadhikatvāt anyānyapi jñeyāni | nāvaśyaṃ samparāyasukhavihārāya, parihīṇordhvopapannaḥ parinirvitatadabhāvāt | divyacakṣurabhijñādarśanāya samādhibhāvanā | prayogajāḥ khalu sarve guṇāstraidhātukānāsravāḥ prajñāprabhedāya samādhibhāvanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: first <s>dhyāna</s>, whether pure or uncontaminated, is the cultivation of concentration for dwelling in happiness in the present life. Because of its predominance — others also should be understood [similarly]. [But it does] not necessarily [conduce] to happiness in future lives, because for one who has fallen away and is reborn in a higher realm, that [happiness] does not exist. The cultivation of concentration for [divine] seeing is through the divine eye superknowledge. All qualities born of effort — whether belonging to the three realms or uncontaminated — are cultivations of concentration for the analysis of wisdom.

body.translated_text: 'There are indeed four cultivations of concentration. There is a cultivation of concentration which, when practiced, developed, and made much of, conduces to dwelling in happiness in the present life' — and so on in detail. The wholesome

body.text: yo 'ntyo vajropame dhyāne sarvakleśakṣayāya sā /
body.translated_text: That last [cultivation], in the diamond-like <s>dhyāna</s> — that is for the exhaustion of all afflictions.

body.text: yaścaturthe dhyāne vajropamaḥ samādhiḥ sa āsravakṣayāya samādhibhāvanā |
body.translated_text: The diamond-like concentration (<s>vajropama samādhi</s>) in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> — that is the cultivation of concentration for the exhaustion of outflows.

body.text: sūtraṃ caitatsamākhyātaṃ buddhenātmopanāyikam // Abhidh-d_587 //
body.translated_text: This <s>sūtra</s> was declared by the Buddha as applied to himself. (Abhidh-d 587)

body.text: ataścaturthameva dhyānamuktamiti ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> alone was stated [as the basis for final liberation].

body.text: abhidharmapradīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau aṣṭamasyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: End of the third section of the eighth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: aṣṭamādhyāye
body.translated_text: Eighth chapter,

body.text: caturthapādaḥ |
body.translated_text: fourth section.

body.text: nirdiṣṭāḥ samādhayaḥ | ataḥ paraṃ samādhisanniśritā guṇā nirdiśyante |
body.translated_text: The concentrations have been stated. Hereafter, the qualities dependent on concentration are set forth.

body.text: apramāṇāki catvāri maitrī karuṇā muditopekṣā ca | apramāṇāḥ, sattvādhiṣṭhānapravṛtterapramāṇapuṇyanirvartakatvādaprameyeṣu phalahetutvācca |
body.translated_text: There are four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>): loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). [They are called] 'immeasurable' because, operating with beings as their basis, they produce immeasurable merit, and because they are causes [of fruit] among immeasurable [beings].

body.text: athāpramāṇānāṃ kaḥ svabhāvaḥ ?
body.translated_text: What, then, is the intrinsic nature of the immeasurables?

children.translated_text: Of the four immeasurables — loving-kindness is non-hatred; likewise compassion;
sympathetic joy is joy (<s>prīti</s>); but for some, equanimity is held to be non-attachment (<s>alobha</s>). (Abhidh-d 588)

body.text: adveṣasvabhāvā maitrī | tathā karuṇā adveṣasvabhāvā | kastarhyetayorapramāṇayorviśeṣaḥ ? ubhayoradveṣātmakatve 'pi maitrī sattvāparityāgavartino dveṣasya pratipakṣo harṣākārapravṛttā ca | karuṇā tāḍanapīḍanābhiprāyavartino dveṣasya pratipakṣo dainyākārapravṛttā ca | ityasti viśeṣaḥ | "somanasyasvabhāvāmuditā" iti paurāṇāḥ | upekṣāpyalobhātmakaiva | eṣo 'pramāṇānāṃ svabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Loving-kindness has the nature of non-hatred. Compassion likewise has the nature of non-hatred. What, then, is the distinction between these two immeasurables? Although both have the nature of non-hatred — loving-kindness is the counteragent of hatred that operates toward abandoning beings, and operates in the mode of delight. Compassion is the counteragent of hatred that operates with the intention of striking and afflicting, and operates in the mode of tenderness. Thus there is a distinction. 'Sympathetic joy has the nature of mental satisfaction' — so [say] the ancients. Equanimity too has the nature of non-attachment alone. This is the intrinsic nature of the immeasurables.

body.text: kasmāccatvāryeva na nyūnānyadhikāni vā ?
body.translated_text: Why are there exactly four — neither fewer nor more?

children.translated_text: This is declared as the counteragent of ill-will, of harmfulness, of discontent, and of craving and hatred —
for the purpose of taming one's own mind. (Abhidh-d 589)

body.text: sūtra uktam- "maitrī āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā vyāpādaprahāṇāya saṃvartate | karuṇā vihiṃsāprahāṇāya | aratiprahāṇāya muditā kāmarāgavyāpādaprahāṇāyopekṣā || "
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sūtra</s> it is stated: 'Loving-kindness, when practiced, developed, and made much of, conduces to the abandonment of ill-will. Compassion [conduces] to the abandonment of harmfulness. Sympathetic joy [conduces] to the abandonment of discontent. Equanimity [conduces] to the abandonment of sensual desire and ill-will.'

body.text: vṛttiḥ punardraṣṭavyā-
body.translated_text: Their mode of operation should be seen thus —

children.translated_text: Loving-kindness operates toward conferring happiness; compassion faces toward the removal of suffering;

children.text: muditā modanānimnā sattvā ebhyeva paścimā // Abhidh-d_590 //
children.translated_text: sympathetic joy inclines toward rejoicing; the last is directed at beings as such. (Abhidh-d 590)
Thus should the mode of operation of these be seen.

body.text: ākārastu punaḥ kathaṃ pratipattavya iti | tadapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: But how should the aspect [of each] be understood? That is indicated:

body.text: ākāraiḥ sukhitādi bhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Through the aspects of 'may they be happy' and so forth.

body.text: sukhitā vata santu sattvā iti manasi kurvan maitrīṃ samāpadyate | duḥkhitā vata sattvā iti karuṇām | modantāṃ vata sattvā iti muditām | sattvā ityeva manasi kurvannupekṣāṃ samāpadyate mādhyasthyāt |
body.translated_text: Attending mentally [with the thought] 'May beings be happy!' — one enters the [concentration of] loving-kindness. 'Beings are suffering!' — compassion. 'May beings rejoice!' — sympathetic joy. Attending mentally merely [with the thought] 'Beings' — one enters equanimity, through impartiality.

body.text: ebhyastvanyatamenāpi brahmasāyujyamaśnute // Abhidh-d_591 //
body.translated_text: Through any one of these, one attains companionship with <s>Brahmā</s>. (Abhidh-d 591)

body.text: ebhyo 'pramāṇebhya ekenāpi bhāvitena brahmatvaṃ pratilabhyata iti ||
body.translated_text: Through even one of these immeasurables, when cultivated, one attains the state of <s>Brahmā</s>.

body.text: kimālambanā apramāṇāḥ, kati bhūmikā vetyapadiśyate-
body.translated_text: What is the object of the immeasurables, and how many levels do they have? That is indicated:

children.translated_text: Among humans, resting on the desire[-realm]; sympathetic joy [exists] in the two <s>dhyānas</s>;
the others are of six levels; some wish [to place them] in seven. (Abhidh-d 592)

body.text: maitrīkaruṇāmuditāstrayaḥ kāmāvacarasattvālambanāḥ | upekṣā aniyatā iti | yeṣāṃ tāvadbhāvanāmayānyetāni muditā ca saumanasyendriyaṃ teṣāṃ prathamadvitīyayordhyānayormuditā | nordhvaṃ saumanasyendriyābhāvāt | anyāni trīṇyapramāṇāni ṣaṭsu bhūmiṣvanāgamye dhyānāntare caturṣu dhyāneṣu | kecit punaḥ cintāmayānyapyetāni pramodyaṃ ca prīterdharmāntaraṃ iti teṣāṃ saptabhūmikā | prāmodyasya vedanādvayasaṃyogitvāt | uktānyapramāṇāni ||
body.translated_text: The three — loving-kindness, compassion, and sympathetic joy — have desire-realm beings as their object. Equanimity is unrestricted. For those for whom these [immeasurables] arise from cultivation, and [for whom] sympathetic joy [is associated with] the faculty of mental satisfaction (<s>saumanasyendriya</s>) — for them, sympathetic joy exists in the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>, not above — because of the absence of the faculty of mental satisfaction [there]. The other three immeasurables exist in six levels: in the access (<s>anāgamya</s>), the inter-<s>dhyāna</s>, and the four <s>dhyānas</s>. But some [hold that] these arise from reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>) as well, and that delight (<s>pramodya</s>) is a dharma different from joy (<s>prīti</s>) — for them, [the immeasurables] are of seven levels, because delight is associated with two [types of] feeling. The immeasurables have been stated.

body.text: atha kati vimokṣāḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, how many are the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>)?

body.text: vimokṣāḥ kathitā aṣṭau teṣāṃ dvāvaśubhātmakau /
body.translated_text: Eight liberations are declared; of those, two have the nature of impurity-[meditation] (<s>aśubha</s>).

body.text: tāvādyadhyānayorantye tṛtīyo 'lobhalakṣaṇaḥ // Abhidh-d_593 //
body.translated_text: The first [two] belong to the first two <s>dhyānas</s> and their last [stages]; the third has the characteristic of non-attachment (<s>alobha</s>). (Abhidh-d 593)

body.text: rūpī rūpāṇi paśyatīti prathamo vimokṣaḥ | ādhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatīti dvitīyo vimokṣaḥ | śubhaṃ vimokṣaṃ kāyeṇa sākṣātkṛtvopasampadya viharatīti tṛtīyaḥ | teṣāṃ dvāvaśubhasvabhāvau prathamau tadākāratvād bhūmitaśca tau sasāmantakayoḥ prathamadvitīyayordhyānayordhyānāntare ca | sasāmantake caturthe dhyāne śubho vimokṣaḥ | ca cālobhasvabhāva eva na tvaśubhātmakaḥ, tacchubhākārapravṛttatvāt | saparivārāstvete pañcaskandhasvabhāvāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Having form, one sees forms' — this is the first liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>). 'Being internally without the perception of form, one sees forms externally' — this is the second liberation. 'Having realized the beautiful liberation with the body, one dwells having attained it' — this is the third. Of these, the first two are of the nature of the unbeautiful (<s>aśubha</s>) [meditation], because they have that aspect. And by level, those two are in the first and second <s>dhyānas</s> with their thresholds, and in the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> [level]. In the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> with its threshold is the beautiful liberation. And that is of the nature of non-greed (<s>alobha</s>) alone, not of the nature of the unbeautiful, because it operates with the aspect of the beautiful. With their accompaniments, these are of the nature of five aggregates.

children.translated_text: Four [more] liberations, called 'formless,' are wholesome and concentrated; (Abhidh-d 594)
the attainment called 'cessation' (<s>nirodha</s>) is declared as the eighth liberation. (Abhidh-d 594)

body.text: catvāro 'nye vimokṣāḥ samāhitāḥ kuśalā evārūpyāḥ draṣṭavyāḥ | saṃjñāveditanirodhastvaṣṭamo vimokṣaḥ | vaimukhyārtho hi vimokṣārthaḥ, nirodhasamāpattiḥ; sarvasālambanapravṛttivaimukhyāt ||
body.translated_text: The other four liberations should be seen as concentrated, wholesome, and formless. But the cessation of perception and feeling (<s>saṃjñāvedita-nirodha</s>) is the eighth liberation. For the meaning of 'liberation' (<s>vimokṣa</s>) is the meaning of 'turning away' — [and] the cessation-attainment [is so called] because of turning away from all object-directed activity.

body.text: tasyāstu saṃmukhībhāvaḥ sūkṣmasūkṣmādanantaram /
body.translated_text: Its coming face to face [occurs] immediately after the 'subtle-subtle' [consciousness]. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: trividhaṃ hi bhāvāgrikaṃ cittaṃ saṃjñāsūkṣmasūkṣmākhyabhedāt | etadyathākramamaudārikam | (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 431)

children.text: ) ataḥ sūkṣmasūkṣmākhyaṃ bhavāgrānantaraṃ tāṃ samāpattiṃ samāpadyante | tathā samāpannānāṃ tu
children.translated_text: ) Therefore, immediately after the [consciousness] at the summit of existence called 'subtle-subtle,' they enter that attainment. But for those who have thus entered —

body.translated_text: For the consciousness at the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) is threefold, by the distinction into [that called] 'perception,' 'subtle,' and 'subtle-subtle.' These are progressively [increasingly] gross. (

body.text: vyutthānacittamapyasyāḥ svaṃ śuddhaṃ nirmalaṃ tvadhaḥ // Abhidh-d_595 //
body.translated_text: the consciousness of emergence from this [attainment] is either one's own pure [consciousness] or undefiled [consciousness] from below. (Abhidh-d 595)

body.text: sāsravānāsravatvāt | tadvyutthānacittasya sāsraveṇa cedvyuttiṣṭhate bhāvāgrikeṇa | anāsraveṇa cedākiñcanyāyatanabhūmikena ||
body.translated_text: Because of being either with-outflow or without-outflow. The consciousness of emergence from that [attainment] — if one emerges with a with-outflow [consciousness], it is of the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). If with a without-outflow [consciousness], it belongs to the level of the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>).

body.text: athaiva vimokṣāḥ kiṃ viṣayāḥ ?
body.translated_text: Now, what are the objects of these liberations?

body.text: kāmāvacaradṛśyārthā vimokṣāḥ prathamāstrayaḥ /
body.translated_text: The first three liberations have visible forms of the desire realm as their objects. (Abhidh-d continuation)

body.text: kāmāvacaraṃ rūpāvacarameṣāmālambanaṃ yathāyogamaśubhataḥ śubhataśca |
body.translated_text: The objects of these [first three liberations] are forms of the desire realm and the form realm, according to applicability, as unbeautiful and as beautiful respectively.

body.text: anye tvanvayadhīpakṣasvordhvaduḥkhādyavekṣiṇāḥ // Abhidh-d_596 //
body.translated_text: But the others contemplate suffering and so forth in their own and higher [levels], belonging to the inferential-knowledge side. (Abhidh-d 596)

body.text: ārūpyavimokṣāṇāṃ svabhūmyūrdhvabhūmikaṃ duḥkhamālambanaṃ taddhetunirodhau ca | sarvacānvayajñānapakṣyo mārga ūrdhvādharabhūmisaṃgṛhītaḥ, apratisaṃkhyānirodhaśca | uktā vimokṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The objects of the formless liberations are suffering belonging to their own and higher levels, together with its cause and cessation. And the path, belonging to the side of all inferential knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>), comprised in higher and lower levels, and <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (cessation not through deliberation). The liberations have been stated.

children.translated_text: In the <s>Sūtra</s>, the eight bases of mastery (<s>abhibhavāyatana</s>) — so named — have been declared. (Abhidh-d 597)
These operate in addition to the liberations, and demonstrate mastery over consciousness. (Abhidh-d 597)

body.text: sūtre bhagavatā aṣṭau abhibhavāyatanānyākhyātāni "adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī (

children.translated_text: (Jaini 432)

children.text: ) bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati suvarṇadurvarṇāni khalu rūpāṇi abhibhūya jānāti, abhibhūya paśyati, evaṃ saṃjñī ca bhavatīdaṃ prathamamabhibhvāyatanam | adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatyapramāṇāni suvarṇadurvarṇānīti vistaro yāvadidaṃ dvitīyamabhibhvāyatanam | evamadhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahī rūpāṇi paśyati parīttānyapramāṇāni ceti catvāri | adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñyeva ca bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati nīlapītalauhitāvadāta......."...............
children.translated_text: ) one sees forms externally — forms that are well-colored or ill-colored, limited [in extent]. Having mastered them, one knows; having mastered them, one sees — thus is one's perception. This is the first base of mastery. Having the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally — unlimited, well-colored or ill-colored' — and so on in detail — 'this is the second base of mastery. Likewise, being without the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally — limited and unlimited' — thus four [more]. 'And being without the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally — blue, yellow, red, white.......'...............

body.translated_text: In the <s>Sūtra</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> declared eight bases of mastery: 'Having the perception of form internally, (

body.text: ........... abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau aṣṭamasyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: ........... End of the fourth section of the eighth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s>.

body.text: aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The eighth chapter is completed.

body.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāvṛttiḥ samāptā ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Abhidharmadīpa Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s> is completed.
